entry.title: Text-Only LLM Correctors Break Correct Transcripts: A Repair-Damage Analysis of Audio Grounding in ASR Error Correction

author.name: Vasiliy Kudryavtsev, Kirill Borodin, Nikita Vasiliev, Mikhail Gorodnichev, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: By decomposing WER changes into repaired, damaged, and inserted tokens, this paper quantifies the harm LLM-based ASR correctors cause: with Gemini 2.5 Flash, text-only correction of its own draft breaks 13-32% of already-correct transcripts versus 1-3% when audio is available, and on medical dictation insertions cancel out net WER gains. The study shows aggregate WER hides substantial damage and that audio grounding is critical.

entry.title: Accelerating Wildfire Hazard Mapping Across Canada with an AI Surrogate Modelling Framework

author.name: Hager Radi Abdelwahed, Toluwaleke Olutayo, Chirag Goel, Jana Osea, Aldo Zaimi, Tom Swystun, Sandy Erni, Francisco Emiliano Lopez Saavedra, Yan Boulanger, Ga\'etan Marceau Caron

entry.summary: An AI surrogate modeling framework that replaces computationally intensive Monte Carlo wildfire simulations (BurnP3/BurnP3+) which currently take days to weeks per regional unit. Developed through collaboration between AI researchers and wildfire experts, it provides a standardized training and evaluation framework plus surrogate models for burn probability and fire behavior, enabling nationwide hazard mapping for mitigation planning.

entry.title: Governance-State Corruption in Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents: A Cross-Model Stress Test

author.name: Bowen Liu, Youting Wang, Bonan Shen, Dingyan Shang

entry.summary: This stress test studies governance-state corruption in LLM agent memory: faults that change which retained records enter model-visible context even when stored content and tasks are fixed. Across six providers with 731 benchmark-grounded bases and 2,080 matched fault pairs, corruption altered the operative context projection in over 96 percent of pairs, and oracle-backed enforcement fully restored it, with large downstream correctness drops. The work exposes a distinct vulnerability class in agent memory systems.

entry.title: DConstrain: Compiling Context-Parameterized Transitions for Diffusion Language Model Constrained Decoding

author.name: Shidong Cao, Jing Ma, Wenhao Chai, Yuchen Tian, Lun Du, Da Zheng

entry.summary: Presents DConstrain, a method for constrained decoding in diffusion language models that compiles schemas into context-parameterized transition programs, enforcing joint token compatibility under a grammar while avoiding exponential state growth. It addresses limitations of prior exact decoders that had to fix property orders and exclude valid outputs.

entry.title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs

author.name: Prajvi Saxena, Sabine Janzen, Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: Separates explicit theory of mind (recognizing beliefs) from applied theory of mind (using beliefs to predict behavior) in LLMs and finds a large gap, e.g., Llama-3.1-8B recognizes mental states at 99.4 percent but predicts behavior at only 28.9 percent on SimpleToM. The paper further tests whether structured prompting and other interventions can recover the gap.

entry.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels

author.name: Thanh Q. Tran, John Russell Himawan, Arun Verma, Kiwan Wong, Wei Xiao, Daniela Rus, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low

entry.summary: DIAL provides fine-grained numerical control over how strongly an LLM adheres to a textual instruction (e.g., how short a response should be), combining classifier-free guidance with a frozen LLM and distilled instruction-adherence levels. It targets joint fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions where prompting alone is unreliable. Authorship includes MIT-affiliated researchers (Daniela Rus).

entry.title: FusionEval: Benchmarking Model Fusion for Large Language Models

author.name: Shuo Cai, Yanggan Gu, Yuhang Liu, Su Lu, Yuanyi Wang, Yang Yu, Zhen Li, Zhitian Hou, Guanghao Zhu, Ming Li, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: FusionEval is a controlled benchmark for model fusion, with expert pools trained from Qwen3 and Llama base models across math, code, science, instruction following, and tool use. It evaluates fusion methods with and without additional training on eight public benchmarks, measuring capability retention and computational cost under comparable data access, revealing that strong averages can mask losses in individual expert skills.

entry.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI

author.name: Konstantinos Vrettos, Eleftherios Tzanis, Haridimos Kondylakis, Evangelia E. Vassalou, Florence X. Doo, Michail E. Klontzas

entry.summary: This paper measures per-patient vulnerability to membership inference attacks across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, arguing that cohort-average privacy risk can hide near-certain exposure of individual patients. It proposes pre-development screening of vulnerable records to make privacy assessment of medical AI more practical.

entry.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Taewhoo Lee, Minju Song, Jungwoo Park, Chanwoong Yoon, Junha Jung, Hyeon Hwang, Sanghoon Lee, Minbyul Jeong, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: SARL is an RL framework that teaches search agents to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, using a dual reward design capturing the corrective effect of retrieved information, without requiring extra assessment at test time. This targets the common failure modes of hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search in retrieval-augmented LLMs.

entry.title: Interpreting Model Reasoning through Behavioral Counterfactuals

author.name: Shawn Im, James Oldfield, Adel Bibi, Sharon Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes behavioral counterfactuals for analyzing model chain-of-thought reasoning: given a fixed response, an intervention to the prompt changes next-token distributions, and a trained module edits the residual stream to minimize KL divergence between output distributions. This localizes and compares reasoning interventions systematically, addressing the variance problem in sampled responses.

entry.title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling

author.name: Yang Liu, Zhiqiang Yuan, Shu-Dong Huang, Jiancheng Lv, Liwei Yang, Qiwei Yan, Kailin Lv, Jinchao Zhang

entry.summary: ULME is a post-training framework that couples embedding and language-modeling objectives so they mutually supervise each other, going beyond parameter-sharing approaches like GritLM where the two capabilities coexist but do not interact. This yields a single model serving both retrieval and generation roles with improved quality in both modes.

entry.title: Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness

author.name: Asal Mehrabi, Mohammad Aliannejadi, Clemencia Siro

entry.summary: This large-scale study measures interactions between prompting strategies and judge models across languages, using 9 prompting strategies, 4 open-weight judges, 27 languages, and 4 tasks over 13 datasets, producing over 1M pointwise scores validated against human judgments. It finds prompting strategies are not transferable: choices validated on English do not reliably hold across judges and languages. This is a significant caution for multilingual LLM-as-a-judge evaluation practice.

entry.title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Mahdi Sabbaghi, George Pappas, Hamed Hassani, Adel Javanmard

entry.summary: AOPD improves on-policy distillation by weighting teacher actions according to their counterfactual advantage under the current student, reinforcing teacher actions that improve the student's expected outcome and downweighting those that do not. This corrects the standard assumption that teacher guidance is uniformly beneficial. The work is relevant to the increasingly important practice of distilling frontier models into cheaper students.

entry.title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Arezoo Bybordi, Favour Achimba, Mariam Gelashvili, Jessy Ramirez, Weigang Qiu, Mand\"e Holford, Anita Raja

entry.summary: Shows that random train/test splits in protein classification cause phylogenetic leakage, inflating reported accuracy in venom ion-channel classification, and reframes cross-species prediction as a structured distribution shift. The proposed multimodal model fuses ESM-2 sequence embeddings with a disulfide-aware graph attention network using persistent homology features to capture phylogeny-invariant structure.

entry.title: GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL

author.name: Shijie Li, Yilin Gao, Tieyuan Chen, Yun Luo, Weiyao Lin, Hang Yu

entry.summary: GIFT addresses conflict between dense token-level distillation gradients and sparse outcome-based RL gradients for reasoning LLMs by performing token-level geometric analysis that decomposes distillation gradients and filters which teacher updates to apply. This principled allocation improves on existing hybrid training approaches.

entry.title: When Forgotten Facts Return: Relearning-Aware Unlearning of Knowledge Graph Embeddings via Tangent Kernels

author.name: Parnian Fazel, Mohammad M Maheri, Hamed Haddadi

entry.summary: This paper shows that approximately unlearned facts in knowledge-graph embeddings reappear under continued training, traced to entity embeddings shared between forgotten and new facts. It proposes Kernel-Anticipated Unlearning (KAU), which uses tangent kernels to anticipate relearning, marking the first study of relearning in KG embeddings.

entry.title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine

author.name: Xiufeng Yang, Konstantinos Vrettos, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Fabian Drexel, Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Johannes Moll, Anirudh Narayanan, Frederike Stumpf, Cosmin I. Bercea, Jiawen Wang, Evangelia E. Vassalou, Krischan Braitsch, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Markus Graf, Marcus R. Makowski, Lisa Adams, Nassir Navab, Michail E. Klontzas, Keno Bressem

entry.summary: A large multi-institutional evaluation of four System 1 models (two proprietary, two open-weight) zero-shot across 86 public clinical tasks in 14 domains and 20 languages, spanning exam questions and medical imaging with capability tiers and AUC-based outcomes. It argues that fast, probability-output models suit high-volume clinical decisions needing calibrated uncertainty and deferral.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks

author.name: Ali Al-Lawati, Elsayed Eshra, Dongwon Lee, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: The paper couples continuous latent-space jailbreak attacks on black-box LLMs to a learned diffusion language model decoder, removing the artificial random mapping that produces unnatural, easily detected prompts. This yields perplexity-aware adversarial prompts that better reflect realistic attack surfaces, including attacks triggering overthinking.

entry.title: EgoHand: Monocular 3D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Video

author.name: Chao-Yeh Chen, Tiffany Chen, Lin Duan, Tianyi Hu, Yu-Hsiang Huang, Umar Iqbal, Jiefeng Li, Edy Lim, Yanchen Liu, Yihan Pang, Hang Qiu, Jun Saito, Shao Su, Qingsi Wang, Xiufeng Xie

entry.summary: EgoHand achieves state-of-the-art monocular 3D hand reconstruction from egocentric video using a 14-million-image curated corpus combining synthetic data, in-the-wild video, and multi-camera motion capture. A transformer encoder with camera cues and an auxiliary 2D branch yields strong zero-shot generalization on HOT3D, ARCTIC, and H2O.

entry.title: Diagnostic Loss: Asymmetric Supervision for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Ignacy Kolton, Wenxuan Li, Zongwei Zhou, Jaros{\l}aw B. \'Cwik{\l}a, Arkadiusz Sitek, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Szymon P{\l}otka

entry.summary: Identifies an objective misalignment in medical vision-language models trained with token-level maximum likelihood, which prioritize textual agreement over diagnostically critical terms, causing missed or hallucinated diagnoses. The authors introduce Diagnostic Loss (DLoss), a differentiable, architecture-agnostic objective encoding the asymmetric requirements of radiology reporting: state supported diagnoses and avoid unsupported ones. This directly targets clinically meaningful report quality.

entry.title: Metric Conformal Prediction via the Conditional Expected Local Radius

author.name: Rui Qiu, Fang Yao, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: Introduces the conditional expected local radius (CELR), a new conformal prediction method for non-Euclidean responses in metric spaces that handles heterogeneity and multimodality without density estimates or vector space structure. It pairs the method with a metric distributional random forest and achieves computational savings by deriving all score components from a single forest fit.

entry.title: TutorCaseBench: A Case-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Tutors in Supporting Students with Challenging Behaviors

author.name: Yeon Su Park, Chanyoung Park, Tae Soo Kim, Seungju Kim, Hyunwoo Kim, Daho Jung, Jinsung Yoon, Juho Kim

entry.summary: TutorCaseBench grounds AI-tutor evaluation in qualitative case studies from pedagogy, educational psychology, and special education, producing 923 dialogues across five challenge types with generation and multiple-choice items. Across 11 frontier LLMs, even the best model satisfies only about 55.8% of rubric criteria. The benchmark reveals substantial gaps in handling students with learning and behavioral difficulties.

entry.title: Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural

author.name: Mustafa Omer Gul, Philippe Laban, Tanya Goyal, Jennifer Neville

entry.summary: The paper identifies a trade-off in LLM-based user simulators: prompted simulators follow complex intents but sound unnatural, while specialized simulators behave realistically but lose task fidelity. The authors propose a reinforcement learning recipe that jointly rewards intent adherence and behavioral naturalness, with a key contribution in designing the reward structure, to enable better evaluation and training of multi-turn AI assistants.

entry.title: RECAP: Looking Once Is Not Enough for Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Zhaolu Kang, Tailong Luo, Chenxin Li, Yingjie He, Zhenyu Yu, Fengyu Zhou, Jiachen Qian, Lei Wei, Shuang Chen, Jiachen Li, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Rongchao Zhang, Zhengtao Yao, Hoi Leong Lee, Guansu Wang, Kaiyue Zhou

entry.summary: The paper studies visual revisit events during chain-of-thought reasoning in VLMs, showing that temporally localized reactivations of image evidence predict answer correctness and causally influence performance. Masking revisit peaks degrades accuracy while injecting them into failed rollouts partially restores correct answers, motivating reward designs that encourage visual grounding during reasoning.

entry.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding

author.name: Advait Gupta, Sachin Konan, Tom Yin, Gabriel Sarch, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces an offline VQA benchmark covering five agentic domains (web, robotics, egocentric video, games, spatial planning) with 1000 manually curated scenarios, enabling scalable, reproducible evaluation of VLM agent capabilities. It complements costly interactive simulator evaluations with faster offline comparisons.

entry.title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Atiksh Bhardwaj, Edward W. Duan, Junwon Seo, Prithwish Dan, Wei-Chiu Ma, Andrea Bajscy, Preston Culbertson

entry.summary: The paper shows that linear probes on a VLA model's own internal activations can serve as runtime monitors detecting when the policy deviates from its intended task, avoiding the cost and complexity of external VLM-based supervision. This offers an efficient route to unsupervised deployment of manipulation policies.

entry.title: From Single-Actor Environments to Multi-Actor Event Worlds: Can LLMs Be Event World Models?

author.name: Juntong Ni, Zewen Liu, Bohan Wang, Lige Zhang, Wei Jin

entry.summary: This paper formalizes event worlds: multi-actor systems where other agents act autonomously and the environment is only partially observed through event logs, then tests whether LLMs can predict future observations from logs and proposed actions. Benchmarks are built from human Diplomacy games and real Polymarket trades, with a hierarchical framework probing rollouts, counterfactual actions, and downstream agent utility.

entry.title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration

author.name: Deepthika S, Pawni Yadav, B. Sankar

entry.summary: A within-subjects experiment with 32 participants interacting with five GPT-5-mini-based assistants containing 0-100% planted plausible falsehoods found that confident, consistent, wrong LLMs cause users to adopt errors: quiz scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 across the manipulation range over 1,040 answers. The study reverses the usual sycophancy question, showing human deference to confident machines and collapse of trust calibration. It has direct implications for human-AI interaction safety.

entry.title: Behind Aggregate Scores: What Systematically Varying Arena-Hard's LLM Judge Reveals

author.name: Louise Yorke

entry.summary: Using 500 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts with fixed answers, the study runs GPT-4.1 as judge under all eight combinations of criteria, output format, and task framing, repeating each setup at temperature zero. It shows similar aggregate scores can conceal substantial verdict instability — rerunning the default setup changes win/tie/loss outcomes on 21.2% of prompts despite about one point of aggregate movement — raising serious concerns about LLM-judge benchmark reliability.

entry.title: MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback

author.name: Xuyang Zhong, Jiuding Yang, Yiwen Guo, Chen Liu

entry.summary: MOER is a mix-policy RL framework that injects a decaying expert chain-of-thought prefix into prompts, letting the model complete reasoning as prefix length is annealed to preserve self-exploration. A selective rollback mechanism replaces failed expert-guided rollouts, addressing training collapse seen in prior expert-guidance methods for RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design

author.name: Zhou Zhang, Hanqun Cao, Minghao Sun, Odin Zhang, Yang Zhang, Pheng Ann Heng, Wujun Li, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: Introduces RiboBridge, a structure-first framework for designing RNA binders to target proteins that separates RNA conformational generation from protein-RNA assembly via cross-frame interaction geometry. It proposes candidate binding interfaces, generates RNA conformations in a pretrained latent space (RiboSphere), and predicts complex geometry without assuming a predefined binding site.

entry.title: Drift Says When, Budget Says How Much: Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Long-Form Multimodal Generation

author.name: Bin Hu, Yingbo Xiao

entry.summary: The paper shows that one-shot KV cache compression at prefill severely degrades long-form multimodal generation, with even oracle selection reaching only 0.44-0.52 ROUGE-L agreement on detailed image description because relevant visual evidence shifts during generation. It proposes rate-controlled KV re-selection, refreshing kept tokens based on attention drift with a budget rather than a fixed threshold.

entry.title: Measuring Research Progress and Linguistic Inclusion in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Atnafu Lambebo Tonja, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Jesujoba Oluwadara Alabi, Israel Abebe Azime, Benjamin Rosman, Ehsan Shareghi, Thamar Solorio, Pontus Stenetorp, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: Analyzes 1,158 peer-reviewed papers from 2020-2025 on low-resource language NLP and introduces the Linguistic Inclusion Framework, measuring research growth, representation expansion, continuity, and distributional equity. Despite a 5.4x publication growth, the analysis reveals persistent inequities in how languages and speaker populations are represented.

entry.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation

author.name: Hongcan Guo, Yian Zhao, Feng Wang, Shen Nie, Guoqiang Wei, Yan Zeng, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Cola2 is a hierarchical language generation framework that separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, dynamically segmenting text into semantic spans with controlled compression rates and training a block-causal masked diffusion decoder under clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions. It jointly optimizes reconstruction, generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. The work contributes to alternative architectures beyond standard token-by-token autoregression.

entry.title: The Fusion Tax: A Diagnostic Analysis of When Hybrid Retrieval Hurts

author.name: Aaditya Chauhan, Arun Agarwal

entry.summary: Treating do-not-fuse as a first-class outcome, this study measures per-query costs of hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion and alternatives across seven BEIR datasets, five dense encoders, SPLADE, and cross-encoder reranking. Even the best fusion method ranks relevant documents below the better of its two components on 13-40% of queries, quantifying a substantial fusion tax that aggregate metrics hide.

entry.title: Same Beliefs, Different Policies: Learning Reusable Representations for Early Stopping in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jingwei Ni, Dmitry Abulkhanov, Vladislav Smirnov, Markus Leippold, Elliott Ash, Timothy Baldwin, Artem Shelmanov, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: BELT (BELief-based Termination) addresses wasted computation in reasoning LLMs by separating outcome prediction from stopping control: it learns beliefs about current and future answers from a frozen LLM's hidden states, then fits a linear stopping policy on frozen features. Because prediction targets are independent of token prices, the same representation supports early stopping at any price without retraining a controller.

entry.title: Group Relative Policy Optimisation Improves Multilingual Speech Recognition in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Tim Wenjie Hu, Evelyn Nafula Ouma, Benjamin Akera, John A. Quinn

entry.summary: The paper extends GRPO-based reinforcement learning from LLM speech models to smaller encoder-decoder ASR systems, using Whisper-large-v3 across 51 African languages to address exposure bias from teacher forcing. Gains are largest when training data is scarce or audio is degraded. The resulting SunflowerASR model achieves the best published macro-averaged WER on AfriVox-v2 and related benchmarks.

entry.title: Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents

author.name: Yunxiang Luo, Xin Xu, Tianhao Chen, Zhixi Xiong, Peiqi Jiang, Fan Zhang, Wei Shao, Xuejian Gao, Yuwei Fan, Can Yang

entry.summary: Introduces OPTICYCLE and OPTISTATE, lightweight inference harnesses that improve LLM translation of natural-language optimization problems into solver programs without any additional training. Evaluated on nine benchmarks with 2,634 problems and 11 Qwen variants (0.6B-27B), execution-guided revision consistently improves macro accuracy.

entry.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ofek Avivi, Eliron Rahimi, Avi Mendelson, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: The authors show that quantization sensitivity in diffusion language models varies by both downstream task and denoising timestep, and that these sensitivity patterns can be predicted without labels. They introduce T2Quant, a mixed-precision quantization framework that allocates activation precision across denoising steps under a fixed bit budget. Validation across three DLMs and six benchmarks makes it relevant as diffusion LMs gain traction.

entry.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Mahdi Salmani, Adel Javanmard, Devansh Gupta, Meisam Razaviyayn

entry.summary: The paper proposes direct optimization of pass@k for pruning partial reasoning chains during test-time scaling, unifying quality-based scoring and diversity-based selection of candidate prefixes. This aims to allocate compute only to promising and diverse candidates, reducing the cost of generating many full solutions.

entry.title: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations

author.name: Cong Cao

entry.summary: This paper addresses a gap in causal inference with high-dimensional multimodal health records: learned representations are typically trained for reconstruction, which may not preserve the information required for causal identification. The authors derive conditions under which representations remain valid for estimating counterfactual outcomes (including patient-level digital-twin risk profiles) and interventional direct/indirect effects under exposure-induced intermediate confounding, and propose doubly robust estimators. They prove that representation learning objectives must go beyond covariate-only reconstruction, and show interventional mediation analysis is strictly more demanding than counterfactual comparison.

entry.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification

author.name: Zhipeng Cao, Peiyang Song, Nikolaus Vertovec, Weiru Cui, Zhihao Yang, Mingkang Liu, Luxia Lin, Bai Xue, Alessandro Abate

entry.summary: LLM2Cert addresses synthesis and verification of Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems, using LLMs to generate certificate candidates that are verified via SMT solvers and the Lean proof assistant. It also reformulates benchmarks beyond the low-dimensional polynomial systems that traditional solvers favor, moving toward engineering-relevant problem classes.

entry.title: Visual Grounding First, Multimodal In-context Learning Follows

author.name: Minhyuk Seo, Minjae Lee, Chaeeun Lee, Wei Lin, Muhammad Jehanzeb Mirza, Tinne Tuytelaars, Jonghyun Choi

entry.summary: The authors identify visual grounding as the key bottleneck in multimodal in-context learning, observing that MLLMs often fail to attend to task-relevant visual evidence in demonstrations and instead over-rely on textual cues, producing hallucinations. They propose ProCoRe to enhance visual grounding and show improved cross-benchmark generalization without ICL-specific training data or the forgetting induced by prior methods.

entry.title: LoRA Superposition across Pretrained Models

author.name: Keigo Watanabe, Hiroshi Kera, Kazuhiko Kawamoto

entry.summary: The paper shows that LoRA adapters trained independently for the same task on different pretrained CLIP backbones can be summed and applied unchanged to all contributing backbones, a construction called LoRA superposition. Across 56 backbone-task pairs the summed adapter nearly matches solo LoRAs, while leave-one-model-out sums fail, indicating the effect depends on participation of each backbone.

entry.title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts

author.name: Mateusz Modrzejewski, Tomasz Radzikowski

entry.summary: The authors show that pairwise reward-model evaluation structurally cancels any score component shared by responses to the same prompt, leaving between-prompt score behavior untested. They propose a human-referenced audit based on between-prompt variance share, sibling-rating regression, and prompt substitutions, applied to eighteen released scorers and six training conditions. Reward model scores are found to cluster by prompt more than human ratings do, meaning cross-prompt comparability assumptions are often violated.

entry.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

author.name: Yancheng Zhu, Yifan Yuan

entry.summary: This empirical study identifies a recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue, termed State Integrity Collapse, where a model retains a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. The authors introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite spanning numerical, format, persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints, and evaluate seven provider-pinned model snapshots across five dialogue depths, finding strict joint retention between 62.4% and 100%. A forked recall audit shows 88.6% of failures are behavioral drift rather than memory loss, a useful diagnostic distinction for instruction-following reliability.

entry.title: Auditing the Hand-Written Inputs of Learned Access Control

author.name: Arsalan Jalil Sarghaleh, Mehdi Hazrati

entry.summary: This paper audits the two hand-built artifacts surrounding learned access control systems: a hard-deny shield and a region map, formalising hard-deny soundness and checking it exhaustively over relations of up to 794,250 tuples. Strikingly, clauses faithfully transcribing explicit restrictions were unsound at rates of 0.50-0.70 across human and LLM elicitors, with 97% of counterexamples stemming from prose scoping ambiguities. The findings expose systematic risks in how access-control restrictions are elicited and encoded.

entry.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ali Najar, Hosein Hasani, Amir Kooshan Fattah, Yasamin Rajabi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

entry.summary: Proposes METTA for meta-RL, splitting fast adaptation into two timescales: a causal neural memory for fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, and compact episode-level summaries for long-range cross-episode task inference. This avoids the quadratic cost of transformer-based trajectory retrieval while retaining adaptation capacity.

entry.title: Optimal Multitask Representations Under a Rate Constraint: An Information Bottleneck Analysis

author.name: Nicholas Stiles, Gregory W. Wornell

entry.summary: Formalizes the choice of pretraining objective as a multitask information bottleneck with a mutual information constraint, characterizing optimal representations for Gaussian inputs and tasks. Results show weakly task-aligned specialists can beat reconstruction generalists at low rates but lose at high rates, and constructs task families where any fixed Gaussian objective incurs unbounded relative regret, while an average task information matrix objective achieves uniform bounds.

entry.title: Federated Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Xiaobao Wang, Renda Han, Zhiliang Xia, Meng Liu, Renxiang Guan, Di Jin

entry.summary: The paper proposes FedGRAG, a framework extending GraphRAG to settings where knowledge graphs are distributed across organizations that cannot share them due to privacy constraints. It addresses constructing global retrieval without a centralized graph and enabling knowledge-enhanced generation across clients.

entry.title: Energy and Latency First: How Deployment Constraints Reverse Time-Series Model Selection

author.name: Shruti Bothe, Illyyne Saffar, Ayush K. Varshney

entry.summary: The authors study time-series model selection under real deployment constraints using handover prediction in cellular networks, where inference must complete within 40 ms deadlines and energy is a cumulative budget. They evaluate eight architectures with a protocol screening for tail deadline feasibility, showing that accuracy rankings can reverse once constraints are considered.

entry.title: Shift-aware score transport for privacy auditing without retraining

author.name: Yaohong Yang, Gauri Pradhan, Qi Chen, Samuel Kaski, Antti Honkela

entry.summary: The paper addresses privacy auditing of deployed models where canaries, retraining, or data-control are impossible, and available non-members differ in distribution from training data. It estimates counterfactual in-distribution non-member score distributions via score transport to correct skewed membership-inference audit results.

entry.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention

author.name: Zi Yang, Ying Li, Alejandro Lancho, Dar\'{i}o C. Larese, Pablo M. Olmos, Michael Minyi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FSKA, a framework that learns expressive nonstationary attention kernels by parameterizing a bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows. The approach remains compatible with scalable linear-attention computation while adapting the similarity structure to complex token interactions. It advances the kernelized-attention view of self-attention beyond fixed stationary kernels.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions

author.name: Marcos Matabuena, Xiaokai Luo, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla

entry.summary: Proposes a deep learning framework for regression with random objects (distributions, graphs, functions) living in general metric spaces, operating directly on the metric structure rather than imposing manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions. Motivated by modern clinical and digital biomarkers, it extends principled deep learning to non-Euclidean outcomes.

entry.title: Silicon Samples Match the Answers but Not the Respondents

author.name: Yusuke Kumagae, Masahiro Kaneko

entry.summary: This paper critiques silicon sampling (using LLMs as synthetic survey respondents) by proposing the respondent coverage gap (RCG), a metric that compares whole answer profiles of synthetic respondents against real human respondents. The authors show generators can reproduce per-question answer distributions while producing respondent combinations never observed in humans. This exposes a blind spot in current synthetic-population evaluation.

entry.title: ChemBART: Pre-training a Reaction Language Model for Comprehensive Synthesis Planning

author.name: Kenan Li, Yijian Zhang, Jin Wang, Haipeng Gan, Zeying Sun, Xiaoguang Lei, Hao Dong

entry.summary: ChemBART is a BART-based language model pre-trained with a reaction-centric mask-filling objective on holistic reaction expressions (Reactant > Reagent > Product), enabling a single model to handle precursor and reagent prediction, temperature-yield regression, and molecular property classification. This moves beyond single-molecule LLM approaches in computer-aided synthesis planning.

entry.title: DeXplicit: Making Physical State Explicit in Dexterous Manipulation World Models

author.name: Adam Lee, Mutian Xu, Yukang Cao, Shulin Tian, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: DeXplicit is a dexterous manipulation world model that explicitly predicts how the world evolves in metric 3D before rendering visual consequences, rather than entangling dynamics, camera motion, and synthesis in a video generator. A lightweight 3D dynamics network predicts object-centric motion and deformation from an initial scene and a future hand trajectory, providing structured, geometrically grounded future states. This improves anticipation of how robot hand motion changes the physical world.

entry.title: Watch and Learn: Teaching Visual In-Context Learning by Removing Textual Shortcuts

author.name: Nimrod Shabtay, Asaf Yehudai, Avihu Dekel, Eli Schwartz, Raja Giryes

entry.summary: The paper shows that VLMs rely on textual shortcuts and underuse visual demonstrations for in-context learning, and constructs MIME, a task-agnostic vICL training set where the linking rule must be inferred from images alone. Fine-tuning on MIME improves vICL accuracy by 8-18 points across three VLMs while also helping multi-image and text-only ICL.

entry.title: MVLoMa: Multi-View Local Feature Matching with Any Geometry Foundation Model

author.name: Xinyang Lu, Shengzhe Wei, Sheng Tang, Weiqi Zhang, Juntong Fang, Zesong Li

entry.summary: Extends local feature matching from image pairs to a sparse star-graph multi-view formulation, jointly describing all images with a frozen geometry foundation model and injecting cross-view geometric context into local descriptors. This avoids duplicated reference-side computation and exploits complementary multi-view evidence for structure-from-motion and visual localization.

entry.title: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Chenxi Song, Yanming Yang, Tong Zhao, Ruibo Li, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces WorldForge V2, a method for achieving precise camera-trajectory control in video diffusion models while preserving their pretrained generative capabilities. It uses a training-free guidance framework that iteratively refines generation along a target camera path via warped references, addressing problems of entangled camera motion and scene dynamics, spatial-temporal inconsistencies, and the artifacts introduced by fine-tuning or post-hoc warping approaches.

entry.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds

author.name: Ava Pun, Kevin Dai, Sally Chen, Maxwell Jones, Ruixuan Liu, Kangle Deng, Changliu Liu, Maneesh Agrawala, Deva Ramanan, Jun-Yan Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a framework where pre-trained frontier coding agents, equipped with tools for assembling builds and verifying physical feasibility, generate physically valid LEGO brick builds from text or image prompts. The key claim is that tool support for assembly and feasibility checking is sufficient to eliminate floating, colliding, or disconnected parts.

entry.title: When One Step Is Enough: An Empirical Study of Euler Integration in Flow-Matching Policies

author.name: Shivakanth Sujit, Luca Nunziante, Rousslan Fernand Julien Dossa, Kai Arulkumaran

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that across six flow-matching VLA robot policies, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step ODE integration at scale, provided models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity. This questions the need for specialized single-shot action generation objectives and enables much higher control frequencies at deployment. Practically important for real-time robot control.

entry.title: UniFlowWAM: A Unified World-Action Model with Visual Semantics and 4D Geometry

author.name: Jialin Tian, Zhuofan Li, Xinkai Wang, Bokai Lin, Chenyi Wang, Xinyu Zhan, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang

entry.summary: UniFlowWAM makes 3D scene flow a first-class modality on par with vision and action inside a unified world-action model, rather than treating flow as an external module or auxiliary head. This gives robot policies an explicit 4D geometric world representation covering both appearance and dynamics. The architectural unification could improve generalization of robot manipulation policies.

entry.title: OlmoEarth v1.3: State-of-the-art embeddings for the whole planet

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 releases OlmoEarth v1.3, providing state-of-the-art satellite embeddings along with precomputed global embedding data and a browser-based Embeddings Explorer for planetary mapping and analysis. This lowers the barrier for geospatial AI applications in areas like agriculture, conservation, and land-use monitoring.

entry.title: From Prose to Properties: Testing Research Claims with ARATest for Agent-Native Science

author.name: Yifeng He, Jiachen Liu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: ARATest is a property-based testing library that makes empirical research claims machine-checkable by abstracting a claim's property skeleton (a parameterized recurring relation) and binding it to the claim via typed declarations fixing compared quantities, scope, and thresholds. This enables executable falsification tests for the growing volume of claims produced by AI agents running experiments.

entry.title: SetCommit: Coordinated Token Commitments for Few-Step Diffusion Language Model Decoding

author.name: Yuannuo Feng, Yubing Ye, Wenshuai Yao, Yizhe Chen, Ngai Wong, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang

entry.summary: Introduces SetCommit, a training-free method for few-step diffusion language model decoding that selects coordinated commitment sets balancing token reliability against local joint commitment risk, plus budget-neutral local exchanges that revise vulnerable earlier commitments. This tackles jointly inconsistent parallel commitments that plague confident independent token selection.

entry.title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Wen Ye, Ailin Deng, Zirui Wang, Shixing Yu, Han Zhang, Tian Yun, Nikhil Mehta, Tarun Kalluri, Xuefei Cao, Xuezhe Ma, Hengduo Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation for visual mathematical reasoning, where a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective and only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss. Reference figure descriptions and verified solutions are used as training-only signals, targeting the perceptual bottleneck where small VLMs misread diagrams and then reason from false premises.

entry.title: Short-to-Long: Detached Features for Long-Horizon Value Learning

author.name: Tong Che, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: The paper introduces Short-to-Long (S2L), which provides a long-horizon behavior learner with features trained by smaller-discount source networks, with detached connections preventing the behavior value loss from disturbing the source objectives. Across Atari and online/offline continuous control, this yields aggregate performance improvements while preserving the true control objective.

entry.title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models

author.name: Bo Liu, Lianyu Wang, Meng Wang, Ching-Yu Cheng, Huazhu Fu

entry.summary: RetiJev introduces a 78,158-question source-grounded ophthalmology corpus plus a 24,662-question benchmark, and a family of 0.8B-9B decision models that select among predefined clinical actions rather than generating text, reducing latency and computational overhead. The approach prioritizes fast, private, grounded clinical decision support for eye disease diagnosis and grading.

entry.title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models

author.name: Athira Gopal, Patil Prathamesh Pravin, Ankush Kadu, Arpit Jain, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: This study documents severe cross-script identity failures in multilingual LLMs: Qwen2.5-7B's same-person accuracy drops from 35.1% to 8.5% when names appear in Devanagari under Marathi prompts, with the effect replicated in Malayalam pairs. Different-person accuracy stays above 98%, indicating a script-dependent response bias rather than general confusion. The audited bilingual identity datasets and cross-model analysis provide a diagnostic resource for multilingual robustness.

entry.title: Bayesian Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with Abstention

author.name: Yuqi Huang, Yunlong Hou, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: Studies Bayesian fixed-confidence best-arm identification where the learner may abstain under an abstention budget, proposing the Screen-and-Confirm algorithm with matching upper and lower bounds on expected stopping time. The analysis shows the rate is governed by the prior density of the top-two gap at zero, highlighting that nearly tied instances dominate sample complexity.

entry.title: Ground-Truth-First Benchmarking of Reinforcement Learning via Converse Optimality: From Smooth, Fully Observed Systems to Non-Smooth or Partially Observed Tasks

author.name: Gr\'egoire Ouerdane, Sinan Ibrahim, Stefan Streif, Pavel Osinenko

entry.summary: The paper proposes a ground-truth-first RL benchmarking framework where tasks come with certified optimal value functions and policies withheld from learners, enabling measurement of true distance to optimality rather than relative rankings. It unifies sensitivity benchmarking over task variations and oracle-referenced policy comparison, covering smooth, non-smooth, and partially observed settings.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale

author.name: Arvid Frydenlund, FuTe Wong, Katherine Lambert, Frank Rudzicz

entry.summary: The authors identify supervision signal and tokenization as two orthogonal causes of language models' failure to learn shortest-path generation on unseen graphs at scale. They theoretically and empirically show multi-token prediction helps in a topology-agnostic way, and with alternative tokenizations break through prior scaling walls on latent multi-hop graph search.

entry.title: PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn

author.name: Zhongkai Shangguan, Yanbin Kang, Yihan Cao, Ruijie Jiang, Qiannan Yin, Chang Yue, Zijian Zhou, Girish Kathalagiri, Changshuai Wei, Zhengming Xing

entry.summary: Describes PAIR, LinkedIn's system for people recommendation that moves beyond profile-similarity embeddings to capture complementary, cross-role intent, such as job seekers engaging recruiters rather than similar peers. The system aligns retrieval with preference signals for premium-member recommendations at production scale. It demonstrates how asymmetric, goal-driven relevance differs from symmetric social-network matching.

entry.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of LLM Fact-Checkers

author.name: Ayana Niwa, Miyu Yamada, Kouta Nakayama, Masahiro Kaneko, Hisami Suzuki, Satoshi Sekine

entry.summary: Argues that fact-checking evaluations depend on underspecified design decisions—claim-question alignment, judging conditions, and evidence sources—and introduces JSFactCheckBench, a Japanese benchmark of 1,913 claims with time-referenced factuality and importance annotations. Across six LLMs it finds systematic weaknesses, notably that models only reliably verify claims directly answering the question.

entry.title: Padding to k: A Minimum Count in the Schema Makes Open-Weight Models Pad Their Extraction Lists

author.name: Abhishek Barali, Aayush Paudel

entry.summary: Under a preregistered plan, this paper shows that open-weight models treat minimum list counts in JSON schemas as targets: a soft minimum raises over-extraction from 34.5% to 55.4% across eight models on 558 real documents, and the fabricated entries are hard to catch because they reuse real document text. This documents a subtle schema-induced hallucination mode relevant to extraction pipelines. The preregistration and contamination-check design are notable.

entry.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports

author.name: Jiahao Meng, Qize Yang, Yuxuan Wang, Yunfei Chu, Wensi Dai, Jin Xu, Yunhai Tong

entry.summary: The paper defines video-centered deep research report generation, where an agent researches a video, retrieves external multimodal evidence, and produces an interactive report linked to relevant video moments. It introduces OmniDR-Bench and Omni Atomic Rubric Trees spanning 23 shared dimensions for evaluation, plus a skill-based workflow for the task.

entry.title: Where Did the Light Come From? Diagnosing Cast-Shadow Reasoning in VLMs and Borrowing the Missing Shadow Prior from Image Generation Models

author.name: Ryugo Morita, Shunsuke Kitada, Stanislav Frolov, Brian Bernhard Moser, Ko Watanabe, Riku Takahashi, Jinjia Zhou, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: The paper introduces ShadowBench, built from real photographs with correct-shadow, shadow-removed, and wrong-direction scene states, to test whether VLMs can read shadow direction, infer absent shadows, and judge physical consistency. Evaluating 19 open VLMs (2B to 78B) and frontier proprietary models, it finds models read visible shadow direction above chance but fail at inference and consistency judgment, and it borrows a shadow prior from image generation models to compensate. This reveals a systematic physical-reasoning gap in modern VLMs.

entry.title: WildFakeToolBench: Benchmarking AI-Generated Image Detectors with Web-Sourced Image Processing

author.name: Mingjie Li, Yukun Jiang, Yicong Tan, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: WildFakeToolBench benchmarks AI-generated image detectors against 156 executable image-processing tools mined from 220 public web sources, simulating how adversaries can trivially evade detection using LLM-assisted code translation. The suite retains source evidence and applies syntax, execution, and distortion checks without detector feedback.

entry.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Zunnan Xu, Shangchen Zhou, Yihang Luo, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: Proposes hierarchical pose graph optimization to achieve globally consistent 3D reconstruction over videos of thousands of frames, reconciling chunk-level graphs (efficient for scale drift and loop closure) with finer-grained graphs for rigid sub-chunk consistency. It addresses inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicated camera estimates from chunked feed-forward reconstruction.

entry.title: GelSlim 5.0: Unifying Vision and Touch with a Single Fingertip Camera

author.name: Xiangdong Wang, I-Hsuan Huang, Xiaohao Xu, Xili Yi, Nima Fazeli, Xiaonan Huang

entry.summary: GelSlim 5.0 is a fingertip sensor that captures both visual and tactile observations from a single fixed camera using a UV-responsive contact layer and switched illumination, eliminating inter-camera calibration. A multimodal transformer, VisTacFusion, fuses both modalities for planar object pose and contact geometry estimation. Unifying vision and touch in one sensor is a meaningful hardware contribution for dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation

author.name: Yi Ge, Pan Wang, Xuehao Cui, Zian Zeng, Xu Hu, Heng Huang, Furong Huang

entry.summary: RoleFlow is a self-evolving multi-agent LLM system that dynamically refines its collaboration structure through feedback-driven atomic edits and on-demand role synthesis, avoiding brittle predefined structures. Its Single-Edit Counterfactual Policy Optimization (SECPO) evaluates each structural edit against its no-edit counterpart to assign credit, solving the credit-assignment problem of trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: Disentangling Robustness and Sycophancy in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Rhitabrat Pokharel, Ameeta Agrawal

entry.summary: The paper introduces the SC-matrix, a framework crossing a multilingual model's competence with its sycophancy to distinguish agreement-under-pressure caused by sycophancy from lack of knowledge in that language. Experiments show identical aggregate sycophancy rates can hide different failure compositions, competence does not guarantee resistance, and reasoning-based mitigations beat directive ones. Multilingual sycophancy is shown to be heterogeneous rather than a single phenomenon.

entry.title: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding

author.name: Valentino Sacco, Saurabh Pandey, Alexander Florian Jercher, Maximilian Schilling

entry.summary: PointerBench is a diagnostic suite of 1,500 screenshot-instruction pairs probing fine-grained GUI grounding: sub-element identification in spreadsheets, character-level grounding in long documents, and mixed grounding across 100 professional applications. It complements end-to-end computer-use benchmarks by isolating a specific capability of multimodal LLMs. It matters as agents are increasingly deployed to operate software UIs.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Static Analysis via LLM Pseudo-Labeling

author.name: Rui Melo, Andre Duarte, Aditya Oke, Shubham Gandhi, Nachiket Kotalwar, Rui Abreu, Lei Li, Carolyn Rose

entry.summary: SESAA is a framework in which an LLM agent starts with no rules and iteratively evolves auditable Joern queries for security bug detection, receiving feedback only from a second LLM critic that flags likely false alarms and suspected misses without ground-truth labels. Evaluated on OWASP benchmark-style code, it addresses the gap where static analysis rules lag new frameworks and APIs.

entry.title: Gender, Sexual Orientation, and the One-Year Refugee Bar: A Computational Study of Bill C-12 and Canadian Refugee Adjudication

author.name: Sean Rehaag

entry.summary: This computational study analyzes Canadian Bill C-12 (March 2026), which bars refugee claims made more than one year after first entry, testing the government premise that genuine refugees claim promptly against data on late claims. It finds late claims concentrated among vulnerable groups, including those fleeing gender- and sexual-orientation-based persecution, who are diverted to a weaker PRRA process without oral hearings or merits appeals.

entry.title: Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models

author.name: Nimun Bajwa, Massimo Poesio

entry.summary: This work systematically ablates design choices for activation probes that detect and steer safety-relevant behaviors (deception, high-stakes awareness, sycophancy) in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It crosses two estimators and three token-pooling schemes within a single pipeline, evaluating each direction both as a detector and as a steering vector, providing practical guidance for interpretability practitioners.

entry.title: Direct Forcing: A Single-Stage Training Recipe for Few-Step Autoregressive Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Haojun Xu, Jie Huang, Xin Lu, Mingchen Zhong, Zihao Fan, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu

entry.summary: Direct Forcing unifies causal adaptation and distribution matching for few-step autoregressive text-to-video generation in a single training stage, using reference videos both as paired continuation examples and as a target distribution. It combines causal continuation alignment with MMD-based rollout distribution matching, enabling low-latency streaming video generation.

entry.title: Mostly Reading: What Open-Book Scores Measure in Document-Level LoRA Adapters

author.name: Martino M. L. Pulici, Cuong Xuan Chu, Evgeny Kharlamov, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: Training 150 single-document LoRA adapters on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the authors show that open-book evaluation scores mostly measure a shared reading behavior rather than stored knowledge: a random adapter recovers 82% of a specialist's open-book advantage but essentially none of its advantage on cloze probes without the source text. Content does reach the weights, but open-book scoring cannot detect it. This is a caution about how adapter-as-knowledge-unit proposals are evaluated.

entry.title: AI Risk Ontologies for the EU AI Act Compliance: AIRO, VAIR, and their Integration with DPV

author.name: Delaram Golpayegani, Harshvardhan J. Pandit, Declan O'Sullivan, Dave Lewis

entry.summary: The authors develop ontologies and taxonomies (AIRO, VAIR) for representing, cataloguing, and querying AI risks in an interoperable manner, aligned with EU AI Act requirements for high-risk systems and integrated with the Data Privacy Vocabulary. The work addresses the need for open, machine-readable risk documentation tools as AI harms proliferate. It matters for building standardised compliance infrastructure for AI governance.

entry.title: DiffLTM: Continuous Diffusions Large Tabular Models for Conditional Generation

author.name: Alankrita Bhatt, Mukur Gupta, Andrea Montanari, Pulkit Tandon

entry.summary: Presents DiffLTM, a continuous diffusion model for conditional generation over mixed numerical and high-cardinality categorical tabular data, using cross-entropy loss for categoricals with a first theoretical justification. It introduces metrics targeting rare sub-populations, a known weakness of tabular generative models.

entry.title: Training Mixed-Monotone Neural Networks for Verification Without Set Propagation

author.name: Jonas Fingerhut, Lukas Koller, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: The authors introduce an architecture realizing mixed-monotone functions as the difference of two monotone subnetworks, reducing tight neural network output enclosure computation to two forward passes rather than costly set propagation. Since enclosure size is a closed-form function of weights, it can be minimized directly during training, with a proven lower bound on attainable tightness.

entry.title: Federated Differentially Private Optimization via Low-Rank Preconditioning

author.name: Antti Koskela, Tejas Kulkarni, Elias Raninen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a federated DP-PCA framework achieving linear communication cost while providing central differential privacy guarantees under secure aggregation, combining DP rank selection, a DP power method, and a noisy low-dimensional covariance release. This improves over quadratic-communication central DP methods and locally private baselines.

entry.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations

author.name: Sarah Liaw, Yuanqi Du, Yilun Du

entry.summary: The paper introduces action learning, recovering latent stochastic actions from trajectory observations to provide a common objective for reasoning about dynamical systems, with LEAP anchoring unknown actions to energy on action paths. This bridges trajectory-level reasoning that transition-local or purely generative approaches miss, targeting scientific simulation control.

entry.title: Fast Iterative Combinatorial Auctions via Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Luis F. Paul Tosta, Quinn Arnold, Gianluca Brero

entry.summary: Introduces FastCombo, a deep RL approach to sequential price discovery in iterative combinatorial auctions used in spectrum allocation and procurement. The authors prove that greedily maximizing immediate clearing probability can require arbitrarily more rounds than an informative policy, and they learn price policies offline that assign credit to queries for the future decisions they enable. This can sharply reduce costly auction rounds versus Bayesian pricing baselines.

entry.title: Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory

author.name: Hao Wu

entry.summary: Presents Delta N-gram, a forward-only write path into a language model's native hashed N-gram table for continual learning: a small 4.1M-parameter writer emits gated targets written into a sparse patch, keeping each row a convex combination of old and new values while never modifying the pretrained table. Writing requires only forward passes, and clearing the patch restores the original model. Experiments on a 0.6B pretrained model demonstrate disturbance-free continual knowledge updating.

entry.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis

author.name: Yuansi Chen, Francesco Pedrotti, Peter A. Whalley

entry.summary: Analyzes the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls means and low-dimensional marginals relevant to statistical practice, showing dimension-free bias and mixing regimes for ridge-separable potentials. In the overparameterized regime the effective dimension reduces, yielding a bell-shaped mixing profile as sample size varies relative to dimension.

entry.title: CiteAnchor: Source-Aware Grounding for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Resolution

author.name: Chenyi Tong, Ping Nie, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CiteResolve, a benchmark of 423 real-world hallucinated citations annotated for source recoverability, and CiteAnchor, a framework that adapts retrieval and field-level verification to source type, separately judging citation validity and source recoverability. It achieves 0.841 F1 on an existing detection benchmark using GPT-5.6, an established model.

entry.title: Once a Tree, Always a Tree? Cross-lingual Transfer of Hierarchical Generalization in Language Models

author.name: Shin Yamaguchi, Masaya Taniguchi, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Taro Watanabe, Yoshinobu Kano

entry.summary: This study introduces a cross-lingual poverty-of-stimulus (CPOS) experimental design to test whether language models transfer hierarchical structural generalization from one language to another during continued training, as opposed to non-linguistic explanations like better positional initialization. The design carefully ablates what drives hierarchical generalization in a second language. It offers a cleaner causal picture of cross-lingual transfer.

entry.title: Investigating Multi-Cultural Value Selection Biases in LLMs

author.name: Siddhesh Pawar, Arnav Arora, Dustin Wright, Dirk Hovy, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: This study probes LLM cultural bias under simultaneous identity cues, combining a country persona in the system prompt with a second identity signaled explicitly (named country) or implicitly (query language), using World Values Survey probing and 1.6 million open-ended generations. It finds language cues shift answers far more than explicit cues, and often away from the associated country's distribution. The results complicate single-label cultural evaluation practice.

entry.title: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition

author.name: Om Tailor, Yucheng Pan, Solaleh Mohammadi, Xinyan Liu, Kaiqing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper argues that end-to-end recovery metrics for LLM steganography cannot distinguish encoder from decoder failures, and introduces a rolewise decomposition framework separately analyzing how messages are represented in transmitted text, what decoders recover, and what deterministic verifiers can check. This enables finer-grained understanding of where steganographic communication succeeds or fails.

entry.title: AgentDreamer: Agentic 3D Motion Reasoning for Text-Controllable Physics Simulation

author.name: Mijeong Kim, Suho Park, Junha Park, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: AgentDreamer is an agent-guided optimization framework that translates text instructions into structured semantic motion priors specified as parametric functions over temporal chunks, producing dense 3D trajectories. These priors are used to optimize a differentiable MPM simulator so its rollout matches the intended motion while respecting scene dynamics. The design cleanly separates language-based semantic guidance from physics-based grounding for text-controllable simulation.

entry.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation

author.name: Wenhao Zheng, Xianggen Liu, Li Yue, Jiancheng Shi, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: GraphCAD introduces an Edge-Adjacency Graph representation for CAD and a hybrid graph diffusion formulation that jointly models discrete topology and continuous geometry in B-rep generation. This adds an explicit topological inductive bias missing from sequence-modeling approaches to CAD generation.

entry.title: PiHand: Latent Hand-Object Interaction Priors for Physics-Based Policy Learning

author.name: Niklas Berndt, Xianghui Xie, Enes Duran, Yixiao Wang, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: Presents a framework for physically grounded dexterous hand-object interaction synthesis that trains expert mocap-tracking policies in simulation and distills them into a unified hand-object latent prior. This captures coupled hand-object motion, improving contact fidelity and sample efficiency over hand-only priors or trajectory tracking.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Motion Planning and Steering with Global Convergence

author.name: Mohsen Amiri, Sima Didari, Davoud Ataee Tarzanagh, Hankyu Moon, Yeongdae Kwon

entry.summary: GlobMP casts motion planning and steering as a single continuous-time nonconvex program and proposes a gradient projection method over piecewise-polynomial curves with provable global convergence even when smoothness costs are combined with constraints. It can steer learned planner proposals while guaranteeing constraints at every instant. A theoretical advance over sampled-time planners.

entry.title: AstroBench: Benchmarking Free-Floating Capture and Space Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zizhe Wang (Astroup Lab, Beijing, China), Jia Deng (Astroup Lab, Beijing, China), Xin Lu (Astroup Lab, Beijing, China), Zehao Jia (Astroup Lab, Beijing, China), Yi Huang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Beijing Research Institute), Yao Zhu (Harbin Institute of Technology, Beijing Research Institute)

entry.summary: AstroBench is an open benchmark for free-floating object capture and space manipulation with a fixed-base arm, featuring nine task definitions and 29 task-target combinations across capture, sample-storage, and servicing tasks. It draws on MELFI hardware and the Robotic Refueling Mission, with 8,414 Objaverse-derived assets for expansion. Space robotics lacks standardized evaluation, so this fills a real gap.

entry.title: Skeleton-Grounded Latent Action Model for Robot World Models

author.name: Qi Lv, Jiayi Lin, Yuxin Jiang, Jianzong Wang, Xiang Deng, Mike Shou Zheng

entry.summary: SkeLAM is a skeleton-guided latent action model for robot world modeling that decomposes latent actions into a kinematic component grounded by robot skeleton supervision and a residual capturing other visual dynamics. Cross-modal swap reconstruction enforces interchangeability between RGB-derived and skeleton-derived kinematic representations. This disentanglement addresses a key weakness of reconstruction-driven latent action models learned from videos.

entry.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models

author.name: Yufeng Liu, Bohao Fan, Juntu Zhao, Xinyi Wang, Hang Yu, Wenzhuan Luo, Yingzhi Wang, Qinghai Li, Yingdong Hu, Junliang Guo, Richard Wang, Dequan Wang, Yang Gao, Cheng Ma

entry.summary: Echo is a VLA framework that learns task status signals (success/failure) without frame-level progress annotations and couples status prediction with action generation inside a single model. This enables robots to stop on success and replan on failure without external monitors or fine-grained supervision.

entry.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3

author.name: Jens Lehmann, Sahar Vahdati

entry.summary: This controlled study asks whether frontier LLMs can autonomously build and improve the harness (the symbolic scaffold orchestrating perception, memory, tools, and inference allocation) on ARC-AGI-3, an interactive exploration benchmark where human-steered systems already reach ceiling scores. Through a fixed coding bootstrap, each model attempts to improve its own scaffold across games.

entry.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes

author.name: Jie Ying, Xutao Zhang, Ningyuan Chen, Mengce Zheng, Jun Li, Zhongjie Zhu, Tiantian Zhu

entry.summary: AgentTriage is an executable contract enabling replayable security diagnosis of tool-use agents across heterogeneous runtimes. It requires conclusions to cite canonical runtime events and mandates abstention when evidence is missing, with runtime overlays normalizing native observations into a typed provenance graph from which a policy-decisive evidence slice is selected. Given the same normalized trace, overlay version, and configuration, diagnoses are reproducible.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jinya Sakurai, Xun Xu, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: This controlled study examines learned unmasking policies in masked diffusion LMs, analyzing what teachers label as committable, which states policies imitate, what the policy observes, and how much NFE reduction is needed to offset policy overhead. Findings include that matching-final-output labels are overly permissive at low NFE, hidden states are weak alone but complement confidence, and roughly 10% NFE reduction is needed to offset overhead. It clarifies design choices for efficient dLLM decoding.

entry.title: VLTest: Finding Joint Image-Text Failures in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bin Duan, Jintao Lin, Guowei Yang

entry.summary: VLTest is a black-box testing approach for vision-language models that generates image variants via VQGAN latent edits and text variants via a rewrite-expand-prune pipeline, testing each mutation alone before combinations. This four-cell design isolates joint image-text failures that only appear when both inputs are mutated, with a VLM judge confirming failures against expected behavior.

entry.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration

author.name: Erik Bodin, Lisa Maria Kreusser, Donney Fan, Henry Moss, Geoff Pleiss, Nicolas Durrande

entry.summary: SABLE is a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces where latent dimension far exceeds the evaluation budget, using a Bayesian affine surrogate whose slope update has bounded dimension after N observations. Higher-order structure is treated as surrogate discrepancy under an isotropic distributional assumption. It targets expensive black-box optimisation over generative latent spaces such as engineering designs and proteins.

entry.title: CTRL-FM: Inference-Time Structural Control for Flow-Based Virtual Sensing under Long-Horizon Node Outages

author.name: Boshra Khalili, Andrew Smyth

entry.summary: Introduces CTRL-FM, an observation-preserving flow-matching framework for virtual sensing during long-horizon sensor outages that treats structural guidance as an outage-conditioned inference-time decision rather than a fixed inductive bias. A missing-only flow-matching backbone learns a conditional velocity field while keeping observed measurements exactly fixed, adapting guidance per outage scenario.

entry.title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving

author.name: Maharani A. P. Irawan, Kuntai Du, Jiayi Yao, Dongjoo Seo, Yuyang Huang, Haryadi S. Gunawi, Junchen Jiang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that KV cache offloading to SSDs in production LLM serving can wear out flash storage in months rather than years, and proposes write-gating based on access patterns that preserves hit rates despite identical access statistics across attention types. Gandalf extends SSD lifetime while maintaining serving cost benefits.

entry.title: The Bayesian Learning Rule Beyond KL Geometry

author.name: Sophia Sklaviadis, Wu Lin, Andre Martins, Mario Figueiredo, Thomas Moellenhoff, Emtiyaz Khan

entry.summary: The authors show that additive Bayesian learning rule updates are not restricted to KL divergence geometry: they derive additive information-geometric optimization algorithms for mixed-space Brefrom Bregman or Fenchel-Young discrepancies, contradicting prior claims that only KLD works. This extends the space of geometries usable for exponential-family variational posteriors.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability

author.name: Guodong Zheng, Yan Sun, Peng Wang, Enneng Yang, Jiafei Lyu, Xiaochun Cao, Dacheng Tao, Li Shen

entry.summary: This work develops an algorithmic-stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD, without assuming specific architectures. It decomposes forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps plus empirical forgetting and tracks how sample perturbations propagate through successive tasks to obtain bounds.

entry.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Chenyuan Chen, Ran Ding, Lechen Zhang, Zewen He, Yoshihiko Nakamura

entry.summary: Presents WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory for humanoid loco-manipulation in non-Markovian dynamic scenes, using SAM3 to track task objects and causally select key frames within an adaptive budget that a VLA action expert reads via cross-attention. The paper also contributes HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Results indicate keeping the right frames, not more frames, drives performance.

entry.title: TRIAD: Benchmarking Omni-Modal Ambiguity in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zhaolu Kang, Yidi Wang, Yile Li, Siqi Zeng, Yingjie He, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao hu

entry.summary: TRIAD is a benchmark of 327 hand-written text-image-audio triplets where all three modalities jointly determine a unique answer but any single modality leaves the answer ambiguous. This design tests whether omni-modal LLMs can perform cross-modal disambiguation rather than simple perception. It fills a gap left by benchmarks focused on determinate inputs.

entry.title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Zizhi Zeng, Jiaqi Zhang, Yiqun Duan, Mingkai Zheng, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Active Preference Acquisition (APA) for web agents that serve the same user across repeated tasks, defining Prospective Personalization Value (PPV) as the expected cumulative utility of learning a preference over future tasks minus asking and disclosure costs. The framework decides which clarification questions are worth asking, unlike myopic current-task clarification methods. It connects personalization, learning, and privacy tradeoffs.

entry.title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning

author.name: Yuanze Hu, Zhichao Yang, Junwei Jing, Xin Yang, Wenxuan Liu, Tinghai Zhang, Jia Fu, Hongzhi Zhang, Xiangyu Wu, Ruiming Tang, Tingting Gao, Han Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a position-aware rubric that decomposes dense captions into atomic visual claims and analyzes supported, hallucinated, and generic content by quartile position, revealing that later generations suffer weaker visual grounding. It then uses this diagnosis to drive reinforcement learning improvements for detailed image captioning.

entry.title: ReCoG: Relational Concept Graph for Training-Free Personalization

author.name: Changseon Yu, Hyeokjun Kweon

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free method for personalizing frozen vision-language models to recognize user-defined concepts from few exemplars using a relational concept graph. By encoding distinctions between a concept and its nearest confusable alternatives, it improves discrimination on fine-grained personalized concept sets where retriever-based baselines retrieve plausible but non-discriminative evidence.

entry.title: Squaring-the-Sphere: Distortion-Free and Seamless Panorama Generation via CubeAtlas

author.name: Xuhui Zuo, Chenjie Cao, Tengfei Wang, Junta Wu, Yisu Zhang, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Proposes CubeAtlas, a new panorama representation that unfolds cubemap faces plus rotated polar regions into a single compact canvas, preserving perspective geometry while enabling seamless spherical continuity. This resolves the classic tradeoff between equirectangular distortion and cubemap seams for 360-degree image generation.

entry.title: RGraph-Eval: Task-Grounded Scene Graphs for Evaluating Robot Video Generation

author.name: Aleksandr Lazarev, Sofia Zimina, Roman Kuznetsov, Tatiana Zemskova, Iaroslav Koshelev, Dmitry Yudin

entry.summary: RGraph-Eval is a reference-based framework for evaluating generated robot videos using task-grounded temporal scene graphs that expose wrong-object or wrong-outcome interactions invisible to visual similarity metrics. A foundation-model pipeline grounds object masks, verifies state transitions, and reconstructs 3D manipulated-object motion within a unified interpretable representation. As robot video generation grows, principled evaluation becomes critical.

entry.title: Monitorability evaluations and policy proposals

author.name: evhub

entry.summary: evhub (Anthropic, writing personally) proposes a four-part taxonomy of AI monitorability — control, training, auditing, and a fourth type — mapping each to concrete evaluations such as sabotage benchmarks, and connects this framework to ongoing policy debates including Redwood's monitorability proposal. The post aims to ground policy proposals in measurable properties.

entry.title: Route-and-Generate: KL-Regularized Router Improvement for Reasoning Routing in LLMs

author.name: Tien-Phat Nguyen, Truong Nguyen, Thanh-Thien Le, Hoang Phan, Thien Huu Nguyen, Linh Ngo Van, Trung Le

entry.summary: Rouge is a hierarchical training framework letting LLMs adaptively decide when and how much to reason, addressing overthinking on easy tasks and underthinking on hard ones. It decouples reasoning-effort allocation from generation via a routing policy with a fixed sampling budget, uses GRPO with rank-based rewards favoring shorter correct solutions, and updates the router via closed-form KL-regularized policy improvement.

entry.title: Agentic Knowledge-Model Co-Evolution via Consistency Regularization

author.name: Sirui Chen, Zhining Liu, Chao Zhang, Jingrui He, Zheng Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPLICE, a framework for consistency-regularized co-evolution of an LLM agent's external knowledge and internal model weights. Rather than trusting a single analysis of accumulated experience, SPLICE selects knowledge whose utility gains are consistent across multiple ways of analyzing the same experience. This addresses the problem that different experience analyses yield guidance of wildly varying utility.

entry.title: PhysTrace: Interpretable Temporal Evaluation of Physical Consistency in Video Generative Models

author.name: Taekoan Yoo, Wonkyung Jung, Kyunghun Kim, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: PhysTrace is a training-free framework that aligns MLLM-generated, history-conditioned physical expectations with observed video windows to temporally localize physical violations in video generation, producing interpretable descriptions. It also contributes IntPhys2-Timing with annotated violation intervals, reaching up to 70.7% hit rate. This improves evaluation of physical realism in video models underpinning world models.

entry.title: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents

author.name: Muheng Li, Wenlong Mou

entry.summary: GAV is a Generator-Agent-Verifier environment that makes new PDE problems verifiable by construction: a generator learns a distribution of continuous reference solutions from simulations or measurements, then uses the method of manufactured solutions to construct matching PDE problems without separate reference computations. This provides reliable feedback for coding agents developing PDE solvers.

entry.title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments

author.name: Tengwei Song, Robert Hoehndorf

entry.summary: MemPlan repositions LLMs as constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning, keeping the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructing the problem each step from parsed observations, hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive and negative graph memories assign action costs to candidate hypotheses and record refuted ones, guiding planners in partially observable text environments while reducing hallucinated actions.

entry.title: One Evaluation Is Enough: Inversion-Free Image Editing with Trajectory Correction
