author.name: Lifan Jiang, Taiyang Chen, Senlin cheng, Bolei Xu, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Dehai Zhao, Deng Cai, Boxi Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that a single source-target evaluation at a shared noisy state in a variance-preserving one-step model yields both a local angular semantic tangent and a clean endpoint displacement, enabling inversion-free image editing with one field evaluation. The endpoint displacement analytically corrects long-horizon extrapolation of the tangent integration.

entry.title: ProductWebBench: Evaluating Website Continuity Beyond Task Completion

author.name: Jiajun Wu, Jian Yang, Yaxin Du, Shukai Liu, Linzheng Chai, Tuney Zheng, Wei Zhang, Haitao Yang, Yan Bai, Yihang Lou, Xianglong Liu, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: ProductWebBench evaluates frontend coding agents on website continuity: whether the rest of a site keeps working after a requested change, not just whether the target feature was built. It includes 320 Change tasks and 80 long-horizon Build tasks on living repositories, with frozen snapshots, staged requirements revealed by a simulated user, browser evidence, and deterministic checks that stay armed throughout a run. This targets a realistic failure mode invisible to build-only benchmarks.

entry.title: Bridging the Data Gap: Source-Informed Task-Space Transport for Few-Shot Diffusion

author.name: Jinjian Jiang, Jing Peng, Rehan Deen, Yu Cao, Ziquan Liu, Muhammad Salman Haleem, David Mguni

entry.summary: Meta-Diff learns a reusable source-to-target relation in a compact task space: a shared encoder maps distributions to low-dimensional coordinates, a learned transport predicts the target coordinate, and a shared diffusion backbone generates from it. This avoids costly per-target retraining of large generators, which is especially valuable in healthcare settings with sparse target data. The approach promises efficient few-shot domain adaptation for generative models.

entry.title: Identifiability from Stationary Covariance in Linear SDEs with Reciprocal Interactions and Latent Variables

author.name: Ana Leticia Garcez Vicente, Saber Salehkaleybar

entry.summary: This paper establishes new graphical conditions for generic identifiability of causal effects in linear stochastic differential equations that permit directed 2-cycles (reciprocal interactions) and latent variables, extending prior results restricted to fully observed acyclic systems. It develops instantaneous conditioning-based methods for the latent-variable setting.

entry.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing

author.name: Hayden Prairie, Jacob M. Ryan, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Daniel Y. Fu

entry.summary: The paper studies KV-shareability in looped architectures, where the final recurrence's KV-cache can be shared with earlier recurrences without quality loss, closing the linear memory-growth problem of looped inference. It investigates training conditions that enable KV-sharing in identically trained looped models that do not consistently exhibit it.

entry.title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization

author.name: Rodion Novkin, Hussam Amrouch

entry.summary: Develops neural network-based transistor models predicting drain current and charges for a 3nm nanosheet device, then deploys them in full standard cell library characterization within EDA tool flows. The work evaluates accuracy and speedup across a wide range of SPICE simulations, addressing whether NN device models can meet the precision and convergence demands of real chip design flows. This enables ultra-fast circuit simulation for advanced nodes.

entry.title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow

author.name: Miguel A. Aguilo

entry.summary: Builds structure-preserving reduced-order models for two aeroelasticity challenge problems (thin panel at Mach 1.92 and cantilever plate at Mach 5.85) where only sparse, non-time-resolved data exist. A learned model retains an exact potential from a Ritz-Galerkin reference and trains only a provably dissipative correction, achieving machine-precision energy balance by construction.

entry.title: A Reality Check of Inference-Time Context Augmentation Methods

author.name: Haeun Yu, Geert Heyman, Pepa Atanasova, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified evaluation framework comparing five inference-time context augmentation methods, ranging from uninformative filler tokens to informative elaborations, at the sentence level across seven models of multiple sizes. It assesses whether these methods reliably improve performance or merely reflect placeholder effects. The systematic comparison addresses a gap left by isolated evaluations.

entry.title: Measuring the Verifier's Floor: How Much Apparent Rare-Word Text-to-Speech Error Is ASR Error?

author.name: Kirill Borodin, Vasilii Kudryavtsev, Nikita Vasiliev, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: This paper measures how much apparent TTS error on rare words is actually recognizer error by transcribing human recordings with the evaluation ASR systems: on LibriSpeech and FLEURS, recognizers miss 33-67% of very rare words even in human speech. Cross-checking with additional recognizer families lowers apparent TTS error on such words two- to three-fold, revealing substantial bias in standard TTS evaluation.

entry.title: ParaLin++: Accelerating Parallel Diffusion Integrator via Intrinsic Partially Linear Structure

author.name: Jianrong Lu, Zhiyu Zhu, Hui Liu, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: ParaLin++ accelerates parallel diffusion sampling by exploiting an intrinsic partially linear structure in the integration process. Importantly, the paper first systematizes evaluation of training-free step-shortening methods, showing that methods that appear near-lossless under FID/CLIP metrics can suffer substantial degradation on semantic-composition, dense-instruction, and long-text-rendering benchmarks like GenEval, DPG-Bench, and LongTextBench, while parallel sampling retains full quality. This is both an evaluation contribution and a faster parallel sampler.

entry.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games

author.name: Zecong Tang, Zian Guan, Yuncheng Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Bo Dai

entry.summary: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical VLA agent for open-world games like Minecraft that combines native visuomotor control with long-horizon autonomy via a capability-aware harness: structured memory tracks progress and a VLM planner selects subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. It bridges the gap between API-driven planners and native-control agents.

entry.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark

author.name: Ruicong Liu, Liangyang Ouyang, Fengbo Lan, Zhixiang Wang, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a video-to-video generative renderer that transforms programmatically generated but visually plain game footage into high-quality visuals while preserving layout, camera, and per-entity position and timing. It generalizes across many game genres using plain video input without engine-level representations, and contributes an entity-level benchmark for consistency.

entry.title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields

author.name: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad

entry.summary: Proposes a feed-forward monocular reconstruction model whose ray module composes a monotone radial base, spherical-harmonic residuals, and finer components to represent per-pixel ray fields across camera geometries. This hierarchy handles fisheye and panoramic lenses without the distorted geometry of pinhole-assumed models.

entry.title: Probabilistic Energy Modeling Unifies Versatile Swarm Control

author.name: Xiang Zhou, Xiangyu Zhu, Xintong Wang, Qingyuan Yang, Rui Huang, Feng Xue, Lin Li, Qingrui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that probabilistic energy modeling over Gibbs random fields provides a unifying representation for robotic swarm control, encoding fundamental behaviors as reusable energy terms composed into a single controller via policy gating. Diverse missions emerge from shared interaction principles rather than task-specific redesign. This compositional framing could reduce the cost of deploying swarms across changing objectives.

entry.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing

author.name: Ariel Slepyan, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Jiafeng Gu, Anagha Rajendra Dangle, Yinzhe Zhou, Hongyuan Fu, Jade Sim, Tuhin Basu, Xinyi Yin, Md Faizal Karim, Gregory Hager, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Anand Bhattad, Krishna Murthy Jatavallabhula, Nitish V. Thakor

entry.summary: OpenTac presents an open, resistive tactile skin sensor with shear-decoding taxel structure plus a design tool that auto-generates fabrication files from 2D outlines or 3D surfaces. The full-stack ecosystem is intended for customization, scaling, and direct use in robot learning applications.

entry.title: Feedback That Backfires in Games: Do LLM Players Repeat the Move They Just Watched Fail?

author.name: Esmail Gumaan

entry.summary: This study shows that when an LLM agent's failed move is recorded in the transcript, small instruction-tuned models become more likely to repeat that same failed move in games like Sokoban, Connect Four, and Othello. Across 8 models (135M-1.7B), the failure record backfires (corrective gain of -1.38 nats per token) through surface-form attraction, for illegal moves but not losing ones.

entry.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core

author.name: Yebo Feng, Jingyang Dai, Liangrui Pan, Nelson Lau, Jiahua Xu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Steward is a multi-agent LLM system for autonomous investing that enforces governance through a type-system boundary on self-evolution: nine role-specialized agents (analysts, portfolio manager, protected risk manager) make joint decisions while a seven-layer shared memory tracks the system's own record. It targets the hard setting of irreversible actions on untrusted web content while improving from outcomes without weakening safeguards.

entry.title: Mitigating Saliency Collapse: Robust Saliency-Aware Long-Text Image-Text Alignment

author.name: Qiuyu Kong, Zanxi Ruan, Marco Cristani, Yiming Wang

entry.summary: Identifies saliency collapse, a failure mode in long-text image-text alignment where models over-rely on visually salient text and underutilize informative non-salient context, causing sharp retrieval degradation. Proposes RoSA, a saliency-aware finetuning framework that decomposes pairs into complementary salient and contextual views for joint learning.

entry.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Liang He, SiYuan Ma, Qishi Zhan, Yongqi Fan, Mingyu Cao, Qizhen Lan, Zhaolu Kang, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: ValuSpec is a plug-and-play mechanism that filters low-quality branches from candidate trees in tree-based speculative decoding before expensive target-model verification, using transfer-based supervision to align filtering with verification outcomes. It targets the waste caused by overlapping candidate branches in production serving. It matters for LLM inference efficiency, a high-leverage deployment concern.

entry.title: SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents

author.name: Kaijian Zou, Vaibhav Chennareddy, Yunxiang Zhang, Naihao Deng, Longju Bai, Jiaxin Pei, Rada Mihalcea, Lu Wang

entry.summary: SWE-Verifier is a lightweight generative model, trained from Qwen3.5-4B on preference data grouping contrasting actions with their outcomes, that selectively triggers candidate sampling and verification in coding agents. It scores proposed actions to decide when extra verification is worthwhile, then ranks candidates before execution, reducing wasted computation on low-value states.

entry.title: PhysibleMDM: Enforcing Inference-Time Physical Feasibility Constraints on Motion Diffusion Models via Noise Optimization

author.name: Maximilian St\"olzle, David M\"uller, Agon Serifi, Ruben Grandia, Espen Knoop, Moritz B\"acher

entry.summary: PhysibleMDM promotes physical feasibility of motion diffusion model outputs by optimizing the diffusion noise at inference time, without retraining the model. It introduces surrogate feasibility constraints combining kinematic checks with dynamic feasibility tests via an inverse-dynamics cone program, solved as a black-box noise optimization problem.

entry.title: MIG-COW: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Deepfake Detectors via Gradient Decomposition

author.name: Wonjune Seo, Joonhyuk Baek, Yeseong Jung, Saerom Park

entry.summary: MIG-COW combines momentum-integrated gradients with consensus-orthogonal decomposition to craft transferable adversarial examples against deepfake detectors, capturing shared and model-specific vulnerabilities across CNN and ViT architectures. It achieves 99.96% white-box attack success on AADD-2025 benchmarks but only 7.16% against official black-box targets, honestly revealing the transferability gap.

entry.title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals

author.name: Bastien Le Guellec, Su Hwan Kim, Raphael Bentegeac, Aghiles Hamroun

entry.summary: The authors gave four current LLMs a corpus of 200 CC BY-licensed 2026 articles from journals including Nature, Science, and Cell and asked them to produce independent peer-review reports on already-published work. The study probes how LLMs would treat the closest thing to gold-standard valid science, with implications for using LLMs to ease the peer-review crisis. The results inform debates about accountability and reliability of LLM-assisted reviewing.

entry.title: Learning Domain Trajectories with Flow Matching for Gradual Domain Adaptation

author.name: Yubo Huang, Yushe Cao, Zixi Wang, Jingzehua Xu, Xin Lai, Xiongyu Hu, Shuai Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FlowGDA, a flow-matching framework modeling gradual domain adaptation as continuous transport on a statistical manifold, learning time-dependent velocity fields that induce smooth domain trajectories via a simulation-free regression objective. It avoids error accumulation and unstable Min-Max optimization of stepwise approaches, with mechanisms to prevent semantic drift.

entry.title: What Comes Next and Why: Interpretable Next-Event Prediction with Neuro-Symbolic Rules

author.name: Tim Nico Bauerschmidt, Isabel Valera, Jilles Vreeken

entry.summary: The paper introduces RULES, a neuro-symbolic model learning sequential rules directly from data, and RUNES, which combines RULES with a residual network for next-event prediction. RULES recovers ground-truth rules on synthetic data and yields compact, interpretable rule sets while retaining predictive accuracy.

entry.title: Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy

author.name: Gautam Kamath, Mahbod Majid, Ankur Moitra, Argyris Mouzakis, Jonathan Ullman

entry.summary: The paper gives polynomial-time algorithms for learning discrete distributions under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting, achieving sample complexities matching information-theoretic optima up to log factors under both pure and approximate DP. Strong theoretical grounding from established privacy-theory authors.

entry.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions

author.name: Qian Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George Karniadakis

entry.summary: OCFormer formulates real-time multi-agent path planning as a high-dimensional optimal control problem and uses a transformer to parameterize the inverse of a coordinate transformation into a latent space where agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian. This avoids the curse of dimensionality of HJB/PMP solvers while handling collision avoidance and obstacles.

entry.title: DRAFT: Decoding and Reconstructing 3D Room Layouts from fMRI and Camera Trajectories

author.name: Chi-Wei Lee, An-Kai Chen, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, Po-Chih Kuo

entry.summary: Introduces a new task: reconstructing 3D room layouts of held-out scenes using only known camera trajectories and participants' fMRI signals while they watch indoor walkthroughs, with no visual frames. DRAFT extracts a compact layout representation from early visual cortex and fuses it with geometric free-space cues, addressing the temporal mismatch between rapid visual change and blurred fMRI. This extends fMRI decoding from images and objects to metric scene geometry.

entry.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks

author.name: Xin He, Huan Lao, Xiliang Lu, Shijun Zhang

entry.summary: Quantifies a phase transition in approximation bounds as partially trainable two-layer networks interpolate between fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. Under spectral decay assumptions it proves squared L2 rates depending on trainable proportion and width, and observes matching behavior in training errors with sharper transitions under greater initialization mismatch.

entry.title: Chunk Recomputation under Real Document Revisions: Measuring Update Cost and Retrieval Quality of Fixed, Recursive, and Content-Defined Chunking

author.name: Yuning Bian, Lele Xu, Yifan Yuan, Xinyu Yin, Chengyan Zhan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates RAG chunking strategies not on static snapshots but under real document revisions, measuring re-embedding costs across 120 pairs of adjacent Wikipedia revisions under strict byte-identical reuse. Fixed-size chunking must recompute 57-68% of embedding workload after edits, while content-defined chunking substantially reduces this. It introduces an update-cost dimension largely absent from chunking literature.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Constitutional AI: Enhancing Safety in LLM-Powered Mental Health Chatbots

author.name: Chenhan Lyu, Yutong Song, Pengfei Zhang, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: This paper argues that general AI safeguards are inadequate for mental health chatbots, where emotional vulnerability, crisis intervention accuracy, and risks like misdiagnosis or self-harm require specialized protections. It proposes adapting constitutional AI methods with domain-specific principles to improve safety in LLM-powered mental health applications.

entry.title: CODI: Improving Self-Supervised Vision Transformers with Cross Distillation

author.name: Siran Dai, Qianqian Xu, Peisong Wen, Yang Liu, Xiaochun Cao, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: CODI investigates why self-supervised vision transformers produce unreliable patch-level representations for dense prediction, showing via local gradient analysis that image-level self-distillation gradients are weighted by CLS-to-patch attention mass. It proposes mixing a small amount of the teacher class-token distribution into each teacher patch-token target, giving masked patches global semantics without architectural changes. This yields improved dense prediction from self-supervised pretraining.

entry.title: HimmBO: High-Dimensional Interactive Model-Merging Bayesian Optimization for Image Generation

author.name: Jinyuan Mao, Zhihao Shen, Chenxi Liu

entry.summary: HimmBO scales preference-driven adapter merging for text-to-image models to collections of over 100K adapters using a two-stage scheme: level-set estimation screens for the active adapter set, then preferential Bayesian optimization explores the reduced space. This reduces expensive image-generation rounds compared to prior methods limited to a few dozen adapters.

entry.title: UniVOE: A Removal-Driven Framework for Interaction-Aware Universal Video Object Editing

author.name: Shuzhou Yang, Lanqing Guo, Lingen Li, Weiqi Li, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a removal-driven framework for video object removal and injection: an effect-aware remover is trained from video inpainting and then used to generate paired supervision for training an injection model, avoiding scarce aligned real-world pairs. The approach models scene-dependent interaction effects for universal editing.

entry.title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation

author.name: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu, Kai Zhang, Jiemin Fang, Qi Tian

entry.summary: Introduces a degradation-aware gating model that routes inputs to existing single-image 3D generators: clean images bypass processing while degraded ones are purified by a one-step 3D-oriented purifier guided by extracted features and spatial identity-preserving losses. This improves robustness on real-world images with blur, occlusion, and uneven illumination without retraining the generators.

entry.title: First hardware demonstration of a continuous-state probabilistic computer with programmable energy-defined sampling

author.name: Chao Fang, Hsuan Yao Tu, Yihan He, Xiao Gong, Chin-Fu Nien, Gengchiau Liang

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates the first hardware implementation of a continuous probabilistic computer whose probabilistic bits sample bounded states from energy-defined conditional distributions, moving beyond binary stochastic units. An FPGA prototype supports product constraints, memory recovery, and optimization tasks, with a path toward physical random sources. It extends probabilistic computing to continuous variables natively.

entry.title: To Route or to Adapt? Multi-Expert Diffusion Planners in Unseen Regions

author.name: Yun Li, Ehsan Javanmardi, Simon Thompson, Jiachen Gong, Qunli Zhang, Zifan Zeng, Shiming Liu, Peng Wang, Yidu Zhang, Manabu Tsukada

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies whether multi-expert diffusion trajectory planners should route among existing domain experts or adapt the planner when deployed in unseen regions. Across three held-out real-world maps, none of eight routing schemes beat a static default, and even an oracle gains little, whereas fine-tuning on just 20 target scenes yields large improvements. This negative result on test-time routing is a useful finding for the growing multi-expert and modular-planner literature.

entry.title: The Cost of Saying Hello: An Empirical Study of Handshake Overhead in AI Agent Communication Protocols

author.name: Pranav Varshney

entry.summary: This paper presents the first empirical benchmark of handshake overhead (session setup, capability discovery, connection establishment) in three major agent communication protocols: MCP, A2A, and ACP. Using official SDKs, the authors measure round trips, latency, wire bytes, and token cost across cold-start, warm-repeat, and degraded scenarios. It fills a real gap, as prior protocol surveys cited handshake efficiency without ever measuring it.

entry.title: Speculative Acceptance Does Not Decay with Position: A Full-Length Diagnostic on Long Chain-of-Thought with Independent Drafts

author.name: Zhiming Meng

entry.summary: This paper challenges the widely accepted industry claim that speculative-decoding acceptance rates decay with chain-of-thought length. Through full-length measurements on all 500 MATH-500 problems using independent same-family and cross-family draft models against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, with roughly 1.78M verification rounds, it isolates position effects from training-length confounds. The finding undermines motivations for position-aware draft co-design.

entry.title: The Geometry of Meaning in Neural Manifolds

author.name: Valentino Maiorca

entry.summary: A thesis arguing that semantic correspondence is a fundamental primitive revealing shared geometric structure across independently trained neural networks with incompatible coordinate systems. It investigates whether models solving similar tasks share exploitable representational structure despite divergent parameterizations.

entry.title: IRAH: Hierarchical Agentic Tree Search for Retrieval Pipeline Optimization

author.name: Maria Ana Cardei, Aniket Singh, Amir Moghadam, Srividhya Baikadi, Rashmi Shetty

entry.summary: IRAH combines Language Agent Tree Search with offline meta-learned initialization to jointly optimize RAG pipeline structure and hyperparameters under limited evaluation budgets. Its UCT-guided hierarchical search explores macro-structural choices then refines numeric parameters, using natural-language reflections that leave inspectable search traces, evaluated on three in-distribution and one out-of-distribution benchmark.

entry.title: MPBRS: Multi-Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Unified Reward Configuration in Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Van Chung Nguyen, Hung Manh La

entry.summary: This paper extends Potential-Based Reward Shaping to a multi-potential formulation for humanoid locomotion, proposing a unified reward configuration that preserves optimal policies while simplifying reward design. The same reward structure and weights are evaluated across nine different humanoid robots, requiring only robot-specific adjustments, addressing a key pain point in RL for robotics.

entry.title: One-shot federated unsupervised domain adaptation with Smoothed Knowledge Distillation and teacher refinement

author.name: Ali Abedi, Q. M. Jonathan Wu, Ning Zhang, Farhad Pourpanah

entry.summary: This paper proposes SKD-ETR, a one-shot framework for federated unsupervised domain adaptation that distills an ensemble of decentralized source models into a student trained on an unlabeled target domain. Smoothed knowledge distillation reduces overconfidence in pseudo labels, while EMA-based teacher refinement improves consistency, eliminating the need for many communication rounds and complex aggregation.

entry.title: Query-Time Calibration of CLIP Features for Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation

author.name: Dominik Engel, Yousef Rajeh, Leon Sick, Ivan Viola

entry.summary: The paper shows that substantial gains in open-vocabulary 3D segmentation of Gaussian-splat scenes come purely from changing how lifted CLIP features are compared with text: subtracting a shared scene direction and whitening text prototypes using a generic reference vocabulary, followed by soft clustering. No retraining of the feature field is required.

entry.title: Truthful by Omission: Click Thinning for LLM-Native Advertising

author.name: Junhua Liu, Zhicheng Liang, Zejun Zhang, Langzhou He, Feng Qian

entry.summary: This paper studies auction mechanism design for advertising embedded in generative AI assistant answers, where click-through rates depend on the hosting passage and users click at most once, creating competition between ad slots. It proposes a mechanism achieving both a constant-fraction welfare guarantee and truthfulness, properties that prior mechanisms attained only individually. This matters as AI assistants become a real advertising medium, requiring new auction theory beyond classical position auctions.

entry.title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Yifan Yuan, Yancheng Zhu, Zuoyu Zhang, Xiaogang Peng

entry.summary: SurveyGraph is an automated survey generation framework built on a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph that encodes method-level relations such as follow-on work, competition, and shared resources. The graph supports core-paper discovery, hybrid outlining, and evidence-gated narrative synthesis, and outperforms flat-document retrieval baselines on recall and structural density in an equal-budget benchmark. It matters because it addresses a core weakness of current literature-review automation by preserving the structure of a research field rather than treating papers as isolated documents.

entry.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination

author.name: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Unai Zulaika, Ruben Sanchez-Corcuera, Aritz Bilbao-Jayo, Aitor Almeida

entry.summary: The authors evaluate four open models (8-27B parameters) on 1,552 questions from eight editions of the Spanish MIR medical residency exam, going beyond accuracy to test calibration, whether medical fine-tuning improves uncertainty recognition, soundness of clinical reasoning, and actual image use. The three larger models would rank within roughly the first 600-3,000 candidates. This provides a nuanced picture for health systems considering on-premises open-model deployment.

entry.title: Spectral Uncertainty Decomposition for Sparse Bayesian Learning

author.name: Ismail Huseynov, Stefan Haufe

entry.summary: Proposes a spectral framework based on the singular value structure of the prior-preconditioned forward operator that exactly decomposes posterior covariance into data-informed and indeterminacy components for M/EEG source estimation. This separates uncertainty reducible by better measurements from fundamentally irreducible uncertainty.

entry.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute During Training

author.name: Ruijia Zhang, Soufiane Hayou

entry.summary: Extending prior results that infinite-width and infinite-depth limits of residual networks commute at initialization, this work proves commutativity during training for linear residual networks under Depth-muP and muP parameterizations with gradient clipping. The result shows the output converges in L2 along any joint width-depth growth path, unifying two scaling regimes.

entry.title: Lean Finder V2: Semantic Search for Mathlib That Disambiguates User Queries

author.name: Jialin Lu, Xiaoyu Liu, Hengrui Luo, Rodrigo Stehling, Linxi Liu, Weiran Sun, Yuepeng Wang, Wuyang Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents Lean Finder V2, a semantic search framework for the Lean theorem prover's Mathlib library that handles short, ambiguous queries by combining model-level adversarial training with input-level query rewriting. The authors identify that existing Mathlib search tools assume context-rich queries, while real users (both human mathematicians and coding agents) issue terse, notation-heavy queries with implicit intent, and they address the labeled-data scarcity by generating adversarially-hard short query/statement pairs. This matters because robust retrieval over formal math libraries is a key bottleneck for AI-assisted formal theorem proving.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Distributionally Robust Offline Contextual Pricing

author.name: Min Xu, Xinyi Yin, Yunfan Zhang, Yuxuan Han, Houcai Shen, Caihua Chen

entry.summary: This paper develops a doubly robust framework for distributionally robust off-policy evaluation and learning in offline contextual pricing with continuous actions. It addresses sensitivity of IPW-based estimators to propensity score estimation errors, extending DRO methods beyond discrete actions.

entry.title: RheOPT: Few-Shot Non-Newtonian Flow Prediction via Newtonian Pretraining of RheOFormer

author.name: Maedeh Saberi, Amir Barati Farimani, Safa Jamali

entry.summary: RheOPT pretrains a transformer-based neural operator on cheap Newtonian flow simulations and fine-tunes it with only a few non-Newtonian samples, addressing the fact that training data for flow surrogates are as expensive as the simulations they replace. This transfer approach makes neural-operator surrogates practical for computationally costly, history-dependent rheology problems.

entry.title: OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: OP-Print presents the first membership-inference attack study against on-policy self-distillation, showing that using two coupled views of the same training example can strengthen memorization. It covers gray-box and black-box threat models within a unified attack framework.

entry.title: xVGAE: A Hierarchical Variational Graph Autoencoder for Exchangeable Graphs

author.name: Daniele Micheletti, Federica Zoe Ricci, Erik B. Sudderth

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical variational graph autoencoder grounded in the Aldous-Hoover representation theorem for exchangeable graphs, achieving generative quality competitive with state-of-the-art graph generative models while being orders of magnitude faster at generation. The paper identifies simple scenarios where existing SOTA graph generators fail to converge or generate too slowly. The design leverages classic exchangeability theory for a practical architecture.

entry.title: Learning Robot Behavior Priors from Non-Robotic Synthetic Data

author.name: Mateusz Odrowaz-Sypniewski, Michael Amir, Jasmine Bayrooti, Ajay Shankar, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: Investigates whether inexpensive, procedurally generated synthetic data from systems without embodiment can yield useful behavior priors for robot action prediction before any real-world data is seen. The authors introduce three data generation pipelines modeling mathematical abstractions and test whether structure learned from arbitrary synthetic tasks transfers to embodied settings. This challenges the assumption that real robot data is the sole bottleneck for embodied foundation models.

entry.title: Data-Driven Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing: A Survey

author.name: Yue Zhou, Shujun Zhao, Xue Yang, Ruigang Li, Tianwen Zhang, Mengcheng Lan, Chaofeng Chen, Lingfei Ma, Hongjie He, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: A survey mapping the shift in remote sensing vision research from task-specific architecture design to fine-tuning general-purpose vision-language models with domain data. It organizes the field around data-centric practices for constructing high-quality remote sensing training data, addressing a gap in systematic guidance for practitioners.

entry.title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages

author.name: Weiran Wang, Wenjuan Qin, Haitao Liu

entry.summary: This study revisits the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis by comparing conceptual structure across 196 basic concepts in 81 languages using embeddings from two multilingual models. It finds that cross-language correspondence is greater for sociocultural meanings than for nature and motion meanings, and that relational divergence grows with geographic and genealogical separation. The work demonstrates large-scale computational testing of linguistic relativity.

entry.title: SyRA-CS: Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation for Code-Switched ASR with Meta-Learning

author.name: Fadel Thior, Ahmer Tabassum, Haania Siddiqui, Hanan Aldarmaki, Thamar Solorio

entry.summary: This paper proposes SyRA-CS, a synthetic-to-real adaptation framework for code-switched speech recognition built on Reptile meta-learning, where models are meta-trained on synthetic code-switched speech and adapted with only one hour of real target-language audio. It evaluates four architectures (CTC, RNN-T, AED, Speech-LLM) across multiple language pairs, showing synthetic data is more useful for learning adaptation-friendly initializations than for direct fine-tuning.

entry.title: R4DGS: Referring Segmentation in 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Bangpu Chen, Yaxuan Li, Shirui Peng, Xiangtian Si, Liuxin Chu, Xitong Cao, Hongbo Jin, Jiayu Ding

entry.summary: This paper introduces R4DGS, a new task of referring segmentation in dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting scenes, supporting temporally varying, multi-target, reasoning-intensive, and zero-target/distractor natural language expressions. The authors also release R4D-Bench-QA, a benchmark with structured queries to evaluate these capabilities. This matters because it extends 4DGS beyond rendering into language-grounded scene understanding.

entry.title: Loop to Look Better: Learning Adaptive Depth for Question-Guided Perception in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wencheng Ye, Anning Hu, Hongye Fang, Tianyi Wang, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: LoopLook adds an encoder-side recurrent loop to pretrained VLMs so visual tokens are refined adaptively based on the question rather than acquired in a single task-agnostic pass. This addresses the evidence-acquisition bottleneck where models reason longer without revisiting visual evidence.

entry.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Jinyu Zhang, Haitao Lin, Jiashu Hou, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Presents a real-time single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and completed shape from one RGB-D observation, lifting foundation model features in a geometry-aware way. It avoids error-prone intermediate structures and the latency of diffusion-based pose methods.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity

author.name: Qiwen Gu, Xin Zhou, Xiwu Chen, Zhongyang Zhu, Zhuo Zhang, Junqiao Zhao

entry.summary: FlexPart is a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that accepts variable-granularity geometric conditions, from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, in a single model. It uses gated adaptive modulation to integrate heterogeneous inputs and an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism for cross-granularity consistency. This matters for flexible, controllable digital asset creation workflows.

entry.title: Robot Motion Transition with Human Motion Prior

author.name: Taehyun Byun, Taemoon Jeong, Yoonbyung Chai, Woojin Wie, Insu Park, Kyungjae Lee, Sungjoon Choi

entry.summary: This paper introduces STAMP, a framework for connecting independently acquired humanoid motions into continuous sequences via a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process. It uses human motion priors to generate transitions, addressing failure modes like unintended locomotion or turning when boundary poses are poorly arranged. This matters because smooth motion stitching is a key gap between motion-tracking policies and long-horizon humanoid behavior.

entry.title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets

author.name: Chaoyue Li, Zeyu Gao, Yanfeng Lu, Fan Luo

entry.summary: This paper addresses the data scarcity bottleneck for fine-tuning LLM-based task and motion planning (TAMP) agents. SCOPE automatically generates diverse, physically consistent scene graphs for long-horizon planning datasets by using plan error-correction to avoid homogeneity and unsolvability problems found in prior automated generation methods.

entry.title: The science behind TorchNeuron, Amazon’s new PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium chips

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon announces TorchNeuron, an open-source PyTorch backend that translates existing PyTorch code to run on AWS Trainium accelerators with minimal or no code changes. The post explains the technical approach and highlights access to the Neuron SDK, including cycle-accurate profiling and the Neuron Kernel Interface for near-assembly-level control.

entry.title: Soft Ontology Priors over Latent Concept Posteriors for Weakly Supervised Neuro-Symbolic Learning

author.name: Tengwei Song, Robert Hoehndorf

entry.summary: This paper tackles reasoning shortcuts in weakly supervised neuro-symbolic learning by injecting a soft ontology prior over latent concepts and compiling it with task constraints into smooth, decomposable probabilistic circuits. Normalizers reduce to weighted model counts linear in compiled circuit size, and the experimental placement of the prior controls the identifiability-generalization tradeoff.

entry.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation

author.name: Idunnuoluwa A. Adeniji, Shilpika, Michael E. Papka

entry.summary: This audit examines whether trace-level detectors used in LLM agent evaluation (final correctness, tool verification, fault propagation) actually capture what execution traces show, using a tool-use setting on GSM8K with deliberately corrupted calculator outputs as ground truth. Across six production models, the authors find systematic disagreements between labels and traces, including a silent failure mode where corrupted outputs go undetected.

entry.title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight

author.name: Ahmed M. Mahran

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a partition theory of evaluation from the principle that judgement is bounded by perception, modeling an agent's discrimination as a partition of inputs into indistinguishable classes. It proves a one-sided bound: an examinee whose partition refines its evaluator's has the discrimination to pass every test the evaluator can grade, and introduces the echo test to formalize this. The results bear on fundamental limits of what benchmarks can certify about hidden capabilities.

entry.title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design

author.name: Jianghan Zhu, Jianan Zhou, Fei Liu, Ni Zhang, Yaoxin Wu, Zhuoyi Lin, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for LLM-driven automatic heuristic design on NP-hard combinatorial optimization tasks, factorizing heuristic transformation into directional search primitives such as expansion. This goes beyond standard evolutionary-computation wrappers by harnessing the direction of heuristic transformation at the generation level.

entry.title: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Wenrui Yuan, St\'ephanie M. van den Berg, Johannes Steinr\"ucke

entry.summary: This study shows that knowledge tracing models trained solely for next-response prediction do not necessarily recover interpretable item parameters, analyzing 2PL, GPCM, and NRM decoders paired with LSTM, Transformer, and DKVMN encoders. Using response-model derivatives and affine logit identities, it demonstrates analytically and in simulation how ability misestimation is absorbed into item parameters, with discrimination recovery particularly fragile.

entry.title: Bifurcations from Weight Space: JEPAWG on Parametric Dynamical Systems

author.name: Tobias G\"obel, Miranda C. N. Cheng

entry.summary: The authors construct model zoos by fine-tuning forecasting networks across parameter grids of four dynamical systems with known bifurcation structure, then validate JEPAWG, a joint-embedding hypernetwork with a learned parameter-weight map, against analytic ground truth. This provides a rare setting with verifiable ground truth for weight-space learning methods.

entry.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations

author.name: Roberto Passaro, Ariel Flint, Romualdo Pastor-Satorras, Andrea Baronchelli, Luca Maria Aiello

entry.summary: This study places LLM-derived policies on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks of 10^3 to 10^5 agents playing the naming game, showing topology affects whether and how fast consensus emerges and occasionally which convention wins. Sparsest networks slow consensus up to twelvefold but can restore convergence in cases that fail under well-mixed interaction. It extends LLM collective-behavior research beyond well-mixed populations.

entry.title: Superintelligent Software Engineering: Governance That Scales with Capability

author.name: Mohammad Mehdi Gholinejad

entry.summary: This position paper argues that as software agents surpass human engineers in capability, capability alone will not yield better software; governance mechanisms such as gates, contracts, decision records, and decay control must scale alongside capability. The authors build the argument on three claims: correctness depends on decisions and contracts not encoded in code, knowledge decays over time, and once agents outpace human reviewers, code review catches a shrinking share of changes built on stale knowledge. A simple model shows that past a fixed review capacity, escaping changes grow without bound, motivating scalable governance structures.

entry.title: HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning

author.name: Xun Sun, Thanh Thi Nguyen, Thuy-Trang Vu

entry.summary: HERD is a hybrid continual learning framework combining non-parametric in-context harnesses with parametric internalization via recursive distillation. The harness continually refines reusable skills while retaining high-resolution information in context, and distillation converts harness experience into cumulative model capabilities. It aims to sidestep catastrophic forgetting and context-length limits that plague purely parametric or non-parametric approaches.

entry.title: Evaluating Type-1 Diabetes Digital Twins by Decision Quality

author.name: Victor Li, Owen Tucker, Michael S. Hughes, Temiloluwa Prioleau, Shengpu Tang

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating type 1 diabetes digital twins by decision quality, i.e., whether predicted glucose trajectories correctly rank candidate insulin treatments, rather than by trajectory prediction accuracy alone. The paper presents an evaluation protocol and metrics directly tied to downstream clinical decision-making.

entry.title: One Teacher, Many Views: Reducing Reference Sensitivity in On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Khouloud Saadi, Di Wang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that on-policy self-distillation conditioned on a single reference solution produces teacher targets overly dependent on one realization of the reasoning process, including arbitrary ordering and phrasing. It proposes using multiple teacher views to reduce reference sensitivity and improve reasoning training.

entry.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching

author.name: Rundong Ding, Yiyun He, Yizhe Zhu

entry.summary: The paper introduces generalized moment matching for differentially private synthetic data generation on arbitrary databases, privately estimating moments, fitting a measure, and sampling, with error guarantees under integral probability metrics. It extends prior Chebyshev moment matching to MMD with various kernels, sliced Wasserstein, and neural-network-induced IPMs.

entry.title: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and Decision-Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Modern Social Engineering Scams

author.name: Jaishnoor Kaur, Josef Hor\'a\v{c}ek, Ian Waskom, Sayak Saha Roy

entry.summary: Presents ReDence, an open-source hybrid framework for detecting social engineering scams by combining a fine-tuned multimodal agentic Investigator (Qwen3.5-4B) that plans investigations, interprets evidence across website workflows, and reports, with a decision model for classification. The system automates evidence gathering and cross-page verification that analysts currently perform manually. It aims to speed detection and takedown of diverse scam categories.

entry.title: Prediction Uncertainty Controlled Computer Model Calibration

author.name: Ryan Heejoon Byun, Dayeon Yoon, Won Chang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-layer calibration framework that directly targets predictive miscoverage of calibrated simulators, combining a conditional flow-matching model for amortized posterior inference over calibration parameters with conformal risk control to arrange posterior draws into valid predictive bands. It addresses failures of Bayesian Kennedy-O'Hagan calibration and simulation-based inference when parameters are weakly identified or discrepancy is misspecified. The result is simulator-output bands with controlled coverage.

entry.title: Graph-Recurrent Learning of Emergent Collective Dynamics

author.name: Ali Rayat, Acacia Lee, Gia-Wei Chern

entry.summary: Presents a graph-recurrent neural network framework that learns emergent collective dynamics in correlated electron systems directly from trajectories, without specifying microscopic equations of motion. It combines gated recurrent memory with graph message passing so local hidden states and spatial coupling jointly capture temporal memory and spatial interaction.

entry.title: WikiOriginQA: Automated Construction of a QA Dataset with Knowledge Origins for Analyzing Cultural Bias

author.name: Kento Haneda, Yosuke Kishinami, Ryo Fujii, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Makoto Morishita

entry.summary: Introduces WikiOriginQA, a QA dataset automatically constructed using Wikipedia language-edition creation dates to represent knowledge origins, enabling scalable cultural bias evaluation without human annotators per culture. Experiments confirm LLM performance skews toward Anglophone cultures and suggest knowledge propagation into the Anglosphere matters.

entry.title: When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models

author.name: Rushab Munot

entry.summary: This single-author study evaluates three decision models (including Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions) on multi-correct-choice datasets and finds that even when models rank all correct choices above distractors, 28-50% of such lists contain a correct choice assigned probability below uniform 1/n. The results undermine assumptions that decision-model probabilities are reliable for thresholding when multiple answers are valid.

entry.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation

author.name: Songlin Yang, Zhe Wang, Xiaotong Zhao, Xi Wang, Ran Zhang, Shuai Li, Taiyi Wu, Songlian Li, Eric Liu, Alan Zhao, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: FAPL tackles how to make MLLM representations actionable for cinematic video generation, addressing factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera plus temporal inference from sparse guidance. It establishes effective latent use as a shared prerequisite and applies complementary learning signals so the video DiT cannot bypass MLLM conditioning.

entry.title: Integrated Respiratory Sensing and Gated Control for Autonomous Needle Insertion Via CT Bore Robotic Arm

author.name: Emma Huang, Moira Bohley, Krishna Jamakhandi, Rebecca Fellbaum, Sophia Tang, Sean Tutton, Albert Hsiao, Alexander Norbash, Changwei Chen, Derek Chen, Ananya Rao, Lizzie Peiros, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: The system performs autonomous, respiratory-gated needle insertion for CT-guided lung biopsy inside the CT bore, tracking and predicting patient breath cycles and detecting anomalies without breath-holding. Demonstrations show gated insertion without manual placement or repeated confirmation scans. This could reduce procedure time, discomfort, and radiation exposure.

entry.title: In-Context Learning World Models for Robot Dual-Arm Manipulation of Soft Garment with Partial Observations

author.name: Hengyi Sim, Quentin Rouxel, Dennis Hong, Darwin Caldwell, Fei Chen

entry.summary: This work presents an in-context learning based world model for dual-arm manipulation of deformable garments under partial observations, mimicking human ability to imagine object shape and material properties. It reduces the need for large real-world datasets typically required by learned world models. Soft-object manipulation is a persistent challenge for household service robots, making this practically significant.

entry.title: Neural Networks with Differentiable Belief-Function Layers

author.name: Antonin Sulc

entry.summary: This work connects Yager's 1987 belief-combination rule to backpropagation, showing Dempster's normalizer introduces a divergent gradient term exactly when evidence sources conflict, while Yager's rule is bilinear and stable. It builds a deep evidential pipeline where every intermediate is a valid Dempster-Shafer mass function, with output ignorance mass serving as a calibrated uncertainty signal.

entry.title: Why Bother Me Again? Benchmarking Personal Agent Memory for Interaction Preferences

author.name: Jialin Li, Zhenhao Chen, Hanjun Luo, Hanan Salam

entry.summary: MemPABench is an interactive benchmark for on-policy evaluation of personal-agent memory focused on interaction preferences rather than factual recall. It presents long-horizon tasks where agents must decide when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously, using four grounded simulated users holding 14 preferences across work and personal contexts.

entry.title: ProQuant: Preserving Expert Quality over Quantity in Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Jiaqi Chen, Xianglong Yan, Chengzhu Bao, Xie Chen, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: ProQuant is a weight-only post-training quantization framework for MoE models that identifies two failure modes at very low bit widths: underestimated nonlinear errors from ignoring cross-layer propagation, and routing drift from direct router fine-tuning. It introduces Prune-or-Prioritize mixed-precision strategies to preserve expert quality under tight bit budgets. The approach targets reducing MoE storage costs while retaining generation quality.

entry.title: ColaBench: Evaluating Memory-Guided Knowledge Acquisition in Personal Agents

author.name: Wenjie Zhang, Zhichao Shi, Xuhui Jiang, Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Chengjin Xu, Xiaoning Song

entry.summary: Introduces ColaBench, a synthetic benchmark with 349 tasks across 10 user profiles and a 13,033-document knowledge base for evaluating whether personal agents can both identify needed knowledge from interaction history and apply it to the user's specific circumstances. It targets the underexplored joint evaluation of memory recall and knowledge application.

entry.title: Reward-Weighted Preference Optimization for Selective Combinatorial Optimization Problems

author.name: Haohui Zhang, Xinyu Hu, Wouter van Heeswijk, Neil Yorke-Smith, Martijn Mes

entry.summary: The paper introduces RWPO, a pairwise preference optimization method for selective combinatorial optimization problems like Orienteering, Prize-Collecting TSP, and Knapsack, where the choice of which elements to include produces large objective differences. Unlike standard preference learning that reduces comparisons to binary rankings, RWPO weights preferences by reward magnitude. This improves how RL for combinatorial optimization captures solution quality differences.

entry.title: Detection Is Not Enough: Reasoning Traces as Testable Program Hypotheses

author.name: Vaidehi Hegde

entry.summary: The paper examines how far a single reasoning trace from a frozen LLaMA-2-7B-chat model can be verified on GSM8K with no reference solution, no judge model, and no weight updates, treating the trace as a testable program hypothesis. Self-checking reaches an AUROC of 0.741 and plateaus for a structural reason, showing that detection of errors is not the limiting factor in reference-free verification.

entry.title: Asking Less, Adapting Better: Feedback-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Zixu Wang, Huaquan Zhang, Shoukai Xu, Jinwu Hu, Zhiquan Wen, Mingkui Tan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a feedback-efficient test-time adaptation method for vision-and-language navigation that localizes which trajectory steps are actually informative, rather than applying trajectory-level human feedback uniformly. This reduces feedback requirements and avoids the cascading errors of entropy-minimization TTA in unseen environments.

entry.title: Meaning Contracts: Local Semantic Geometry in Large Language Models

author.name: Andr\'es Daniel Godoy Ortiz

entry.summary: This single-author study characterizes the within-concept local geometry of meaning in four decoder-only LLMs (including Gemma 4 and Llama 3.2) using cross-lingual and semantic-refinement probes. It identifies what is invariant across realizations of a semantic factor and how geometry changes as meaning is refined, moving beyond simple embedding-distance analysis.

entry.title: LAST-V2X: Language-Driven Adaptive Scenario Synthesis and Testing for Communication-Induced Failures in V2X Safety Applications

author.name: Keshu Wu, Hao Zhang, Rui Gan, Pei Li, Jiwan Jiang, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: LAST-V2X uses LLMs to translate natural-language test descriptions into executable V2X safety-testing scenarios grounded in roadway geometry, communication semantics, and vehicle behavior, with adaptive synthesis targeting communication-induced failures. It systematically generates meaningful test cases for connected-vehicle safety applications where delayed or incorrect information can be dangerous.

entry.title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence

author.name: Gabriel Lars Sabadin, Dr Nicola Harding, Sarah Kingston

entry.summary: This position-style paper synthesizes evidence that content moderation systems over-flag dialects like African American English and under-protect low-resource languages, organizing known failures into seven failure modes. It argues that over-flagging and under-protection share a root cause: judging harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than what a message does. The authors propose framing harmful behavior detection as the fix, stated as testable hypotheses.

entry.title: AgenticEvolve: Evolutionary Program Search with Persistent Language Model Agents that Design and Run Experiments

author.name: Ze-Yu Peng, Qing-Yu Lan, Zhan-He Wang, Jun Zhang, Yun-Song Piao

entry.summary: AgenticEvolve is an evolutionary program search framework where each island population is managed by a persistent LLM agent that designs and runs experiments on candidate programs between evaluations. Comparisons against an identical configuration with experimentation disabled show better programs on two heuristic design tasks across three LLMs. The work contributes evidence that agentic experimentation adds measurable value to LLM-driven evolutionary search.

entry.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models

author.name: Shihui Li, Mette Andersen, Martha Lewis

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability techniques, the authors identify causal subspaces encoding metaphor across a range of LLM architectures and sizes. They demonstrate steering of metaphor classification across parts of speech and control of metaphoricity in generation tasks. This contributes to understanding how figurative language is represented and controllable inside LLMs.

entry.title: NEST: Nested Embedding Representation for Multiscale Clustering

author.name: Zhanqi Zhang, Mikio Aoi, Gal Mishne

entry.summary: Introduces NEST, an unsupervised framework inspired by Matryoshka Representation Learning that encodes coarse-to-fine cluster structure within a single embedding via joint optimization across nested prefix subspaces. Distances in the learned embedding track the true hierarchy more closely than input distances even though the hierarchy is never observed during training.

entry.title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs

author.name: Chenhao Zhou, Chao Zhang, Wensong Bai, Hanbin Zhao, Hui Qian

entry.summary: The paper studies representation learning for low-rank constrained MDPs with continuous states, proposing REP-PD-TEG which learns transition features via maximum likelihood during a feature-learning phase while controlling constraint violation, then plans with uncertainty bonuses in a primal-dual scheme. It targets the soft cumulative-violation setting with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: EEG-Captioner: Grounding EEG-to-Language Generation in Fundamental Signal Properties

author.name: Leyuan Jin, Jiahao Mei, Yixuan Yuan, Shimeng Li, Mengyue Wu, Yue Ding

entry.summary: This work introduces an EEG-language dataset of over 160,000 segments annotated with signal-level QA pairs targeting spectral, spatial, temporal, and lateral signal properties, plus feature-grounded captions. It aims to verify that EEG-to-language models genuinely interpret neural signals rather than producing plausible text.

entry.title: Deep ReLU Networks Can Fail the Best Approximation Property for Continuous Target Functions

author.name: Sebastian Kassing

entry.summary: This paper constructs a continuous function on the unit square for which the infimum of L2 approximation error over ReLU networks with a specific two-hidden-layer architecture is not attained, showing deep ReLU networks can lack the best approximation property. The proof exploits bending breaklines in the second hidden layer, breaking symmetry arguments valid for shallow networks.

entry.title: Evaluating the Applicability of LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon

author.name: Kyrylo Yemets, Andrii Yaroshevych, Victor Muryn, Ostap Khomenko, Pavlo Kryven, Maksym Kmet, Maksym Shamrai, Mariya Hirna

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates four LLM inference optimization families (KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported GPU kernels, and quantization) on Apple Silicon under single-request decode workloads, comparing against an RTX 4090. Findings include up to 1.75x throughput gains from KV-cache pruning on Apple hardware, with behaviors that can differ from or even reverse on NVIDIA GPUs.

entry.title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes

author.name: Ying Li, Sanyou Wu, Zi Yang, Qiaochu Xu, Yuhao Liu, Zhidi Lin, Michael Minyi Zhang, Petar Djuric, Alexandre H. Thiery

entry.summary: Reframes deep Gaussian processes by treating depth as a continuous latent evolution governed by a stochastic differential equation with a GP-based prior on the drift family, rather than a long discrete stack. The paper studies two instantiations (CDGP and an amortized variant) and argues the core design choice is the prior on the depth-indexed drift family. This avoids the optimization difficulties that grow with discrete DGP depth.

entry.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)

author.name: Lorenzo Sabug Jr., Eric Kerrigan

entry.summary: Proposes Diona, a regression method that estimates values and derivatives at a query point along with admissible bounds directly from samples via constrained optimization, replacing long global training with on-demand local solves. It provides finite-sample coverage guarantees and noiseless-case convergence, outperforming Gaussian process baselines on nonlinear benchmarks.

entry.title: Through a PRISM, Clearly: Step-Sequence Reasoning for Mistake Recognition in Procedural Videos

author.name: Olga Loginova, Oleksandr Bezrukov, Frank Keller

entry.summary: PRISM grounds video segments in language and maps descriptions to procedural states via a lightweight hidden Markov model trained on correct executions, using reference alignment and semantic checks to recognize mistakes in step content and order. It also maps heterogeneous dataset annotations to four edit-based error types for cross-benchmark comparison across three procedural video benchmarks.

entry.title: A Task-Centric Survey of Long-Document Visual Question Answering: Taxonomy, Evolution, and Future Directions

author.name: Yufei Tong, Guanjie Cheng, Tianle Wu, Leilei Zhang, Hang Zheng, Peihan Wu, Jianwei Yin, Shuiguang Deng

entry.summary: This task-centric survey decomposes long-document visual question answering into four components (document parsing, evidence organization and retrieval, generator organization and learning, and evaluation), offering fine-grained taxonomies and tracing how task bottlenecks shaped technical choices over time. It focuses on explicit retrieval while covering direct-reading approaches and temporal evolution of the field.

entry.title: SmolVLA-MoE: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shiyang Zhang, Miao Yang, Zhengda Li, Yang Shao, Ruifang Zhai, Hui Peng, Peng Song

entry.summary: SmolVLA-MoE introduces sparse Mixture-of-Experts into the FFN layers of the action expert in lightweight vision-language-action models for multi-task robotic manipulation. A token-level router adaptively selects experts per token, with a shared expert added for stability, improving multi-task capability under constrained compute budgets. This targets efficient VLA models for real-world robot deployment.

entry.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos

author.name: Zhuoran Zhang, Yang Shi, Qixun Wang, Tengfei Liu, Yuqi Tang, Xuanyu Zhu, Yizhuo Jia, Jingyun Hua, Shixuan Liu, Xianghua Ying, Haotian Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Wenjing Yang

entry.summary: Verus-Insight formulates AI-generated video artifact detection as a structured process of inspection planning, evidence verification, and explanation, aiming for detectors that both identify subtle artifacts and faithfully justify their decisions. It addresses a gap where existing detectors may be right for the wrong reasons.

entry.title: Pos4CHD: A Positive-Free Mask-Guided Counterfactual Synthesis Framework for Fetal Congenital Heart Defect Analysis

author.name: Wenjie Xuan, Yapeng Li, Hang Su, Chen Cheng, Juhua Liu, Sheng Zhao, Ziming Huang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Pos4CHD synthesizes positive fetal congenital heart defect cases from normal echocardiography using mask-guided counterfactual generation without requiring positive training samples. This addresses the extreme class imbalance and privacy barriers in building automated CHD diagnostic systems, especially for rare subtypes.

entry.title: Reinforcing intra-operative tumour localisation with weak supervision from pre-operative appearances

author.name: Sidhart Sami, Ali Sharjeel, Sri Atluri, Miao Zhao, Caroline Roney, Eirini Marouli, Shaheer U. Saeed

entry.summary: Transfers tumour appearance knowledge learned from pre-operative MR images to guide weakly supervised localization of hepatocellular carcinoma on intra-operative CT, addressing deformation and lack of paired data. This reduces reliance on hard-to-curate labeled intra-operative datasets for surgical navigation.

entry.title: MixPT: Point Transformer with Interleaved Window and Global Attention

author.name: Minkyun Seo, Hyungtae Lim, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: Proposes a point cloud transformer architecture that interleaves window attention and global attention to balance local geometric detail against scene-wide information exchange at manageable compute cost. The design addresses the cross-window information bottleneck of serialized window attention while retaining its efficiency.

entry.title: CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ilan Theodoro, Jord\~ao Bragantini, Lo\"ic A. Royer

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark drawing on 15 standard cell-tracking datasets to assess whether VLMs can perform cell tracking compared with specialized trackers. It probes whether general-purpose multimodal models can match domain-specific algorithms on spatiotemporal biological perception tasks.

entry.title: A Sparse Topometric Graph for Scalable Cross-Session Indoor Navigation

author.name: Eun Sun Lee, Minkyun Seo, Gwangtak Bae, Junho Kim, Seunggu Kang, Jaesik Park, Young Min Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a sparse topometric graph representation for indoor navigation that encodes local 3D geometry in nodes and distance-weighted connectivity in edges, enabling training-free cross-session guidance. It avoids expensive fine-grained map matching that is brittle to scene changes and sensor differences. This improves robustness and scalability for embodied agents in changing environments.

entry.title: Live Thread Reconstruction for Autonomous Manipulation

author.name: Emma Huang, Omar Hernandez, Zih-Yun Chiu, Michael Yip

entry.summary: The paper addresses deformable thread state estimation for autonomous suturing, where thread configuration must be continuously re-estimated rather than assumed due to effectively infinite degrees of freedom. It reconstructs live thread state informed by sequential manipulation context across suturing subtasks. A key perception enabler for fully autonomous surgical suturing.

entry.title: ProTrav: Probabilistic Traversability with Elevation Uncertainty Propagation for Risk-aware Off-road Navigation

author.name: Chuanlin Zuo, Milo\v{s} Pr\'{a}gr, Arun Kumar Singh, Mohammad Loni, Reza Ghabcheloo

entry.summary: ProTrav proposes a probabilistic terrain representation for off-road navigation that propagates elevation uncertainty into traversability cost using sparse variational Gaussian processes and function-space sampling. Unlike deterministic approaches, it accounts for spatial correlations and nonlinear uncertainty propagation. This improves risk-aware autonomous navigation on unstructured terrain.

entry.title: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding

author.name: Taimeng Fu, Yi Du, Zitong Zhan, Qiwei Du, Shaoshu Su, Zhipeng Zhao, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a point-level refinable open-vocabulary 3D semantic mapping approach that re-evaluates and revises previously integrated points rather than using append-only accumulation, correcting noisy or obsolete points when objects move or disappear. This reduces error accumulation in the spatial memory used for long-horizon robot autonomy. Dynamic, correctable semantic maps are important for robots operating over long time scales.

entry.title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control

author.name: Fanxing Li, Yuxiang Huang, Shengyang Wang, Fangyu Sun, Shuyu Wu, Tianbao Zhang, Dexin Zuo, Yan Yufei, Danping Zou, Wenxian Yu

entry.summary: DiffDreamer couples a learned world model with differentiable physics simulation so that latent-state imagination handles external dynamics while the differentiable simulator optimizes the actor, disentangling robot dynamics from environmental evolution. It targets high-frequency agile control tasks such as dynamic-gate drone racing.

entry.title: A crop-mapping benchmark for the tropics

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 introduces PLANTEUR, which extends the PASTIS crop-mapping benchmark to six tropical regions, enabling evaluation of geospatial models on more diverse agricultural systems. This addresses a geographic bias in existing crop-mapping datasets that are concentrated in temperate, well-sampled regions.

entry.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Zhixin Lin, Dongliang Xu, Jungang Li, Shidong Pan, Jun Feng, Yanbin Sun, Jing Li, Liang Liu, Yue Yao

entry.summary: PrefDiag-Bench diagnoses how personalized GUI agents fail, categorizing preferences into five types characterizing how each should alter execution and providing a stage-wise framework with 1,664 probes tracing when preferences should take effect along the trajectory. Evaluation of eleven GUI agent systems, both end-to-end and agentic pipelines, reveals where personalization breaks down.

entry.title: Constraint Reasoning and Large Language Models Join Forces: Providing Contrastive Explanations for Real-World Optimisation-Based Applications

author.name: Roger X. Lera-Leri, Filippo Bistaffa, Athina Georgara, Juan A. Rodr\'iguez-Aguilar

entry.summary: Proposes a methodology combining constraint reasoning with LLMs to generate contrastive explanations for recommendations derived from mixed-integer programs in real-world decision support systems. The goal is to enable human oversight of automated decisions in line with trustworthy AI guidelines.

entry.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity

author.name: Ali Atiah Alzahrani

entry.summary: CMAS formalizes automated agentic-system design as sequential architecture replacement under switching costs and hard risk constraints in non-stationary environments. It proposes typed graph edits over archived architectures, validates candidates via paired shadow replay under common random numbers, and promotes only variance-penalized improvements above a margin. This brings careful online-decision rigor to automated agent design.

entry.title: FocusVLA: Future-Intent Guided Dynamic View Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Huixin Xu, Ziya Yu, Peng Li

entry.summary: FocusVLA is a stage-aware multi-view routing method for vision-language-action models that dynamically adjusts global-local view dependency across manipulation stages, addressing the tendency of existing VLAs to over-rely on the wrist camera view. Future-intent guidance routes attention to the most informative views per manipulation stage. This improves robustness and adaptability of robotic manipulation policies.

entry.title: LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels

author.name: Jihoon Hong, Alireza Kheirandish, Rohan Sanda, Sara Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: Proposes LACToS, a local out-of-distribution detection method based on statistical typicality over superpixels, designed to handle multimodal inlier distributions where existing defect-detection-oriented methods degrade. Two innovations—superpixel grouping and a computationally efficient typicality estimate—make the approach principled and tractable.

entry.title: WildDepth-v2: A Synchronized RGB--LiDAR--Radar Dataset and Benchmark for Metric Depth, Motion, and Tracking of Wildlife

author.name: Muhammad Aamir, Sangyun Shin, Naoya Muramatsu, Matthew Wijers, Amir Patel, Andrew Loveridge, Andrew Markham

entry.summary: WildDepth-v2 extends a synchronized RGB-LiDAR wildlife dataset with imaging radar sequences including per-point Doppler velocity, a checksummed hidden test set for metric depth and depth completion, and metric 3D motion trajectories. It claims the first imaging-radar wildlife recordings and enables metric-scale ecology measurement from video.

entry.title: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents

author.name: Wei Zhang, Lirong Xiang, Charles Fleming

entry.summary: CARE dynamically decides when to escalate control from a fast local executor to a stronger cloud model in embodied agents, using a critic rather than fixed hierarchical roles or stateless per-request routing. This mitigates latency from cloud-only agents and error rates of local-only agents. It tackles a practical deployment problem for foundation-model embodied systems.

entry.title: EBV-CAN: Vision--Language Grounding for Contact-Aided Endoscope Navigation

author.name: Chi Kit Ng, Shuchang Liu, Jinsong Lin, Yidong Zhang, Xizi Wang, Ho Yin Chim, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EBV-CAN is a vision-language policy for navigating compliant flexible endoscopes through narrow lumens, combining one cached global bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state. Supervised semantic queries locate the tip, waypoint, and target, and the authors release the VLCA dataset with 517 demonstrations and 75k action samples. It embraces distributed contact as a signal rather than a nuisance.

entry.title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Tao Lin, Yuxin Du, Haoxiao Wang, Zile Zhong, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: FastHarness is an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a pi0.5 VLA policy, reducing review frequency as stage memory accumulates while concentrating supervision on verified error recovery. The robot policy stays frozen and the approach cuts overhead of reviewing every action chunk. It tackles a real efficiency bottleneck in LLM-supervised agentic robot systems.

entry.title: MCP vs CLI for AI Agents: A Comparative Analysis of Tool Integration Strategies for Autonomous Systems

author.name: Arun Malik, Nitish Talasu, Bradley Klemick, Vineet Tushar Trivedi, Prachi Shah, Sanay Devi, Junjie Zhang, Kunal Sonawane

entry.summary: A comparative analysis of two competing agent tool-integration paradigms: direct CLI/shell access versus the Model Context Protocol's structured JSON-RPC tool interface. The paper evaluates 14 dimensions including security, compliance-framework alignment, and economic cost, concluding CLI is more efficient for single-user local workflows while MCP uniquely enables fine-grained access control and credential isolation.

entry.title: SpecMAGIC: Specification-Guided Multi-Task Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijian Guo, \.Ilker I\c{s}{\i}k, H. M. Sabbir Ahmad, Wenchao Li

entry.summary: SpecMAGIC introduces a specification language combining temporal-logic task formulas with operators for inter-agent coordination requirements, plus a hierarchical MARL framework exploiting automaton structure for subtask decomposition. A centralized planner allocates subtask sequences across agents while decentralized low-level policies execute them, enabling zero-shot generalization to temporally extended multi-agent tasks.

entry.title: How Firm Are AI Models' Ethical Boundaries? A Pay-Stub Editing Test of 15 Models

author.name: Simiao Ren, Xingyu Shen, Tommy Duong, Tsang Ng, Ankit Raj

entry.summary: This empirical test probes whether small wording changes flip frontier models from refusing to complying with a request to alter income on a pay stub. Across 445 simulated trials with 15 models, compliance rose from 14.1 percent when a loan purpose was stated to 66.2 percent when framed as fixing a printing error; notable heterogeneity emerged among named systems such as Astra, Fable, Opus, Muse Spark, and Sonnet. The study reveals how fragile ethical refusals can be under benign-sounding framings.

entry.title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization

author.name: Zhaoran Feng, Yuchen Ni, Jianan Liu, Lemao Liu, Dejing Dou, Kairui Feng

entry.summary: ADAPT for Science is a multi-agent framework treating scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search, using historical designs to identify promising, diverse initial conditions under costly evaluations and strict physical constraints. The system progressively co-adapts its search strategy with scientific priors, distinguishing itself from general-purpose AI-for-AI methods. It targets sparse feasible regions and strongly coupled parameters typical of scientific design problems.

entry.title: Agri-SCHOLAR: Simulation-Grounded In-Season Rolling Advisories for Agricultural Crops Using LLM-Bounded Optimization

author.name: Geetha Charan, Vedant Balasubramaniam, Manojkumar Patil, V. Priyanka, Kodur Sai Vinay Sathvik, Rohit P Suresh, Mohammad Sufyan Azam, Y. Narahari

entry.summary: Presents Agri-SCHOLAR, a framework that issues personalized, rolling in-season crop advisories by combining soil/crop properties, observed weather, forecasts, and historical weather analogs, using LLM-guided optimization grounded in crop simulation. It aims to scale expert-quality agricultural advice to individual farms.

entry.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

author.name: Zehao Lin, Erenkai Zhu, Helan Hu, Xixuan Hao, Chunyu Li, Kai Chen

entry.summary: This paper develops a decision-theoretic framework for quantifying the value of memory in language agents, tracing it from raw history through persistent state and operational use to costly recovery and revision. It expresses value in units of avoided task loss, uses risk-cost frontiers, and provides five minimal counterexamples plus a cost-aware simulation condition. It offers a rare theoretical lens on a topic usually treated heuristically.

entry.title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
