author.name: Suyash Mishra, Qiang Li, Subhabrata Adak, Upender Phogat, Srikanth Patil, Satyanarayan Pati

entry.summary: This is a production case study of Composer, a deployed tool generating personalized, regulation-compliant pharmaceutical claims using a Golden Data Model of 1,867 claims across four products. It asks whether moving compliance and personalization signals from prompt-level rules into retrieval-time structured context improves output quality. It offers rare production-scale evidence in a regulated domain.

entry.title: TauIndianBankBench: Procedure-Aware, Action-Oriented Evaluation of Tool-Using Conversational Agents

author.name: Krishanu Adhikary, Prashant Devadiga

entry.summary: TauIndianBankBench evaluates tool-using conversational agents in an Indian banking context, checking not just final conversation records but whether agents follow required procedural steps (such as obtaining a closure quote before closing a deposit). It contains roughly 1,000 tasks and shows that record-only judging can credit assistants that skip mandatory steps.

entry.title: MPIDetector: Detecting Multi-modal Prompt Injection via LLM-based Reasoning

author.name: Yiheng Li, Jingyue Li

entry.summary: MPIDetector detects multi-modal prompt injection attacks against multimodal LLMs by leveraging LLM reasoning through few-shot in-context learning rather than fine-tuning, using prompt templates and representative attack examples. It aims to outperform signature- and perplexity-based detectors that fail on sophisticated cross-modal payloads.

entry.title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures

author.name: Shanmuka Sadhu, Harshvardhan C. Takawale, Yehia Zakaria, Ahmed Allam, Nirupam Roy

entry.summary: AcoustiPrint is a physics-informed neural architecture for inverse design of 3D acoustic structures that uses implicit neural representations and enforces discrete printability constraints during optimization rather than via soft penalties or post-processing. This reduces the gap between physics-optimized geometry and the final fabricated object, combining additive manufacturing constraints with neural inverse design.

entry.title: Future of Time Series Anomaly Detection: From Historical Review to Unified Outlook

author.name: Zhijie Zhong, Zhiwen Yu, Pengyu Li, Liujian Zhang, Qiaoli Ni, Jiang Jun, Jianming Lv, Kaixiang Yang, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: This survey of time series anomaly detection provides a refined anomaly categorization and structured taxonomy of paradigms including recent diffusion, state space, and LLM-based architectures, covering multivariate anomalies, cross-domain unified modeling, metric reliability, and evaluation challenges. It aims to unify a fragmented literature with contemporary coverage that prior surveys lack.

entry.title: Neural Spectral Capacity with Residual Context for Heterogeneous Resource Allocation within Transformers

author.name: Chenyu Zhu, Ruoyu Zhao, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: ResNSC extends Neural Spectral Capacity, a training-free heuristic for predicting a Transformer architecture's trained performance from specifications alone, by modeling residual-stream statistics so earlier layer choices affect later capacity scores. This enables better architecture resource allocation when heterogeneous residual widths are used, without data or instantiated weights.

entry.title: SecLog-Bench: A Scalable Benchmark for Cybersecurity Log Reasoning with Scaffolded Evidence

author.name: Yifan Wang, Dongliang Xu, Xiaoyong Li, Jing Li, Peter S. Pan, Yue Yao

entry.summary: SecLog-Bench is a scalable benchmark for LLM-based cybersecurity log analysis, built on an extensible simulation platform covering 29 attack scenarios with multi-source logs (audit, application, network traffic) and dense attack-stage annotations rather than only coarse labels. It addresses limitations of existing small, single-source datasets. It enables rigorous evaluation of how well models reconstruct attack reasoning from realistic heterogeneous evidence.

entry.title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials

author.name: Hagen Holthusen, Matthias Knipper, Kevin Linka

entry.summary: This paper combines intrusive model order reduction (proper orthogonal decomposition with energy-conserving sampling) with adjoint sensitivities to accelerate finite element model updating used to discover neural constitutive material models. The key challenge addressed is keeping the reduced model accurate while network weights change at every training step. This enables substantially cheaper training of neural materials, relevant to computational mechanics and simulation-based ML.

entry.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act

author.name: Robin Qu\'eriaux, Solveig Bachellery, L\'ea D\'el\'eris, Saurabhsingh Rajput, Mariam Barry, Tushar Sharma, J\'er\^ome Lebecq

entry.summary: VERA is an open-source, self-hosted dashboard that lets non-engineering compliance reviewers run public benchmarks against candidate LLM deployments and score the twelve EU AI Act technical requirements that current benchmarks can measure, based on the COMPL-AI interpretation. It was deployed within a large European bank. The tool bridges the gap between CLI-driven benchmark suites and governance approval workflows.

entry.title: Spike-Aware Gradient-Based Mixed-Precision Quantization of Spiking Neural Networks for Vision Applications

author.name: Rajshekhar Rakshit, Devgokul B. V, Rakshitha Kalkura, Gopalakrishnan Srinivasan

entry.summary: Proposes a mixed-precision quantization framework for spiking neural networks that adaptively assigns bit-widths using first-order gradient information, avoiding the costly Hessian computations and temporal unrolling of methods like HAWQ-V2. The approach targets maintaining SNN accuracy under low-precision constraints for energy-efficient vision deployment.

entry.title: Solvable models of learning to pursue a moving target

author.name: John J. Vastola, Kanaka Rajan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a continuous-time linear-quadratic optimal control model of agents pursuing moving targets, with closed-form solutions whose interpretable parameters interpolate between reactive chasing and predictive interception strategies. It offers a mathematically tractable lens on how pursuit strategies might be learned, connecting to observations of animal pursuit behavior.

entry.title: Random Initialization as a Baseline for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Pinar Sungu Isiacik, Georgiana Ifrim

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks seven pretrained time series foundation models against architecture-matched randomly initialized counterparts on the UEA multivariate classification archive using frozen representations and four classifiers. Across 183 paired comparisons, it quantifies how much pretraining contributes beyond architecture alone, finding improvements that are modest in many cases.

entry.title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning

author.name: Junyu Lin, Bosong Qi, Pengcheng Shi, Jiayuan Li

entry.summary: The authors propose an evaluation protocol for personalized federated learning that supplements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations and personalization floors among worst clients. They present FedGRC, a unified PFL framework using geometric consensus and support-adaptive personalization to improve global recognition while raising the personalization floor.

entry.title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization

author.name: Ioannis Kouroudis, Zhaosu Gu, Poonam, Leon Muller, Alessio Gagliardi

entry.summary: PYTHIA combines a foundational model pretrained on chemically similar molecules with transfer learning via frozen weights and subspace alignment to predict properties of novel, understudied materials. It enables simultaneous optimization of defects and adsorption sites with far fewer samples than conventional ML approaches.

entry.title: CRANE: Post-Hoc Counterfactual Retrieval for Multimodal Classifiers

author.name: Franco Rugolon, Ioanna Miliou, Panagiotis Papapetrou

entry.summary: CRANE is the first post-hoc, model-agnostic framework for generating counterfactual explanations for multimodal classifiers by retrieving real multimodal training examples as nearest-neighbour counterfactuals. Unlike per-modality attribution, it produces coherent cross-modal explanations transferable to arbitrary pretrained multimodal architectures.

entry.title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility

author.name: Germ\'an Pardo-Gonz\'alez, Shaghayegh Vosough, Katerina Papadaki, Claudio Roncoli

entry.summary: Applies multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically allocate incentives to drivers to reroute onto alternative paths, reducing total travel time and emissions in urban networks. The work addresses a policy-relevant alternative to road pricing, which is restricted in some jurisdictions such as Finland. Evaluation uses traffic simulation software for travel-time estimation.

entry.title: Random Projections for Spectral Algorithms: Optimal Rates in Sobolev Norms

author.name: Caixing Wang, Yue Wang

entry.summary: This arXiv paper analyzes the generalization performance of kernel-regularized spectral algorithms combined with random projections for dimensionality reduction. Using RKHS embedding properties and refined operator similarity analysis, the authors establish optimal learning rates in Sobolev norms under general conditions, extending prior work that held only in well-specified settings with restrictive assumptions. The result matters because it shows random projections can cut computational and storage costs without sacrificing statistical efficiency in kernel methods.

entry.title: Convex Equilibrium Potentials for Monge--Amp\`ere: Curvature Bounds and A Posteriori Evaluation

author.name: Edison V\'azquez, Yingdong Lu, Tomasz Nowicki

entry.summary: Analyzes equilibrium neural networks applied to the fully nonlinear Monge-Ampere equation, deriving sharp bounds on Hessian growth with effective depth for softplus networks with contraction. It also develops a posteriori evaluation error control, addressing two obstacles that explicit networks avoid when used for fully nonlinear PDEs.

entry.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark

author.name: Firoj Paudel

entry.summary: This paper introduces a 13,044-utterance benchmark of spontaneous Nepali-English code-switched podcast speech, carefully audited against machine-translation and acoustic-loop contamination, and proposes a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework using TTS-synthesized speech for fine-tuning multilingual ASR models. It targets script confusion and switch-point errors. The synthetic-to-real recipe is valuable where human code-switched data is scarce.

entry.title: CrisiLangs: A Multilingual Resource for Crisis Warning Generation

author.name: Giacomo Gonella, Stefano Menini, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: CrisiLangs extends the English CrisiText dataset for crisis warning message generation to Italian, Bulgarian, German, and Greek via expert native-speaker translations, yielding 5,000 event-message pairs across five languages. The resource enables fine-tuning and evaluation of models that generate guideline-compliant public warnings during emergencies. Multilingual crisis communication is a high-stakes, under-resourced application area.

entry.title: Bilingual Language Models Capture Cross-Linguistic Influence in Second-Language Reading

author.name: Abderrahmane Issam, Irene E. Winther, Stefan L. Frank

entry.summary: Using eye-tracking data from readers of 12 first-language backgrounds reading English, this paper shows that bilingual language models trained on text matching the reader's L1 better predict second-language reading times than monolingual baselines or mismatched bilingual models. This suggests cross-lingual transfer inside LMs mirrors human L1-driven biases during L2 reading.

entry.title: MixJudge: Learning a Language-Queryable Critic for Vocal Mixing

author.name: Kuan-Hsun Ho, Yuan-Chiao Cheng, Yen-Tung Yeh, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: MixJudge is a language-queryable audio-language critic trained on a curriculum of 11 vocal-mixing issues at multiple severity levels, enabling retrieval of mixing issues, discrimination of opposite issues, and severity ordering. It transfers to practical menu selection, favoring processing candidates acoustically closer to held-out professional mixes despite scarce professional supervision.

entry.title: FiLM-CAM: Keyed Feature Modulation for Conditional-Access Watermarking

author.name: Yash Kulthe, Vishal Asnani, Shruti Agarwal, Andrew Gilbert, John Collomosse

entry.summary: FiLM-CAM is a conditional-access image watermarking scheme where a secret key conditions FiLM-based feature modulation before embedding, coupling the watermark payload to the key at feature level. The decoder must present the same key to recover the payload, and training maximizes the gap between authorized and unauthorized extraction. It also introduces removal control, relevant for content provenance in the generative-AI era.

entry.title: PhyEvolve: Multi-Agent State-Evolution Planning for Physics-Aware Video Generation

author.name: Yang-Hao Zhou, Lixing Tan, Zhiqi Li, Guang Yang, Xiao Yang

entry.summary: PhyEvolve is a multi-agent framework that enhances text-to-video prompts through structured state-evolution planning to capture physical state evolution implicit in user prompts. It uses three agents - a Director that grounds the scene, a Physical Evolver that identifies physical mechanisms and builds causally linked state transitions, and a Composer that synthesizes output. The goal is physically coherent video generation with continuous state evolution.

entry.title: CAVC: Convergence-Adaptive Audio-Visual Cache for Modality-Asymmetric Diffusion Generation

author.name: Lifan Jiang, Yibo Zhao, Senlin cheng, Bolei Xu, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Dehai Zhao, Deng Cai, Boxi Wu

entry.summary: CAVC accelerates joint audio-visual diffusion generation by exploiting modality-asymmetric recoverability: cached audio computation can be recovered with a few terminal joint denoising steps, while video degradation from caching is persistent. The method selectively caches audio-side computation while preserving full video computation.

entry.title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Ronald Fecso, Jos\'e Morano, Botond Fazekas, Paul Widmann-Sedlnitzky, Dorota Himel, Laetita Hinterhuber, Virginia Mares, Andreas Pollreisz, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: RetinaGroundBench is the first benchmark for biomarker visual grounding in retinal OCT, with 815 expert-annotated B-scans, 4,537 bounding boxes, 13 biomarkers, and 8 diseases. It evaluates whether MLLMs localize pathologies they report, including handling of fragmented lesion predictions.

entry.title: Lightweight Frame Compensation for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation under Frame Skipping

author.name: Weihao Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a 77K-parameter plug-and-play module (LFC) that compensates for motion blur and lesion misalignment when inference is performed every K frames in real-time colonoscopy polyp segmentation. It fuses consecutive frames via spatio-temporal attention and is trained entirely on pseudo-labels without expert annotation, while the segmentation backbone remains frozen.

entry.title: GigaBench: Benchmarking Learnable Representations for Gigapixel Image Compression and Super-Resolution

author.name: Matteo Fusconi, Alex Costanzino, Pierluigi Zama Ramirez, Luigi Di Stefano

entry.summary: Introduces the first benchmark for deploying learnable representations (neural-native data formats) on gigapixel imagery, covering compression and super-resolution across images from diverse scientific, cultural, and industrial domains. It adapts a representative set of LRs to enable systematic comparison.

entry.title: H-2DGS: Height-Field Gaussian Splatting for Sharp and Deformable Neurosurgical Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Zhang Zichuan, Bart Brouwers, Rembrandt Bakker, Maud Landers, Geert-Jan Rutten, Maxime Chamberland

entry.summary: H-2DGS adapts Gaussian splatting with a height-field formulation to reconstruct sharp, deformable cortical surfaces during neurosurgery, combining photorealistic microscope views with MRI and tractography context. The height-field constraint prevents the diffuse, geometrically ambiguous reconstruction typical of 3DGS under limited surgical viewpoints. This has direct clinical value for image-guided tumor surgery.

entry.title: Alpha: Systematic Fault Injection and Robustness Evaluation for LLM-Driven Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Jona Joy

entry.summary: Alpha is a fault-injection framework that evaluates LLM-driven robotic manipulation under calibrated faults in perception, actuation, kinematics, and planning, comparing an LLM agent against a deterministic Scripted Oracle to isolate planner sensitivities from physical vulnerabilities. It fills a gap left by benchmarks that only measure nominal task success. Relevant to reliable deployment of LLM planners in robotics.

entry.title: OASIS: Online Anchor-centric Scene Inference System for Open-Vocabulary Retrieval and Navigation in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Kaiyao Liao, Qingfeng Li, Chen Chen, Xiaoze Wu, Qing Sun, Jianwei Niu

entry.summary: OASIS is a unified system for online mapping, open-vocabulary object retrieval, and navigation in dynamic environments, built around stable semantic anchors in indoor scenes. It balances lightweight online efficiency with richer semantics and supports relocalization after scene changes. Targets long-term autonomy in real-world settings.

entry.title: TEAR: Task-Evidence Authority Routing for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Shicheng Zhang, Hui Liu, Haoliang Li

entry.summary: TEAR formulates shared-control robotics as an online control authority routing problem, deciding when human teleoperation versus local autonomy should hold authority during field-deployed manipulation. It exploits the complementary reliability profiles of humans (strong in contact-rich, ambiguous situations) and autonomy (no communication dependency). This is relevant to reliable real-world deployment of robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Consistent Distributed Invariant EKF SLAM with Point and Object Features

author.name: Mengya Xu, Xianjia Yu, Ha Sier, Shoudong Huang, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: Joint-CI is a unified fusion method for distributed right-invariant EKF SLAM that handles point, object, and mixed feature maps using covariance intersection without tracking inter-robot correlations. It resolves the issue that a neighbor's map estimate is expressed in its own error coordinates and entangled with its pose. This advances consistent multi-robot SLAM, a long-standing coordination problem.

entry.title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing

author.name: Jian Hou, Xin Zhou, Adam J. Spiers

entry.summary: VecTile is a low-cost, 6 mm-thin flexible tactile array measuring three-axis forces including shear, using a piezoresistive layer with passive silicone nubs that convert shear into distinguishable pressure patterns. A 4x4 array costs under 35 USD and can be fabricated without specialized equipment, validated with finite element analysis. Accessible shear sensing could democratize tactile research.

entry.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination

author.name: Shashank A. Deshpande, Blake T. Edwards, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: The authors extend a single-robot tree-search control framework to decentralized, real-time multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems, approximating the joint optimal solution in an anytime fashion. The approach bridges the usual gap between centralized joint-optimal offline planners and fast decentralized safe-navigation methods.

entry.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations

author.name: Chenglong Wang, Yuwei Xiao, Alper Sarikaya, Michel Galley, Chris Quirk, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Microsoft Research introduces Flint-interactive, a language and compiler that lets users and AI agents define interactive visualization behaviors via high-level semantic events and update operators rather than low-level code. The system supports connected experiences across charts, text, tables, and applications, targeting AI-generated exploratory data stories.

entry.title: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning

author.name: Firuz Kamalov, Hana Sulieman, Ahmed El Sayed, Sivaraj R., Nitesh Sughnani

entry.summary: Formalizes algorithmic drift in adaptive learning systems as a coupled learner-tutor dynamical system in which small, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound into systemic inequities over time. The theory is corroborated with agent-based Monte Carlo simulations using IRT-based curriculum policies driven by either an online tracker or an LSTM knowledge-tracing network.

entry.title: Subgoal-aware Memory Graph for GUI Agent

author.name: Dezhao Luo, Daniel Beechey, Derek Yuen, Weilin Luo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a subgoal-aware memory graph for mobile GUI agents that distills past trajectories into structured, reusable evidence at intermediate subgoal granularity, avoiding the over-fineness of single-action memories and the over-coarseness of full trajectories. This enables better experience reuse in long-horizon task automation. It addresses a concrete limitation of existing memory-based GUI agent methods.

entry.title: Generalizing Metropolis-Hastings for DAG Sampling

author.name: Daniele Nikzad, Mikko Koivisto

entry.summary: The paper introduces duet sampling, a generalization of Metropolis-Hastings that selects two proposal distributions per iteration (one for proposing, one for evaluating the reverse move), enabling novel MCMC moves that resample parents for multiple DAG nodes simultaneously. This advances posterior approximation for Bayesian network structure learning on large, high-dimensional datasets.

entry.title: Separate Field Scoring Protects Unused Tools When Agents Pool Tool-Use Experience

author.name: Abhijit Chakraborty

entry.summary: This single-author study measures how pooling tool-usage examples among agents affects tool retrieval, finding that indexing usage as entries for used tools boosts their retrieval but degrades retrieval of never-used held-out tools. The proposed SYNAPSE method scores usage in its own field, preserving gains while limiting harm to unused tools, evaluated on StableToolBench.

entry.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Tool-Augmented Model Comparisons

author.name: Mateusz Modrzejewski, Tomasz Radzikowski

entry.summary: The authors test whether giving language models tools makes benchmark comparisons more stable across question rewordings, using a matched protocol that separates answer readout, reasoning, call decision, tool answer, and call-free reporting. Across six open models, five domains, and five wordings, tools raise accuracy when a program can answer the question but widen the wording sensitivity of many pairwise comparisons. This challenges the assumption that tool augmentation yields more robust model rankings.

entry.title: MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models

author.name: Khaled Waleed Dawoud, Muhammad Zaigham Zaheer, Khan Muhammad, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: MoG-VLM accelerates VLM-based video anomaly detection by using motion as a lightweight control signal deciding when VLM inference is necessary, introducing Temporal Gradient Magnitude for content-aware sampling and a hierarchical dual-stream design. This avoids the wasted computation of uniform sampling and enables near-real-time deployment. It matters for making powerful VLMs practical in video surveillance workloads.

entry.title: An Agent Architecture with Tools and Memory for Selective Correction of Wrist PPG Heart Rate Estimates

author.name: Xu Wang, Shuhan Yi, Zhen Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes an agent architecture with tools and memory wrapped around a fixed PPG heart-rate estimator, where candidate corrections are generated from pulse, motion, and historical evidence and gated by an independent risk mechanism that decides to retain, correct, or reject each output. Across four public datasets with frozen weights, macro-averaged MAE dropped by up to 44.5 percent.

entry.title: Local Discrimination of Binary Classifiers via Localized AUC Functional

author.name: Wenye Ren, Anna Gy\H{o}rffy-Kerekes, Tancredi Dorsi, Olga Demler

entry.summary: The authors introduce Localized AUC (LAUC), a weighted AUC variant, and LOCATOR, a method that identifies patient cohorts for whom a clinical risk prediction model is inaccurate. The approach includes statistical foundations and validation on real-world data and simulations, addressing the blindness of global AUC to performance heterogeneity.

entry.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation

author.name: Luoxi Wang, Alessio Quercia, Hanno Scharr, Arya Bangun

entry.summary: SciFusion is a latent-diffusion framework for unified 3D scientific image generation that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations, sharing factors across modalities for knowledge transfer. This enables synthesizing unseen domain-object-contrast compositions at inference time.

entry.title: Nonparametric autoregressive estimation of probability distributions with parallel gradient boosting

author.name: R\'emy Chapelle (CB, EVDG, CESP)

entry.summary: Studies estimation of joint distributions by factorizing them autoregressively via conditional distribution estimators, showing that for subadditive losses, convergence rates of the autoregressive estimator follow from those of conditional estimators. It instantiates this with parallel gradient boosting, offering a practical nonparametric alternative to neural density models.

entry.title: IndoNutriQA: An Indonesian Clinical Nutrition Question Answering Benchmark

author.name: Tirana Noor Fatyanosa, Ummu Ditya Erliana, Mahendra Data, Muhammad Nurwegiono, Eleazar Tadeo Eman, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: IndoNutriQA is an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs from real clinical-nutrition reports, structured around eight standardized Nutrition Care Process question types and enriched with metadata such as diagnoses and document provenance. It is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource rather than a training corpus. It fills a gap for clinical QA in low-resource languages.

entry.title: Finitely Verifiable Segmentation: Decidability for Every Tokenizer with a Finite-State Verifier

author.name: Nicklas Nidh\"ogg

entry.summary: The paper introduces finitely verifiable segmentation policies for tokenizers, where a finite automaton over marked strings accepts exactly the policy's own segmentations. It proves that several practically relevant questions, such as whether a window certifies a token boundary, whether boundary gaps are bounded, whether masks keep generation completable, and whether two policies are equivalent, become decidable under this hypothesis, connecting to classical automata theory.

entry.title: Latent Space Jam: Layout Guided Video Synthesis

author.name: Asaf Joseph, Moshe Mandel, Ohad Fried

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free method for controlling object layout and motion in pretrained video diffusion models using coarse layouts. It runs two passes: prompt-guided cross-attention steers spatiotemporal placement into a coarse visual guide, which then conditions the same model to produce a layout-consistent, temporally coherent video. This avoids the cost of fine-tuning or architectural changes for controllable video generation.

entry.title: ResGVC: Residual Coding for High-fidelity Generative Video Compression

author.name: Ding Ding, Daowen Li, Ying Chen, Kai Li

entry.summary: ResGVC improves generative video compression by transmitting residual signals that guide decoder-side diffusion denoising toward original pictures. Distortion between a learned codec reconstruction and the source is decomposed into residual segments compressed by a novel codec with a distortion-adaptive rate allocation.

entry.title: Moving Regions, Not Moving Objects: Segmenting What Actually Moves under Camera Motion

author.name: Wenhua Jin, Tiancheng Chen, Sheng Tang, Jiahao Li, Yupeng Liu, Weiqi Zhang, Juntong Fang, Zesong Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that motion is not an intrinsic property of an object instance and reformulates moving object segmentation to localize the regions that actually move rather than labeling whole instances. This addresses artifacts of instance-level proposals that produce masks even when nothing in the instance moves, especially under camera motion.

entry.title: Motion Retargeting with Spatiotemporal Preferences for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xiongbo Shi, Shihang Du, Zongyou Yu, Ao Zhou, Xudong Zhang, Ziyu Lin, Haodong Zhang, Junqiao Zhao, Guang Chen

entry.summary: STR allocates retargeting optimization effort non-uniformly across keyframes and key body parts, with a vision-language model selecting relevant motion signals and keyframes identified from changes in body-object relations. This improves accuracy at critical stages of humanoid loco-manipulation while increasing computational efficiency. It addresses the embodiment gap between human demonstrations and humanoids.

entry.title: Causal Analysis of Failures of Cyber-Physical Systems with Continuous Inputs

author.name: Tom Yaacov, David A. Kelly, Khen Elimelech, Hana Chockler

entry.summary: The paper extends the actual causality framework for explaining CPS failures to continuous inputs by introducing a notion of distance, overcoming the limitations of prior discrete binary causal models. This enables principled failure analysis for black-box systems like self-driving cars where pre-deployment verification is impossible. Bridges formal methods and safety analysis of autonomous systems.

entry.title: TRACE: Traversability-aware Reactive Navigation via VLM-driven Adaptive Constraints Estimation

author.name: Mario A. V. Saucedo, Midhun Edatharam Kunnath, Elias Small, Akash Patel, Shruti Kotpalliwar, Christoforos Kanellakis, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: TRACE combines vision-language-model confidence maps from positive and negative language prompts, fused evidentially, into dense traversability maps for ground robots in unstructured forests. Extracted path boundaries become soft constraints in a nonlinear model predictive control formulation. It demonstrates a practical pipeline from foundation-model perception to reactive robot control.

entry.title: Contestable Agents for Data Governance: Recording Human Stewardship of AI-Generated Metadata Across Structured and Unstructured Systems

author.name: Humza Akhtar, Brian Freeman

entry.summary: The paper presents contestable governance for LLM-based metadata agents in industrial organizations: specialist agents produce scored, cited arguments for disputed metadata decisions, and human reviewers' stewardship is recorded explicitly rather than as perfunctory approvals. This prevents unreviewed agent proposals from propagating errors into downstream systems. It targets accountability in enterprise data governance.

entry.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering

author.name: Aman Behera, Namit Solanki, Mehul Anand

entry.summary: This paper compares position bias in long-context question answering across Transformer, state-space, and hybrid Mamba architectures by moving a gold document among nine distractors. Evaluated Transformers show a beginning advantage absent in state-space models, while both families favor end-position evidence; some effects remain statistically uncertain. The findings suggest architecture choice affects how models use mid-context evidence.

entry.title: RecallGS: Geometry-Grounded Recall for Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Thanh-Khoi Nguyen, Thien-Phuc Tran, Minh-Triet Tran

entry.summary: RecallGS is a training-free mechanism for online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting that retrieves geometric-semantic evidence from the agent's own observation history via CLIP rather than learning an additional 3D network, following a recall-ground-fuse pipeline. This reduces training and runtime overhead for open-vocabulary scene understanding from streaming observations. The insight that the needed prior already exists in past observations is the core contribution.

entry.title: Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure

author.name: Pellegrino Casoria, Simon Pietro Romano

entry.summary: Social-HUMINT quantifies social-media exposure by measuring how accurately a target can be profiled from unstructured content via LLMs, and how far that profile enables social engineering attacks, unifying SOCMINT and Cyber Human Intelligence frameworks. It reframes exposure as what can be inferred rather than what is posted. The framework provides a shared basis for assessing and mitigating LLM-enabled profiling risks.

entry.title: Memory-Augmented Online Test-Time Adaptation for EEG Motor Imagery via Perturbation Consistency and Confidence Calibration

author.name: Kunkun Zhang, Kehao Wu, Zhitao Chen, Haigen Hu, Qianwei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes MOPC, a source-free online test-time adaptation framework for EEG brain-computer interfaces that uses memory augmentation, perturbation consistency, and confidence calibration to handle cross-subject distribution shifts in real time. It avoids the offline source or aggregated target data access required by prior adaptation methods.

entry.title: One Pretrained Decision Model Is Enough for Training-Free Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Qingyun Sun, Ziwei Zhang, Tianchen Zhu, Daqing Li, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: Jev-GAD is a training-free graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence (structural, attribute, neighborhood) with a pretrained decision mechanism, enabling generalist detection across graphs without task-specific optimization. It converts statistical scores into semantically interpretable evidence for a decision model.

entry.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset

author.name: Yen-Ku Liu, Hongjie Chen, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan Rossi

entry.summary: The paper studies how well proposed time-series dataset similarity metrics correlate with downstream forecasting error in out-of-distribution and transfer settings, and proposes DISC, a Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost summarizing transfer-related relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation. It aims to guide source selection before model adaptation.

entry.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders

author.name: Aakash Saini, Jafar Aco Mohammadi, Wolfgang Gerstacker

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard gradient-based attacks on neural 5G receivers with unrolled LDPC decoders fail to beat matched Gaussian perturbations due to gradient masking from tanh saturation in belief-propagation check-node updates. The authors propose two loss functions that restore attack effectiveness, clarifying the true robustness of these receivers.

entry.title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters

author.name: Tardelli Ronan Coelho Stekel

entry.summary: Empirically studies whether small encoders used for closed-set decisions (such as tool selection) should read options jointly or score each option separately, across scales from 17M to 1B parameters. At 32M parameters, per-option scoring beats joint scoring by 5.8 points of chance-corrected skill at matched optimizer steps, and the advantage depends on reranker-style initialization whose query-candidate input format matches per-option scoring. The work offers practical guidance for replacing slow, order-sensitive LLM prompting with compact encoders.

entry.title: Interpretive Variation and Discourse Structure in Detecting Enthymemes in Controversial Political Discourse

author.name: Martial Pastor, Nelleke Oostdijk

entry.summary: This paper studies enthymeme detection (arguments with unstated premises or conclusions) in tweets about vaccination and immigration, where annotator disagreement is intrinsic. Fine-tuned models plateau around F1 0.67 regardless of data or features, prompting the authors to propose distribution-aware evaluation metrics and a model that directly predicts the annotator vote distribution. It highlights how inherent label ambiguity limits standard evaluation.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models to a Low-Resource Agglutinative Language: A Corpus, Datasets, and a Reproducible Benchmark for the Bashkir Language

author.name: Mullosharaf K. Arabov, Svetlana S. Khaybullina

entry.summary: This paper releases a Bashkir web corpus (46.9M tokens), three classification datasets, and a systematic benchmark of adaptation methods spanning eight architectures and full fine-tuning, QLoRA, in-context learning, and continual pretraining. QLoRA on 3.8-8B decoder models outperforms encoder-only fine-tuning on binary classification. It provides the first reproducible adaptation baseline suite for Bashkir.

entry.title: Tracing Hallucinations in LLM Reasoning for UML Class Diagram Generation: An Empirical Taxonomy and Mitigation Study

author.name: Mojdeh Rahmanian, Foutse Khomh, Ashkan Sami, Yanchao Yu

entry.summary: Using 60 manually annotated DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces, this paper develops a taxonomy of eleven hallucination sub-types across prompt faithfulness, code faithfulness, and reasoning quality for LLM-generated UML class diagrams, then applies it to characterize where hallucinations arise in intermediate reasoning rather than only final outputs. It also explores mitigations informed by the taxonomy.

entry.title: VisCurate: Evaluating Behavioral Equivalence of Visual Skills

author.name: Md Farhan Ishraq, Md Farhan Ishmam, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Md Hasanul Kabir

entry.summary: VisCurate is a framework and benchmark for curating libraries of executable visual skills (image-to-image operations) based on observed execution behavior rather than names, descriptions, or code. It runs skill pairs on shared probe batteries and assigns one of six behavioral relations tied to safe library edits, including tests against seven injected defect types. This addresses growing redundancy and defect accumulation in skill-based vision agents.

entry.title: WovenAnchor Matcher: Specialized Intra- and Inter-Image Context Modeling for Feature Matching

author.name: Zhiyang Li, Ruijiang Jin, Thibaut Klenke, Yusuke Sekikawa, Nakamasa Inoue

entry.summary: WAM is a semi-dense feature matching framework with role-specialized context aggregation: WovenMamba performs intra-image aggregation via horizontal-then-vertical state-space propagation preserving 2D structure, while a complementary operator gathers plausible cross-image correspondences while limiting noise. This separates the distinct roles of intra- and inter-image context modeling in coarse-to-fine correspondence estimation. The design improves matching quality over prior uniform aggregation.

entry.title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes

author.name: Shuhuan Wang, Yuanyuan Cui, Pengju Wang, Huimin Guo, Ling Yue, Yin Gu, Yanchao Zhang, Wei Feng, Yunhe Liu, Wei Qian, Mingjun Xu, Shuang Liu, He Ma

entry.summary: DPIF is a plug-and-play dual-path framework for multi-view medical image segmentation that works with arbitrary encoder-decoder networks and unpaired samples, using Sinkhorn optimal transport for cross-view distribution alignment to reduce annotation requirements. It targets the severe performance drop of segmentation models in small-sample clinical settings.

entry.title: GLOW-FM: Efficient Generative Low-Light Image Enhancement with One-Step Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Ariel Lapid, Yuval Haitman, Reuven Peretz, Arnon Netzer, Idit Diamant

entry.summary: GLOW-FM performs low-light image enhancement with a single function evaluation using one-step latent flow matching in the latent space of a frozen Tiny-VAE. It aims to match the perceptual quality of diffusion-based enhancement while drastically reducing sampling cost.

entry.title: Revisiting Distribution Matching for State-to-Vision Policy Distillation in Laparoscopic Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mingyu Sheng, Jianan Fan, Dongnan Liu, Guoyan Zheng, Ron Kikinis, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: This work distills privileged state-based RL policies into vision-based policies for laparoscopic surgical manipulation, revisiting distribution matching as the distillation objective. It avoids unreliable explicit state estimation in surgical settings while retaining the sample efficiency of state-based training. Relevant to bringing learned control into real surgical robotics.

entry.title: Multimodal Progress-Residual Fusion for Anticipating Navigation Retreat in Robotic Flexible Endoscopy

author.name: Chi Kit Ng, Tianchun Wu, Jiatan Sun, Yuming Sun, Jianru Zhang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: MPRF is a causal multimodal model that anticipates operator retreat decisions in flexible robotic endoscopy by fusing motor commands, electromagnetic tracking residuals, and endoscopic video. A nominal-progress model predicts expected distal response, and residuals feed a temporal predictor. Validated over a 150-episode colon study, this could enable earlier failure recovery in medical robotics.

entry.title: Better Reasoning, Not Just Bigger Models: A Structure-Grounded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Inference

author.name: Amirhossein Aghaei, Liangyan Li, Shiyi Yang, Shaohua Wang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: SGUR is a training-free framework that complements token-level generation with active uncertainty reduction over structured hypothesis spaces: incomplete observations are represented as query graphs aligned with candidate hypothesis graphs via prior-weighted partial graph matching, with database-derived empirical priors emphasizing decision-relevant structure. It targets reliable multi-turn agentic inference under incomplete observations.

entry.title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications

author.name: Leming Shen, Qiang Yang, Xinyu Huang, Zijing Ma, Yuanqing Zheng

entry.summary: AgentDP automates optimization and adaptation of pre-trained AI models for heterogeneous embedded devices using LLM agents, reducing manual effort while improving inference efficacy by injecting device-specific domain knowledge. It tackles three challenges: user requirement standardization, operator-aware model partitioning to bridge environment mismatch, and related robustness mechanisms. The system targets fully automated end-to-end deployment.

entry.title: Evaluating Artificial Wisdom (AW): A Trajectory-Based Framework for Context-Sensitive Decision Regulation

author.name: Md. Jalil Piran

entry.summary: Proposes a trajectory-based measurement framework and validation protocol for artificial wisdom, defined behaviorally as context-sensitive regulation of judgment, with seven stage-level criteria plus transition components assessing material-update adequacy and commitment-preserving stability. It aims to measure whether LLM recommendations remain appropriate as decision conditions change.

entry.title: Can AI Co-Design Structures? An AI Agent for Early-Stage Structural Design

author.name: Ricardo Maia Avelino, Mennatallah El-Assady, Tom Van Mele, Philippe Block

entry.summary: Introduces a proof-of-concept prompt-to-structure workflow in which an AI agent connected via a Model Context Protocol server to a COMPAS-based structural modeling API translates design intent into graph-based structural models. This moves beyond generic text-to-3D by enforcing domain-specific geometry and semantically rich structural data types.

entry.title: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents

author.name: Ping-Lin Kuo, Suman Navaratnarajah, Christian Frey, Gresa Shala, Josif Grabocka

entry.summary: MUFFIN proposes an asynchronous multi-agent coordination protocol based on a shared memory buffer, replacing synchronous turn-taking and debate-style information exchange. It targets the problem that failures in multi-agent systems often stem from ineffective inter-agent information exchange. The system-level protocol design could improve coordination in target-driven agentic reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery

author.name: Dingxuan Zhang, Yanhui Jiang, Jun Wang, Hefeng Zhou

entry.summary: This paper treats skill granularity in coding agents as a runtime action-abstraction policy, choosing among primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery. A feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state machine govern this selection conditioned on task structure and execution state. It adds a runtime control dimension to the skill libraries literature.

entry.title: Externalise the Memory: A Pre-Registered Study of Where an Embodied Agent's Experience Should Live

author.name: Cheng-Yin Tu

entry.summary: This pre-registered study compares whether an embodied agent's experience should be baked into policy weights or stored externally and retrieved: a memory-augmented VLM teacher produces trajectories on a vision-conditioned reach task, from which LoRA student policies are distilled and evaluated under matched protocols. The registered primary test proves underpowered, with distilling memory-augmented behavior beating an action-only control by only a non-significant 1 percentage point.

entry.title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective

author.name: Haotian Zheng, Zhanwei Wang, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes Mixture-of-Experts LLM inference in proposed space data centers, where skewed expert activation conflicts with uniform solar power in sun-synchronous orbit, and proposes SpaceWPT, a framework using inter-satellite laser wireless power transfer to rebalance energy. The work connects MoE inference scheduling with orbital power constraints.

entry.title: GateFormer: Forecast-Space Decomposition for Intra-Hour Solar Irradiance Prediction from Sky Images

author.name: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Jonathon Hare, Tasmiat Rahman

entry.summary: GateFormer is a GHI-conditioned dual-decoder ViT for intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting from sky images, embedding observed irradiance into the visual token stream and decomposing prediction into a trajectory head and a delta head for different short-term regimes. It targets grid dispatch and storage control that depend on anticipating rapid solar variability.

entry.title: MQAScore: Fine-Grained Text-Music Alignment Evaluation via Large Audio Language Model

author.name: Wei-Jaw Lee, Chun-Ping Wang, Xuanjun Chen, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: MQAScore replaces global embedding-similarity evaluation of text-to-music alignment with fine-grained verification of atomic musical concepts across five dimensions (genre, instrument, mood/theme, vocal, usage), using an audio-language model's probability of affirmative answers. It introduces verification labels from presence/absence annotations plus LLM-guided concept substitutions and a Sensitivity-Invariance Ratio metric for evaluator reliability. This gives the music-generation community a more diagnostic evaluation tool.

entry.title: CoWriter: Guiding Methodological and Synergetic Human-LLM Co-Authoring

author.name: Shmuel Amar, Benjamin Lieber, Ori Shapira, Debanjana Kar, Sebastian Maximilian Dennerlein, Yufang Hou, Ido Dagan

entry.summary: CoWriter is a proactive agentic writing system that adapts expert human co-authoring methodologies from cognitive science to steer the entire long-form, source-grounded writing workflow while keeping the human actively engaged, rather than reducing users to passive supervision of chat output. An exploratory user study found authors using CoWriter better expressed their personal perspective than with a standard LLM baseline. It addresses review fatigue and over-reliance in human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: Automating Feature Flag Cleanup at Scale with Multi-Agent LLM Systems: An Industrial Experience at DoorDash

author.name: Atharv Chandratre, Jai Datar

entry.summary: DoorDash engineers describe an end-to-end LLM-based multi-agent system for cleaning up stale feature flags across 623 repositories and over 56,000 flags, integrating live rollout data via MCP, Jira processing, and automated pull request creation. Rule-based tooling proved insufficient at their scale, with an estimated one to two hours of manual effort per cleanup. This is a valuable industrial case study of practical agentic software engineering deployment.

entry.title: Benchmarking Model Compression Techniques Across Heterogeneous Edge Platforms: A Predictive Maintenance Use Case for Rotating Machinery

author.name: Matheus Calheira Guimar\~aes de Oliveira, Marco Aur\'elio da Silva Cruz, Regis Cardoso, Lucas Cambuim, Rafael Macieira, Arthur Paim, Helaine Neves, Alex Santos, Lilian Guarieiro, Jean Schmith, Prashant Kumar, Erick G. Sperandio Nascimento

entry.summary: Provides a comparative analysis of four state-of-the-art model compression techniques for deploying deep learning on heterogeneous industrial edge hardware, using predictive maintenance of rotating machinery as the use case. The goal is to give practitioners clear guidance on which compression methods are practical under real hardware constraints for Industry 5.0 settings.

entry.title: Stability Analysis of Signed Graphs under Structural Perturbations

author.name: Ning Zhang, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Studies the stability of signed graph filters under edge additions, deletions, and sign flips, extending prior stability work limited to unsigned graphs. The analysis shows how signed perturbations and node feature correlations jointly affect learned representations, and yields a theory-guided perturbation strategy for data augmentation.

entry.title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra

author.name: Jihwan Kim, Jaeseong Heo, Yujin Kim, Sang Bin Yoon, Chanjoong Kim, Kwang-Im Oh, Hyon Bin Na, Kyungwon Kwak, Myeongkee Park, Joonyoung F. Joung

entry.summary: This paper replaces fixed-grid spectral inputs with intensity-wavenumber pairs, computing Transformer positional encodings from the physical wavenumber coordinate. The representation improves robustness to noise, sparser sampling, and partial coverage across convolutional, residual, and Transformer architectures on bacterial Raman spectra.

entry.title: Towards Field-Deployable Wearable IMU Systems for Occupational Activity Recognition

author.name: Ihsan Ul Haq (Centre for Computational Science and Mathematical Modelling, Coventry University, United Kingdom, School of Architecture and Built Environment Deakin University, Australia), James Brusey (Centre for Computational Science and Mathematical Modelling, Coventry University, United Kingdom), Farnad Nasirzadeh (School of Architecture and Built Environment Deakin University, Australia), Chandan Karmakar (School of Information Technology Deakin University, Australia)

entry.summary: This study performs a systematic configuration sensitivity analysis of the VTT-ConIoT benchmark for construction worker activity recognition under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, spanning classifiers, sensor placements, window sizes, calibration, and augmentation. It reveals that headline accuracies above 95% often mask substantial per-individual variance relevant to real deployment.

entry.title: Piano2Pop: Expanding Piano Demos into Pop Productions Without Aligned Supervision

author.name: Yun-Chen Cheng, Chih-Pin Tan, Tzu-Hung Huang, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: Piano2Pop transforms piano MIDI into full pop productions using a flow-matching model conditioned on piano rolls, trained with pseudo-supervision from synthetic piano-instrumental pairs instead of aligned piano-pop data. Evaluation on 476 real-world pairs shows a pair-supervised pseudo-demo approach outperforms pair-free transcription variants on audio fidelity metrics.

entry.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining

author.name: Houssam Eddine Boukhalfa, Mourad Bouache, Mourad Dahmane

entry.summary: AQL-Lite adapts a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic through a quality-first data curation pipeline plus a partial-parameter continual pretraining recipe using RS-LoRA adapters, the last eight blocks, and embeddings with layer-wise learning rates. At a matched 1B-token budget it improves a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over baselines.

entry.title: Equilibria and Learning in Competitive Market Making

author.name: Matteo Onger, Luigi Foscari

entry.summary: Analyzes a market-making game among multiple strategic market makers and a non-strategic trader, proving that pure-strategy Nash equilibria exist under minimal assumptions and that equilibrium bid-ask spreads widen strictly with asset volatility. The paper then discretizes prices and shows convergence results for no-internal-regret learning dynamics. This tackles a setting where non-convex, discontinuous payoffs rule out classical existence arguments.

entry.title: Track finding and particle identification performance with particle physics foundation models

author.name: Shuhang Li, Haiwang Yu, Gabor Galgoczi, Yeonju Go, Yi Huang, David Park, Michael Peters, Christof Roland, Jin Huang, Yihui Ren, Joseph D. Osborn

entry.summary: Evaluates particle physics foundation models on charged-particle track finding and particle identification using Time Projection Chamber spacepoint data, assessing whether foundation-model-based reconstruction can match specialized pattern-recognition pipelines. The study shows competitive performance on downstream reconstruction tasks in high energy physics experiments. This informs the applicability of general foundation models to large sparse scientific datasets.

entry.title: Direct cueing of word identity through word duration: evidence from Mandarin homophones

author.name: Xiaomeng Zhu, Megan Niu, Jason Shaw, Kevin Tang

entry.summary: This psycholinguistics study uses a homophone ordering task in Mandarin Chinese to test whether word duration differences between high- and low-frequency words are functionally used in spoken word recognition. Participants could exploit duration cues to identify homophone pairs, supporting the view that the mental lexicon stores fine phonetic detail. The work matters for theories of lexical representation and has implications for speech technology.

entry.title: A Systematic Comparison of Search Space Complexity and Efficiency for Time-Synchronous End-to-End ASR Models

author.name: Simon Berger, Larissa Kleppel, Ralf Schl\"uter

entry.summary: This paper provides a comparative analysis of search space complexity and pruning efficiency for CTC and neural transducer ASR models under different pruning strategies and language model configurations. It shows these end-to-end models usually operate in small search spaces but exhibit large temporary hypothesis-count peaks during uncertain segments. The analysis informs beam-search design for modern E2E ASR.

entry.title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries

author.name: Bayram Ayadi, Florian Geissler, Johanna Schmidhuber

entry.summary: This work investigates LLM-generated health summaries for menstrual health monitoring, introducing a constrained generation framework combining structured evidence conditioning with retrieval-augmented generation to reduce semantic drift when translating clinical records into patient-readable narratives. It evaluates semantic alignment of the generated summaries against the source clinical data.

entry.title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation

author.name: Guantian Zheng, Shan Jin

entry.summary: MoRE addresses articulated 3D object generation from a single image by encoding joint lines with axis classification and Plucker moment coefficients, eliminating arbitrary origin choices along the axis. It regularizes the encoding by comparing decoded joint-driven anchor motions against annotated joint motions via a differentiable expectation. This improves the preservation of articulation mechanisms in generated 3D objects.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning

author.name: Shiming Chen, Shuhuang Chen, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan

entry.summary: DoP (Domain Prompt Learning) enables zero-shot domain generalization by learning target-domain prompts with a vision-language model like CLIP, recognizing unseen classes in unseen domains without access to source-domain data. This departs from standard DG methods that require collecting and annotating multi-source datasets. The approach improves practical applicability of domain generalization in data-scarce settings.

entry.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Jiarui Guo, Haojia Wei, Yifei Liu, Yifan Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Zhihang Zhong

entry.summary: FilmFlow is an agentic framework converting natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. A Director agent composes high-level motions from atomic translation, rotation, and framing operations, supported by an Interpreter for intent extraction, a Scout for initial viewpoints, and a Critic for rendered-result evaluation. The system aims to make cinematographic intent executable and controllable.

entry.title: RankAlign: Vision-Language Representation Alignment via Rank Transformation

author.name: Enzhe Zhao, Marco Fiorucci, Lamberto Ballan

entry.summary: RankAlign addresses unpaired vision-language matching under the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by transforming within-modality similarity kernels into ordinal (rank-based) representations before permutation matching. This handles the case where the same semantic structure is parameterized numerically differently across modalities.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Online Textual Memory for Episodic Memory Video Question Answering

author.name: Raffaele Cali, Giuseppe Lando, Rosario Forte, Antonino Furnari

entry.summary: Systematically studies retrieval design choices (retrieval units, query formulations, context budgets, reranking) for question answering over long egocentric videos compressed into textual memory. It isolates retrieval as the key variable and identifies a best-performing configuration on QAEgo4D-Closed.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI

author.name: Claudia Giardina, Montse Pard\`as, Ver\'onica Vilaplana

entry.summary: Presents a conditional 3D diffusion framework for anatomy-conditioned synthesis of complete prostate biparametric MRI from anatomical masks, supporting both sequential and joint modality synthesis. Trained on PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate, and PROSTATEx, it addresses dataset scarcity for prostate deep learning applications.

entry.title: Bound-Conditioned Latent Inference for Progressive Image Compression

author.name: Jaeseok Jang, Seungmin Jeon, Kwang Pyo Choi, Chang-Su Kim

entry.summary: BLI reformulates progressive trit-plane image coding as sequential latent inference under shrinking interval constraints, exploiting decoded trits as bounds on continuous latents rather than mere discrete symbols. Combining bound centers and widths with hyperprior information improves rate-distortion performance in progressive decoding. It is a principled reframing for learned image compression codecs.

entry.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives

author.name: Jingyi Xiang, Yixuan Wang, Wenzhen Yuan

entry.summary: A review tracing tactile manipulation research from mechanics-driven approaches that interpret signals through contact mechanics to modern data-driven methods that learn representations and policies directly. It covers tactile sensing fundamentals and bridges the two perspectives. A timely synthesis as tactile sensing becomes central to dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Co^2Gen: Collaboratively Generating Task Plans for Decentralized Multi-Robot and Human Collaboration

author.name: Yi Loo, Siddhant Shrivastava, Minh Long Pham, Malika Meghjani

entry.summary: The framework automates generation of multi-robot collaborative demonstration data for decentralized VLA training without human teleoperation, using decentralized collaborative planning to produce executable plans and corresponding demonstrations. This addresses the underexplored question of teaching VLA models to collaborate with other robots and humans. Could reduce the data bottleneck for multi-agent VLA training.

entry.title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation

author.name: Sang-Hun Han, Changyeon Won, JunGyu Lee, Min-Gyu Park, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: IORA is a support-aware grasp synthesis framework enabling low-DoF coupled hands to immobilize irregular objects by using support surfaces as active contact forces rather than mere geometric constraints. It represents hand and object surfaces as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings. This extends dexterous grasp synthesis to constrained, low-actuation hardware.

entry.title: Whole-Body Motion Guided Reference Generation for Uncertainty-Aware Compliant Assistance

author.name: Muyuan Ma, Long Cheng, Lijun Han, Haotian Zhai, Xinpan Meng, Xiuze Xia, Houcheng Li, Zeyu Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes a dual-loop exoskeleton assistance strategy coupling diffusion-based trajectory generation from whole-body human motion with variable admittance control, where trajectory variance provides uncertainty awareness. A three-stage training pipeline reduces cross-modal representation mismatch. It addresses the variability of human motion patterns in personalized physical assistance.

entry.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures

author.name: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: This theory paper derives accelerated, Nesterov-style damped Hamiltonian dynamics on Wasserstein and related density spaces to construct new attention blocks interpreted as interacting particle systems. It develops the geometric and differential calculus (including a quotient Stein geometry) needed to make these inertial attention variants rigorous.

entry.title: Opening up Attention: A QK Transcoder Dashboard for Feature Pairs

author.name: nuppal

entry.summary: The post introduces a query-key transcoder based on bilinear sparse dictionary learning applied to multi-head attention in GPT-2 small, plus an interactive dashboard for investigating monosemantic features in attention across all layers and heads. It aims to fill the gap in feature visualization tooling for the attention mechanism.

entry.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Jianle Gan, Zhuoyan Feng, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Jev-DLC studies how typed user feedback (accepting a decision or revoking it for an alternative) can persist across requests as decision-level continual learning. Corrections are stored as action identities and directed preference relations in bounded channels above a frozen scorer, with no raw interaction history retained. It addresses post-deployment preference adaptation efficiently.

entry.title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions

author.name: Miguel Mochizuki Silva, Samuel Ismael, Mateus C. Dias, Tha\'is Gaud\^encio, Yuri Malheiros, Barufaldi

entry.summary: This clinical RAG study over breast lesion management literature describes an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol that maps relevance to evidence spans across all containing chunks, addressing how annotation coverage distorts retrieval scores. It evaluates dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking across chunk sizes and configurations using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG. The protocol offers a template for more honest retrieval evaluation in medical RAG systems.

entry.title: X-pressing Intimacy: Mental Health Disclosure After Twitter Acquisition

author.name: Olivia Pal, Yunhao Yuan, Meghana Mandava, Talayeh Aledavood, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Analyzing roughly 824K tweets about anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, BPD, and suicidal ideation around Elon Musk's October 2022 Twitter acquisition, this study uses LIWC and an LLM-based intimacy classifier to track changes in psycholinguistic expression and disclosure intimacy. It finds declines in affective and social dimensions of mental health disclosure following the platform governance shift.

entry.title: KinoUAV: A Benchmark for Safe and Stable UAV Vision-Language Navigation with Kinodynamic Modeling

author.name: Chenyao Yang, Peijin Wang, Yingchao Feng, Wenhui Diao

entry.summary: KinoUAV introduces a kinodynamic benchmark for UAV vision-language navigation that explicitly incorporates kinodynamic modeling and safety distances into trajectory generation, addressing high yaw rates, collisions, and low success rates in prior work. It includes a hierarchical trajectory generation pipeline driven by acceleration actions and an agent built on it. The benchmark targets safe, stable navigation for remote-sensing UAV applications.

entry.title: Adaptive Aerial Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning via LLM-Assisted Proactive Task Generation

author.name: Jingyu Ru, Xiangyuan Xie, Lixuan Jin, Jian An, Xingming Zhang, Binghao Li, Siyu Wang, Xiang Zhou, Lei Yuan, Hongli Xu, Yang Yu

entry.summary: The work trains adaptive controllers for aerial loco-manipulation, where arm motion disturbs the aerial platform dynamics, using LLM-assisted proactive task generation to broaden the training distribution. Learning-based controllers infer disturbance effects rather than modeling them explicitly. Extends loco-manipulation learning into 3D aerial settings for environments inaccessible to ground robots.

entry.title: Calibration-free IMU-based Relative Orientation Estimation under Dynamic Human Motion

author.name: Ruiyuan Li, Hassan Osman, Ajay Seth, Manon Kok

entry.summary: This paper proposes an extended Kalman filter that jointly estimates relative IMU orientation and sensor location without offline calibration, joint-model assumptions, or global orientation anchors. It explicitly handles high-frequency impacts such as foot strikes and avoids numerical differentiation of noisy signals. This simplifies human motion capture with wearable IMUs for robotics and biomechanics.

entry.title: QuaNAS: Uncertainty-Aware Reuse of Earlier Searches for Query-Efficient Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Brama Seta Putra Satria, Dwi Sunaryono, Misbakhul Munir Irfan Subakti, Irzal Ahmad Sabilla, Laras Suciningtyas

entry.summary: QuaNAS treats libraries of earlier architecture searches as uncertain priors over candidates in a new NAS run, combining learned main effects of design decisions and zero-cost proxies within a Gaussian process that re-estimates trust after each evaluation. It targets query-efficient search when only tens of short training runs are available.

entry.title: How Different, or Different How? Stance Granularity in Viewpoint Selection for Dialog Systems that Engage Users with Alternative Views

author.name: Morita Tarvirdians, Reeve Lorena, Catharine Oertel

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bandit-based viewpoint selection policy for dialog systems that expose users to alternative views, comparing scalar stance scores with Perspectivized Stance Vectors that decompose positions into concept-level stances. In a between-subjects study (N=63), concept-level stance produced more varied exposure sequences and broader coverage of alternative views.

entry.title: GSHeadRelight: Fast Relightability for 3D Gaussian Head Synthesis

author.name: Henglei Lv, Bailin Deng, Jianzhu Guo, Xiaoqiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Di Zhang, Lin Gao

entry.summary: GSHeadRelight addresses relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits using generative 3D Gaussians with a unified neural radiance transfer representation. It avoids reliance on expensive light-stage data and overcomes the poor 3D consistency and slow rendering of generative NeRF approaches. The work targets photorealistic, real-time, generalizable portrait relighting for VR/AR applications.

entry.title: When Stable and Preferred Semantics Agree: A Path-Based Approach

author.name: Yan Zhang, Kehan Liu

entry.summary: A theoretical paper establishing path-based structural criteria under which preferred and stable semantics agree in abstract argumentation frameworks. The general criterion is instantiated via classes of paths and well-foundedness of induced binary relations, strictly generalizing Dung's limited controversiality condition and the SCC-symmetry condition.

entry.title: TwinStore: A Synthetic Consumer Platform Using Vision--Language Models

author.name: Minhyeok Lee

entry.summary: TwinStore is a source-available synthetic consumer platform that turns physical stores into digital twins from floor plans or shelf photos, populated with synthetic shoppers powered by vision-language models who plan trips, navigate aisles, and make purchase decisions against rendered shelves. Every simulated trip yields receipts, enabling pre-deployment testing of layouts, prices, and promotions, with supporting features like layout optimization, shopper interviews, and counterfactual shelf edits. It is a comprehensive retail simulation environment.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model

author.name: Mohammad Talaei, Mohammad Goudarzi, Maille Todd, Vanessa N. L. Wong, Iadine Chad\`es

entry.summary: Evaluates TimesFM, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on sensor telemetry from a semi-arid land-restoration site to forecast soil moisture and temperature across multiple lead times. This avoids the need for hydraulic parameters or per-site training data that conventional physical and data-driven models require.

entry.title: Rethinking Fisher Vectors for Second-order Multi-scale Deep Feature Aggregation in Scalable Scene Retrieval

author.name: Alexy Bhowmick, Sarat Saharia, Shyamanta M. Hazarika

entry.summary: This paper proposes a codebook-free method within the Fisher Kernel framework to encode second-order statistics of multi-scale CNN features for scene image retrieval. Experiments on the INRIA Holidays and UKBench benchmarks show improved retrieval accuracy over prior state of the art with only a small increase in vector dimensionality. It matters because it revives classical feature aggregation methods for modern retrieval pipelines.

entry.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination

author.name: Ziyi Jiao, Heng Zhang, Drishti Regmi, Xiaokang Ye, Lianhui Qin, Peter Yichen Chen

entry.summary: DuoCook is an Overcooked-inspired benchmark in Unreal Engine where a single vision-language model controls two players via top-down observations, testing scene-state tracking, recipe sequencing, and shared-resource allocation under time constraints. It includes 20 maps across five categories with explicit visual cues. It provides a targeted evaluation of multi-agent visual planning and coordination for VLMs.

entry.title: Lighthouse: On Building a Trustworthy Digital Assistant for Exploring History with Civil Rights Archives

author.name: John A. Aydin, Angelica Williams, Steven Dindl, Nathan Saunders, Kate Boyd, Vandana Srivastava, Biplav Srivastava

entry.summary: Lighthouse is a chatbot for exploring US Civil Rights history using South Carolina archival data, built on a neuro-symbolic design that combines an LLM with rule-based symbolic solving to improve trustworthiness and reduce harm from generated answers. The paper emphasizes design principles for reliable content in a sensitive historical domain.

entry.title: Protegrity-PII Technical Report

author.name: Hardeep Bassi, Hui Ma, Lu\'is Seabra, Koowum Joshi, Daniel Pereira, Averell Gatton

entry.summary: This technical report presents Protegrity-PII, a PII detection model for structured and unstructured text achieving 0.915 typed recall and 0.907 precision on a proposed new benchmark, PII-SCOPE. It offers fast, cheap inference (0.49 seconds and $0.0005 per million characters on a single RTX 6000) and strong out-of-distribution generalization attributed to an expansive entity-type taxonomy.

entry.title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images

author.name: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Tasmiat Rahman

entry.summary: This study proposes a dual-framework approach for estimating diffuse horizontal irradiance from sky images in data-scarce regions, integrating calculated atmospheric parameters and cyclic time encodings with ViTs. It aims to replace costly ground-based irradiance instrumentation for photovoltaic optimization where long-term imagery is unavailable.

entry.title: A Grammar of French Civil Cassation: A Ground-Level Dataset and Tool

author.name: Avrile Floro, Tamara Dhorasoo, Nils Holzenberger, Thomas Le Goff, Tiphaine Viard, Maria Boritchev

entry.summary: The paper releases a dataset of 121,536 ground-reasons pairs across 86,464 rulings of the five civil chambers of the French Court of Cassation (2016-2025), pairing each appeal ground with the court's doctrinal answer category via a deterministic pipeline. It yields a descriptive grammar of civil cassation reasoning. This supports legal NLP work and helps lawyers drafting points-of-law appeals in France's final civil court.

entry.title: Predicting Music Valence and Arousal via Textual and Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chi-En Dai, Chih-Pin Tan, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper applies in-context learning with large language models to continuous music emotion prediction, targeting valence, which is hard to model from audio alone due to its subjectivity. Rather than predicting scores directly, the framework uses contextual demonstrations from an auxiliary dataset to refine outputs from a small task-specific base model, comparing text-based ICL (lyrics plus generated audio captions) with a multimodal variant that includes raw audio. Evaluation on the MER60 dataset as a held-out test set provides a clean benchmark for this refinement approach.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Disentangling Decomposition from Typed-State Quality Assurance in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines

author.name: Maria Gabriela Alves Zuppardo, Vinicius Cardoso Garcia

entry.summary: This paper tackles attribution in multi-agent LLM pipelines: whether gains come from typed contracts between agents or from specialized prompts enabled by decomposition. Comparing single-call, two-call unvalidated, and Pydantic-validated typed-state architectures for requirements classification and MoSCoW prioritization across 18 conditions, it quantifies the F1 contribution of each factor. The result clarifies what actually drives multi-agent pipeline benefits.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification

author.name: Sachin Gupta

entry.summary: Evaluates cost-aware abstention for IT support ticket routing, selecting a routing policy on calibration data under explicit misrouting costs and testing it frozen on a public 47,837-ticket corpus. Simple TF-IDF logistic regression with calibrated thresholds reduces test cost by about 38 percent relative and lowers wrong routes compared to zero- and few-shot LLM prompting under the illustrative cost model.

entry.title: Building Presentation Intelligence for High-Quality Slide Generation

author.name: Yuhang Xie, Cheng Li, Chenliang Li, Mingyu Xu, Mingwei Sun, Suhang Zheng, Ming Yan, Xiaoxiao Xu, Lin Qu

entry.summary: This work presents a unified training framework for automatic PowerPoint generation, combining cross-validated data synthesis with difficulty and validity control, teacher enhancement, and verifiable reward optimization. It targets presentation intelligence as an agentic LLM application.

entry.title: XALIGN: A Human-centric Visual Analytics Approach to Understanding AI Explanations

author.name: Bahavathy Kathirgamanathan, Gennady Andrienko, Natalia Andrienko, Tatiana von Landesberger

entry.summary: XALIGN is a visual analytics interface that displays rule-based explanations alongside multiple feature attribution methods (TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, LIME) for the same Random Forest model, making agreement and disagreement between explainers visible. Case studies include the German Credit dataset, letting experts cross-check explanations against domain knowledge.

entry.title: GM-GReFEL: Geometry-Guided Spatiotemporal State-Space Learning for Robust Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition

author.name: Yudhistira Arditya Pratama, Yi-Zeng Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes GM-GReFEL, a spatiotemporal state-space network (Modulated GroupMamba backbone) for dynamic facial expression recognition that achieves linear-cost sequence processing instead of quadratic self-attention, plus a reliability module that weights classifier output using prediction entropy to handle noisy crowdsourced labels. Six channel groups are scanned across spatial and temporal dimensions with a gating mechanism to re-mix them. It targets both efficiency and label-noise robustness.

entry.title: IFC-MCQ: Automatically Generating Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Agents on IFC Data Retrieval

author.name: Rabindra Lamsal, Sisi Zlatanova, Xuesong Shen

entry.summary: Presents IFC-MCQ, a method that automatically generates multiple-choice benchmarks from Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) building data files for exact, cheap grading of LLM agent performance. The taxonomy spans 15 categories and 36 subtypes, with answer keys and distractors derived from the files themselves.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks

author.name: Priyanka, Renaud Delbru, Souhail Bakkali, Micka\"el Coustaty, Antoine Doucet
