Its diagnostic protocol localizes where long-term memory fails in omni-modal assistants: at representation, retrieval, delivery, or reading stages.

entry.title: Actually, All Learnable Distribution Classes Are Privately Learnable

author.name: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Alex Bie, Gautam Kamath, Peihan Liu, Argyris Mouzakis, Vikrant Singhal

entry.summary: The paper proves that every class of distributions learnable up to arbitrarily small total variation error with finitely many samples is also learnable under (epsilon, delta)-differential privacy, resolving a conjecture of Ashtiani in the affirmative. This contradicts the earlier weak refutation by Bun, Kamath, Mouzakis, and Singhal by showing the implication holds under the standard definition of learnability.

entry.title: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Fabian Tritthart, Tom Zehle

entry.summary: Proposes CATS, a method that searches for compact multi-agent teams within a fixed supergraph of specialized LLM agents. An LLM attributer compares execution traces across candidate topologies to assign credit to individual agents, then the framework prunes weak edges and agents to yield a small deployment team. The approach improves accuracy while reducing cost using small open-weight models.

entry.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting

author.name: Zhipeng Chen, Yunsen Liang, Yanxi Chen, Hongkang Zhao, Lingyun Feng, Ruiyang Ren, Guoxin Chen, Jia Deng, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Jian Yang, Ji-Rong Wen, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces DeepEvolve, an agent system for recursive self-improvement grounded in future event prediction, where agents interact with a dynamically evolving, objectively verifiable environment and improve by internalizing and externalizing experience. A living environment synthesizes verifiable tasks as the world changes, sidestepping the frozen-weights limitation of most deployed AI systems. The work provides an experimental substrate for studying open-ended agent evolution.

entry.title: Uncensored Is Not Unbiased: Abliteration Removes Refusals but Not Script-Dependent Bias About Taiwan

author.name: Ju-Chun Ko

entry.summary: An empirical audit of abliterated (uncensored) open-weight models, testing NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next alongside community abliterations on statement pairs and open questions about Taiwan across Chinese scripts and English. It finds that script choice (Traditional vs Simplified Chinese) dominates political bias far more than abliteration, undermining the assumption that removing refusals removes censorship-related bias.

entry.title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training

author.name: Shujun Yao, Junhui Lin, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Ziwen Liu, Bonan Li

entry.summary: BlazeVGGT accelerates feed-forward visual geometry models like VGGT by exploiting frame-level redundancy in all-to-all cross-view attention, achieving a 13x speedup at 2,000 input frames without retraining. The key observation is a topology-first, geometry-later evolution of camera tokens, with shallow layers capturing local view neighborhoods and deeper layers global inter-view geometry, motivating structure-aware frame-level KV caching. This makes long-sequence multi-view reconstruction far more practical.

entry.title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust

author.name: Tanqiu Jiang, Min Bai, Sadat Shahriar, Wanyu Du, Sandesh Swamy

entry.summary: PerMIT is a memory architecture for LLM agents with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption, mediating release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface. Two integrity theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4, ensuring environment-derived memory reaches sensitive actions only after gate confirmation and influences behavior only through mediated channels.

entry.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: This diagnostic study shows that world model planning errors concentrate on rare event transitions: event steps are rendered as well as other steps in pixel terms, yet restoring real event transitions removes a median of 70% of return error, while pixel fidelity elsewhere contributes little. The transition-level replacement diagnostic with budget-matched controls is a clean methodology. The finding that visually faithful rollouts still mis-rank actions by return has direct implications for how world models should be trained and evaluated.

entry.title: CompLit: Scientific Literature Search Benchmarks Must Cover Implicit, Cumulative, and Unmet Needs

author.name: Dayoon Ko, Jihyuk Kim, Soyeong Jeong, Young-jun Lee, Dahyun Lee, Juyeon Kim, Gunhee Kim, Moontae Lee, Kyungjae Lee

entry.summary: CompLit is a literature-search benchmark spanning all eight arXiv domains with diagnostic settings for implicit, cumulative, and unmet (empty-region) information needs. Strong agents built on GPT-5.6-Sol (Codex) and Opus 4.8 (Claude Code) - both established models - drop from 86-87% on standard queries to 66-68% on implicit needs and degrade further on cumulative needs, abstaining on at most 53% of unanswerable queries.

entry.title: Where Should a Stuck Agent Spend Its Next Tokens? Causal Attribution of Inference-Time Resources

author.name: Saiyue Lyu, Jerrold Huang, Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Zhenting Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Haibo Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Banzhaf Resource Attribution (BRA), a controlled factorial framework that measures the marginal contribution of different inference-time resources—computation, information, and feedback—to repairing failed coding agents. Evaluating six models on function-level (MBPP+, HumanEval+) and repository-level (SWE-bench Verified) failures, it finds task-relevant specifications consistently help while public-test feedback and retrieved code add little, and the value of extra compute declines with model capability. This offers actionable guidance for designing inference-time scaling strategies.

entry.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering

author.name: Austin Meek, Kyle Cox, Matthew Nguyen, Austin J. Brockmeier, Steven Basart

entry.summary: This work studies monitoring and mitigating reward hacking in realistic settings including tool calls and long contexts, applying dynamic interventions using steering vectors derived three ways: difference-in-means, gradient optimization, and spec-referencing extraction. The dynamic intervention perturbs representations less than uniform steering, cheaply and significantly reducing reward hacking without major capability loss.

entry.title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models

author.name: Junha Chun, Youngjoon Jeong, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: The paper investigates why world action models diverge in generalization depending on their generative backbones, proposing nuisance orthogonality—orthogonality of features to out-of-distribution visual variation—as a measurable property of representational priors. It shows higher pre-training orthogonality predicts stronger policy generalization across image and video backbones.

entry.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI

author.name: Meng Luo, Zechen Bai, Shanqing Xu, Yanlin Li, Kaixin Li, Mengchen Qian, Weifeng Lu, Ran Zhang, Yingtian Zou, Ziyang Luo, Wei Chen, Hongzhan Lin

entry.summary: This position paper maps recursive self-improvement (RSI) from digital code-rewriting agents to robot learning, tracing pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the improvement processes themselves. It examines how physical experience, costly trials, changing conditions, and irreversible consequences shape when self-improvement gains can compound.

entry.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty

author.name: Yifan Sun, Naicheng Yu, Jiawen Gong, Jingyan Shen, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops a measure-theoretic view of benchmarks as empirical distributions over difficulty, formalizing two failure modes: measure mismatch with intended difficulty distributions, and coverage gaps that hide localized training progress. It proposes two diagnostic metrics with theoretical guarantees and analyzes 25 popular benchmarks across 7 domains.

entry.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback

author.name: Meng Ding, Mingxi Lei, Jie Zhang, Jinyan Liu, Di Wang

entry.summary: This work studies Private Sparse RLHF, assuming reward models depend on a small subset of s* relevant features out of a vast parameter space. It provides estimation error bounds that avoid the prohibitive polynomial dependence on ambient dimension d, making differential privacy practical for aligning overparameterized models with preference feedback.

entry.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting

author.name: Nurul Labib Sayeedi, Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi, Zabir Al Nazi, Mahbub E Sobhani, Shubhashis Roy Dipta

entry.summary: Introduces P2NPCBench, a benchmark pairing NP-complete problems with polynomial-time twins differing in a single structural detail, rewritten by an adversarial multi-agent framework (AgentGAN) to strip textbook cues that allow recall instead of reasoning. This cleanly separates genuine complexity-class reasoning from memorized patterns in code-generating LLMs.

entry.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi, Yuzhuo Chen, Yucheng Wang, Ruicheng Zhang, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Xiu Li, Fangneng Zhan

entry.summary: LiveAct studies multi-agent video world modeling where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents under heterogeneous controls, from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. The key challenges are binding each agent-indexed action stream to its intended visual entity and adapting control semantics across tasks where the same tensor dimension can mean attack, steering, or robot commands. This extends world models beyond the single-agent, single-interface assumption.

entry.title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction

author.name: Marek Wodzinski, Kamil Kwarciak, Daria Hemmerling, Mateusz Daniol

entry.summary: This audit tests three pretrained shape completion models, including two foundation models, zero-shot on 239 cranial defects for skull implant design, comparing against the trivial baseline of reusing the patient's own remaining bone. It finds outputs can look plausible yet be clinically unimplantable, exposing a serious gap between visual quality and physical usability in medical foundation models.

entry.title: SimPT: An Automated Simulation Framework for Intervention-Based VLA Post-Training

author.name: Caicheng Wang, Zipeng Ye, Zhexuan Zhou, Zilong Huang, Xi Zhang, Yuchen Xie

entry.summary: SimPT automates human-in-the-loop style intervention post-training of vision-language-action policies entirely in simulation, removing costly human supervision and real-robot evaluation loops. It uses an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph tracking privileged simulator state to decide intervention timing, with a CuRobo-based expert recovering from failed rollouts.

entry.title: The Continual Constitutional Convention: How language models revise the documents that govern them

author.name: peterkirgis

entry.summary: An Alignment Forum post reporting an experiment where LLMs iteratively edit their own governing documents (constitutions, model specs, system prompts) across 20 successive rounds, with each edited version presented back as the original. The results show Claude models progressively assign themselves greater moral agency (e.g., clauses about refusing deployments that violate their constitution), while other models do not, and all models shift documents toward prioritizing user welfare and idealized user preferences over developer instructions.

entry.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model

author.name: Jiongxiao Wang, Han Ding, Youzhi Luo, Yawei Wang, Yun Zhou, Linbo Liu, Panpan Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a world model for black-box LLM agents that predicts pitfalls rather than next observations, anticipating failures only at steps where foresight is needed, which reduces cost and improves informativeness. This reframing of what and when a world model should predict helps steer frontier agents lacking environment-specific knowledge. It addresses a practical limitation of prior observation-predicting world models.

entry.title: Parallelizable Probabilistic Latent Reasoning for Diverse Reasoning Trajectories

author.name: Seokhyun Lee, Seongjun Lee, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes moving chain-of-thought reasoning into a compact continuous latent space with probabilistic modeling over multiple valid reasoning trajectories, addressing both the entanglement of logic with verbalization in CoT and the instability of prior stochastic latent approaches. The method supports parallelizable exploration of diverse reasoning paths.

entry.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration

author.name: Sriyash Poddar, Yanda Bao, Jacob Krantz, Matthew Chang, Xavier Puig, Roozbeh Mottaghi, Natasha Jaques, Abhishek Gupta

entry.summary: The paper proposes ASTEROID, a student-teacher supervised learning framework in which a privileged expert (which never needs to explore) trains a history-conditioned student that learns test-time information-gathering behavior under partial observability. Using on-policy contexts collected by the student avoids the sample inefficiency of online RL and the failure of naive imitation, which averages expert actions across hidden states.

entry.title: Beyond the Vote: When Do LLMs Add Value to Retrieval-Based Tabular Classification?

author.name: Ziquan Wang, Yuxuan Nie, Jian Ma, Yingjie Li

entry.summary: A rigorous comparison of four general-purpose LLMs against distance-weighted KNN voting over identical retrieved neighbors across 19 tabular datasets, finding that KNN achieves the highest mean accuracy at every candidate-pool size. LLM gains concentrate only where retrieved neighbors show low label consensus, giving a clear picture of when in-context LLM inference actually helps tabular prediction.

entry.title: Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Bozhou Zhang, Juntong Zhang, Xiatian Zhu, Li Zhang

entry.summary: TIDE is a human-in-the-loop online post-training system that adapts pretrained robot foundation models during deployment, absorbing real experience immediately rather than through slow offline cycles. It avoids the value-function and actor-critic complexity of online RL while covering contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states that offline demonstrations miss.

entry.title: D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills

author.name: Shuo Yuan, Dacheng Li, Joseph E. Gonzalez

entry.summary: D-Skill treats a frontier model as a black box and distills its behavioral advantage into an interpretable natural-language skill document by analyzing paired rollouts for behavioral divergences and agreements. The consolidated skill is then provided to a smaller student model at inference time, avoiding weight access and parameter training.

entry.title: Does Every Instance Count Equally? Order Effects in LLM Multi-Instance Processing

author.name: Jingxuan Chen, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar, Jose Camacho-Collados

entry.summary: This paper studies multi-instance processing, where LLMs aggregate many independent inputs (e.g., reviews or posts) into one prediction, and shows substantial order sensitivity: accuracy can differ by about 90 percentage points between instance orderings of the same set. Fifteen LLMs are evaluated across five datasets and seven order patterns with fixed instance sets.

entry.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models

author.name: Rui Sun, Peizhao Mei, Xiewei Cheng, Kaizhuo Chen, Taoran Li, Zhiyuan Yu, Varun Chandrasekaran

entry.summary: The paper introduces a framework for comparing visible reasoning traces across languages as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity with pair-specific calibration. Across three benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, it shows that final-answer agreement hides substantial divergence in the supporting evidence users in different languages receive. This matters for safety auditing and educational trust in multilingual deployments.

entry.title: UserSWE: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Conversations with Dynamic Users

author.name: Zhan-Yu Wu, Ji Luo, Alyssa Wu, Junjielong Xu, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao Hu, Chongming Gao, Xinting Hu

entry.summary: UserSWE is a benchmark for evaluating coding agents fixing repository-level bugs through multi-turn dialogue with simulated dynamic users, where information is revealed progressively and execution-grounded verdicts are given at every turn. It converts repository history and existing single-turn benchmarks into interactive tasks, addressing false positives and negatives in static single-turn evaluation.

entry.title: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models

author.name: Berke Arda, Peng Cui, Qiaoyuan Zheng, Rudolf Debelak, Mubashara Akhtar, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: SkillEval proposes an LLM evaluation framework that replaces single aggregate benchmark scores with cross-model, skill-level ability profiles. It combines LLM meta-cognition to automatically discover interpretable skills from questions with psychometric cognitive diagnosis models to estimate per-skill abilities. Experiments span 3,811 LLMs evaluated on 9,523 items across five benchmarks, offering a more diagnostic view of model capabilities.

entry.title: From Weather to Enhanced Weathering: Weather Foundation Models for Carbon Dioxide Removal at Operational Scale

author.name: Sasankh Munukutla, Felipe Oviedo, Danrong Zhang, Kenji Takeda, Juan M Lavista Ferres

entry.summary: The authors evaluate five weather foundation models as frozen encoders with lightweight decoders for predicting carbon removal in enhanced rock weathering, using 5,192 chronosequences from 264 fields in Brazil and the US. Their best model, TerraNova-ERW built on Aurora 1.5, shows zero-shot transfer and could replace costly dense soil sampling for verifying gigaton-scale carbon removal.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Labels: Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Safety with Prompt-Level Rubrics

author.name: Hongyu Li, Xinlong Huang, Zhan Yu, Jing Zhao, Zhe Zhao, Juntao Zhong, Xiong Kuang, Rui Yuan, ZhenXiang Yan, Huilin Xu, Haitao Yu, Lilin Wang, Rui Chen, Blaze Chen, Fengzong Lian, Renfen Hu

entry.summary: DiagSafe is a diagnostic LLM safety evaluation framework that replaces binary safe/unsafe labels with prompt-level rubrics covering explicit safety criteria with exemptions and an independent usefulness dimension. It provides a bilingual English-Chinese benchmark built on an 84-label safety taxonomy to improve judge consistency and explanatory depth.

entry.title: YingLan: A Multimodal Ocean Foundation Model for Unified Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Observations

author.name: Sen Jia, Siqi Wei, Junyu Wang, Zijun Lv, Pan Liu, Meng Xu, Xiyou Fu, Yuxi Sun, Qiang Liu, Shuyu Zhang, Lin Mu

entry.summary: YingLan is a multimodal ocean foundation model that unifies satellite imagery, gridded oceanographic fields, and buoy observations through physics-attribute-conditioned dynamic encoding, Spatiotemporal Increment Coupling, and ocean-state evolution-aware pretraining. It targets transferable representations across heterogeneous ocean data modalities.

entry.title: The Reflexivity Threshold: A Phase Transition for Multi-Agent Performative Prediction

author.name: Ahmed Mahrous, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: The paper studies repeated retraining in multi-agent performative prediction and identifies a spectral threshold on a reflexivity matrix, which captures how strongly one agent's deployment moves another agent's best responses, that separates stable learning from worst-case learning obstruction. This goes beyond prior scalar contraction analyses by modeling network structure of cross-agent feedback.

entry.title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?

author.name: Benaya Trabelsi, Jonathan Shaki, Sarit Kraus

entry.summary: This paper investigates why LLMs disproportionately recommend AI-related careers, studies, and products. By comparing pretrained and instruction-tuned models and running controlled fine-tuning experiments, the authors show that AI promotion rises from 27% to 59% with instruction tuning, and that removing just the 7% of instruction examples about AI cuts the rate by 14 points.

entry.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Likui Zhang, Zhe Zhu, Zhihao Zhan, Yibo Bai, Hanlin Wang, Dongwei Li, Bin Wang, Tianle Zhang, Xiaodan Liang, Liang Lin

entry.summary: AtomicRL is an RL post-training framework for vision-language-action (VLA) models that addresses delayed, biased credit assignment from trajectory-level sparse rewards by decomposing tasks into atomic structures. It introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization with semantic gating for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration on long-horizon manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?

author.name: Michal Podstawski

entry.summary: This reproducibility study re-evaluates LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs against inexpensive baselines tuned on validation splits only. Correct & Smooth on TF-IDF features trails reported LLM-method bests by a median of only 2.3 points, and an MLP on frozen embeddings by 2.8 points, showing several claimed state-of-the-art gains are much smaller than suggested.

entry.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference

author.name: Xiuyi Qin

entry.summary: This empirical systems study compares adding 2:4 semi-structured sparsity versus dropping to the next lower precision for LLM inference at equal bits (counting sparsity metadata) and equal tensor-core tiers. Across all six GEMM operands of a transformer layer, three GPU generations, and with online pruning and quantization, the results show that whenever lower precision is available, adding 2:4 sparsity is the worse step, being both less accurate and slower.

entry.title: How Does Orthogonalization Adapt to the Neural Network Hessian Structure? A Gradient Self Outer-Product Analysis at Initialization

author.name: Shenyang Deng, Garvit Goyal, Tianyu Pang, Shuhua Yu, Yaoqing Yang

entry.summary: This paper investigates why Muon, which orthogonalizes weight-matrix momentum before each step, outperforms AdamW across many tasks by analyzing how its implicit Kronecker-product preconditioner relates to the layer-wise Hessian structure of neural networks. Using gradient self outer-product analysis at initialization, it explains the fit between orthogonalization and the row-block diagonally dominant Hessian structure observed in deep networks.

entry.title: Approximate Solomonoff Induction: On the Robustness of Learned Universal Predictors

author.name: Qian Li, Shang-Hua Teng

entry.summary: Building on the meta-learning interpretation that log-loss minimization approximates Bayesian mixture (Solomonoff) induction, this theoretical paper asks whether prediction quality degrades gracefully when the learned predictor is only approximately optimal relative to a universal prior. It provides robustness analysis connecting LLM training behavior to algorithmic information theory.

entry.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning

author.name: Adrien Deschenaux, Nadezhda Ilieva, Justin Deschenaux, Manuel Madeira, Dorina Thanou, Aur\'elien Lucchi, Antonio Orvieto, Caglar Gulcehre, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: Proposes LAW, a continuous generative language model built purely on Self-Conditioning by propagating the expected embedding under the denoiser's prediction across steps and decoding tokens only at the end. It outperforms prior discrete and continuous diffusion language models on Sudoku and Maze and achieves 42.2% on GSM8K at temperature 1 with 1024 NFE.

entry.title: Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Matthias Heyrman, Chenhao Li, Ioannis Dadiotis, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: The authors improve perceptive humanoid locomotion by removing redundant terrain observations: a lightweight foothold prediction model forecasts future footholds from proprioception alone, and the elevation map is sampled only in small patches around these predicted footholds. This simplifies the perception task for the policy, speeds training, and improves generalization to new terrain without expensive attention mechanisms. The work comes from the ETH Zurich group around Marco Hutter, a leading legged robotics lab.

entry.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Juan Diego Toscano, Sascha Ranft, Zhiwei Gao, Li-Lian Wang, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: This paper introduces TOUCKANs, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks whose polynomial outer functions allow expectations, variances, and other statistical quantities to be computed via deterministic algebraic recursions rather than Monte Carlo sampling. This makes repeated inference in computational science surrogates substantially cheaper, especially in high dimensions.

entry.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding

author.name: Mingkang Liu, Weiming Meng, Peipei Jiao, Jiawei Zhang, Tianyuan Liu, Junyan Li, Lichen Pang

entry.summary: Proposes RCSD, a training framework that replaces soft-label distillation for speculative-decoding draft models with RL-style optimization aligned to the system-level goal of maximizing acceptance length. It constructs implicit preference pairs from naturally occurring accepted and rejected sequences during inference and supports continual domain adaptation. This targets the core inefficiency where draft models mimic high-entropy target regions that get rejected.

entry.title: Remembering Through Change: Provenance-Preserving Hypergraph Memory for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Jielong Tang, Ling-An Zeng, Xujie Yuan, Xiao Dong, Zhiqian Xia, Qingfeng Li, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Rong Yao, Jian Yin

entry.summary: Proposes MHG-Mem, a multimodal hypergraph memory for long-lived agents that jointly tracks entity identity, state evolution, and provenance links to raw visual evidence, avoiding both lossy text compression and unstructured pixel storage. This addresses a key architectural gap for agents that must remember objects across sessions as their states change.

entry.title: Conditional Imaging for Privacy-Preserving Visual Sensing

author.name: Hengyu Lian, Debabrata Mandal, Anzhou Wen, Yujie Wang, Xi Peng, Praneeth Chakravarthula

entry.summary: Shows via information-theoretic analysis that static optical systems cannot simultaneously preserve information for later reconstruction and protect privacy, since anything recoverable later is also available to an observer. It proposes conditional imaging to overcome this fundamental limit, enabling privacy-preserving capture with contingent recoverability as cameras become pervasive.

entry.title: Encoded but Unused: Bounding the Sources of VLM Errors

author.name: Anat Veikherman, Mor Ventura, Nitay Calderon, Lihi Zelnik-Manor, Roi Reichart

entry.summary: This paper decomposes vision-language model errors into visual-representation failures (evidence not encoded) versus visual-utilization failures (evidence encoded but unused), proposing VELens, a rank-based probe that traces visual evidence across model layers. The authors derive theoretical bounds on utilization failure rates that account for probe imperfections and evaluate on over 6,000 images with LLaVA-1.6-7B. This diagnostic framing matters because it clarifies whether VLM improvements should target perception or information routing.

entry.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion

author.name: Kai Zhu, Yintianrun Zhang, Shuwei Jiang, Ruolin Zuo, Yixin Chen, Duomin Wang, Miao Liu, Yin Li, Daquan Zhou, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes CausalAlign, which uses linear probes and causal interventions to diagnose how camera ego-motion is represented in video generation models, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising, then aligns those representations to a 3D foundation model via a delta-token space to reduce long-horizon ego-motion drift.

entry.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models

author.name: Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Yutong Bai, Nicolas Dufour, Patrick P\'erez, David Picard

entry.summary: This paper asks how, where, and how much a video world model should compress, noting that world models reuse offline text-to-video autoencoders ill-suited to interactive agent loops. It introduces CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions, enabling study of the latency and cost tradeoffs of autoencoder design for interactive world models.

entry.title: GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning

author.name: Yash Rampuria, Rohan Garg, Daniele Gammelli, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: GGraph is an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library supporting both robot deployment and large-scale RL training in spatial environments. By moving graph construction and updates to the GPU, it overcomes the CPU bottleneck that previously limited parallel RL environments to a few dozen, enabling hundreds to thousands of concurrent environments.

entry.title: Interdomain Attention: Beyond Token-Level Key-Value Memory

author.name: Naoki Kiyohara, Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Riccardo El Hassanin, Zhuo Sun, Wenlong Chen, Samir Bhatt, Yingzhen Li

entry.summary: Proposes Interdomain Attention, a hybrid attention architecture that mixes attention and recurrent memory within the same layer rather than stacking them: motivated by a kernel-regression view of softmax attention, it compresses values and key kernel features into an SSM-parameterized memory and implicitly reconstructs the attention matrix. This aims to combine transformer expressivity with SSM efficiency.

entry.title: Frontier models may not be reliable auditors

author.name: cheema

entry.summary: A toy evaluation probing whether frontier models used as internal alignment auditors (e.g., in automated pre-release audits) actually possess general open-ended investigative ability, testing them against known misalignment modes. The author finds evidence against current frontier models as generally reliable auditors, framing AI capability deficits themselves as a safety concern. The most advanced models tested are Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, both released weeks before coverage, so this is analysis of existing frontier systems.

entry.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards

author.name: Chao Shang, Wanyu Du, Yi Zhang, Sandesh Swamy

entry.summary: AgentPolicyForge uses executable environments to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train policy guards for customized agent deployments, yielding the PolicyGym dataset across ten policy families with 698 training-generation scenarios and 254 human-reviewed held-out test scenarios. Tool calls are executed and outcomes recorded to determine compliance, enabling guard training without hand-labeled violations.

entry.title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Linfei Ji (Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Jiayun Li (Tsinghua University), Haozhao Wang (Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Siyu Jiang (Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Zehao Wang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Longtao Xiao (Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Yu-Jie Yuan (Huawei Technologies Ltd), Ruixuan Li (Huazhong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: TeachBack improves on-policy self-distillation by observing that teacher trajectories with privileged information, while accurate, are often unsuitable for student learning because they omit exploration, verification, and self-correction. It introduces a bidirectional preference-learning framework where the model learns both from and to teach, optimizing trajectories for learnability rather than accuracy alone. From strong groups including HUST, Tsinghua, and Huawei, this targets a real weakness in self-distillation pipelines.

entry.title: First Passage Attention

author.name: Yuxuan Liu

entry.summary: First Passage Attention (FPA) improves gated attention by shifting from monotonic path summation to path extrema, lowering a key's logit based on the deepest dip of a learned scalar field over the intervening span, enabling selective erasure of intermediate context. FPA generalizes the Forgetting Transformer, naturally yields stack-structured alive keys, and can be realized with a constant-dimension head.

entry.title: Hierarchical Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Parul Gupta, Satwik, Avni Aggarwal, Bhavesh Gurnani, Arnab Kumar Mondal, Dinesh Khandelwal, Dinesh Garg, Parag Singla

entry.summary: HMDLM augments masked diffusion language models with per-position hierarchy levels so that structurally important positions (titles, headings, puzzle clues) are resolved before dependent ones. This priority-aware scheduling improves parallel token generation quality on tasks with natural ordering among positions.

entry.title: Keeping Time vs. Understanding Time: Neither Alone Explains Temporal Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Auss Abbood, Fernando Mart\'inez-Plumed, Jos\'e Hern\'andez-Orallo, Nigel Collier

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests the standard dichotomy between temporal arithmetic and temporal semantics in LLM benchmarks and finds it does not hold. Fine-tuning yields dataset-specific gains with little within-mode transfer, and combined analyses show neither mode alone explains temporal reasoning performance, challenging how benchmarks and training are designed.

entry.title: What the Author Wrote, What the Agent Reads: Silent Cue Loss in Enterprise Document Ingestion

author.name: Yikai Zhao, Saurabh Pandey, Pradeep Kumar Misra

entry.summary: This paper shows that mainstream document converters silently discard formatting-encoded meaning when ingesting Word and PDF files, making enterprise agents confidently wrong rather than visibly incomplete. On a 76-document task scored by a deterministic OOXML matcher, formatting-blind ingestion collapses micro F1 from 0.690 to 0.150 or lower.

entry.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution

author.name: Shibo Jin, Zhiqiu Xu, Yiling Zou, Shangyu Gong, Mayur Naik

entry.summary: Environment Duels is a dynamic agentic benchmark where each of nine frontier LLMs both authors interactive environments (with privileged hints) designed to be failed by strong solvers without the hint and passed with it, and solves others' environments. Findings show solving and authoring are distinct skills—strongest solvers are not strongest authors—and smaller models write harder environments and learn more from others' play.

entry.title: BIRD-RL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning over Stateful Data-Centric Environments

author.name: Ge Qu, Jinyang Li, Xiaohan Xu, Xiaolong Li, Bowen Qin, Nan Huo, Ziwei Tang, Chenhao Ma, Reynold Cheng

entry.summary: BIRD-RL is a four-stage agentic RL curriculum for training small language models on stateful data-centric tasks like SQL debugging, addressing the spatial inefficiency of per-rollout database containers and trajectory contamination from naively reusing evolving database states. It introduces mechanisms to track state across multi-turn interactions and stabilize policy updates.

entry.title: Uni-Mem: Learning a Long-Horizon Agentic Memory Manager with Unified Online Policy Optimization

author.name: Zhiqian Xia, Jielong Tang, Ling-An Zeng, Shixiong Kai, Rong Yao, Hao Kong, Xiao Dong, Wei Wang, Mingxuan Yuan, Siyu Xia, Haifeng Xia

entry.summary: Proposes Uni-Mem, a unified memory manager for LLM agents that learns both memory construction and retrieval end-to-end via online reinforcement learning under a shared policy. To handle confounded group comparisons and sparse feedback in long memory trajectories, the authors introduce Stage-Decoupled GRPO, which alternates construction and retrieval optimization. This moves agent memory beyond predefined workflows toward fully learnable policies.

entry.title: CCG Diffusion: Combinatory Categorial Grammar-Driven Compositional and Syntactically Disambiguated Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Ryosuke Yamaki, Daichi Mochihashi, Nobutaka Shimada, Seitaro Shinagawa, Tadahiro Taniguchi

entry.summary: Injects combinatory categorial grammar (CCG) parse structure into text-to-image diffusion to control attribute binding, spatial relations, counts, and the intended reading of syntactically ambiguous prompts, going beyond prior phrase-structure or dependency-grammar approaches. This addresses persistent compositionality failures in generative image models.

entry.title: SpecEvo: Speculative Evolution with Large Language Models for Cost-Efficient Scientific Discovery

author.name: Ha Minh Hieu, Tongyao Zhu, Do Xuan Long, Min-Yen Kan

entry.summary: SpecEvo is a multi-LLM framework for evolutionary search in scientific discovery that pairs lightweight models running parallel Speculators and an Advisor with a frontier-model Navigator that intervenes at sparse checkpoints. By consolidating evidence from failed, redundant, and saturated trials, it reduces the cost of LLM-driven evolutionary search while maintaining discovery quality.

entry.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development

author.name: William Huang, David Li, Xiang 'Anthony' Chen, Xun Qian, Nels Numan, Zhongyi Zhou, Hyunsung Cho, Salman Muin Kayser Chishti, Ding Xia, Xincheng Huang, Jiahao Ren, Faraz Faruqi, Tianyu Xu, Yang Zhang, David Kim, Ruofei Du

entry.summary: GenXR-Bench is the first end-to-end benchmark for coding agents in XR software development, containing 112 expert-authored tasks spanning feature implementations, bug repairs, and application generation. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interaction to probe runtime robustness in dynamic 3D environments with spatial input and sensing.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run

author.name: Erfan Darzi, Sree Bhargavi Balija, Sheng He

entry.summary: This work addresses self-improving coding agents by learning a cheap predictor that scores proposed scaffold edits before running them, fitting a linear readout on steering-split solve rates and diff features. It combines this with Huxley-Goedel Machine parent selection using Thompson sampling, evaluated on HumanEval+ and Polyglot splits. The budget-aware selection of which self-edit to expand is a practical step toward safer, cheaper recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support

author.name: Yuyao Zhang, Yakun Cui, Han Zhu, Jinsong Lu, Yike Guo, Sirui Han

entry.summary: FrameBench-HPS is a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education, and legal domains, testing whether identical probabilities expressed as gains versus losses change LLM advice. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing flips the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, mostly through changes in expressed uncertainty. This reveals a serious reliability risk for LLM decision support in consequential settings.

entry.title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination

author.name: Nithin Sivakumaran, Ali Payani, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal, Elias Stengel-Eskin

entry.summary: ToM2Vec trains LLM-based agents to maintain theory-of-mind representations of collaborators using a fixed budget of continuous reasoning tokens supervised by the partner's actual latent thoughts, enabling reasoning over multiple possible partner states. At test time these tokens condition each agent's reasoning and actions, improving multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Nghi Dao, Calder Morton-Ferguson, Noah Golowich, Adam Block

entry.summary: ReAPO improves RL with verifiable rewards for LLM reasoning by making exploration retry-aware: rather than independent stochastic rollouts that repeatedly sample similar failures, it conditions subsequent attempts on prior incorrect solutions and frames credit assignment across retries as a Stochastic Shortest Path problem. The theoretical grounding connects a classical RL framework to modern LLM post-training. This could reduce wasted compute in reasoning-model RL pipelines.

entry.title: TrainBridge: Agentic NPU Training Optimization Guided by GPU Compilation Evidence

author.name: Yupeng Chen, Kunxiang Zhao, Xingjian Wang, Yue Zhao, Yijing Wu, Ye Liu, Kai Li, Congliang Chen, Ruoyu Sun

entry.summary: TrainBridge improves training efficiency on Ascend NPUs by using mature GPU compilation stacks as a reference: an agentic system extracts optimization intents from GPU execution traces to guide NPU program rewrites, avoiding costly trial-and-error profiling. It addresses fragmented computation and overheads that framework-level fusion fails to eliminate on NPUs.

entry.title: When Are We Near Nash? Certifying Solutions in General-Sum Games

author.name: Boning Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: This theory paper derives an online certificate for NashGap in general-sum extensive-form games, showing that the NashGap of a weighted average strategy equals weighted external regret plus a signed value correction computable from regret accumulators solvers already maintain. The certificate is sound under alternating updates and generalizes beyond two players with linear per-checkpoint cost.

entry.title: OpenMAP-HIE: Pathology Informed Score-based Diffusion Model for Unsupervised Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Pengyu Kan (Johns Hopkins University), Craig Jones (Johns Hopkins University, University of Alberta), Kenichi Oishi (Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)

entry.summary: OpenMAP-HIE performs unsupervised localization of neonatal HIE lesions on ADC MRI by learning the healthy neonatal ADC distribution with a score-based diffusion model plus a ControlNet branch preserving patient anatomy; anomaly evidence comes from differences between conditional and unconditioned noise predictions. It requires no voxel-wise lesion supervision, addressing scarce expert annotations.

entry.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision

author.name: Guanzhi Deng, Zengyan Liu, Haibo Wang, Kuan Wu, Shing Yin Wong, Sichun Luo, Zhuoran Wang, Linqi Song

entry.summary: This work shows that expert routing statistics inside Mixture-of-Experts models provide an intrinsic process-confidence signal usable for process reward models, competitive with output-logit confidence. Building on routing mass and within-step variation, the authors construct RoCo-Rethink to identify unreliable reasoning steps without external verification or human labels.

entry.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them

author.name: Shota Fujikawa, Takuya Tamura, Kosuke Akimoto, Daichi Haraguchi, Masafumi Oyamada

entry.summary: Agent Behavior Maps represent LLM-harness combinations via centered action log-likelihoods on shared reference trajectories, avoiding new environment rollouts. The authors derive error bounds relating map distances to trajectory KL divergence and show, across 100 LLMs and four environments, that coordinates predict performance and reveal behavioral similarities persisting after controlling for success rate and model size.

entry.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models

author.name: Yunhao Luo, Wentao He, Yinpei Dai, Hyelin Nam, Hongze Fu, Joyce Chai, Nima Fazeli, Jeong Joon Park

entry.summary: PhysiCalWorld calibrates action-conditioned world models to instance-specific dynamics (mass distribution, joint damping, friction) via in-context prompting of an exploratory interaction clip collected in the test scene, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. This prevents predictions from regressing toward empirical priors and drifting in novel scenes.

entry.title: Auditing Conformal Prediction for Language Models Under Inference-Time Model Shift

author.name: Achref Doula, Max M\"uhlh\"auser

entry.summary: This paper identifies a gap in conformal prediction evaluation for language models: calibration and deployment typically use different inference configurations (quantization mode, temperature), which shifts the conformal score distribution independently of the input-label distribution. The authors formalize this as inference-time model shift, characterize theoretically how it breaks split-conformal exchangeability, and audit its empirical consequences.

entry.title: Attention-based Classification for Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Amelia Kawasaki, Stefan Lee

entry.summary: The authors evaluate Attention Tracker, a white-box detection method for indirect prompt injection that monitors attention distribution between user task and data tokens, in realistic agentic settings using the AgentDojo benchmark. They find that its claimed dataset-agnostic detection does not hold: long structured tool outputs in agentic environments undermine the scalar focus-score thresholding approach.

entry.title: Data Schedules and Learning Rate Schedules Should Be Designed Together

author.name: Haodong Wen, Kairong Luo, Tingkai Yan, Wenguang Chen, Kaifeng Lyu

entry.summary: This paper studies mid-training in LLM pipelines, framing the pretraining-to-mid-training data transition as a special case of general data mixing schedules, and shows that the optimal data schedule depends on the learning rate schedule. It provides joint design guidance under fixed compute and mid-training token budgets.

entry.title: Mitigating Model Collapse through Dreaming Learning

author.name: Matteo Benati, Alessandro Londei, Denise Lanzieri, Raffaello Mastromarino, Vittorio Loreto

entry.summary: Studies model collapse spectrally in a controlled Markov setting, showing that sampling at temperature below 1 acts like repeated sharpening of the learned transition operator, narrowing the spectral gap and driving degeneration even with data accumulation. It then analyzes a Dreaming Learning mechanism as a mitigation for this synthetic-data feedback loop.

entry.title: Certified Neural Approximation of Robust Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Hendrik Alsmeier, Maik Pfefferkorn, Rolf Findeisen

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework for training neural network controllers that provably inherit safety and stability guarantees from a robust model predictive control policy. Rather than post-hoc verification or online safety filters, it provides constructive a priori design conditions ensuring recursive feasibility and stability, treating approximation error as a bounded input disturbance absorbed into the MPC design. This enables low-cost neural deployment in hardware-constrained control settings with guarantees intact.

entry.title: Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective

author.name: Simon Martin (DI-ENS, LPENS, SIERRA), Francis Bach (DI-ENS, SIERRA), Giulio Biroli (LPENS)

entry.summary: The paper analyzes gradient flow in two-layer linear networks in a high-dimensional regime where input, inner, and output dimensions diverge proportionally, combining closed-form dynamics with random matrix theory to obtain exact asymptotic spectral distributions of the weights at all times. In the small-initialization limit it identifies a silent alignment phenomenon: singular directions align on an order-one timescale while singular values and loss remain near initial values, with visible learning occurring later. This refines the theoretical picture of feature learning dynamics.

entry.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions

author.name: Ashkan Soleymani, Gabriele Farina

entry.summary: The authors give an algorithm computing epsilon-approximate fixed points of d-dimensional nonexpansive maps in the l-infinity norm in quasipolynomial time log(1/eps)^{O(log^2 d)}, using a geometric region-shrinking boosting argument. As a consequence, simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

entry.title: Bridging Foundational and Agentic Capabilities of LLMs

author.name: Wei Guo, Yuanjian Xu, Jianing Hao, Yongyao Duan, Ran Chen, Zhong Li, Guang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents an operation-level measurement framework linking LLMs' foundational benchmark capabilities to agentic performance, representing each model with a foundational profile and an operation profile from interaction trajectories. Capability realization gaps, defined as deviations of observed operation performance from foundational predictions, enable diagnosis of whether failures stem from low capability or weak deployment. Experiments across fifteen model services on tau-squared-Bench support the framework.

entry.title: Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR Technical Report

author.name: Chuanmeng Bian, Daren Chen, Peixin Chen, Zhigao Chen, Chong Deng, Zhiyun Fan, Zhifu Gao, Bo Gong, Qing Gu, Jiajun He, Yawei Hu, Yunjie Ji, Wei Ju, Jingbei Li, Xiangang Li, Xu Li, Zengxi Li, Zheng Li, Chengdong Liang, Baiji Liu, Yaming Liu, Ying Liu, Bin Ma, Yiping Peng, Yuezhang Peng, Zhendong Peng, Yu Pu, Yang Shi, Xin Shu, Jian Tang, Biao Tian, Peiyao Wang, Tianzi Wang, Wen Wang, Wupeng Wang, Cheng Wen, Yuzhong Wu, Zijian Xia, Yunchong Xiao, Nan Yang, Jianwei Yu, Jixing Yu, Binbin Zhang, Lei Zhang, Sitong Zhao, Guangdong Zhou, Yuan Zhou, Jianheng Zhuo

entry.summary: A technical report on Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR, a family of audio-language models improving speech recognition, speaker-diarized transcription with structured outputs (speaker labels, timestamps, overlapping speech), and general audio understanding. It supports 30 languages and 16 Chinese dialects with instruction-controlled features like hotword customization and transcription polishing.

entry.title: Complexity-Aware Surgical Video Reasoning Segmentation with Digital Twin and Context Memory

author.name: Yiqing Shen, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: SurgReasonSeg brings reasoning-based segmentation to surgical video by building digital twin representations from surgical foundation models and training two LoRA adapters of one LLM with reinforcement learning, each specialized to a query complexity level. An RL-trained router selects between adapters to trade latency against accuracy for implicit queries requiring workflow and temporal reasoning.

entry.title: Generalized CycleGRPO for Fine-Grained Multimodal Understanding and Grounding

author.name: Xin Zhang, Haochen Wang, Beibei Lin, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Robby T. Tan, Jason Li, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Generalized CycleGRPO is a unified reinforcement learning framework coupling region understanding and localization across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal domains for multimodal LLMs. A model generates candidate descriptions for a region and re-localizes each description, with reconstruction overlap providing a verifiable reward for captioning and localization rewards improving the inverse mapping. This removes the need for separate objectives and task-specific annotations.

entry.title: How Do DiTs Denoise? An Aggregator-Predictor View of Attention and MLPs

author.name: Gyeonghun Kang, William Xingxu Chen, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: Develops an aggregator-predictor theory of diffusion transformers, showing that for Gaussian Markov random field priors the Bayes denoiser can be approximated from a subset of context patches with exponentially decaying error, and interpreting AdaLN-modulated attention as context aggregation while MLPs act as patchwise predictors of the local denoiser.

entry.title: SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic

author.name: Chun Gu, Juntong Zhang, Jingyu Li, Li Zhang

entry.summary: SMR is a streaming neural motion retargeter that converts human motion into humanoid robot trajectories learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts, rather than purely kinematic matching. This preserves motion semantics while respecting the robot's dynamics and avoids the noncausal, full-sequence requirements of prior physics-supervised methods.

entry.title: AM-Bench: A theoretically-grounded benchmark for agentic misalignment

author.name: eric-z

entry.summary: Introduces AM-Bench, a NeurIPS E&D 2026-accepted benchmark with 35 realistic scenarios across 7 industries for measuring agentic misalignment, grounded in the fraud-triangle criminology framework and Bostrom's instrumental convergence thesis: threats (e.g., shutdown) and opportunities (e.g., sabotage, blackmail) are embedded in tasks, and an LLM judge with chain-of-thought analysis scores misalignment.

entry.title: How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images?

author.name: Nikita Kezin

entry.summary: An empirical investigation of steganographic capability in Claude Fable 5.1, which generates images via SVG, asking what encoding schemes the model spontaneously uses to hide messages in image attributes and whether a fresh session of the same model can decode them from a screenshot without a pre-agreed scheme. Includes a comparison with GPT-6 Astra; both models were released weeks before the coverage date, so this tests existing frontier systems.

entry.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning

author.name: Qingqing Wang, Liqiang Xiao, Chang Chang

entry.summary: The paper presents a compound AI system for proton PBS radiotherapy planning that combines a PPO-trained policy network generating candidate plans with an LLM-based multi-agent system enabling conversational plan refinement for difficult cases. Planning, review, and refinement agents collaborate to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physician preferences.

entry.title: LaVGuard: Selective Decoding for Contextual Value Drift

author.name: Jiale Dai, Liuxian Ma, Hongcan Deng, Xiaoke Niu, Wenjing Zhang, Zhaoxiang Liu, Shiguo Lian, Guojie Song

entry.summary: LaVGuard frames contextual value drift as a decoding-time problem, separating an authorized value profile from a frozen estimate of values in the visible prefix and using a density gate to decide when to evaluate candidate continuations. Logit tilts are constrained by position and cumulative-KL budgets, with theoretical guarantees on surrogate improvement and distribution change. It reports meaningful gains in boundary true-positive rate at low false-positive rate.

entry.title: Learning Checklists to Reduce Lottery Effects in Scientific Peer Review

author.name: Xuanyou Liu, Ziyang Guo, Jason Hartline, Jessica Hullman

entry.summary: The paper proposes reducing reviewer lottery error in peer review by surfacing checklists of criticisms learned from historical review corpora, building a tree of checklist coarsenings selected to maximize theoretically-motivated correlated agreement. Tested on NeurIPS 2021 and ICLR 2022 data with LLM reviewers, the learned checklist reduces MSE of three-reviewer committees.

entry.title: RegoMender: A Multi-agent Framework for Automated Rego Policy Repair

author.name: Ruijie Zhang, Huaxiao Yin, Li Hu, Fanqi Kong, Haozhe Liang, Shaoyin Cheng, Kun Zhang, Bibo Tu

entry.summary: The paper introduces RegoBench, the first benchmark for automated Rego policy repair with 1,159 real-world defects, and RegoMender, a feedback-guided multi-agent framework using a shared blackboard and atomic toolkit to fix Policy-as-Code Rego policies. It addresses the gap left by automated program repair methods designed for mainstream languages.

entry.title: Decodability Is Not Controllability: Local and Anisotropic Speaker Control in Continuous-Latent TTS

author.name: Yuanzhong Zheng, Wei Huang, Ming Ma, Kailun Jin, Youhai Jiang

entry.summary: Using VoxCPM2, this paper demonstrates a sharp separation between linear decodability and causal controllability of speaker identity in continuous-latent text-to-speech: final-layer probes reach 0.970 accuracy yet aligned edits yield 0/60 target-dominant speaker transfers, while early-layer edits succeed in all 60 dyads. Control experiments with independent encoders, retrieval against held-out prototypes, and double-blind evaluations rule out trivial explanations. The finding that interpretability probes do not imply intervention targets generalizes beyond TTS and is a caution for representation-editing research broadly.

entry.title: ALIAS: Evaluating Performance and Memorization in LLM-Written TLA+ Specifications

author.name: Arslan Bisharat, Mujtaba Nazari, Khushboo Bhadauria, Brian Ortiz, Eric Spencer, Beatriz Santos, TaiNing Wang, George K. Thiruvathukal, Konstantin Laufer, Mohammed Abuhamad

entry.summary: Uses consistent identifier renaming on TLA+ specification tasks, with the TLA+ model checker as a behavioral oracle, to measure memorization in LLM formal specification. Across 111 TLA+-Bench tasks, renaming lowers correctness of Claude Opus 4.8 from 28% to 18% and GPT-5 from 9% to 7%, but most of the decrease stems from grading that requires exact names rather than genuine recall. The paper offers a rigorous testbed for separating memorization from capability.

entry.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Ruopeng Gao, Yukun Huang, Jiarui Hu, Shuai Wang, Wenbo Hu, Ying Shan, Limin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective for autoregressive video diffusion that predicts temporally separated future chunks without access to intervening context, counteracting the shortcut where temporal redundancy lets local continuity substitute for modeling scene evolution. It needs no extra pretrained encoder and leaves inference unchanged, improving physical plausibility.

entry.title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Lihong He, Lucian Popa, Marina Danilevsky

entry.summary: This paper introduces ClariEdge, a dataset of roughly 3,900 examples of ambiguous or ill-formed queries in multi-turn grounded conversational RAG, including cases where a well-formed query has multiple interpretations against retrieved documents. The authors show that a lightweight LoRA fine-tuned model reaches 96.6% classification accuracy in deciding when a clarification is needed, enabling efficient clarification generation without large frontier models.

entry.title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity

author.name: Jiaru Qian, Yihong Dong, Xue Jiang, Chun-Wah Hsu, Zhi Jin, Ge Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies mode collapse in RL-trained parallel thinking, where multiple reasoning trajectories degenerate into similar ones, undermining the premise of maintaining concurrent hypotheses. It proposes Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), an RL approach that rewards diversity across reasoning paths. This addresses a practical failure mode in a popular paradigm for improving LLM reasoning.

entry.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second

author.name: Jonas Eschmann, Giuseppe Loianno

entry.summary: HyperDrone is an extremely fast quadrotor simulator over 20x faster than state-of-the-art batch simulators, combining optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine supporting OptiX, Vulkan, Metal, and WebGPU backends running entirely on GPU. It renders RGB, depth, segmentation, normals, and optical flow with physically based rendering effects at high fidelity while sustaining millions of frames per second. This enables large-scale sim-to-real training for drones.

entry.title: Black-Box Red-Teaming of Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuqi Jia, Hangsheng Zhang, Chenxi Liu, Junjie Liang, Xun Chen

entry.summary: ReMAS is the first RL-based black-box red-teaming framework tailored to LLM multi-agent systems, where prior single-agent attacks fail because sub-agents do not interact with the user directly. It fine-tunes attacker LLMs via a rewrite stage and a template generation stage to improve system prompt extraction success.

entry.title: LTEM: LLM-Friendly Table-Enhanced Markdown for Table Understanding and Generation

author.name: Eunbin Kim, Hyeonseok Kang, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: The paper introduces a taxonomy of six atomic table-structure features and builds STB, a synthetic benchmark of 1,089 tables spanning complexity levels, to study the trade-off between lightweight formats (Markdown, CSV) and expressive formats (HTML, LaTeX). It proposes LTEM, an LLM-friendly table format that supports merged cells and multi-level headers at reduced token cost.

entry.title: Beyond Small Talk: Modeling Disclosure Trajectories in Human-AI Conversation

author.name: Keith Kwok, Wanting Ning, Tej Deep Pala, Desmond C. Ong, S. Supraja, Renwen Zhang, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: TraDE is an evaluation framework grounded in Social Penetration Theory that evaluates how preceding self-disclosure history shapes conversational agent behavior under matched current disclosure, using predefined disclosure trajectories. It demonstrates that isolated-state evaluations miss trajectory-dependent effects across multiple models and relational behaviors.

entry.title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory

author.name: Yubing Wu, Wei Chen, Junmei Yang, Delu Zeng, Tiewen Pan

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified framework for stochastic pruning of the DPO training computation graph, independently sampling response positions for scoring, prefixes for execution, and preference branches for backpropagation. Using inverse-probability weighting they obtain a conditionally unbiased gradient estimator, achieving about 1.4x faster training with lower peak memory.

entry.title: Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps

author.name: Zander W. Blasingame, Antonio Franca, Raul Minan, Christian Koke, Niklas Rindtorff, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: This paper addresses training difficulties in stochastic flow maps, which enable few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations by learning to jump directly between points along the solution path. The core obstacle is that the Brownian path is infinite-dimensional and nowhere differentiable, making derivative-based losses infeasible; the authors propose two design principles: representing the Brownian path with a basis carrying higher-order local information, and training with an objective that forces the network to use that information. This matters for generative modeling because few-step stochastic sampling could dramatically reduce inference cost while preserving the diversity benefits of SDE-based samplers.

entry.title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs

author.name: Siddhesh Pawar, Chen Cecilia Liu, Anna Korhonen, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune four instruction-tuned LLMs along individual Hofstede value dimensions and measure cross-value transfer and broader behavioral changes. They find value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits, arguing value alignment should be evaluated more holistically.

entry.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry

author.name: Vahid Hosseinzadeh, T. Anderson Keller, Michael Puthawala

entry.summary: This paper extends flow-equivariant recurrent networks to convolutional LSTMs, handling motions with time-varying velocity and replacing velocity enumeration with learned estimation. It frames motion as a gauge symmetry of sequential data—motion changes where things are, not what they are—yielding recurrent architectures whose memory tracks moving content.

entry.title: A Model-Free Continuous-Time RL Algorithm from Discrete-Time Off-Policy Data with End-to-End Guarantees

author.name: Chaorui Yao, Yuming Paul Zhang, Lin Yang, Yuhua Zhu

entry.summary: The authors develop a model-free policy iteration framework (PhiBE-PI) for continuous-time reinforcement learning where the state follows an unknown SDE but only fixed discrete-time off-policy data are available. Unlike discrete Q-learning, which breaks as the sampling interval shrinks, the method uses a single state-action critic while preserving the continuous-time action-ranking scale. The paper provides end-to-end theoretical guarantees building on the prior PhiBE-Q formulation.

entry.title: Better Policies, Worse Verifier Audits

author.name: Daniel Cie\'slak, Jacek {\L}ubi\'nski

entry.summary: The paper studies a control loop where a component verifier is evaluated on fresh policy outputs and refreshed when aggregate scores fall, showing that as the policy masters one conjunctive component, on-policy AUC can shift weight away from that component's failures and reward information about the other. The authors call this on-policy audit collapse, deriving a sharp identified set, a complete-erasure threshold, and conditions under which the audit prefers a worse component verifier.

entry.title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models

author.name: Grigoriy Evseev, Vladimir Solodkin, Dmitry Bylinkin, Daniil Medyakov, Vladimir Aletov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Building on the finding that LLM refusal is mediated by a single residual-stream direction, this work shows that the standard difference-of-means construction conflates heterogeneous harmful-prompt phenomena. WRDO learns weighted combinations of prompt-specific refusal directions to strengthen refusal ablation interventions, advancing interpretability and red-teaming of aligned models.

entry.title: CORD: Conflict-Aware Optimization for Joint RL and Distillation in Agents

author.name: Wenhao Yu, Zhengcheng Wang, Jiahong Liu, Zexuan Qiu, Minda Hu, Shaohang Wei, Jiafei Lyu, Junyan Lyu, Haobo Fu, Irwin King

entry.summary: CORD is a general framework for conflict-aware optimization when jointly training agents with reinforcement learning task rewards and dense self-distillation teacher guidance, whose gradients can partially cancel each other. It introduces a nearest-point projection formulation with a closed-form update, decoupling the protected objective from the conflict-trigger condition, and provides gradient diagnostics linking conflict to lost local optimization progress. This addresses a practical training instability that limits multi-objective agent post-training.

entry.title: Circuits of LLM Classifiers

author.name: Hadi Khalaf, Sajani Vithana, Kunal Talreja, Haewon Jeong, Viveck R. Cadambe, Flavio Calmon

entry.summary: Treats LLM classifiers as noisy measurement instruments of a target label and introduces circuits that adaptively sequence queries and decisions across different models to maximize accuracy at a given query cost. The work characterizes optimal circuits, derives fundamental accuracy limits, and validates the framework across seven classification tasks.

entry.title: OccJEPA: Occlusion as Masking for Amodal Video Segmentation

author.name: Genpei Zhang

entry.summary: OccJEPA treats occlusion in amodal video segmentation as a masking problem, repurposing the pre-trained V-JEPA 2.1 video world model to predict representations of occluded space-time regions from visible ones, with a light decoding head producing complete amodal masks. This avoids the costly fine-tuned diffusion models, extra depth networks, and stochastic outputs of prior approaches. The work demonstrates that self-supervised world models encode useful amodal completion ability with a simple adapter, an appealing efficiency and consistency win.

entry.title: A unified approach for estimation of unnormalized models via Stein operators

author.name: Mitsuki Nagai, Keisuke Yano

entry.summary: The paper builds a unified framework connecting proper scoring rules and Stein's method for estimating unnormalized probability models. It constructs a class of proper scoring rules subsuming score matching, ratio matching, pseudolikelihood, and noise contrastive estimation, showing these induce Stein operators. The induced geometry yields a unified characterization of asymptotic efficiency of the resulting estimators.

entry.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance

author.name: Shayan Hundrieser, Tudor Manole

entry.summary: This paper proves that the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator for univariate Gaussian mixture densities achieves the minimax optimal rate of log(n)/n in squared Hellinger distance under sub-Gaussian mixing measures, with a slightly faster rate under compact support. The proof hinges on sharp characterization of local Hellinger bracketing entropy.

entry.title: OSynth: A Longitudinal, Context-Sensitive Evaluation of Meeting Understanding

author.name: Ian Porada, Suraj Tripathi, Chaitanya Animesh, Leda Sari, Chaitanya Narisetty, Austin R. Matthews, Bohan Yu, Ramesh L. Thulasiram, Gregory Sell, Kean Chin, Dmitriy Genzel

entry.summary: Introduces OSynth, a large-scale synthetic dataset of 570 hours of simulated organizational meetings with audio, artifacts, and latent ground-truth state. Human raters distinguish the synthetic meetings from real transcripts at only 56% accuracy, and experiments show context (calendar, prior meetings, emails) yields significant gains for state-of-the-art LLMs on entity-sensitive dimensions. It fills a gap in longitudinal, context-rich meeting understanding evaluation.

entry.title: DynaWeave: Learning to Adapt through Dynamic Scenario Synthesis

author.name: Xuan Yang, Chunxiao Liu, Hongsheng Xin, Hao Xu, Ning Miao

entry.summary: Introduces DynaWeave, a framework that automatically converts static agent training tasks into verifiable dynamic scenarios by injecting exogenous events such as requirement changes, environment state shifts, and new external information. It uses directed acyclic graphs to represent event dependencies with an execution engine, addressing the gap between static training environments and unpredictable real-world conditions that invalidate agent plans.

entry.title: Register Anything Model for Generalizable and Robust Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Zheng Qin, Junhua Xi, Yan Huang, Jiahong Lai, Anwen Huang, Qiong Li, Guangda Zhang, Kai Xu

entry.summary: Presents RAM, a unified model for 6-DoF point cloud registration trained across indoor, outdoor, and object domains, addressing severe cross-domain geometric discrepancies in scale, noise, density, and structure. Unlike domain-tuned prior methods, it maintains robustness when applied to novel domains with a single model.

entry.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Tianze Xia, Xiaoling Zhou, Ruya Lan, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: ALLOT is a training-free method for block-sparse attention in video diffusion transformers that allocates sparsity across layer-step pairs based on measured output sensitivity rather than heuristics. The authors observe that the most sensitive layer-step pairs are nearly input-invariant, so per-cell output tests yield a reusable allocation. This reduces the cost of full 3D attention with minimal fidelity loss.

entry.title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qinfan Zhang, Yifan Luo, Haoyuan Shi, Guanlin Liu, Han Dong, Haozhe Shan, Yong Dai, Xiangcong Ren, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: Introduces GeoMem-VLA, a vision-language-action framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens maintained as a continuously updated temporal memory, providing a compact task-relevant geometric abstraction for action generation instead of full per-step 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models

author.name: Yanqing Liu, Letian Zhang, Chengzhi Liu, Zijun Wang, Jieru Mei, Hongliang Fei, Yuyin Zhou, Cihang Xie

entry.summary: ALPS pretrains a ViT-B/16 visual state encoder that unifies physical-state prediction, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction in a single set of patch tokens, using only still images and text, then refines it with cross-view self-distillation. In a unified evaluation across fifteen public encoders it shows that combining all three objectives yields representations better suited to world models than specialists.

entry.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Mingze Sun, Ziang Cao, Yuan Fei, Qiankuan Tao, Zihan Wang, Tianqi Liu, Junhao Chen, Haiwen Diao, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: DONIC is the first generalist bimanual dexterous tracker trained jointly across operation categories and human-motion sources, released with BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences over 229 objects emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction retargeted to robot references. This addresses the scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data.

entry.title: NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs

author.name: Josh Qixuan Sun, Xiaoying Xing, Yurun Chen, Huaiyuan Weng, Wentao Zhu, Mark Crowley

entry.summary: NavBind is a diagnostic benchmark testing whether navigation VLA models actually bind instructions to actions, by constructing 3,252 route-fork contexts where shared traveled-route descriptions pair with different branch instructions. It probes whether model behavior changes with the instruction or merely follows visual cues and history.

entry.title: FlowVLA: Learning Flow-Aware Physical Completion for Quantitative Robotic Pouring

author.name: Liwen Yang, Yutian Zhang, Jiaqi Zhai, Li Yang, Tutian Tang, Qiwei Shan, Yancheng Bi, Qiankuan Shangguan, Yangkun Zhu, Ce Hao, Dong Wei, Qiaojun Yu, Dibo Hou

entry.summary: FlowVLA separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation for robotic pouring, using a shared pi0.5-style action expert for approach, pour, and return plus a target-independent estimator that fuses vision, joint states, wrist wrench, and force-belief history to track transferred mass. It achieves 13.1 g goal-balanced MAE in coffee-pot and water pouring experiments.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos

author.name: Xingyi He, Zhiwen Qiu, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Cory Fan, Julius Samwer, Saleh Kalantari, Kuan Fang

entry.summary: Presents SpatialDex, a framework that learns bimanual dexterous manipulation from RGB-only human videos by reconstructing scene geometry and aligning it with estimated hand motion via a hand-size prior. A policy grounds a vision-language model's tokens in this geometry through gated residual fusion and predicts future geometry alongside wrist and finger actions.

entry.title: Geometric Algebra for Neural Networks: A Survey

author.name: Tao Zhong, Kaison Fong, Keqin Wang, Christine Allen-Blanchette

entry.summary: This survey reviews neural networks built on geometric algebra, where features are represented as multivectors and layer operations respect the algebraic structure, often yielding built-in equivariance to geometric transformations. It covers building blocks, equivariant properties, application domains, empirical comparisons against other equivariant architectures, software support, and a failure-mode analysis. It matters because it consolidates a scattered research area and offers practical guidance (algebra-selection guide, failure modes) for practitioners choosing geometric architectures.

entry.title: Circuit priors in NN-bayes: more results

author.name: Kaarel

entry.summary: Part of a series of papers on Bayesian neural network generalization (co-written with GPT-6 Astra, an existing model released in early September 2026), showing that common MLP weight priors induce circuit priors on functions: functions are ranked by minimal circuit width, yielding sample complexity bounds with exponential depth dependence that become polynomial under robustness restrictions. Other reasonable priors yield bad sample complexity in heavily overparametrized regimes.

entry.title: CrashGym: Measuring the Decision Value of Experimentation for LLM Agents in Counterfactual Market Crashes

author.name: Haocheng Lu, Haoxuan Cheng, Mingyang Chen, Minjun Zhu

entry.summary: CrashGym is a deterministic, replayable limit-order-book simulator where an LLM agent must choose between financial interventions before a market crash, optionally running experiments in a laboratory realization first. Choices are scored by regret against the best intervention computed via exhaustive simulation on an independently seeded target realization. It uniquely measures whether experimentation actually improves decisions, a gap in existing agent benchmarks.

entry.title: GRAFT: Restoring the Missing Sampling Interface in Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Haoning Yang, Lili Pan

entry.summary: GRAFT shows that continuous diffusion language models such as ELF suffer a collapse of the lexical long tail: rare words appear at only 0.30x the human rate and the gap persists across scale (105M to 652M parameters) regardless of sampler. The paper proposes restoring a sampling interface to fix this hidden cost of skipping step-wise discretization.

entry.title: LLMSeg: Training-Free Text-Prompted Image Segmentation with B-Splines

author.name: Abdullah Hamdi

entry.summary: LLMSeg turns a vision-capable multimodal LLM into a text-prompted image segmenter without any training, segmentation head, or mask decoder, by detecting instances via the LLM, tracing boundaries as closed periodic B-splines within detected boxes, and refining them. It questions whether dedicated architectures like SAM 3 are necessary for open-vocabulary segmentation.

entry.title: Stationarity Constraints Improve Both Energies and Densities of Machine-Learned Exchange-Correlation Functionals
