entry.title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models

author.name: Saurav Jha, Qianli Liao, Robert Vernon, Sarath Chandar, Quentin Fournier

entry.summary: recAMPLIFY adapts recursive pretraining to masked protein language models using a weight-tied Transformer core that refines residue-aligned hidden states over an adjustable number of cycles, enabling test-time scaling where autoregressive LLM recipes do not transfer. With 155M unique parameters trained on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M, it matches or exceeds the larger baseline with 56% fewer parameters. This offers an efficiency-oriented alternative to brute-force scaling in protein modeling.

entry.title: Your Self-Supervised Projection Head Captures Object Co-Occurrence Statistics

author.name: Arthur Aubret, Jochen Triesch, C\'eline Teuli\`ere

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that common SSL pretext tasks implicitly model object co-occurrence statistics and test this across many SSL models on curated segmented-object datasets. They find a hierarchical division of labor: the visual backbone encodes object categories while the projection head specializes in co-occurrence structure, with the projection head outperforming the backbone on certain co-occurrence tasks.

entry.title: Interpretability of AI weather models via intermediate decoding

author.name: Matthias Beylich, Kirsten I. Tempest, Tobias Selz, George C. Craig

entry.summary: Proposes intermediate decoding as an interpretability method for AI weather models, decoding latent states from intermediate network depths back into meteorological fields using the trained forecast decoder. Applied to GraphCast, Aurora, and ArchesWeather, it offers a way to see how forecasts are constructed inside high-dimensional latent spaces. This addresses the black-box criticism of ML weather models that now rival numerical methods.

entry.title: RATION: Towards Quantitative Risk-Based Access Control for AI Agents

author.name: Yuntao Du, Harsh Chaudhari, Yuetian Chen, Ron Heichman, Ashish Jayamohan, Kumar Pallav, Mahim Patel, Kaiyuan Zhang, Kyle Polley, Jerry Ma, Ninghui Li

entry.summary: RATION is a security framework for AI agents that tracks measurable risks associated with agent actions and enforces quantitative risk constraints during task execution, rather than bluntly restricting actions and suffering a security-utility trade-off. It directly targets threats like indirect prompt injection in open-ended agent tasks, with a large author team including established security researchers.

entry.title: Knowledge Diversion: A Novel Paradigm for Pre-training Decomposable Image Generation Models

author.name: Yucheng Xie, Fu Feng, Ruixiao Shi, Jing Wang, Xin Geng, Yong Rui

entry.summary: The paper proposes Knowledge Diversion (KDiv), a condition-aware pre-training paradigm that factorizes generative image models into decomposable components during pre-training rather than after. This makes transferable and task-specific knowledge separable from the start, enabling selective reuse and more efficient downstream adaptation across diverse domains and conditions.

entry.title: Measuring Data Diversity with Embeddings: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Diversity Measures

author.name: Cantao Su, Anna Wegmann, Esther Ploeger, Dong Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper systematizes the fragmented landscape of embedding-based data diversity measurement by proposing a taxonomy of 21 measures organized into four computational families, and introduces EmbDivBench, a benchmark evaluating these measures along three conceptually distinct components of diversity. This enables principled selection of diversity measures for data curation, test design, and generalization studies.

entry.title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic API Use

author.name: Tianhe Lu, Sakuna Harinda Jayasundara, Eric Spero, Ewan Tempero, Robert Biddle, Giovanni Russello

entry.summary: The authors build 48,000 matched program pairs spanning four languages and ten cryptographic API misuse categories, and show that internal representation differences between insecure and secure programs yield consistent repair vectors. A shared steering direction can be used to nudge code models toward safer cryptographic API usage without retraining.

entry.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction

author.name: Yotam Peled, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: LiftDiff trains a discrete denoising diffusion model to generate base matrices for lifted product quantum LDPC codes, with reverse diffusion guided by an energy function over code properties such as girth, degree, and sparsity. This offers a generative route to discovering high-rate, sufficient-distance quantum error-correcting codes beyond hand-designed algebraic constructions.

entry.title: RARE: Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Rubric Evolution for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Xueyun Tian, Bingbing Xu, Chuyue Li, Jiaming Liu, Chao Zhang, Weijia Feng, MingHua Ma, Yu Zhao, Jingchu Wang, Ruihua Huang, Yuanzhuo Wang, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: RARE tackles rubric-based RL for open-ended generation, where some criteria become non-discriminative as training progresses and dynamic rubric revision risks discarding useful criteria. The method adapts rubrics conservatively so that evolving criteria restore discrimination without destroying informative ones.

entry.title: CODA: Cohort- and Drift-aware Foundation Model for Multimodal Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Changshuo Liu, Jiaqi Zhu, Wenqiao Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: Introduces a multimodal clinical foundation model that explicitly models population-level cohort structure alongside patient-specific deviations, mirroring how clinicians reason over similar patients. The system also addresses distribution drift, aiming to improve real-world clinical reasoning beyond per-sample prediction.

entry.title: Towards instance-dependent regret optimality in Episodic MDPs with Posterior Sampling

author.name: Victor Boone, Cyrille Kone, Waris Radji, Odalric-Ambrym Maillard, Dorian Baudry

entry.summary: Proposes pi0-PSRL, a posterior-sampling RL variant that decouples the test for when to explore from the policy used during exploration episodes, following a fixed reference policy while exploring. Proves instance-dependent regret guarantees for finite-horizon episodic MDPs, addressing a limitation of standard PSRL.

entry.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning

author.name: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju, Kai Ye, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in bimanual imitation learning where models exploit incidental timing schedules in demonstrations as shortcut cues, creating spurious cross-arm coupling. It introduces Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that retimes arm-local segments while preserving task-required constraints. CTR improves Diffusion Policy and Action Chunking Transformer training.

entry.title: Preservation and loss of algorithmic structure in experimental diffusion of joint-action norms

author.name: Dhara Yu, Bill D. Thompson

entry.summary: A large-scale human-subjects study of how novel social norms diffuse through populations, using program synthesis to characterize the procedures participants develop. Shows diffusion selects against complex algorithms early, with inherited procedures becoming structurally simplified during interactions.

entry.title: Beyond Clean Accuracy: The Practical Challenges and Benefits of Pixel-Based Language Models

author.name: Haowen Tang, Wei Xia, Raoyuan Zhao, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Yihong Liu

entry.summary: Systematically examines pixel-based language models through fine-tuning behavior, typographical robustness, and zero-shot crosslingual transfer. Finds they need longer training and broader labeled coverage than text-based models, with delayed learning and learning-rate-dependent failures, and that task-relevant information is less accessible in pretrained pixel representations.

entry.title: EGIP: An Evidence-Grounded Interaction Protocol for Clinical Agents

author.name: Zecheng Ren, Ruichen Cong, Yi Min Chen, Jing Zhang, Feiyang Chen, Wutong Zhang, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, Jiong Lou, Jie LI, Qun Jin

entry.summary: EGIP is an interaction protocol for clinical LLM agents that enforces role-specific information boundaries, exposes diagnostic actions without revealing results, and retrieves examination findings from stored clinical records. By separating evidence acquisition from decision-making, it prevents final-answer accuracy from conflating diagnostic reasoning quality with interaction-environment effects. This addresses a real evaluation confound in interactive medical AI.

entry.title: Beyond Factual Accuracy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Perspective Alignment in LLMs

author.name: Sunghoon Kim, Sangyeop Kim

entry.summary: PerspectiveBench quantifies how well LLMs adhere to user-specified perspectives in scenarios where multiple valid reasoning paths coexist, introducing a Perspective Alignment Score. Experiments show SOTA models include requested content but fail to exclude unwanted perspectives, and RAG improves factual grounding without fixing perspective control.

entry.title: Do LLMs Reproduce the Age Gap in Loneliness? Evaluating Survey Simulation against European Survey Data

author.name: Yuliya Li, Achim Rettinger, Dominik Beyer

entry.summary: The study tests whether LLM survey simulation reproduces within-country age gaps in loneliness from the 2022 EU Loneliness Survey across four countries. Mistral Small 4 and GPT-5.6 Terra reverse the true younger-adult-higher ordering under age-specified simulation, showing that matching survey averages masks failure on demographic substructure.

entry.title: Shaping the Document, Not the Model: Optimized Suffixes for Context Following

author.name: Gia-Bao Dinh Ho, Sekh Mainul Islam, Masahiro Kaneko, Timothy Baldwin, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: The authors ask whether a document alone, without instructions or model access at inference time, can steer a language model to follow the document even against its parametric knowledge. They optimize document suffixes via discrete token search, generalizing from single questions to passage sets, multi-hop questions, and later conversation turns on counterfactual passages.

entry.title: Bridged Self-Distillation for On-Policy Learning

author.name: Runsheng Chen (Technical University of Munich, Germany), Yihong Liu (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Raoyuan Zhao (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Michael A. Hedderich (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Hinrich Sch\"utze (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Matthias Grabmair (Technical University of Munich, Germany)

entry.summary: Bridged Self-Distillation (BSD) is a unified framework for distilling reasoning from any teacher that provides traces: the teacher's reasoning is supplied as privileged context, the student generates its own rollups, and learning proceeds on-policy. This sidesteps mismatches where teacher solutions are hard to imitate or teacher token probabilities are unavailable or incompatible.

entry.title: Monsoon: Scalable Spontaneous Speech Collection for Low-Resource ASR in 50 Languages

author.name: Shobhit Banga, Manas Dhir, Aaditya Pareek, Amritansh Walecha, Bhaskar Singh, Hanuman Sidh, Manmeet Kaur, Sagar Jain, Supriya Paul, Vanshika Chhabra, Utkarsh Singh

entry.summary: Monsoon is a framework for collecting transcribed spontaneous speech at scale across 50 languages, using paired-contributor conversations, automated screening, multi-level human transcript review, and coverage-based segment selection. Its quality stages reduce semantic WER by 10-39% relative to a conventional protocol, and Whisper fine-tuned on Monsoon data outperforms an architecture-matched baseline trained on public corpora.

entry.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement

author.name: Jaeyeon Kim, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Luoyi Zhang, Chan-Jan Hsu, Fernando Ruiloba Portilla, Jinchuan Tian, Shinji Watanabe, Carlos Busso

entry.summary: LLT is a four-stage pipeline for building post-training datasets for audio reasoning, combining dense multi-aspect audio descriptions, harder questions, synthesized incorrect reasoning traces, and thought-continuation to elicit cognitive behaviors. It targets the perceptual errors that currently limit large audio-language models. The result is improved audio understanding and reasoning from post-trained models.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models with Indigenous Community Cosmovision through Constitutional AI

author.name: Silvia Fern\'andez-Sabido, Jorge Reyes-Maga\~na, Jes\'us Adri\'an Chay Tun, Jean Carlos Buenfil, Victor Gonz\'alez Nahuat, Francisco Morales

entry.summary: This work builds a cultural constitution of 12 principles from interviews with five Indigenous leaders in Latin America and implements a Constitutional AI pipeline (SFT plus direct preference optimization) to align model responses with that cosmovision. It addresses the anglocentric bias of LLM training corpora on questions of territory, authority, and nature. The paper demonstrates a concrete method for pluralistic, community-grounded alignment.

entry.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms

author.name: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies functional CAD design, where LLM agents must build mechanisms that actually perform their intended physical function, not merely look plausible. The proposed FunCAD-Harness translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical simulation tests and uses simulation feedback for iterative revision. It includes a benchmark for systematically evaluating functional correctness.

entry.title: Memory Internalization via Test-Time Training for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Haonan Zhao, Jiaxuan Chen, Qingyang Liu, Shuochen Chang, Siyu Sun, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

entry.summary: MIT^3 is a per-video test-time training framework that writes a long video into compact, video-specific adaptive parameters, enabling video-free, text-only question answering without repeatedly encoding frames or retrieving evidence per question. The work explores where video knowledge should be stored and how visual evidence should shape the internalized memory, moving beyond text-synthesized memory approaches.

entry.title: Reusing Assurance Evidence in AI Pipelines: Validity Conditions, a Fail-Closed Release Gate, and a Replay of 714 Public Data Version Control Pipelines

author.name: Atanu Mukhopadhyay, Shravya Reddy Nalla

entry.summary: The paper formalizes when signed assurance evidence can be safely reused across AI pipeline changes, defines validity conditions and sufficient conditions for change-local re-execution, and implements a fail-closed release gate using Ed25519 signatures. A replay of 714 public pipelines measures how often dependency-declaration failures occur, blocking eight of nine manipulation scenarios.

entry.title: World Models with Configurable Perception

author.name: Yijun Shen, Delong Chen, Xianming Hu, Kai Zhang, Pascale Fung

entry.summary: ConfigWM introduces task-conditioned state extraction for world models: a language description of the task acts as a configuration signal steering how visual embeddings are abstracted into world states, filtering task-irrelevant information. This addresses the brittleness of non-adaptive encoders that get distracted by irrelevant observations during planning. A conceptual improvement to world model architecture.

entry.title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding

author.name: Huachen Gao, Yang Yang, Xiaoqian Liang, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang, Qi Zhang, Baorui Ma, Anpei Chen, Wei Yang

entry.summary: HRoPE shifts geometric relative positional encoding in multi-view transformers from sensor-centric formulations (camera frustums, ray depth) to surface-aware encoding, representing each patch's local geometry as a slanted 3D plane grounded in classical multi-view support-window assumptions. This grounds cross-view token attention in physical surface geometry rather than only observation geometry.

entry.title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training

author.name: Zhizhuo Kou, Heming Li, Jian Yang, Junyu Luo, Jingshu Peng, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: This paper studies how post-training stages (SFT, DPO, RL) affect whether chat models match a user's dialect or informal style instead of defaulting to Standard English. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes responses, yet after likelihood adjustment the DPO update still favors matching certain dialects like British and AAVE, which has fairness implications for training data and evaluation.

entry.title: CAPS: Clinically-Verifiable Anatomy-Prioritized Synthesis for Missing MRI Imputation in Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Arthur Longuefosse, Mario Rub\'en Paz Campos, \'Alvaro Garc\'ia-Mart\'in, Jesus Bescos

entry.summary: CAPS is a multi-modal generative framework for imputing missing MRI modalities in brain tumor segmentation that reconciles segmentation precision with clinical interpretability. It uses a hybrid objective combining L1, anatomy-preserving, and dual-Dice terms to enforce structural priors, addressing the compromise between opaque segmentation-only systems and blurry diagnostically unreliable synthesis. This addresses a real clinical deployment barrier in neuro-oncology where complete four-modality protocols are often unavailable.

entry.title: What Novice Operators See Changes What the Policy Learns: A User Study of Keypoint Hand Visual Representation for Teleoperated Demonstration

author.name: Amane Yamaguchi, Shohei Kamiguchi, Masashi Hamaya, Shigeo Yoshida, Takuji Narumi, Mai Nishimura

entry.summary: Using the PointHand teleoperation interface that renders a robot hand as sparse keypoints matching policy observations, the authors run a 2,200-trial user study with 18 novices and 4 experts under three visual renderings in a mug-in-box task. Novices shown only thumb-and-index-finger keypoint emphasis produced demonstrably different demonstration quality than those shown the full hand, and these interface choices propagated into learned policy quality. The study establishes that teleoperator-facing visualization is a controllable factor in imitation-learning data quality.

entry.title: Temporal Difference Learning of Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Value Functions

author.name: Elias Fontanari, Pietro Noah Crestaz, Matteo Saveriano, Andrea Del Prete

entry.summary: The paper develops a temporal-difference method for learning probabilistic reach-avoid value functions, relaxing the worst-case adversarial disturbance assumption of classical Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and its neural extensions. By treating disturbances stochastically rather than adversarially, the approach computes less conservative reach-avoid sets while still supporting runtime task-feasibility monitoring for robots under uncertainty. This addresses both conservatism and the computational burden of classical HJR methods.

entry.title: CAPSafe: A Benchmark for Contextual Action and Plan Safety Reasoning in Embodied Agents

author.name: Youmna Farag, Svetlana Stoyanchev, Simon Keizer, Mohan Li, Rama Doddipatla

entry.summary: CAPSafe is a benchmark evaluating safety reasoning in LLM-powered embodied agents at two levels: whether individual actions are safe given environmental context, and whether agents generate safe long-horizon plans for hazardous household tasks. Hazards are situational, can co-occur, and carry severity annotations. Evaluations of nine closed and open-source LLMs reveal substantial shortcomings.

entry.title: Ask to Learn: Query-Based Collaborative Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kaicheng Zhang, Hongqian Niu, Laixi Shi, Didong Li, Guannan Qu, Zhun Deng

entry.summary: The paper proposes query-based collaborative RL, where a learner with an offline dataset can adaptively query state-time pairs from a collaborator following a fixed, possibly suboptimal policy, avoiding costly or unsafe environment interaction. The work studies how to acquire complementary information efficiently to overcome offline data coverage limits.

entry.title: Modeling Authentic Research Trajectories: A Graph View of Research Ideation

author.name: Ruochen Li, Zhiyu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes modeling the authentic research trajectory, the evidence-backed closed-loop path from an initial idea to the published one, as a graph structure that existing LLM research agents fail to capture because they only evolve the idea text. The framework aims to make ideation agents mirror how real researchers run experiments, derive insights, and revise ideas.

entry.title: When PTQ Calibration Helps or Hurts: Dose-Driven Collapse and Validation-Gated Abstention in Quantized Text Embedders

author.name: Hyojung Han, Ryangkyung Kang, Youngeun Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: Studies learned post-training quantization calibration for text embedders at 4-bit across three models and 161 runs, showing outcomes range from gains to catastrophic collapse depending on the functional displacement of the quantized model; on EmbeddingGemma the same grid spans +1.47 to -71.53 NDCG@10. The paper proposes a dose-based measure and a validation-gated abstention rule to decide whether to calibrate at all.

entry.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning

author.name: Shao-Jun Xia, Yuner Zhang, Huixin Zhang, Di Wang, Yifan Jiang, Liangxi Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AMOD, reframing automated multi-agent system design around identifying functionally necessary responsibilities, their allocation, and when they should change, treating organization itself as a first-class design object rather than only searching over architectures. The paper argues for a shift from architecture search toward organizational learning.

entry.title: Give the Model a Finger: Developmentally Aligned Evaluation of Counting in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yingxin Jia, Hui Geng, Wenxin Yang, Mohan Zhang

entry.summary: Inspired by how children learn counting through epistemic actions like pointing, this work gives VLMs dumb marking tools in a training-free agent loop, turning the visible marks on the image into an auditable trace of serial visual reasoning. The framework classifies each tag against point-level ground truth, providing an interpretable diagnostic of where counting procedures break down.

entry.title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?

author.name: Yeyin Eva Zhu, Rishabh Ranawat

entry.summary: This paper builds a large RTL (hardware description) repair dataset and benchmark with simulation and formal-equivalence evaluation, then uses it to expose measurement confounds in how repair quality is scored. It shows simulation and formal scoring can give opposite conclusions about specification benefits, and that reset-aware rescoring explains most disagreements. It also analyzes mined model failures to show what benchmark deltas actually capture.

entry.title: GRaSP: Latency-Aware Optimization for Geo-Distributed Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Hardik Ruparel, Raj Kumar Pandey, Pramod Kumar

entry.summary: GRaSP formalizes the Geo-RAG Selection Problem, a drop-in re-scoring layer that decays retrieval relevance by wide-area latency and adds cost penalties under cardinality budgets and per-region caps, with no retraining. The paper proves the base formulation is a linear objective over a partition matroid solvable optimally by an O(N log N) greedy algorithm, correcting a knapsack-based NP-hard framing. It addresses the tension between retrieval quality, tail latency, egress cost, and data residency in geo-distributed RAG.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Optimized Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Jelena Markovic-Voronov, Petros Prastakos, Kayhan Behdin, Jincheng Cao, Zhipeng Wang, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Wenhui Zhu, Rahul Mazumder

entry.summary: OptEP formulates post-training expert pruning of MoE language models as a subset-selection problem optimized via a scalable continuous relaxation over differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by reconstruction-based weight updates. It reduces stored expert parameters across multiple MoE architectures and tasks while preserving performance.

entry.title: Scaling Graph Reasoning in Language Models with Learnable Graph Positional Encodings

author.name: Javier Porras-Valenzuela, Arush Arora, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: The paper augments language reasoning models with scalable, permutation-equivariant graph positional encodings computed by a GNN followed by a Graph Transformer, modulating attention logits and fusing structural information into hidden states. This eliminates serialized adjacency descriptions whose length grows with edge count and whose performance degrades on larger graphs. The approach enables solving larger graph reasoning tasks than in-context serialization permits.

entry.title: SLM-SS: Token-Based Speech Separation with Speech Language Models

author.name: Chenda Li, Tianhua Li, Yiming Chen, Wei Wang, Jiahe Wang, Xin Zhou, Yanmin Qian

entry.summary: SLM-SS reformulates speech separation as token-based generative modeling with speech language models, discretizing speech into multi-codebook tokens and serializing multi-speaker targets via Serialized Output Training. The approach optimizes for downstream intelligibility rather than signal-level metrics, where waveform-optimized systems can be suboptimal. This connects speech separation to the emerging speech-LM paradigm.

entry.title: Identifying Dependent Components from Multi-domain Linear Mixtures

author.name: Danru Xu, Lauri Parkkonen, Sara Magliacane, Aapo Hyv\"arinen

entry.summary: The authors generalize independent component analysis to multi-domain linear mixtures with dependent latent components, using domain-specific scalings to separate sources without parametric dependency assumptions, multi-view data, or interventions. This extends identifiability theory for source separation to settings like multi-sensor recordings. It is a solid theoretical contribution to representation learning and causal/disentanglement research.

entry.title: Racer: Hunting GPU Kernel Bugs with Symbolic Equivalence Checking

author.name: Tuan Truong Vu, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: Racer proposes symbolic equivalence checking for GPU kernels, executing a kernel and its reference symbolically to catch logical bugs that differential testing misses, such as errors smaller than the numerical tolerance required for optimized kernels. This addresses a reliability gap in the repeatedly rewritten GPU operators underpinning AI services. Verified kernel equivalence is directly relevant to AI infrastructure correctness.

entry.title: Do Knowledge and Reasoning Oriented Benchmarks Induce Stable Representation Signatures in LLMs?

author.name: Parsa Rahimi, Azim Dehghani Amirabad

entry.summary: The paper probes whether knowledge versus reasoning tasks produce stable internal signatures in five 7B-31B LLMs, using task-held-out probes with permuted labels and per-permutation layer reselection. Raw probes separate an MMLU partition well, but prompt text alone predicts it nearly as well, with activation advantages of only 0.017-0.070 macro-F1 — challenging claims of reusable knowledge/reasoning representations.

entry.title: PAC Learning with Query Feedback

author.name: Chase Hutton, Adam Melrod, Han Shao

entry.summary: The paper studies multiclass PAC learning where each training example returns a binary answer about whether its true label lies in a chosen query subset. It introduces the query dimension, generalizing the bandit DS dimension, and proves matching Omega(D/eps) lower and Otilde(D^2/eps) upper sample-complexity bounds, with improved bounds for structured query families.

entry.title: What "Form'' of Uncertainty Does Conformal Prediction Quantify?

author.name: Soroush H. Zargarbashi, Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Rebekka Burkholz, Aleksandar Bojchevski

entry.summary: This paper connects the set-size difference between full and split conformal prediction to Bayesian posterior variance, showing that set size aggregates model accuracy gains against a formability effect that vanishes with stronger models or more calibration data. This clarifies what epistemic versus aleatoric uncertainty conformal set sizes actually quantify.

entry.title: First-Order LoRA Training with Phone NPUs

author.name: Xu Zheng, Wei Cheng, Zhuomin Chen, Dongkuan Xu, Mo Sha, Jingchao Ni, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: This systems paper enables first-order LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs entirely on-device by running the three frozen-weight matrix products on a phone NPU while keeping the training graph, adapters, and optimizer on the CPU. Custom input-gradient kernels reuse resident weight tiles, working around the NPU inference interface's lack of gradient support, enabling private on-device learning.

entry.title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Csaba Balogh

entry.summary: The paper identifies representation-level blind spots where language models treat semantically distinct inputs interchangeably, framing the issue as feature-basis orientation and adding a differentiable Gini-based regularizer to SAE training drawn from algebraic error-detection theory. Evaluation on GPT-2, Gemma 2, and Qwen 2.5 shows reduced blind spots via frozen multi-seed testing.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Hui Yang, Wan Tian, Tao Ren, Zhongyi Li, Yijie Peng

entry.summary: CSPO adaptively calibrates sequence-level clipping bounds in RL fine-tuning of reasoning LLMs using conformal prediction on recent training statistics, replacing fixed clipping bands whose tail probabilities drift as the score distribution evolves. The band targets a specified marginal tail budget and adapts to policy drift, including length-conditional calibration. This improves on GRPO-style methods for verifiable-reward training.

entry.title: Operator-Mismatch Contrastive Learning for World-Relative Trajectory Coherence

author.name: One Octadion, Firmansyah Sundana, Novanto Yudistira

entry.summary: The paper formalizes operator-blindness in world model evaluation: scorers can rank plausible futures well while failing to distinguish trajectories consistent with the actually governing dynamics rule from those of other rules. It introduces Operator-Mismatch Contrastive learning with valid-but-wrong-operator hard negatives and a matching evaluation protocol. This is a meaningful critique and remedy for how world models are trained and judged.

entry.title: A Simple and Unified Method for Gradient-Variation Regret

author.name: Hang Yu, Peng Zhao

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified method for gradient-variation online learning based on surrogate losses with a quadratic movement penalty, yielding gradient-variation regret bounds in both non-stationary (dynamic regret) and universal (unknown curvature) settings that previously required separate techniques. This simplifies and connects two active online-learning literatures. The optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction it induces applies broadly.

entry.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs

author.name: Zhuoshi Pan, ZhiYuan Feng, Yukuo Cen, Honglin Lin, Junru Lu, Zhongxia Chen, Shuo Yang, H. Vicky Zhao, Jie Tang

entry.summary: HarnessPro is a label-free method for recursively self-improving agent harnesses while reducing execution cost, using LLM-generated tests in place of ground-truth solutions. Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories, plan updates with different performance-cost priorities, and implement candidate harnesses, with normalized weighted squared-distance selection returning a cost-conditioned Pareto set rather than a single harness. This advances agent infrastructure research by jointly optimizing capability and cost in recursive self-improvement loops.

entry.title: VERDICT: Visual Extraction-Result Decoder with Integrated Confidence and Traceable Evidence

author.name: Harikrishnan P M, Goutham Vignesh, Siva Prasad, Zishan Ahmad, Mahesh Basveshwar Deshmukhe, Varun V, Rohit Agrawal, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: VERDICT is a plug-in framework that adds evidence grounding and calibrated confidence to enterprise document extraction pipelines without modifying the underlying extractor. A small vision-language model localizes the document evidence for each extracted value and calibrates confidence in both the value and its evidence. This addresses a real trust and auditability gap in production systems that use frontier multimodal models for schema-guided field extraction.

entry.title: IMPULSE: Push First, Then Predict in V-JEPA 2 Feature Space

author.name: Tingan Jin

entry.summary: IMPULSE enables a predictor in frozen V-JEPA 2 feature space to infer object physical properties through interaction: a Bayesian contact memory summarizes three short calibration pushes, and a lightweight pose head injects pose into the predictor. In a pre-registered held-out evaluation on 512 fresh objects, the memory lowers 1-second feature-forecast error.

entry.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles

author.name: C\'elian Vasson, Daniil Ognev, Kentaro Inui, Benjamin Heinzerling

entry.summary: Uses Sajaniemi's taxonomy of eleven variable roles (accumulator, traversal, best-so-far, etc.) to study whether language models encode semantic program structure, introducing annotation rules and a 126,926-file natural-code corpus across five languages. Residual probes outperform individual sparse-autoencoder features and lexical baselines, and combining SAE features closes much of the gap. The work connects mechanistic interpretability with program understanding.

entry.title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ziang Gao, Pengqi Liu, Archer Yi Yang, Mouloud Belbahri, Jesse C. Cresswell, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: The paper examines a gap in fairness guarantees for conformal prediction: Mondrian calibration provides group-level finite-sample coverage but substantial disparities can persist within finer strata. The authors introduce propensity standardization to diagnose how population composition distorts aggregate comparisons, and propose Tilted Mondrian to mitigate fine-grained unfairness relative to standard group-wise calibration.

entry.title: On Reasoning Correctness Directions

author.name: Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Zayd M. K. Zuhri, Rifo Genadi, Abzal Nurgazy, Ali Mekky, Alham Fikri Aji, Zangir Iklassov, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Using ChainSearch, a controlled arithmetic reasoning task with explicit search and backtracking, the authors train a 3M-parameter model and rigorously probe whether internal linear directions encode reasoning correctness. They find statistically significant correctness directions that are decodable, but evidence that they are not straightforwardly causally useful for steering.

entry.title: RECAP: Reciprocal Sparse Attention and Hierarchical Caching for Efficient Video Diffusion

author.name: Tiange Xu, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free method combining sparse attention with hierarchical temporal caching for video diffusion transformers, addressing how sparsification errors propagate when sparse-attention outputs become sources for cross-step reuse. Exploits directional alignment of errors across nearby denoising steps to share correction information rather than recompute it.

entry.title: CoDA: A Human-LM Collaborative Codebook Development Assistant for Domain-Specific Text Annotation

author.name: Jaspreet Ranjit, Swaminathan Chellappa, Augusto Rivas Costante, Chandan Manjunath, Laura Onasch-Vera, Hailey Winetrobe Nadel, Eric Rice, Swabha Swayamdipta

entry.summary: Presents CoDA, an open-source tool where domain experts and LMs iteratively develop annotation codebooks by reviewing incorrect model predictions and incorporating expert feedback. Addresses the neglected problem that annotation guidelines are assumed but hard to produce for expert-knowledge concepts.

entry.title: Analyzing Repetition and Interference Effects in Memory-Constrained User Simulators

author.name: Cara Su-Yi Leong, Nicholas Tomlin, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: Evaluates memory-constrained LLM user simulators against human memory phenomena, testing sensitivity to repetition and interference from competing information. Finds some simulators match human overall accuracy and effect magnitudes, but models forget facts while humans misremember them, yielding different error patterns; a challenge benchmark is released.

entry.title: PV-Decoding: Progressive Verification Decoding with Decode Gating for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Renxi Liu, Yiming Li, Shengyin Sun, Chen Chen, Xian Wang, Shuai Yang, Huiling Zhen, Xianzhi Yu, Yaoyuan Wang, Weizhe Lin, Xiaosong Li

entry.summary: PV-Decoding is a confidence-driven speculative decoding framework for block diffusion language models that partitions masked positions into directly decoded, speculative, and unresolved tokens, applying progressive verification with decode gating. This addresses the problem that speculative tokens within a diffusion block may depend on each other, causing error propagation under aggressive acceptance. It targets the key inference-efficiency bottleneck limiting dLLM practicality.

entry.title: Where Are Language-Specific Features Represented in Multilingual LLMs? Everywhere

author.name: Mikaela Martins, Jonathan Dunn

entry.summary: Challenges the view that multilingual LLMs encode language-specific features mainly in initial and final layers with language-agnostic intermediate layers. Via four experiments, including a large-scale language identification study over 200 languages, the authors show language-specific information permeates all layers in Llama 3.2 1B.

entry.title: Balance-Aware Pivot Selection for Parallel Diffusion LLM Decoding

author.name: Yejin Lee, Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes Balance-Aware Pivot Decoding (BPD) for diffusion language models, replacing pure confidence-based token commitment with selection of central pivots within contiguous masked intervals. This positional balancing accounts for how token choices shape the remaining decoding schedule and inter-token dependencies.

entry.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development

author.name: Yuchi Wang, Rongyao Fang, Weihao Yu, Xilin Wei, Tiancheng Gu, Dingkang Yang, Hang Zhang, Dayiheng Liu, Hongsheng Li, Shuai Bai

entry.summary: RefCraft is a benchmark of 300 realistic multimodal webpage-development tasks that combine natural-language instructions with screenshots from one to five reference webpages, testing how agents incorporate visual references into generation. It moves beyond idealized screenshot-reconstruction settings toward the common workflow of developing from visual examples, with apparent involvement from Baidu researchers.

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks

author.name: Rohan Menon, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces ASR_STEP, a jailbreak evaluation metric that penalizes each additional victim-model call while retaining binary success judgments, reflecting that repeated calls give deployed defenses more chances to intervene. Evaluating GCG, PAIR, and PAP on JailBreakBench across three model families, discounting substantially lowers GCG's and iterative PAIR's scores while single-step PAP is unaffected. This reframes attack strength comparisons by cost sensitivity.

entry.title: REST: Reliability-Guided Spatial Transcriptomics Supervision for Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathological HE-Stained Images

author.name: Lanfeng Zhong, Xiangyu Sun, Guixuan Xu, Rongzhao Zhang, Jie Xu, Shaoting Zhang, Guotai Wang

entry.summary: REST is a training framework for predicting spatially resolved gene expression from routine HE-stained histopathology images, using a Biological Program Bank and reliability-guided supervision that accounts for unequal assay coverage and spot informativeness. This enables molecular characterization of tumors from standard pathology slides. The work connects computational pathology with biomarker discovery and prognosis.

entry.title: A Principled Optimal Transport Framework for Frame Selection in Long Video Understanding

author.name: Ziwei Zhao, Yuhang Liu

entry.summary: The paper recasts query-aware frame selection for long-video understanding with multimodal LLMs as a structured evidence-collection problem solved via optimal transport, replacing heuristic score-then-sample pipelines with an explicit optimization objective.

entry.title: EndoWorld-JEPA: Motion-Guided Global-Local Latent World Modeling for Endoscopic Video Representation Learning

author.name: Jie Wang, Shilong Yang, Tao Zhou, Juan Yu, Rong Qu, Jianfeng Ren, Zhicheng Zhang, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: EndoWorld-JEPA is presented as the first latent world-model pre-training framework for endoscopic video, reformulating passive video pre-training as causal motion-guided latent-state prediction. It conditions predictions on optical-flow-derived motion signals instead of recorded actions or robot kinematics, separating image-plane displacement from residual tissue and instrument motion. This brings action-conditioned JEPA ideas to surgical/medical video.

entry.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models

author.name: StreamEval Team

entry.summary: StreamEval is a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks including avatar dialogue, world generation, and instruction editing, with 300 scripted test cases of 15-300 seconds featuring incrementally arriving multimodal requests. It evaluates task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination via ten task-specific metrics.

entry.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering

author.name: Guian Fang, Shengju Qian, Dongyue Lu, Junchao Huang, Lutao Jiang, Xin Wang, Yiren Song, Li Jiang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: SolarRenderer is a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs to turn coarse structural inputs from game engines or coding agents into realistic video in few steps. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway at frame positions with only plain-text description, avoiding engine-specific conditioning and costly distillation.

entry.title: EchoNav: Evidential BEV Completion from Historical Observations for Visual Navigation

author.name: Diwen Liu, Yiyang Shao, Borui Wang, Chi Zhang, Yunhui Liu

entry.summary: EchoNav combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view representation predicted from short RGB sequences for navigation in cluttered environments. A decoder adapts frozen VGGT-Omega features and merges historical residual proposals with a learned no-update option, producing local maps in the ego frame without depth, camera poses, or explicit warping. The evidential formulation predicts occupancy with confidence and treats observed free space separately.

entry.title: High-Precision RCM Motion for Ophthalmic Robotics via Hierarchical QP Control and Authority-Guided Recovery Planning

author.name: Huanyu Tian, Adriana Namour, Lingyun Zeng, Zicong Wu, Sebastien Ourselin, Lyndon da Cruz, Christos Bergeles

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a failure mode in ophthalmic robotic surgery where remote-centre-of-motion and tip-tracking objectives conflict at otherwise nonsingular configurations, naming it a constraint-induced task singularity, and presents a high-precision RCM servo architecture with built-in singularity recovery. An authority-guided planner selects well-conditioned arm configurations and plans RCM-consistent motions, while hierarchical QP control handles execution. This directly improves the reliability of robot-assisted eye surgery motion control.

entry.title: Safe Multi-Robot Collaboration With Uniform Exclusion Using Trust

author.name: Thomas Kaminsky, \'Aron V\'ek\'assy, Hammad Izhar, Angelia Nedi\'c, Stephanie Gil

entry.summary: The authors present a communication wrapper for robot swarms that identifies trusted incoming links under potentially compromised, time-varying communication. The wrapper applies Safe Anytime-Valid Inference to a stream of trust values from per-robot anomaly detectors, requiring only better-than-chance detectors, and provides statistical guarantees that all compromised links are uniformly excluded.

entry.title: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning

author.name: Daniel Marew, Sangjun Park, Nisal Perera, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: The paper presents FRDV, a scalable framework for retargeting large-scale human motion capture data to humanoid robots, combining rapid constrained kinematic retargeting with a dynamics validation pipeline. A custom SQP solver with parallel chunk-based processing achieves up to 9,156 frames per second, roughly 136 times faster than GAPS-like baselines, with reduced manual adjustment.

entry.title: A plug-in estimator of the non-iterative conditional expectation g-formula using long short-term memory models

author.name: Jing Li, Sophia M. Rein, Zilong Wang, Zixiao Wang, Sean McGrath, James M. Robins, Thomas Kolokotrones, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Miguel A. Hern\'an

entry.summary: This paper develops an LSTM-based plug-in implementation of the NICE g-formula estimator for causal effects of sustained treatment strategies under treatment-confounder feedback. It examines when such flexible sequential deep learning models yield valid statistical inference in longitudinal causal settings, with an applied epidemiology-oriented author team.

entry.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: FairStress is a new benchmark from Ai2 that measures demographic differences in how LLMs justify and explain their decisions, revealing disparities in reasoning quality even when final choices appear fair on the surface. This shifts fairness evaluation from outcome-level to explanation-level analysis of model decision-making.

entry.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents

author.name: Ran Zhou, Zehui Kong, Fanyu Lin, Jiaheng Liu, Zhen Zhang, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: SPEM is a procedural memory framework for LLM agents that maintains atomic skill memories plus a Skill-DAG memory capturing dependencies, execution order, and data-flow constraints from successful executions. For new tasks it reuses high-confidence DAG templates or retrieves and composes atomic skills, reducing token and runtime overhead versus full skill loading.

entry.title: A Semi-Analytical Inference Framework for Structural Causal Models

author.name: Tatiana Boura, Robert Peharz

entry.summary: This work performs probabilistic inference directly on structural causal models via a message-passing scheme that represents structural mechanisms and densities in a shared finite-dimensional function space. Forward propagation uses a numerical realization of the Law of the Unconscious Statistician with spline-projected densities, also yielding backward messages for the same framework.

entry.title: PW-Pruning: Phase-Aware Expert Selection for Speech-Centric Omni-Modal Models

author.name: Junjie Cao, Fengping Tian, Wenjie Zhou, Xuanfan Ni, Chenyang Lyu, Siyou Liu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: PW-Pruning is a phase-aware expert pruning method for speech-centric omni-modal models that builds separate importance statistics for acoustic-prefill and answer-generation phases, then combines phase-weighted gains to select a static expert bank. Applied to Qwen3-Omni, retaining 32 of 128 experts per layer improves MMAU-mini and MMSU accuracy over pooled selection by 3.20 and 4.38 points after fine-tuning. It targets memory reduction while preserving quality.

entry.title: When Models Know but Can't Linearly Say: Relational Encoding Limits Linear Vulnerability Classification in Code LLMs

author.name: Rui Melo, Andre Catarino, Claudia Mamede, Corina Pasareanu, Rui Abreu

entry.summary: This interpretability study analyzes 8 code models (6.7B-15B parameters) on C programs and finds that vulnerability information is more accessible as a paired relational signal (whether code A is riskier than B) than as a globally separable categorical label under linear probing. Models encode code patterns with high fidelity, but absolute vulnerability classification is structurally harder. This has implications for how vulnerability detection systems should probe model internals.

entry.title: Pairwise Learning Increases Data Efficiency in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Robert Bain, Marjan Rashidi, Elizabeth Chrastil

entry.summary: The authors reframe regression as aggregated relative rankings via a pairwise comparison framework, improving data efficiency in small-sample settings. On UTKFace, pairwise learning generates over a billion comparisons without extra supervision, and a lightweight ResNet10 trained from scratch achieves a 3.64-year MAE, surpassing models with large-scale pretraining. The approach benefits both regression and classification across architectures.

entry.title: Auditing Where Concept Bottleneck Accuracy Comes From on CUB

author.name: Sascha Saralajew, Eleonora Poeta, Eliana Pastor, Ammar Shaker

entry.summary: This audit examines whether Concept Bottleneck Models and Concept Embedding Models on CUB-200 actually predict labels from exposed concept scores supported by visual evidence of those concepts. The authors find CUB annotations too noisy to explain reported accuracy, with class-level training labels agreeing with per-image annotations on only about 82 percent of image-concept pairs.

entry.title: RayCo4D: Ray-Conditioned Continuous Motion Model for Monocular 4D Dynamic Reconstruction

author.name: Yuanxiang Ni, Xianliang Huang, Ruihan Hou, Feng Xie, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: RayCo4D reconstructs dynamic 3D scenes from monocular video by separating visual measurements from latent 3D motion states, associating fragmented long-range tracks with shared latent motion nodes carrying SE(3) pose and velocity. Ray-constrained reference-time queries handle noisy and intermittently visible observations. This is a technically substantive advance in monocular 4D reconstruction, relevant to robotics, AR/VR, and video understanding.

entry.title: VisualEvolve: A Skill Self-Evolution Framework for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Jiawei Wang, Yucun Li, Xueqi Li, Shenghao Wang, Xinquan Gong, Dan Zhang, Zheqi Lv, Yuquan Le, Shaozu Yuan, An Zhang, Da Cao, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: VisualEvolve is a training-free framework in which vision-language models self-evolve executable visual operations and tool-use strategies as reusable external skills, using a Select-Examine-Refine loop that guards against skill-regression performance drops and evolution-evidence overload. This enables improvement without parameter updates. It contributes to the growing agentic tool-use paradigm for VLMs.

entry.title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification

author.name: Vasilii Feofanov, Zhenghan Tai, Andrei Ermakov, Irina Rish

entry.summary: The authors show that TS2Vec, a strong 2022 self-supervised method for time series classification, can be converted into a foundation model with three changes: pre-training on a synthetic corpus, feeding raw amplitude and instance-normalized views, and adapting the architecture for one-encoder reuse across variable-length datasets. This retains TS2Vec's compact convolutional design while matching foundation-model usage patterns.

entry.title: SAGE-CP: When Marginal Coverage Hides Route-Conditional Failures in Adaptive VLM Ensembles

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: SAGE-CP addresses a subtle failure of conformal prediction in adaptive VLM ensembles: a single marginal threshold can hide severe coverage failures on individual computation routes, with conditional coverage potentially falling to 1-alpha/pi for a route of prevalence pi. The pipeline freezes the router, then applies Mondrian split conformal calibration separately to early-exit and escalated inputs for route-conditional guarantees.

entry.title: Continual Test-Time Learning with Evolution Strategies

author.name: Guangya Hao, Yiting Duan, Longyan Tan, Yunbo Long, Hao Wu, Ge Zheng, Alexandra Brintrup, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes Evolution Strategy Reinforcement-based continual test-time learning for LLMs operating in open-ended environments without external supervision. It addresses the failure mode where self-generated supervision from a single drifting policy leads to collapse and forgetting, by drawing learning signals from a population-based evolution strategy instead. This targets robust unsupervised continual adaptation.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret for Semi-Bandit Learning of Monotone Stochastic Problems

author.name: Zhengjia Zhuo, Viswanath Nagarajan

entry.summary: The authors give an algorithm achieving near-optimal O-tilde(sqrt(nkT)) regret for weakly monotone and O-tilde(sqrt(nT)) for strongly monotone stochastic problems under semi-bandit feedback. The framework covers many classic problems including prophet inequality, Pandora's box, stochastic knapsack, and stochastic matching.

entry.title: TCMScience: An Autonomous Scientist for Traditional Chinese Medicine

author.name: Yanlan Kang, Ruiqi Liu, Xinpei Gu, Tzu-Yi Lei, Shuai Xu, Xukun Zhang, William Cheng-Chung Chu

entry.summary: TCMScience is an autonomous scientific knowledge-discovery agent for traditional Chinese medicine that separates LLM proposal generation from execution and release authority. Its architecture combines a trusted kernel, a scientific compiler, and claim-support contracts that verify candidate findings against source provenance, study design, and claim scope before release.

entry.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Annabelle Sujun Tang, Rohan Mahapatra, Christopher Priebe, Hanyang Xu, Manya Ghobadi, Christopher Rossbach, Hadi Esmaeilzadeh

entry.summary: Conjugate Compilation reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem, jointly optimizing the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than compiling each in isolation. An iterative loop uses measured performance of co-located shared execution to inform recompilation, unlocking stranded GPU capacity for LLM serving.

entry.title: Memory as Belief: Bayesian Evolution of Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Yiming Xu, Qian Yang, Zihan Chen, Yuefei Wu, Wenhan Zeng, Bin Shi, Bo Dong

entry.summary: BEAM reformulates memory valuation for LLM agents as a Bayesian cognitive process, replacing historical retrieval success rates with a framework that accounts for context dependency of memory usefulness and varying reliability of estimates under different evidence amounts. Inspired by the Bayesian brain hypothesis, it enables more reliable reuse of accumulated experience across tasks. This targets a real weakness in self-evolving agent memory systems.

entry.title: Follow the Mixed Groups: Ridge-Tracking Gaussian Sampling for Zero-Variance Web Rollouts

author.name: Tomas Duncun, Jonah Ellison, Owen Pell, Mateo Ruiz, Hanae Fujita, Ingrid Solberg, Caleb Nguyen

entry.summary: This companion paper to Aperture tackles zero-variance groups in GRPO for web agents, where wasted rollouts cost real searches and fetches. RIDGE keeps a Gaussian curriculum over pass rates but changes the coordinate, center, and width using Beta posteriors per prompt to concentrate sampling on questions where finite groups can still split. This directly improves the economics of RL training for web-using agents.

entry.title: Learning to Couple: Context-Adaptive Joint Denoising for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zilei Shao, Ian Li, Heng Zhao, Kewei Lian, Guy Van den Broeck, Zhe Zeng, Anji Liu

entry.summary: Codpula introduces a context-parameterized denoiser for diffusion language models that jointly models dependencies among simultaneously predicted tokens, combining a Transformer with a tractable probabilistic inference layer. Unlike prior approaches that bolt separate coupling layers onto frozen denoisers, the backbone adapts to the joint objective and coupling parameters vary with context. This addresses the conditional-independence error source in parallel token prediction.

entry.title: Provable Adversarial Detection: Prime Quantization meets Gromov--Wasserstein

author.name: Manohar Kaul, Sadbhavana Babar, Aditya Ramesh, Aditya Saibewar, Fumiyoshi Kasahara, Maki Inui, Hiroaki Kurihara

entry.summary: The paper constructs a theory-backed adversarial detection method based on the insight that perturbations cannot simultaneously preserve geometric structure in two metric spaces: a standard CNN embedding space and a novel prime-quantized space that absorbs small perturbations. Using Gromov-Wasserstein distance between these spaces, it provides provable detection guarantees for adversarial samples across CNNs and vision-language models. This moves adversarial detection from heuristics toward certified guarantees.

entry.title: SEAM: Spectral Embedding Alignment and Merging for Low-Resource TTS

author.name: Walaa Othman, Baher Mohammad, Stamatios Lefkimmiatis, Ammar Ali

entry.summary: SEAM is a zero-audio method for constructing embeddings of unseen tokens in TTS models from known subtokens, using a spectral filter to preserve temporal phonetic order and closed-form ridge regression to align with the pretrained conditioning manifold. Across three languages and two architectures it approaches baseline quality with up to four times less training data. This meaningfully lowers the barrier to extending TTS vocabularies for low-resource and cross-lingual settings.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments

author.name: Tom\`as Garriga, Munib Mesinovic, Luke De Bretton-Gordon, Gerard Sanz, Axel Brando, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: This work introduces a doubly robust learner for heterogeneous survival treatment effects when treatments are time-varying, jointly handling sequential adjustment for both treatment decisions and censoring. Existing survival learners handle only baseline treatment assignment while longitudinal effect learners assume uncensored outcomes, a gap this method fills. The problem is central to personalized medicine questions like which treatment sequence maximizes survival probability.

entry.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Adrian Remonda, Jiajun Xi, Nicklas Hansen, Marcus Greiff, Thomas Lew, John Talbot, John Subosits, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: Prior-Informed Adaptation is an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulation and then adapts it with limited real interaction via uncertainty-regularized planning. Crucially, it treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected online, rather than requiring an accurate simulator for transfer. Evaluation in autonomous racing demonstrates the approach for safety-critical physical systems where data collection is costly.

entry.title: Modeling Uncertainty Propagation in 3D Morphable Models

author.name: Megh Shukla, Edo Collins, Prashanth Chandran, Karel Petr\'anek, Sergio Orts-Escolano, Mathieu Salzmann, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: CLUE provides a closed-form approximation for mapping parameter-space variance of 3D Morphable Models to per-vertex variance, derived from the law of total variance and replacing expensive sampling or error propagation. The method is modular, fast, and accurate, and the authors integrate it into in-the-wild human mesh recovery training. Reliable per-vertex uncertainty matters for downstream 3D perception safety and filtering.

entry.title: MM-LeJEPA: Correlated Gaussian Regularization for Multimodal Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Haowen Bai, Rui Gong$, Meichen Liu, Ming-Xuan Weng, Bihan Wen, Kim-Hui Yap

entry.summary: This work extends LeJEPA, a self-supervised method using isotropic Gaussian embedding targets, to multimodal settings where tasks read both shared and modality-specific information. MM-LeJEPA models multimodal tasks as strength-weighted combinations of independent and shared components, enabling decoder-free, teacher-free multimodal joint-embedding predictive learning with correlated Gaussian regularization.

entry.title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains

author.name: Jiayi Li, Carl Kingsford

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing LLM planning frameworks assume enumerable discrete actions, which breaks in continuous-state domains, and proposes Medaka, a structured prompting framework inspired by Newell and Simon's Means-Ends Analysis that encourages recursive goal decomposition, algebraic derivation, and per-step state tracking. The work also introduces evaluation settings for native LLM planning in continuous domains.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Early Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via E-processes

author.name: Dong-Jae Lee, Gyojin Han, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: The paper reframes adaptive early stopping for reasoning LLMs as sequential evidence accumulation, running two e-processes on a shared per-chunk signal to decide when to commit or abstain from further reasoning. This avoids threshold calibration that fails to transfer across models and datasets, offering guarantees robust to test-time horizon shifts.

entry.title: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere

author.name: Arber Zela, Artavazd Maranjyan, Pol Puigdemont, David Berghaus, Valentyn Boreiko, Volkan Cevher

entry.summary: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM) reformulate damped fixed-point adaptive computation for looped transformers on the unit hypersphere, aligning with normalized transformers (nGPT) so that injection, damping, and halting become geodesic operations. The paper proves fixed-point existence and convergence results and shows empirical gains on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and related reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits

author.name: Zhehang Du, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Polar Switch is a new approach to the polynomial gradient orthogonalization used in the Muon optimizer, using polynomial circuits of symmetric matrix products on square buffers to reach high polynomial degree at lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations like Polar Express and Gram Newton-Schulz. This improves the GPU efficiency of a widely adopted LLM training optimizer.

entry.title: Compositional Activation Steering Across Languages and Behaviors with Contextual Gates

author.name: Daniil Gurgurov, Akansh Maurya, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: This work trains contextual gates that adapt the strength of fixed activation-steering directions to the current hidden state, enabling composition of multiple steering directions to control several behaviors simultaneously, including in multilingual settings. The approach outperforms constant-strength steering, prompting, and four baselines across many languages, behaviors, and models while better preserving general knowledge. It turns training-free steering vectors into a composable, state-aware control mechanism.

entry.title: MemBubble: Benchmarking How Agent Memory Shapes LLM Response Diversity

author.name: Jiajun Tan, Fei Sun, Xinyu Ma, Shixuan Zhang, Du Su, Qi Cao, Daiting Shi, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: MemBubble is a benchmark of 1,000 instances built from preferences extracted from real user-assistant conversations, testing whether agent memory narrows response diversity. It measures how memory concentrates response distributions in scenarios distinct from stored preferences, addressing a gap left by synthetic-interaction evaluations.

entry.title: CoMem: Learning to Anticipate Failures from Retrieved Experience

author.name: Yun Shen, Ming Shen, Tianjun Yao

entry.summary: Introduces CoMem (Compounding Memory), which makes retrieved cross-task experience condition the parametric reflective memory rather than being combined additively, allowing agents to anticipate failure modes more effectively. This addresses the limitation that retrieved memory and internalized parametric memory never interact in existing cross-task reflective memory agents.

entry.title: Large-Scale Biomedical RAG: Corpus Scaling, Document Representation, and Efficiency Trade-offs

author.name: Adri\'an S\'anchez-Freire, Gonzalo P\'erez-G\'omez, Aitziber Atutxa, Ander Barrena

entry.summary: A controlled large-scale study of biomedical RAG varying corpus size, document representation (abstract, flat full-text, hierarchical full-text), and reranking, evaluated on five external benchmarks plus a held-out test set with latency and storage costs measured. It provides practical guidance on effectiveness-efficiency trade-offs for biomedical retrieval systems.

entry.title: The Judge Can Debias Itself: Awareness and Self-Debiasing for Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge

author.name: Youbing Yin, Jingyu Wu, Anoop Kumar, Scott Novotney, Daben Liu, Erin Babinsky

entry.summary: The paper shows LLM judges can reduce their own systematic biases without additional training through bias-aware prompting and self-debiasing, where the judge critiques its initial judgment for bias influence. It introduces three new bias benchmarks covering authority, confidence, and formatting bias, evaluating seven bias types across three frontier models. Self-debiasing improves judge reliability while remaining lightweight.

entry.title: SynCalib: Breaking Dataset Shortcuts in LiDAR-Camera Calibration via Extrinsic-Controllable Synthesis

author.name: Huihua Zhu, Shuyang Zhang, Dongqing Chen, Zhuo Yu, Jianhao Jiao, Yilong Zhu, Siyu Teng, Xiaopin Zhong, Zongze Wu

entry.summary: SynCalib identifies a dataset shortcut problem in learned LiDAR-camera calibration: networks overfit fixed nominal extrinsics due to low extrinsic diversity in training data. It proposes a data generation framework with extrinsic-controllable synthesis to train calibration networks that generalize to real deployments.

entry.title: CrossFit-GS: Out-of-Fold Pose Estimation for COLMAP-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zijian Wu, Jinliang Wang, Mingfeng Jiang, Zidian Lin, Ying Song, Ziqian Lu

entry.summary: CrossFit-GS addresses pose-free 3D Gaussian Splatting by partitioning input sequences into interleaved subsets and maintaining two complementary submaps, so each pose is refined against a frozen submap that never saw the target frame. This out-of-fold scheme mitigates cumulative trajectory drift and error self-reinforcement, with validation safeguards rejecting unreliable updates.

entry.title: Touch-JEPA: Tactile Representation Learning from Hand-Object Video with Limited Tactile Supervision

author.name: Minseong Kweon, Qiao Feng, Yiming Huang, Lingjie Liu

entry.summary: Touch-JEPA learns tactile representations from hand-object video with limited tactile supervision via a self-supervised objective that predicts masked visual features at hand-surface locations, capturing latent contact dynamics. It extends to joint video-tactile representations, reducing dependence on costly tactile measurements for physically intelligent systems.

entry.title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos

author.name: Heran Hu, Yuhang Dong, Zhucun Xue, Kaiwei Chen, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: PsycheMME is a psychology-grounded video benchmark with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk, built on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle frameworks. It includes 1,000 expert-reviewed questions and a Reasoning-Verified protocol that weights answer credit by rationale support and logical consistency; evaluation of 17 models shows timing-related judgments are weakest.

entry.title: LocoPilot: Single-Operator Bilateral Teleoperation for Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning

author.name: Antonio Langella, Giovanni Minelli, Giovanni B. Dessy, Lorenzo Amatucci, Giulio Turrisi, Victor Barasuol, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: LocoPilot is a single-operator bilateral teleoperation and data-collection framework implemented on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with an AgileX Piper arm, wrist and head cameras, enabling coordinated base-and-arm demonstrations for loco-manipulation policy learning. It bridges the gap between robot-free interfaces, which miss platform-specific signals, and on-robot teleoperation, which previously lacked concurrent whole-system command interfaces. This makes high-quality loco-manipulation demonstration collection substantially more practical.

entry.title: Optimal aggregation in multiclass classification

author.name: Felix Abramovich, Or Davidovitch-Servadio

entry.summary: The paper studies aggregation given a finite dictionary of score functions for multiclass classification, deriving optimal rates for model selection and convex aggregation under 0/1 and multinomial logistic losses. Notably, optimal aggregation rates under 0/1 loss do not depend on the number of classes K, and ERM achieves rate optimality.

entry.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models

author.name: Koki Takeshita, Kenji Uebayashi, Hikaru Tomonari, Masaya Tsunokake, Koichiro Yawata, Tatsuya Sasaki, Yusuke Ohtsubo, Kota Dohi, Yasuhiro Sogawa

entry.summary: The paper reframes LLM-based RTL (hardware description) code generation as a multi-objective RL problem, moving away from scalarized PPA rewards toward producing diverse Pareto-optimal circuit designs across power, latency, and area trade-offs. This lets designers pick a preferred trade-off a posteriori rather than committing to one aggregation upfront.

entry.title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents

author.name: Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Junyao Yang, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang

entry.summary: RiseHarness iteratively improves agent harnesses with model weights frozen, focusing on tasks that flip between success and failure under identical configuration and using successful runs as references for failure analysis. It combines trajectories with internal runtime-monitor traces and a Harness Handbook linking evidence to harness behaviors and source code changes.

entry.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects

author.name: Sadia Asif, Israel Antonio Rosales Laguan, Shumaila Asif, Haris Khan, Muneeb Asif, Muhammad Zeeshan Karamat

entry.summary: Proposes a behavioral computing framework quantifying how manipulative LLM outputs affect users, generating controlled manipulative stimuli targeting authority, urgency, and social-proof biases via Manipulation Gradient Descent, then modeling cross-user influence and temporal persistence of behavioral harm. It defines behavioral vulnerability as user susceptibility to manipulative AI responses.

entry.title: COMPASS: Routing via Capability-Oriented Model Profiling with Adaptive Search, Selection, and Tool Use

author.name: Amin Rezaei, Pouya Parsa

entry.summary: COMPASS is an agentic LLM router in which an LLM follows a routing recipe, gathers performance and cost evidence through tools, and optionally inspects candidate answers, requiring no routing-specific training. It improves accuracy and lowers cost versus specialized trained routers on LLMRouterBench and DeepSWE, e.g., 69.85% accuracy at lower spend than the RLCascadeRouter baseline.

entry.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent

author.name: Rui Gong, Ruoyu Wang, Yalun Dai, Hao Li, Sidi Yang, Qihao Zhao, Hongyu Li, Zeyang Guan, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Kim-Hui Yap, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: S-Agent 2.0 equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line 3D perception toolkit for spatial reasoning, designing the interface so the VLM can close the evidence loop between raw tool readings and usable conclusions. It targets the observed failure where tools return correct evidence but the model still answers incorrectly.

entry.title: INCARBench: A Benchmark for Scientific Configuration in VASP INCAR by Large Language Models

author.name: Bin Shao, Jixiang Li, Xinyue Zhang, Baishun Yang, Zhiyang Liu, Weichao Wang

entry.summary: INCARBench evaluates LLMs on configuring inputs for the VASP first-principles simulation package via configuration generation and repair tasks, covering 19 model configurations. Results show substantial capability differences, with semantic and policy accuracy often high while task-critical scientific correctness remains much lower. Failure analysis shows parameter-level correctness does not imply scientifically valid configurations.

entry.title: ICLHerd: Herding-Based Data Selection for LLMs with In-Context Learning as a Proxy

author.name: Yuqiao Wen, Lili Mou

entry.summary: ICLHerd improves data selection for LLM training by replacing max-similarity selection (which exhibits mode-seeking bias) with a von Mises-Fisher kernel balancing mode-seeking and mode-averaging, and uses in-context learning as a cheap proxy signal to rank candidate data against a curated development set encoding desired skills.

entry.title: Beyond Scalar Leaderboards: Adaptive Sampling for Pareto Frontier Identification in Multi-Objective LLM Arenas

author.name: Liang Twist Shan, Jiahao Ai, Zhimei Ren

entry.summary: The paper presents VB-EGE, a fixed-confidence adaptive sampling algorithm for identifying models on the Pareto frontier in arena-style LLM evaluation, where each human comparison rates a model pair on a prompt along a chosen performance dimension. It progressively eliminates models once sufficient evidence accumulates, reducing the number of costly comparisons needed. This offers a statistically grounded alternative to scalar leaderboards for multi-objective model assessment.

entry.title: Benefit and Cost of Random-Token Replacement under Repeated Data: A Known-Entropy Decomposition and Evidence from Ten Real Corpora

author.name: Wonsup Shin, Jingu Kim

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical decomposition of validation loss into approximation, estimation, and memorization terms to explain why random-token replacement (input corruption augmentation) helps when pretraining data is repeated. It shows replacement shrinks predictions toward the corpus average, implying a bias cost independent of memorization but a benefit requiring memorization. Empirical evidence spans ten real corpora.

entry.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Injae Kim, Minseok Joo, Jihwan Park, Sehyung Kim, Minseong Bae, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: RLSplat addresses the flaw that existing budget-controllable feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods predict a dense Gaussian set before pruning, incurring nearly constant latency and memory regardless of the target budget. It instead makes resource usage linear in the requested number of Gaussians, suiting storage- and latency-constrained deployments. This improves the practicality of single-pass 3D reconstruction on limited hardware.

entry.title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models

author.name: Mich-Seth Owusu

entry.summary: Africa-Papers is a 10-billion-token multi-domain academic corpus aimed at correcting the severe underrepresentation of African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship in pretraining datasets like The Pile and Dolma, where such content constitutes under 0.5 percent of tokens. The corpus targets improved reasoning on tropical epidemiology, smallholder agriculture, and indigenous linguistic structures.

entry.title: DISTRACT: Degradation-Indexed Study of Textual Reference Across Competing Targets

author.name: Dan Zlotnikov, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: DISTRACT is a matched-intervention benchmark that holds video, target, and distractor fixed while crossing four text priors with four image-degradation severities to test whether vision-language trackers actually use textual descriptions. Using behavioral contrasts, layerwise probes, and activation patching across five trackers, it finds that only some models (Molmo2, JointNLT) exhibit directed text use while others respond weakly. This mechanistic-evaluation approach to tracking is unusually rigorous.

entry.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng, Qian Yu, Juncheng Yan, Bin Fu, Tai Wang, Yu Qiao, Yihao Liu, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: MindView is a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes, spanning seven tasks in two families: geometry-dominant tasks (camera position/orientation changes) and semantics-dominant tasks (inferring viewpoints from object references and spatial relations). Evaluation of eleven image generators reveals substantial room for improvement, with a paired comparison analysis.

entry.title: Compaction-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Ascend Triton Kernel Generation

author.name: Chuansai Zhou, Yanlin Liu, Bingning Huang, Shidi Xi, Chao Huang, Boxing Chen, Mingming Zhu, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Zongzuo Wang

entry.summary: ATRL is a post-training method for LLM agents generating Ascend Triton GPU kernels, refining GRPO with a compaction-aware, segment-level objective to handle long-horizon context accumulation and sparse terminal rewards. It also constrains context growth during multi-turn interaction with execution environments.

entry.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Dariush Wahdany (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Jesse Cresswell (Layer 6 AI), Naiqing Guan (Layer 6 AI), Atiyeh Ashari Ghomi (Layer 6 AI), Franziska Boenisch (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Adam Dziedzic (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security)
