This replaces the uniform merging ratios of prior token merging methods.

entry.title: WorldSR: Harnessing World Knowledge Search for Grounded Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Junyuan Deng, Xinyi Wu, Zhenyao Wu, Song Wang, Yu Wang, Congchao Zhu

entry.summary: WorldSR replaces or augments stochastic generative priors for image super-resolution with explicit, entity-aligned retrieval from a large external corpus, decomposing inputs into semantic entities and retrieving structurally and semantically matching images. This targets hallucination and stale-knowledge problems in generative-prior SR while keeping reconstruction deterministic and high fidelity. It connects super-resolution to retrieval-augmented generation ideas.

entry.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets

author.name: Jad Yammine, Malek Wahidi, Abrar Anwar, Yan Chang, Mihir Acharya, Anthony Rizk

entry.summary: IndustrialRemembr extends NVIDIA's ReMEmbR to warehouse robot fleets as a shared spatiotemporal memory system that generates scene descriptions only on demand to cut server costs. Robots encode video locally on Jetson hardware using Cosmos-Embed1, Cosmos3-Edge, and Wan2.2 VAE without uploading raw frames, enabling fleet-scale queries such as explaining recurring aisle blockages.

entry.title: LatLM: Line-Parallel Language Models with Deferred Commitment

author.name: Shaorong Zhang, Shiyuan Li, Longxuan Yu, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: LatLM introduces an adaptive decoding-time commitment schedule for line-parallel language models, which advance multiple lines of text concurrently for speedups. Unlike prior frameworks such as LCLM that enforce a fixed commitment schedule, LatLM treats text as a 2D lattice, scores eligible frontier tokens each round, and commits confident candidates while deferring unready ones for extended context, avoiding premature commitments and cascading reasoning errors. Training supervises entire sampled trajectories with a single forward pass, making the approach potentially efficient for parallel decoding architectures.

entry.title: TWIN-MoE: Two-stage Intra-Expert Imputation Network for Incomplete Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liang Nathan Zheng, Jiyuan Liu, Wenhao Liang, Wei Emma Zhang, Weitong Chen, Lin Yue

entry.summary: TWIN-MoE handles missing modalities in MoE models by imputing within experts rather than routing each missingness pattern to a dedicated expert, deriving an imputation-error bound controlled by the local feature dispersion of expert-conditioned neighborhoods. The two-stage design avoids both combinatorial expert scaling and costly global retrieval.

entry.title: Bootstrap Stochastic Interpolant Tree for Inference-time Search Under Sparse Reward

author.name: Binglin Ji, Anindya Sarkar, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Bootstrap Stochastic Interpolant Tree (BSIT), a tree-based inference-time search method that avoids the systematic bias of SMC-style per-step reward/gradient dependencies and the restricted exploration of DDPM-like transition coupling in existing tree samplers. By decoupling neighbor states, BSIT improves coverage of the target marginal distribution for sparse-reward search. It addresses a recognized weakness in inference-time scaling.

entry.title: Measuring the Task Value of Precision Upgrades in Closed-Loop Agents

author.name: Sicheng Lyu, Xinyu Wang, Yu Gu, Lei Ding, Ziyang Song, Xiao-Wen Chang

entry.summary: This work proposes measuring the true task value of selectively upgrading a low-precision LLM agent to full-precision BF16 fallbacks, using paired counterfactual branches to separate action replacement from later takeover effects. Experiments on Qwen3 agents with simulated 4-bit weights in tau2-bench show that a single precision upgrade can both rescue and spoil tasks, motivating a net-value router.

entry.title: fxBench: Evaluating and Understanding Formula Suggestions in Spreadsheets

author.name: Sanket Mhatre, Sumit Gulwani, Vu Le, Yasharth Bajpai, Gust Verbruggen

entry.summary: From a Microsoft-affiliated team including Gulwani, fxBench is the first public benchmark for proactive spreadsheet formula suggestions on real spreadsheets. It frames the challenges of context collection, correct formula generation, and latency constraints for triggering on every keystroke in tools like Excel and Google Sheets.

entry.title: CARTA: Self-Supervised Reusable Transaction Embeddings via Heterogeneous Tokenization and Cross-Attention

author.name: Shreyas K. Chandrahas, Jose Munoz, Satish Babu Bellapu

entry.summary: CARTA learns compact 16-dimensional self-supervised embeddings from raw payment transactions using type-specific projections and contrastive learning with token excision, enabling label-efficient fraud detection without retraining. Its frozen embeddings exceed raw-feature probes that use 100 times more labels on IEEE-CIS and perform strongly on IBM TabFormer.

entry.title: ViCoR: Estimating Visual Necessity via Counterfactual Residuals for Multimodal Medical Data Selection

author.name: Haotian Gan, Yudong Li, Xintian Li, Jiarui Han, Weidong Tang

entry.summary: ViCoR targets hidden stratification in medical vision-language models caused by modality imbalance, where strong linguistic priors suppress visually grounded learning. It scores image-text pairs by estimating visual necessity through image-dependent counterfactual optimization residuals, separating visually necessary samples from shortcut-solvable ones during fine-tuning data selection. This addresses a clinically meaningful failure mode of Med-VLMs.

entry.title: CHSM8: A Chess Transformer that Follows Natural-Language Style Prompts

author.name: Ilia Badanin

entry.summary: CHSM8 is a 210M-parameter chess transformer conditioned on free-text style descriptions, pretrained without search on 1.07B filtered Lichess games, reaching 1837 Elo and beating larger public search-free models. It is then fine-tuned to follow style instructions using synthetic data generated with Gemma models. The work is a clean testbed for instruction-following grounded in verifiable game outcomes.

entry.title: Divergence based Ranked Preference Alignment for LLMs

author.name: Rajdeep Haldar, Yue Xing, Qifan Song

entry.summary: The paper introduces f-RPO, an f-divergence objective family for ranked preference alignment of LLMs, unifying divergence-based alignment views with richer ranked (listwise) feedback that captures more information per annotation than pairwise comparisons. It provides an interpretable theoretical foundation for alignment objectives extending beyond DPO-style pairwise losses. Relevant to more data-efficient post-training.

entry.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation

author.name: Yanjin He, Cuifeng Shen, Wanzhou Lei, Maohua Li, Tao Lan, Kan Liu, Hanlin Tang, Qing Qu

entry.summary: SWIFT is a self-guided training method for diffusion models that uses a frozen weak denoiser, such as an early checkpoint, to extrapolate clean regression targets away from the weak model's prediction, amplifying underfit components without any inference-time overhead. The weak guide requires no backpropagation during main training and is discarded afterward. This offers a cheap weak-to-strong improvement path for expensive diffusion training.

entry.title: DeltaTrace: Efficient Signed Attribution for Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Chen Liang, Daoping Wu, Donghua Yang, Zhiyu Liang, Ying Zhang, Shuguang Xiong, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: DeltaTrace is an attribution framework that explains how input tokens support or oppose a fixed language model response by measuring log-probability changes under masking. It distributes the score difference among tokens using operator-specific local rules and effective secant slopes, assigning signed attributions that sum exactly to the measured difference via local conservation. The method targets attribution for reasoning LLMs where exhaustive counterfactuals are infeasible.

entry.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization

author.name: Suwan Yoon, Seongryong Jung, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes APSD, a self-distillation policy optimization method that constructs asymmetric targets depending on rollout correctness: interpolating between student and self-teacher on correct rollouts to preserve successful behavior, and extrapolating beyond the self-teacher on incorrect rollouts for stronger correction. The authors support the design with divergence decomposition, reverse-KL barycentric geometry, and gradient analysis. This targets a known failure of naive self-teacher matching in dense token-level LLM post-training.

entry.title: Typed Decision Models under Prevalence Shift: Decision Training, Calibration, and Implicit Priors

author.name: Abdul Rahman Iqbal, Muhammad Fawad Nasim, Amir Saleem

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether typed decision models (TDMs) that return calibrated probabilities over caller-defined options maintain calibration and threshold validity under prevalence (label) shift, comparing three TDMs against their base backbones and fine-tuned classifiers. It separates the gains of vendor decision training from backbone improvements. The work addresses an underexplored robustness question for a new class of decision-oriented model interfaces.

entry.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps

author.name: Jean-Loup Dupret, Patrick Cheridito

entry.summary: The authors develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. Instead of differentiating through the full time-discretized dynamics as in direct policy optimization, the method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement using the stochastic maximum principle, with pathwise adjoint labels regressed onto the Markov state. This offers a more stable and scalable approach to stochastic optimal control.

entry.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding

author.name: Zhuofan Josh Ying, Guanglong Sun, Nolan Ho, Kieran Liu, Rui Yang, Andrew Chen, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Pony Ma, Hossein Adeli

entry.summary: This work shows that parameter-efficient fine-tuning can adapt very large pretrained multimodal backbones for brain encoding, predicting neural responses to stimuli, where full fine-tuning has been infeasible due to scarce and costly neural data. It also exploits the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single pass, dramatically cutting feature-extraction cost compared to sliding windows. This makes large-backbone adaptation practical for neuroscience and could improve encoding model quality broadly.

entry.title: InJePA: Intention-First Latent Planning with Coupled JEPA World Models for Visual Navigation

author.name: Siming Zhou, Bowen Ma, Ruiran Du, Pengcheng Zheng, Sheng Zheng, Dongshen Han, Zhijie Li, Wei Dong, Fan Mo, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: InJePA proposes an intention-first planning paradigm for visual navigation where a goal-conditioned JEPA proposes latent intentions and an action-conditioned JEPA predicts future latent states, operating in a shared latent space. Predicted consequences feed back into the next intention proposal, making predictions guide stepwise action construction rather than only evaluating complete candidate actions.

entry.title: Unified Multiparadigm Fusion Intelligence for Rare Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Jian Yang, Peiling Liu, Songda Li, Yu Cao, Yuqing Feng, Lan Yu, Jiarong Pan, Jing Ye, Xinwen Huang, Chaochun Zou, Xudong Lu, Huilong Duan, Haomin Li

entry.summary: FusionRare integrates knowledge-driven symbolic reasoning, deep-learning pattern recognition, and LLM-based analysis into a unified framework for rare disease diagnosis, explicitly addressing the structural limits of each paradigm individually. Targeting the diagnostic odyssey of an estimated 300 million rare disease patients, it aims to combine interpretability, pattern recognition, and broad knowledge.

entry.title: Can This LLM Annotate My Data? Estimating Zero-Shot LLM Performance

author.name: Tong Lin, Grant Schoenebeck, Sabina Tomkins

entry.summary: This paper asks whether one can predict how well an LLM will perform as a zero-shot annotator on a new dataset, constructing two task families spanning 461 text classification datasets for evaluation. It finds performance is predictable to a useful degree, and that internal log-probabilities are more predictive than LLM verbalized self-confidence.

entry.title: Margin-Based Generalization for Quantum Machine Learning with Classical Data Encoding

author.name: Ju-Young Ryu, Tak Hur, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: This paper develops a margin-based generalization theory for quantum models on classically encoded data, treating the encoding as part of the effective hypothesis class. For trainable encodings it derives a bound via a two-scale covering argument that adds an encoding-capacity term of order O~(sqrt(L/m)). It provides the first structured generalization account for this setting.

entry.title: Bridging Concepts: Multi-Agent Reasoning over Scientific Concept Graphs for High-Impact Research Prediction

author.name: Donggyu Yoon, Minsung Hwang, Juneha Baek, Donghyuk Shin, Joyce Jiyoung Whang

entry.summary: The authors construct scientific concept graphs from paper text using LLM-extracted concepts and introduce MiroGraph, a multi-agent reasoning system for forecasting unconnected concept pairs that will become high-impact. They release benchmarks from CIKM, KDD, and SIGIR papers with settings including emerging concepts unseen during training.

entry.title: Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surface Reconstruction via Additive Martingales

author.name: Haochen Luo, Sifan Lin, Xiaolong Luo, An Binh Minh, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu

entry.summary: AddMart reconstructs continuous implied volatility surfaces from sparse option quotes by mapping them to non-negative increment densities of an exponential additive martingale, recovering valid risk-neutral marginals and IVs. By building no-arbitrage structure into the architecture rather than penalizing violations in the loss, the method guarantees static no-arbitrage by construction.

entry.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks

author.name: Wanjie Wang

entry.summary: Introduces FLICKER, a gradient-based power iteration for federated spectral estimation on horizontally partitioned matrices using only local matrix-vector products, with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and a spectral-target selection procedure. Builds BiFLICKER for federated community detection in bipartite networks plus a projected variant for nearby singular directions.

entry.title: Translating in style: An open-weight alternative to GPT-4 for culturally aligned machine translation

author.name: Thomas Rietman, Hadi Mohammadi, Robert A. Bagheri

entry.summary: Evaluates Hunyuan-MT-7B as an open-weight replacement for GPT-4 in retrieval-augmented stylistic machine translation, comparing base, LoRA fine-tuned, and GRPO-steered variants across three style dimensions and twelve language pairs. Targets the problem that MT systems flatten linguistic style, especially for non-Western languages.

entry.title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models

author.name: Wang Yang, Xinpeng Li, Yanyan Zhang, Chuang Ma, Shouren Wang, Jianzhe Wei, Liqin Ye, Xiaoran Cai, Mohsen Hariri, Vipin Chaudhary, Xiaotian Han

entry.summary: This analysis probes the limits of Jev-style single-forward-pass decision models, finding a crisp characterization: such models fail exactly when a reference LLM needs to write out intermediate steps. Jev handles record selection flawlessly up to 20k tokens and 64 options but degrades to 53-80% accuracy when answers depend on sixteen state updates due to record interference, and it follows stale summaries blindly. It answers 97.5% of real items solvable in one forward pass, defining where fast decision models can be safely deployed.

entry.title: CALM: Consistency-Aware Logit Masking in Decoding Space for Mitigating Overthinking of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Shengjing Liu, Feiyang Li, Yuxuan Yang, Yile Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Proposes CALM, a training-free decoding intervention against overthinking in large reasoning models: it monitors trial answers at step boundaries and applies logit masking to action tokens, avoiding the disruption caused by truncation methods that force early exit on local agreement signals. This preserves useful reflection while cutting unnecessary reasoning steps.

entry.title: Verifying Human-Written Reasoning References

author.name: Ali Ansari, Farhana Ferdousi Liza

entry.summary: The authors present a reference-centered assessment method for human-written reasoning chains, combining entailment checking against cited premise sets, full-premise rechecking, and failure attribution. They find prior work rarely verifies whether step conclusions in human reference derivations are entailed by their premises. This matters because such references underpin reasoning evaluation and reward modeling for AI systems.

entry.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law

author.name: Daan Boven, Gregor Behnke, David Graus

entry.summary: The paper presents a neuro-symbolic formalization of Article 42 of the Dutch Bankruptcy Act (actio pauliana), with a symbolic core written in Catala in literate style and neural components structuring case facts into boolean and date inputs for the symbolic solver. Open-textured legal terms are represented as boolean inputs where neural subroutines supply values. It is a thoughtful case study in combining verifiable legal reasoning with neural NLP.

entry.title: BUMP: Body-driven Unified Multi-object Physics for HOI Synthesis

author.name: Wonjung Woo, Hyeonwoo Kim, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: BUMP generates text-driven human-object interactions with multiple objects by separating intentional motion from physical consequences: human motion and driver-object trajectories are generated, while surrounding responder objects move via physics simulation from contact and collision. This principled decomposition yields more plausible multi-object HOI synthesis. It targets a long-standing challenge in motion generation.

entry.title: PACE-MoE: Adaptive Domain Sampling and Domain-Specific LoRA for Medical Visual Grounding

author.name: Zhenxuan Wang, Jisheng Dang, Ronghao Lin, Bimei Wang, Jingwen Zhao, Wenjun Ma, Bin Hu, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: PACE-MoE is a policy-guided framework for medical visual grounding that adaptively samples which imaging domains to train on based on policy feedback, while applying domain-specific LoRA adapters for where updates land. It includes domain admission, replay, and final all-domain balancing.

entry.title: PixelSR: Pixel-Space Orthogonal Flow Decoupling for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Xiang Lv, Kai Zhao, Qiang Wang, Qiao Mo, Chao Zhou, Mingwen Shao

entry.summary: PixelSR is a single-stage pixel-space diffusion transformer for real-world super-resolution that combines pixel-space conditional diffusion with orthogonal flow decoupling. It targets the seesaw effect in two-stage latent diffusion SR pipelines where perceptual realism degrades structural fidelity.

entry.title: Beyond the Evidence Boundary: Behavioral Mirage Under Progressive Degradation in Medical VLMs

author.name: Edric Castel C. Hao, Rez Samantha Z. Floresca

entry.summary: The study introduces a baseline-anchored framework tracing previously correct medical VLM predictions through progressive image degradation to identify an evidence boundary, defining mirage as continued model commitment at that boundary regardless of correctness. Across three VLMs and three datasets, only MedGemma yielded a sufficient baseline-correct pool for analysis. It highlights reliability risks of medical VLMs under real-world input degradation.

entry.title: PACE: Plan, Attend, Check, and Emit for Training-Free Response Timing in Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Siqi Guo, Yuxia Chen, Wenbo Zhu, Yangguang Ji, Zhenxiang Jiang, Teng Zhong, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: PACE addresses premature responses in streaming video understanding by classifying chunk-wise failure patterns and providing a training-free decision procedure for when an answer becomes final. It organizes timing errors into instability, lack of evidence, and unfinished-event cases, offering explicit timing logic beyond scalar gating signals.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Machine Learning with Evidence-based Planning for Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Yiqing Shen, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: MedicalMLOmni is a multi-agent AutoML framework that automates model training for diverse single- and multi-modal medical imaging tasks from natural-language instructions, using evidence-based planning to handle architecture selection and hyperparameter optimization. It addresses gaps in both general-purpose AutoML, which lacks medical specifics, and narrow medical AutoML tools.

entry.title: Adaptive Traversal Tubes for Posture-Aware Navigation of Bipedal Humanoids

author.name: Zijian Ge

entry.summary: This work presents a navigation framework for bipedal humanoid robots that exploits the ability to change effective footprint via body yaw, enabling traversal of narrow passages and socially aware yielding. It introduces Adaptive Traversal Tubes to encode corridor width as a unified geometric-plus-social-comfort signal, Interval Velocity-Heading control to map width to frontal-to-sidestep posture schedules, and a velocity-conditioned AMP locomotion policy trained on retargeted motion data. The integration links high-level navigation planning with learned whole-body locomotion control.

entry.title: Confessions of a Masked MDP

author.name: Sebastian Reboul, Lorenzo Croissant, H\'el\`ene Halconruy

entry.summary: The paper isolates the problem of learning unknown valid-action masks in RL, studying joint optimization of the policy and the mask itself in linear MDPs where each attempted action reveals a linear validity score. The authors construct a minimax-optimal, computationally efficient optimistic algorithm and analyze its limitations.

entry.title: ACS Infra: free access to large base models for LLM psychology research

author.name: Martin Vaněk

entry.summary: The author announces a free platform providing researchers access to large open base models with logprobs, activation harvesting and steering, a browser workbench, and a loom, targeting LLM psychology and adjacent research. The motivation is that distinguishing pre-training from post-training effects on model psychology requires studying large base models, which are otherwise hard and costly to access.

entry.title: KPHarness: Co-Evolving Knowledge and Probing for Long-Horizon Gaming Harnesses

author.name: Zhikang Chen, Yueqing Sun, Sen Cui, Ziang Ye, Yu Wang, Yan Feng2, Xierui Song, Yu Zhang, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: KPHarness adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model through knowledge-probing co-evolution: recovery knowledge supplies intervention hypotheses that guide active probing, and probe outcomes refine both the knowledge and future probe selection. This lets the harness learn when interventions apply, not just which to apply, in long-horizon gaming tasks.

entry.title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems

author.name: Nikolay Yavich, Alexander Ryabov, Viacheslav Naumov, Sayan Ranu, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Evgeny Burnaev, Vladimir Vanovskiy

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver for PDEs on unstructured grids that treats the large equation systems arising in stiff evolutionary and static problems as constraints. It is evaluated on forward modeling, inverse coefficient and right-hand-side estimation, and learnable graph coarsening for acceleration.

entry.title: Building Telecom Language Models with RSOD: Domain Data, Specialist Post-Training, Memory-Conscious Distillation, and Networking Evaluation

author.name: Anil Srirangapatna Nagesh, Nitin Gupta, Anuj Taneja, Vivek Singh, Shane Eleniak, Theo Zhao, Moulidharan N, Shashank Keshetty

entry.summary: The authors present an end-to-end framework for telecom language models: synthetic training data from networking taxonomies, 212,559 routed records across fourteen networking routes, six frozen specialist LoRA teachers over one continued-pretrained backbone, and Routed Specialist On-Policy Distillation consolidating them into a single deployable student adapter.

entry.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems

author.name: Xialie Zhuang, Mingcong Lei, Zunhai Su, Ri Liu, Jianjin Li, Peixian Ma, Jia Pan, Ngai Wong, Guanhua Chen, Chuan-Wei Kuo

entry.summary: DecisionPivot is a diagnostic benchmark with 48 tasks and over 40,000 items across seven decision roles like routing, guardrails, and output verification, using contrast groups with solver-verified answers to test calibrated decision-making. It evaluates 40 decision models and 14 general models with documented prompts.

entry.title: Disentangling Depression from Cognitive Decline in Elderly Speech Using Concurrent Clinical Assessments

author.name: Woori Jeon, Seunghee Ha, Sang-Kyu Lee, Ji Hye Yoon, Tae-Jin Yoon, Seung Jin Lee, Woojae Han, Jungmin So

entry.summary: Using a Korean elderly speech corpus of 89 MCI speakers collected over three years with concurrent depression and cognitive assessments, this study disentangles acoustic markers of depression from cognitive decline. It finds only formant features remain associated with depression after controlling for cognitive function, while widely used F0 features carry no depression signal. A compact 12-feature F1+F2 model achieves UAR 0.760, outperforming baselines.

entry.title: Profile-DP: Differential Privacy for User-Controlled Profile Release in Personalized LLM Inference

author.name: Mingchen Li, Zifan Peng, Kewei Sha, Lavinia F Pieptea, Heng Fan, Junhua Ding, Meikang Qiu, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: Profile-DP is a policy-aware local differential-privacy framework for releasing user profiles in personalized LLM inference, provably bounding disclosure of user-withheld facts while treating public instructions, schemas, and authorized facts as side information. The privatized profile composes with the public instruction before answer generation, decoupling privacy guarantees from the downstream model.

entry.title: CityPaint: A Free Lunch from 2D Diffusion for City-Scale 3D Texturing

author.name: Yuchen Zou, Lihuang Fang, Siyu Zhu, Xiao Hu

entry.summary: CityPaint leverages 2D diffusion priors to generate globally consistent, city-scale 3D textures without any city-scale 3D training data, integrating geometric priors with generative models. This addresses the scarcity of real urban 3D data for VR, gaming, and digital twins. The free-lunch framing of reusing abundant 2D priors for 3D content is the key insight.

entry.title: How Much Do $\ell_1$ Attacks Need Concentrated Perturbations?

author.name: Melika Shirian, Kianoosh Vadaei, Arshia Hemmat

entry.summary: The authors ask how much of an l1 adversarial attack's success depends on large concentrated coordinate changes, adding a per-coordinate cap enforced by exact in-loop projection across APGD-l1, SLIDE, and FMN-l1. Across 18 settings, caps of at most 32/255 retain a median 97% of attack success while peak magnitudes fall 80% and effective support nearly triples. This suggests l1 robustness evaluations may understate threats from spatially distributed perturbations.

entry.title: VISH-ASR: Viterbi-Guided Selection of Hotwords for Speech-LLM Contextual ASR

author.name: Xiaoyu Gu, Yu Xi, Chencheng Wang, Zonghan Zhou, Haoyu Li, Jing Peng, Kai Yu

entry.summary: VISH is a training-free, plug-and-play framework for selecting compact hotword subsets from large dynamic inventories in prompt-based contextual ASR. It verifies candidate-specific acoustic support over frame-level CTC posteriors via constrained Viterbi search, with scalable variants (M-VISH, Bi-MVISH) using shared-prefix search and bounded top-K pruning. Results across five benchmarks improve contextual biasing without extra training.

entry.title: From Complex Histories to Simple Predictors: Predictive Dimension in Dynamic Graph Learning

author.name: Hantong Feng, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: The paper argues that continuous-time dynamic graph learning should identify low-dimensional predictive states sufficient for future prediction rather than reconstruct full interaction histories. It defines and estimates an intrinsic predictive dimension, quantifying the effective predictive degrees of freedom a task requires, informing simpler model design.

entry.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V

author.name: Zhenghan Chen, Zekai Shao, Xin Lin, Leting Cheng, Siming Chen

entry.summary: Code2Video-Compass is a benchmark of 2,104 tasks across 10 categories and 24 subtypes for evaluating MLLMs that generate executable programs producing complete videos, covering text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video settings. It addresses the gap left by specialized code-generation benchmarks that do not evaluate complete video creation. It is relevant as programmatic video generation gains attention for controllability and editability.

entry.title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems

author.name: Noor Abo Mokh, Teresa Lynn, Nizar Habash, Ahmed Elshabrawy, Sara Alhajeri, Alaa Elsetohy, Preslav Nakov, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: The paper introduces DAR-MGSM, the first manually curated benchmark for mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic, covering five major dialects plus Modern Standard Arabic with translated and culturally localized versions of math word problems. Evaluations of eleven Arabic-centric and multilingual LLMs reveal performance gaps, particularly on dialectal and culturally localized variants.

entry.title: Organizing LLM Inference for Aggregate Predictions from Behavioral Data

author.name: Varun Gupta, Vijay Kamble

entry.summary: This work asks how to organize LLM calls when predicting aggregate outcomes, such as product-level conversion rates from individual browsing sessions, studying bias-variance tradeoffs between session summarization, per-session prediction, and batching products into one prompt. It provides guidance on cost-accuracy tradeoffs for population-level LLM simulation without task-specific training.

entry.title: BEM: Learning Bregman Divergences for Concept Erasure in Flow Matching Models

author.name: Mohamed-Hicham Leghettas, Markus P\"uschel

entry.summary: BEM targets concept erasure in flow-matching text-to-image models such as FLUX and Stable Diffusion 3 by learning the Bregman divergence used as the fine-tuning loss via bi-level optimization, exploiting the fact that Bregman divergences are exactly the losses under which flow matching recovers correct velocity fields. This lets practitioners shape what is erased versus preserved beyond the standard Euclidean loss.

entry.title: AdamPM: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization via Moment Pooling

author.name: Xiaowei Ji, Lishan Xu, Jianing An, Jie Luo, Wenjun Wu, Lei Huang

entry.summary: AdamPM is a memory-efficient Adam variant for LLM pre-training that groups adjacent first and second moment entries along rows or columns and represents each group with a shared mean. It inherits Adam's hyperparameter settings directly and avoids the extra computational overhead and hyperparameter tuning burden of many alternative memory-efficient optimizers.

entry.title: RAFT: Redundancy-Aware Input Filtering for Temporal Graph Neural Network Training

author.name: Yue Dai, Sarah Zhou, Youtao Zhang

entry.summary: RAFT studies whether all events in temporal graph neural network training are necessary, exploiting redundancy between events' roles as prediction targets and historical context to filter inputs upstream. This relaxes event dependencies that block parallelism, improving training scalability on growing dynamic graphs.

entry.title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Xi Xiao, Jihun Hamm, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: UtoMe incorporates observation uncertainty (via ensemble data assimilation spread) into token merging for weather transformers, combining dynamics saliency with input-reliability to anchor important tokens and calibrate bipartite matching. It improves ERA5 72-hour forecasting efficiency across resolutions and training/inference configurations.

entry.title: Polynomial Learning of Positive ReLU Networks under Gaussian Inputs

author.name: Zhijie Zheng

entry.summary: This theory paper gives polynomial-time algorithms for learning one-hidden-layer positive ReLU networks under Gaussian inputs without separation or conditioning assumptions on hidden directions. It achieves squared prediction error epsilon with controlled output width and complexity, including results for arbitrary labels with bounded second moment. This removes assumptions that limited prior work on network learnability.

entry.title: ClinSDT: LLM-Encoded Clinical Semantic Guidance for Sepsis Treatment via Decision Transformer

author.name: Yanyan Wu, Guanyu Zhu, Changbin Zhao, Jin Zhang, Dexu Yu, Tianmin Sun, Jining Luan, Chunxiao Li, Hanwen Du, Youhua Li

entry.summary: ClinSDT uses a frozen LLM as a semantic bridge in a Decision Transformer for offline sepsis treatment from ICU trajectories, constructing clinical semantic views such as patient severity and treatment response rather than relying only on raw physiological tokens. The LLM encodes clinician-relevant concepts without making treatment decisions itself. This improves the representational basis for offline medical RL policies.

entry.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds

author.name: Jize Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Xinyi Le, Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This perspective paper argues that as JEPAs become latent world models supporting prediction and planning, interpretability research must shift from what latents encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive predictions. It proposes a four-stage research agenda: Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act. The paper helps set a research direction for interpreting emerging world-model architectures.

entry.title: Neural Video Coding under Limited Delay: Theoretical Optimality and System Design

author.name: Likun Cai, Jun Chen, Ashish Khisti

entry.summary: The paper reframes delay as an explicit design parameter in neural video compression, proving via rate-distortion analysis based on clique factorization of Markov networks that limited frame delay can improve rate-distortion tradeoffs over strictly causal prediction. It then proposes Graph-Factored Sequential Coding (GFSC), a principled framework realizing these gains. This bridges information theory and practical neural video codec design.

entry.title: Detection Augmented Learning In Non-Stationary Bandit Environments

author.name: Argyrios Gerogiannis, Yu-Han Huang, Subhonmesh Bose, Venugopal V. Veeravalli

entry.summary: DAL is a modular black-box paradigm for non-stationary bandits combining any stationary bandit algorithm, a change detector, and a forced exploration schedule. The authors prove a single regret bound showing DAL transfers the regret of the stationary input algorithm to the piecewise-stationary setting, matching or improving best known bounds across settings. The modularity makes it applicable from classical to highly structured bandit problems.

entry.title: Keep the Lineages Alive: Diversity-Preserving SMC for Diffusion LLM Decoding

author.name: Minoo Ahmadi, Seyedarmin Azizi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: The paper improves sequential Monte Carlo decoding for masked diffusion language models by preserving particle diversity during resampling, preventing multinomial resampling from duplicating high-weight candidates and discarding lineages that could still reach correct solutions. It handles both internal confidence rewards and external process reward models. This improves reasoning accuracy at inference time without any post-training.

entry.title: CAST: Cast-Admissible Generative Design and Shape Optimization with Paired Depth Images

author.name: Jihoon Kim, Yongmin Kwon, Namwoo Kang

entry.summary: CAST reformulates 3D generative shape design under mold-opening constraints as 2D generation of paired top and bottom depth images, so generated shapes are guaranteed castable (no undercuts) by construction. Diffusion models generate candidates from limited training data (211 samples) and an FEA-guided optimizer refines the designs. This is a clever constraint-encoding trick connecting generative AI with manufacturing feasibility.

entry.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows

author.name: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes, Tianyi Peng, Nairen Cao

entry.summary: This paper tackles the practical problem of assigning different LLMs to different roles within agentic workflows while balancing task quality, cost, and latency. It introduces Cost-Coupled Gittins search, a multi-objective extension of cost-aware Gittins search that exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs to recommend Pareto-optimal model assignments. This is immediately useful for practitioners deploying heterogeneous multi-model agent pipelines.

entry.title: DUET: Decoupled Upper- and Lower-Body Execution for Task-Agnostic Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Kapalik Khanal, Biswash Khatiwada, Stephen Afrifa, Fan Wu, Ramesh Bahadur Bist

entry.summary: DUET decouples humanoid locomotion and manipulation by training an RL locomotion policy for the leg and waist joints on a 23-DoF Unitree G1 while excluding arm joints from the action space and observing them only, combining controllers only at the robot interface. This allows swapping manipulation policies without retraining balance controllers.

entry.title: Extending Myerson's Optimal Auctions to Correlated Bidders via Neural Network Interpolation

author.name: Mingyu Guo, Jiayuan Liu, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: This paper addresses optimal single-item auction design with correlated bidders, a setting where extensions of Myerson's classic solution become non-strategy-proof and approximation is NP-hard. The authors establish an empirical pipeline synthesizing neural interpolation of Myerson's greedy approach to produce deterministic, strategy-proof, ex post individually rational auctions with near-optimal revenue.

entry.title: Private Evaluation of High-Dimensional Functions

author.name: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Adam Smith

entry.summary: The authors design differentially private black-box evaluators for arbitrary high-dimensional functions with unknown or unbounded sensitivity, reducing the problem to high-dimensional private quasi-concave optimization. The evaluators provide a geometric utility guarantee under both pure and approximate DP using only down-neighborhood queries. This extends the frontier of private evaluation theory.

entry.title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles

author.name: Qihao Zhou, Shanshui Niu

entry.summary: SICBO is a new algorithm for nonconvex-strongly-convex finite-sum bilevel optimization that combines penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections using only first-order oracles. The authors prove an improved complexity bound with square-root finite-sum dependence, matching the best known deterministic fully first-order results. Bilevel optimization underlies hyperparameter tuning, meta-learning, and regularization.

entry.title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes

author.name: Joshua Rooijakkers, Edwin Fong

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), which reformulates Bayesian nonparametric intensity estimation for event data as inference over unobserved future events conditioned on the observed history. This avoids expensive MCMC sampling and complex priors over indirect latent structures while retaining nonparametric flexibility.

entry.title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect

author.name: Shaoxiu Wei, Bhaskar Rao, Florian Meyer

entry.summary: This work proposes a neural track-before-detect framework that operates on complex-valued raw sensor signals and learns environment-dependent latent intensity representations online using a normalizing flow within sequential Bayesian inference. It targets multi-object tracking in radar, sonar, and 6G sensing settings without requiring pre-training on propagation effects.

entry.title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement

author.name: Reza T Batley, Sourav Saha

entry.summary: This work combines a conditional rectified-flow generative model with exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities to concurrently optimize lattice microstructures and their spatial assignments for printable bone scaffolds. On a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produced printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1% across six prescribed moduli.

entry.title: EvoSkill v2: Fully Agentic Skill Evolution from Benchmark Adaptation to a Stateful Evolver

author.name: Dastin Huang, Baran Nama, Salaheddin Alzubi

entry.summary: Presents a three-agent system in which a stateful coding-agent evolver rewrites an agent's instruction skills each epoch while the model and harness stay frozen, with a benchmark adaptor turning user-supplied graders into plugins. Contrasts its persistent evolver design with common patterns of one-shot model calls or fresh agents per round, and analyzes solver rollout variability.

entry.title: A Probabilistic, Rotation-Preserving Kernel Operator Surrogate for Continuum-Robot Design Spaces

author.name: Branden Frieden, Alan Kuntz, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: This paper develops an uncertainty-aware operator-learning surrogate for tendon-driven continuum robots that generalizes across robot designs and actuation while predicting full equilibrium configurations. A nonstationary GP kernel metric is learned by a shallow network from mechanics-aware design coordinates, and orientation is reconstructed directly on SO(3) to preserve valid material frames. The framework also defines a sequential acquisition criterion for simulator queries.

entry.title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity

author.name: Youran Dong, Junfeng Yang, Wei Yao, Jin Zhang

entry.summary: Develops two Newton-based bilevel optimization methods (Newton-based GALET and BAMM) that remove the standard lower-level strong convexity assumption, handling singular lower-level curvature. Targets ML tasks like hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning.

entry.title: Prosodic Structure as a Critical Component in Phonemic Language Modelling at BabyLM Scale

author.name: Bill K. S. Ku, Janet B. Pierrehumbert

entry.summary: Tests whether adding prosodic structure to phonemic (rather than orthographic) language modeling improves learning at BabyLM scale, comparing an orthographic baseline to three phonological- richness conditions at 10M and 100M words. Introduces a lexical decision task and semantic organization tasks better suited to small-data regimes.

entry.title: Modeling Discourse Profiles in Climate Misinformation Discourse

author.name: Ge Gao, Zhengyang Shan, Bryan A. Plummer, Margrit Betke, Derry Wijaya

entry.summary: Using a large-scale TikTok climate discourse dataset, the authors cluster comments into recurring rhetorical patterns called discourse profiles and incorporate them via late fusion into fine-grained climate misinformation classifiers. The profile-aware models significantly improve macro-F1 over text-only baselines under video-disjoint evaluation across three seeds. The work recognizes that misinformation is sustained through recurring rhetorical structures rather than isolated claims.

entry.title: Design Considerations in Low-Resource Archival OCR: A Case Study in Lakota

author.name: T\'ea Wright, Laura X. Ma, Claudia Iron Hawk, Hannah J. Haynie, Alexis Palmer, Alane Suhr, Abteen Ebrahimi, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: Examines adapting small (under 3B parameter) vision-language models as OCR tools for Lakota, a North American Indigenous language, considering constraints identified with community members: training budgets, segmentation noise, scan degradation, and orthographic variance. The work supports language reclamation and community-driven digital archiving.

entry.title: Inside the Scorer: Mechanistic Evidence on Rubric Control in LLM-Based Automated Essay Scoring from 25 Base Models

author.name: Chungche Huang, Po-Ya Angela Wang, Shu-Kai Hsieh

entry.summary: Probes and steers 25 open-weight LLMs (0.13B-10.31B, 14 families) on human-scored English writing tasks to determine whether scoring rubrics have distinct, independently controllable internal representations. Holistic scores are decodable from activations for longer tasks and rubric representations are partly separable, with implications for verifiable high-stakes automated essay scoring.

entry.title: How Benchmark Graph Construction Shapes Multi-Hop KG Navigation: A Controlled Audit of PathQuestion and PathQuestion-Large

author.name: Eduin E. Hernandez, Sergio A. Diaz, Luis F. Garcia, Nurassyl Askar, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: This audit holds PathQuestion and PathQuestion-Large questions, answers, and splits fixed while swapping the released task-filtered graphs for the larger source KGs, isolating how graph construction affects multi-hop KGQA difficulty. Source restoration expands the navigation search space and changes measured method performance, showing graph construction is a consequential, entangled part of these benchmarks.

entry.title: ASTOR: Benchmarking and Improving Autoformulation for Soft-Constraint Optimization with a Formal Grammar

author.name: Amer Goel, Yeganeh Alimohammadi, Andrew Daw

entry.summary: ASTOR introduces a benchmark and formal grammar for autoformulation, the task of translating natural-language decision problems with both hard and soft constraints into executable optimization models. It addresses the neglect of soft constraints in prior LLM-based optimization work by providing structured evaluation of this capability.

entry.title: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL

author.name: Youbing Yin, Xujun Peng, Muhammad S. Uddin, Erin Babinsky, Daben Liu, Anoop Kumar

entry.summary: AIR is a training-free multi-agent framework for text-to-SQL that constructs competing interpretations of ambiguous queries, verifies via execution that they yield different results, and generates targeted clarification questions grounded in the observed data differences. It shows strong performance and efficiency on leading ambiguity benchmarks with robust cross-domain behavior. The approach directly addresses the one-query-to-many-valid-SQL mismatch common in practice.

entry.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations

author.name: Meng-Chen Wu, Umesh Bodhwani

entry.summary: This position/survey paper organizes the pluralistic alignment literature with a two-layer taxonomy separating Overton, Steerable, and Distributional pluralism, and distinguishing whose preferences define references and what evidence demonstrates success. It disentangles three questions that existing work often conflates. The framework should help clarify goals and evaluation in value-diverse alignment research.

entry.title: Understanding When Reflective Prompt and Skill Optimization Helps on Locally Served Reasoning Models: A Two-Model Study of GEPA and SkillOpt

author.name: Andrea Giummarra, Carmelo Baglieri, Antonio Di Maria, Andrea Farruggio, Michele Piatto, Giovanni Micale

entry.summary: This replication study tests GEPA and SkillOpt reflective optimizers on locally served DeepSeek V4 Flash and Qwen3.8-27B under frozen protocols on HotpotQA and MATH-500. Gains are fragile and configuration-dependent: SkillOpt validation gains reverse into held-out degradation, while GEPA helps on MATH-500 (0.828 to 0.904) but reproduces baseline behavior on HotpotQA. The paper contributes much-needed negative and conditional results about prompt/skill optimization generalization.

entry.title: MatchCityLoc: Aerial Localization in LoD City Models via Surface Normal Matching

author.name: Oussema Dhaouadi, Zuria Bauer, Johannes Michael Meier, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Cremers, Olaf Wysocki

entry.summary: MatchCityLoc localizes UAVs against textureless LoD city models by shifting from 2D silhouette-overlap scoring to direct feature matching from a noisy 6-DoF pose prior, using surface normals extracted from the query image. This addresses geometric ambiguities in GNSS-denied urban navigation while using lightweight, privacy-preserving city models. Strong author list including Pollefeys and Cremers.

entry.title: HiQGS: Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Querying for Feed-Forward Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Qiaowei Miao, Qifeng Cheng, Yijing Guo, Yuru Xiao, Ziqian Ni, Sheng Yang

entry.summary: HiQGS is a query-based hierarchical framework for feed-forward Gaussian splatting reconstruction from sparse posed monocular frames. It explicitly organizes evidence by temporal relation to the requested timestamp across spatial scales and viewpoints, overcoming frame-coupled or compact-latent-query limitations.

entry.title: Gaze2HOI: Gaze-Aware Intention Disambiguation for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Forecasting

author.name: Chuanyang Ma, Chenye Wang, Yixuan Wang, Huiling Zhou, Xingqun Qi, Muyi Sun, Man Zhang, Caifeng Shan, Zhenan Sun

entry.summary: Gaze2HOI uses gaze cues to disambiguate intention in egocentric hand-object interaction forecasting, decomposing the problem into intention inference, contact grounding, and coupled hand-object motion generation. This matters for proactive AR/VR and embodied assistants where similar observation histories can precede different futures. The hierarchical formulation is grounded in behavioral evidence about gaze.

entry.title: DocLayout-YOLO: Axis-Attentive Document Layout Detector with Mesh-Guided Synthetic Pretraining

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhao, Hengrui Kang, Guang Liang, Bin Wang, Conghui He

entry.summary: DocLayout-YOLO adapts real-time YOLO detectors to heterogeneous document layout analysis via a large synthetic pretraining corpus (MeshLayout-1M) generated by a mesh-candidate best-fit algorithm, plus page-axis context modeling. It targets efficient, accurate document parsing needed by modern document AI pipelines.

entry.title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Om Shivam Verma, Shaya Farahmand, Lingjun Zhao, Lu Gan

entry.summary: CoGaussian enables collaborative semantic occupancy prediction with open vocabulary by representing scenes as sparse foundation-model-aligned 3D Gaussians that agents share and fuse, going beyond predefined class sets and dense voxel annotations. It targets multi-robot and transportation safety scenarios where agents must understand beyond their individual fields of view.

entry.title: Using Set Learning to Improve Set-Valued Classifiers on Long-tailed Data

author.name: Kevin Kasa, Scott C. Lowe, Graham W. Taylor

entry.summary: This work investigates why set-valued classifiers, which communicate uncertainty by predicting variable-sized label sets, degrade badly on long-tailed datasets under macro-average evaluation. The authors study how training dynamics, loss functions, and training strategies affect post-hoc set calibration, proposing set learning approaches that improve SVC performance on imbalanced data. It matters because set-valued prediction is a promising uncertainty-communication mechanism whose imbalance weaknesses had been poorly understood.

entry.title: Migrate Computation, Not Data: Fault Recovery in Neuromorphic Many-Core Systems

author.name: Muyang Cao, Di Yu, Peiling Zhu, Linshan Jiang, Xin Du, Shuiguang Deng, Gang Pan

entry.summary: SpikeRelay is an online fault-recovery framework for neuromorphic many-core systems that migrates computation rather than full neuron states when a compute datapath fails, exploiting separability between memory and compute units. This avoids the high recovery traffic and scarce-destination bottleneck of whole-core retirement, which fails at high utilization when free storage is insufficient. It addresses a genuine longevity problem as neuromorphic hardware scales to thousands of cores.

entry.title: Minimum-Time Escape from the Conic Field of View of a Reeds-Shepp Pursuer: Classification and Game Value for a Slower or Equally Fast Evader

author.name: Ubaldo Ruiz

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves a global escape/holding classification for an omnidirectional evader escaping the conic field of view of a Reeds-Shepp car-like pursuer, covering speed ratios below, within, and above a critical threshold dependent on the cone half-angle. For the slower evader case, the authors construct the solution via Isaacs' characteristics with feedback-form verification, reducing escape-time computation to the root of a scalar equation. The work provides closed-form guarantees for a pursuit-evasion game with realistic vehicle constraints.

entry.title: Physical AI for Intralogistics: Benchmarking the NVIDIA Sim-to-Real Ecosystem for Cosmos-Enhanced COMPASS Navigation on Industrial Mobile Robots

author.name: Charbel Abi Hana (Idealworks), Rayan Zaitouni (Idealworks), Kameel Amareen (Idealworks), Mohamad Mostafa (Idealworks), Hasan Sayour (Idealworks), Wei Liu (NVIDIA), Yan Chang (NVIDIA), Mihir Acharya (NVIDIA), Anthony Rizk (Idealworks)

entry.summary: An industry collaboration between Idealworks and NVIDIA benchmarking the sim-to-real reliability of learned navigation policies trained via NVIDIA's X-Mobility and COMPASS workflow, extended with the Cosmos ecosystem, on real industrial mobile robots. The study covers differential-drive and omnidirectional humanoid mobile platform embodiments plus a digital twin of the Idealworks R&D center.

entry.title: A Bayesian machine learning approach to direct and spillover effects in cluster-randomized trials with noncompliance

author.name: Saurabh Bhandari, Fan Li, Michael J. Daniels

entry.summary: The paper combines Bayesian additive regression trees with cluster-level random effects to estimate direct and spillover effects in cluster-randomized trials with treatment noncompliance. A peer-treatment clever covariate mitigates regularization-induced bias, and Bayesian g-computation yields cluster-average ITT and LATE estimates with sensitivity analyses.

entry.title: Agent Action Steering

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: The author explores whether activation steering techniques, previously used to change what models say (like Golden Gate Claude), can compel agents to take specific external actions during task execution. The post extends the linear representation hypothesis and steering toolkit from text-level behavior to agentic behavior, with encouraging initial results.

entry.title: DIVE: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Interaction with Visual Engagement in Continuous Streams

author.name: Yuhang Chen, Guangyue Liu, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: DIVE is a benchmark evaluating full-duplex multimodal interaction, testing whether models can continuously identify task-relevant cues in evolving audio-visual streams and decide when and how to respond. It organizes six tasks across three interaction scenarios, moving beyond timestamped QA used by existing streaming benchmarks.

entry.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition

author.name: Sasi Kiran Gaddipati, Gollam Rabby, S\"oren Auer

entry.summary: CollabSciReM is a goal-conditioned reward framework for aligning LLMs as multi-turn scientific research collaborators, decomposing session-level rewards into conversational quality, scientific rigor, and structural efficiency. It shows that general collaborative rewards can compress responses at the cost of scientific rigor, and its science-aware decomposition aims to balance accuracy, methodological justification, and token efficiency. This targets the growing use of LLMs in hypothesis refinement and analysis.

entry.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery

author.name: Yazhuo Liu, Kunqing Ding, Xiaoguo Gong, Zifeng Wang, Yichen Yang, Yifeng Che, Wen Chen, Josh Kacher, Olivier Pierron, Shigenobu Ogata, Ting Zhu

entry.summary: GBClaw is an agentic AI framework integrating LLMs into a modular architecture (orchestrator, specialized agents, domain tools, simulations) for investigating structure and deformation of general grain boundaries in polycrystalline materials. It aims to automate complex mechanistic investigations that have been bottlenecked by structural complexity of general grain boundaries.

entry.title: Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform

author.name: Sho Sonoda, Luca Galimberti, Yuanchao Xu, Isao Ishikawa, Masahiro Ikeda

entry.summary: This theory paper extends the ridgelet transform to continuous maps on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, relevant to operator learning, replacing unavailable Lebesgue measure with Gaussian weights on the direction space. The resulting transform has a Plancherel identity and reconstruction formulas, yielding constructive rather than existence-based universal approximation for infinite-dimensional networks. This addresses a gap in the theoretical foundations of operator learning.

entry.title: Structured Latent Dynamics for Long-Horizon Embodied World Models

author.name: Kevin Chen, Yu-Wei Zhan, Haoran Liang, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HWM, a world-model framework that structures latent evolution in a learned phase space of generalized coordinates and momenta, propagating states via dissipative Hamiltonian dynamics to stabilize long-horizon action-conditioned prediction. This counters the drift that unconstrained transition modules exhibit during recursive rollouts.

entry.title: Learning without Overwriting: Structural Knowledge Fusion for Continual Learning

author.name: Kanishk Bakshi, Amitansu Pattanaik, Kathiravan Srinivasan

entry.summary: The Knowledge Fusion Network mitigates catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental learning by learning each task in an isolated lightweight specialist network and fusing it into a global model via a Structural Fusion Module that allocates dedicated channel capacity conditioned on a novelty score. This novelty-gated structural expansion decouples task acquisition from knowledge consolidation. It attacks the stability-plasticity trade-off architecturally rather than through parameter negotiation.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning Teaches LLMs Long-Horizon Implicit Reasoning, Up To A Limit

author.name: Jimson Huang, Maxwell Nickell, Ruowang Zhang, Abulhair Saparov

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether curriculum learning can extend LLMs implicit (single-forward-pass) reasoning depth, which matters because strong implicit reasoning lets models search ahead during chain-of-thought without costly backtracking. The title-telegraphed finding is that curricula help but hit a limit, consistent with prior evidence that implicit reasoning does not scale with model size. A careful empirical study of a fundamental reasoning limitation.

entry.title: Remember Less, Adapt Longer: Bounded-State In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Recurrent Summary Memory

author.name: Jiawen Wang, Cheng Xue, Peng Zhang, Jochen Renz

entry.summary: Recurrent Summary Memory (RSM) is a Transformer policy for in-context RL that attends exactly to a short working buffer of recent interactions while using recurrently updated summary memories to retain longer-horizon experience under bounded state. This avoids the growing costs of full-history attention and accumulating summaries while preserving more access than sliding windows or pure hidden states. It enables continual adaptation without parameter updates at constant per-decision cost.

entry.title: ProtGlycanDock: Towards Accurate Protein-Glycan Docking with Tailored Dataset, Benchmark and Model

author.name: Minghao Xu, Jiaze Song, Jinyu Wang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: The authors curate ProtGlycanDock, the first tailored benchmark for protein-glycan docking with protein and glycan generalization splits, and evaluate ten models across physics-based docking, ML docking, and structure prediction categories. They further propose two fine-tuning techniques that inject glycan conformational knowledge to improve binding poses. This fills a real resource gap in structural biology for interactions governing many biological processes.

entry.title: Cross-Fitting for Neural Posterior Estimation

author.name: Jeffrey Regier

entry.summary: The paper identifies a degeneracy in Neural Posterior Estimation: the log-likelihood training objective rewards arbitrarily high density on training points, and flexible density estimators oblige, producing overconfident posteriors that generalize poorly. Early stopping and related regularizers are limited because they operate along an unfavorable trajectory set by in-sample residuals. The proposed cross-fitting scheme offers a principled alternative for fitting amortized conditional density estimators, relevant to simulation-based inference across the sciences.

entry.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Zhaoxin Yu, Xinglin Xiao, Nan Xu

entry.summary: TIRE is a framework for generating verifiable physics reasoning training data by instantiating problems from reusable physical formulas with controlled applicability conditions, then validating answers through reliable execution rather than trusting LLM outputs. This combines expert-style top-down control with scalable synthesis.

entry.title: AudioScorer: Learning Question-Aware Token Relevance for Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Marwan Farag, Bin Yang

entry.summary: AudioScorer is a lightweight module that scores audio tokens by relevance to the user question, trained by distilling answer-gradient saliency rankings from the frozen LALM plus answer supervision. It outperforms heuristic audio-pruning baselines (attention, similarity, temporal sampling) and reduces the cost of processing long-form audio. This extends question-aware token pruning, common in vision, to audio language models.

entry.title: Counting Contributions, Not Views: Occlusion-Aware Densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Marcel Rogge, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: The paper identifies a flaw in 3D Gaussian Splatting's adaptive density control: the frustum-based visibility filter counts fully occluded Gaussians as observed, diluting gradient statistics and suppressing densification in occluded regions. The proposed occlusion-aware filter and average-contribution normalizer improve all image-quality metrics within a StopThePop-based framework. This is a precise diagnosis-and-fix contribution to a widely used pipeline.

entry.title: PanoGraphGS: Unifying Panoptic Segmentation and Hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs with Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jinghan Gao, Siyu Wang, Dongyu Feng, Yiyuan Pan, Rong Xiong

entry.summary: PanoGraphGS integrates panoptic 3D Gaussian representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph construction, learning semantic and instance features on shared Gaussian geometry for view-consistent predictions. The structured maps support language-guided navigation and novel-view panoptic segmentation.

entry.title: Auto-Director: Leveraging Multi-Agent Collaboration for Autonomous Video Editing

author.name: Yuxia Chen, Wenbo Zhu, Yangguang Ji, Zhenxiang Jiang, Teng Zhong, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Auto-Director is a tool-augmented multi-agent framework for autonomous video editing that mirrors professional post-production workflows, with planning, material indexing, and editing agents coordinating retrieval-augmented scripting, shot segmentation, and structured multi-stage reasoning over open-world footage. It aims to combine retrieval flexibility with long-horizon coherence that neither retrieval nor generative approaches alone achieve.

entry.title: Continual Concept Personalization in Diffusion Models via Residual-Space Adaptation

author.name: Yuzhi Liu, Enis Simsar, Giulia Lanzillotta, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: The paper addresses continual personalization of text-to-image diffusion models, where user concepts arrive sequentially, by extending residual-space adaptation to the stochastic adaptation process of pretrained diffusion models. It reports the highest concept fidelity among competing continual personalization methods while limiting interference with previously learned concepts.

entry.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring

author.name: Shrish Shrinath Vaidya, Minmini Selvam, Ganapathy Krishnamurthi

entry.summary: MedPAO-Assist is an agentic system that converts radiologist dictation and voice commands into structured radiology reports while running entirely on a standard laptop CPU, requiring about 3.3 GB peak RAM with roughly 31-second end-to-end latency. It targets clinical privacy and offline-operation constraints that block cloud-based LLM adoption.

entry.title: An LLM-Based Agent for Legal Compliance Assessment: Architecture, Memory, and Evaluation in a Canadian and Quebec Context

author.name: Soukaina Alaoui Ismaili, Jean-Sebastien Dessureault

entry.summary: Describes ComplianceAgent, the legal-compliance sub-agent of the COMPASS multi-agent framework, which scores texts against a rubric grounded in a reference legal corpus and triggers a corrective chain of self-healing rewrites, explainability reports, and human escalation when scores fall below a critical threshold. Evaluated in the Canadian and Quebec legal context across sovereignty, carbon, compliance, and ethics axes.

entry.title: The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task

author.name: Pei Liu

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of single-agent versus three-agent LLM setups reviewing credit-assessment memos against six requirements, using 300 synthetic memos with known labels to measure misses and false alarms separately across four models. The multi-agent team catches 0.08 to 0.10 more requirements but the paper tests whether the popular practitioner claim about multi-agent review holds under rigorous conditions.

entry.title: TriGeoBench: A Multimodal Mathematical Geometry Benchmark with Figures and TikZ

author.name: Jing Wang, Yitong Yang, Hao Dou, Yaomin Wu, Shuting He, Tingfei Shen, Jia Wu, Jiaqi Li, Yinglin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces TriGeoBench, a 7,000-question multimodal geometry benchmark from Chinese secondary-school exams featuring 12,235 figures with TikZ source code across plane, solid, analytic, function, and vector geometry. Symbolic figure representations enable assessment of whether models genuinely reason over geometric structures rather than exploit rasterized visual patterns.

entry.title: How Fine-Tuning Objectives Shape Layer-Wise Information in LLM Hallucination Detection

author.name: Kaiyang Wan, Forrest Sheng Bao, Amin Ahmad, Yuxia Wang

entry.summary: Explains why classifier-head fine-tuning outperforms LLM-as-Judge seq2seq fine-tuning on binary hallucination detection by tracing representation geometry: classifier objectives learn discriminative directions with clear two-cluster separation, while seq2seq objectives leave hidden states near the pretrained backbone. The analysis illuminates how fine-tuning objectives reorganize layer-wise information.

entry.title: LatBridge: Efficient and Stable Model Replacement in Latent-Communication Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jiajun Zhu, Haobo Li, Zixin Chen, Huamin Qu, Wenshuo Zhang

entry.summary: LatBridge addresses interface failure in latent-communication multi-agent systems when agent models are replaced, connecting agents through a shared Bridge and separate interfaces under a shared protocol. It reuses unchanged interfaces, selects matching low-rank interfaces, and combines them to maintain communication after model swaps.

entry.title: From Comparison to Selection: Enhancing Cross-Scale Generalization of Pointer Networks Trained with Reinforcement Learning for Capacitated Drone Delivery Routing

author.name: Sofiene Lassoued, Devara Tertia, Stefan Lier, Andreas Schwung

entry.summary: This work improves cross-scale generalization of RL-trained Pointer Networks for capacitated routing problems (a proxy for drone delivery), proposing a shift from comparison-based to selection-based output so a single policy generalizes across problem sizes without retraining. It addresses quality degradation under both upscaling and downscaling of client counts.

entry.title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning

author.name: Qi Wang, Peijie Wang, Jun Cao, Haoyang Tong, Xiao-Hui Li, Fei Yin, Cheng-Lin Liu

entry.summary: ChartEvo is a recursive self-improvement framework that lets chart-reasoning agents adapt their harnesses to underperforming long-tail chart types through experience, avoiding manual tool engineering. It targets the sharp accuracy drop of multimodal LLMs on charts with uncommon visual structures.

entry.title: Value-Rich, Differently Organized: Measuring Value Expression and Organization in AI-Generated Debates

author.name: Maoyuan Li, Haoyuan Li, Zhongsheng Wang, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: This work presents a diagnostic metric framework comparing how values are expressed and organized in human-reference versus AI-generated debates, grounded in Schwartz's Basic-10 value theory. It separates value expression from value organization and models debates as multi-level value distributions over argumentative units, enabling metrics for coverage, alignment, diffusion, and cross-turn dynamics. Findings indicate AI debates are value-rich but organized differently from human debates.

entry.title: Uncertainty Gates the Gradient: Adaptive Updates for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Segmentation

author.name: Yifei Zhao, Fanyu Zhao, Shengtang Wu, Han Zhang, Ruike Cao, Yinsheng Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes Uncertainty-Gated Adaptive (UGA), the first framework that uses uncertainty as update-level gating for generalized few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation, rather than merely reweighting losses. It prevents low-quality, sparse, or occluded support annotations from steering optimization toward spurious geometric patterns. This improves robustness when adapting to novel concepts with compromised annotations.

entry.title: Representing short-term movement to reveal animal identity and learning progress

author.name: Ping Zhang, Quang-Huy Nguyen, Yingtie Lei, Sameera Shridhar, Zachary Leveroni, Ellie Quattrocchi, Jai Y Yu, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: The authors introduce a self-supervised representation learning framework based on the hypothesis that behavioral characteristics tied to identity and learning remain stable over nearby time intervals, showing that short-term movement trajectories in freely behaving animals can reveal individual identity and learning progress. This offers an observable behavioral measure of learning beyond task performance.

entry.title: LoWAgent: A Low-Resource Multilingual Benchmark for Web Agents

author.name: Ocean Monjur, Daud Ahmad Nisar, Shahriar Kabir Nahin, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Sushruti Mishra, Israel Abebe Azime, Anshuman Chhabra

entry.summary: LoWAgent is a benchmark evaluating web agents on localized websites in four low-resource languages (Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, Amharic) versus English, comprising six fully localized websites across five languages yielding 3,000 task instances. It evaluates closed-source and open-source agents, revealing gaps in multilingual web-agent capability.

entry.title: Generalizing Multimodal Foundational Models in Context-Driven Class Incremental Learning

author.name: Avi Gupta, Nilotpal Sinha, Vishnu Raj, Sambuddha Saha, Pratik Joshi, Koteswar Rao Jerripothula, Tammam Tillo

entry.summary: The paper extends class-incremental learning to the underexplored audio-visual modality, showing that frozen multimodal foundation model representations struggle in incremental settings and proposing an attention-based contextual guidance module where audio representations act as task stabilizers. This generalizes frozen MFMs to audio-visual continual learning without forgetting. It addresses a real gap at the intersection of continual learning and multimodality.

entry.title: HealBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Psychological Comfort in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Junjie Xu, Yuzhe Yang, Rui Yang, Luwei Xiao, Wenxin Wu, Xingjiao Wu, Liang He

entry.summary: HealBench defines psychological comfort as a measurable property of text-to-image outputs and provides a benchmark of 30,000 image-text pairs across 19 categories and 92 subcategories, curated via a human- and expert-in-the-loop pipeline. The work opens a human-centered evaluation dimension for generative image models beyond photorealism and aesthetics. It has potential relevance for therapeutic and supportive applications of image generation.

entry.title: Beyond Calibration: Temporal LLM Confidence Assessment Across Languages and Local Settings

author.name: Sahil Kale

entry.summary: Inspired by meta-memory theory, this paper distinguishes anticipatory pre-solve confidence (Feeling-of-Knowing) from retrospective post-solve confidence (Judgement-of-Learning) in LLMs, testing whether these temporal signals encode distinct epistemic information. Evaluation spans two frontier LLMs, multiple reasoning domains, and both translated and genuinely local Marathi benchmarks. The multilingual, local-knowledge focus extends confidence research beyond English-centric settings.

entry.title: Physical-Variable-Informed Deep Learning for Robust Diagnosis in Industrial Fluid Transport Systems

author.name: Yu Sha, Junqi Tao, Dixin Zhou, Horst Stoecker, Domagoj Vnucec, Andreas Widl, Kai Zhou

entry.summary: PhyNet is a physics-informed deep learning framework for fault diagnosis in industrial fluid transport systems that treats physical variables as global operating constraints and response signals as local diagnostic evidence. A physical-to-response cross-attention mechanism connects sequence-level physical-variable tokens with a learnable global response token, avoiding strict temporal alignment across heterogeneous sampling regimes. This improves robustness under real-world sampling heterogeneity.

entry.title: Same Judgment, Different Yes: Measuring Multilingual Judgment Profiles in Language Models

author.name: Haonan Huang, Yuwei Lu, Chengkun Cai

entry.summary: A large-scale study collecting 1.1 million replies from eight models in six languages on moral vignettes, showing that story-level judgment profiles converge across elicitation formats except for yes/no tokens after negative interrogatives, where token and sentence-level readouts disagree. The work distinguishes genuine judgment from answer-format habits in multilingual evaluation.

entry.title: PI-MLLM: Psychophysics-Inspired Multimodal Large Language Model for Oddly Satisfying Video Emotion Analysis

author.name: Yuheng Zhang, Jie Zhang, Yuecong Min, Yunwei Zhao, Meichen Liu, Qiankun Li, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Oddly Satisfying Video emotion analysis, a challenging setting where repetitive motion and ASMR-like sensory cues, not semantic content, drive viewer emotion. The authors release OSVD, a dataset of 12,000 annotated clips with video-only, audio-only, and audio-visual emotion labels plus sensory-grounded explanations, and propose a psychophysics-inspired multimodal model for the task. This opens a novel affective-computing problem with an accompanying resource.

entry.title: A Digital Twin to Improve Cyber-Social Impact

author.name: Vita Santa Barletta, Danilo Caivano, Gabriel Cellammare, Andrea Dimauro, Pasquale Mesagna, Massimiliano Morga

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework combining Digital Twin technology with a Cyber-Social Security model to simulate and quantify cyber threats in industrial control systems, extending beyond the traditional CIA triad to capture societal and operational impacts of attacks. Virtualized ICS environments built with Mininet and MiniCPS are used to model attack scenarios across technical and social dimensions.

entry.title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration

author.name: Karl Li (Columbia University)

entry.summary: This paper formally distinguishes conformal reliability (per-time coverage gap of a reset rule after an announced boundary) from frequency calibration (realized error rate in a closed window) for forecasting after distribution breaks. The authors prove minimax per-time rates for an empirical-quantile reset rule and characterize a frequency gap recursion, showing with synthetic experiments that their reset rule outperforms five adaptive methods on the per-time metric.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining on Multi-Domain Raman Spectra

author.name: Charalampos Davalas, Georgios Levantinos, Anastasios Dimitriou, Nikolaos Papanikolaou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Dimitrios Michail

entry.summary: The paper presents a masked-autoencoder framework for Raman spectroscopy that combines masked intensity reconstruction with a sparse Voigt-profile decoder capturing peak structure via differentiable parameters, plus a denoising objective. Pretrained across heterogeneous biological, chemical, forensic, and materials datasets, the encoder transfers to downstream substance identification tasks.

entry.title: Alliance of Stochastic Routing and Reinforcement Fusion for Multi-Model Reasoning

author.name: Selim Furkan Tekin, Ling Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents VL-Scout, a vision-language framework for routing and composing multiple models under uncertainty using turn-based reinforcement fusion. It combines Bayesian priors, policy gradients, and a Dirichlet belief model to represent epistemic uncertainty over model quality, aiming to avoid premature convergence to suboptimal routers. The system targets efficient multimodal multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Budgeted Bayesian Bandits for Future Utilization

author.name: Sudipto Guha
