entry.summary: This theory paper studies multi-armed bandits where exploration has a hard budget preceding exploitation. The authors show prior 1/3 and 4/27 approximation analyses are tight, then provide a new efficient algorithm achieving 0.43 approximation and one approaching 1-e^{-1} (~0.63) for bounded exchangeable reward observations. It meaningfully advances the approximation guarantees for this bandit variant.

entry.title: Power-Law Correlations Without Apparent Temperature-Tuned Criticality in Fixed-Tree Hierarchical Languages

author.name: Marcel K\"uhn, Bernd Rosenow

entry.summary: Using a controlled analogue of temperature sampling in probabilistic context-free grammars on fixed trees, the authors measure two-point mutual information between tokens and find it follows a power-law envelope across temperatures. This suggests temperature-induced changes in long-range correlations need not reflect genuine phase transitions, challenging interpretations of temperature effects in autoregressive models.

entry.title: Exact Risk Certificates for Pairwise-Judged Reranking

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Jingrui Tian, Sicheng Lyu, Yu Gu, Ziyang Song, Xiao-Wen Chang, Lei Ding

entry.summary: The paper derives exact worst-case nDCG loss bounds for reranking proposals judged by pairwise comparisons, reducing threshold verification to maximum-closure problems. On TREC-DL it saves roughly 2 comparisons per query versus exact verification, with savings transferring to BEIR and alternative proposers.

entry.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series

author.name: Zhaodong Guo (Imperial College London), Haoyun Feng (Imperial College London)

entry.summary: The paper introduces HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that compiles irregular time series into a fixed-rank functional space supporting direct coordinate queries, using kernel-smoothed HiPPO coordinates and Gram-based readout. This avoids repeatedly resolving observation-dependent representations for each temporal query.

entry.title: Theory-Guided Instance-Dependent Early Stopping via Second-Order Loss Dynamics

author.name: Ahad Bin Islam Shoeb, Jamal Uddin Tanvin, Kamrul Hasan, Alve Reduan, Imtiaz Ahmed

entry.summary: TG-IES provides the first theoretical justification for instance-dependent early stopping, which skips backpropagation on examples whose losses have stabilized. The authors derive a noise-calibrated mastery threshold and stability bounds, showing second-order loss differencing has favorable bias-variance trade-offs in a specific signal-to-noise regime.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations

author.name: Weibo Huang, Qing Feng, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua

entry.summary: AI-GPB is a variance-reduction method for Bayesian optimization that combines an offline auxiliary mean estimate with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. It exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective, with finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning with General Utilities via Neural Dual Critics

author.name: Ankur Naskar, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: The authors develop a natural actor-critic method for reinforcement learning with general utilities (nonlinear functionals of occupancy measures) that learns the policy-gradient pseudo-reward directly with a neural critic trained via projected stochastic updates. Multilevel Monte Carlo controls critic bias at logarithmic expected cost, with theoretical separation of actor and critic biases.

entry.title: Block Recursive Transformers for Structured Parameter Sharing

author.name: Josep Marques, Hyunyoung A. Cho, Youngeun Kim, Youjia Zhang, Aecheon Jung, Kyuhong Shim, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: BRT proposes an intermediate parameter-sharing topology for recursive Transformers, partitioning layers into contiguous blocks that are recursively reused before advancing, balancing layer-wise repetition against global cyclic reuse. This enables local refinement while preserving depth-wise transitions without extra routing modules.

entry.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Pointwise Replicable Agnostic Learning

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper determines the optimal agnostic sample complexity for pointwise replicable learning, where two learners sharing a random seed must agree at each query with high probability. It establishes matching upper and lower bounds of Theta(d/(rho^2 alpha^2) + log(1/beta)/alpha^2) for finite VC dimension classes. It resolves a definitional question in the growing replicability literature.

entry.title: M-JEPA: Predictive Self-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs with Scaffold-Shift Evaluation on Tox21

author.name: Karthik Iyer, Nasser Sabar

entry.summary: M-JEPA adapts JEPA-style predictive self-supervision to molecular graphs by masking chemically coherent subgraphs and training a context encoder to regress EMA-teacher target embeddings. It also introduces a leakage-resistant, compute-matched three-phase evaluation protocol including scaffold-shift testing on Tox21. The work contributes both a method and a more rigorous evaluation standard for molecular representation learning.

entry.title: Predicted Class Correction: Conformal Thresholds for Classes with No Calibration Data

author.name: One Octadion, Novanto Yudistira, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: The paper proposes Predicted Class Correction (PCC), which regresses the offset between per-class and marginal conformal quantiles from label-free geometric descriptors of the classifier head, enabling class-conditional conformal prediction for rare classes with no calibration data. This addresses a real gap in long-tailed deployments. The work extends practical conformal prediction to settings where calibration data is inherently scarce.

entry.title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data

author.name: Abdelkrim Alfalah

entry.summary: The paper identifies three timing pitfalls causing look-ahead leakage in electricity price studies: delayed availability of archived weather forecasts, timezone mismatches between auction gates and UTC archives, and unflagged revisions of outturn series. It quantifies leakage using 128,656 forecast runs matched to auction gates. This is a valuable reproducibility contribution showing published energy forecasting results may be optimistically biased.

entry.title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Junyu Chen, Franklin Liu, Moshu Xu, Lijian Yang

entry.summary: LOBGrad is a conditional DDPM framework for probabilistic limit order book forecasting that combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion generator, and provides an excess-risk oracle inequality for the one-step noise-prediction objective under mixing assumptions. It brings formal statistical guarantees to a domain where diffusion models previously lacked them. Relevant to market simulation and execution-strategy evaluation.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning on the EPRI AI-ccelerating Unit Commitment benchmark: diagnosing over-commitment and guiding MILP with learned policies

author.name: Maharani Devira Pramita, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: This is the first study of RL on the EPRI 51-generator, 72-hour unit commitment benchmark, showing that PPO and action-branching DQN agents commit roughly twice the units of the MILP optimum at 39-64% higher cost, and tracing the gap to exploration behavior. The authors then show the learned policy can accelerate an exact MILP solver rather than replace it. A sober, honest assessment of RL versus classical optimization in power systems.

entry.title: A "feature ODE" describing the learning behavior of shallow MLPs on simple functions

author.name: Joseph Turnbull, Berkan Ottlik, Jamie Simon

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes a simplified feature ODE to describe gradient flow training dynamics of two-layer MLPs on anisotropic Gaussian data, testing it on low-order Hermite polynomials and staircase functions. Surprisingly, real training loss trajectories roughly track the ODE predictions despite the lack of a rigorous approximation chain. The work offers a tractable lens on neural network learning dynamics that could inform deeper theoretical understanding.

entry.title: Rubrics Beyond Evaluation: Exploiting Rubric Structure in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuxun Huang, Yunyao Zhang, ZeLiang Chen, Yi-Ping Phoebe Chen, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: RSRL is an RL framework that uses the structure of rubrics, decomposing open-ended quality into explicit criteria, as training guidance rather than treating them merely as direct reward signals. It models the capabilities behind rubric criteria and exploits this structure throughout training. This extends rubrics from an evaluation tool into a structured supervision signal for RL fine-tuning of open-ended generation.

entry.title: Learn the Interface, Not the Implementation: Output Representation Dominates Training Regime in LLM-Based RTL Generation

author.name: Siddharth Patel, Vikram Singh, Siddharth Savyasachi Malu, Rohit Singh

entry.summary: This controlled study argues that for LLM-based hardware (RTL) code generation, the choice of output representation matters more than the training regime. Holding task, data, and a formal equivalence oracle fixed for SECDED ECC wrapper generation, the authors vary seven training settings and four output abstraction levels. The finding that representation dominates is counterintuitive and actionable for applied LLM-for-code work.

entry.title: FinHopper: A Progressive Multi-Hop Benchmark for Complex Financial Agents with Step-wise Evaluation

author.name: Yuxuan Wu, Miaopei Lin, Qiufang Ying, Lin Dan, Hao Zhao, Qirui Liu, Yuteng Shen, Shaohui Wu, Weihong Luo, Xiku Du, Xing Tang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: FinHopper is a benchmark for financial multi-hop agents with controlled reasoning depth from 1 to 6 hops over stocks, funds, and macroeconomic facts, featuring gold intermediate answers for process-level evaluation. It exploits the strict answer-conditioned dependency structure of financial retrieval, where each intermediate answer is a typed constraint that determines the next query, and includes a state-transition-based synthesis framework for scale construction. This enables diagnosis of error cascades in agentic search.

entry.title: TaQFormer: A Treatment-as-Query Transformer with Data-Fusion for Multidimensional Treatment Modeling in Coupon Allocation

author.name: Jiahong Li, Zeqin Yang, Yu Xiang, Zhifan Jiang, Jingqi Ma, Enzheng Hua, Jixing Xu, Jun Wu, Fei Wang, Enyun Yu, Jiecheng Guo

entry.summary: TaQFormer is a Transformer that models multidimensional treatments (category-specific coupon discounts) by treating each treatment coordinate as a query token with cross-attention estimating response to the full treatment vector. A two-stage pipeline pretrains on policy-biased observational logs and fine-tunes with LoRA on smaller randomized controlled trial data. This is relevant to causal inference and uplift modeling in industrial marketplace settings.

entry.title: CTLite: Lightweight Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Reusable Continuous-Time Summaries

author.name: Shusen Ma, Xudong Zuo, Yangchun Xie, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: CTLite decouples historical summarization from learned prediction in irregular multivariate time series forecasting, using a parameter-free continuous-time moment encoder that summarizes local levels and trends at multiple scales, plus a compact readout with damped extrapolation and low-rank cross-variable correction. This avoids repeatedly re-encoding observations and offers strong efficiency. Lightweight, interpretable IMTSF methods are valuable for deployment on constrained hardware.

entry.title: SleepPairNet: Learning Multimodal Pediatric Sleep Representations with Random-Pair Cross-Attention

author.name: Saurav Raj Pandey, Harlin Lee

entry.summary: SleepPairNet is a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns pairwise interactions between physiological sleep signals via cross-attention, using a random modality-pair selection strategy during pretraining for flexibility at test time. Pretrained on the NCH dataset, it outperforms SSL baselines on all respiratory tasks while staying competitive on EEG-related tasks. It demonstrates a practical route to modality-flexible clinical representation learning.

entry.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions

author.name: Rui Shi, Xunjian Yin, Jiacheng Sang, Zichuan Liu, Shuyan Zhou

entry.summary: WeAct addresses catastrophic forgetting and fixed parameter configurations in long-horizon agents by training capability-specific LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone and adding adapter selection to the agent action space via the native tool-calling interface. This enables on-demand capability composition within a shared context as task requirements change across trajectory stages.

entry.title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction

author.name: Josef Biberstein, Sertac Karaman

entry.summary: Presents Orbital Terrain Networks, a neural inverse rendering method that jointly optimizes a textured height map and orbital camera corrections directly from calibrated line-scan satellite images, replacing complex multi-view stereo pipelines for digital terrain map creation. Applications include landing site selection and terrain-relative navigation in planetary exploration. The joint optimization handles pose error and varying illumination that plague traditional approaches.

entry.title: Reducing double-dipping in single-cell topic models with three-way count splitting

author.name: Zheng Qu

entry.summary: This work identifies severe statistical leakage in single-cell topic models where the same counts are used both to learn gene programs and test gene/donor associations, and shows the standard two-way count splitting fails when an encoder is involved. The proposed three-way count splitting with beta-binomial thinning reduces null-gene false rejections from roughly 36-38% down to about 7.7% on a large lupus cohort.

entry.title: CoCoNet: Convex Conformal Network for Multi-Dimensional Uncertainty Regions

author.name: Alireza Moradi, Thomas Bruys, Pascal Van Hentenryck, Reza Zandehshahvar

entry.summary: CoCoNet learns convex conformity scores for conformal prediction in multivariate regression, optimizing prediction-region efficiency on held-out data while enforcing convexity in the residual, then applying split-conformal calibration to retain finite-sample coverage guarantees. This produces flexible, data-adaptive joint uncertainty regions that better capture cross-output dependencies than standard conformity scores.

entry.title: MSCR: Jointly Balancing Utilization Across Modalities and Discovering Synergistic Information

author.name: Xinyu Chen, Liangjian Wen, Jiang Duan, Dongkai Wang, Yong Dai, Jiayu Bai, Jianzhuang Liu, Zhen Tian, Guoping Qiu, Zhao Kan

entry.summary: MSCR extends the Multimodal Competition Regularizer to jointly balance modality utilization and promote synergistic information during fusion, i.e., predictive gain unattainable from any single modality. This targets the modality imbalance problem in multimodal learning where one modality dominates optimization.

entry.title: Contrastive Hypergraph Source-free Domain Adaptive Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions--Extended Version

author.name: Jicheng Yuan, Tung Kieu, Manh Nguyen-Duc, Manfred Hauswirth, Danh Le-Phuoc

entry.summary: REUNION is a source-free domain adaptation framework for object detection under fog, rain, snow, and low illumination, using a contrastive hypergraph over target-domain object proposals to capture high-order relations. It addresses weaknesses of pairwise contrastive SFDA methods, such as agreement collapse under severe corruption. The setting where source data is unavailable due to privacy constraints is practically important for autonomous driving and surveillance.

entry.title: Evidence Field: Adaptive Covering Programs for Medical Imaging

author.name: Isarar Siddique, Raiyan Siddique, Arshi Niyaz, Jamyang Ugyen Tshomo, Atish Raza

entry.summary: Evidence Field is a trainable spatial-program architecture for medical image classification that jointly produces class scores, selected covering programs, and signed spatial evidence, allowing independent reconstruction of the classifier's spatial decision computation. The paper establishes formal guarantees including exact one-fold coverage, grammar-constrained optimality, and signed-score conservation.

entry.title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring

author.name: Hao Fang, Miao Zhang, Haoyuan Zhao, Long Chen, Yi Ching Chou, Chi Xu, Cheng Pan, Jiangchuan Liu

entry.summary: ATLAS is an expert-guided edge-to-cloud system that treats LEO satellite bandwidth as a scarce resource for off-grid wildlife monitoring, using foundation models to select which imagery merits transmission instead of wasteful motion triggers or fixed vision models. The system dynamically adapts to evolving expert objectives while balancing solar power constraints and variable satellite link quality.

entry.title: Integrable building blocks for symplectic neural networks: learned-type layers, fiber-preserving layers, and what a single layer can do

author.name: Andrew Qing He

entry.summary: The author introduces three new families of exactly symplectic neural network layers, including learned-type layers that rotate, squeeze, or shear by state-dependent amounts, and fiber-preserving layers combining point transformations with fiber translations. This expands the design space beyond the shear maps that currently dominate symplectic network construction.

entry.title: RAIL-5G: A Challenging Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for AI-Based 5G Indoor Localization

author.name: Jonas Pirkl, Andreas Eidloth, Maximilian Kasparek, Tobias Feigl, Christopher Mutschler

entry.summary: RAIL-5G is a public real-world 5G benchmark recorded in an operational railway maintenance facility, covering 811 square meters with distributed radio units, robot-mounted user equipment, high-accuracy ground truth, and severe metal-induced multipath and NLOS conditions. It enables rigorous evaluation of AI-based indoor localization under realistic industrial conditions.

entry.title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody

author.name: Luigi Rivolta

entry.summary: This paper addresses query-by-melody retrieval for whistled and wrong-lyrics sung queries, which existing benchmarks ignore. The authors train a small 5.2M-parameter contour encoder using a physics-grounded generator that renders synthetic whistles and nonsense-syllable singing from over 11,000 songs, improving top-1 retrieval on synthetic queries, but also show that synthetic training data alone fails to close the gap to real-world queries.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning

author.name: Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: The paper characterizes fundamental communication limits of information-theoretically secure aggregation in federated learning under user dropouts, covering key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask-elimination phases. It shows existing fixed-threshold designs cannot adapt communication to actual dropout realizations and derives improved adaptive schemes with provably optimal tradeoffs.

entry.title: MITRA-lexicon: Lexica of attested translations from Sanskrit into English, Tibetan and Chinese

author.name: Sebastian Nehrdich, Kengo Harimoto, Sven Sellmer, Oliver Hellwig

entry.summary: Releases corpus-grounded multilingual lexica linking Sanskrit headwords to attested translation equivalents in English, Tibetan, and Chinese, derived from span annotations of Buddhist literature corpora. The resource totals 2.18 million headword entries across six directional lexica, grounding traditional lexicography in digitized, linked texts.

entry.title: TriScore: Post-Hoc Out-of-Distribution Detection with Energy, Boundary Probes, and Transform Consistency

author.name: Ege Gursoy, Nicolas Mansard

entry.summary: Introduces TriScore, a post-hoc OOD detector fusing three ID-calibrated signals from a frozen classifier — an energy prior, a boundary-fragility score, and a transform-consistency score — to improve robustness under classifier-level adversarial shift where single-cue detectors fail. Signals are standardized on in-distribution validation data and combined with an interpretable fusion.

entry.title: Selecting the Best Few with Human Evaluators: Adaptively Combining Ratings and Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Motti Goldberger, Nils Rudi

entry.summary: This work studies adaptive evaluation policies for identifying the top-k items from a large pool using costly human evaluations, allowing both ratings and pairwise comparisons. Ratings provide coarse signal early while comparisons refine among top candidates, and the paper develops strategies for combining them under a limited budget. Applications include LLM evaluation and hiring.

entry.title: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models

author.name: Agus Sudjianto, Denis Burakov

entry.summary: This paper analyzes training ingredients of candidate-scoring models (soft targets from teacher models, frozen pretrained backbones, temperature calibration) in Gaussian surrogate settings where finite-sample risk can be computed exactly. Key findings include that a student inherits teacher bias that more data cannot remove and agreement with the teacher does not reveal, and that frozen representations help only below an explicit sample-size threshold. The analysis targets systems like Jev and its open counterpart JevAny.

entry.title: Reasoning with Context Management and External Memory

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, William Hartmann, Jiangying Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes RCMEM, which augments context management with an external memory so reasoning models retain intermediate information without consuming context window. Reduces computation time on problems requiring repeated intermediate computation and improves performance on complex problems in small models (0.4M-25M parameters).

entry.title: When Opposite Premises Translate Identically: A Source-Conditioned Diagnostic for Multilingual Commonsense Items

author.name: Shuai Wang, Rui Hu

entry.summary: This paper presents a source-conditioned diagnostic that detects when translated multilingual benchmark items collapse: reversing the polarity of an English premise and translating both arms independently reveals whether the target-language outputs become identical, destroying counterfactual contrast. Across five languages and three translation checkpoints, Swahili shows dozens to over a hundred exact collisions among 710 pairs, and round-trip NLI validation fails for several colliding arms. The work exposes a systematic data-quality threat to multilingual reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Table Serialization Determines Which Relations Language Models Preserve

author.name: Junwei Ma, Arun Kumar Chithanar, Palash Goyal, Chul Lee

entry.summary: This diagnostic study shows that how tables are serialized into text dramatically affects instruction-tuned LLMs' ability to perform row lookups: row-major serialization wins on tall tables while column-major wins on wide tables, with gaps of 35-59 percentage points at the extremes. Error analysis maps wrong answers to which cross-column relations each format destroys. The work provides actionable guidance for table-to-text input formatting.

entry.title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations

author.name: Amirreza Mohseni, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: The authors build a multi-axis taxonomy of legal queries and apply it to 2,122 WildChat-1M conversations with a human-reviewed gold set, finding 71.1% of legally-themed conversations seek personal legal guidance. Taxonomy, checkpoints, and code are released, enabling study of how people actually seek legal help from chatbots.

entry.title: Quality-Controlled Reply and Summary Data for Post-Training Small Language Models in AI Call-Screening Agents

author.name: Jiaqi Gan, Tsang Ng, Ankit Raj, Tommy Duong, Xingyu Shen, Kidus Zewde, Huaiyu Guo, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: Constructs quality-controlled synthetic supervision to post-train small on-device language models for privacy-respecting call screening, teaching them to reply within the owner's authority during calls and produce faithful post-call summaries. Released small models currently over-alarm on ordinary callers and misreport caller claims as fact.

entry.title: VISAGENT: An Agent-Based End-to-End Voice Interaction System

author.name: Xiang Wang, Zhaoxiang Liu, Xiang Chen, Liqiang He, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: VISAGENT is an end-to-end agent-based voice interaction system for large-scale public services, combining speech interaction, hierarchical agent routing, a scalable voice-agent marketplace, and user memory. It replaces rigid menu-driven workflows with natural speech and two-level routing that achieves sub-second dispatch to general or domain-specific agents.

entry.title: SNO-PI: Label-Scarce SNOMED CT Entity Linking with Pre-trained Encoders and Curated Terminology Knowledge

author.name: Piyawoot Songsiritat

entry.summary: SNO-PI is the top-performing submission on SNOMED International's Entity Linking Benchmark as of October 2026, achieving a macro character IoU of 0.5387 versus the reference system's 0.4582. It tackles the extreme label scarcity of clinical entity linking (only 6,595 of ~219,000 eligible concepts annotated) using high-recall span proposal, SapBERT retrieval, listwise reranking, and curated terminology knowledge.

entry.title: The Geometry of Agent Memory: Forecasting Retrieval-Bound Memory Failures, and Characterizing Its Limits

author.name: Iliya Zhechev, Radoslav Ralev, Chris Coleman, Srijith Rajamohan, Jen Agarwal, Tyler Hutcherson, Simba Khadder

entry.summary: The authors test whether geometric relationships among conversation turns, memory texts, and queries can predict answer correctness before generation across four memory implementations. On LongMemEval-small, pooled AUROC is 0.640, below a question-difficulty baseline of 0.655, and after controlling for difficulty and system identity, geometry adds limited predictive value.

entry.title: WenSight-Decision-1 for Direct Decisions under E-commerce Rules

author.name: Mingwen Liu (WenSight AI Lab), Jun Sun (TooChuang), Sichen Wang (WenSight AI Lab)

entry.summary: WenSight-Decision-1 is a shared model that scores candidate options directly against natural-language e-commerce rules and case evidence across six operational tasks in six languages, fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-9B (an existing model released earlier in 2026) with reference options as supervision. On 1,440 held-out synthetic cases, accuracy rises from 61.60% to 92.92% under identical inputs and scoring.

entry.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting

author.name: Sanghyun Lee, Wonjin Nam, Seungho Jang, Jaeho Lee, Jiho Park, Jaewoon Lee, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: ReAnchor is a training-free method that reuses hidden states computed during target verification beyond the first rejection point to reanchor a block diffusion drafter, generating parallel draft blocks that extend beyond the original block endpoint. It improves speculative decoding speedups, with the largest gains at temperature zero.

entry.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics

author.name: Yupei Lin, Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Guoming Ling, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Yukai Shi, Liang Lin

entry.summary: HoloCosm addresses benchmark compression when evaluation spans multiple metrics, showing that sample subsets selected for one metric fail to preserve rankings on others, often performing worse than random sampling at 80% compression. The proposed method jointly minimizes normalized scores across metrics to produce more faithful compressed evaluations.

entry.title: Latent Multimodal Memory Reasoning

author.name: Cai Ke, Xinghao Chen, Yuanchen Bei, Yuni Lai, Keyu Chen, Ruizhi Qiao, Siyu An, Junnan Dong, Ruifeng Xu, Xing Sun

entry.summary: LMMR is a neuro-symbolic framework for long-term personalized agents that organizes multimodal memory in a continuous latent space rather than prematurely compressing visual evidence into text, unifying cross-modal and cross-session evidence. It addresses stale observations and the computational cost of fine-grained visual grounding over entangled raw memories.

entry.title: LogicVal:A Logic-Formalized Benchmark for Constraint Satisfaction in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Savitha Sam Abraham, Marjan Alirezaie, Hossein Rahnama

entry.summary: LogicVal recasts text-to-image evaluation as a constraint-satisfaction problem, with a logical framework formally specifying objects, attributes, relations, and constraints that generated images must satisfy. Four state-of-the-art T2I models are evaluated across nine classes of constraints from single-object attributes to multi-object relations. This gives a more rigorous, compositional yardstick than existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Dual Task Vector Merging: Leveraging Emotion and ASR Knowledge for Low-Resource Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Yuan-Chao Li, Yin-Long Liu, Liu He, Sizhe Liu, Ji-Xuan Deng, Yin Zhang, Zhen-Hua Ling, Jiahong Yuan

entry.summary: This paper introduces Dual Task Vector Merging, a parameter-efficient approach for detecting Alzheimer's disease from speech when training data is scarce. The method injects weight-delta task vectors from emotion- and ASR-fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 models into a frozen backbone, training only merging coefficients and a linear head to avoid overfitting while exploiting transferable paralinguistic and linguistic knowledge.

entry.title: Stable Signer V3: 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting Is All You Need for Sign Language Production

author.name: Sen Fang, Liwei Che, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Stable Signer V3 is a high-resolution sign language avatar system built on 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting, adding shared face primitives for expression, test-time body primitives for identity-specific muscle-like deformation, and TunnelingNet super-resolution for fine details. Test-time modules are optimized once per signer identity, after which inference runs from stored parameters. It targets fidelity limits of prior sign-language avatars.

entry.title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: Enhancing LLM Agents for Automated Fact-Checking with Human Expert Skills

author.name: Xinwen Chen, Haorui He, Yupeng Li

entry.summary: SkillCheck distills AFP Fact Check guidelines into a modular Professional Fact-Checking Skill that LLM agents can dynamically access at inference time, guiding evidence retrieval and claim verification without costly post-training. Experiments show improvements in automated fact-checking performance. It offers a cheap, scalable route to injecting professional expertise into agents.

entry.title: Beckmann World Models: Direct Terminal-Map Learning for One-Step Action-Conditioned Prediction

author.name: Adam Lee, Shobhit Agarwal, June Pyo Suh

entry.summary: This paper adapts the terminal-map conservation law from Beckmann Transport Models to action-conditioned video prediction, learning a direct map from noise, visual history, and actions to future frames without a pretrained generative teacher. It trains from noise-data pairs without the conditional generated-sample populations required by DriftWorld, and addresses the gap between transport consistency on interpolated inputs and accurate prediction from pure noise using endpoint-based techniques.

entry.title: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Fuping Wu, Xi Jia, Le Zhang, Jiahua Li, Rima Mustafa, Thomas E. Nichols, Bartlomiej W. Papiez

entry.summary: The paper proposes an auxiliary learning framework for medical image segmentation where auxiliary task labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, avoiding extra expert labeling cost. Formulated as bilevel optimization, the method transfers knowledge between tasks through feature-level optimization. This addresses the high cost of expert annotation in medical imaging.

entry.title: Test-time Adaptation for Point Cloud Denoising under Unseen Noise

author.name: Kun Jiang, Shida Fu, Fanhao Yi, Weiqing Li, Zhiyong Su

entry.summary: TTAD is a test-time adaptation framework that lets pre-trained point cloud denoisers handle unseen noise distributions without retraining or extra supervision. It estimates sample-specific noise via a residual-driven module and adapts the model at inference time.

entry.title: Geometry Regularization for Vanilla NeRF via Self-Supervised Cross-Ray Consistency

author.name: Zongji Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses noisy geometry in vanilla NeRF by adding a self-supervised geometry-optimization branch based on cross-ray consistency. It samples candidate surface points, casts virtual rays from multiple directions, and constrains the density field via visibility-weighted color consistency. This reduces shape-radiance ambiguity without extra supervision.

entry.title: AdaptMIL: Domain Adaptation for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology

author.name: Ben Vardi, Dana Schonberger, Yuval Friedmann, Zohar Yakhini, Iris Barshack, Alexander Loebel, Ariel Shamir

entry.summary: AdaptMIL integrates domain adaptation into multiple instance learning for whole-slide pathology, addressing cross-hospital distribution shift that degrades pathology foundation model task heads. Notably, it finds naive application of DA objectives during MIL training interferes with aggregation learning, and resolves this with a modified training strategy. A practical contribution for clinical deployment robustness.

entry.title: A Process-Informed, Photorealistic Digital Twin for Vision-Based Inline Inspection of C-SMC Strip Deposition

author.name: Patrick Flore, Fabian R\"oder, Kevin Chen, Andreas Gebhard

entry.summary: This paper builds a physically grounded digital twin for carbon-fiber sheet molding compound manufacturing that generates photorealistic, exactly labeled training images for inline quality inspection. It combines rigid-body deposition simulation with polarization rendering to produce synchronized labels across bounding boxes, point annotations, density maps, and polarization channels, addressing the scarcity of labeled industrial image data.

entry.title: CPVB-RG: Cross-Prior Visual Bridging for Prior-Aware Chest X-Ray Report Generation

author.name: Sike Xiang, Shuang Chen, Julie Cox, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei

entry.summary: CPVB-RG incorporates longitudinal comparison into chest X-ray report generation by contrasting current and prior radiographs with clinical text, using progression-guided focus attention to distinguish interval changes from stable anatomy. This mirrors how radiologists actually read follow-up studies, an underexplored axis in report generation.

entry.title: CLOSER: Evidence-Aware Active Visual Verification for Embodied Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Pengying Wu, Mingye Jiang, Yunze Hu, Zhejia Wen, Kangjie Zhou, Zongru Yang, Zhe Peng, Chang Liu

entry.summary: CLOSER treats the stopping decision in object-goal navigation as closed-loop evidence acquisition, combining VLM-based verification with active perception so agents resolve detector false positives (e.g., mistaking a sofa for a bed) before stopping. The system explicitly maneuvers to reduce occlusion and partial observation of candidates.

entry.title: Copyright Leakage Detection in AI Generated Videos

author.name: Shaif Chowdhury, Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy

entry.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark for detecting copyright leakage in AI-generated videos, covering 50 copyrighted concepts with paired image+prompt and prompt-only generated videos, and proposes a contrastive retrieval framework that formulates detection as video-to-image retrieval. This targets a largely unexplored legal and safety concern around video generation models.

entry.title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli

author.name: Manar Ali, Lisa Gottschalk, Simeon Junker, Lisa Hudalla, Alon Fishman, Joana Cholin, Stefan Kopp, Hendrik Buschmeier, Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: This paper compares how humans and state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs describe abstract visual stimuli that are progressively harder to map to familiar concepts, using two controlled datasets (SilCC with increasingly complex shape combinations and PixCC with increasing visual noise). It scores responses on originality and effectiveness, finding that humans remain more productive at associative description as naming difficulty rises. The work matters because it offers a systematic benchmark for a creative-cognitive gap in multimodal models rather than a vague notion of machine creativity.

entry.title: Design and Control of a Multimodal Legged-Aerial Robot Through Separate Control Contraction Metrics

author.name: Kaushik Venkatesh Krishnamurthy, Eric Sihite, Alireza Ramezani, Morteza Gharib

entry.summary: The paper presents the design and unified control of a quadrupedal aerial-legged robot capable of thruster-assisted locomotion, using separately computed domain-specific Control Contraction Metrics for walking and flight fused online through an energy-based CLF-QP for cross-domain control allocation. This formal contraction-metrics approach to hybrid legged-aerial control is more principled than typical heuristic mode-switching. It is a solid hardware-plus-theory contribution in an active robotics area.

entry.title: Sensitivity-Orthogonal Residual Learning for Adaptive Sideslip and Cornering Stiffness Estimation

author.name: Kyoungtae Ji, Dongyeol Won, Kyoungseok Han

entry.summary: This paper addresses a conflict in vehicle state estimation where a learned neural corrector can absorb the filter innovation signal that should drive online adaptation of tire cornering stiffness, suppressing the adaptation. The authors construct a residual corrector constrained to be orthogonal to the stiffness sensitivities, using null-space parameterization to enforce this without penalty coefficients. Full-vehicle simulations show the unconstrained corrector degrades stiffness estimation, while the proposed orthogonality-preserving method maintains accurate adaptive estimation.

entry.title: Prescribed Performance Guided Safe Reinforcement Learning for Roundabout Navigation of Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Wenhan Li, Yangrui Zhang, Hang Zhou, Peiran Liu, Yiding Ji

entry.summary: The paper proposes RLTrajGen-PPMPC-CBF, a hierarchical framework for safe roundabout navigation of connected and autonomous vehicles that couples RL-based planning with MPC-based control. Prescribed performance constraints regulate the coupling between pointwise RL decisions and trajectory-level MPC optimization, addressing a structural mismatch in prior frameworks, with control barrier functions providing safety guarantees. The approach targets smooth, comfortable navigation in dense roundabout traffic.

entry.title: SPAR: Search-trained Push Action Ranker for Efficient Navigation Among Movable Obstacles

author.name: Dhruv Metha Ramesh, Tri-An Nguyen, Junshan Huang, Jingjin Yu, Kostas E. Bekris, Abdeslam Boularias

entry.summary: SPAR learns to prioritize push primitives for Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO), trained on outcomes of short physics-based searches that distinguish immediate openings from setup pushes. A transformer with regression and ranking losses scores primitives using contact tokens conditioned on scene geometry and reachability, avoiding exponential search over push sequences.

entry.title: MARE: An Open-Source Lunar Rover Simulator with Shadow Ground Truth for Perception and Autonomy

author.name: Ra\'ul Castilla-Arquillo, Miguel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: MARE is an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2, targeting the extreme low-sun, high-contrast shadow conditions near the lunar poles. It integrates three components and provides sensor data with accurate shadow ground truth, which is costly to obtain from field campaigns.

entry.title: VampPrior Unleashed

author.name: Andrew A. Stirn, Abhejit Rajagopal, David A. Knowles, Grace Huynh

entry.summary: The paper identifies two limitations of the VampPrior for deep latent variable models: tied prior/posterior uncertainty via a single amortized covariance and poor clustering from fixed uniform mixture weights. The authors decouple prior and posterior covariances and replace uniform mixture weights, substantially improving model evidence in applications such as single-cell genomics.

entry.title: Practical Advantages of Online Conformal Prediction for Data Streams

author.name: St\'ephane Chr\'etien, Maryam Hoseini-Behbahani, Guillaume Metzler

entry.summary: The paper empirically compares four sequential conformal regression procedures against a weighted full-conformal benchmark on coverage, interval width, and computational cost across stationary controls, synthetic distribution shifts, and four real data streams. It demonstrates practical advantages of online conformal methods for non-stationary data streams where classical guarantees do not extend.

entry.title: M-Plan: Comprehensive Planning For LLM Agents with Memory Arrangement

author.name: Ziyang Liu, Jiakang Yuan, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen

entry.summary: M-Plan improves LLM-agent performance on long-horizon tasks in unseen environments by arranging and preprocessing long-term memory rather than directly reusing retrieved knowledge, which often contains historical noise. It adapts memory content to the current task to support continuous decision-making.

entry.title: Robust Representation Learning for Spiking Neural Networks based on Conditional Information Bottleneck

author.name: Yuli Zha, Wang Fan, Yixiao Dai, Lingjie Wang, Bang Hu, Wei Cao, Fengzhe Zhang, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that SNNs trained with cross-entropy retain excessive input-specific information, contributing to vulnerability to perturbations, hardware noise, and adversarial attacks. It proposes SCIB, a Conditional Information Bottleneck training objective that improves robustness of spiking networks for low-power neuromorphic deployment.

entry.title: AnchorRM: Parallel Intra-Batch State Reconstruction with Anchor-Based Residual Memory for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Haroon Gharwi, Kai Shu, Yue Dai

entry.summary: AnchorRM fixes a fidelity problem in memory-based temporal graph neural networks, where temporal mini-batching causes later interactions to use stale pre-batch memory. It reconstructs event-specific intra-batch node states in parallel using an anchor-based residual memory rather than sequential recurrent updates. This improves both accuracy and scalability of temporal GNNs.

entry.title: RAG-NIMBF: A Non-Invasive, Modular Benchmarking Framework for Automated RAG Configuration Analysis

author.name: Niclas Hart, Nicolas Weeger

entry.summary: RAG-NIMBF is a modular, non-invasive evaluation layer that attaches to existing RAG pipelines and benchmarks the vast configuration space of chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, prompting, and generation components through controlled ablations. It combines LLM-based quality scores, retrieval correctness measures, and runtime indicators with end-to-end experiment tracking. This addresses a real practitioner need for principled RAG configuration guidance.

entry.title: JAXbounce: A Continuous-Control Pong-Like Benchmark for Active Inference Beyond Low Dimensional Environments

author.name: Chaitanya Kaul, Markus Klar, Sebastian Stein, Fraser C. Paterson, John H. Williamson, Roderick Murray-Smith

entry.summary: JAXbounce is a fully differentiable, JAX-parallelized continuous-control benchmark for active inference, combining continuous states, stochastic dynamics, and composable observation models from state vectors to corrupted pixel grids. The authors run over 10,000 simulations comparing deterministic baselines, UKF-based active inference agents with expected free energy planning, and pixel-based agents.

entry.title: Parameter misspecification in physics-informed neural networks: A closed-form audit and its limits

author.name: David McShannon, Nicholas Dietrich

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form least-squares audit that estimates a possibly misspecified physical coefficient from a trained PINN in one frozen-network evaluation when the residual is linear in the parameter, without retraining or reference data. It quantifies how recovery accuracy relates to a normalized residual via log-log correlation across convection-diffusion configurations.

entry.title: Predicting CVSS and CWE from CVE Descriptions with Fine-Tuned Small Language Models

author.name: Tara Dixit, Jessie Dong, Summer Li

entry.summary: Responding to a 2026 NIST policy change that stops enriching most CVEs with CVSS and CWE labels, this work fine-tunes small language models to predict CVSS v3.1 vector components, base score, severity, and CWE type from vulnerability descriptions alone. Training carefully avoids leakage from near-duplicate descriptions by restricting to 2022-2023 CVEs. The models fill a real operational gap in automated security triage.

entry.title: Uncovering Semantic Hierarchies in Text-Attributed Graphs via Variational EM-based LLM-GNN Synergy

author.name: Yunhui Liu, Xudong Jin, Qizhuo Xie, Chunhui Zhao, Xiao Luo, Tao Zheng, Bin Chong, Tieke He

entry.summary: SHiFT combines LLMs and GNNs in a variational EM framework to learn hierarchical semantic structures in text-attributed graphs. In the E-step, LLMs act as taxonomists to induce an explicit semantic tree with a cost-saving Mapping & Diagnosis strategy for selective updates; in the M-step, the GNN encoder is aligned with the induced hierarchy.

entry.title: Shallow Probes Are Sufficient for Near-Oracle Personalization Depth Allocation in Federated Learning

author.name: Beyazit Bestami Yuksel, Emrah Dikbiyik, Ayse Yilmazer Metin

entry.summary: This paper audits whether small client-specific probe measurements can replace exhaustive depth evaluation for cost-aware personalization decisions in federated learning, defining an offline oracle over six depths. Training-free greedy probing achieves 98.3 percent oracle recovery with tiny regret on CIFAR-10/100 and patient-disjoint PTB-XL across 900 clients. The result supports cheap deployable personalization policies.

entry.title: CD-OPD: Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Yucheng Li, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper identifies a collaboration failure mode in on-policy distillation where teacher takeover produces incorrect answers even when both teacher and student independently solve the problem, quantified via a Collaboration Failure Rate. CD-OPD structures teacher guidance through dependency-graph-based contextual digests and online meta-reweighting against student-only task gradients. This improves the reliability of on-policy knowledge distillation for LLMs.

entry.title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

author.name: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan

entry.summary: The authors build a quantitative RAG benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed from 45,441 measured device records, rather than from text overlap or model-based scoring. They benchmark six retrieval-augmented systems against verified experimental ground truth. This addresses a real evaluation gap for scientific literature assistants that must answer aggregate quantitative questions.

entry.title: Predictive Bandit Curriculum Reinforcement Learning via Gradient-Based Sample Group Discovery

author.name: Liang Xu, Shufan Shen, Zhongni Hou, Chao Bi, Yufei Zhang, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: The proposed PGB Curriculum discovers optimization-aware curriculum units by clustering projected sample-level gradients, then uses a lightweight temporal predictor inside a bandit framework to forecast future sample utility for reinforcement learning training. This anticipates how sample value evolves with the policy, addressing limitations of static property-based curricula. It improves RL training efficiency through smarter data ordering.

entry.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection in Continual Learning

author.name: Nimeshika Udayangani, Flora D. Salim, Christopher Leckie, Sarah Erfani

entry.summary: The paper tackles joint continual learning and OOD detection without rehearsal buffers, proposing a framework inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks whose local neuroplasticity mitigates catastrophic forgetting. It addresses identifying unknown samples without access to past-task in-distribution data, where confidence-based OOD scores degrade. This targets realistic open-world deployment scenarios that most prior OOD-CL methods ignore.

entry.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-Layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction

author.name: Jianglong Liu, Zhicheng Zhu, Jia Hao, Liangyue Jia

entry.summary: CIS-Transolver is a neural operator for automotive aerodynamics that extends fine-scale flow modeling from local information extraction to cross-layer reuse via an incremental-state mechanism, targeting the spectral-bias problem in reconstructing fine flow details near complex geometries. This enables faster, more accurate data-driven CFD prediction. It is a solid architectural advance in the neural operator literature.

entry.title: On Learning Expand-and-Sparsify Representations

author.name: Alireza Asghari, Parikshit Ram, Kaushik Sinha

entry.summary: This paper investigates what is gained by learning expand-and-sparsify lifting maps via gradient descent instead of using random constructions, which previously required exponentially large expansion dimensions. Using a controlled protocol across 73 OpenML classification and 48 regression tasks with Wilcoxon statistics, it quantifies how the learned map's benefit depends on expansion width. This provides a useful empirical-theory bridge for random-feature and sparse-representation methods.

entry.title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: D. Sorokin, A. Granovskiy, M. Stokolesov, E. Adishchev, M. Nurgaliev, G. Subbotin

entry.summary: The paper uses a Fourier Neural Operator surrogate of a 1D particle transport solver as a differentiable forward model to reconstruct unobserved tokamak core electron density profiles in real time, with uncertainty quantification from reflectometry and interferometry data. Four UQ methods (ensembles, Laplace approximation, Metropolis-Hastings, Gaussian approaches) are compared. This supports real-time plasma control in fusion-relevant devices.

entry.title: Conditional Weight of Evidence for Gradient-Boosted Credit Models: Estimation, Additivity and Its Relation to Adverse Action Reasons

author.name: Agus Sudjianto, Denis Burakov

entry.summary: The paper introduces conditional weight of evidence for credit risk models, measuring how a characteristic changes an individual applicant's default log odds given all other known information, enabling applicant-specific explanations for gradient-boosted models. The authors derive estimators, additivity properties, and connections to adverse action reason codes required in lending. This bridges machine learning models with regulatory explainability requirements.

entry.title: Decision-Target Reversal under Informative Label Missingness

author.name: Farinborz Setoudehtazangi, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: The paper identifies decision-target reversal: a phenomenon where informative label missingness helps classification under one loss function but hurts under another, with the underlying data distribution held fixed. The authors derive cost-sensitive excess-risk expansions for binary Gaussian discrimination and characterize critical cost ratios where risk orderings flip.

entry.title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing

author.name: Jiayan Yang, Ad Feelders, Arno Siebes

entry.summary: The paper bridges the gap between clinical risk prediction models and real operational decisions by proposing an uncertainty-aware anticipatory staffing framework for ICUs that translates probabilistic deterioration risk into staff planning under constraints like shift rigidity and hiring delays. It explicitly moves evaluation beyond discrimination metrics toward downstream decision quality.

entry.title: SAR: Learning Global Item-Space Matching and Geometry-Aware Placement Ranking for Buffered Online 3D Bin Packing

author.name: Xinpeng Lei, Jin Zhang, Yizhe Yang, Yihong Duan, Fucheng Wan

entry.summary: SAR is a learning-based framework for online 3D bin packing with a bounded buffer that separates spatial reasoning between a picker performing global item-space matching against residual container occupancy and a geometry-aware ranker for placement. A voxel-token encoder represents 3D occupancy, enabling placement decisions that preserve future packing opportunities rather than merely ensuring feasibility.

entry.title: NIOCIS: Typed-Decision Next-Hop Routing with Node-Conditioned Option Spaces for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Jin Han, Mingfeng Xin, Feng Liang, Jingtao Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight routing layer that compiles tool-use agent execution logs into a loop-collapsed action graph, letting a small model select the next typed action from calibrated distributions in about 10 ms without generating text. Evaluated on 1,615 production security-operations episodes, where the typed encoder matches logged next hops on roughly a third of held-out decisions.

entry.title: R2-GP: Variance-Calibrated Priors for Additive Gaussian Processes

author.name: Javier Enrique Aguilar, Soham Mukherjee, David Kohns

entry.summary: R2-GP introduces an R2D2-type prior for Gaussian process additive models that directly calibrates each component's explained variance (R-squared) for Matern kernels. Because Matern function variance couples amplitude and length-scale, independent amplitude priors overestimate variance, especially in high dimensions. The method rescales components by length-scale and observed inputs to control prior variance contributions.

entry.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context

author.name: Hui Wang, Bohao Chu, Qianli Wang, Shuning Zhang, Norbert Fuhr

entry.summary: MisleadQA is a diagnostic dataset of multiple-choice questions with abstention options that contrasts factually true but out-of-scope context against false but in-scope context to measure how each misleads LLMs answering from provided context. The study asks whether true-but-irrelevant context misleads as much as false context and whether adding gold context mitigates this. This refines the taxonomy of context-reliance failures beyond the usual false-context focus.

entry.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning

author.name: Zixuan Qin, Qi Qin, Erbo Li, Ting Wei, Yifan Sun, Zhaoxin Fan

entry.summary: Hidden Cartographer is a two-stage framework using model hidden states to guide expert annotation budgets and exact training dynamics to select final instruction-tuning subsets under strict budgets. Progressive candidate expansion avoids pseudo-label distortion that affects label-dependent selection methods.

entry.title: RESIN: Multi-Chain Reasoning with Entity-Structured Indexing

author.name: Xuanyu Meng, Jash Rajesh Parekh, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: RESIN tackles multi-chain reasoning by decomposing questions into one-hop needs, retrieving source-grounded evidence units per hop via entity-structured indexing, and maintaining a compact reasoning buffer, keeping the original sources as the basis for reasoning. This avoids both the noise of flat retrieval and the information loss of early single-path selection.

entry.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum

author.name: Zhongxin Chen, Songhao Wu, Heng Cui, Cong Li, Xiao Zhou, Rui Yan

entry.summary: SpecMRL improves Matryoshka Representation Learning by reorganizing the feature space into a parameter-derived spectral basis ordered by feature importance, so prefix readout occurs in a learned spectral space. On MTEB it outperforms standard MRL at all reduced dimensions, with larger gains under aggressive compression.

entry.title: SciFigBench: A Benchmark for Scientific Method Figure Understanding

author.name: Lijia Wu, Zheng Li, Yuxuan Liu, Jingwen Zhang, Penghai Zhao, Xiang Li

entry.summary: SciFigBench evaluates how well VLMs understand dense scientific method figures, targeting three capabilities: dense content perception, visual relations, and inter-module reasoning within complex methodological diagrams. Existing benchmarks mostly cover coarse-grained retrieval or holistic comprehension. This fills a gap relevant to AI-assisted scientific literature understanding.

entry.title: PRIMFLOW: Learning Trajectory Primitives for Few-Step Distillation

author.name: Hongyi Fang, Benjia Zhou

entry.summary: PRIMFLOW learns a continuous trajectory primitive representing cumulative displacement along a diffusion teacher's sampling trajectory, supervising finite differences with local teacher velocities to enable few-step distillation. This avoids prescribing a temporal basis or fixed query grid, relaxing constraints in prior distillation parameterizations. The goal is accurate few-step generation from dense local supervision.

entry.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?

author.name: Xingsong Ye, Yongkun Du, Jiaxin Zhang, Chong Sun, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: This work challenges the reliance on synthetic paired data in scene text editing by constructing self-paired supervision from real images via controlled disruptions such as cropping, shuffling, and masking. The result avoids artifacts and hallucinations common to synthetic-pipeline training.

entry.title: HistoLoop: Iterative Contextual Inference with a Looped Transformer for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction

author.name: Ziang Liu, Jie Liu, Shuai Li, Yigui Feng, Qinglin Wang

entry.summary: HistoLoop formulates spatial gene expression prediction from H&E histology images as iterative contextual inference using a looped transformer with memory-mediated spot-state updates. At each refinement step it aggregates spot states into multi-resolution context tokens and retrieves spot-specific information via cross-attention.

entry.title: SenseAlign: Understanding Vision and Touch through Language at Test Time

author.name: Chuyang Ye, Qinting Jiang, Jingyan Jiang

entry.summary: SenseAlign is a test-time adaptation method for tactile-visual-language models that detects which modality is reliable under distribution shift (lighting changes, contact quality, sensor hardware) by comparing accumulated observations against text embeddings of candidate classes. It refines features during deployment without requiring labeled data.

entry.title: KoalaGS: Complexity-Aware Continuous Level of Detail for Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Radu Beche, Raoul de Charette

entry.summary: KoalaGS introduces continuous level-of-detail control for 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, using an image-complexity prior computed before optimization to predict where reconstruction error concentrates and to bias Gaussian allocation during training. This lets one primitive set remain effective under shrinking render budgets, with the study showing oversallocation in simple regions hurts low-budget rendering.

entry.title: Real-Time Disturbance-Aware Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors in Spatially Varying Winds

author.name: Stella Kombo, Masih Haseli, Alejandro A. Stefan-Zavala, Peter I. Renn, Morteza Gharib, Joel W. Burdick

entry.summary: The DA-KCF framework preserves an offline-identified nominal Koopman model for quadrotor MPC while a lightweight residual ensemble learns only a low-dimensional disturbance correction online from causal state-command-state transitions, enabling flight in spatially varying winds. The disturbance-aware model is embedded in MPC with corrections evaluated along the prediction horizon. This is a well-structured combination of Koopman operator theory, learning, and MPC for a practical aerial robotics problem.

entry.title: How I discovered an Exoplanet & the science apocalypse

author.name: jonathanbreitg

entry.summary: The author describes using agentic LLM tooling, primarily Claude Opus 5.5, to identify exoplanet candidates in TESS survey data, walking through the technical process. The second half reflects on the implications of increasingly capable agentic systems for the near future of scientific practice and the structure of scientific institutions.

entry.title: Teaching AI Agent to Play Poker Strategically Through Preference Optimization

author.name: Phurinat Polasa, Thanapon Thanadunpremdet, Phatthanasak Kraiduang, Saksorn Ruangtanusak

entry.summary: The authors propose SPOKE, a strategic preference optimization method with teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, to train a compact 4B-parameter poker agent under hidden information. They compare it against SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO baselines across exact-game and six-player settings.

entry.title: Measuring Consensus in AI Agent Networks

author.name: Jin Gao

entry.summary: The paper presents an evaluation framework treating consensus formation in connected AI agent networks as the evolution of publicly stated positions toward a shared region, using accumulated communication history as context. It tracks position trajectories, group dispersion, and information content of messages, validated through case studies on staffing decisions with distributed and duplicate facts. Results from 1,872 runs associate specific communication patterns with consensus outcomes.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Reusability of LLM Pipelines: Financial Extraction, Multilingual Reasoning, and Semantic Screening

author.name: Joong Ho (Joshua), Choi, Sherine George, Jiayang Zhao, Jayesh Rathi, Ashwin Kandath, Ananya Sane, Vishvak Srinivasan

entry.summary: An empirical study testing whether LLM pipelines validated in English can be reused across languages, evaluating accuracy, reasoning-effort transfer, and behavioral stability across cheque extraction, multilingual QA (Mintaka, nine languages), and a FinanceBench pilot over SEC 10-K filings in four languages. It finds accuracy reusability is bounded in key ways.

entry.title: AnomalyJev: Towards Evaluating Image Anomaly Explanations via Claim-Level Verification

author.name: Qizhou Wang, Jiawen Zhu, Guansong Pang, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: AnomalyJev evaluates textual anomaly explanations from multimodal LLMs by extracting verifiable claims and checking them against ground-truth annotations, avoiding costly LLM-judge token generation. This grounds explanation evaluation in available truth rather than subjective rubrics. It improves scalability and reliability of evaluating explainable anomaly detection.

entry.title: Learning Inter-Graph Interactions Between Heterogeneous Substructures of Chemical Systems

author.name: Gyoung S. Na

entry.summary: The paper proposes a data descriptor and graph neural network for modeling interactions between heterogeneous substructures, specifically organic and inorganic components within complex chemical systems such as hybrid solar cell materials. Prior graph methods assumed homogeneous graph-level interactions. This extends graph representation learning to practically important mixed organic-inorganic materials.

entry.title: Radar-Based 3D Human Pose Estimation via Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement

author.name: Woo-Jin Jung, Chan-Bin Lim, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: I2R-Pose is a two-stage framework for privacy-preserving 3D human pose estimation from millimeter-wave radar, combining motion-aware pose initialization with observation-guided refinement to handle insufficient or overlapping body-part reflections. It targets smart-home monitoring where lighting robustness and non-image capture matter. The refinement stage addresses a known core limitation of radar-based perception.

entry.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Jiapu Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes co-aligning retrieval and parameter adaptation for LLM reasoning over temporal knowledge graphs, addressing retrieval methods that ignore temporal validity and event order and PEFT methods with fixed, input-agnostic low-rank updates. The approach seeks temporally coherent evidence and time-aware parameter updates to improve temporal reasoning.

entry.title: Gated Prototype Transfer for Zero-Support Medical Vision Language Model

author.name: Sumaiya Fazal, Rizwan Qureshi, Laleh Behjat, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: GProtoT is a training-free module that transfers visual residual information from supported classes to missing (zero-support) classes in medical vision-language few-shot adaptation, combining VLM similarity with ontology-based clinical distance and a validation-free evidence gate to limit unsupported extrapolation. Evaluated in paired one-shot trials on MESSIDOR, it improves on purely textual prototypes for low-prevalence classes. This targets a realistic clinical constraint where rare classes lack labeled examples.

entry.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk

author.name: Qianli Ma, Limengxi Yue, Shuyang Xu, Yanpei Shi, Hongrui Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constrained agentic RL model for web agents that unifies page accesses, search requests, and API calls into a long-term decision framework with multidimensional costs, jointly optimizing success rate with budget constraints and tail-risk control. It addresses unrealistic behaviors like high success with high cost or conservative failure under risk.

entry.title: Hidden Trajectories Don't Lie: Correcting Corruption Drift for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Amirhossein Sabour, Amir Khasahmadi, Mengliu Zhao

entry.summary: Drift-TTA adapts pretrained models at test time by exploiting hidden trajectories, the ordered sequence of intermediate representations across network layers, which are shown to become more separable between clean and corrupted inputs as severity increases. Zero-initialized low-rank adapters on a frozen backbone are trained to align corrupted trajectories with cleaner ones, in source-dependent and source-free variants. It offers a new signal for test-time adaptation beyond output logits.

entry.title: Contrastive Adversarial Training for Robust Graph Neural Networks under Label Poisoning

author.name: Manshika Charvi Bissessur, Melis Ilayda Bal, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: CoLAT is a contrastive adversarial training framework defending GNN node classification against label poisoning, where a few corrupted training labels propagate errors via message passing. Its structure-aware detection model uses contrastive label-flipping to distinguish adversarial poisoning from naturally hard examples, unlike prior defenses built for label noise.

entry.title: Label-Space Mismatch Distorts Cross-Cohort Evaluation in Breast Cancer Molecular Subtyping

author.name: Suxing Liu, Byungwon Min, Zhijian Zheng, Jiahao Wang

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that cross-cohort evaluation of breast cancer subtype classifiers is distorted when annotation standards differ (METABRIC six-class versus PAM50 five-class), showing that label-space restriction alone accounts for the dominant accuracy correction on TCGA-BRCA and GSE21653. It disentangles evaluation-rule effects from genuine calibration gains such as EM prior correction.

entry.title: FHKAN: Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Arsha Farnoush, Amirhossein Sadr, Aida Pakniyat, Dara Rahmati, Saeid Gorgin, Kourosh Parand

entry.summary: FHKAN equips Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with a trainable fractional-order generalized Hermite basis that is orthonormal on the entire real line, removing the need for saturating squashing of pre-activations required by bounded-interval Chebyshev bases. The paper derives closed-form derivatives supporting data-driven and physics-informed learning. It advances the KAN architecture family with better spectral foundations.

entry.title: DROD: Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout for Federated Continual Learning on Heterogeneous Devices

author.name: Berk Sezer, \"Ozg\"ur Soysal

entry.summary: DROD extends FjORD's Ordered Dropout with two independent reduction axes (shortcut ratio and branch ratio) to extract sub-models, targeting the underexplored intersection of capacity-heterogeneous federated learning and continual learning on drifting data streams. Trained from scratch on Split-CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18 fleets, it achieves the highest mean accuracy on a shared parameter/FLOP budget ladder among compared strategies. It addresses a practical deployment gap.

entry.title: Paloma: Phase-Conditioned Residual Modulation for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jingru Fei, Wei Fan, Kun Yi, Qi Zhang, Zhendong Niu

entry.summary: Paloma shows that residuals remaining after removing periodic components from time series exhibit structured, phase-dependent deviations rather than being unstructured noise, supported by empirical and theoretical analysis. It proposes a phase-conditioned residual modulation module inspired by classical signal processing. This offers a simple, general improvement for periodic time series forecasting models.

entry.title: FracTS: Hierarchical and Autoregressive Time Series Generation

author.name: Jiayu Li, Umair Afzal, Zilong Zhao, Milad Abdollahzadeh, Uzair Javaid, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: FracTS adapts fractal generative modeling from images to multivariate time series via a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine autoregressive model that captures global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales. It targets known weaknesses of flat autoregressive generators: low diversity, error accumulation, and poor long-range modeling. Relevant to privacy-preserving data sharing and augmentation.

entry.title: How Much Does One Wrong Answer Cost? Error Propagation in Constraint Pruning with Noisy LLM Oracles

author.name: Zhengtao Gui (University of California, Irvine), Weining Shen (University of California, Irvine)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how errors from noisy LLM oracles propagate through constraint pruning systems, such as entity resolution and LLM-based ranking, where one accepted wrong answer corrupts every question it implies. It derives first-order risk results showing, for example, that implication-rule pruning in random order adds no first-order risk. The work provides a principled risk framework for judging pruning under oracle errors.

entry.title: A Simple and General Approach to top-$k$ Selection

author.name: Motti Goldberger, Nils Rudi

entry.summary: The paper studies Bayesian top-k identification under a fixed adaptive sampling budget, proposing a batch allocation rule that minimizes a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on expected opportunity cost. The method is general across arbitrary k, batch sampling, and many sampling distributions, with theoretical and empirical support. This connects to best-arm identification and adaptive experimentation.

entry.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Yuheng Ma, Chendi Wang, Qiong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates inference-time collaboration in decentralized federated learning as budgeted local expert referral: a query moves only between neighboring clients, and only visited clients contribute to the prediction, exploiting complementary client expertise without global coordination. EdgeDRM learns a density-based routing potential per client, using potential differences between neighbors to select successive referrals. This is a novel angle on federated systems, improving predictions at inference time rather than through model averaging.

entry.title: Censored Flow Matching for Synthetic Time-to-Event Generation

author.name: Jianbin Tan, Xingran Chen, Kevin He, Zhenke Wu, Bhramar Mukherjee, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes censored flow matching (CFM), a flow-based generative method for synthesizing time-to-event data that handles censoring without survival likelihoods, exploiting monotonicity of differential flows via pullback sampling in an alternating procedure. This enables flexible generation and density learning for survival data that standard generative models struggle with.

entry.title: Prototype-Guided Optimization of Quantum Data Embeddings with Linear Cost

author.name: Seokhoon Jeong, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes a prototype-guided framework for data-adaptive quantum embeddings that replaces O(B^2) pairwise fidelity evaluations with an O(B) objective based on class-prototype separation and compactness, with a measurable lower certificate for class distinguishability. This removes a key computational bottleneck in quantum machine learning embedding optimization.

entry.title: Knowledge Manifold Optimization for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Shigeru Obayashi, Yoshiaki Kawagoe, Kazuhiko Komatsu, Tomonaga Okabe

entry.summary: KMO treats scientific discovery as multiobjective search over a continuous literature-derived knowledge space, evaluating candidates via boundary strength, white-space novelty, semantic-gradient magnitude, and evidential support to identify Pareto-optimal Supported Knowledge Gaps. It aims to point researchers to where new, supportable knowledge may emerge as literature grows.

entry.title: GLOSS-MT: Controllable Low-Resource Machine Translation with an Editable Dictionary

author.name: Mich-Seth Owusu, Stephen E. Moore, Akwasi Asare, Lawrence Adu Gyamfi, Paul Azunre, Joel Budu, Jonathan Asiamah

entry.summary: GLOSS-MT enables terminology control in machine translation for low-resource languages by looking up source noun phrases in an offline English-Twi dictionary, replacing them in place with Twi translations, and fine-tuning once on these mixed inputs. Applied to NLLB-200 at three scales, OPUS-MT, and TranslateGemma 4B, every fine-tuned model beats its pretrained baseline on a document-level English-to-Asante Twi benchmark. The approach reduces the costly fine-tuning cycle typically needed for terminology adaptation.

entry.title: DiaLong: Benchmarking Reminiscence in Long-Context Dialogues

author.name: Owen Bianchi, Samer Aslan, Ryunosuke Saito

entry.summary: Presents DiaLong, a benchmark of 100 human-created, LLM-augmented long-context dialogues with a fact-recall task where models classify 40 candidate facts about a conversation as true or false. It standardizes quantitative evaluation of how LLMs retain and retrieve long-range dialogue information.

entry.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction

author.name: Murat Guney Kemal, Robert Lieck

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively combines tokens to test whether meaningful hierarchical structure, evaluated via unsupervised grammar induction, can emerge from compression alone. This connects representation learning and structured linguistics without explicit structural supervision.

entry.title: Rate as a Feature, Not a Nuisance: Curriculum FiLM Training for Event-Based Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Kavyansh Tyagi, Andreas Ziegler

entry.summary: This paper argues that event-camera data rate, typically normalized away or treated as a nuisance, is informative signal. The authors show rate normalization costs about 6 percentage points of accuracy on N-Caltech101 and propose curriculum FiLM conditioning so graph neural networks exploit variable event rate instead of being invariant to it. This reframes a standard preprocessing choice in event-based vision.

entry.title: Provisioning Robust and Efficient LiDAR Perception for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tingxu Han, Zijie Shen, An Guo, Lyuke Wang, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen, Wei Song

entry.summary: This work formulates LiDAR perception provisioning as jointly satisfying robustness to point-cloud corruption and constraints on latency and GPU memory. It trains candidate detectors on corruption samples mimicking extreme weather and selects configurations meeting both robustness and resource budgets.

entry.title: From Proper Scoring Rules and Edge Biases to Mumford-Shah Models: Robust Unsupervised Hyperspectral Image Segmentation

author.name: Fabian Conrad, Benjamin Berkels

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives an unsupervised hyperspectral segmentation framework from strictly proper scoring rules and parametric probability families, connecting them to the piecewise-constant Mumford-Shah functional. The feature-agnostic method targets spectral variability, mixed pixels, and band correlation without labeled data. An elegant theory-driven contribution.

entry.title: Unified RAW Image Exposure Correction and Restoration via Linear Illumination and Frequency-Adaptive Enhancement

author.name: Yingkai Zhang, Yunhao Zou, Ying Fu

entry.summary: This paper proposes RIECR, a unified framework in the RAW domain that jointly corrects exposure and restores degradations for both under- and over-exposed images. It decomposes the problem following the RAW imaging model into linear illumination correction and residual degradation restoration with frequency-adaptive enhancement, unifying previously separate single-degradation methods.

entry.title: Neural Implicit Energy Optimization for LiDAR Mapping

author.name: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Md Ashiqur Rahman, Chi Lin, Damon Conover, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: The authors formulate large-scale LiDAR mapping as optimization of classical surface energy functionals over the parameter space of neural implicit SDF representations, regularizing the field through the curvature (shape operator) of its level set to suppress jitter and artifacts from sparse, noisy inputs. This bridges classical geometric processing and neural implicit mapping.
