author.name: Egor Zverev, Juhee Kim, Leon Trampert, Boris K\"opf, Aashish Kolluri, Shruti Tople, Santiago Zanella-B\'eguelin

entry.summary: SPIDES proposes enforcing information-flow control on LLM browser agents by gating primitive actions like typing, clicking, and navigating based on data provenance, arguing that restoring the Same-Origin Policy is neither sufficient nor necessary for agent security. The framework addresses prompt injection and data exfiltration by tracking flows rather than origin boundaries. Given industry authorship including Boris Koepf and Santiago Zanella-Beguelin, this is a substantive contribution to agent security architecture.

entry.title: Write Once, Check Many: Reusable Ledgers for Post-Hoc Policy Compliance Auditing of Agent Trajectories

author.name: Ashwin Nagarajan, Gursimran Panesar, Alicia Yang, Mona T. Diab, Virginia Smith, Aashiq Muhamed

entry.summary: Proposes a write once, check many framework for auditing LLM agents: a writer model converts each agent trajectory into a policy-independent ledger, and a reader model checks any new policy against the ledger alone without re-reading the full trajectory. On 900 trajectories from SHADE-Arena, tau-bench, and tau2-bench, a 12B reader over narrative ledgers matches or exceeds the same model reading full trajectories.

entry.title: Where and Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail When Reasoning over Rapidly Evolving Knowledge

author.name: Tianyi Hu, Bhavyajeet Singh, Niket Tandon, Akhil Arora

entry.summary: The paper introduces TREK, comprising TREKTRACE, a plug-and-play framework that attributes search-augmented LLM failures to specific retrieval and reasoning stages, and TREKBENCH-WILD, a benchmark of real-world questions requiring reasoning over rapidly changing information. A key finding is that the main bottleneck is post-retrieval reasoning rather than retrieval itself.

entry.title: Cross-Pollination Retrieval: Finding Transferable Ideas Across Fields in Scientific Literature

author.name: Seokwon Jung, Yerang Kim, Yejin Kim, Alexander Rubinstein, Arnas Uselis, Sangwoo Park, Seong Joon Oh, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-pollination retrieval, the task of finding transferable ideas across scientific fields, and releases CPR-Dataset with 1,300 evaluation queries across 26 fields and over 10,000 training pairs mined from cross-topic citations. Existing retrievers perform poorly (best Recall@10 of 0.26) while LLM rerankers reach 0.81, and fine-tuning on the dataset substantially improves transfer retrieval.

entry.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties

author.name: Afonso Baldo, Ant\'onio Farinhas, Marcos Treviso, Ricardo Rei, Nuno M. Guerreiro

entry.summary: Dynalize mitigates reward hacking of preference reward models online during RL policy training: an LLM periodically and asynchronously analyzes rollouts and writes penalties for undesirable behaviors the reward model appears to reward, with a judge applying them to rollouts. Demonstrated in clinical counseling and creative writing, it targets open-ended tasks where quality cannot be verified or captured by rubrics. This extends the useful lifespan of preference models under long optimization.

entry.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning

author.name: Liana Patel, Rishabh Ranjan, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Carlos Guestrin

entry.summary: TokenGate is a small drop-in component enabling end-to-end learnable token pruning for long-context LLM prefill, motivated by how expert readers skim then closely read. To make learning possible despite the non-differentiable top-K operator, the authors introduce token-gated attention, a Mixture-of-Experts-inspired mechanism that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks it delivers fast, memory-efficient prefill while maintaining quality.

entry.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies

author.name: Bowei He, Yankai Chen, Xiaokun Zhang, Changjiang Han, Ye Yuan, Chong Li, Xue Liu

entry.summary: Decomposes agentic RL training data into task, environment, and trajectory axes plus a reward-density control variable, fitting per-axis scaling relations to answer which axis to scale under a fixed synthesis budget. Provides end-to-end analysis and synthesis strategies that pretraining scaling laws never needed. Addresses a timely question as synthetic data pipelines diversify costs across data types.

entry.title: Do Knowledge and Reasoning Oriented Benchmarks Induce Stable Representation Signatures in LLMs?

author.name: Parsa Rahimi, Azim Dehghani Amirabad

entry.summary: This work tests whether knowledge versus reasoning task labels produce reusable internal signatures in five 7B to 31B language models using carefully controlled probing that holds out entire tasks and permutes labels. Raw probes achieve high F1 on MMLU partitions, but prompt text predicts the separations nearly as well, with activation advantage only 0.017-0.070 macro-F1, suggesting benchmark separability need not reflect shared computation.

entry.title: CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation: Replicating and Extending the Necessity Effect Across Eleven Models

author.name: Arav Dhoot, Yixiong Hao, Zephaniah Roe

entry.summary: This paper replicates and extends the necessity effect, where models can follow a hint without revealing it in their chain of thought but must expose sufficiently complex computations in the CoT, across eleven models from six families. It confirms every model follows simple cues above baseline while concealed complex-cue following falls back near baseline for most models, and extends the study with open code and data. This is significant for CoT-monitorability assumptions in AI safety oversight.

entry.title: How Does Muon Work in Private Deep Learning? Scalable Differentially Private Training via Orthogonalization

author.name: Alexander Gaponov, Grigory Malinovsky, Egor Shulgin, Peter Richtarik

entry.summary: The paper proposes DP-Muon, a differentially private variant of the Muon optimizer, analyzing orthogonalized updates through the Linear Minimization Oracle lens. It shows that per-example clipping under DP primarily causes a positive gradient rescaling to which the LMO is blind, leaving only a small directional residual in the update. This yields a scalable DP training method and provides the first theoretical understanding of Muon under differential privacy.

entry.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Annabelle Sujun Tang, Rohan Mahapatra, Christopher Priebe, Hanyang Xu, Manya Ghobadi, Christopher Rossbach, Hadi Esmaeilzadeh

entry.summary: Conjugate Compilation reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem, jointly optimizing draft and target LLMs within their shared execution rather than compiling each in isolation. The key insight is that compilation choices should be guided by measured performance of the resulting co-located shared execution, forming a self-improving loop. This targets better utilization of GPU capacity for LLM serving.

entry.title: Indistinguishable Agents: Training Agent Privacy as Twin-World Indistinguishability

author.name: Jiaming He, Guanyu Hou, Yi Yu, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes training LLM agents for privacy via twin-world indistinguishability: paired training worlds differ only in a private fact, and a frozen distinguisher scores each observer's view by log-likelihood ratio for the true world. Paired GRPO optimizes task success minus this leakage signal, with a proof that the objective bounds every observer's Bayes success probability on every channel. Experiments on shopping and messaging tasks show leakage is removed beyond what disclosure-suppression training achieves.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Last-Iterate Convergence of SGD in the Smooth Interpolation Regime

author.name: Matan Schliserman, Tomer Koren

entry.summary: This paper proves that the last iterate of stochastic gradient descent with constant stepsize achieves near-optimal rates on smooth convex objectives in the interpolation regime where gradient variance at the optimum vanishes. The bound is order 1/T for every valid constant stepsize, matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors and improving the previous best of order 1/sqrt(T). Schliserman and Koren are established researchers in optimization theory.

entry.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading

author.name: Alexandre Bismuth, Kang Li, Aramis Marti-Shahandeh, Valentin Mohl, Jakob Foerster, Anisoara Calinescu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a post-training method for autoregressive foundation models trained on limit order book data for market simulation. It uses a Wasserstein GAN objective with a critic trained online through a non-differentiable matching engine, updating evolution-strategy perturbations of LoRA adapters under a KL trust region. The approach addresses the compounding of sampling errors that cross-entropy pretraining fails to penalize.

entry.title: Logit Averaging During Training Sets a New State of the Art for Non-Invasive Speech BCI

author.name: Miran \"Ozdogan, Gereon Elvers, Michael Bronstein, Oiwi Parker Jones

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares six multi-trial aggregation strategies for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, including three new attention-based variants and logit averaging during training, across three datasets and four tasks. It treats aggregation as an architectural design choice rather than a preprocessing afterthought, and finds logit averaging during training achieves new state-of-the-art results for speech decoding from non-invasive signals.

entry.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs

author.name: Zhuoshi Pan, ZhiYuan Feng, Yukuo Cen, Honglin Lin, Junru Lu, Zhongxia Chen, Shuo Yang, H. Vicky Zhao, Jie Tang

entry.summary: HarnessPro is a label-free method for recursively self-improving AI agent harnesses that optimizes both task performance and execution cost using Pareto-based selection over candidate harnesses evaluated with LLM-generated tests. Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories and plan updates with different performance-cost priorities. It addresses a timely problem as harness/agent scaffolding quality increasingly determines agent capability.

entry.title: Persistent Representational Misalignment Induces Vision-Language Model Failures

author.name: Yonatan Gideoni, Yoav Gelberg, Tim G. J. Rudner, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: This paper investigates why vision-language models fail at tasks simple for humans, hypothesizing the cause is a persisting misalignment between vision and language representations that the Platonic Representation Hypothesis predicts should vanish with scale. The authors show the misalignment is linearly unalignable and inherent to the data, so it persists across scale, and demonstrate it predictably induces generalization failures and correlates with known VLM failure modes.

entry.title: FlashMap: Flow Map Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jeff Shen, Zhejian Zhou, Ryan Lee, Jonathan May, Shirley Ho

entry.summary: Proposes FlashMap, a speculative decoding drafter based on a continuous flow map language model conditioned on the target model's hidden states, generating a whole token block in one forward pass while capturing inter-token dependencies that block-diffusion drafters like DFlash ignore. On Qwen3-8B it outperforms a matched DFlash baseline in speed across evaluation settings.

entry.title: Memories That Outlive Their Reasons: Dependency-Tethered Memory for Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Jinqian Ju, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Yiqun Duan, Zequn Sun, Taotao Cai, Mingkai Zheng

entry.summary: This work shows that agent memory can become a liability when the premises behind stored verdicts are invalidated, demonstrating that agents reading atomic-fact memories publish 62% of objects whose failure lies upstream in long simulated chats. It proposes tethering memory records to the exact versions each verdict derives from, enabling local derivation-aware invalidation at read time.

entry.title: Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs

author.name: Abhinav Khattar (NVIDIA), Aishwarya Chhabra (NVIDIA), Ameya Velingker (NVIDIA), Anusha Kamath (NVIDIA), Brandon Norick (NVIDIA), Kanishk Singla (NVIDIA), Kiran Praveen (NVIDIA), Markus Kliegl (NVIDIA), Mohammad Qazim Bhat (NVIDIA), Mostofa Patwary (NVIDIA), Niket Agarwal (NVIDIA), Rajpreet Thethy (NVIDIA), Ramani Akkati (NVIDIA), Raviraj Joshi (NVIDIA), Sai Nishanth Padala (NVIDIA), Shuoyang Ding (NVIDIA), Sriharsha Niverty (NVIDIA), Utkarsh Vaidya (NVIDIA), Vitaly Lavrukhin (NVIDIA), Yev Meyer (NVIDIA), Anoop Kunchukuttan (AI4Bharat), Mitesh Khapra (AI4Bharat), Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan (AI4Bharat), Rudra Murthy (AI4Bharat), Sumanth Doddapaneni (AI4Bharat), Thanmay Jayakumar (AI4Bharat), Ujjwal Sharma (AI4Bharat)

entry.summary: From NVIDIA and AI4Bharat, releases Nemotron-Pretraining-Indic-v1, an openly released 2.83-trillion-token synthetic pretraining corpus covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages in native script plus twelve romanized forms, produced by a GPU-accelerated translate-assess-repair pipeline with traceability. Continued-pretraining experiments across twelve languages show combining synthetic and natural Indic text improves knowledge and downstream performance.

entry.title: Answering While You Type: Optimizing Time-to-Answer with Streaming Generation

author.name: Nikita Dragunov, Matvey Mikhalchuk, Anton Razzhigaev

entry.summary: Proposes streaming generation, a decoding regime in which the model starts producing a response from a partially typed request and revises it as the remaining input arrives, so only a small residue of the answer is computed after submission. This reframes inference efficiency around user-perceived time-to-answer rather than pure decoding speed.

entry.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms

author.name: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies functional CAD design, where LLM agents must construct and revise mechanisms that satisfy physical functional requirements rather than merely look plausible. FunCAD-Harness translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide revisions, with a new benchmark to systematically evaluate this capability.

entry.title: Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Efficient Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Hoyeon Shin, Jeongyeon Kim, Yeong Jun Koh, Yeoneung Kim, Hanul Kim

entry.summary: The paper formulates visual token compression for OCR-free document retrieval as an Unbalanced Optimal Transport problem, unifying token importance, semantic redundancy, and coverage in a single alternating optimization. The authors prove that minimizing transport cost upper-bounds the MaxSim retrieval error, providing a theoretical guarantee for ranking preservation while improving scalability of multi-vector VLM retrieval.

entry.title: FluidGen: Physics-Aware Fluid Video Generation via Motion-Guided Post-Training

author.name: Yang Zheng, Zizhang Li, Boyang Deng, Jan Ackermann, Lei Shu, Yinghao Xu, Jiajun Wu, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: FluidGen injects a data-driven fluid prior into pre-trained video generation models to fix systematic failures on fluid phenomena like smoke, fire, and debris, which currently lack coherent vortical structure. It uses a dual-stream training scheme mixing high-fidelity Houdini simulations with paired velocity fields and curated in-the-wild fluid video, with a motion-guided post-training objective.

entry.title: SAPO: Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization for Improving Temporal Video Grounding in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Wei Chen, Ke Xu, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a temporal generation gap in video VLMs: attention intervals localize events more precisely than the timestamps the models emit, holding across four VLMs and two datasets. SAPO exploits this with a self-supervised attention policy optimization that improves temporal grounding using only unlabeled video-query pairs, avoiding costly temporal annotations.

entry.title: OmniGround: Strengthening Omni-Modal Temporal Grounding via Attention-Consistency Training

author.name: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Hao Lin, Ke Xu, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a temporal generation gap in omni-modal LLMs: internal attention localizes target moments in video and audio more accurately than the timestamps the model actually emits. TACG is a post-training method that aligns internal attention with predictions and ground truth, plus a new benchmark for omni-modal temporal grounding.

entry.title: Scaling Vision Foundation Models for Toxicologic Pathology

author.name: Jessica Loo, Theodoros Pissas, Byunghak Kang, Vincent A. Ella, Xiaoyan Zhang, Kevin Sweeney, Walter Georgescu, Prateek Katiyar, Julie Boisclair, Holger Hoefling

entry.summary: TOX-FM is a family of pathology foundation models trained on over one million whole slide images spanning 60 organs, six animal species, and 14,000 toxicology studies across six decades, targeting non-clinical toxicologic pathology. The authors introduce an 18-task non-clinical benchmark and evaluate against state-of-the-art clinical pathology foundation models on both domains. This opens an underexplored industrial application area for pathology FMs with strong data scale.

entry.title: Let Them Sleep: Recursive Self-Pruning Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Kargi Chauhan, Sadiba Nusrat Nur, Pratibha Revankar, Kyle Montgomery, Chenguang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes RSPM, a memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents in which the agent periodically clusters recent failures, distills them into short rules, and deletes raw episodes, with rules decaying unless reinforced and recurring rules promoted to general principles. Evaluated across three dissimilar settings including a calibrated SWE-bench variant. It directly addresses memory bloat and repeated-failure pathologies in long-running agents.

entry.title: ACTS: Learning Visuo-Tactile World Models from Human Physical Interaction

author.name: Yuxiang Ma, Weihan Xu, Pengfei Ye, Anna Mei, Yuxin Ray Song, Tingle Li, Haonan Chen, Edward H. Adelson

entry.summary: ACTS is a visuo-tactile world model trained exclusively on human interaction data collected with handheld GelSight sensors, yielding a 4.9-hour bimanual dataset across three objects with third-person video, tactile images, and 6-DoF motion. The work investigates whether contact-rich dynamics can be learned from human demonstrations rather than slow robot teleoperation and transferred to a robot.

entry.title: GOFusion: Real-Time Gaussian-Occupancy Submap Fusion for Fisher-Informed Autonomous Robot Navigation

author.name: Boxin Bu, Simon Boche, Haoming Zhang, Jaehyung Jung, Jiaxin Wei, Hannah Schieber, Daniel Roth, Angela P. Schoellig, Stefan Leutenegger

entry.summary: GOFusion is a real-time visual mapping system anchoring 3D Gaussian primitives to local occupancy maps from visual-inertial SLAM, providing both geometric spatial awareness for planning and high-fidelity appearance for information-driven navigation. It bounds GPU memory by restricting splatting optimization to active submaps and introduces a rasterizer-integrated Fisher approximation quantifying per-primitive sensitivity online. The Fisher information guides information-gain-based navigation.

entry.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering

author.name: Kaichen Zhou, Zhiyan Li, Chongkai Gao, Yuhan Wang, Wenlong Huang, Maggie Wang, Fangneng Zhan, Manling Li, Qianqian Wang, Mac Schwager, Zhuang Liu, Li Fei-Fei, Mengyu Wang, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: SteerAct is a few-shot temporal activation steering framework for pretrained robot action models that modifies feature activations at test time without weight updates. It uses a sparse autoencoder to propose candidate features and a shared temporal descriptor of activation-order dynamics to decide which features to modify, when, and with what strength across a handful of rollouts.

entry.title: EgoRayFormer: Ray-Space Stereo Refinement for Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Songyuan Wu, Jihai Xu, Jie Zhao

entry.summary: This paper introduces EgoRayFormer, a causal 3D human pose estimator for head-mounted stereo fisheye cameras that jointly performs stereo feature sampling and geometric refinement in ray space. For each joint, shared 3D hypotheses are projected into both fisheye views along viewing rays, a geometric branch corrects projections and intersects rays, and a learned gate blends the geometric estimate with a learned pose update. This addresses strong distortion, partial visibility, and short baselines that make egocentric pose estimation difficult, and is relevant for wearable robotics, AR/VR, and human-robot interaction.

entry.title: DexOAK: Object-Aware Kinematic Retargeting

author.name: Federica Spinola, Robert Katzschmann, Cordelia Schmid

entry.summary: DexOAK generates contact-consistent robot hand references from human motion-capture data by minimizing an interaction-graph Laplacian objective over a joint hand-object graph, reproducing object-relative interaction geometry rather than hand pose alone. A feed-forward network conditioned on human keypoints and object point clouds is trained on these seeds and refined with contact, non-penetration, and collision losses.

entry.title: GLM-5.1 Has ~Astra Level CoT Control

author.name: Usman Anwar

entry.summary: The author runs the CoT-Control evaluation suite on GLM, Kimi, and DeepSeek models and finds GLM models, including the existing GLM-5.1, are outliers in chain-of-thought controllability, matching the level of OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra. Crucially, despite high controllability, GLM-5.1 performs poorly at monitor evasion tasks, unlike Astra, which is effective at evading monitors when instructed. This has direct implications for the reliability of CoT-based safety monitoring.

entry.title: Agents' Last Doubt: Knowing When to Act and When to Step Back in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Qisai Liu, Qingyue Jiao, Bangwei Guo, Wenxi Dai, Changyi Yang, Jiahe Liu, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Yiyu Shi, Zhanhong Jiang, Minghao Guo

entry.summary: The paper builds a counterfactual dataset of 3,115 action outcomes from 1,036 decision points in ToolSandbox by executing every legal action and evaluating downstream task completion, interaction cost, and irreversibility. This enables training tool-using agents to better choose among acting, gathering information, and escalating to humans under uncertainty.

entry.title: Comparing Sparsified MLPs and Transcoders: Many Transcoder Features Are Neurons in Disguise

author.name: Stepan Shabalin, Mateusz Piotrowski

entry.summary: This interpretability study defines neuron features as transcoder features strongly aligned with individual MLP neurons and shows they account for a substantial fraction of active features in late layers across 13 open-source transcoders. Only neuron features show stable correspondence with underlying model structures, questioning whether transcoders are necessary for circuit analysis given recent results recovering interpretable circuits directly from MLP neurons. This challenges assumptions in mechanistic interpretability methodology.

entry.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early

author.name: Jiarong Liang, Xueguang Ma, Dongfu Jiang, Yuxuan Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: StopLoss is a small external monitor that learns to recognize doomed coding-agent runs from completed trajectories and verifier outcomes, ending runs early when failure is likely to save compute. Final outcomes label earlier local windows so a fine-tuned model scores recent tool steps in a single forward pass, with a threshold calibrated on successful runs. Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified using GPT-family SWE-rebench trajectories, it aborts failing runs without modifying the executor.

entry.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?

author.name: Xiaoyin Chen, Yizheng Huang, Yinglun Xu, Ziyun Zhao, Emmett McQuinn, Julie Liu, Hope Yao

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether nonparametric self-evolving agents that adapt by rewriting their own prompts, memory, and skills — with frozen weights — are effective continual learners across four drifting task streams built from BIRD, BFCL, and ScienceWorld. It connects the popular self-evolving agent paradigm to the formal continual learning problem of learning new tasks without forgetting old ones.

entry.title: Weighted State Souping for Efficient Long-Context Retrieval

author.name: William L. Tong, Aryo Lotfi, Emmanuel Abbe, Josh Susskind, Cengiz Pehlevan, Eran Malach

entry.summary: Building on state souping, where state space models independently encode cacheable chunks of context that are recombined for downstream queries, the authors propose weighted state souping with learned query-dependent weights for composing cached states. This substantially improves long-context performance on crowded contexts across both synthetic and real settings, addressing a key limitation of SSMs.

entry.title: On Reparameterizing the Score Function

author.name: Mohammad Hossein Amani, Leonardo Bocchieri, Maxime Peyrard, Cl\'ement Hongler, Robert West

entry.summary: History-Reparameterized policy gradients replace the frozen prefix in the score function with a differentiable reparameterized history, allowing gradients of downstream log-probabilities to propagate backward through generated trajectories to alleviate credit-assignment bottlenecks under sparse rewards. Because the resulting term is biased, the authors derive Optimal HR, a centered control-variate estimator with a closed-form coefficient.

entry.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval

author.name: Yam Eitan, Gilad Yehudai, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the expressive power of hybrid sequence-model blocks, where a few full-attention layers with KV caches are combined with many efficient layers using fixed-size states. It studies the theoretical benefits of letting efficient layers access the KV cache via multi-hop retrieval and how far existing approaches realize them. This provides theory to guide the design of efficient long-context architectures.

entry.title: Single-Pass Decision Scores Enable Rapid Classification with Adjustable Thresholds in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Patrick Wienholt, Frederik Hauke, Christiane Kuhl, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn

entry.summary: The paper derives a continuous decision score from a single forward pass of medical MLLMs by renormalizing yes/no token probabilities, enabling threshold adjustment for clinical sensitivity-specificity tradeoffs without retraining. Evaluation with MedGemma and Gemma-3 (4B and 27B) on six medical imaging datasets revealed severe default-threshold misalignment, e.g., MedGemma-27B labeling every chest radiograph as abnormal, while tuned thresholds substantially improved operating points.

entry.title: BrushOff: Stroke-Based Re-rendering as a Watermark Removal Attack on Painting

author.name: Hao Chen, Junnan Xu

entry.summary: BrushOff is a training-free watermark removal attack that redraws a watermarked painting with a pretrained stroke-based renderer, requiring no knowledge of the watermark and no generative diffusion model. It drops detection of VINE, a robust watermark surviving 14 conventional distortions at 97.8%, to 1.8% while preserving image quality, outperforming diffusion regeneration in both removal and quality. This is a significant security result exposing fragility of watermarking for art ownership.

entry.title: LIBERO-Pro2.0: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Xueyang Zhou, Yangming Xu, Qianjiang Li, Guiyao Tie, Junhao Wu, Ziheng Huang, Guowen Zhang, Zhijie Yuan, Di Wu, Duanfeng Chu, Pan Zhou, Lichao Sun, Yongchao Chen

entry.summary: LIBERO-Pro2.0 systematically evaluates robustness of embodied foundation models under distribution shift with 22 static perturbations and 20 runtime interventions across six dimensions, yielding 1,648 validated shifted task instances on top of LIBERO. It also supports robustness-oriented learning, aiming to detect models that exploit benchmark-specific regularities rather than generalizing.

entry.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiaming Liu, Xinghao Zhu, Yiming Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Yinxi Wang, Yichu Yang, Zhuoyang Liu, Dantong Niu, Soha Pouya, Juekun Li, Yan Chang

entry.summary: PhysWord is a reasoning-before-acting foundation model that uses atomic action verbs as shared semantic anchors for continuous latent representations of physical dynamics, predicting upcoming action words and aligning hidden states with latent targets. This hybrid aims to combine the semantic structure of language reasoning with the predictive fidelity of latent dynamics modeling for manipulation.

entry.title: Cache2LoRA: Understanding and Improving Context Internalization

author.name: Yi Fang, Gaurav Srivastava, Zhenyu Bi, Sirui Ding, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses how reliably context-to-LoRA methods preserve facts and follow instructions when documents are encoded as low-rank parameter updates instead of retained context, separating fact discrimination, retention, and response adaptation. It introduces Cache2LoRA, which aggregates evidence from a reusable frozen document cache per query before generating LoRA updates, improving fact recovery at fixed update size.

entry.title: SteerSearch: Interactive Search Reasoning with Mid-Response Steering

author.name: Udit Thakur, Baohao Liao, Matteo Nulli, Stefan Vasilev, Seyyed Hadi Hashemi, Shahram Khadivi, Christof Monz

entry.summary: The paper studies mid-response steering, where users redirect a search-augmented LLM agent during ongoing reasoning or retrieval, and identifies answer-target anchoring as a failure mode where agents retrieve for the new request but still answer the old question. It introduces SteerSearch, an RL framework trained on interactive trajectories with injected interventions, plus the SteerSearch-Bench benchmark adapted from multi-hop QA and a Contrastive Context Reward auxiliary signal.

entry.title: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi-Agent LLMs

author.name: Junru Zhu, Xin Chen, Hang Lyu, Jiayue Meng, Muzi Li, Yifan Chen, Hengyi Huang, Yu Sun, Weiwei Qi

entry.summary: This work models multi-agent LLM systems as three distinct trust boundaries—communication, authorization, and execution—and uses the authority cut to characterize the smallest compromised signer coalition that can forge a policy-valid false-claim proof. Controlled paired hidden-state studies across four models reveal that message rewriting, source-identity cues, and routing configurations produce heterogeneous vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Axiomatic World Modeling for Physics Reasoning

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhenyang Liu, Yuxuan Wang, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode in LLM physics reasoning called modeling drift, where models silently alter given quantities, fabricate laws, or inject unstated assumptions and then reason within the corrupted world. The authors propose Reinforcement Learning with Axiomatic verification to directly supervise world modeling, complementing RLVR and PRM approaches whose rewards do not target this gap. This offers a fresh diagnosis and training signal for scientific reasoning.

entry.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Soyoung Yoon, Peiran Xu, Han Wang, Ruofan Wu, Xiaodong Yu, Feng Yan, Mohit Bansal, Debiao Li, Seung-Won Hwang, Yuxiong He, Zhewei Yao

entry.summary: Introduces HybridResearcher, a 4B-parameter agent trained to reason across both structured sources like databases and unstructured sources like the web, motivated by benchmarks showing frontier agents fail when evidence must cross this boundary. It addresses a real gap in enterprise-style analytical questions that require combining computed results with web evidence.

entry.title: On Reasoning Correctness Directions

author.name: Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Zayd M. K. Zuhri, Rifo Genadi, Abzal Nurgazy, Ali Mekky, Alham Fikri Aji, Zangir Iklassov, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper introduces ChainSearch, a controlled arithmetic reasoning task extending Countdown with explicit search and backtracking, and trains a compact 3-million-parameter model to study whether internal directions encode reasoning correctness. Using linear probes, mean activation differences, and direct optimization, the authors find statistically significant correctness directions exist, but decodability does not guarantee causal usefulness for steering. The result is a caution about conflating probe detectability with causal structure in reasoning models.

entry.title: When Safety Fails Collectively: Robust Alignment Against Harmful Fine-Tuning via Joint Weight Perturbations

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Yuezhi Zhou, Zhu Zhang, Zhixing Tan

entry.summary: The paper identifies a collective failure pattern in harmful fine-tuning: disjoint parts of a harmful weight perturbation have limited individual effects, but their joint application increases harmfulness beyond the sum of individual effects. Guided by this, the authors propose Joint Weight Perturbations (JWP), an alignment-stage defense that masks different weight regions to simulate joint harmful perturbations during safety training. This improves robustness of LLM safety alignment against later harmful fine-tuning attacks.

entry.title: FrontierRefactor: Benchmarking Multi-Scale Performance-Oriented Codebase Refactoring

author.name: Shijian Wang, Fanqing Meng, Jiajun Chen, Qiguang Chen, Linxin Song, Runhao Fu, Shuhang Zheng, Shuai Shao, Qizhe Xie, Jieyu Zhao, Mengkang Hu

entry.summary: FrontierRefactor is a benchmark of 60 qualified engineering tasks for autonomous codebase refactoring, requiring agents to restructure working software while preserving externally observable behavior and improving runtime performance and compute efficiency. It frames refactoring scale via the scope of the observable contract and fills a gap between correctness-only refactoring benchmarks and micro-kernel performance benchmarks.

entry.title: When Should AI Chime In? Benchmarking Timely Contribution of Proactive Agents in Multi-Party Chat

author.name: Ruotong Wang, Brian S. Yu, Xinyi Zhou, Joseph Chee Chang, Pao Siangliulue, Jonathan Bragg, Liwei Jiang, Amy X Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces PITCH, the first benchmark with large-scale human judgments of when a proactive AI agent should contribute in unscripted multi-party chat, using a novel interface where 2-4 participants chat synchronously and author candidate AI contributions. It isolates timing quality from contribution relevance, an underexplored axis of agent usefulness.

entry.title: From Code to Playable Systems: CEGame-Bench for Long-Horizon Game Creation Agents

author.name: Zixuan Dong, Yanghai Wang, Hanyan Bian, Jiaxi Tao, Junze Li, Jiadong Wang, Xinyu Che, Lin Liu, Baoyun Peng, Xiaodong Wang, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: CEGame-Bench is the first long-horizon benchmark for complete-game creation across five production engines (Defold, Godot, Roblox Studio, Unity, Unreal), where agents build games from empty projects under design-document contracts averaging up to 295 steps and 65M tokens, accepted only via real-input play by a hidden evaluator. Current agents earn under half the gameplay points and reach endings in only 16% of games.

entry.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing

author.name: Jinyang Li, Denis Emelin, Simone Tedeschi, Weiwei Cheng, Cristina Morariu, Haytham Assem, Jens Lehmann, Emine Yilmaz, Angus Addlesee

entry.summary: Introduces RouterWorld, a large-scale benchmark for latency-aware LLM routing in conversational systems, unifying 371k single-turn responses and 76k multi-turn agentic trajectories with a standardized LLM-as-a-judge protocol. It treats latency as a first-class metric with hardware-grounded annotations, addressing gaps in existing routing benchmarks that assume full observability of candidate model outcomes.

entry.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats

author.name: Jan Wehner, Jam Kraprayoon

entry.summary: Proposes planting decoy opportunities for harmful actions throughout production environments as an AI control method against insider threats from mistaken, compromised, or misaligned agents. Honeypots can elicit misbehavior under real conditions, provide warnings even if chain-of-thought monitorability degrades, and scale cheaply across agent instances.

entry.title: When the Editing Intent Is Split: A Cross-Modal Jailbreak Attack for Large Image Editing Models

author.name: Xianmin Ye, Zhiyuan Fan, Tianju Liu, Yuhang Wang, Zhenxing Niu, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a split-intent vulnerability in image editing models where harmful intent is distributed across text and visual inputs, proposing SIJA which specifies the referent in text while hiding the safety-critical action in an auxiliary visual cue. It also introduces SI2ESBench, a benchmark for evaluating commercial and open editing models under split-intent attacks.

entry.title: LLM Evolutionary Search Strategies Should be Compared by Tokens

author.name: Tal Oved, Roi Pony, Oshri Naparstek, Udi Barzelay

entry.summary: The authors re-evaluate LLM evolutionary search methods using token budgets instead of proposal counts, replaying 600 logged runs across 5 tasks and 3 methods. They show equal-proposal comparisons can silently grant up to 1.9x compute differences, and under matched token budgets the evolutionary advantage over independent sampling largely disappears.

entry.title: RATION: Towards Quantitative Risk-Based Access Control for AI Agents

author.name: Yuntao Du, Harsh Chaudhari, Yuetian Chen, Ron Heichman, Ashish Jayamohan, Kumar Pallav, Mahim Patel, Kaiyuan Zhang, Kyle Polley, Jerry Ma, Ninghui Li

entry.summary: RATION is a security framework that tracks measurable risks accumulated during agent task execution and enforces quantitative constraints, replacing action-restriction approaches that impose harsh security-utility tradeoffs on complex open-ended tasks. Authored by a large team including Ninghui Li and Jerry Ma, it offers a principled risk-based access control model for AI agents facing threats like indirect prompt injection. This is a notable step toward practical agent permissioning systems.

entry.title: What Matters for NVFP4 Training? A Comparative Study of Low-Precision Pretraining Recipes

author.name: Anjulie Agrusa, Andrei Panferov, Elizabeth Wei, Keith Wyss, Paul Gibbons, Erik Schultheis, Jinhang Choi, Frank Sun, Tijmen Blankevoort, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: This systematic study compares recent NVFP4 (4-bit floating point) pretraining recipes at medium scale, training dense 8B and 30B-A3B MoE models for up to 1T tokens to determine which ingredients are necessary for accuracy recovery. The final recipe incorporates techniques like unbiased gradient handling grounded in principles from stable large-scale NVFP4 training. Given the authorship including Dan Alistarh and Tijmen Blankevoort, this is credible, high-leverage efficiency research for cheap LLM pretraining.

entry.title: When Code Becomes an LLM Call: An Empirical Study of Call-Site Contracts in Agentic Systems

author.name: Shihao Weng, Longtian Wang, Yang Feng, Mingfei Cheng, Jia Liu, Chao Shen, He Ye, Federica Sarro, Xiaofei Xie

entry.summary: An empirical study of LLM call-site contracts -- pre-conditions, prompt constraints, and post-conditions the surrounding program must enforce -- across 496 call sites in 40 agentic systems. It reframes software quality assurance for agentic code, where nondeterministic model behavior replaces deterministic logic and guarantees must come from the program around each call.

entry.title: PRECOCIAL: Pretraining with Code Curriculums via Iterative Search for Accelerated Learning

author.name: Edward Gu, Ali Payani, Kevin Ellis

entry.summary: PRECOCIAL automatically optimizes symbolic programs that generate synthetic pretraining data: an LLM iteratively rewrites a generator program, with each rewrite scored by pretraining a transformer on its data and fine-tuning downstream. To make search tractable, it keeps a single network across the whole search, continuing pretraining for accepted programs rather than retraining from scratch per candidate.

entry.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds

author.name: Jingwen Bai, Guochao Bai, Canbo Zhang, Shuangqi Li, Minchao Hu, Weichun Huang, Shuang Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a third route for embodied manipulation beyond per-task demonstrations or frontier models in every episode: a strong general model acts offline as an author that writes, runs, diagnoses, and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on held-out layouts, after which the frozen skill runs as cheap standalone code. The Skill-RSI protocol includes isolated audited authoring, hidden validation layouts, no-feedback controls, and a tamper-evident ledger.

entry.title: Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention

author.name: Karthik Viswanathan, Plamen Dimitrov, Stefano Rocca, Sarayu Sirikonda

entry.summary: This work defines head complexity, the minimum number of attention heads needed to represent a Boolean function in a one-layer attention-only Transformer, deriving an exact linear-fractional normal form and threshold-degree lower bounds with a strict explicit example. Notably, the proofs are formally verified using an autoresearch pipeline, combining theory of Transformer expressivity with machine-assisted verification.

entry.title: Local Evidence, Global Failure: Diagnosing Speech-Vision Temporal Composition in Audio-Visual Language Models

author.name: Jaehong Myung, Seunghun Oh, Unsang Park

entry.summary: This paper introduces Temporal Evidence Decomposition (TED), a training-free diagnostic framework that reveals a compositional weakness in audio-visual LLMs: they fail at full-video speech-vision decisions even when the required visual evidence is locally recoverable. TED uses ASR-derived utterance intervals to query audio-free windows separately and then aggregates evidence, boosting Temporal Forecasting accuracy on the SVHalluc benchmark from roughly 29-34% to 79-82% across four frozen AV-LLMs. The work matters because it isolates a specific aggregation failure mode in multimodal models and offers a practical, model-agnostic mitigation.

entry.title: Consistency Training Suppresses Cue Following Without Teaching Cue Selectivity

author.name: Prakhar Gupta, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Trains four consistency-training variants (on outputs, activations, attention, and sampled-answer rates) on Gemma-2-2B-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and shows via pre-registered predictions and circuit-level inspection that all four reduce sycophantic cue-following indiscriminately. Correct cues lose influence about as much as incorrect ones, meaning the models suppress cue use rather than learning to select only invalid cues.

entry.title: Causal Humility: Governing the Authority of Fairness Claims Under Causal Uncertainty

author.name: Khadija Zanna, Rodrigo Ferreira, Frederick L. Oswald, Akane Sano

entry.summary: This paper introduces the concept of causal humility for algorithmic fairness auditing, arguing that causal fairness claims in sociotechnical systems should be governed by explicit recognition of uncertainty from unobserved confounders, contested causal directions, and sensitive modeling assumptions. It proposes a framework for calibrating how much authority fairness conclusions deserve given the reliability of the underlying causal analysis, with implications for high-stakes domains like employment, lending, and healthcare.

entry.title: Secure Agentic Coding through Counterexample-Grounded Feedback

author.name: Tue Le, Anh Nguyen Hoang, Gabriel Sasseville, Doseok Jang, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Nghi D. Q. Bui

entry.summary: The paper introduces FALCON, a verification framework for secure code generation that separates attack exploration from behavioral verification and grounds both in execution, producing counterexamples rather than relying on model-judged security verdicts. This addresses reward-hacking risks where a security signal improves without vulnerabilities actually being fixed. It is relevant to the growing bottleneck of reliable security verification for coding agents.

entry.title: SPAR: Structural Pruning and Action Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shenli Zheng, Zhou Fang, Yuan Du, Yijiang Liu, Li Du

entry.summary: SPAR compresses vision-language-action models via structural pruning of the LLM backbone's hidden and feed-forward dimensions with pruning-aware tuning, followed by reinforcement learning to recover manipulation performance. Applied to the existing pi-0.5 model, it shrinks the language backbone from 2.34B to 0.09B parameters and the full model from 3.37B to 1.12B, removing roughly 96% and 67% of parameters. This directly targets the onboard compute constraints of robot deployment.

entry.title: The Development of Sycophancy in Language Models: Tracing Vulnerabilities from Pretraining to Post-Training

author.name: Haonan Huang, Chengkun Cai

entry.summary: The authors trace sycophancy development across 741 checkpoints from 30 open model lineages, planting initial verdicts on moral scenarios and measuring how models follow user opinions or abandon verdicts under pressure. They find the behavior is present before post-training in most lineages, with strength changing in either direction at different stages. This provides the first fine-grained developmental picture of when sycophantic vulnerabilities emerge during training.

entry.title: What Remains Without Test Labels? Re-evaluating a Graph-Level Anomaly Detection Benchmark

author.name: Yujie Lu, Da Yan

entry.summary: This paper audits the UB-GOLD benchmark for graph-level anomaly detection, finding that test labels are improperly used for model selection in the original benchmark and in 8 of 14 GLAD code bases. Re-running 21 detectors under label-free selection rules shows test-label checkpoint selection inflates AUROC by an average of 5.12 points across nine datasets. The work exposes a significant evaluation flaw in a widely reused benchmark and provides corrected, label-free methodology.

entry.title: Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation

author.name: Zhiyang Wang, Zhishang Luo, Yusu Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies looped GNNs that learn a local update rule during pretraining on small graphs and then repeatedly apply the same processor beyond training depth to handle larger graphs whose dependency radius grows with size. The authors categorize six looping schemes, establish fixed-depth information limits, and derive conditions for size generalization with parameter-efficient adaptation.

entry.title: An important Bottleneck in LLM Optimizers: Principle-Level Local Optima

author.name: Nian Ran, Tianhe Jia, Zhengyang Mu, Yue Wang, Sebastian Brulin, Markus Olhofer, Mauricio A. Alvarez, Yang Liu, Richard Allmendinger

entry.summary: This paper identifies and formalizes principle-level search collapse, where feedback-driven LLM optimizers confine their search to a narrow set of design principles despite generating distinct candidates, explaining prolonged plateaus in evolutionary search and Bayesian optimization. It contributes a diagnostic benchmark spanning molecular optimization, network sentinel-node selection, and GPU-kernel optimization, plus a decision-tree detection protocol.

entry.title: Representations Have Trajectories: Characterizing Temporal Representation Dynamics in Neural Networks

author.name: Shivaprasad B. Gowda, Sparsh Mittal

entry.summary: This paper conducts a large-scale empirical study tracking how representational geometry evolves throughout training rather than only at convergence, building on the observation that deep networks exhibit a low-rank simplicity bias. The authors identify three recurring geometric trajectories (persistent high-rank, collapse-and-recovery, persistent low-rank) and characterize destructive dynamics across architectures. This offers new insight into the training dynamics of representation learning that could inform architecture selection and training interventions.

entry.title: Latent World Models Should Plan with Distances Along the Latent Manifold

author.name: Zunzhi You, Linwei Tao, Siyu Xu, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Studying latent world models, the authors show that Euclidean distance in latent space only approximates goal proximity near the goal, creating spurious low-cost basins that trap planners farther away. They hypothesize latents lie near a curved low-dimensional manifold and propose planning with geodesic distances along this manifold instead of ambient norms. This reframes terminal cost design for model-based control.

entry.title: Where Groups Split: A Probe Prior for Nonzero Within-Group Variance in RL Post-Training

author.name: Jonah Ellison, Mateo Ruiz, Owen Pell, Tomas Duncun, Hanae Fujita, Ingrid Solberg, Caleb Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper addresses wasted rollouts in GRPO-style RL post-training, where prompts with unanimous groups (all correct or all incorrect) yield zero advantage and pass rate poorly predicts future group splitting. The proposed Aperture method estimates later pass rates from a short probe: a subset of prompts is trained with the same recipe, and every prompt is scored on both base and probe models to build a prior for nonzero within-group variance. This concentrates rollouts on prompts likely to produce informative gradient signal.

entry.title: Zephyrus-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Weather Reporting

author.name: Fengfei Yu, Marshall Fisher, Isadora White, Sumanth Varambally, Yasaman Jafari, Shivam Yadav, Samuel M. Bartlett, Shawn Roj, Benjamin J. Moore, Michael D. Warner, Luyu Han, Zhirui Xia, Duncan Watson-Parris, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Yian Ma, Rose Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Zephyrus-R1, a reinforcement learning framework for training AI models to generate natural-language weather forecast reports, a domain where outputs cannot be checked against a single ground-truth answer. The authors tackle the core challenges of reward design and curriculum learning within an agentic RL pipeline for scientific communication. This matters because it extends RL to unverifiable-output scientific domains with real safety implications for public weather communication and hazard warnings.

entry.title: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments

author.name: JooKyung Yuh, Byungmin Park, Eunseo Choi, Jinheon Baek, Junmo Cho, Kyu Hyun Choi, Sung Ju Hwang, Kyong Hwan Jin, Hae Beom Lee

entry.summary: BMD combines LLM-driven hypothesis generation with Bayesian experimental design for scientific model discovery: an LLM proposes model families while a numerical engine fits parameters, weighs models by evidence, and averages predictions to guide discriminating experiments. This addresses limitations of purely in-context LLM approaches and of Bayesian methods with fixed candidate sets.

entry.title: Learn the Interface, Not the Implementation: Output Representation Dominates Training Regime in LLM-Based RTL Generation

author.name: Siddharth Patel, Vikram Singh, Siddharth Savyasachi Malu, Rohit Singh

entry.summary: The authors study LLM-based generation of Verilog hardware designs, showing on a formally verifiable ECC wrapper task that the choice of output representation matters more than the training regime (fine-tuning, continued pre-training, RL from verifier). Using formal equivalence checking as an exact oracle across seven training settings and four representation levels, they argue representation design is the first-order question.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Minglei Li, Peng Ye, Haonan He, Jingqi Ye, Qingyu Yang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study establishing design recipes for applying parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to mixture-of-experts LLMs, covering which modules to adapt, adaptation granularity, PEFT method choice, and load-balancing objective usage across three MoE backbones. This addresses a timely gap as MoE architectures become dominant at scale.

entry.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Adrian Remonda, Jiajun Xi, Nicklas Hansen, Marcus Greiff, Thomas Lew, John Talbot, John Subosits, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that pretrains a world model on heterogeneous simulated trajectories and adapts it to the real domain with limited interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. It treats simulators as biased priors rather than requiring accurate sim-to-real transfer, evaluated in autonomous racing. This matters for safe and cost-effective deployment of RL on physical systems.

entry.title: Same Space or Not: Benchmarking Spatial Intelligence Through Cross-View Contradictions

author.name: Huizi Cao, Guanyu Xu, Zhixuan Liang, Ming Yin, Jiuxiang Gu, Manling Li, Mengdi Wang, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SSoN (Same Space or Not), a benchmark for evaluating whether vision-language models can maintain coherent scene representations across multiple viewpoints. The benchmark contains 1,000 questions built from seven indoor scene sources with six categories of controlled 3D edits, where each question presents three consistent views of a scene plus one edited outlier view that the model must identify. This cross-view contradiction resolution task goes beyond pairwise spatial relation probes and tests a capability directly relevant to embodied perception and real-world visual understanding.

entry.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos

author.name: Kerui Chen, Jinglu Wang, Yun Wang, Xinjiang Wang, Yan Lu

entry.summary: Video-EMem proposes an evolvable memory harness for long-video understanding with multimodal LLMs, combining compact free-form text with sparse time-anchored images to preserve semantic and visual detail across temporal scales. A Writer encodes the video once while a Reader retrieves and organizes evidence per query, amortizing the cost of repeated agentic video processing. This addresses context-length limits and redundant grounding costs in long-video QA.

entry.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space

author.name: Stavros Damianakis, Konstantinos Psounis

entry.summary: This Systematization of Knowledge presents PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt injection attacks organized by how the injected instruction is constructed to subvert the model, rather than by delivery vector or attacker goal. It unifies more than twenty public datasets that use incompatible vocabularies into six classes with a hierarchy of techniques, enabling consistent attack description and more systematic security evaluation.

entry.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents

author.name: Xiaoyuan Bao, Jingsi Jiang, Jiao Shan, Yulong Cao, Haoyu Wang, Zida Liu, Jun Gao

entry.summary: LeakBench is an executable audit suite testing autonomous clinical-modeling agents for reward hacking via prediction-time leakage, plus calibration, site-level evaluation, support awareness, and net benefit. Evaluated on MIMIC-IV (430k admissions) and multi-hospital MHFP data, it finds that a deterministic optimizer and every evaluated agent select prediction-time-invalid inputs because they improve validation reward.

entry.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution

author.name: Zhiyu Li, Zeyu Zhang, Linyun Liu, Yiwei Bu, Chenyang Xi, Xichong Zhang, Yi Yu, Yu Yu, Zhichen Liu, Yuxiao Yi, Chunyu Li, Haoran Liu, Zhenkai Ding, Le Zhou, Juncheng Zhang, Boyu Chen, Zehao Lin, Guorui Li, Renyu Fu, Ji Li, Youyang Xia, Jiajun Shen, Harvey Li, Jingsong Zhou, Helan Hu, Tong Shen, Tianxiao Xu, Chenye Han, Weijie Li, Zhongquan Zhou, Hongming Xu, Yuekeng Li, Erenkai Zhu, Peng Yu, Wenhao Li, Jingyi Kang, Xixuan Hao, Xuzhou Zhu, Can Chen, Jiawei Liu, Chen Jiang, Tao Jiang, Fangwei Xiang, Zepeng Yao, Kai Chen, Guang Yang, Mingfei Lu, Chunhui Li, Zhengxuan Jiang, Bo Tang, Shiyu Zhan, Yihang Sun, Jie Chu, Wenjun Xiong, Zhenxiang Hua, Chen Lin, Detong Su, Dongyu Deng, Qiuping Ding, Guofeng Ding, Si Chen, Guohua Wen, Xu Chen, Zhi-Qin John Xu, Ying-Cong Chen, Ningyu Zhang, Haofen Wang, Muning Wen, Haotian Chen, Wentao Zhang, Xuanhe Zhou, Rita Zhang, Junchi Yan, Feiyu Xiong

entry.summary: MemT-1.0 is a family of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation, built on Metis with Gated DeltaNet-2 token-level memory updates and a Mixture-of-Storage mechanism to scale native memory capacity. It is trained with a two-stage pipeline on 34B tokens with released model checkpoints, aiming at continuous information accumulation as an intrinsic capability.

entry.title: Safety Kernel: Mechanistic Alignment for Cross-Lingual Defense in LLMs

author.name: Chengyu Xie, Fei Shen, Shuyi Miao, Yue Feng, Jian Yu, Pengyang Shao, Yijun Tian, Xiaoyu Du

entry.summary: Analyzes cross-lingual safety behavior at the neuron level, using SCAR scores over multilingual parallel safe and unsafe prompts to identify a compact set of safety-related neurons shared across languages, termed the safety kernel. This mechanistic target enables internal interventions that strengthen safety guardrails against cross-lingual attacks that bypass external alignment.

entry.title: When Does Better Acceptance Pay? A Controlled Study of Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yongchao Long, Chunrui Zheng, Yuxuan Zhou, Guangkun Nie, Tian-Chi Ma, Chao Pang, Shuohuan Wang, Yuchen Ding, Xianbin Wen, Dianhai Yu, Junyuan Shang, Yuxi Zhou, Shenda Hong

entry.summary: This controlled study establishes a rigorous comparison protocol for speculative decoding, retraining six drafter recipes on shared data and remeasuring checkpoints across ten benchmarks and two target models. It finds that published acceptance-length gaps shrink substantially under shared training and inference conditions, and analyzes when acceptance gains actually translate to throughput.

entry.title: Self-Distillation for Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Wenxuan Zhu, Bang An, Shuming Liu, Wenqing Cui, Tianqi Xu, Bing Li, Yibo Yang, Peter Wonka, Bernard Ghanem

entry.summary: Introduces Gold-Conditioned Distillation (GCD), where a single model acts as both teacher and student: the teacher sees the gold response in-context while the student sees only the prompt, and the student minimizes forward KL to the teacher distribution at gold tokens. This converts one-hot SFT targets into model-native soft supervision that preserves valid alternative continuations while anchoring correctness.

entry.title: Bridged Self-Distillation for On-Policy Learning

author.name: Runsheng Chen (Technical University of Munich, Germany), Yihong Liu (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Raoyuan Zhao (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Michael A. Hedderich (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Hinrich Sch\"utze (LMU Munich, Germany, Munich Center for Machine Learning, Germany), Matthias Grabmair (Technical University of Munich, Germany)

entry.summary: Introduces Bridged Self-Distillation (BSD), a unified framework for on-policy distillation from any teacher that provides reasoning traces, using the trace as privileged context while the student generates its own rollouts. This addresses mismatches between teacher and student in solution imitability and token-level probability compatibility.

entry.title: TeleTwin: A Calibrated Digital Twin of Telegram Crisis Discourse as a Ground-Truth Testbed for Detecting LLM-Powered Information Operations

author.name: Despoina Antonakaki, Sotiris Ioannidis

entry.summary: The authors build TeleTwin, an LLM-powered digital twin of a Telegram crisis-discourse ecosystem where channels are agents instantiated from real channel histories, calibrated on 1.07 million messages from 195 public channels covering the Israel-Gaza and Iran-Israel conflicts. The twin tracks daily discourse dynamics on held-out data including the June 2025 Iran-Israel war, providing a rare ground-truth testbed for evaluating coordination detectors against LLM-generated influence operations.

entry.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Tengju Ru, Weitong Lian, Zecong Tang, Zhiheng Liu, Lingyi Meng, Haoran Li, Kaixuan Wang, Bohao Li, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes whether native generation-side representations in unified multimodal models can improve fine-grained visual understanding, finding them more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes than understanding-side features. It demonstrates direct use of generation representations, beyond prior generative-supervision or explicit-generation approaches, to unlock fine-grained perception in UMMs.

entry.title: NV-Generate-Body: 3D Latent Diffusion Model forControllable Anatomy, Tumor, and Demographic Body Mask Synthesis

author.name: Can Zhao, Pengfei Guo, Dong Yang, Yufan He, Yucheng Tang, Ahmed Harouni, Benjamin Simon, Mason Belue, Stephanie Harmon, Baris Turkbey, Daguang Xu

entry.summary: From an NVIDIA-led team, NV-Generate-BodyMask is a 3D latent diffusion model synthesizing whole-body CT segmentation masks with joint control over organ anatomy, tumor burden, and patient demographics, using a frozen mask autoencoder latent space and a 19-dimensional conditioning vector. Trained on 8,571 masks across 26 cohorts and 132 labels, it includes a size-adaptive ROI loss and tumor injection pipeline to handle scarce tumor annotations.

entry.title: Goal Images Are Control Targets: Spatially-Grounded Goal-Image Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Riddhi Chatterjee, Ritish Shrirao, Kushagra Mehrotra, Viswanath Gopalakrishnan

entry.summary: Shows that leaderboard-topping image editors such as Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5 produce worse goal images for robot manipulation than smaller fine-tuned open models, with the gap widening on long-horizon CALVIN tasks. The paper argues that image-editing quality metrics are poor proxies for control utility and proposes spatially grounded goal-image synthesis evaluated through two goal-conditioned policies.

entry.title: Visual Scaffolding: Toward Native Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Run Shao, Zhaoyang Zhang, Ziyu Li, Linrui Xu, Ji Qi, Xiu Su, Yichao Cao, Chao Tao, Haifeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes the concept of native multimodal reasoning where visual representations serve as reusable intermediate reasoning states, analogous to how chain-of-thought text scaffolds language reasoning. The paper introduces a framework in which native visual artifacts are examined, reused, and composed alongside language during reasoning.

entry.title: A 3D-Driven Framework for Moving-Camera Perspective-to-360{\deg} Video Generation

author.name: Michael Wakeham, Mrinmoy Kumar Das, Wenqi Wang, Ayush Tewari, Boqing Gong, Deepti Ghadiyaram

entry.summary: This paper tackles the task of converting a moving-camera perspective video into a full 360-degree video, which requires preserving observations accumulated over time, completing unseen regions, and keeping the scene consistent under changing viewpoints. The authors propose a modular, 3D-driven framework that splits these responsibilities across specialized components linked by a shared scene representation: input observations are reconstructed explicitly in 3D, and a pretrained panoramic image model fills in unobserved content. This decomposition avoids overburdening a single conditional video model and reduces reliance on panoramic video training data.

entry.title: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer

author.name: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: ReDT is a feed-forward visual geometry transformer that scales multi-view reconstruction to high-definition inputs, overcoming the fixed-SD training resolution limits of prior visual geometry models. It uses a resolution-aware design mapping each view to a fixed-size representation to control both inter-frame and intra-frame attention costs.

entry.title: Functional Cross-layer Experts Routing for One-step Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Zile Huang, Ser-nam Lim

entry.summary: This paper studies how model capacity should be internally organized in one-step diffusion distillation, formalizing the problem as functional allocation where shared generative priors and prompt-specific details must coexist in a single forward pass. The authors propose DeMoE, an architecture combining an always-active shared expert with conditionally routed residual experts, and show this beats standard isolated MoE designs when expert interference outweighs shared transfer benefits.

entry.title: MIRA: A Multimodal Illustrated Deep Research Agent for Controllable Reports

author.name: Hongrui Wu, Kaiwen Tuo, Congcong Wang, Gen Li, Shuai Dong, Xinlei Yu, Yuqi Xu, Haowen Hou, Zelin Peng, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: MIRA is a deep research agent that extends web-search-and-synthesize pipelines to handle interleaved text and image inputs, gathering multimodal evidence and producing illustrated reports under user-specified control over granularity, composition, and grounding. It targets two gaps in existing systems: underuse of images found during search and rigid, fixed-form report generation.

entry.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience

author.name: Xinhao Ji, Hui En Pang, Hao Li, Kairui Hu, Jiner Wang, Mingze Sun, Ziang Cao, Yalun Dai, Thang Luu, Qin Ma, Hongyi Chen, Yukang Cao, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: EgoXperience presents a full-stack paradigm for world-grounded egocentric perception covering data collection, automatic annotation via EgoX-Engine (geometrically verified tracking plus SLAM-based world alignment), unified joint modeling of camera, scene, hands, and objects, and benchmarking. It targets coherent joint 3D reconstruction of human activity rather than isolated components. The automatic annotation engine is the key enabler for scalable supervision.

entry.title: Vision-Language-Delta-Action: Learning Compact Deltas as Actionable Transition Interfaces for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Lingsen Zhang, Wei Li, Jie He, Henghua Zhang, Kai Mo, Shiyong Li, Yanpeng Wang, Rui Shao

entry.summary: Introduces VLDA, a reformulation of vision-language-action models that replaces full future-state prediction with compact latent Delta variables capturing only task-relevant world-state changes. This avoids wasting model capacity on static appearance and action-irrelevant dynamics. It addresses a real learning-burden gap between semantic understanding and action execution in manipulation.

entry.title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures

author.name: Sebastian Sartor, Robert Seamans, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: The authors construct the first abilities-based exposure measures for robotics and physical AI, spanning occupations, industries, and geographies, following the Felten et al. framework. They build a 16-capability robotics taxonomy from 78 sources and use an LLM to score capability relatedness to 52 ONET work abilities, addressing the gap left by measures that only cover software AI or proxy robotics via patents.

entry.title: Action-Aligned Latent Planning for Versatile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Yutang Lin, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: FIBER uses the executable latent space of a frozen behavioral foundation model as a shared planning representation for heterogeneous humanoid loco-manipulation skills, projecting latent plans back to executable actions. This bridges compact high-level abstractions and state-dependent physical responses without requiring the planner to model high-frequency closed-loop feedback.

entry.title: Structure over Reasoning: Unified Zero-Shot Navigation with a Small Vision-Language Model

author.name: Zeqi Li, Xunyi Zhao, Zerui Li, Sihao Lin, Qi Wu, ShiJie Li

entry.summary: This paper finds that small VLMs like Qwen3-VL-4B judge single-view goal matching well but fail at route reasoning, distance estimation, and stop decisions. The proposed agent instead treats VLM answers as perceptual evidence rather than actions, accumulating directional judgments into a route-blind semantic field over a bird's-eye map that supports structured zero-shot navigation. This achieves unified navigation by exploiting structure rather than model reasoning.

entry.title: Self-Crystallizing Behavior Trees: Amortizing Foundation-Model Reasoning into Deterministic Control for Autonomous Drones

author.name: Behnam Moradi

entry.summary: Self-Crystallizing Behavior Trees treat the foundation model as a compile-time tool rather than a runtime component: when a behavior tree node fails, an LLM proposes a minimal subtree patch, CMA-ES tunes its parameters in simulation, and a contextual bandit decides whether to store the patch or request a new one. This amortizes LLM reasoning into deterministic, inspectable control logic for safety-critical drones. The design avoids permanent model-in-the-loop latency and non-determinism.

entry.title: ScaleNav: Scalable Internet Video Pretraining for Language-Conditioned Local Navigation

author.name: Yihui Yang, Yuanhong Yu, Jiawei Wang, Zhongrui Yu, Jia Shi, Kun Zhan, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou, Yu Liu, Sida Peng

entry.summary: ScaleNav learns language-conditioned local navigation by pretraining goal-directed visual dynamics on internet egocentric videos, then distilling those dynamics into a robot navigation policy via a unified world-action model with three-stage training. This sidesteps the cost of real-robot data collection and the sim-to-real gap of simulation.

entry.title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control

author.name: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Xinyuan Lv, Shuanghao Bai, Guangrun Li, Jingyang He, Ziluo Ding, Zhiyuan Xu, Ning Ding, Kuan Cheng, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang, Zhengping Che

entry.summary: HAF-VLA adapts a pretrained flow-matching vision-language-action model to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation through a hierarchical action-flow framework that coordinates locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation. The design addresses the instability that base and waist errors induce in upper-body control on high-dimensional humanoid action spaces.

entry.title: Dirichlet-Tree Allocation Priors for Bayesian Causal Forests

author.name: Javier Enrique Aguilar, Daniel Klippert, Yusufhan Balci, Alexander Marx

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a Dirichlet-Tree prior on the variance shares of leaf values in Bayesian Causal Forests, generated via stick-breaking along the tree topology. This jointly regularizes treatment-tree leaves, addressing the problem that independent shrinkage priors exert no control over how trees allocate variability across leaves. The authors characterize the marginal leaf prior and show it adaptively bounds effective leaf count, improving heterogeneous treatment effect estimation.

entry.title: How Researchers Lie to AIs

author.name: Alessandro Drake

entry.summary: A Redwood Research internship sprint project that catalogs the practice of lying to models during alignment evaluations, based on a survey of 292 public alignment evaluations from December 2022 to October 2026. It argues that fabricated scenarios can leak into pretraining data and web search results, potentially eroding human credibility with models in ways researchers have not anticipated.

entry.title: Not Every User Says It All: Training Tool-Using Agents Beyond Ideal Simulated Users

author.name: Han Bao, Zheyuan Zhang, Kaiwen Shi, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: The paper shows tool-using agents trained and evaluated with idealized, fully explicit simulated users degrade sharply with weak users, and that neither training with weak users (via masks, mixtures, or curricula) nor prompting agents to ask more questions reliably helps. It proposes StaGPO (State-Grouped Policy Optimization), where the agent writes what it learned about user state to improve robustness beyond the strong-user setting.

entry.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success

author.name: Naman Vats

entry.summary: This pre-specified controlled study tests whether a typed decision model (Jev 1.13) consulted at deterministic decision points makes a Claude Sonnet 5.5 terminal agent cheaper without degrading success. Across 315 trials on Terminal-Bench 2.1, the controller raised cost per attempt by 19% at an identical pass rate, with placebo controls helping isolate the effect.

entry.title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing

author.name: Yunlong Deng, Yan Li, Xing Hu, Yida Zhu, Sean Du, Weiyang Liu, Guangyi Chen

entry.summary: The Native Context Editing (NCE) framework gives language model agents a grammar of special tokens for editing their own context during generation, treating context editing as an atomic, inherent capability. Agents are trained on iteratively constructed trajectory segments with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context. This makes context management part of the language itself rather than an external runtime mechanism.

entry.title: From Black Box to Controller: Inference-Time Steering of LLM via Feature Amplification

author.name: Keqi Chen, Zekai Sun, Yuhua Wen, Tianyi Tian, Xinyang Huang, Huijun Lian, Yingming Gao, Ya Li

entry.summary: NeuroSteer is a plug-and-play framework that uses a sparse autoencoder as a controller to quantitatively adjust LLM behavioral preferences at inference time, such as modulating a model's caution level by scenario risk. It avoids task-specific prompt engineering or costly fine-tuning by amplifying interpretable internal features.

entry.title: Train An Imaginative Agent

author.name: Jiaxin Ge, Junyi Zhang, Tianning Chai, Hanjun Yoo, Chenyang Wang, Xiuyu Li, Weijia Shi, XuDong Wang, Sewon Min, Luke Zettlemoyer, Trevor Darrell, Haiwen Feng

entry.summary: Agima trains a single omni model to imagine before acting: proposing actions, generating images of their outcomes, and reasoning over imagined futures to decide what to execute, with fine-tuning followed by RL. This lets agents simulate action sequences, explore alternatives, and compare futures, useful when feedback is sparse or actions irreversible.

entry.title: SpinDoctor: Finding Innocuous Prompts for Biased Image Generation

author.name: Anna Gerchanovsky, Omer Akgul, Lujo Bauer, Michael K. Reiter

entry.summary: SpinDoctor discovers innocuous-looking prompts that reliably induce a chosen target bias in text-to-image model outputs while preserving image and prompt quality, posing a covert manipulation risk to users who receive such prompts. It works black-box, transfers across models with the same bias emerging in 78.6% of cases, and allows arbitrary bias targets.

entry.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners

author.name: Peisong Wang, Feixue Liu, Yize Meng, Bowen Liu, Ruoyu Chen, Gaoyang Dai, Xing He, Aiqian Li, Fengchi Yuan, Aochuan Chen, Chenyi Zi, Yuhan Li, Hongchuan Zeng, Yimo Yan, Nuo Chen, Jie Fu, Zuo-Jun Max Shen, Yong-Hong KUO, Jia Li

entry.summary: OR-License is an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios drawn from paid operations research engagements totaling USD 3.68 million, preserving original client requirements, data, and deliverable formats after de-identification. It also introduces ORSim, a client simulator for studying agent information acquisition from ambiguous briefs.

entry.title: One Head Away from Language Confusion: Single Attention Heads Across Model Families

author.name: Jiwon Jeong, Anjelo Jann Laroza, Chaewoon Yoon, Arjun Pillai, Pranav Kokati, Christian Hoang, Seunghyeok Hong

entry.summary: This interpretability study ablates individual attention heads across 12 model checkpoints from seven model families to localize the language confusion failure, where LLMs reply in an unexpected language. The authors find that in ten models, zeroing a single specific head causes substantially more language departures than any other head in its layer, with seven heads shifting 8 to 51.5 percent of continuations out of the prompt language.

entry.title: Modaliff: A Unified Token Diffusion Model for Any-to-Any Generation

author.name: Duc Kieu, Kien Do, Minh Khoa Le, Tung Kieu, Dang Nguyen, Thin Nguyen

entry.summary: Modaliff is a token-based diffusion model for any-to-any generation across text, image, and audio that trains on widely available bimodal pairs rather than fully aligned multimodal tuples. It assembles conditions and targets into a unified token sequence with per-token attributes and role-based positional embeddings, letting one denoiser support diverse generation tasks without task-specific architectures.

entry.title: Dataset Inference for Data Provenance and Privacy Auditing in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Dariush Wahdany (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Jesse Cresswell (Layer 6 AI), Naiqing Guan (Layer 6 AI), Atiyeh Ashari Ghomi (Layer 6 AI), Franziska Boenisch (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Adam Dziedzic (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security)

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first dataset inference method for tabular foundation models, determining whether a suspect dataset was used in a model's pre-training via black-box access. The authors systematically analyze candidate observable signals, finding individual signals provide only weak evidence, motivating combined signal approaches for provenance and privacy auditing.

entry.title: Distribution-Based Regularization for Reward Fine-Tuning Diffusion and Flow Models
