author.name: Romeo Passaro, Jeongjae Lee, Jong Chul Ye, Michael M. Bronstein, Yoshua Bengio, Alexander Tong, Danyal Rehman

entry.summary: The paper proposes DFR, which augments task rewards in diffusion/flow-model fine-tuning with a distribution-dependent per-sample reward acting explicitly on the generated distribution, generalizing the KL-regularized objective beyond expected rewards. This directly targets mode collapse and distributional drift that reverse-KL velocity penalties only address indirectly. A strong author group (Bengio, Bronstein, Ye, Tong) working on a central problem in reward fine-tuning of generative models.

entry.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?

author.name: Jiaqi Su, Guibin Zhang, Jie-Jing Shao, Cong Pang, Tiankuo Yao, Ivor Tsang, Haiyan Yin, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: CoEvo-RSI studies the brain-body mismatch problem in recursive self-improving agents, where an evolving harness demands behaviors the model lacks or restricts capabilities it already has. The framework uses a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback so a meta-agent coordinates harness development with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation. This advances joint model-harness co-evolution for RSI agents.

entry.title: Beyond the record: evaluating probabilistic AI weather forecasts deep in the tail

author.name: Bastiaan Van Velthoven, Cas Decancq, Diego G. Miralles, Stijn Luca, Thomas Mortier

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether probabilistic AI weather models retain skill beyond their training domain by assessing four state-of-the-art systems (ArchesWeatherGen, U-Cast, WeatherNext2, GenCast-mini) against the physics-based IFS-ENS on 2022 record events relative to 1979-2021 ERA5 boundaries. Using record-threshold weighted CRPS and Brier scores with record depth characterization, it measures magnitude and probability of record exceedances including misses and false alarms. This addresses the critical tail-risk question for AI weather forecasting.

entry.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation

author.name: Xuyuan Xiong, Siyu Chen, Zihan Shao, Yue Su, Weiyang Jin, Ping Luo, Zhuoran Yang, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: This paper fits a unified scaling law across nearly 600 training runs of looped transformers, jointly varying model size, tokens, and forward/backward loop counts with truncated BPTT. Counter to compute-saving intuitions, the fitted law favors full backpropagation through time when loop counts are jointly optimized.

entry.title: Wet-Biased Data Pipelines Mislead the Training and Evaluation of Generative Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Christoph Metzl, Stefan Kapsreiter, Kianusch Vahid Yousefnia, Virginia Poli, Richard M\"uller, Frank Kr\"uger, Tobias B\"olle

entry.summary: This paper shows analytically and empirically that wet-biased sampling in precipitation nowcasting datasets shifts the conditional distribution learned by generative models, and that target-dependent test sampling conceals this training bias. Using a fixed satellite-to-radar diffusion model, it demonstrates evaluation biases can mask significant training distribution distortions.

entry.title: Learning to Reason Efficiently with Interventional Step Credit

author.name: Guanda Li, Xuefeng Bai, Yulong Chen, Zhiyong Wang, Kehai Chen, Min Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes interventional step credit, a causal-intervention measure that assesses each chain-of-thought step's contribution to the final answer through targeted parameter-level interventions, unlike attention or entropy heuristics that reflect step behavior rather than causal value. Building on this, IGPO uses ISC for fine-grained advantage rescaling in reinforcement learning, trimming redundant reasoning steps while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Zilin Xiao, Zhiyuan Wang, Avinash Atreya, Ke Yang, Jinwoo Shin, Kecheng Hao

entry.summary: Introduces Retrieval Program Learning (RPL), a framework in which an RL policy composes search primitives into executable retrieval programs with local state and control flow, enabling adaptive multi-step search that decouples retrieval breadth from context consumption. The authors also address the resulting hard exploration problem for reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Atoms, Not Knowledge: What Production-Scale Addressed-Memory Writes Deposit

author.name: Wei Gao, Cheng Tian, Duan Yang, Jianqing Yin

entry.summary: This paper audits whether deterministic hash-addressed conditional memory can truly inject knowledge at production scale, testing beds from 124M to 176.95B parameters including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It finds a coverage threshold dependent on backbone training, with coverage collapsing from 98% at 50 facts to 12.7% at 1,000 facts at fixed budget.

entry.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation

author.name: Kesav Kumar Jayakumar, Karthigeyan Thilak

entry.summary: While attempting to reproduce a hallucination-mitigation result on POPE, the authors found that common evaluation code compares the wrong vocabulary token IDs for yes/no decisions: LLaVA-1.5-7B never generates the assumed two tokens, instead emitting space-prefixed variants due to SentencePiece tokenization. The audit shows this readout choice alone shifts F1 by 1.2 to 8.7 points across 9,000 questions.

entry.title: Causal Spatio-Temporal Neural Distance Fields for Counterfactual Cardiac Anatomy

author.name: Mathias Lowes, Kurt Butler, Kristine Aavild S{\o}rensen, Klaus F. Kofoed, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris, Rasmus R. Paulsen, Steven McDonagh

entry.summary: This work couples spatio-temporal neural distance fields with a structural causal model over clinical variables to enable counterfactual prediction of a patient's cardiac anatomy under altered clinical conditions, supporting risk modeling and intervention planning. The representation separates clinical conditioning from subject-specific shape while remaining continuous across the cardiac cycle.

entry.title: SwitchSplat: Learning Discrete Object States from Casually Captured Scenes

author.name: Yizheng Xie, Yalda Foroutan, George Shramko, Daniel Rebain, Shrisudhan Govindarajan, Andrea Tagliasacchi

entry.summary: Introduces SwitchSplat, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting representation that models discrete object state changes (open doors, toggled switches) in casual captures, using a base-plus-slot decomposition where a shared static base captures the invariant scene and slots encode alternate states. This goes beyond time-conditioned 4D methods by enabling composition of arbitrary object configurations rather than replaying observed sequences.

entry.title: UBD-Bench: Benchmarking and Analyzing Unimodal Branch Degradation in Multimodal Perception for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ang Liu, Xiang Gu, Ruikai Li, Qiyue Wang, Yizhe Fan, Hao Shan, Ziyang Yan, Han Jiang, Zhenning Li, Xiaoshuai Hao, Yilong Ren, Zhiyong Cui, Haiyang Yu

entry.summary: UBD-Bench systematically studies unimodal branch degradation in multimodal autonomous driving perception, revealing that stronger multimodal outputs can mask weakened per-modality representations. Its Paired Frozen-Branch Probe compares representation quality after unimodal versus joint training across four tasks and ten models, finding camera branches are particularly prone to degradation.

entry.title: Procedural Exposure Bias in Skill-Augmented Language Model Agents

author.name: Qing Yang, Yuqi Xiong, Pengcheng Huang, Zhipeng Xu, Zhenghao Liu, Zulong Chen, Yu Gu, Ge Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies Procedural Exposure Bias (PEB): language model agents increasingly favor actions as their associated procedural patterns are repeatedly exposed in supplied skills, even when state and relevance are unchanged. Notably, presenting the same skill content visually rather than textually substantially attenuates this bias, apparently due to visual encoding rather than layout.

entry.title: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models

author.name: Tianyu Xin, Wanqi Zhong, Bowen Hu, Zhangchi Guo, Lijie Wang, Yiming Wang, Haoran Liao, Heyang Yu, Xiaoyu Tian, Zhiding Yu, Yiming Li

entry.summary: PrismWAM argues that world action models should separate how the world appears (semantic context) from how it evolves under action (physical state), factorizing embodied tasks into semantic planning and physical state components. This addresses the entanglement problem when WAMs rely on latent embeddings from pretrained video models. The representational disentanglement question is central to building reliable embodied agents.

entry.title: GenOlympiad: Benchmarking Frontier Image Models at Their Capability Boundaries

author.name: Xi Hu, Martin Bell, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: GenOlympiad is a benchmark of extremely challenging text-to-image prompts across nine capability axes, including counting, deep reasoning, and hard physical consistency, designed so that prompt alignment is visually verifiable rather than subjective. It includes an automated evaluation framework that decomposes prompts for objective scoring. This provides a much-needed rigorous stress test for frontier image generation models.

entry.title: From Likelihood to Utility: Quality-Axis Diffusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junjie Yang, Ziyi Shi, Shuqi Shen, Xinhu Zheng, Hongliang Lu, Hai Yang

entry.summary: Proposes QualiDrive, which reformulates diffusion-based end-to-end driving planners to generate trajectories along a driving-quality axis rather than the Gaussian-noise axis, ranking observed trajectories by measured utility and learning ordered low-to-high-quality refinement. On NAVSIM it achieves 94.5 PDMS. A conceptually novel reframing that makes driving utility central rather than auxiliary to trajectory generation.

entry.title: ContactBench 1.0: A Benchmark for Everyday Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jingyi Xiang, Yixuan Wang, Jeannette Bohg, Wenzhen Yuan

entry.summary: ContactBench 1.0 defines eight recurring skill categories from observations of everyday human manipulation and instantiates them through 36 reference tasks and over 40 3D-printable object assets with paired simulation models featuring tunable resistance. It aims to make evaluation of contact-rich manipulation reproducible across laboratories.

entry.title: Escape Without a Recipe: Maneuver-Agnostic Mars Rover Recovery from Granular Entrapment

author.name: Meraj Hossain Promit, Chandak Chakma, Md Jubair Ahmed Sourov, Sejuti Rahman

entry.summary: The paper introduces a recurrent policy that lets planetary rovers escape granular entrapment without predefined recovery maneuvers, trained in an MPM-based regolith simulator. The authors first rigorously verify a genuine trap configuration where the best of ten scripted controllers succeeds in only 7/32 trials, then use a frozen entrapment detector trained on 81,771 windows to provide belief states. This addresses a real operational hazard for Mars missions.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions

author.name: Kallol Saha, Yining Hong, Amber Li, Yejin Choi, Maxim Likhachev, David Held

entry.summary: DISCO transfers long-horizon reasoning from tree search into manipulation policies over continuous action spaces. It runs progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation with a learned policy proposing actions and a learned value function scoring them, then distills the search results back into the policy for long-horizon multi-object rearrangement.

entry.title: Unified Multiparadigm Fusion Intelligence for Rare Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Jian Yang, Peiling Liu, Songda Li, Yu Cao, Yuqing Feng, Lan Yu, Jiarong Pan, Jing Ye, Xinwen Huang, Chaochun Zou, Xudong Lu, Huilong Duan, Haomin Li

entry.summary: FusionRare is a unified framework integrating symbolic knowledge-driven reasoning, deep-learning pattern recognition, and causal/LLM components for rare disease diagnosis, addressing the structural weaknesses of each paradigm alone. It targets the diagnostic odyssey affecting an estimated 300 million people with rare diseases.

entry.title: Joint, Decoupled, or Agent: When Each Multimodal Alignment Paradigm Wins

author.name: Yi Fang, Gaurav Srivastava, Sirui Ding, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: This large-scale comparison evaluates three multimodal alignment paradigms—jointly pretrained encoders, independently pretrained decoupled encoders, and frozen-LLM agents—across 16 paired datasets, five domains, and multiple label budgets (144 combinations). No paradigm dominates: DECOUPLED wins 54, AGENT 46, and JOINT 44 by mean utility, providing practical guidance for practitioners.

entry.title: Train Locally, Learn Together: Distributed Multi-Agent Training via ADMM

author.name: Yiwei Chen, Changsheng Wang, Yicheng Lang, Qing Qu, Alfred O. Hero, Sijia Liu

entry.summary: The authors introduce the first optimization-grounded framework for distributed multi-agent LLM training based on consensus ADMM, enabling agents to improve system-level capabilities through role-local learning and decentralized communication without a central trainer. This addresses the scalability and resilience limitations of centralized multi-agent training. It paves the way toward self-organizing multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Toward Collective Model Intelligence: Characterizing and Coordinating Models

author.name: SinapisAI Team, Jian-Dong Liu, Qun Dai, Zhendong Du, Guannan Lai, Hao-Yu Liu, Yi-Fan Ma, Zi-Yu Mao, Tengzhong Sun, Xin-Yi Zhang, Zi-Chen Zhao, Gelin Bian, Zongyuan Cai, Ju Cang, Zhangqin Chen, Shilei Gu, Guoding Ji, Taojian Jiang, Hao-Xuan Ma, Fan Wu, Lin-Xing Wu, Tao Yu, Xiao Zhang, Tianyi Zhou, Rong Gu, Ming Li, Zhi-Hao Tan, Han-Jia Ye, Yang Yu, De-Chuan Zhan

entry.summary: This large-team paper presents a systematic approach to collective model intelligence via three components: Model Eval for evidence-based capability profiling with limited evaluation, Mio for organizing complementary model candidates, and efficient model-call execution under resource constraints. The goal is to coordinate independently developed models to collaborate across diverse tasks.

entry.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents

author.name: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li, Xiyu Ren, Wei Fan, Tianshi Zheng, Weizhi Du, Jingqiao Yu, Xingsu Li, Zhaowei Wang, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Presents CoworkEnv, a framework for automatically synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers, including requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks, validated programmatically with feedback repair. It produces SFT demonstrations from teacher executions and RL rollouts and rewards from student interactions, enabling training of long-horizon agents.

entry.title: When Empathy Misses the Goal: A Benchmark for Goal Displacement in LLM Advice

author.name: Dean Ariel, Guy Laban

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Goal Displacement Benchmark (GDB), with 230 scenarios across nine domains and 4,134 human-scored responses from 18 models, measuring when LLMs substitute persona-maintenance warmth for goal-relevant substance in advice. A 2x2 taxonomy crosses hard constraints with emotional distress, capturing both failures to confront infeasible goals and reverse displacement where unsolicited problem-solving replaces emotional support. A deletion-test rubric assesses whether responses contain substantive content.

entry.title: When to Stop Asking: Factor Coverage Bias and LLM Determinability Judgments with Underspecified Information in Medicine

author.name: Yusuke Watanabe, Yohei Kobashi, Taisei Tosaki, Takeshi Kojima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yasushi Okuno, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: This paper studies whether LLMs can judge determinability — whether available information suffices for a clinical decision — and identifies factor coverage bias, where models use the amount of decision-relevant information as a cue rather than assessing whether missing information could change the conclusion. Such bias could cause premature conclusions or excessive information gathering, including unnecessary invasive tests.

entry.title: MASIF: Implicit Failures for Process Observability in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yanwei Huang, Arpit Narechania, Atanu Sinha

entry.summary: MASIF studies implicit failures in multi-agent systems — local execution errors corrected, bypassed, or carried forward without determining task outcome — across 1,828 traces from nine MAS-benchmark configurations, finding IFs in 54.3 percent of successful and 75.2 percent of failed traces. It develops taxonomies of error types and absorption mechanisms, uses counterfactual replay, and shows IF-based best-of-N trace selection outperforms existing process reward models.

entry.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement

author.name: Ruotian Peng, Yuanyi Ren, Shuaiqi Liu, Xin Guo, Fang Zhu, Yangyi Huang, Yue Wu, Zheng Wang, Yandong Wen, Zhihang Fu

entry.summary: VibeTraining-Bench evaluates recursive self-improvement capability by asking research agents to jointly optimize training data, the trainer, and the inference harness of an identical starting agent system under a fixed resource budget. Tasks span terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning, with agents iterating against validation feedback before final test evaluation. This targets cross-component co-design as the core RSI skill.

entry.title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed

author.name: Raimondas Lencevicius (Microsoft)

entry.summary: A Microsoft-authored study showing that context truncation in agent harnesses costs a low-cost reasoning model nothing when facts can be re-looked-up, but drops success to chance when facts cannot be re-observed, with a 92.5 percentage-point difference between the two conditions. Pre-registered probes and a replication on a second provider model support the contrast.

entry.title: UMI-WM: Interactive World Modeling for Bimanual Manipulation from Wrist Cameras

author.name: Jingxiang Guo, Haoyu Zhao, Xidong Zhang, Yuhang Zheng, Hao Wu, Chen Gao, Jianshu Zhou, Shuicheng Yan, Weihao Yuan

entry.summary: UMI-WM is an action-conditioned bimanual world model that jointly generates both wrist-camera views from observation history, per-arm relative poses, and gripper widths, with mechanisms for cross-view consistency and action following. It extends interactive world modeling beyond text or single-camera control to scalable UMI-style bimanual manipulation data.

entry.title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive

author.name: Ziqian Zhang, Junjie Liao, Zhining Zhang, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Across four agent environments, this study probes whether multi-turn RL gains in vision-language model agents reflect improved grounded visual understanding. Representational probing shows vision-encoder accuracy stays stable while LLM-layer probes improve, with attention shifting toward visual tokens, suggesting RL improves attention routing rather than perception itself.

entry.title: Indirect Influences of Artificial Intelligence Advice on Complex Sepsis Treatment Decisions

author.name: Venkatesh Sivaraman, Joel Levin, Eric P. Mason, Victor Talisa, Suchi Saria, Jean Feng, Andrew J. King, Jeremy M. Kahn, Adam Perer

entry.summary: The authors retrospectively evaluated an AI sepsis system on 6,928 patients, finding it improved on original provider decisions overall but performed significantly worse in complex cases, then ran a pre-registered experiment with 228 US critical care physicians on how AI advice influences hemodynamic decisions. The work examines not just AI accuracy but how advice shapes clinician decisions, including subtle indirect influences. This is high-value human-AI interaction evidence in a high-stakes clinical domain.

entry.title: Do 3D Large Language Models Really Use 3D Evidence?

author.name: Yifei Zhao, Fanyu Zhao, Han Zhang, Yixuan Lin, Yuyang Hou, Bin Wu, Ruike Cao, Li Xiao, Yinsheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces UNICORNS, an 11,387-question benchmark over 557 ScanNet scans that tests whether 3D-LLMs ground responses in actual scene evidence under referential ambiguity, insufficient evidence, and false presuppositions. Strict pass criteria requiring no unsupported scene claims likely reveal significant reliability gaps in current 3D-LLMs.

entry.title: DiffuPlan: Editable Planning State for Diffusion Language Model Agents

author.name: Qisheng Zhou, Zhen Xiong, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: Introduces DiffuPlan, a diffusion search agent that maintains a single editable planning state, directly revising earlier plan steps as new evidence arrives instead of only appending text as autoregressive agents must. It exploits diffusion LLMs' ability to reconstruct earlier text conditioned on surrounding context, proposing a new agent-state paradigm.

entry.title: Arctic-SWE: Revisiting the Long Horizon Agent Training by Modeling-System Co-Design

author.name: Boyi Liu, Yite Wang, Xinyu Lian, Fan Shu, Sida Li, Feng Yan, Mingjia Zhang, Yuxiong He, Zhewei Yao

entry.summary: Arctic-SWE is a fully asynchronous RL framework for long-horizon software engineering agents that establishes a reproducible, well-tuned baseline through model-system co-design, using deliberate overfitting on a small task pool to expose failures hidden by early reward gains. It integrates gated rewards, importance-weight control, aligned training and inference engines, and consistent state across policy updates.

entry.title: MemDerive: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Agent Memory over Evolving Data

author.name: Sen Gao, Yongan Li, Han Chen, Bingsheng He, Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Michael Heinrich, Shixuan Sun

entry.summary: MemDerive is a diagnostic benchmark for agent memory that targets derived state: information not stored in any single record but computable via rules from an evolving interaction history. Using symbolic scenario specifications and Datalog, it produces gold answers, derivation DAGs, and supporting events so errors can be traced to specific missed or outdated states.

entry.title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories

author.name: Tianqi Liu, Yandong Guan, Songze Li, Wenkai Wang, Gang Yu, Chengfei Lv

entry.summary: The authors introduce PACE, a benchmark of 43 enterprise tasks with 750 expert-audited Code Points for evaluating whether coding agents fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents in mature repositories, combining requirement reconstruction, criterion construction, and evidence-based evaluation. Across 11 model-scaffold configurations, most scores fall in a limited range, exposing systematic delivery gaps. This fills a real gap left by issue-resolution and from-scratch benchmarks.

entry.title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models

author.name: Saurav Jha, Qianli Liao, Robert Vernon, Sarath Chandar, Quentin Fournier

entry.summary: recAMPLIFY adapts recursive pretraining to masked protein language models, using a weight-tied Transformer core that refines residue-aligned hidden states over adjustable cycles, enabling test-time scaling where autoregressive reasoning methods do not transfer. The 155M-parameter model is trained on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M but uses 56% fewer parameters. This offers a cheaper, repeat-compute-based alternative to pure model scaling for protein annotation and mutation-effect prediction.

entry.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy

author.name: Zekai Li, Jiayi Yu, Jinlu Zhang, Luyang Niu, Zekun Qi, Jun Zheng, Xuchuan Chen, Dairu Liu, Yintianrun Zhang, He Wang, Li Yi

entry.summary: Systematically studies physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) of VLM policies on 18 manipulation tasks with a five-axis evaluation metric (performance, efficiency, success, budget, improvement-from-failure) via PhysRSI-eval. Introduces a Physical Barrel Hypothesis about which capabilities constrain improvement, and fits observational scaling relations for physical RSI. Connects embodied AI to scaling-law analysis.

entry.title: A Statistical Viewpoint on Adam, Shampoo and Muon

author.name: Tetiana Parshakova, Robert M. Gower, Paulo Orenstein

entry.summary: The paper derives stochastic optimization methods from a statistical whitening perspective: modeling gradients as Gaussian and whitening them by their covariance, estimated online via regularized likelihood (MAP). Diagonal covariance approximation yields a method closely matching Adam, while Kronecker approximation yields a new MN method, a Shampoo variant. This provides a unifying probabilistic lens on the most important modern optimizers, connecting to the Muon line.

entry.title: Decentralized Online Exp-Concave Optimization

author.name: Hao Qiu, Mengxiao Zhang, Yuanyu Wan

entry.summary: The paper resolves an open question in decentralized online convex optimization by showing logarithmic regret is achievable for exp-concave losses. The proposed Decentralized Online Newton Step combines blocking and accelerated gossip with the Online Newton Step algorithm, achieving a regret bound scaling with network spectral gap and log-squared horizon terms. This closes the gap between convex, strongly convex, and exp-concave settings.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Hui Yang, Wan Tian, Tao Ren, Zhongyi Li, Yijie Peng

entry.summary: CSPO adaptively calibrates sequence-level clipping bounds for policy optimization of reasoning LLMs using conformal prediction on recent training statistics. Unlike fixed clipping bands, the resulting band targets a specified marginal tail probability and adapts to policy drift, with length-conditional calibration also addressed. This improves on GRPO-style token-level and fixed-band sequence-level methods for RL with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: Steered Not Stirred: Effective Reward Tilting using Surrogate Reward Mixing

author.name: Alec Sargood, Olivia Gallup, Georg Maierhofer, Noam Ghenassia, Paul Duckworth, Krisztina Sinkovics, Avishek Joey Bose

entry.summary: This paper addresses steering pretrained continuous-time generative models (diffusion, flow matching, flow maps) toward a latent oracle reward that is unavailable or expensive, using multiple cheaper surrogate rewards instead. Given a small feedback set, the method composes surrogates to tilt the output distribution toward the oracle-rewarded distribution. This is relevant wherever reward oracles like human judgments or experiments are costly.

entry.title: Learning to Couple: Context-Adaptive Joint Denoising for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zilei Shao, Ian Li, Heng Zhao, Kewei Lian, Guy Van den Broeck, Zhe Zeng, Anji Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Codpula, a context-parameterized denoiser for diffusion language models that jointly models dependencies among parallel-predicted tokens instead of treating them as conditionally independent. A Transformer with a tractable probabilistic inference layer produces context-specific coupling over token potentials, addressing the root cause of factorized denoising errors.

entry.title: Maestro: Agentic Formal Proof Development by Coordination

author.name: Haoyu Li, Zeren Shui, Yuhao Zhang, Ferhat Erata, Benjamin Mikek, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: Maestro is an agentic system for Lean formal proof development that coordinates revising flawed proof plans rather than recursively decomposing stubborn lemmas. It distinguishes why a lemma resists proof (bad guidance, false statement, or flawed decomposition) and revises the plan above the failing node, addressing a key failure mode of divide-and-conquer provers.

entry.title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds

author.name: Snir Hordan, Harm Derksen, Mircea Petrache, Nadav Dym

entry.summary: The paper establishes the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations, and derives the first explicit quadratic bound on the representation order needed for Tensor Field Networks and MACE to express all invariant polynomials of a given degree.

entry.title: When Do Repetition Loops Lock? Truncation Sampling, Bounded Penalties, and a Blind Spot in DRY

author.name: Yichuan Chen, Xin Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the exit dynamics of verbatim repetition loops in language model generation, showing loop survival under any sampler can be computed exactly from one forward pass since context is deterministic along the loop. It proves pure sampling always leaves positive escape probability, top-p with threshold above 1/2 can lock positions, and penalties that outgrow model preference guarantee escape. The analysis predicts a previously unnoticed blind spot in the widely deployed DRY sampler's sequence-based penalty.

entry.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Xiyue Zhang, Keru Zhou, Ziyi Wang, Bing Hu, Li Wang

entry.summary: TempoMoE finds that fast and slow chain-of-thought reasoning in multimodal Mixture-of-Experts models exhibit distinct, stable expert-routing patterns that can be causally manipulated: suppressing slow-thinking experts shortens reasoning chains while suppressing fast-thinking experts lengthens them. It leverages this to steer reasoning depth at inference, reducing token cost and latency on easy inputs without external control or retraining the reasoning mechanism.

entry.title: Do Conversational Agents Need Explicit Memory? A Controlled Comparison with Raw-History Retrieval

author.name: Yongjie Zhou, Shuai Wang, Bevan Koopman, Guido Zuccon

entry.summary: Compares six state-of-the-art explicit memory systems for conversational agents against simple raw-history RAG on LongMemEval-S and BEAM-100K under controlled retrieval settings, finding only localized gains and no consistent advantage. Oracle experiments reveal that some systems lose answer-supporting information during memory construction.

entry.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Rubin Wei, Siyuan Sun, Hao Sun, Yuliang Liu, Xiang Shi, Jiarui Wang, Junming Zhang, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Deep Fusion Memory is a parametric memory architecture that injects retrieved knowledge into intermediate hidden states rather than interpolating at output level, using a causal memory predictor trained on chunk embeddings from the corpus as supervision. It aims to avoid catastrophic forgetting of continued pretraining and the overhead of online retrieval.

entry.title: FisherEdit: Fisher Information Guided Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models

author.name: Yizhou Yang, Jiahong Fu, Zhiwu Wang, Kailong Fan, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Zhenan Sun, Renzhen Wang, Deyu Meng

entry.summary: Revisits projection-based sequential knowledge editing methods like AlphaEdit and finds their robustness stems mainly from update regularization rather than null-space projection. Building on this insight, FisherEdit replaces coarse activation-space projections with Fisher-geometry importance-aware regularization in parameter space, admits an efficient row-wise closed-form solution, and reduces cumulative capability degradation.

entry.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Xingyu Shen, Yingfa Chen, Ziqing Qiao, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: Reveals a competing learning phenomenon in hybrid architectures combining linear recurrence and softmax attention, where different mixer types compete to learn the same function and whichever learns first suppresses the other's learning signal. Attribution analysis shows modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster, causing attention to undertrain on retrieval.

entry.title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback

author.name: Zhicheng Fang, Han Sun, Jiachen Lei, Xinyi Fang, Zongmin Zhang, Chenxu Fu, Sizhe Fang, Wei Xu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes budgeted attack scheduling for LLM red-teaming: prioritizing which jailbreak attacks from a large library to run under limited attempt budgets, since effectiveness varies across victim-defense settings. It studies how static priors, semantic guidance, and online feedback contribute to efficient robustness evaluation, avoiding exhaustive and costly attack-library evaluation.

entry.title: LVMH: A Meta-Optimization Harness for Long-Video Agent Memory

author.name: Liwei Che, Benlin Liu, Dai Li, Xiangyan Li, Zijian Wu, Changjiang Li, Minghao Guo, Chengzhi Mao, Vladimir Pavlovic, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: LVMH formulates memory-policy design for long-video agents as multi-objective code search around a fixed answer model, with independent review and protected observation boundaries guarding against self-certification and development-set overfitting. Persistent meta-memory records past proposals, traces, and costs, enabling automated joint optimization of memory performance and efficiency under token and latency budgets.

entry.title: Pretrained Features as Teachers, Not States: Compact Latent World Models for Visual Planning

author.name: Yanbo Wang, Nan Lin, Wendelin B\"ohmer, Javier Alonso-Mora

entry.summary: Anchor-WM proposes using pretrained visual features as a distillation teacher for learning a compact action-conditioned latent state, rather than treating frozen pretrained features as the world-model state itself. This avoids both the collapse risk of pure latent-prediction objectives and the rigidity of planning in a frozen state space, targeting visual planning tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Geometric Closure: Measuring and Diagnosing Mechanical Consistency in Visual Dynamics

author.name: Qibin Gu, Yunfeng Yan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for measuring whether predicted visual dynamics obey physical mechanics, decomposing performance into geometric admissibility, reaction-free actuator effort, and work-energy balance via an independent physics audit of rigid closed chains. Evaluations across hundreds of planar assemblies and multiple video prediction models show that models reducing image MSE still fail to attain valid native geometry.

entry.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling

author.name: Kien T. Pham, Yuhao Liu, Chong Hou Choi, Zhenqi He, Yanghao Wang, Chenyang Lei, Rui Liu, Qifeng Chen, Long Chen

entry.summary: Proposes UniAVC, a single model for text-conditioned joint audio-video synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing. It reduces dependence on scarce paired corpora through progressive training that exploits abundant unimodal data, and introduces modality-specific noise schedules reflecting the differing information density of audio and video.

entry.title: LEAP: Accelerating ODE-based Diffusion Sampling with Optimal Linear Leaps

author.name: Haowei Zheng, Zhenyu Zhou, Jiawei Chen, Can Wang, Defang Chen

entry.summary: LEAP is a training-free method for accelerating ODE-based diffusion sampling that formulates a supervised least-squares optimization within the local trajectory subspace, exploiting low dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency to approximate future states without extra model evaluations. Experiments show it outperforms prior methods across text-to-image models like Stable Diffusion 3.5 and FLUX.1-dev and other modalities.

entry.title: AVTime: Reinforcing Dense Audio-Visual Captions with Bidirectional Alignment

author.name: Mingyang Wu, Kaituo Feng, Bohao Li, Kaixiong Gong, Zihao Yin, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: AVTime contributes AVTime-50K, a 50K-sample dataset of temporally precise dense audio-visual captions on longer videos, plus a model trained with a Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment reward that avoids checklist-dependent RL. It also introduces a benchmark that jointly evaluates event semantics and temporal accuracy in both directions.

entry.title: From Cause to Effect: Generating Intermediate Event Chains in Videos

author.name: Ridouane Ghermi, Vicky Kalogeiton, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: This paper introduces Causal Chain Generation (CCG), a new task requiring video-language models to generate the sequence of intermediate events connecting a cause and an effect, with two automatic metrics: SODA-Embedding for semantic matching and Causal-QA for probing causal coherence. This addresses flawed multiple-choice QA evaluations that permit shortcuts in causal video reasoning. Authors include well-known video understanding researchers (Kalogeiton, Laptev).

entry.title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding

author.name: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Bokang Yang, Jiaxu Wang, Xiaolou Sun, Mingxing Wen, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Unisense is a unified embodied MLLM framework supporting diverse physical sensory modalities beyond basic vision and audio, using a two-stage design that connects heterogeneous sensor representations to a shared multimodal architecture with high-level reasoning. It addresses the problem that physical-environment modalities are weakly coupled to MLLM representations and vary in structure and statistics. Extending MLLMs to rich embodied sensing is important for robotics and agents.

entry.title: Dependency, Compression, and Synergy: A Unified Information-Theoretic View of Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liangjian Wen, Linjie Li, Jiang Duan, Yong Dai, Jianzhuang Liu, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: This survey unifies Mutual Information, the Information Bottleneck, and Partial Information Decomposition as progressively refined views of multimodal information processing: MI captures inter-modal dependency, IB covers task-oriented compression, and PID decomposes information into redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy. It reviews 170 studies from 2018-2026 and connects these tools into a coherent framework. Such theoretical unification can guide multimodal model design and analysis.

entry.title: EvoAD: Self-Evolving Autonomous Driving via Latent World-Model Guided Post-hoc Reflection

author.name: Junjie Yang, Qiming Zhang, Yuyan Li, Shuqi Shen, Yusong Huang, Yanggang Sheng, Wenpeng Xu, Ziyi Shi, Tianshun Li, Yijie Chen, Yujia Wang, Jun Ma, Xinhu Zheng, Hongliang Lu, Hai Yang

entry.summary: Proposes EvoAD, a framework enabling end-to-end driving systems to self-evolve after deployment by storing driving experiences in bird's-eye-view latent memory and using a latent world model to guide post-hoc reflection on failures. This contrasts with frozen deployed policies that require costly retraining to fix recurring mistakes. It targets lifelong improvement analogous to human drivers.

entry.title: ESCAPE: Egocentric Sensing for Collision Avoidance and Policy Execution

author.name: Weiqing Shen, Wenhao Huang, Baokang Zhang, Shuo Shang, Yanmiao Hu, Haojun Li, Yifan Han, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: Proposes ESCAPE, an egocentric motion-planning framework that aggregates sparse measurements from distributed onboard depth sensors into obstacle-aware point clouds, trained on over 100K safety-critical trajectories with a flow-matching generative policy jointly optimizing goal reaching and collision avoidance. This avoids blind spots and fragility of external-camera visuomotor policies. A significant step toward deployable collision-free trajectory generation in cluttered environments.

entry.title: Gen2Dex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Simulation-Initialized Generated Video Demonstrations

author.name: Xiaowen Qiu, Yian Wang, Haoxiang You, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: Gen2Dex presents an end-to-end framework converting simulation-grounded generated videos into physically executable dexterous robot demonstrations, exploiting known scene geometry, articulation, and camera parameters while correcting geometric distortions and contact inconsistencies in generated video. This enables learning dexterous manipulation from video demonstrations without costly real data collection.

entry.title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy

author.name: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Tianchun Wu, Zhiqing Tang, Hanlin Zhao, Siu Hing Lui, Tao Yang, Jingsong Lin, Huxin Gao, Yeung Trevor, Raymond Tang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EndoVLA-OOV is a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for robotic endoscopy that reacquires previously seen suspicious regions that have moved out of view, adapting a pretrained backbone to two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands using initial, intermediate, and current images. The authors also release an open-source VLA dataset of 1,050 episodes across six tasks, supporting policy learning for this clinically relevant scan-then-revisit workflow.

entry.title: AeroDASH: Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control for Continuous UAV Flight

author.name: Zhe Liu, Yuxuan Zheng, Jinzhe Qin, Ziqi Gao, Boyu Zhou

entry.summary: AeroDASH tackles the latency mismatch between VLA policy predictions and ongoing UAV motion with an asynchronous framework: a B-spline policy fine-tuned on expert data provides continuous trajectory references, and trajectory fusion stitches expired prediction prefixes to active references with derivative continuity. Execution-aware GRPO further trains the policy to account for asynchronous execution deviations, enabling continuous language-conditioned flight.

entry.title: Revealing and Bridging the Physical Executability Gap in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Gang He, Zhile Cheng, Kepeng Xu, Zhenyang Liu, Yu-Wing Tai

entry.summary: This paper identifies a physical executability gap in continuous vision-and-language navigation: permissive simulator contact models can mask physically infeasible actions, so goal-reaching success overstates embodied competence. The proposed VeSTA framework aligns VLN policies with trajectories that are semantically valid, geometrically feasible, and physically robust.

entry.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models

author.name: Shengbang Liu, Zhengye Du, Zhilong Wan, Honghao Su, Chenxiang Xia, Chang Ge, Jinyang Xiao, Nan Wang, Zhipeng Hu, Huining Yuan, Shu'ang Yu, Yue Chen, Tianxing Chen, Chuankang Li, Maoqing Yao, Wenbo Ding, Yu Wang, Guanghui Ren, Chao Yu

entry.summary: RoboValue is a sim-and-real benchmark for evaluating robotic value models that provide feedback for policy learning and execution monitoring. It assesses four capability dimensions: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure and recovery reasoning, and value consistency, using diagnostic trajectories and instruction variations.

entry.title: Causal Robustness from Synthetic Environments

author.name: Linying Yang, Cyrill Scheidegger, Xinwei Shen, Peter B\"uhlmann

entry.summary: The paper shows that under a structural additive-noise mechanism, both an invariant prediction function and the perturbations it is robust against can be recovered from a single observational distribution. Synthetic environments are generated by reweighting the covariate distribution, with a Cramer-von Mises criterion measuring departures from constant conditional MSE invariance, from an authoritative causal inference group (Buhlmann and colleagues).

entry.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse

author.name: Sicheng He, Yi Pan, Qiuting Yu, Jiaming Huang, Qi Lu, Shuyan Wu, Hongyan Feng, Xuanyu Liu, Jun Zhang, Jie Zhang, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: Observes that flow-matching vision-language-action models discard unexecuted action tails when replanning, and shows these tails retain transferable denoising progress that can replace full re-denoising with fewer steps. VLA-Rolling adaptively adjusts the denoising budget per sample based on how much the environment has changed.

entry.title: ToolOPD: Credit-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Chu Zhao, Lei Tang, Yanming Wang, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo, Zhengzong Chen, Yuanyuan Zhao, Fei Huang

entry.summary: ToolOPD improves on-policy distillation for small tool-use agents by replacing the uniform-credit assumption with credit-aware supervision. Through credit-distribution analysis and outcome-reversal counterfactuals, the authors show trajectory credit concentrates on a few critical actions and that reversing final outcomes changes credit across turns. The method concentrates dense token-level teacher supervision on high-credit actions in student-generated trajectories.

entry.title: Not Every Rollout Needs Distillation: Correctness-Filtered On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Harrison Zhao, Lei Huang, Fei Liu, Wen Shi, Zijian Jin

entry.summary: Analyzing on-policy self-distillation, the authors show via gradient measurements on Qwen3-1.7B that incorrect responses carry roughly three times the coherent gradient share of correct ones with largely overlapping population-mean directions, motivating C-OPSD, which filters rollouts by correctness to cut distillation cost while retaining supervision quality. A signal-noise model fitted at small group size predicts alignment at larger sizes without refitting.

entry.title: LLM Evolution in a Simple Simulated Market

author.name: Charlie Pilgrim, Christopher Krupenye, Dora Biro, Richard P. Mann

entry.summary: Populations of twenty LLM agents solve arithmetic problems in simulated markets where bankrupt agents are replaced by mutated copies of successful prompts. Accuracy-rewarding markets yield high-accuracy, high-token agents, while per-token-charging markets produce low-accuracy, low-token agents, demonstrating concrete evolutionary selection pressures on LLM behavior.

entry.title: Tensor Network Datamodels for Training Data Attribution

author.name: Farzaneh Heidari, Md Rifat Arefin, Louis Jaburi, Guillaume Rabusseau

entry.summary: Introduces Tensor Network Datamodels (TNDMs), which use low-rank tensor networks to extend linear datamodels for training data attribution so they can represent non-additive interactions such as complementary and redundant training groups. The paper proves these interactions induce high-degree subset functions with compact low-rank representations, enabling reuse of a single fitted model across queries.

entry.title: Reasoning-Aware Multicalibrated Reliability Predictors for Language Models

author.name: Ekaterina Fedorova, Alessandro Morosini, Chara Podimata

entry.summary: The paper introduces reasoning-aware multicalibration, extending hallucination reliability prediction beyond topic-based groups by adding groups derived from chain-of-thought properties, since responses with different CoT characteristics can exhibit opposing errors that cancel within a topic and confidence level. This yields per-response reliability estimates that are meaningful across finer, application-relevant groups. It improves how providers can communicate trustworthiness of individual LLM responses.

entry.title: UltraData-Code: From Raw Repositories to Algorithmically Dense and Task-Oriented Code Data

author.name: Chengying Tu, Hengyu Zhao, Shuaikang Xue, Zhongming Qu, Jihao Zhou, Xinle Lin, Junshao Guo, Zixuan Fu, Qiang Ma, Jie Zhou, Chaojun Xiao, Hongfei Yan, Yudong Wang, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Presents a tiered data management framework for code pretraining data, defining four states from L0 repository archival with provenance, through L1 scalable filtering/normalization, L2 algorithmic selection, to L3 task-oriented synthesis. This produces data suited to different training objectives as high-quality public code becomes scarcer. From a strong Tsinghua-affiliated team (Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun group).

entry.title: PACT: NVFP4 Data-Flow LoRA Fine-Tuning on Consumer GPUs

author.name: Lei Gao, Hossein Entezari Zarch, Chaoyi Jiang, Murali Annavaram

entry.summary: PACT is a LoRA fine-tuning system that accelerates frozen projections using native NVFP4 GEMMs while reducing quantization overhead and error. It cuts activation memory by reusing quantized RMSNorm outputs and storing gate/up activations in NVFP4 for backward, keeping BF16 inputs for nonlinearities and calibrating frozen weights offline with GPTQ adapted to NVFP4 scales. The goal is practical fine-tuning of language models on consumer hardware.

entry.title: Text Dominance in Paralinguistic Conflict: Tracing Suppression Through Audio LLM Circuits

author.name: Ankur Banerjee, Vishnu Guntakala, Danity Pike, Advay Roongta, Kevin Yang, Ruizhe Li

entry.summary: This paper tests whether audio LLMs actually use acoustic cues rather than just transcripts in conflict-relevant settings like crisis hotlines, finding a mean text-dominance rate of 0.78 on mismatched text-plus-audio items across six models. Probing shows speaker identity remains linearly decodable at the language model input in the most text-dominant model, indicating the failure is not perceptual, and back-patching, previously reported to fix lexical dominance, has no measurable effect. The work reveals a systematic multimodal integration failure and challenges an existing proposed fix.

entry.title: Is it RL or Data? A Controlled Comparison of GRPO and Rejection-Sampling Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lakshya Chaudhry

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether a reported 5x sample-efficiency benefit of mixed-difficulty prompts in GRPO is specific to RL or available to any post-training method, comparing GRPO against rejection-sampling fine-tuning on the same prompts, verifier, and token cap using Qwen3-4B-Base with LoRA. A six-arm experimental design with pre-registered hypotheses separates the effect of the algorithm from the data.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Memories: Low-Overhead Language Modeling with Modular Knowledge Injection

author.name: Yifan Lu, Rubin Wei, Ziyun Zou, Junhong Liang, Haolin Yang, Xinlin Zhuang, Abhijit Das, Adinath Madhavrao Dukre, Shadab Khan, Zhouhan Lin, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: Mixture-of-Memories combines a frozen base LM with two neural memory experts, a latent memory providing hidden-state corrections and a lexical memory providing a token-space knowledge path, separating routed neural memory from writable factual memory. This applies differently shaped corrections to tokens with different knowledge demands, at low overhead.

entry.title: Risk Decomposition for Hallucination-Aware Video Sampling

author.name: Chenyan Zheng, Fan Wu, Ruibo Li, Jiaxing Li, Minghao Yang, Bang Zhang, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-dimensional risk framework for physical hallucinations in video generation, decomposing them into low-density sampling risk (unlikely generations, e.g., teleporting objects) and high-density drifting risk (physically inconsistent but high-likelihood outputs, e.g., energy-gaining bounces). This unified lens explains the roles and limitations of existing mitigation signals.

entry.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels

author.name: Chan Yan Ki, Yanran Zhang, Wenzhao Zheng, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Lei Chen, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: Stateful Harness separates world evolution from video rendering: it maintains an explicit evolving world state under user-specified rules, renders each event with a frozen video model, and feeds generated clips back to update state. This supports stateful, rule-governed interaction where outcomes depend on invisible state, going beyond camera-movement world models. The decoupling of simulation logic from rendering is a conceptually important direction for world models.

entry.title: PrismPlan: A Shared GPU Substrate for Motion Planning Across Paradigms

author.name: Hong Wu, ChaoXuan Liu, ShuJie Wang

entry.summary: Builds PrismPlan, a shared GPU substrate of batched collision-detection and forward-kinematics device code consumed by sampling, search, and optimization planners alike. By holding the backend fixed by construction, it enables the first fair head-to-head comparison of GPU-accelerated planning paradigms, which previously conflated planner and collision-checker differences. Six planners are evaluated on this common foundation.

entry.title: LIBERO-Dynamic: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Shaojie Ren, Jingwen Sun, Zezhi Liu, Hongjin Chen, Xin Jin, Wei Zou, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: LIBERO-Dynamic extends all 40 LIBERO manipulation tasks with moving objects driven along three trajectory families and speed tiers, while advancing the physical world according to calibrated model-specific inference latency. It also provides 9,000 quality-filtered dynamic trajectories for training and evaluates multiple policies, exposing the effect of stale observations on action execution.

entry.title: Vector-Quantized World Model: Latent Feedback Motion Planning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xuezhou Xu, Chung-Pang Wang, Zhenzhen Li, Benjamin Riviere

entry.summary: VQ-WM combines discrete long-horizon search with continuous visual feedback control for manipulation planning: a discrete latent predictor over vector-quantized states allows the planner to search for shortest paths to the goal over long horizons, while a learned continuous controller sequentially reaches planned states with visual feedback that corrects deviations. This addresses compounding prediction errors and unreachable latent plans in visual world models.

entry.title: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices

author.name: Ritvik Garimella, Biplav Srivastava, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests when agentic AI is actually preferable to established integration alternatives such as local computation, REST, SOAP, and MCP, comparing seven methods on 1,000 arithmetic expressions across development speed, performance, and cost. It pushes back on agentic hype by quantifying where agents are slower and costlier than simpler architectures.

entry.title: Training-Free Prompt Selection for Efficient Reinforcement Learning With Partial Rollouts

author.name: Lei Jiang, Honghui Bao, Yue Zhou, Zhengyao Gu, Langzhou He, Natalie Parde

entry.summary: The paper introduces LIFT, a training-free data selector for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that identifies high-value prompts using only partial reasoning rollouts rather than complete ones. It addresses the practical issue that 26-32% of full greedy rollouts fail to terminate within the generation budget, making efficient selection important for reducing RLVR training cost.

entry.title: CME-SpectrumBench: Can LLMs Analyze Condensed Matter Spectral Data?

author.name: Jin Gene Wong, Anjney Midha, Joseph Mathew Tennyson, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Zhi-Xun Shen

entry.summary: This paper introduces CME-SpectrumBench, an expert-designed benchmark of 190 questions testing whether frontier LLMs can analyze research-level spectral data from condensed matter experiments. Models must identify structures from noisy 2D intensity arrays under limited instrumental resolution, complementing existing theory-focused benchmarks. It matters because experimental data-analysis capability is essential for future domain-specific scientific foundation models.

entry.title: Beyond Next-Screen Prediction: The Decision Value of GUI World Models

author.name: Sizhe Tang, Hanhan Zhou, Jeffrey Svajlenko, Rashmi Gangadharaiah

entry.summary: This paper examines how much of the performance gain from GUI world models in agent action selection actually comes from predicting future screens versus from the evaluator that interprets those predictions. Through controlled interventions with candidates and predictions held fixed, the authors show that lookahead gains can shift depending on how predictions are presented, meaning end-to-end gains cannot be credited to prediction alone. They then propose Direct Action Ranking (DAR), which learns to score candidate actions from reference actions without generating future screens, and compare it to prediction-augmented variants under matched supervision.

entry.title: Neuro-Inspired Inhibitory Message Passing for Accurate and Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Nima H. Siboni, Magdalena Springer, Vahid Rostami

entry.summary: Inspired by cortical inhibitory circuits, the authors propose inhibitory message passing, a training-free communication router for multi-agent LLM systems that cancels redundant evidence per sentence while preserving rare, decisive evidence. This keeps crucial information visible in agent contexts as messages accumulate, improving accuracy and token efficiency.

entry.title: Means-Ends Analysis Helps LLMs Plan in Continuous-State Domains

author.name: Jiayi Li, Carl Kingsford

entry.summary: Develops Medaka, a prompting framework based on Newell and Simon's Means-Ends Analysis that enables LLM planning in continuous-state domains where actions cannot be enumerated, via recursive goal decomposition, algebraic derivation, and per-step state tracking. This extends LLM planning research beyond the discrete-action settings that dominate the field.

entry.title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix

author.name: Parsa Razmara, Seyedarmin Azizi, Ardalan Aryashad

entry.summary: This paper introduces SkillClash, a benchmark of 16 pairs of conflicting same-job agent skill files, and measures how models behave when both are loaded into context. Across seven models from 4B to large frontier-scale systems, rule compliance drops from 93-99% with a single skill to 61-62% with two competing skills, with most failures showing one skill taking over entirely. The authors also propose a lightweight one-file mitigation.

entry.title: Auditing Tool Traces in Agentic LLMs: Source Localization and Counterfactual Dependence Testing

author.name: Junhao Liu, Tianxiao Li, Yongxian Wu, Ziheng Duan, Ren Li, Jing Zhang, Martin Renqiang Min

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage audit for agentic LLMs in scientific prediction: Per-Tool TF-IDF Decomposition localizes label-predictive shortcut patterns to individual tool results, and Token-Class Redaction counterfactually tests whether a frozen LLM actually depends on the localized patterns. This targets hidden label shortcuts in serialized tool outputs, such as dataset identifiers, that create apparent success without genuine reasoning. It offers a practical audit methodology for evidence-grounded agents.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Units, Flat Decisions: Hierarchical Micro-Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Zukang Xu, Xinpei Gao, Xing Hu, Zhe Jiang, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes UC-RAMP, a two-stage post-training pruning framework for mixture-of-experts models that separates capacity allocation across experts (CAPE) from channel selection within experts (RAMP). It shows that finer pruning granularity alone does not preserve task capability, since similar perplexity can hide large task-performance differences.

entry.title: A Cue's Hidden Price: Auditing Seller Influence on AI Shoppers

author.name: Felix Buecheler, Gerardo Berbeglia, Mingyu Guo

entry.summary: The paper introduces price-equivalent (PE) auditing, which quantifies seller-controlled cues (badges, endorsements, framing) in LLM shopping agents by raising the cued product's price until choice rates equalize, avoiding the ceiling effect of choice-rate measures. This addresses a core generative engine optimization question: not whether seller content shifts agent choices, but by how much.

entry.title: Understanding When Reflective Prompt and Skill Optimization Helps on Locally Served Reasoning Models: A Two-Model Study of GEPA and SkillOpt

author.name: Andrea Giummarra, Carmelo Baglieri, Antonio Di Maria, Andrea Farruggio, Michele Piatto, Giovanni Micale

entry.summary: Replicates reflective prompt/skill optimizers GEPA and SkillOpt on locally served DeepSeek V4 Flash and Qwen3.8-27B, finding mixed results: one SkillOpt validation gain reversed into held-out degradation, while GEPA improved MATH-500 exact match from 0.828 to 0.904 yet sometimes reproduced baseline behavior exactly. The study probes when text-space optimizers actually transfer.

entry.title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Arjun Ashok, Mihir Parmar, Palash Goyal, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Chun-Liang Li, Irina Rish, Alexandre Drouin, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: A semi-synthetic benchmark measuring whether time series foundation models can reliably use covariates for scenario analysis, i.e., forecasting a target's response to future interventions. Tasks come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks with controlled covariate-target relationships.

entry.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy

author.name: Ke Zhang, Sahchit Chundur, Jerry Peprah Owusu, Mohammad Javad Abdolhosseini Qomi, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: Using the deterministic PHREEQC geochemistry simulator, the study traces how offloading long tool outputs to files costs LLM agents accuracy: GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 (both existing models) lose 11.3 and 7.9 accuracy points when reading reports via a section index rather than in context, while Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 show no detectable cost. All 11,007 logged simulations are rerun for verification.

entry.title: Latent Multimodal Memory Reasoning

author.name: Cai Ke, Xinghao Chen, Yuanchen Bei, Yuni Lai, Keyu Chen, Ruizhi Qiao, Siyu An, Junnan Dong, Ruifeng Xu, Xing Sun

entry.summary: LMMR is a neuro-symbolic framework that organizes long-term multimodal memory for personalized agents in a continuous latent space rather than compressing images to text, enabling cross-session and cross-modal reasoning. It targets problems of premature visual compression and temporally stale observations in long-horizon agent memory.

entry.title: ReTTT: Reflection-Driven Test-Time Training via Experience-Based Parametric Memory

author.name: Kangcong Li, Hangfan Zhang, Shuyue Hu, Shengji Tang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: ReTTT enables LLM agents to self-improve during multi-turn task execution by reflecting on interaction feedback, constructing and continually revising lessons, and encoding them via test-time training into parametric memory. This allows experience-driven adaptation within a single episode rather than relying on static retrieval.

entry.title: Encoder-Free Multimodal LLMs Learn Implicit Encoders

author.name: David Harwath, Desh Raj, Xavier Velez, Sandra Arcos-Holzinger, Willie Jeng, Karen Livescu, Leibny Paola Garcia-Perera, Sanjeev Khudanpur

entry.summary: The authors analyze encoder-free multimodal LLMs, including Gemma-4 12B, which consume raw audio samples and image pixels without modality-specific encoders, and find that early layers function as implicit encoders largely invariant to cross-modal context. They further show independent encoding emerges during multimodal reasoning. This is an interpretability contribution to an architecturally important trend of removing dedicated perception frontends.

entry.title: Koi: Evidence-Guided, Self-Calibrating Planning for Multi-Cloud, Heterogeneous LLM Inference Fleets

author.name: Mankeerat Sidhu, Gangmuk Lim, Hetarth Chopra, Maximillian Eisenberg, Quan Hao Ng, Aryan Gosaliya, Shu Liu, Luka Govedi\v{c}, Jiaxin Shan, Hongkuan Zhou, Vikram Sharma Mailthody, P. Brighten Godfrey, Ion Stoica

entry.summary: Koi is a self-calibrating cluster planner for heterogeneous multi-cloud LLM inference fleets, tackling the roughly 140 intertwined deployment variables (accelerator, parallelization, engine configuration, replicas) whose optimal values shift with workload contention. It pairs a Recursive Language Model hierarchy for hypothesis generation with deterministic components that predict serving behavior and control placement via a fixed causal graph. With Ion Stoica among the authors, this targets a real production problem in inference infrastructure.

entry.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement

author.name: Jaeyeon Kim, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Luoyi Zhang, Chan-Jan Hsu, Fernando Ruiloba Portilla, Jinchuan Tian, Shinji Watanabe, Carlos Busso

entry.summary: Introduces Long Listening Thoughts (LLT), a four-stage post-training data construction pipeline for large audio-language models that combines dense multi-aspect audio descriptions with deliberately long reasoning traces, including synthesized incorrect reasoning and a thought-continuation strategy. It targets the finding that LALM failures stem largely from perceptual errors rather than reasoning deficits.

entry.title: ReTrace: Visual Backtracking for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Guangzong Si, Dong Wang, Yifan Yu, Miao Liu, Panwang Pan, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a visual backtracking pattern in MLLMs: visual pivot tokens remain spatially stable but in middle layers retrieve context from early low-saliency tokens, meaning early pruning of such tokens irreversibly deletes information later needed. ReTrace exploits this insight to decouple temporary computational deactivation from permanent information deletion for more efficient visual token handling.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Early Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via E-processes

author.name: Dong-Jae Lee, Gyojin Han, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: This paper reframes adaptive early stopping for reasoning LLMs as sequential evidence accumulation using e-processes rather than threshold calibration on validation data. Two e-processes run on a shared per-chunk signal: a commit stream tracking the signal relative to its slow trend and an abstain stream tracking signed velocity, giving guarantees that survive shifts in test-time horizon where calibrated thresholds fail.

entry.title: Learning When to Abort in Transformer Planning: A Mechanistic Study

author.name: Shi Feng, Qimin Zhong, Siwei Wang, Yifei Shen, Shang-Hua Teng, Hao Liao, Wei Chen

entry.summary: This paper mechanistically studies whether Transformers can learn to recognize their own planning errors by training them to emit an abort token when generating invalid transitions in graph path-finding tasks. It constructs a Transformer with feed-forward width proportional to the graph size that provably detects all invalid transitions, connecting error recognition to improved planning capacity.

entry.title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models

author.name: Seungjong Sun, Hyunmin Jun, Minsik Yoon, Eungu Lee, Choongwon Kang, Young Seok Woo, Jang Hyun Kim

entry.summary: Hypothesizes that post-training instills addressivity, the orientation of outputs toward an addressee, which in turn creates pressure toward sycophancy, and tests this using sparse autoencoders to extract addressivity directions in pre- and post-trained models. It examines how these directions relate to sycophantic behavior and to user identity.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages

author.name: Mohsen Fayyaz, Ali Modarressi, Daniel Israel, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes how diffusion language models dynamically allocate compute, showing that the number of forward passes per generated token varies dramatically by task — copying or light editing is cheap while open-ended generation is expensive, with DiffusionGemma requiring over three times more passes for story writing than grammar correction. The authors identify two output properties (novelty relative to input and word rarity) that largely explain cost variation, with practical implications for cost estimation in diffusion LM deployment.

entry.title: UtilityBench: Measuring Language Model Utility When Errors Have Different Costs

author.name: Qifeng Lei, Zhiyong Yang, Zitai Wang, Shilong Bao, Linchao Zhang, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: UtilityBench is a 15,000-instance benchmark that evaluates language models with a utility-based paradigm where errors carry differentiated, data-driven costs elicited via Best-Worst Scaling, rather than treating all mistakes equally. This better reflects high-stakes deployments like medicine. It challenges mainstream correctness-only evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM Fine-Tuning via Weight Space Reparameterization: Preserving Safety during Downstream Adaptation

author.name: Minseong Kim, Jongbok Won, Jeesup Park, Yonghee Choi, Dongjun Han

entry.summary: WSR-Tune is a weight-space reparameterization framework that preserves safety alignment during downstream fine-tuning by constructing a safety-conditioned basis and reparameterizing weight matrices so updates do not overwrite safety-encoding directions. This addresses the known trade-off between task adaptation and safety degradation that arises because safety information is distributed across many parameter directions. It offers a structural alternative to neuron- or layer-identification approaches.

entry.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development

author.name: Yuchi Wang, Rongyao Fang, Weihao Yu, Xilin Wei, Tiancheng Gu, Dingkang Yang, Hang Zhang, Dayiheng Liu, Hongsheng Li, Shuai Bai

entry.summary: Presents RefCraft, a benchmark of 300 realistic webpage-development tasks where agents must build pages from natural-language instructions plus screenshots of one to five reference webpages, rather than reconstructing a single visual target. This tests a more realistic visual-reference-conditioned agentic workflow. Authors appear affiliated with a major lab (Baidu-related names and a large team).

entry.title: Dynamical Kernel Attention: Estimating the Present from a Record of the Past

author.name: Peter Racioppo

entry.summary: Dynamical Kernel Attention (DKA) reframes self-attention as robust estimation of a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics, so attention weights reflect how much past-state information survives to the present. Unlike recency biases, DKA can abstain when evidence is weak and offers bounded error guarantees under token discard, at the same computational cost as standard attention.

entry.title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark

author.name: Zhichao Deng, Haichuan Tan, Xin Hong, Huaizhi Wang, Tao Huang, Bowen Gao, Yanyan Lan

entry.summary: This paper reformulates reverse target fishing (identifying protein targets for a query molecule) as generative retrieval with GenFish, which uses residual vector quantization of protein language model features as semantic identifiers and autoregressively ranks proteins by likelihood, avoiding the harmful missing-not-at-random negatives of discriminative approaches. It also introduces ProTargetBench, a proteome-scale benchmark for the task. This is a notable methodological and benchmarking contribution for drug discovery and repurposing.

entry.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends

author.name: Yuhua Zheng, Xueyi Chen, Xinze Zou, Xin Li, Haoji Hu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: EdgeKernelBench is the first systematic benchmark for LLM-based GPU kernel generation on edge backends, combining a unified IR deployment framework with a hierarchical benchmark spanning operators to model graphs across heterogeneous edge hardware. This fills a gap since prior LLM kernel-generation work targeted only server GPUs. The benchmark enables measuring code-generation models on a practically important but understudied deployment setting.

entry.title: Block Recursive Transformers for Structured Parameter Sharing

author.name: Josep Marques, Hyunyoung A. Cho, Youngeun Kim, Youjia Zhang, Aecheon Jung, Kyuhong Shim, Sungeun Hong

entry.summary: The paper proposes Block Recursive Transformers (BRT), which partition layers into contiguous blocks that are recursively reused before advancing, sitting between layer-wise repetition and global cyclic weight sharing. This intermediate topology permits local refinement within blocks while preserving depth-wise transitions without extra routing modules. It argues sharing granularity, not just the amount of sharing, determines recursive transformer quality.

entry.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xi Zhu, Yuanlin Duan, Changyi Yang, Kai Mei, Riyang Bao, Shichao Zhu, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: TrackRL is an agentic RL framework where per-skill tracking drives full lifecycle management of skill libraries for LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. It tackles free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding, and the absence of counterfactual evidence that prevent assessing each skill's true contribution. Skills can become redundant, remain valuable scaffolding, or turn harmful as the policy evolves, motivating dynamic curation.

entry.title: Operator-Mismatch Contrastive Learning for World-Relative Trajectory Coherence

author.name: One Octadion, Firmansyah Sundana, Novanto Yudistira

entry.summary: This work identifies a failure mode in world model evaluation called operator-blindness, where a scorer ranks plausible futures well but cannot distinguish trajectories valid under the current world rule from those valid under other latent rules. The authors introduce Operator-Mismatch Contrastive learning using valid-but-wrong-operator trajectories as semantic hard negatives, plus an evaluation protocol that measures world-relative coherence directly. This improves how world models are judged beyond generic plausibility ranking.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning Teaches LLMs Long-Horizon Implicit Reasoning, Up To A Limit

author.name: Jimson Huang, Maxwell Nickell, Ruowang Zhang, Abulhair Saparov

entry.summary: This study examines whether curriculum learning can extend implicit reasoning (single-forward-pass reasoning without chain-of-thought) to longer horizons in LLMs. The authors find curriculum training helps but only up to a limit, with abrupt performance cliffs persisting on very long-horizon tasks even for frontier models.

entry.title: Asynchronous On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Xidong Wu, Qi Qi, Yuqiong Ji, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: This paper introduces AsyncOPSD, a framework for on-policy self-distillation in language models where a single model acts as both teacher and student, decoupling rollout generation from learner updates to improve training throughput. By sharing parameters between teacher and student, it avoids the multi-model coordination overhead of conventional on-policy distillation setups.

entry.title: Bombadil: A Foundation Model for Plant Electrophysiology

author.name: James Kirk, Piotr Bednarski, Filip Twardy, Justin Mast, Lee von Kraus

entry.summary: Bombadil is a foundation model for plant electrophysiology designed to transfer across tasks, species, and environments, addressing the limitation that prior plant stress-prediction models were single-task. This enables scalable plant monitoring applications across agriculture, forestry, and horticulture.

entry.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?

author.name: Ivan Rubachev, Nikita Lazarev, Artem Babenko

entry.summary: This empirical study assembles eight real-world tabular datasets with up to ~10 million training examples to characterize how GBDTs, MLPs, and tabular foundation models scale with training data under natural distribution shifts. It finds broadly similar scaling for GBDTs and MLPs, while recent tabular foundation models benefit more consistently from larger contexts. It fills an under-explored large-scale niche in tabular ML evaluation.

entry.title: ToolRosetta: Surface-Form Invariance of Tool-Call Guards

author.name: Hasan Demirkiran, Jens Ernstberger

entry.summary: ToolRosetta re-renders candidate agent actions (JSON tool calls) as Python calls, shell commands, and rationale-stripped forms while preserving semantics, to test whether safety guards for tool-using agents are invariant to surface form. Across eleven guards on AgentDojo and AgentHarm splits, frontier guards are stable (error shifts under 3.4 points) but four of five specialized agent guards degrade, exposing a real robustness gap.

entry.title: Private Evaluation of High-Dimensional Functions

author.name: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Adam Smith

entry.summary: This paper studies differentially private black-box evaluation of high-dimensional functions with unknown or unbounded sensitivity, where the evaluator can only query f on subsets obtained by removing bounded numbers of elements from the dataset. The authors design generic evaluators for pure and approximate DP via a reduction to high-dimensional private quasi-concave optimization. This connects privacy-preserving model evaluation with private convex-style optimization theory.

entry.title: No Escape from the Quadratic Barrier: Adaptive Attacks on Linear $\ell_2$ Sketches

author.name: Edith Cohen, Uri Stemmer

entry.summary: The paper resolves an open question about the resilience of linear sketches, such as Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms, against adaptive black-box queries. The authors construct attacks showing that the known privacy-based quadratic guarantee of roughly k-squared queries is optimal up to logarithmic factors, even against a computationally unbounded responder with full knowledge of the sketching matrix and attack algorithm.

entry.title: Internalizing Chain-of-thought into Looped Transformers

author.name: Kehang Zhou, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: This theory paper constructs looped transformers that interpolate between explicit chain-of-thought generation and latent recurrent computation, simulating time-t, space-s Turing machines with context window O(s/L) and O(t s^(1/k)/L) generated tokens for loop count L. This shows looped recurrence can internalize CoT, reducing both context length and generated token counts by a factor of L.

entry.title: ForagerSim: Evaluating Embodied Map-Based Reasoning in Large-Scale Dynamic Worlds

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Musil, Martin Kot\'ik, Michal Vavre\v{c}ka, Karla \v{S}t\v{e}p\'anov\'a, Sebastian Scherer, Martin Saska

entry.summary: ForagerSim is an interdisciplinary benchmark and research platform for embodied AI agents that must build and use cognitive-map-like representations in large, dynamic 3D environments, inspired by how animals perform map-based navigation. It fills a gap in existing embodied benchmarks, which rarely require explicit map-based reasoning over spatial and task spaces.

entry.title: PV-Decoding: Progressive Verification Decoding with Decode Gating for Diffusion Language Models
