It addresses the gap where the action causing a defect, its symptom, and the state needing repair diverge.

entry.title: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Yong Liang Goh, Song Guo, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Diagnoses why LLM agents in multi-turn RL get stuck in loops of invalid or repetitive high-confidence actions, attributing this to mismatches between the agent's internal state representation and environment dynamics. Proposes methods to encourage productive state-space exploration for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Selective Transfer through Sequence Distillation: From Benchmark Knowledge to Backdoor Behaviour

author.name: Jonibek Mansurov, Sholpan Bolatzhanova, Filbert Aurelian Tjiaranta, Vallerie Alexandara Putra, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: The paper studies which teacher properties survive distillation, comparing benchmark knowledge and refusal backdoors across four distillation channels. Benchmark knowledge transfers reliably through all channels, including students trained only on teacher-generated number sequences with no natural language, while refusal backdoors do not transfer the same way. This reveals that distillation selectively transmits different kinds of hidden model properties.

entry.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhen Li, Mingfa Feng, Yiming Zhang, Yang Yu, Changhai Zhou, Pengxiang Li, Dongkuan Wu, Congkai Xie, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: miniTE shows that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient for consistent policy evaluation across separate training and sampling engines in native 4-bit RL for LLMs, and provides execution diagnostics plus cross-engine numerical alignment with native W4A4 GEMM. It improves consistency without altering the RL objective.

entry.title: Unbounded Losses, Unchecked Inputs: Measuring the Safeguards of LLM Options-Trading Agents

author.name: Mengxiao Wang, Nitesh Saxena

entry.summary: This is the first measurement of safeguards in real deployed LLM options-trading agents, screening 765 GitHub repositories and broker documentation to score 26 systems including all broker-native interfaces by enforced safeguards and worst-case loss of documented order paths. It moves beyond academic equities decision-flipping attacks to financial harm potential in shipped systems. The findings expose significant real-world risk in an unregulated agent ecosystem.

entry.title: UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop

author.name: Tieyuan Chen, Huabin Liu, Yingtao Zhang, Shijie Li, Tengyu Pan, Weiyao Lin, Jianguo Li

entry.summary: UpLoop is a post-training recipe that upcycles pretrained non-looped LLMs into looped (recurrent-depth) models by looping each selected layer locally, preserving the pretrained depth hierarchy, with hidden-wise gates on attention and MLP residual branches so later loops act as progressive refinements. This avoids the expense of pretraining looped models from scratch and reportedly breaks a commonly observed failure pattern.

entry.title: CHSM8: A Chess Transformer that Follows Natural-Language Style Prompts

author.name: Ilia Badanin

entry.summary: CHSM8 is a 210M-parameter chess Transformer trained without search on 1.07B Lichess games that reaches 1837 Elo against strength-limited Stockfish and beats larger search-free public models. It is then fine-tuned on synthetic data generated with Gemma-4-31B (an existing model) to follow free-text style prompts such as requesting a specific opening or playing style.

entry.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation

author.name: Yanjin He, Cuifeng Shen, Wanzhou Lei, Maohua Li, Tao Lan, Kan Liu, Hanlin Tang, Qing Qu

entry.summary: Introduces Swift, a training method in which a frozen weak denoiser (e.g., an early checkpoint) guides a stronger diffusion model by extrapolating the regression target away from the weak prediction, amplifying underfit components at no extra inference cost. The weak guide requires no backpropagation during training and is discarded afterward, preserving the original sampler and conditional/unconditional modes.

entry.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction

author.name: Moritz Wagner, Christophe Roux, Max Zimmer, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: KV-Surgeon addresses offline KV-cache compaction by accounting for the nonlinear coupling that softmax attention creates between deletion decisions, using calibration data and a tractable quadratic surrogate with closed-form solutions. Existing methods score candidates independently, ignoring these interactions. This could improve long-context serving efficiency where a fixed context is queried repeatedly.

entry.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing

author.name: Jianqiang Xia, Han Xu, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: The paper identifies Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence in rubric-based RL, where as total rubric score rises, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, indicating the policy sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregate. The authors diagnose dimension imbalance and dimension absence, then propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation, which makes generations compete within each dimension separately. This mitigates rubric hacking and improves training robustness.

entry.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory

author.name: Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun, Di Wu, Sibo Peng, Mingyang Zhang, Zhen Yang, Ruiyi Zhang, Nanyun Peng, Zhe Gan, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness with a capability layer for tool interfaces plus persistent multimodal memory, motivated by a controlled study over 22 benchmarks showing that larger inference budgets alone give only modest gains. It enables grounded perception, external knowledge access, and interpretable tool outputs retained across reasoning steps. A systems contribution for visual agentic tool use.

entry.title: Muon Operates Beyond the Edge of Stability

author.name: Niko Covic, Baraq Lipshitz, Alexander Padula, Stefan Visnjic

entry.summary: This study provides the first empirical evidence that the Flat Minima Hypothesis extends to the Muon optimizer, showing sharpness strongly correlates with generalization gap on CIFAR-10 within each optimizer family. Notably, Muon operates stably above the sharpness-based Adaptive Edge of Stability threshold that bounds diagonally-preconditioned optimizers like Adam, suggesting it occupies a fundamentally different optimization regime.

entry.title: The Certification Exponent: Instance-Optimal Sequential Certification of Policy Improvement from History Dependent Logs

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper addresses how many logged episodes are needed to certify that a new policy improves on a deployed one when the logging policy is history-dependent. It characterizes the answer via an exponent K-star, the smallest KL divergence to a non-improving law matching logged action probabilities, proving any sound certifier needs at least log(1/delta)/K-star episodes and that a plug-in Kelly certifier attains this rate to first order. This provides instance-optimal guarantees for sequential policy certification from offline data.

entry.title: Uncovering Semantic Hierarchies in Text-Attributed Graphs via Variational EM-based LLM-GNN Synergy

author.name: Yunhui Liu, Xudong Jin, Qizhuo Xie, Chunhui Zhao, Xiao Luo, Tao Zheng, Bin Chong, Tieke He

entry.summary: SHiFT combines LLM reasoning with GNN structural representation in a variational EM framework to learn hierarchical (rather than flat) semantic spaces on text-attributed graphs. The E-step uses LLMs as expert taxonomists to induce a semantic tree with a lightweight Mapping and Diagnosis strategy for cost-efficient hierarchical updates, while the M-step aligns the GNN encoder to the induced hierarchy. This addresses an important gap in capturing coarse-to-fine granularity in graph representation learning.

entry.title: Trust Your Targets: Is Target Propagation Block-Diagonal Gauss-Newton?

author.name: Giuseppe Castiglione, Christopher Buckley, Ivor Simpson

entry.summary: The paper rederives target propagation as trust-region optimization under a previously unexamined norm, clarifying when TP corresponds to Gauss-Newton updates, and introduces CGTP, which solves layer-local subproblems in parallel with conjugate gradients. A single adaptive parameter jointly controls the trust region and a matching bound on weight updates.

entry.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows

author.name: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes, Tianyi Peng, Nairen Cao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of cost-aware Gittins search for recommending model-to-role assignments in LLM agentic workflows along the quality-cost (and latency) Pareto frontier. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs so each evaluation informs both quality and cost searches.

entry.title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ziang Gao, Pengqi Liu, Archer Yi Yang, Mouloud Belbahri, Jesse C. Cresswell, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: The paper shows that Mondrian conformal prediction's group-wise coverage guarantees are coarse, allowing substantial disparities within finer strata, and introduces propensity standardization to assess how group composition drives disagreement between aggregate and fine-grained fairness comparisons. For mitigation, Tilted Mondrian improves fairness relative to group-wise calibration. This addresses a real gap in fair uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Jinghua Hou, Xueli Sun, Ruihua Han, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: TILDE transfers capabilities from large action-pretrained embodied foundation models to smaller policies via on-policy distillation at student-induced states combined with teacher-executed recovery trajectories. Its AutoDAgger pipeline uses a robotic reward model to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, reducing the data and compute needed to reproduce foundation-model pretraining benefits.

entry.title: A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models

author.name: George Panagopoulos, Saman Omidi, Tsz Pan Tong, Jun Pang

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard evaluation practices for gene perturbation prediction models are unstable: varying the number of top differentially-expressed genes flips the winning method 86.7% of the time under precision-based rankings across eight methods and six datasets. It further exposes that repeating a single predicted profile across cell-level rows, a common practice, can inflate metric scores.

entry.title: Toward a Universal Local Speech Feature Extractor Through Distillation

author.name: Jessica Yang, Marcelo Beramendi Caballero, Ju-Chieh Chou, Karen Livescu

entry.summary: Shows that the computationally heavy CNN feature extractors at the front of self-supervised speech models like HuBERT, WavLM, and data2vec can be replaced by a single small distilled two-layer extractor. The universal extractor retains most teacher performance on SUPERB(-SG), transfers to unseen models such as wav2vec 2.0, and needs only about 3% of the original MACs.

entry.title: A Thousand Faces: A Persuasion Benchmark with Experience-Grounded Persuadees Informed by Psychology and Pragmatics

author.name: Ziqing Zhuang, Dingyi Zhang, Deyu Zhou

entry.summary: ATF-Persu is a persuasion benchmark with 1,000 personas across 200 topics and nine domains, where personas are grounded in the experiences that shaped their beliefs and draw on attitude theory and conversational implicature. It evaluates whether persuasive arguments address a person's actual reasons rather than merely matching a belief description.

entry.title: Representations in Motion: Layer-wise Rotation and Trajectory Divergence in LLMs

author.name: Zhuonan Yang, Yik Siu Chan, Wannan Yang, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: Studies the layer-wise evolution of factuality representations and finds that factuality directions extracted under lying versus honest prompting conditions rotate away from each other across layers. A similar rotation appears in a 3D visual perspective-taking task, suggesting activation-trajectory divergence may be a general signature of controlled internal state manipulation.

entry.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression

author.name: Ziqing Man, Di Wu, Jia-Chen Gu, Junyi Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: Introduces KEEP-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with 4,102 cases directly assessing whether context compression preserves critical evidence for plausible references, explicit qualifiers, and minority perspectives, beyond what QA metrics capture. Even the strongest long-context models prove unreliable despite compression inputs averaging only 3.1K tokens in windows exceeding 100K.

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks

author.name: Rohan Menon, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces ASR_STEP, a metric that penalizes jailbreak attacks for repeated victim-model calls while retaining binary success judgments, reflecting the added detection opportunities each call gives deployed systems. Evaluations on JailBreakBench across GCG, PAIR, and PAP show meaningful score reductions for iterative attacks, changing relative attack rankings.

entry.title: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs

author.name: Luther Wei, Ling Zou, Kang-Yang Huang, Yu-Syuan Xu, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free, hierarchical visual token pruning framework for high-resolution large vision-language models that applies query-aware relevance computation before any LLM blocks execute, operating on the thumbnail-plus-local-crops token structure. This addresses the computational bottleneck of thousands of vision tokens while improving on prior query-agnostic or late, crop-level query-aware pruning.

entry.title: Visual Sufficiency Landscapes: Understanding Query-Conditioned Reliability in Visual Token Pruning

author.name: Zhenghan Li, Kexin Sun, Wei Zheng, Peng Hu, Xiao Wei, Anbo Huang

entry.summary: Introduces visual sufficiency landscapes to characterize how many visual token subsets preserve a vision-language model's behavior at a given layer and budget, measured across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL2-8B, and LLaVA-v1.5-7B on GQA and TextVQA. The analysis reveals that sufficiency abundance varies by query beyond estimation noise, offering a principled view of when token pruning is reliable.

entry.title: PoSTCache: From Forecasting to Postdictive Smoothing for Revisable Diffusion Caching

author.name: Liwei Lan, Hui Chen, Jungong Han, Guiguang Ding

entry.summary: PoSTCache reformulates diffusion caching as revisable trajectory inference, allowing approximations from skipped evaluations to be corrected using feedback from later full-computation steps, unlike prior forward-only caching schemes. The training-free, plug-and-play framework adds postdictive smoothing to existing caching methods for diffusion and flow matching acceleration.

entry.title: HORIA: 4D Human and Object Reconstruction from a Monocular Video with Interaction-Aware Re-Rendering

author.name: Hyeongjin Nam, Taeryung Lee, Daniel Sungho Jung, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: HORIA performs joint 4D reconstruction of humans and objects from monocular video, handling composite interaction phases and occlusion-induced geometric inconsistency via interaction-aware decomposition and re-rendering. It aims to reconstruct how people physically interact with their environment from a single camera.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Yuanyu He, Zhuokun Chen, Yefei He, Zhiwei Tang, Jiasheng Tang, Yinghao Yu, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: DASA shifts autoregressive diffusion transformers from dense spatiotemporal computation to sparse, motion-driven generation, decoupling video into regions analogous to video codecs to eliminate storage and compute redundancy. This targets the prohibitive memory and compute costs of long video generation. Video-codec-inspired sparsity is a pragmatic efficiency lever.

entry.title: CheckDistill: Adaptive Checklist Distillation for Efficient Distributional Reward Modeling in Image Editing

author.name: Yaqi Cai, Zuan Gao, Mengting Chen, Wei Li, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: CheckDistill is a pointwise reward modeling framework for RL-based instruction-guided image editing that decomposes editing conditions into atomic, independently verifiable requirements distilled into internalized instruction-adaptive checklists, producing four-dimensional scoring labels efficiently. This avoids the cost of long generative reasoning trajectories during online RL while retaining explicit, decomposed judgment. Reward model quality and cost are key bottlenecks for RLHF in image editing.

entry.title: SpaRV: Sparse Radiance Voxels for Scalable Geometrically Consistent LiDAR-Visual Mapping and Rendering

author.name: Jianheng Liu, Yunfei Wan, Fangming Cheng, Xiangyu Hong, Zuhao Zou, Haotian Li, Longji Yin, Chunran Zheng, Jiarong Lin, Fu Zhang

entry.summary: SpaRV builds sparse radiance voxel maps from robot data via differentiable ray marching, using LiDAR depth and occupancy to anchor under-constrained geometry while handling camera pose and intrinsics errors and bounding GPU memory growth with scene size. It targets photorealistic, geometrically accurate mapping for robotic simulation, navigation, and inspection. The work addresses the mismatch between robot trajectories and reconstruction-friendly viewpoints.

entry.title: A Time-Variant Spiking Neuron from a Unified State-Dynamics Perspective

author.name: Jing Yang, Qianhui Liu, Gang Pan, Zhanglu Yan

entry.summary: Introduces a unified state-dynamics framework for characterizing spiking neuron models, revealing that existing neurons keep their integration, evolution, and readout rules fixed over time. Building on this insight, the authors propose a time-variant spiking neuron whose dynamical rules adapt across temporal processing. This offers both an analytical lens and a new neuron design for SNNs.

entry.title: Solving a Giant Rubik's Cube with a Quadruped Robot

author.name: Lukas Amiet, Gabriel S\'anchez-Blanco Repgen, Mayank Mittal, Victor Klemm, Andrei Cramariuc, Marco Hutter, Cesar Cadena

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a quadruped robot autonomously solving a giant Rubik's Cube using only its feet, requiring precise pedipulation of a freestanding articulated object while maintaining balance. The system integrates onboard RGB-D perception for metric pose and color state estimation, a planner converting solutions into skill sequences, and learned whole-body skills for reorienting and turning cube layers.

entry.title: CusADi2: Latency-Optimized Batch Computation of Robot Kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians on the GPU

author.name: John Viljoen, Lasse Peters, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: CusADi2 is a software framework for computing batched robot dynamics quantities (forward kinematics, Jacobians, Hessians) on GPUs with latency rather than throughput as the optimization target. Recognizing that trajectory optimization requires many independent parallel evaluations with tight wall-clock deadlines, it optimizes per-batch completion time, unlike prior frameworks that parallelize only across batch instances. This enables faster online sampling-based and gradient-based planning.

entry.title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Weishuo Sun, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu, Yuang Xie, Qicheng Zeng, Peng Ye, Jiajun Deng, Jianmin Ji

entry.summary: TrajWAM is a trajectory-guided world action model for dynamic manipulation that grounds future visual prediction in predicted target trajectories rather than scene-level video objectives. This reduces the latency of iterative video-action denoising while making the model explicitly anticipate target motion for fast replanning.

entry.title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial

author.name: Vanessa Rodriguez, Brieuc Lehmann, Karla Diaz-Ordaz

entry.summary: The paper introduces the gDR-Learner, which generalizes conditional average treatment effects from an RCT to a broader target population using cross-fitted machine-learning nuisance estimation. Excess-risk bounds show nuisance errors enter only as products, yielding oracle-rate convergence despite slower individual nuisance estimation.

entry.title: The Case for Building AI Safety Tools

author.name: ankurpandey42

entry.summary: The author maps the AI safety ecosystem and finds it heavily siloed: of 500+ safety organizations, roughly 80 build tools of any kind, and none of 100 mapped fellowships or courses target tool builders. The post identifies gaps in multi-agent safety, incident reporting, CBRN monitoring, and epistemic risks, and describes a pilot AI Safety for Builders fellowship.

entry.title: Agentic inequality

author.name: Lewis Hammond

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence commentary discussing Sharp et al.'s conceptual framework for how unequal access to AI agents, and differences in agent quality and number, could produce societal inequality. It outlines sources of agentic inequality and proposes a research agenda to address the challenge.

entry.title: Hippo: Training-Free Agent Self-Evolution via Hippocampal Replay

author.name: Yutong Song, Jiang Wu, Yuxuan Ren, Tony Qin, Baoyuan Wang

entry.summary: Hippo is a training-free memory framework enabling LLM agent self-improvement through external memory inspired by selective hippocampal encoding and replay. It compares attempts at the same task to identify reusable decisions and refine when they apply, addressing the finding that naive memory accumulation eventually underperforms a no-memory baseline. This contributes to parameter-free recursive self-improvement for agents.

entry.title: Where Natural Language Ends in Agents: Executable Skill Composition with MetaSkill

author.name: Meng Shu, Wei He, Hang Zhou, Runke Liu, Kai Han, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: MetaSkill proposes a hybrid representation for agent skills: substantive task judgments stay in natural language while coordination relations, references, and machine-checkable constraints become executable via a DAG runtime. Across 20 multi-Skill artifact tasks, this selective formalization supports explicit composition without prescribing internal skill behavior.

entry.title: Pattern-Driven Evaluation of LLM Code Optimization: Isolating Compiler-Transcendent Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Wesley Lu, Runzhou Liu, Hongru Du, Xinyao Yi

entry.summary: PatternBench is a benchmark for evaluating whether LLM code optimization produces improvements beyond what modern optimizing compilers already achieve, spanning seven transformation classes. It pairs runtime evaluation with AST-based faithfulness analysis verifying that intended optimizations actually occur, isolating model-attributable optimization behavior.

entry.title: SteadyThought: Mitigating LLM Under-Thinking via Thought-Level Preference Optimization

author.name: Zhenyue Peng, Lin Yang, Jie Wang, Xiaoqi Ni, Hanzhu Chen, Xize Liang, Yanjun Wu, Rujing Wang, Kaiwen Zhou, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Identifies under-thinking in large reasoning models, where excessive thought switching abandons promising reasoning trajectories, and proposes SteadyThought, a thought-level preference optimization framework. It forces single-path continuations from identified switching points to generate preference pairs, steering a middle ground between over-switching and over-suppression.

entry.title: Memory, Know Your PLACE: Governing Lifecycle State and Query-Time Eligibility in Persistent-Memory Agents

author.name: Chen-Fang Hu, Hong-Han Shuai, Woan-Shiuan Chien

entry.summary: PLACE introduces a governance layer for persistent agent memory with write-side state certification and read-side authorization, controlling whether stored memory remains valid and whether it may influence a later query. A factorial evaluation on Mem0 with small Qwen2.5 models shows write-side governance improves lifecycle state correctness while read-side governance eliminates causal leakage from ineligible memories.

entry.title: Think, Compress, Answer: Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Grounding via Reasoning Compression

author.name: Jinbae Seo, Hyeongjun Kwon, Jiyoung Lee, Hyunsung Jang, Namkoo Ha, Jungin Park, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: The paper proposes Think-Compress-Answer (TCA), a reinforcement learning framework for multimodal grounding that decomposes reasoning into free-form reasoning, target-aware compression, and answering, motivated by the information bottleneck principle. It addresses the problem that long reasoning trajectories dilute grounded perceptual evidence with peripheral scene narratives. Compressing reasoning toward target-specific compact representations improves precise localization.

entry.title: TRACE: Tracking Multimodal Clinical Trajectories for Inpatient Risk Prediction

author.name: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon

entry.summary: TRACE organizes heterogeneous clinical evidence (structured EHR data, chest x-rays, clinical text) into day-level trajectories, separating day-invariant global context from day-specific local events for inpatient risk prediction across mortality, length of stay, and readmission. It shifts focus from modality fusion to temporal trajectory modeling over an admission.

entry.title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents

author.name: Jiasheng Mao, Jiacheng Liu, Hengwei Ye, Zheng Tian

entry.summary: Introduces QuantHarness, a two-layer trajectory-level framework for governing LLM agents that translate natural-language financial research requests into backtested strategies, controlling how intermediate outputs become downstream state and preserving evidence for the terminal outcome. It targets failures where a successful-looking run implements the wrong rule or uses look-ahead information.

entry.title: GeoForward: Geometry-Guided Cross-View Alignment for Feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yiming Shu, Peng Sun, Lang Zhang, Mingyue Feng, Yaonong Wang, Pei Liu, Chen Sun, Jun Ma

entry.summary: GeoForward proposes a geometry-conditioned feedforward reconstruction paradigm for 3D Gaussian Splatting in which calibrated camera geometry and sparse metric measurements establish cross-view correspondence before representation formation, with learned features refining rather than discovering correspondence. This contrasts with the prevailing appearance-driven paradigm.

entry.title: Tactix: Towards a Programmable Strategy Interface for Flexible SAT Solving

author.name: Haoze Wu, Andr\'e Schidler, Armin Biere, Nina Narodytska

entry.summary: Tactix is a proof-producing sequential CDCL SAT solver that cleanly separates proof rules from solving strategies, exposing a public interface to invoke techniques, observe their effects, and program new strategies. Its programmable default strategy outperforms state-of-the-art solvers. This enables strategy research without modifying solver internals, benefiting both the SAT community and formal-methods applications.

entry.title: CorrFlow: Self-Correcting Flow Matching

author.name: Hangwei Zhang, Nathan Rouill\'e, Chuanxia Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces CorrFlow, a self-correcting flow-matching framework in which a lightweight refiner predicts residual corrections from the base model's clean prediction, conditioning, noise level, and hidden states from the same forward pass, motivated by an identity linking one-step prediction error to the realized velocity residual. Corrections are added to the base velocity before each sampling update, improving subsequent predictions.

entry.title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models

author.name: Wang Yang, Xinpeng Li, Yanyan Zhang, Chuang Ma, Shouren Wang, Jianzhe Wei, Liqin Ye, Xiaoran Cai, Mohsen Hariri, Vipin Chaudhary, Xiaotian Han

entry.summary: This analysis probes the limits of Jev-style one-pass decision models used in agent loops, finding they fail when a decision requires multi-step reasoning an LLM could only perform by writing intermediate steps. Accuracy degrades with multi-update state dependencies (53-80% at sixteen updates) due to record interference, and the model defers to stale summaries, while answering 97.5% of items solvable in one pass.

entry.title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Jingrui Wu, Wangyun Dan

entry.summary: The authors propose a residual flow matching method for predicting single-cell responses to combinatorial genetic and chemical perturbations. The key insight is that most of the post-perturbation response is additive from single-perturbation effects, so the model generates only the smaller non-additive residual induced by perturbation interactions, allocating capacity to the biologically informative synergy signal.

entry.title: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference

author.name: Mobina Kashaniyan, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: ATEST is a resource-aware test-time scaling framework that jointly weighs the expected value of additional reasoning samples against live GPU energy costs, which the authors show can vary up to 4.1-fold under contention for identical queries. ATEST-Online requires no offline calibration, incrementally sampling while estimating answer stability and learning step energy costs online to decide when to stop.

entry.title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

author.name: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan

entry.summary: The authors present a quantitative RAG benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics in which all 755 ground-truth answers are computed from 45,441 measured device records spanning human-curated data through 2021 plus records extracted from 2022-2026 literature. Benchmarking six retrieval-augmented systems against verified experimental ground truth exposes weaknesses of text-overlap and model-scored evaluations.

entry.title: Computation, Not Memory: Chain-of-Thought and State Tracking in LLM Agents

author.name: Pedram Mouseli, Massieh Moayedi

entry.summary: Using a file-system task with lock-state tracking on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B, the study separates two roles of reasoning: generating chain-of-thought at the moment of action versus retaining earlier reasoning in context. The main reduction in erroneous actions comes from reasoning written at action time, while retaining prior reasoning adds little, suggesting CoT functions as computation rather than memory.

entry.title: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding

author.name: Matthias Eder, Pantelis Emmanouil, Vivek Farias, Fabian Fischer, Adam Jozefiak, Tianyi Peng, Thomas Ulz, Raphael Watschinger, Fangyu Wu, Andrew Zheng

entry.summary: The authors show that policy search directly in code space, where coding agents iteratively propose, implement, evaluate, and refine algorithms using simulation feedback, can outperform both hand-engineered and RL-derived coordination policies. Case studies include a challenging League of Robot Runners 2024 map. This offers an interpretable third path for multi-agent policy design.

entry.title: Conducting Reliable Keyword Estimation with Unreliable ASR in Police Audio Data

author.name: Robert Cole Molloy, Rhiannon N. Miller, Stephen Morgan, Anjalie Field

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether imperfect ASR transcripts of police radio communications can still yield statistically valid keyword frequency estimates by combining model outputs with small human-labeled samples via Prediction Powered Inference and Design-based Supervised Learning. Evaluated on Baltimore and Chicago police audio, the approach quantifies and corrects systematic ASR transcription bias. This enables trustworthy downstream analysis at scale in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions

author.name: Rui Shi, Xunjian Yin, Jiacheng Sang, Zichuan Liu, Shuyan Zhou

entry.summary: WeAct trains capability-specific LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone and adds adapter selection to an agent's action space via its native tool-calling interface, allowing on-demand capability composition during long-horizon tasks. This avoids catastrophic forgetting and static parameter configurations. Evaluated across eight diverse settings.

entry.title: Measuring Empowerment from Offline Data for Intrinsically Motivated Exploration

author.name: Ishir Garg, Vivek Myers, Qiyang Li, Catherine Ji, Benjamin Eysenbach, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: The paper explores how large offline datasets can guide exploration during subsequent online learning by measuring empowerment, a count of realizable future states, from prior data. The authors connect offline-data-derived empowerment signals to exploration efficiency, arguing high-empowerment states require more exploration. The work bridges offline RL, intrinsic motivation, and the pretrain-then-finetune recipe common in robotics and coding agents.

entry.title: ProbePO: Sparse Probes, Redistributed Credit for Critic-Free LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Diyi Hu, Ruizhong Qiu, Lin Qiu, Hanghang Tong, Hanqing Zeng

entry.summary: ProbePO tackles credit assignment in RLVR-based LLM training by framing it as budgeted measurement: it selects partial-solution states via a reward-free uncertainty score, estimates expected verifier rewards under capped continuations, and redistributes terminal rewards across reasoning steps. This offers finer-grained credit than GRPO's group-normalized broadcast without dense auxiliary rollouts or altering update data. The method is critic-free and budget-aware.

entry.title: Mining the Self-Rewriting System: A Vision for Data Mining on AI-Native Infrastructure

author.name: Mayank Darbari, Chiman Salavati, Liang Wu, Dawei Wang, Jiong Zhang, Kelly Wan, Krishna Chakka, Liangjie Hong

entry.summary: This position paper argues that AI-native infrastructure, where agents observe, act on, and reshape their own logs, retrieval stores, and serving paths, invalidates the classical data mining assumption that data is generated outside the learner. The authors define the resulting object as a self-rewriting system and the associated shift as endogenous drift, with a falsifiable claim that cross-surface failures are not identifiable from per-surface monitoring alone. It proposes joint multi-surface analysis as a new research agenda for AI-era data mining.

entry.title: ProtGlycanDock: Towards Accurate Protein-Glycan Docking with Tailored Dataset, Benchmark and Model

author.name: Minghao Xu, Jiaze Song, Jinyu Wang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ProtGlycanDock, a curated benchmark for protein-glycan docking under protein and glycan generalization settings, evaluating ten methods spanning physics-based, ML docking, and structure prediction approaches. The authors also propose finetuning techniques that inject glycan conformational knowledge for more precise binding poses.

entry.title: ITU-DESC: a missingness-aware machine-learning dementia risk score in the UK Biobank cohort

author.name: Abdullah Kavakl{\i}, Faik Boray Tek

entry.summary: ITU-DESC is an explainable machine-learning dementia risk score built on roughly 500,000 UK Biobank participants with 16.6 years median follow-up, combining broad feature selection across about 8,000 candidates with explicit control of informative missingness via unconditional random hot-deck imputation and stabilized BorutaSHAP feature selection.

entry.title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models

author.name: Alessandro Palma, Charles Jones, Tristan Cinquin, Fabian J. Theis, Frederik Wenkel

entry.summary: Trajectory replay addresses catastrophic forgetting in lifelong adaptation of continuous-time generative models by training an updated velocity field to match both a frozen historical velocity along its trajectories and the incoming task's velocity field, bypassing full sample generation used in generative replay and avoiding accumulated discretization error.

entry.title: Interpretability of AI weather models via intermediate decoding

author.name: Matthias Beylich, Kirsten I. Tempest, Tobias Selz, George C. Craig

entry.summary: Proposes intermediate decoding as an interpretability method for AI weather models, decoding latent states at intermediate depths back into meteorological fields using the trained forecast decoder, applied to GraphCast, Aurora, and ArchesWeather. This opens the black box of how high-dimensional latent representations are progressively transformed into forecasts.

entry.title: Knowledge Diversion: A Novel Paradigm for Pre-training Decomposable Image Generation Models

author.name: Yucheng Xie, Fu Feng, Ruixiao Shi, Jing Wang, Xin Geng, Yong Rui

entry.summary: KDiv is a condition-aware pre-training paradigm for image generation models that factorizes randomly initialized parameters before training so that transferable and task-specific knowledge remain inherently decomposable rather than entangled. This supports selective knowledge reuse and efficient downstream adaptation across diverse conditions and domains. It rethinks pre-training objectives with downstream modularity in mind.

entry.title: Fair Regression under Approximate Demographic Parity

author.name: Weiwei Wang, Xianyang Zhang, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: The paper relaxes exact demographic parity in regression by bounding pairwise Wasserstein distances between group-specific prediction distributions with a tunable tolerance. It establishes an equivalence between the prediction and constrained transport problems, characterizes deterministic transport-form predictors, and reduces the problem under standard conditions to convex bounded quantile optimization.

entry.title: Language Models are Lazy Poets: Creative Mode Collapse at Scale

author.name: Jacob A. Matthews, Sil Hamilton

entry.summary: The authors generate over 1.1 million poems across 15 poetic forms, 248 subject tags, and 16 open-weight models, constituting the largest LLM poetry corpus to date, and quantify creative mode collapse: vocabularies and rhyming abilities are substantial but severely underutilized. The study provides the first comprehensive large-scale genre-specific survey of LLM creative self-similarity.

entry.title: Compositional Activation Steering Across Languages and Behaviors with Contextual Gates

author.name: Daniil Gurgurov, Akansh Maurya, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Proposes contextual steering that trains gates to adapt the strength of fixed activation-steering directions to the current hidden state and to interactions between interventions, enabling simultaneous control of multiple behaviors across languages. It outperforms constant-strength steering, prompting, and four baselines while better preserving general knowledge.

entry.title: Do LLMs Reproduce the Age Gap in Loneliness? Evaluating Survey Simulation against European Survey Data

author.name: Yuliya Li, Achim Rettinger, Dominik Beyer

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLM survey simulations reproduce within-country age gaps in loneliness using the 2022 EU Loneliness Survey across four countries, comparing age-specified simulation and distribution estimation against probability samples. It finds that models including Mistral Small 4 and GPT-5.6 Terra reverse the true ordering, with younger adults actually lonelier in human data.

entry.title: Monsoon: Scalable Spontaneous Speech Collection for Low-Resource ASR in 50 Languages

author.name: Shobhit Banga, Manas Dhir, Aaditya Pareek, Amritansh Walecha, Bhaskar Singh, Hanuman Sidh, Manmeet Kaur, Sagar Jain, Supriya Paul, Vanshika Chhabra, Utkarsh Singh

entry.summary: Presents Monsoon, a framework for collecting spontaneous, accurately transcribed speech at scale across 50 languages, using paired-contributor unscripted conversations, automated screening, and multi-level human transcript review. Its quality stages reduce semantic WER by 10 to 39 percent relative to a conventional protocol, and Whisper fine-tuned on Monsoon data beats architecture-matched baselines.

entry.title: AudioScorer: Learning Question-Aware Token Relevance for Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Marwan Farag, Bin Yang

entry.summary: AudioScorer is a lightweight module that scores audio tokens by relevance to the user question, enabling pruning of dense audio token sequences in large audio language models. It is trained by distilling token rankings from answer-gradient saliency of the frozen LALM plus downstream answer supervision, reportedly outperforming heuristic pruning baselines.

entry.title: ProV-Mem: Proactive Memory for Streaming Video Question Answering

author.name: Bingbing Wang, Jing Li, Han Gao, Yishi Lin, Ruifeng Xu, Peng He

entry.summary: ProV-Mem is a training-free proactive memory framework built on a frozen VLM for streaming video question answering, decomposing proactive decisions (when to speak, what to say, whether to respond) into three lightweight memory tiers covering temporal triggers, instructional guidance, and content management. It balances the cost of retaining long visual histories against the risk of missed events and repeated responses.

entry.title: PREEMPT: Proactive Robustness Evaluation under Editing for Media Protection Techniques

author.name: Qiuyu Tang, Aparna Bharati

entry.summary: PREEMPT is a holistic evaluation framework assessing whether proactive image protection methods (which embed protective signals against unauthorized manipulation and generative misuse) remain effective under one-shot and sequential, multi-step image editing workflows. It systematically characterizes robustness dynamics across protection paradigms, going beyond the static one-shot edits of prior evaluations.

entry.title: SCOPE-VSR: A Broad-Coverage Training Dataset for Video Super-Resolution

author.name: Gengyu Liao, Yechun Yong, Zheng Chen, Jianze Li, Ziqing Zhang, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: SCOPE-VSR provides a 27k-video open-domain training dataset for video super-resolution built via a structured curation pipeline combining task-oriented video selection with hierarchical semantic rebalancing, addressing the semantic imbalance of existing VSR data. The authors also release SCOPE-test and demonstrate a one-step diffusion-based VSR framework, GraCo-VSR, trained on it.

entry.title: PCHMR: Empowering and Benchmarking Human Mesh Recovery in Privacy-Constrained Real-World Settings

author.name: Zeyu Cao, Qingxuan Wu, Zhiyang Dou, Rui Xu, Yuan Liu, Javier Fernandez-Marques, Nicholas D. Lane, Taku Komura, Wenping Wang

entry.summary: Studies human mesh recovery (HMR) improvement and evaluation under privacy constraints, benchmarking state-of-the-art HMR models trained with federated learning and a secure-aggregation variant that never centralizes raw images. It evaluates across a wide range of client-scale and data-heterogeneity settings relevant to real HMR-deployed devices.

entry.title: GroundedVDR: Grounding Video-to-Web Evidence Dependencies in Video Deep Research

author.name: Xiyuan Liang, Yu Wang, Zuhao Yang, Ziting Wang, Duo Li, Sudong Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: GroundedVDR is an evidence-grounded benchmark for video deep research that verifies whether models actually use temporal video information and retrieved web evidence, rather than only scoring tool-use trajectories and final answers. It combines human review with restricted-access probing and provides structured video-to-web evidence annotations linking relevant sources.

entry.title: When Guidance Becomes a Guard: Early Interception of Unsafe Inputs in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Yanchun Li, Yujin Wu, Gangkai Shen, Ming Yang, Li Zeng, Xianlong Wang, Hangtao Zhang, Shujuan Tian

entry.summary: CSTI shows that classifier-free guidance exposes strong safety signals in conditional responses, enabling early detection of unsafe and adversarial text-to-image inputs via compact statistics and linear readouts on activation contrasts at early checkpoints. It fits concept-specific detectors without attack samples, image decoding, or generator modification. Moves safety filtering from post-hoc output screening to pre-generation interception.

entry.title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models

author.name: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Guanbo Jiao, Jianming Ma, Guanjie Zheng, Xing Gao

entry.summary: PICA-WAM identifies that world action models are sensitive to task-irrelevant appearance changes because video prediction rewards preserving appearance while action generation never enforces invariance. It proposes a self-supervised cross-appearance self-alignment training scheme requiring perturbed and nominal observations to yield consistent action representations. Robustness to cosmetic visual changes is important for sim-to-real and deployment reliability of robot policies.

entry.title: StreamAhead: Real-Time Streaming Video Question Answering via Adaptive Precomputation

author.name: Haoyang Fan, Dhruv Parikh, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: StreamAhead is an algorithm-system co-design for real-time streaming video question answering that balances precomputing KV caches as video arrives against query-time computation for retrieved content. It adaptively precomputes only what is likely needed, reducing query latency while sustaining the required video-processing rate. This addresses a fundamental latency-throughput trade-off for VLM video systems.

entry.title: Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding for 3D Manipulation Policies under Depth Corruption

author.name: Zhiyuan Yang, Jiaju He, Ruiteng Zhao, Anqi Cheng, Haiyue Zhu, Kezhi Mao

entry.summary: The paper identifies a sharp depth-noise cliff in modern 3D manipulation policies under realistic RGB-D corruption, persisting even with matched noisy training data. It proposes a spatial-encoding approach that prevents corrupted depth from entangling with token coordinates and geometry features, improving robustness of 3D policies on transparent, reflective, thin, or textureless objects.

entry.title: SurGPT: A Multi-Task Foundation Model for Robotic Surgical Skills Assessment and Gesture Recognition

author.name: Parham M. Kebria, Saeid Nahavandi, Mehrdad Saif, Fernando Bello

entry.summary: SurGPT is a foundation model combining a visual encoder and transformer architecture that analyzes da Vinci surgical videos for three simultaneous tasks: surgical task classification, standardized skill-level assessment, and natural-language description of surgical gestures. It aims to automate subjective human expert evaluations that bottleneck surgical education. The model produces human-readable assessments from video sequences.

entry.title: Dimension-free comparison inequalities between $f$-divergences for Gaussian location mixtures

author.name: Jeonghwan Lee, Cong Ma

entry.summary: The authors establish dimension-free comparison inequalities between KL and chi-squared divergences and squared Hellinger distance for Gaussian location mixtures with compactly supported mixing distributions, with constants depending only on the support radius. The results resolve an open question and are proved via a Gaussian interpolation argument relating divergence derivatives to posterior mean differences.

entry.title: High-dimensional covariate-assisted ranking

author.name: Yujia Liu, Yuanyuan Lin, Ruijian Han, Yiming Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies a Plackett-Luce ranking model that incorporates high-dimensional covariate effects alongside item-specific utilities, under sparsity assumptions on covariate coefficients. It establishes a necessary and sufficient identifiability condition based on the Kruskal rank of the restricted covariate design and proposes an l1-regularized maximum likelihood estimator with existence and statistical guarantees. This matters for modern ranking problems where covariate dimension grows with the number of objects.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Resolve Service Failures? Simulating Multi-Turn Complaint Handling under Information Asymmetry

author.name: Wailing Ng, Mengze Hong, Chen Jason Zhang, Shiqi Fan

entry.summary: The authors introduce ServiceBench, a benchmark for complaint handling with 2,500 scenarios across 184 complaint categories and five industries, plus an Asymmetric Progressive Complaint Simulation protocol and justice-based evaluation. Experiments show even capable LLM agents struggle, failing to proactively gather information and often conceding prematurely.

entry.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents

author.name: Adarsh Vatsa, William Eiers

entry.summary: Observing that bounded agentic workflows repeatedly encounter saturated decision spaces, the authors propose Discretize, Then Decide: treat in-bounds agent decisions as an optimization problem, solve it once, and reuse solutions rather than re-deriving them from context each turn. This can make agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable, using workflow logs or synthesized data.

entry.title: CorrectRTL: Boost RTL Generation Quality Through Automated Self-Correction with Instruction Decomposition

author.name: Jing Wang, Shang Liu, Hangan Zhou, Wenji Fang, Yuchao Wu, Yugao Zhu, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: Contributes ScaleBench, a harder 200-design RTL generation benchmark for cases where existing benchmarks are saturated, plus CorrectRTL, an agentic framework that decomposes specifications into instructions so self-correction targets localized fixes instead of monolithic whole-design rewrites. This reduces error corruption of previously correct code in LLM-based hardware design.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models with Indigenous Community Cosmovision through Constitutional AI

author.name: Silvia Fern\'andez-Sabido, Jorge Reyes-Maga\~na, Jes\'us Adri\'an Chay Tun, Jean Carlos Buenfil, Victor Gonz\'alez Nahuat, Francisco Morales

entry.summary: This paper builds an operational cultural constitution with 12 principles derived from interviews with five Indigenous leaders and defenders in Latin America, then applies a two-phase Constitutional AI pipeline (SFT and direct preference optimization) to align models with Indigenous cosmovisions on questions of territory, authority, and nature. It addresses the anglophone, Western skew of dominant LLM training corpora.

entry.title: Neither Over- nor Under-Constrained: Evaluating LLM Personalization under a Constraint Qualification Audit

author.name: Xuran Li, Guanqin Zhang, Imran Razzak, Hakim Hacid, Eleanna Kafeza, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: ConQual-Audit is a three-stage framework for evaluating LLM personalization: extracting semantic constraints from user profiles, qualifying them by pruning unnecessary and recovering missing constraints, and verifying candidate responses via natural language inference. It reduces the false rejections and acceptances that plague over- or under-constrained evaluation paradigms. Across PrefEval and LaMP it outperforms nine baselines with top AUCs of 0.88 and 0.90.

entry.title: OpenSaC: A Python Library for Search as Code in Deep Research Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: OpenSaC is an open-source Python library implementing the Search as Code paradigm, where deep research agents write programs composing search, source reading, reranking, model calls, and local processing instead of alternating reasoning with individual search actions. Configurable interfaces preserve evidence for inspection, and it improves on standard Codex with built-in web search.

entry.title: ClueFlow: Learning Long-Horizon Search through Attributed Research-State Transitions

author.name: Yicheng Wang, Wentao Tan, Yidan Huang, Yifei Liu, Qiong Cao

entry.summary: ClueFlow learns long-horizon search by constructing Source-State-Final attribution chains that link evidence-acquiring browser actions to evidence and candidate updates and the final answer, using gold-conditioned semantic validation of typed state changes. This grounds training signals in explicit, attributable state transitions.

entry.title: REFLEX: RNA Ensemble Generation via Flexibility-Calibrated Stochastic Bridge

author.name: Wanli Ma, Tianmeng Hu, Ke Li

entry.summary: REFLEX is a sequence-conditioned generative model for RNA backbone conformational ensembles using a heteroscedastic stochastic bridge on SE(3), where experimental B-factors calibrate residue-wise bridge widths during training. A learned flexibility condition keeps constrained regions sharp while exposing flexible regions as perturbation neighborhoods, capturing ensemble diversity without collapsing to averaged structures or drifting into unsupported conformations.

entry.title: EMMA: Event-Driven Multimodal Memory System with Multi-Agent Retrieval

author.name: Ruochen Zhao, Jiazheng Kang, Gezi Li, Dongying Lin, Ting Bai

entry.summary: EMMA organizes long video memory around semantic events rather than fixed clips, using a dual-stream detector that fuses visual semantic drift with spoken transitions to locate event boundaries, followed by a three-level memory hierarchy. A multi-agent retrieval layer supports long video understanding beyond MLLM context windows.

entry.title: Prefix-Tuning for Arbitrary Output Sequences on Pretrained Transformers

author.name: Peter Cho-Ho Lam, Ziyi Wang, Zirui Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical work proves that for a pretrained autoregressive Transformer, for any input-output pair where the output is in the model's range, there exists a prefix that induces the model to generate the target output. It resolves an open expressiveness question about prefix-tuning.

entry.title: CoDA: A Human-LM Collaborative Codebook Development Assistant for Domain-Specific Text Annotation

author.name: Jaspreet Ranjit, Swaminathan Chellappa, Augusto Rivas Costante, Chandan Manjunath, Laura Onasch-Vera, Hailey Winetrobe Nadel, Eric Rice, Swabha Swayamdipta

entry.summary: CoDA is an open-source human-LM collaborative assistant that helps domain experts iteratively develop annotation codebooks by reviewing incorrect model predictions and folding expert feedback back into evolving guidelines. It targets the neglected bottleneck that most LLM annotation systems assume high-quality guidelines already exist, which is especially problematic for expert-knowledge-dependent concepts. With credible authorship including Swabha Swayamdipta, it bridges HCI and NLP for data-centric annotation.

entry.title: AdamPM: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization via Moment Pooling

author.name: Xiaowei Ji, Lishan Xu, Jianing An, Jie Luo, Wenjun Wu, Lei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces AdamPM, a memory-efficient Adam variant that groups adjacent first- and second-moment entries along rows or columns and represents each group by a shared mean, reducing optimizer state memory. It inherits Adam's hyperparameters and is a drop-in change, avoiding the extra tuning or compute overhead of many alternative memory-efficient optimizers.

entry.title: Robust Direct Preference Optimization under Preference Label-Flip Attacks

author.name: Chenye Yang, Weiyu Xu, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: The paper designs robust variants of DPO to defend against adversarial preference label-flip attacks that steer the learner toward attacker-chosen policies. Exploiting that label flips induce parameter-independent gradient shifts in log-linear DPO, it proposes Trim-K and Soft-Trim-K Robust-DPO with deterministic perturbation bounds over all attack sets of bounded size.

entry.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds

author.name: Jize Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Xinyi Le, Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This Perspective argues that as JEPAs move toward latent world models supporting prediction, planning, and control, interpretability must shift from what latents encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. The authors propose a four-stage research agenda (Ground, Structure, Verify, Act) toward actionable latent-world understanding.

entry.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Sagar Kumar, Shailja Sharma, Tirthajit Baruah, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: The authors show that post-training compression of medical segmentation models can keep Dice scores stable while degrading uncertainty signals that clinicians rely on to detect unreliable predictions. They propose SGAV-MP, a mixed-precision compression framework for MRI/CT segmentation that selects layer precisions under explicit reliability constraints.

entry.title: Progress-Guided Preference Generation for Aligning Generative Control Policies

author.name: Tung M. Luu, Tri Ton, Duc M. Nguyen, Xuan Thanh Nguyen, Nguyen Gia Binh, Quang Tan Nguyen, Vu Duong, Daniel Sonntag, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Vien Anh Ngo, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes PGPG, an unsupervised preference-alignment framework for generative imitation-learning policies that derives pseudo-preference labels automatically from autonomously collected rollouts using ordered coverage alignment against a small set of expert demonstrations. This removes the need for costly human preference annotation in preference-based fine-tuning of control policies.

entry.title: Accelerated Drift of Scientific Prose in the LLM Era: Evidence from an Interrupted Time-Series Analysis

author.name: Hanna Hubarava, Benjamin V. Ineichen

entry.summary: Using ChatGPT's November 2022 release as a breakpoint, this interrupted time-series analysis compares pre- and post-2022 trajectories of vocabulary, punctuation, readability, and syntax in arXiv abstracts across AI, statistics, and quantitative biology. It finds accelerated linguistic drift in scientific prose coinciding with LLM writing tools. This provides quantitative evidence of LLM impact on scientific communication.

entry.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning

author.name: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju, Kai Ye, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: The paper identifies that standard bimanual imitation learning conflates task-required cross-arm constraints with incidental timing schedules, letting policies exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue. Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination retimes recorded arm-local segments at training time to realize admissible schedules while preserving task constraints, and is applied to Diffusion Policy and Action Chunking Transformer variants. This improves generalization in bimanual manipulation.

entry.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models

author.name: Simon A. Lee, Jiahang Hank Sha, Soomin Chung, Kai Akamatsu, Eran Halperin, Jeffrey N. Chiang

entry.summary: Introduces a world model for EHR that represents patient histories as action-conditioned latent trajectories, separating patient states from clinical actions with a state-dependent linearization predictor. This enables time-resolved prediction, multi-step rollout, and action-conditioned simulation while preserving downstream predictive signal and subgroup statistics. Moves beyond autoregressive token prediction for clinical data.

entry.title: Alliance of Stochastic Routing and Reinforcement Fusion for Multi-Model Reasoning

author.name: Selim Furkan Tekin, Ling Liu

entry.summary: VL-Scout is a unified vision-language framework that dynamically routes and composes multiple models for multimodal, multi-step reasoning under uncertainty. It combines Bayesian priors, policy gradient optimization, and a context-dependent Dirichlet belief model to avoid premature convergence to suboptimal models that plagues standard RL-based routing. This addresses the practical problem of cost-efficient inference across pools of large models.

entry.title: Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform

author.name: Sho Sonoda, Luca Galimberti, Yuanchao Xu, Isao Ishikawa, Masahiro Ikeda

entry.summary: This paper extends the ridgelet transform to continuous maps on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, replacing unavailable Lebesgue measure with Gaussian weights, yielding constructive universal approximation results for operator learning networks. The transform comes with a Plancherel identity and explicit reconstruction formulas, moving beyond mere existence arguments.

entry.title: BEM: Learning Bregman Divergences for Concept Erasure in Flow Matching Models

author.name: Mohamed-Hicham Leghettas, Markus P\"uschel

entry.summary: BEM addresses concept erasure in flow-matching text-to-image models such as FLUX and Stable Diffusion 3, observing that Bregman divergences are exactly the losses under which flow matching recovers the correct velocity field. The method learns which divergence to use via bi-level optimization so the fine-tuned model forgets target concepts while preserving others. This generalizes Euclidean-loss fine-tuning used by prior erasure methods.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning with General Utilities via Neural Dual Critics

author.name: Ankur Naskar, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: The paper develops a natural actor-critic method for reinforcement learning with general utilities (RLGU), optimizing nonlinear functionals of occupancy measures with exact variational dual representations for concave objectives. Rather than estimating the occupancy measure then forming pseudo-rewards, it learns the pseudo-reward directly with a neural critic trained via projected stochastic updates, using multilevel Monte Carlo to control bias at logarithmic cost. Theory separates actor bias from estimator error for sample-efficiency guarantees.

entry.title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Junyu Chen, Franklin Liu, Moshu Xu, Lijian Yang

entry.summary: LOBGrad is a conditional DDPM framework for probabilistic limit order book forecasting that combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion generator, addressing the lack of learned recurrent encoders and statistical guarantees in prior LOB snapshot models. The authors prove an excess-risk oracle inequality for the one-step DDPM noise-prediction objective under mixing assumptions and reduce conditioning-window dependence to latent-state dependence under contractive dynamics. This brings both performance and theory to financial market microstructure forecasting.

entry.title: DeltaTrace: Efficient Signed Attribution for Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Chen Liang, Daoping Wu, Donghua Yang, Zhiyu Liang, Ying Zhang, Shuguang Xiong, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: DeltaTrace is an attribution framework explaining how context tokens support or oppose a language model's fixed response by measuring log-probability changes under masking and distributing them via backward-composed secant slopes. It assigns signed attributions with local conservation so contributions sum exactly to the measured score difference.

entry.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection in Continual Learning

author.name: Nimeshika Udayangani, Flora D. Salim, Christopher Leckie, Sarah Erfani

entry.summary: This work proposes a rehearsal-free OOD detection framework for continual learning built on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, exploiting their local neuroplasticity to mitigate catastrophic forgetting while flagging unknown samples. It removes the reliance on rehearsal buffers of past data that limits prior methods in realistic open-world settings.

entry.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes

author.name: Jinchen Zhang, Zheyuan Liu, Yihan Zhu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper examines how sparse autoencoder (SAE) code interventions compare under different strength controls, comparing norm matching and output calibration for fixed feature groups in Gemma and Llama models. It finds that the choice of strength control changes conclusions about intervention effects, with KL calibration and total-norm matching yielding different rankings across codes.

entry.title: Your Self-Supervised Projection Head Captures Object Co-Occurrence Statistics

author.name: Arthur Aubret, Jochen Triesch, C\'eline Teuli\`ere

entry.summary: This paper hypothesizes that SSL pretext tasks implicitly model object co-occurrence statistics and tests it across many SSL models using curated datasets of segmented objects. It finds a hierarchical division of labor: the visual backbone encodes object categories while the projection head specializes in encoding co-occurrences between categories, explaining why projection-head features excel at certain semantic tasks. This clarifies a previously underexplored mechanism behind SSL success.

entry.title: Extending Myerson's Optimal Auctions to Correlated Bidders via Neural Network Interpolation

author.name: Mingyu Guo, Jiayuan Liu, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Tackles revenue-maximizing single-item auctions with correlated bidders, where optimal allocation design is NP-hard to approximate and naive extensions of Myerson's solution lose strategy-proofness. The authors build an empirical pipeline using neural interpolation of Myerson's greedy solution to produce deterministic, strategy-proof, ex post individually rational auctions, setting a new empirical rigor standard for this theoretically intractable model.

entry.title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes

author.name: Joshua Rooijakkers, Edwin Fong

entry.summary: The Martingale Posterior Cox Process recasts Bayesian intensity estimation for point-process data as inference over unobserved future events given observed history, avoiding complex prior specification over latent structures. This martingale-posterior perspective sidesteps expensive MCMC and approximate inference while retaining nonparametric flexibility. It offers a more interpretable and computationally lighter alternative for event-based modeling.

entry.title: The Explainability Illusion: Must ViTs Exhibit Patch-Decoding Interpretability?

author.name: Ronen Schaffer, Hila Manor, Tomer Michaeli

entry.summary: The paper questions whether token-decoding explainability in vision transformers, a popular interpretability diagnostic, is an inherent property of transformers or merely an artifact of implicit bias. Through systematic experiments across architectures, scales, and training objectives, the authors show that patch-decoding interpretability should not be assumed, challenging a widespread interpretability practice.

entry.title: Towards instance-dependent regret optimality in Episodic MDPs with Posterior Sampling

author.name: Victor Boone, Cyrille Kone, Waris Radji, Odalric-Ambrym Maillard, Dorian Baudry

entry.summary: The paper introduces pi0-PSRL, a posterior sampling RL variant that uses posterior samples to decide when exploration is needed while following a fixed reference policy during exploration episodes, decoupling the exploration trigger from the information-gathering policy. It proves instance-dependent regret guarantees for finite-horizon episodic MDPs, addressing a limitation of standard PSRL where the sampled optimal policy is not ideal for exploration.

entry.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits

author.name: Zhehang Du, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Polar Switch is a new family of polynomial circuits for gradient orthogonalization in the Muon optimizer, reaching a given high polynomial degree at lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations such as Polar Express and Gram Newton-Schulz. Circuits are built from short sequences of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers.

entry.title: Table Serialization Determines Which Relations Language Models Preserve

author.name: Junwei Ma, Arun Kumar Chithanar, Palash Goyal, Chul Lee

entry.summary: Diagnoses how table serialization format affects table lookup in instruction-tuned LLMs, rendering identical synthetic 256-cell tables in row-major and column-major form across five aspect ratios. The better format flips with table shape - row-major wins on tall tables by up to 54 points, column-major on wide tables by up to 59 - and error analysis reveals systematic relational biases.

entry.title: MemBubble: Benchmarking How Agent Memory Shapes LLM Response Diversity

author.name: Jiajun Tan, Fei Sun, Xinyu Ma, Shixuan Zhang, Du Su, Qi Cao, Daiting Shi, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: MemBubble is a benchmark of 1,000 instances built on preferences extracted from real user-assistant conversations, measuring how memory concentrates LLM response distributions even for queries outside stored preference scenarios. It addresses a gap left by synthetic-interaction evaluations of memory systems.

entry.title: RhinoNet: Unsupervised Learning for Phenoscaping and Generation of High Dimensional Point Clouds

author.name: Siddharth Viswanath, Hiren Madhu, Eddie Cavallin, Benjamin Jones, Alistair Wilkinson, Christopher Tape, Michael Perlmutter, Rex Ying, Ian Adelstein, Smita Krishnaswamy

entry.summary: RhinoNet is a simplicial complex-based point cloud network that produces geometry-preserving embeddings of high-dimensional point clouds, using Vietoris-Rips filtrations, simplicial wavelets, and an autoencoder latent space optimized to preserve optimal transport distances between point clouds. Applications include single-cell data cohorts, supporting phenotyping and generation.

entry.title: Functionalizing AI-Generated 3D Shapes via Interior Geometry Construction

author.name: Haoyu Tang, Fancheng Gao, Kan Chen, Peng Song

entry.summary: Addressing a practical weakness of AI 3D generation models like Hunyuan 3D and Meshy, which produce appealing exteriors but implausible interior geometry, this paper presents a method to construct functional interior geometry so generated shapes become valid for simulation and fabrication. The approach leverages the observation that a part's functional role implies smooth, simple interior geometry related to its external shape.

entry.title: O-SCD++: Replay-Free Online Scene Change Detection via Recursive Evidence Fusion

author.name: Chamuditha Jayanga Galappaththige, Jason Lai, Lloyd Windrim, Timothy Patten, Donald G. Dansereau, Niko Suenderhauf, Dimity Miller

entry.summary: O-SCD++ extends O-SCD, which treats scene change as a persistent property of a 3D Gaussian splatting reference map, by replacing per-frame refitting over all past cue maps with recursive evidence fusion. This removes the dominant computational bottleneck (>50% of runtime) while retaining the causal, replay-free online setting and state-of-the-art accuracy above 10 fps.

entry.title: Meta Inverse Prompting for Video Generative Models

author.name: Yerin Jung, Jongheon Jeong

entry.summary: Addresses the inversion problem for video generative models: recovering controllable textual conditions from a given video, enabling reverse workflows in media production. The method extends inverse prompting from images to video while avoiding the heavy computational cost of per-video optimization and capturing temporal dynamics beyond static appearance.

entry.title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion

author.name: Yushi Lan, Zeren Jiang, Koichi Namekata, Xingang Pan, Chuanxia Zheng, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: Holo4D combines feed-forward 4D reconstruction with video diffusion for monocular video reshooting from novel camera trajectories, using reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic 4D scaffold that grounds generation in observed geometry while letting the diffusion prior complete newly visible regions.

entry.title: PCXR-Copilot: Device-aware pediatric chest radiographic analysis with segmentation, suppression, and edema-related cues

author.name: Xueyang Li, Alec Girten, Peng Zeng, Mingze Jiang, Shaoyang Huang, Gelei Xu, Danny Z. Chen, Yiyu Shi, John N. Kheir

entry.summary: PCXR-Copilot provides device-aware analysis of pediatric chest radiographs for ICU patients, segmenting support devices and extracting edema-related cues obscured by anatomical and iatrogenic structures. It introduces PediaDeviceSeg-1K, a curated dataset of 1,000 radiographs with clinically grounded fine-grained device annotations, addressing pediatric data scarcity.

entry.title: UniJev: Separating Accuracy from Calibration in Trimodal System One Decision Models

author.name: Jianing Wang, Youwen Jian, Derong Wang, Jinyang Yu, Qingyi Si, Chuanyu Qin, Yanghua Xiao, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: UniJev is a trimodal framework that scores candidate answers across text, images, and video with a shared head under joint supervised training, designed to disentangle the effects of supervised fine-tuning from reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD). Findings show supervised decision training improves accuracy across all modalities, while existing RLCD algorithms barely change accuracy and affect visual calibration inconsistently.

entry.title: Learning the Dose Manifold: A Latent Diffusion Framework for Volumetric Dose Prediction in Automated Radiotherapy Treatment Planning

author.name: J. Boyer-Chammard, R. Vauclin, M. C. Biston, P. Maury, M. Gau, S. Stathakis, V. Gr\'egoire, N. Paragios, E. Deutsch, N. Komodakis

entry.summary: LaDose is a latent diffusion framework for fully volumetric 3D dose prediction in automated radiotherapy planning, addressing the slice-wise limitations of prior diffusion approaches and the unrealistic one-to-one anatomy-to-dose mapping assumption. It is evaluated within an end-to-end ATP pipeline rather than only on dose-matching metrics.

entry.title: Real-Time Radar Semantic and Panoptic Scene Understanding

author.name: Santosh Parit, Julia Hindel, Rohit Mohan, Georgi Pramatarov, Paul Newman, Daniele De Martini, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: StreamRPS enables real-time semantic and panoptic segmentation of FMCW spinning radar for autonomous driving, combining an automated label-generation pipeline via LiDAR scene completion with a streaming encoder-decoder network. Radar offers reliable 360-degree perception in adverse weather where cameras and LiDAR degrade, but scarce annotations have limited progress. The label-generation pipeline plus real-time network is a practical advance for all-weather perception.

entry.title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token

author.name: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim, Joon-Young Lee

entry.summary: VideoMaMa++ improves diffusion-based video matting by solving chunk-boundary inconsistencies that cause flickering edges and discontinuous transparency in long videos. It represents RGB and mask conditioning as separate interacting token streams and introduces a preserve-and-refine token to carry information across chunks. This enables temporally consistent matting beyond the 6-24 frame limits of diffusion backbones.

entry.title: Small Average Error, Wide Individual Error: General-Purpose LLMs Estimating Energy Intake from Meal Photos in a Feeding Trial

author.name: Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: Evaluates six frontier multimodal LLMs, including Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 variants, on estimating consumed energy from meal photos using 802 weighed-intake meals from a controlled feeding trial. Counterintuitively, before/after photo subtraction underestimates intake, and small average errors hide wide individual errors. It is a valuable reality check on using general-purpose LLMs for dietary assessment.

entry.title: Retrieval-triggered Action Projection Adjustment for Frozen VLA Policies: An Empirical Study and Failure Analysis

author.name: Jinming Wang, Ruiheng Zhang, Yong Wang, Zipan Xiong, Keyuan Luo

entry.summary: The paper presents RTPC, an auditable external-memory wrapper for frozen OpenVLA policies that retrieves stress-collected depth records and applies translation-only projection corrections. In CALVIN evaluations, the initial reduction in near-collision proxy events was not reproduced in an independent replication cohort, and the paper includes a candid failure analysis.

entry.title: AQUAACT: A Joystick-Level Underwater Teleoperation Dataset and Closed-Loop Benchmark

author.name: Zhenqi Wu, Trung Tien Dong, Aditya Penumarti, Mohamed A. Fouad, Menna A. Fouad, Mingyang Mao, Jane Jaejeong Shin, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: AQUAACT addresses the data scarcity blocking autonomous underwater manipulation by recording pilot joystick commands alongside camera observations, mirroring how underwater tasks are flown today, to create a dataset suitable for training vision-language-action models. It also provides a closed-loop benchmark to evaluate learned policies on underwater tasks such as inspection and reef survey. The dataset bridges the gap between land VLA progress and underwater deployment.

entry.title: PhantomTac: Hijacking Robotic Tactile Systems with Deploy-and-forget Tags

author.name: Binbin Zhang, Yifeng Zhang, Xiaomeng Chen, Dongyao Chen

entry.summary: The paper reveals PhantomTac, a physical vulnerability in magnetic tactile sensors where an attacker can spoof interpreted force readings by attaching a thin, battery-free magnetic tag to an object's surface. This deploy-and-forget attack exposes a security loophole in tactile perception systems increasingly used for dexterous closed-loop robot control.

entry.title: Certifiably Correct Fr\'echet Means in Orbit Spaaces

author.name: Dustin G. Mixon, Tom Needham, Nathan Willey

entry.summary: This paper studies Fréchet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions, a problem that is NP-hard in general, and develops tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations inspired by group synchronization. The authors provide pairwise-alignment certificates of global optimality, extend certification via semidefinite programming, and prove their certificate succeeds in a high-noise Gaussian regime where alignment fails. Applications include summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series.

entry.title: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities

author.name: Benedict Cummins-Mburu, Mariana Garcia Mejia, Oscar Heath, Sabrina Kreyzerman, Ellie Murray, Arusan Surendiran, Rohan Alexander
