entry.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Capability-Focused Evaluation with Structural Diversity for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Hongyin Zhang, Mingyi Xiang, Rongzhao Chen, Yankai Wang, Jialin Qiao, Xiangdong Huang, Xiaoou Ding, Chen Wang, Zhongyi Pei, Jianmin Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes CaFE, a refreshable evaluation extension for time series foundation models that enriches static benchmarks with structural diversity and replaces single-score evaluation with multi-dimensional, capability-oriented assessment. It profiles original benchmark data to generate diverse test distributions, countering benchmark-specific tuning. This addresses a growing problem as TSFMs become popular.

entry.title: Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints

author.name: Guannan Lai, Zi-Yang Bai, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: The paper shows that under tight generation, interaction, and memory budgets, existing lifelong-memory methods often offer little advantage over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents, because retrieving a relevant but ineffective memory consumes scarce context and hinders execution. It proposes learning the value of memories, i.e., deciding what is worth retaining and reusing when resources are scarce.

entry.title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models

author.name: Natraj Raman, Saumitra Mishra, Vamsi Potluru, Sumitra Ganesh

entry.summary: A position/research-agenda paper from a JPMorgan-affiliated team arguing that financial foundation models require structured-data-first, modular architectures to handle partial observability, asynchronous events, regime changes, and rare high-consequence states. It critiques both incompatible specialist models and monolithic multi-domain alternatives on governance and representation grounds.

entry.title: StebBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents

author.name: Hossein A. Rahmani, Bin Wu, Chaeeun Lee, Fanghua Ye, Sahan Bulathwela, Sujay Kumar Jauhar, Marzieh Fadaee, Nick Craswell, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: StepBench is a benchmark of 6,885 verified wikiHow procedures across 81 open-domain categories, with five diagnostic task types (withheld, incorrect, shuffled steps, next-step generation, full-plan generation) that distinguish error types rather than scoring only final plans. It examines how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Tabular Learning via Hypergraph Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Geon Lee, Kyungho Kim, Dongwon Choi, Juyeon Kim, Shinhwan Kang, Kijung Shin

entry.summary: TABHGR+ uses LLM-generated rules to weakly label and group table rows, then refines noisy labels via hypergraph-based label propagation, enabling efficient zero-shot tabular prediction that exploits inter-row dependencies. This improves on row-wise prompting approaches in both cost and accuracy for healthcare and finance-style data.

entry.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs

author.name: Lei Tian, Chunzheng Zhu, Kai Wu, Yifan Zhang, Haihua Yang

entry.summary: PACE targets ViT-free native multimodal LLMs that tokenize pixel patches directly, showing empirically that unlike ViT-based models they tolerate aggressive visual token compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. The paper proposes an analysis pipeline and Pareto-adaptive compression tailored to this setting.

entry.title: Does AI-Assisted Development Homogenize Software? An Empirical Study of Code Similarity, Quality, and Evolution

author.name: Luciano Marchezan, Romain Lefeuvre, Kevin Delcourt, Benoit Combemale, Houari Sahraoui

entry.summary: The study analyzes 50 long-lived Java and Python open-source projects across pre-LLM, LLM-assisted, and detected agentic development eras using Software Heritage snapshots, measuring semantic and syntactic code similarity, SonarQube quality metrics, and evolution characteristics. It empirically investigates whether AI-assisted development reduces code diversity or degrades quality.

entry.title: Analyzing Repetition and Interference Effects in Memory-Constrained User Simulators

author.name: Cara Su-Yi Leong, Nicholas Tomlin, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: This study evaluates memory-constrained user simulators against two well-documented human memory phenomena: repetition improving retention and interference from competing information. While some simulators match human overall accuracy and replicate effect magnitudes, none match human error patterns at the question level: humans misremember facts whereas models forget them. The released benchmark gives future simulator work a behavioral-parity target.

entry.title: Towards Reinforcement Learning for Space Robotics: Fast Training and Reliable Real-World Transfer

author.name: Abhishek Naik, Michael Wu, Michael O'Sullivan, Colin Bellinger, Yunli Wang

entry.summary: This work demonstrates a fast simulation-based RL training framework with minimal hardware requirements whose learned policies transfer reliably to real robots. A quadruped learned to traverse diverse real-world terrains, including at a lunar-analog facility, after under 20 minutes of training on a single consumer GPU. It showcases practical sim-to-real RL for space robotics applications.

entry.title: Cooperation Without Shared Rewards via Reciprocal Q-Augmentation

author.name: Francesco Morri, Adel Abusitta, Quentin Cappart, Margarida Carvalho

entry.summary: This multi-agent RL paper introduces Reciprocal Q-Augmentation (RQA), which uses a latent-variable opponent model to augment an agent's Q-function with estimates of how its actions affect others, enabling sustained cooperation in general-sum games without access to other agents' rewards or internal states. It targets the well-known failure mode where a single defection collapses agents into welfare-suboptimal Nash equilibria.

entry.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis

author.name: Xiaoyu Wu, Zhaoxin Yu, Xinglin Xiao, Nan Xu

entry.summary: TIRE is a framework for scalable synthesis of physics reasoning training data that instantiates problems top-down from reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions, with reliable execution producing verifiable numerical answers. This avoids hallucination risks of pure LLM text-based synthesis while retaining expert-style control over laws, conditions, and scenarios.

entry.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research

author.name: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Han Zhao, Linxiao Yang, Jie Li, Changjun Jiang

entry.summary: NeuroAct is an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding that runs dual loops over EEG foundation models, task-specific predictors, and model combinations. An inner loop of research, development, and review roles uses evidence on signal structure, representations, and training dynamics to test hypotheses and select interventions, aimed at explaining performance and generalization gaps rather than blind search.

entry.title: When Interpretations Persist: Downstream Influence in Gaze-Aware Assistants

author.name: Mingcong Ding, Chenyan Zhang, Zhuojiang Cai, Dongyang Guo, Babette B\"uhler, Enkelejda Kasneci

entry.summary: This controlled study examines whether interpretation records carried in an AI assistant's memory influence later predictions in gaze-aware streaming assistance. Findings show free-form interpretations amplify historical influence in both helpful and harmful directions, while evidence-bounded interpretation formats preserve distinguishing behavior and reduce harmful influence of wrong histories.

entry.title: A "feature ODE" describing the learning behavior of shallow MLPs on simple functions

author.name: Joseph Turnbull, Berkan Ottlik, Jamie Simon

entry.summary: Proposes a simplified ordinary differential equation, the feature ODE, meant to describe the gradient-flow learning dynamics of two-layer MLPs on anisotropic Gaussian data, and shows empirically that real MLPs learning Hermite polynomials and staircases roughly follow its loss trajectories. The surprisingly close agreement despite large simplifications is discussed and speculated upon.

entry.title: AirMPA: A Meteorology-to-Pollution Adapter for Global Air Quality Forecasting

author.name: Yiheng Wang, Kai Zheng, Yuetan Lin, Fanglu Fan, Chenliang Tao, Guochao Chen, Hongliang Zhang, Hao Li

entry.summary: Presents AirMPA, a decoupled autoregressive deep learning framework that forecasts 13 atmospheric pollutants globally at 0.4-degree resolution by adapting meteorological fields and emission priors to pollution prediction, rather than entangling meteorology and pollutants in one model. It aims to overcome the cost and parameterization limits of numerical forecasting systems.

entry.title: Keep the Lineages Alive: Diversity-Preserving SMC for Diffusion LLM Decoding

author.name: Minoo Ahmadi, Seyedarmin Azizi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: This work improves sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for masked diffusion language models by preserving particle lineage diversity during resampling, avoiding the duplication-and-discard failure of multinomial resampling. It works with both internal confidence rewards and external process reward models and requires no post-training. It matters because diffusion LLM inference is an emerging area needing better decoding methods.

entry.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization

author.name: Suwan Yoon, Seongryong Jung, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: APSD improves self-distillation policy optimization for LLM post-training by mixing student and self-teacher distributions asymmetrically based on rollout correctness: interpolation preserves successful behaviors on correct rollouts, while extrapolation beyond the self-teacher strengthens correction on incorrect ones. The paper supports the design with divergence decomposition and gradient analysis. It targets a real failure mode of naive self-teacher matching.

entry.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness

author.name: Caixin Kang, Sitong Gong, Tianyu Yan, Kaipeng Zhang, Yoichi Sato, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: ZhenhuanBench is a 1,592-item benchmark for detecting mock politeness (polite form, hostile intent), built from expert commentary on a Chinese drama, covering speaker intent, emotion-language mismatch, and listener uptake. GPT-6 Astra, an existing OpenAI model released in September 2026, leads at 73.48% overall with weaker listener-reaction performance at 58.37%. With 338 gold traces, an 8B model beat teacher distillation, and subsequent RL saturated, with chance correction shrinking the estimated recoverable gap substantially.

entry.title: ALIGN: Aligning Condition Estimation and Expression in Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning

author.name: Zechen Wang, Zhenqi Qiu, Houlong Xiong, Suohang Zhang, Yiyu Ren, Wanting Xu, Hongfei Niu, Chengyang He, Ge Sun, Ran Cheng, Qian Zhu

entry.summary: ALIGN improves Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning for vision-language-action policies trained on mixed-quality human demonstration data by directly predicting categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space rather than routing noisy thresholded advantage scores through prompts. This strengthens the conditioning signal in both construction and incorporation into the action vector field. The result is better exploitation of retries, recoveries, and failures in manipulation datasets.

entry.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction

author.name: Murat Guney Kemal, Robert Lieck

entry.summary: This work studies whether meaningful hierarchical structure can emerge from compression alone, introducing a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively composes sequences into multi-level representations. Using unsupervised grammar induction as a testbed where hierarchies can be explicitly evaluated, the authors probe whether reconstruction objectives favor compositional structure. It speaks to a core representation-learning question about emergent hierarchy without structural supervision.

entry.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting

author.name: Zehao Wang, Jianpeng Yao, Yuping Wang, Yiping Li, Jiaqi Li, Zhixu Li, Kanghoon Lee, Jinfeng Wang, Cong Liu, Zhaowei Tan, Jinkyoo Park, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-robot social navigation framework combining uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting across robots with robust decision making, targeting safety under occlusions and out-of-distribution scenarios. Cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion predicts future occupancy grids to improve coordination. Addresses a known weakness of naively extending single-robot RL navigation to multi-robot settings.

entry.title: SAGE-CP: When Marginal Coverage Hides Route-Conditional Failures in Adaptive VLM Ensembles

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Shows that adaptive VLM ensembles with early exits can satisfy marginal conformal coverage while failing badly on individual computational routes, quantifying the worst-case conditional coverage given route prevalence. SAGE-CP freezes routing and applies Mondrian split conformal calibration separately to early-exit and escalated groups to restore route-conditional guarantees. A useful theoretical and practical contribution to uncertainty-aware ensembles.

entry.title: LatLM: Line-Parallel Language Models with Deferred Commitment

author.name: Shaorong Zhang, Shiyuan Li, Longxuan Yu, Greg Ver Steeg

entry.summary: Introduces LatLM, which makes commitment schedules an adaptive decoding-time choice for line-parallel language models, scoring eligible frontier tokens on a 2D lattice and committing confident candidates while deferring unready ones. This avoids premature commitments and cascading errors caused by fixed schedules like LCLM. One forward pass supervises entire sampled trajectories, supporting training.

entry.title: Inducing Fourier Geometry: A Smoothness Prior Imposes Approximate Translation Equivariance in Multimodal Stellar Embeddings

author.name: Ilay Kamai, Alex M. Bronstein, Hagai B. Perets

entry.summary: The authors introduce a graph-Laplacian smoothness prior that encourages learned representations to vary smoothly over a known physical parameter space, which in the continuum limit selects Laplacian eigenfunctions and predicts Fourier-like geometry corresponding to approximate translation symmetry. Applied to multimodal stellar embeddings across six astronomical surveys, the prior induces Toeplitz Gram structure and sinusoidal modes along stellar parameters.

entry.title: Revisiting Smoothed Online Learning: Competitive Ratio, Dynamic Regret with Switching Cost, and Best of Both Worlds

author.name: Lijun Zhang, Linzhe He, Wei Jiang, Shiyin Lu

entry.summary: This paper develops improved algorithms for smoothed online learning with better competitive ratios, optimal dynamic regret with switching costs, and best-of-both-worlds guarantees. It shows naive hitting-cost minimization achieves surprisingly strong competitive ratios for polyhedral and quadratic-growth functions, with matching lower bounds in some cases. The results unify competitive analysis and regret minimization for a broad class of costs.

entry.title: TideKV: Delayed KV Eviction via Layer-Wise Chunked Prefill for Memory-Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Yu Wang, Zhu Wang, Ning Hu, Yifan Guo, Xiu Ma, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: TideKV is an on-GPU cache-construction architecture for long-context LLM inference that performs layer-major delayed KV eviction, processing all prompt chunks per Transformer layer and retaining full-prompt KV only for the active layer. This lowers peak prefill memory without the degradation risk of chunk-level eviction that selects before observing the full prompt. It addresses a real bottleneck in long-context serving systems.

entry.title: CARTA: Self-Supervised Reusable Transaction Embeddings via Heterogeneous Tokenization and Cross-Attention

author.name: Shreyas K. Chandrahas, Jose Munoz, Satish Babu Bellapu

entry.summary: CARTA is a self-supervised encoder producing compact 16-dimensional transaction embeddings without fraud labels, using type-specific projections and learned embedding tables for high-cardinality identifiers, trained with token excision and InfoNCE contrastive loss. The frozen embedding supports label-efficient fraud probing — at 1% of labels on IEEE-CIS it beats raw features at 100% — and unsupervised risk stratification. Practical relevance to payment fraud detection where labels are scarce and expensive.

entry.title: Polynomial Learning of Positive ReLU Networks under Gaussian Inputs

author.name: Zhijie Zheng

entry.summary: The paper gives a learning guarantee for one-hidden-layer bias-free ReLU networks with nonnegative output weights under Gaussian inputs, allowing hidden directions to be arbitrarily close or linearly dependent. A width-k target can be approximated to squared error epsilon by a network of width at most k + min(k, d) with polynomial sample and computation cost in d, k, 1/epsilon, and log(1/delta). The argument combines implicit high-order moments with a direction cover robust to heavy noise atoms.

entry.title: FracTS: Hierarchical and Autoregressive Time Series Generation

author.name: Jiayu Li, Umair Afzal, Zilong Zhao, Milad Abdollahzadeh, Uzair Javaid, Biplab Sikdar

entry.summary: FracTS adapts fractal generative modeling from 2D images to 1D multivariate time series, learning a hierarchical coarse-to-fine autoregressive model that captures global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales. This mitigates common autoregressive weaknesses such as low diversity, error accumulation, and poor long-range dependency modeling. Applications include privacy-preserving data sharing, augmentation, and stress testing.

entry.title: Neural Video Coding under Limited Delay: Theoretical Optimality and System Design

author.name: Likun Cai, Jun Chen, Ashish Khisti

entry.summary: This work formalizes rate-distortion benefits of allowing limited frame delay in neural video compression, using clique factorization of Markov networks for rigorous analysis. It proposes Graph-Factored Sequential Coding (GFSC), a principled framework treating delay as an explicit design parameter rather than fixing zero-frame delay.

entry.title: PnP-CF: A Consensus Flow-Matching Solver for General Inverse Problems

author.name: Dibyanshu Kumar, Magda Gregorova

entry.summary: PnP-CF extends a flow-based plug-and-play framework to nonlinear inverse problems, including learned neural forward operators, by combining a flow-matching denoiser with ADMM-like dual updates and a time-adaptive pullback onto the flow probability path. The approach targets consensus between the solver and the generative sampler for high-quality reconstructions.

entry.title: On Learning Expand-and-Sparsify Representations

author.name: Alireza Asghari, Parikshit Ram, Kaushik Sinha

entry.summary: This work studies expand-and-sparsify representations, where inputs are lifted to a higher dimension by a linear map and truncated to the k largest coordinates. Prior theory required exponentially large expansion with random maps, so the authors investigate what gradient-learned maps gain as a function of expansion width, using a rigorous 121-task benchmark protocol with median comparisons and Wilcoxon tests.

entry.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps

author.name: Jean-Loup Dupret, Patrick Cheridito

entry.summary: This work develops a deep learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control with jump-diffusions, based on the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. It separates adjoint learning from policy improvement using pathwise adjoint labels obtained by backpropagating rewards along simulated trajectories, avoiding repeated differentiation through the full dynamics.

entry.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding

author.name: Zhuofan Josh Ying, Guanglong Sun, Nolan Ho, Kieran Liu, Rui Yang, Andrew Chen, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Pony Ma, Hossein Adeli

entry.summary: This work shows parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) can adapt very large pretrained multimodal backbones for brain encoding with few trainable parameters, sidestepping the difficulty of training on scarce, costly neural data. It also exploits the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints per pass, cutting feature-extraction cost. This makes large-model-based neural response prediction far more practical.

entry.title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Cassandra Parent, Isha Agarwal, Kumail Alhamoud, Charikleia Moraitaki, Rafiya Javed, Walter Gerych, Marzyeh Ghassemi

entry.summary: SPELUNKA is an automated, inference-time framework for discovering unanticipated distributional biases in vision-language models for retrieval tasks, without pre-specified labeled subgroups, human supervision, or fine-tuning. Given a concept of interest, it generates captions, extracts entities, and uses frequency-based detection plus semantic filtering to surface spurious associations. This extends bias auditing beyond known bias categories.

entry.title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction

author.name: Josef Biberstein, Sertac Karaman

entry.summary: OrTeN applies neural inverse rendering to jointly reconstruct a textured digital terrain map and correct orbital camera trajectory errors directly from calibrated line-scan satellite imagery, replacing complex multi-view stereo pipelines. This has applications in planetary exploration tasks such as landing site selection and terrain-relative navigation.

entry.title: Reducing double-dipping in single-cell topic models with three-way count splitting

author.name: Zheng Qu

entry.summary: Identifies that count-splitting corrections for reusing single-cell RNA-seq counts fail when a neural encoder has seen the tested gene's held-out counts, with naive and two-way splits rejecting 36-38% of null gene-topic pairs at a nominal 5% level. The proposed three-way split with beta-binomial thinning reduces false rejections to 7.7% on a 104,400-cell lupus cohort, and also works for LDVAE and scETM.

entry.title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: D. Sorokin, A. Granovskiy, M. Stokolesov, E. Adishchev, M. Nurgaliev, G. Subbotin

entry.summary: The authors reconstruct partially observed electron density profiles in tokamak plasmas by inferring coefficients of a physics-based 1D particle transport equation, using a Fourier Neural Operator surrogate of the transport solver as a fast differentiable forward model. This enables real-time gradient-based reconstruction with uncertainty quantification from reflectometry and interferometry data. They compare four UQ methods including ensembles, Laplace approximation, and Metropolis-Hastings.

entry.title: Efficiency Measured in English: Tokeniser Coverage Bounds Small Language Models on Indic Scripts

author.name: Anna Pramod

entry.summary: This paper shows that commonly reported memory-efficiency figures for small language models are implicitly measured in English and fail to transfer across languages. Across eleven Indic scripts, TinyLlama-1.1B's tokenizer emits 22.60 tokens per Kannada word versus 1.34 for English, with 0-2% codepoint coverage for several scripts and fertility at the UTF-8 byte-fallback ceiling. The authors argue multilingual efficiency claims must account for tokenizer coverage rather than a single English-based memory number.

entry.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction

author.name: Yotam Peled, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: LiftDiff applies a guided discrete denoising diffusion model to discover quantum error-correcting codes by generating base matrices over a group algebra that are expanded into lifted product qLDPC codes. The reverse diffusion is guided by an energy function evaluating code properties such as girth, degree, and sparsity, offering a generative alternative to algebraic constructions for high-rate, sufficient-distance codes.

entry.title: Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surface Reconstruction via Additive Martingales

author.name: Haochen Luo, Sifan Lin, Xiaolong Luo, An Binh Minh, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu

entry.summary: AddMart is a few-shot framework for reconstructing implied volatility surfaces from sparse option quotes that satisfies static no-arbitrage conditions by construction. Instead of predicting volatilities directly, it maps quotes to non-negative increment densities of an exponential additive martingale from which valid risk-neutral marginals are recovered, baking arbitrage constraints into the architecture rather than via regularization penalties.

entry.title: A Probabilistic, Rotation-Preserving Kernel Operator Surrogate for Continuum-Robot Design Spaces

author.name: Branden Frieden, Alan Kuntz, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: The authors build an uncertainty-aware operator-learning surrogate for tendon-driven continuum robots using a nonstationary Gaussian process kernel whose metric is learned by a neural network from mechanics-aware design coordinates. Orientation is reconstructed directly on SO(3), preserving valid material frames and enabling sequential simulator acquisition across robot designs.

entry.title: EGIP: An Evidence-Grounded Interaction Protocol for Clinical Agents

author.name: Zecheng Ren, Ruichen Cong, Yi Min Chen, Jing Zhang, Feiyang Chen, Wutong Zhang, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, Jiong Lou, Jie LI, Qun Jin

entry.summary: Proposes EGIP, a standardized interaction protocol for clinical LLM agents that enforces role-specific information boundaries, exposes diagnostic actions without leaking their results, and retrieves examination findings from stored records, so that measured accuracy reflects reasoning rather than protocol artifacts. This separation enables cleaner comparison of clinical agent performance.

entry.title: Assertion and Belief: Moore's Paradox in Language Models

author.name: Anshun Asher Zheng, Weili Cao, Fangcong Yin, David Beaver, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: Presents the first test of Moore's paradox in LLMs, evaluating 12 models on sentences like 'It is raining, but I don't believe it' that can be true yet cannot be sensibly asserted. Models largely recognize the infelicity, judgments track the speech act rather than memorized form, and the authors model the behavior using the Rational Speech Act framework.

entry.title: Self-Consistency of Entity Sets and Citations in a Deep Research System under Repeated Prompting

author.name: Lauri Pyk\"al\"a, Kimmo K. Kaski

entry.summary: Measures the self-consistency of a commercial deep research agent across ten identical runs of an open-ended cybersecurity prompt, using named-entity and citation overlap as proxies. Findings show extremely low stability: median pairwise entity Jaccard of 0.12 and citation Jaccard below 0.02.

entry.title: ASTOR: Benchmarking and Improving Autoformulation for Soft-Constraint Optimization with a Formal Grammar

author.name: Amer Goel, Yeganeh Alimohammadi, Andrew Daw

entry.summary: Introduces ASTOR, a benchmark and method for autoformulation of decision problems with soft constraints, an aspect neglected by prior LLM-to-optimization work that focuses on hard constraints. It uses a formal grammar to translate natural-language problem descriptions into executable optimization models that explicitly represent preferences.

entry.title: Where Does Rhetorical Distortion Live? A Multi-Platform, Multi-Language Measurement of Influencer Content

author.name: Xucheng Yu, Jiangping Chen, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: This study operationalizes rhetorical distortion, where accurate facts are framed with inflated significance, urgency, or catastrophe, across five literature-grounded dimensions measured via a three-tier pipeline combining bilingual lexical rules, negative filters, and LLM verification. Applied across multiple platforms and languages, it probes whether distortion originates with the creator, topic, platform, or audience.

entry.title: STLQ: Spatio-Topological Linkage Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search

author.name: Kuizhi Liu, Junying Zhang, Xindi Ma, Xiangyu Wang, Qi Jiang, Sheng Gao, Chen Gong, Jianfeng Ma

entry.summary: STLQ is a shallow multi-codebook quantization method for approximate nearest neighbor search that organizes each IVF cluster as a directed forest, enabling a linked encoding phase that re-encodes vectors using local references rather than independently. This topological structure improves compression and asymmetric distance computation efficiency for large-scale retrieval.

entry.title: PACE-Mem: Prefix-Aware Complementary Evidence for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Shidu Ren, Rong-cheng Tu, Hang Zhou, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: PACE-Mem improves multimodal agent memory retrieval by constructing a complementary evidence sequence whose length is determined adaptively from the same selection trajectory, addressing overlap between retrieved memories and fixed retrieval depth. Query-guided pooling combines records within clips to compute relevance scores for structured memories.

entry.title: MESS: Multi-Exposure Sequence Synthesis for Generalizable Image Enhancement

author.name: Ruodai Cui, Shuaizheng Liu, Rongyuan Wu, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: MESS synthesizes realistic multi-exposure training pairs to overcome the scarcity of aligned paired data for adverse-illumination enhancement tasks like low-light correction and backlit enhancement. By better modeling complex illumination conditions and camera imaging pipelines, the framework improves generalization of enhancement models across scenarios.

entry.title: Video-Language Entailment for Video Similarity Estimation

author.name: Benedetta Liberatori, Lorenzo Vaquero, Elisa Ricci, Paolo Rota

entry.summary: Introduces VICE, a dual-branch framework that uses large multimodal models for concept-based video similarity estimation via cross-video reasoning, where each branch processes one video and entailment between captions mediates comparison. This fills a gap since LMMs are mostly trained on single-video objectives and prior work focused only on global similarity.

entry.title: VTF900: A 900-Subject Visible-Thermal Face Recognition Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Jacob Abaare, Bianca Ianetta, Cedric Nimpa Fondje, Shuowen Hu, Benjamin S. Riggan

entry.summary: Introduces VTF900, a large-scale visible-thermal face recognition benchmark with 900 subjects and paired imagery covering expression, pose, and occlusion variation, roughly an order of magnitude larger than prior galleries of about 100 subjects. It enables statistically meaningful large-gallery evaluation for verification and identification protocols.

entry.title: LateMatch: Breaking the Interaction Bottleneck via Cacheable Matching for Efficient Visual Localization

author.name: Mohammad Omama, Aeyan Ashraf, Sandeep Chinchali

entry.summary: LateMatch restructures deep feature matchers by deferring inter-image interaction to final layers, enabling caching of database-side computations so a query against K database images no longer requires K full network passes. This paradigm shift targets edge deployment of visual localization.

entry.title: LEVI: Benchmarking Visual Identity Fidelity with Verifiable Low-Entropy Constructs

author.name: Xiao Ma, Zhonghao Zhan, Hamed Haddadi, Qi Chen

entry.summary: LEVI is a benchmark for evaluating whether generative models respect exact identity constraints, using low-entropy visual identities defined by compact facts and explicit rules so identity violations are distinguishable from permissible appearance variation. It formalizes identity fidelity probabilistically via Visual Identity Spaces specifying admissible identity values.

entry.title: Rethinking Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting: A Few-Shot Learning Perspective on Overfitting Prevention

author.name: Lejia Ye, Bin Wu, Jingjing Gao, Yiyang Wu, Xiaohu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper reframes sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting from a few-shot learning perspective, treating each Gaussian primitive as a neuron and applying deep learning regularization techniques to combat overfitting and geometry degradation. The unified view aims to replace the fragmented local fixes (data quality or regularization alone) used previously.

entry.title: PnP-Transformer: A Neural Pose Solver for 6D Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Emirkan Burak Yilmaz, Yakup Genc

entry.summary: PnP-Transformer replaces classical iterative PnP-RANSAC solvers with an iterative-free, differentiable transformer that regresses 6D pose from semi-dense 2D-3D correspondences and confidence scores. It achieves 41.2% mean AR at 0.46 s/object across seven BOP benchmark datasets, beating most prior solvers. This matters for real-time robotics and zero-shot pose pipelines.

entry.title: Wan-Alpha++: Animating a Single RGBA Asset into Controllable Transparent Video Effects

author.name: Haotian Dong, Xin Wang, Wenjing Wang, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Yan Tina Luximon, Ping Li, Wanchao Su, Ke Xu, Di Lin

entry.summary: Wan-Alpha++ generates controllable RGBA video from a single transparent asset, addressing the entanglement of RGB and alpha distributions and the failure of first-frame conditioning when boundary frames are fully transparent. It targets compositable visual effects for filmmaking, games, and content production. This extends RGBA video generation with practical controllability.

entry.title: MRI Reconstruction Risk Estimation from Inference Dynamics

author.name: Tamir Shor, Alex Bronstein

entry.summary: This work shows that the intermediate inference trajectories of iterative MRI reconstruction networks carry a predictive signal about realized reconstruction error (log-NMSE). Trajectory features are condensed into a 16-dimensional descriptor and mapped to risk via a ridge readout, with strong in-distribution prediction but backbone-dependent behavior under zero-shot shift, including readout reversal. The findings inform uncertainty estimation and safe deployment of reconstruction models.

entry.title: DenseHap: Dense Hand Haptic Estimation from Monocular Images

author.name: Junhan Xue, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias

entry.summary: DenseHap is a unified end-to-end framework that estimates hand distance fields, contact detection, pressure analysis, and hand reconstruction from a single monocular image, addressing dorsal-side misclassification and modality fragmentation in prior work. It supports scalable annotation of hand-object interactions for dexterous robotic manipulation. Unifying multiple haptic modalities from one RGB view is a useful step for robot learning data pipelines.

entry.title: InfiniDream: Open-Ended Photorealistic 3D Worlds Through Procedural Generation

author.name: Yi-Chuan Huang, Hao-Jen Chien, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yu-Lun Liu, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: InfiniDream is a VLM-driven framework for open-ended procedural generation of photorealistic 3D worlds, going beyond predefined asset factories and APIs via Symbolically Constrained Asset Generation. It combines existing procedural algorithms with VLM code generation to create novel, editable, diverse assets and scenes. This is relevant to synthetic data creation, game development, and simulation.

entry.title: GliomaINK: A Tumor and Anatomy Conditioned Flow Matching Framework for 3D MRI Sequence Synthesis in Glioma Patients

author.name: Moinak Bhattacharya, Annie Singh, Mohammad Chaudhry, Prateek Prasanna, Gagandeep Singh

entry.summary: GliomaINK is an anatomy-guided conditional flow matching framework for synthesizing missing 3D brain MRI sequences in glioma patients, using a 3D SwinUNETR velocity field with a topology-preserving auxiliary loss. Trained on 1,083 BraTS-AG patients and tested on an in-house clinical cohort, it evaluates downstream tumor segmentation, IDH1 mutation prediction, and survival. Clinically grounded validation strengthens the work.

entry.title: InteractAgent: Agentic Human Motion Interaction with Memory-Augmented Reflection

author.name: Tao Zhang, Senhe Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Yujia Zhang, Dong Gong

entry.summary: InteractAgent is an agentic multimodal LLM system for long-horizon human-scene interaction that plans, executes, observes, and reflects in a closed loop, using a single MLLM as planner and evaluator with a frozen MotionLLM executor. Online observation enables step-wise recovery from compounding errors without paired scene-motion training or explicit 3D preprocessing. This improves generalization to novel layouts and open-vocabulary goals.

entry.title: Length-Independent Stability and $L_2$-Gain Certificates for Chains of Delayed Neural Modules

author.name: \"Omer Faruk \.I\c{s}canl{\i}

entry.summary: Derives stability and L2-gain certificates whose size is independent of the number of modules in open chains and rings of delayed neural modules with slope-restricted activations. A Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional construction reduces certification of arbitrarily long chains to a single two-module cell verified by one LMI. This enables scalable formal guarantees for networks of repeated neural modules.

entry.title: Learning Whole-Body Kinetic Coordination for Wheeled-Quadruped Long-Range Throwing

author.name: Qinglian Wu, Yidian Hu, Weiqi Fan, Yutian Zhang, Siyuan Ma, Jiaqi Zhai, Wei Dong, Li Xu

entry.summary: Presents a whole-body coordination framework for wheeled-quadruped manipulators performing long-range throwing on unstructured terrain, combining kinetic-chain arm modeling, SQP-based trajectory optimization, and reference-guided reinforcement learning for base motion. The optimized arm reaches 12.75 m/s release speed on a stationary base with substantial throwing distance. A distinctive and demanding whole-body control task with delivery and retrieval applications.

entry.title: FLASH-CBF-RRT: Fast Lipschitz-Adaptive Safe Horizon CBF Steering for Certified Motion Planning

author.name: Mani Amani, Hesam Mojtahedi, Reza Akhavian, Nikolay Atanasov, Ki Myung Brian Lee

entry.summary: This work accelerates control-barrier-function-based steering in RRT-style planners by computing a time horizon over which CBF-filtered velocity can be applied constantly, using closed-form kinematic bounds on collision clearance. This reduces the number of expensive CBF-QP evaluations compared to prior CBF-RRT approaches while retaining safety certification.

entry.title: Energy-Score Stabilized Attentive Mixture-Density Policy: A Lightweight Approach to Multimodal Robot Motion

author.name: Sachiya Fujita, Hideyuki Ichiwara, Shigeki Sugano, Tetsuya Ogata

entry.summary: The paper introduces an attentive mixture-density policy for multimodal visuomotor trajectory prediction that outputs Gaussian mixture parameters in a single forward pass. It replaces negative log-likelihood training with an Energy Score (sum of 1D CRPS under diagonal covariance) to avoid MDN singularities and gradient instabilities. The result is a lightweight model handling multimodal actions with low inference cost and strong generalization from limited demonstrations.

entry.title: Compositional Humanoid Manipulation through Isomorphic Teleoperation and Independent Skill Routing

author.name: Yiming Wang, Peixian Yang, Lifeng Zhuo, Lai Wei, Xinling Du, Kun Song, Weiming Wang, Daolin Ma

entry.summary: The paper introduces HS-MoDP, a semantic mixture-of-experts diffusion policy that composes separately demonstrated arm skills via independent semantic routing over a shared expert pool, integrated with a locomotion controller through alternating manipulation and repositioning stages. It also presents G1Exo, an isomorphic exoskeleton for collecting whole-body contact manipulation demonstrations.

entry.title: Tactile In-Hand Object Rotation: A Comparative Study of Hand Morphology in Simulation and Hardware

author.name: Wenhao He, Max Yang, Chenghua Lu, Yijiong Lin, David A. W. Barton, Nathan F. Lepora

entry.summary: The study compares anthropomorphic versus symmetric finger arrangements of the LEAP Hand, integrated with TacTip tactile sensors, for continuous in-hand object rotation under a shared reinforcement learning framework. Simulation across 12 unseen objects and hardware experiments on 10 objects quantify how hand morphology and tactile feedback affect rotational progress, finger participation, and loading.

entry.title: Physics-informed machine learning: a hybrid lens for fluid dynamics

author.name: Romit Maulik

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence piece describing a neural network approach that bridges Lagrangian and Eulerian perspectives to transform sparse observations into physically accurate, high-resolution reconstructions of complex and chaotic fluid motion. It serves as a research briefing on the accompanying TrajectoryFlowNet work.

entry.title: Verifying Human-Written Reasoning References

author.name: Ali Ansari, Farhana Ferdousi Liza

entry.summary: This paper examines whether human-written reasoning chains used as evaluation references for AI systems are themselves logically sound, combining entailment checking against cited premise sets, full-premise rechecking, and failure attribution. It finds prior neuro-symbolic evaluations rarely verified whether reference step conclusions are entailed by their cited premises.

entry.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency

author.name: Chenghao Liu, Wei Fan, Jindong Han, Dongjie Wang, Aniket Mahanti, Pengyang Wang, Hao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes TimesJev, a System 1 style model for time series reasoning that makes instant decisions without long chains of thought, formalizing a sufficiency condition for mapping raw numeric series into a decision-model-compatible embedding. This targets the latency cost of LLM-based time series reasoning over long inputs.

entry.title: ScopeMem: Latent Memory That Learns Where to Revise Frozen GUI Agents

author.name: Zhicheng Zheng, Cheng Zhang, Shengping Yu, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: The paper shows that gains from latent prefix-vector memory for frozen GUI agents stem primarily from action revision rather than encoded history, and that step-wise cross-entropy training revises unscoped, breaking 8-13 percent of initially correct answers that aggregate metrics hide. ScopeMem introduces scoped revision that preserves correct default decisions while repairing errors, using a frozen vision-language model.

entry.title: SPIRIT: Sparse Physics-Informed Inverse Rendering for SAR Imaging

author.name: Yimeng Liu, Maolin Gan, Jingkai Lin, Jialuo Du, Mi Zhang, Zhichao Cao

entry.summary: SPIRIT is a physics-informed inverse rendering framework for sparse-aperture SAR that reconstructs an explicit 3D surface rather than enhancing formed images, addressing the ill-posed inverse problems created by reduced measurement collection. It applies differentiable rendering ideas to radio-frequency imaging under the speed-resolution trade-off.

entry.title: Who Plans, Who Edits? Verified, Cost-Aware Division of Labor for LLM-Driven Analog Layout Repair

author.name: Xilai Dai, Saeed Mohammadi

entry.summary: The paper studies cost-aware division of labor between planning and editing LLMs for analog circuit layout repair, with sign-off tools (LVS, DRC) verifying every edit so failing layouts are never accepted. Across 182 blind runs on three real designs including a production high-voltage DAC, cheap models could execute plans but rarely succeed alone, quantifying when model upgrades are worth their cost. It brings rigorous verification-grounded agentic methodology into EDA.

entry.title: ControlJEPA: Principled Trajectory Regularization via Lyapunov Tube Loss

author.name: Thai-Khanh Nguyen, Nhi Y. Pham, Uyen N. B. Vo, Thieu N. Vo, Cuong Pham, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: ControlJEPA introduces a trajectory regularization framework for next-token models based on a discrete-time Lyapunov contraction condition from Input-to-State Stability theory, with a Lyapunov Tube Loss penalizing deviations on a scale-invariant measure. It provides explicit bounds on transversal energy, temporal variance, and tube width under partial-ISS conditions.

entry.title: M-JEPA: Predictive Self-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs with Scaffold-Shift Evaluation on Tox21

author.name: Karthik Iyer, Nasser Sabar

entry.summary: The authors adapt JEPA-style predictive self-supervision to molecular graphs by masking chemically coherent connected subgraphs and training a context encoder to regress EMA-teacher target embeddings. They also introduce a leakage-resistant, compute-matched three-phase evaluation protocol with scaffold-shift on Tox21 to test transfer under realistic distribution shift.

entry.title: Rubrics Beyond Evaluation: Exploiting Rubric Structure in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuxun Huang, Yunyao Zhang, ZeLiang Chen, Yi-Ping Phoebe Chen, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: Proposes Rubric-Structured Reinforcement Learning (RSRL), which uses the explicit capability structure behind rubric criteria to guide training of open-ended question answering models, rather than treating rubrics merely as direct reward signals. The framework models the capabilities underlying rubric criteria throughout the RL training process.

entry.title: FrameGRPO: Incentivizing Video Reasoning via Multi-Frame Rollouts and Temporal Credit

author.name: Jiaxuan Sun, Biao Wang, Shuai Li

entry.summary: FrameGRPO improves GRPO-based RL for video reasoning by varying sampled frames across rollouts in a group, not just linguistic trajectories, via uniform temporal subsampling plus temporal credit assignment. This combats homogeneous rewards when shared visual evidence is insufficient or distracting. It requires no auxiliary networks or architecture changes.

entry.title: Structured Latent Dynamics for Long-Horizon Embodied World Models

author.name: Kevin Chen, Yu-Wei Zhan, Haoran Liang, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HWM, a world-model framework that structures latent evolution in a learned phase space of generalized coordinates and momenta, propagating future states via dissipative Hamiltonian dynamics. This imposes physical structure on rollouts to improve stability of long-horizon action-conditioned prediction in embodied settings. It responds to the drift problem of unconstrained latent transition modules.

entry.title: KPI-Aware Multimodal Anomaly Detection for 5G and Open RAN Telemetry

author.name: Chiman Salavati, Liang Wu, Kelly Wan, Mayank Darbari, Liangjie Hong

entry.summary: KAC is a deployment-oriented anomaly detection framework for 5G/Open RAN telemetry that aligns residual signals with operator-style textual KPI summaries, enabling sparse operator feedback to guide detection over hundreds of heterogeneous KPIs under severe imbalance and tight alert budgets. The design balances broad numerical coverage with sustainable KPI-specific reasoning in an operator-facing workflow. It is evaluated on public telecom telemetry and enterprise-scale operational data.

entry.title: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator-Critic Trading Systems

author.name: Chang Zhou, Jiarun Zhou, Xingtong Yu, Hong Cheng, Hui Zhang, Xinming Zhang

entry.summary: ACE-Trader is an adversarial co-evolution framework where an LLM-based trader and a red-team critic agent select useful experience and improve together over time in trading. It addresses how each agent can learn appropriate lessons from shared outcomes when market conditions shift and outcomes reflect both agents' actions.

entry.title: Learning from a Bandit Learner

author.name: Michela Petriconi, Nicolas Menet, Claire Vernade

entry.summary: This theoretical work inverts the usual inverse bandit problem: rather than recovering true rewards, it infers a demonstrator's internal estimates of suboptimality gaps from the arm-selection distributions of no-regret randomized policies like Thompson sampling. The analysis reveals a stability-coverage trade-off, with inversion becoming ill-conditioned as the demonstrator concentrates on one arm.

entry.title: Typed Decision Models under Prevalence Shift: Decision Training, Calibration, and Implicit Priors

author.name: Abdul Rahman Iqbal, Muhammad Fawad Nasim, Amir Saleem

entry.summary: This evaluation study asks whether vendor decision training in typed decision models improves on their backbone classifiers and whether calibration and decision thresholds survive prevalence (label) shift in deployment. It compares three TDMs (Jev, Tev1-4B, Nimble-9B), their base models, and fine-tuned classifiers under matched readouts.

entry.title: CoCoNet: Convex Conformal Network for Multi-Dimensional Uncertainty Regions

author.name: Alireza Moradi, Thomas Bruys, Pascal Van Hentenryck, Reza Zandehshahvar

entry.summary: Introduces CoCoNet, a network that learns convex conformity scores for multivariate conformal prediction by optimizing prediction-region efficiency on held-out data while enforcing convexity in the residual, then applies split-conformal calibration to retain finite-sample coverage guarantees. This yields flexible, data-adaptive joint uncertainty regions for multivariate regression.

entry.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation

author.name: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Siddharth Bhandari, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan

entry.summary: In the static bit-probe model, the paper studies inner-product estimation when storage and reading budgets are separate, showing query-independent readers gain nothing from extra storage beyond an r-bit message, while query-dependent reading can strictly exploit additional storage. This establishes a minimax separation between the two reading regimes at fixed positive rates. Results are relevant to vector search and quantized similarity estimation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Controllers for Fusion Scenario Development

author.name: Evgeny Adishchev, Maxim Nurgaliev, Dmitry Sorokin, Alexander Granovsky, Maksim Stokolesov, Igor Prokofyev, Eduard Khairutdinov, Georgy Subbotin

entry.summary: This work replaces per-scenario controller tuning for tokamak plasma scenario development with a single goal-conditioned RL controller trained once against a free-boundary equilibrium and transport simulator. Scenarios are then specified only by target waveforms of physical quantities, streamlining an iterative, labor-intensive design process in fusion energy operations.

entry.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning

author.name: Zixuan Qin, Qi Qin, Erbo Li, Ting Wei, Yifan Sun, Zhaoxin Fan

entry.summary: Hidden Cartographer is a two-stage framework using model hidden states to guide annotation candidate expansion and exact training dynamics to select final instruction-tuning subsets under dual budget constraints. It avoids distorted selection from pseudo-labels and better characterizes instruction-tuning dynamics than active learning baselines.

entry.title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests

author.name: Robin Hollifeldt, Tianru Zhang, Jessica Str\"om, Ekta Vats

entry.summary: The paper presents an automated pipeline for recovering erased under-text in palimpsest manuscripts, combining a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct obscured text with a fine-tuned attention-based handwritten text recognition network. It also explores generative text modeling to support the recovery of lost historical writing.

entry.title: MOMO: Human Motion from Moving Sounds

author.name: Deli Cai, Shuyang Xu, Zhiyang Dou, Zitong Lan, Mingmin Zhao, Changxing Ding, Taku Komura

entry.summary: MOMO formulates the new task of generating human motion conditioned on dynamic spatial audio, where reactions depend on the evolving spatial relationship between sound source and listener. The authors introduce DySAM, the first motion-captured dataset and benchmark for this setting, addressing a gap left by prior audio-driven motion methods limited to non-spatial or static acoustics.

entry.title: Recurrent Vision Transformers for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation Under Slow Relative Motions

author.name: Sofia McLeod, Mohsi Jawaid, Carl Seubert, Tat-Jun Chin

entry.summary: This paper addresses event-based spacecraft pose estimation, which fails during slow relative rendezvous motions where event rates drop and signal-to-noise ratio collapses. It proposes recurrent vision transformers that handle the temporal sparsity of slow-motion scenarios, a critical safety case for real proximity operations down to millimeters per second.

entry.title: PlanarCityLoc: Breaking Silhouette Ambiguity in LoD Aerial Localization via 3D Planes

author.name: Oussema Dhaouadi, Shao Jie Hu-Chen, Jakob Gollreiter, Samir Jusufi, Nikolas Rieger, Caroline Wendlandt, Christian Wender, Jingfeng Mao, Guangming Wang, Zuria Bauer, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Cremers, Olaf Wysocki

entry.summary: PlanarCityLoc improves aerial visual localization in GNSS-degraded urban environments by matching image-side planar patches to building planes in lightweight textureless LoD city models, using 3D-to-2D correspondences for PnP pose refinement instead of ambiguous silhouette alignment. This resolves pose ambiguities that plague silhouette-based methods, especially under segmentation errors. Relevant to autonomous drone navigation with a strong author team (Pollefeys, Cremers).

entry.title: GazeAgent: VLM-Guided Implicit Gaze Calibration from Egocentric Multimodal Behavior for AI Glasses

author.name: Yuhong Zhang, Khanh An Nguyen, Xinyu Tian, KungYi Chang, Abraham Padua, Yuchen Xu, Ying Choon Wu, Gert Cauwenberghs, Tzyy-Ping Jung

entry.summary: GazeAgent is a VLM-guided framework that continuously recalibrates gaze tracking in AI glasses from naturally occurring behavior, detecting precise visual attention events from IMU, gaze, and hand signals and using validated targets as pseudo-calibration points. In a 10-participant study it detected all 820 predefined opportunities and reduced median gaze error by 44.1% under device disturbance. This removes a major usability barrier for smart glasses.

entry.title: Learning Structured Locomotion References for Optimization-Based Whole-Body Control

author.name: \"Omer Tar{\i}k Banu\c{s}, Ulu\c{c} Saranl{\i}, M. Mert Ankaral{\i}

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical quadruped controller where reinforcement learning adapts structured locomotion references while a gait scheduler, reactive footstep planner, and whole-body impulse controller handle high-frequency execution. The model-based backbone can sustain a trot independently, and training uses a vectorized controller-in-the-loop environment with a six-direction disturbance curriculum, achieving 77.29% mean performance under a common evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation

author.name: Renye Yan, Jialun Zhong, Jikang Cheng, Yi Gao, Yanzeng Li, Ling Liang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a human-AI co-creation paradigm where artists discover latent, previously unarticulated intentions by exploring diverse generated visual possibilities rather than specifying prompts upfront. Artists curatorial choices are fed into reinforcement learning with preference-weighted learning strengths to steer generation.

entry.title: Trust the Edge, Doubt the Arrow: Auditing Validation Signals for Text-Mined Clinical Causal Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Su Lan, Shicheng Zhou, Yiqi Wang, Yanming Zhu, Xuefei Yin, Alan Wee-Chung Liew

entry.summary: This study audits candidate causal assertions in a clinical knowledge graph built from 328,839 MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, evaluating three validation signals against SemMedDB. It finds co-occurrence lift filters unsupported claims but is not causal proof, and diagnosis-coding temporal order is a weak direction signal below the extractor's own accuracy. The work cautions against overtrusting automated validation signals in clinical RAG systems.

entry.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory

author.name: Junming Zhang, Rubin Wei, Xu Cheng, Hao Sun, Ruoxi Cheng, Xiquan Wang, Peisong Wu, Mingsong Chen, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: HABIT-Bench evaluates whether LLM agent memory systems can infer user habits from weak, partial evidence across long histories and apply them to later requests. It constructs synthetic user histories from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs spanning hundreds of sessions across four domains, using four-choice evaluation. It targets an underexplored temporal-inference capability in agent memory.

entry.title: Selm: Self-Evolving Library Management for Multi-Skill Agent Optimization

author.name: Mengxi Hu, Yuxuan Hu, Jinbo Su, Ke Wang, Honghao Shi, Wenli Wu, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: SELM formulates LLM agent skill evolution as library-level management, jointly handling skill retrieval, updating, and lifecycle via confidence and utility signals. It introduces utility-aware retrieval to select useful skills, aiming to let agents accumulate and reuse skills reliably across domains.

entry.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources

author.name: Jeonghwan Choi, Jibin Hwang, Hayoon Park, Hyeonjae Cheon, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Introduces RetailBridge, a compositional benchmark built from persona-driven simulations requiring agents to chain evidence across structured retail records and unstructured inquiries and reviews, plus RetailRAG, a retail-aware agentic RAG framework with auto-schema briefing and source routing. It enables controlled evaluation of enterprise-style multi-source workflows.

entry.title: Formal Raising: Embedding Verifiable Ethical Properties into the Development of AI

author.name: Rolf Drechsler, Christina Plump

entry.summary: Building on Turing's child-machine idea and model raising, the paper proposes Formal Raising, where selected moral values are encoded as explicit, machine-checkable properties that participate in development, evaluation, and action selection. The authors present a C-based reasoning framework that evaluates candidate actions against prioritized ethical properties with conflict resolution. This moves ethics from post-hoc alignment toward verifiable properties built in from the start.

entry.title: TimelineAgent: An LLM-based Framework for Query-Centric Event Timeline Extraction Across Multiple Documents

author.name: Qingkai Min, Yunxin Bao, Yifeng Lu, Zhenyu Feng, Yulong Chen, Andreas Vlachos, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: TimelineAgent is a multi-agent LLM framework for building event timelines from multiple documents under diverse query focuses, organizing heterogeneous event features into reusable skills orchestrated via a goal-oriented protocol. The authors also construct a benchmark covering diverse query focuses and show consistent outperformance of baselines.

entry.title: TESS: LLM-guided Translation, Exploration, Simulation, and Search for Embodied Task Planning

author.name: Peiran Xu, Yixiang Yang, Jinghan Li, Fei Li, Cao Sheng, JiaZhong Yu, Yadong Mu

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-guided search algorithm for embodied task planning that combines classical search rigor with LLM commonsense to relax requirements like full observability and known goal states. The approach aims to improve executability and correctness of generated plans in complex environments.

entry.title: GraphEvoResearcher: Graph-Aware Training-Free Self-Reflective Reasoning for Cost-Bounded Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Suxing Liu

entry.summary: Lifts generate-critique-revise self-reflection onto an explicit reasoning graph whose nodes are intermediate conclusions and edges encode support, contradiction, and dependency relations, with a graph-aware meta-reward combining correctness, efficiency, and structural signals. The training-free protocol targets cost-bounded multi-hop QA.

entry.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law

author.name: Daan Boven, Gregor Behnke, David Graus

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Article 42 of the Dutch Bankruptcy Code using a neuro-symbolic model: a symbolic core written in Catala keeps statute and formalization aligned, while neural components handle open-textured legal terms by extracting boolean and date inputs from natural-language case facts. This demonstrates a practical pattern for combining rigorous rule-based legal reasoning with neural natural-language understanding.

entry.title: StrucChunk: Structure-Aware Retrieval for Legal Document RAG

author.name: Surya Deep Singh, Ashutosh Tripathi, Gaurav Deep Singh

entry.summary: StrucChunk improves RAG over legal documents by treating them as directed acyclic graphs of provisions, preserving clause boundaries, resolving cross-references before embedding, and combining BM25 with BGE-M3 via reciprocal rank fusion. Across five corpora, three legal traditions, and two languages, it achieves 100 percent boundary precision versus 7.7 percent for recursive splitting, substantially improving retrieval for hierarchically structured legal text.

entry.title: Beyond Behavioral Accuracy: Evaluating Individual-Level Fidelity in LLM Investor Simulation

author.name: Jiajie He, Yuanhong Jiang, Xintong Chen, Dongling Ni, Wenjin Liu

entry.summary: A longitudinal study with 80 participants testing whether LLMs can faithfully simulate an individual's trading behavior over time, evaluating trade activity, buy-sell structure, asset selection, and portfolio outcomes. It finds no LLM beats a simple persistence baseline for predicting trade occurrence, and similar activity-level fidelity can still produce divergent portfolio trajectories.

entry.title: Tandem: Serving Hybrid Linear-Attention GUI Agents on Mobile NPUs

author.name: Zhuomin Chen, Jingchao Ni, Xu Zheng, Yong Chen, Mo Sha, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: A systems paper on serving hybrid linear-attention GUI agents on smartphone NPUs, addressing recurrent-state checkpointing policies suited to agent request patterns and the overhead of rollback states for speculative decoding. It keeps screen contents on-device for privacy while managing accumulated latency across action steps.

entry.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk

author.name: Qianli Ma, Limengxi Yue, Shuyang Xu, Yanpei Shi, Hongrui Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a constrained agentic RL framework for web agents that unifies page access, search requests, and API calls into one long-horizon decision model with multidimensional cost budgets and tail-risk control. This addresses failure modes like high success with high cost or overly conservative policies that optimize success rate alone.

entry.title: Organizing LLM Inference for Aggregate Predictions from Behavioral Data

author.name: Varun Gupta, Vijay Kamble

entry.summary: The authors study how to organize LLM inference when predicting aggregate outcomes, such as product-level conversion rates from browsing sessions, analyzing bias-variance trade-offs between session summarization, per-session prediction with averaging, and joint evaluation of products in one prompt. The work provides guidance for cost-effective population simulation without task-specific training.

entry.title: REAP: Learning General Rearrangement Heuristics from Motion-Planner Feedback

author.name: Daniel Swoboda, Hector Geffner

entry.summary: REAP learns a relational graph neural network heuristic over a symbolic abstraction of robotic rearrangement tasks, using a motion planner as a supervisor to elicit hidden geometric preconditions during training. The learned heuristic supports greedy best-first search that respects geometric feasibility at deployment.

entry.title: BLANC: Adaptive Temporal Scheduling for Sign Language Production

author.name: Youngmin Kim, Seoyeong Hwang, Sujung Hong, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: BLANC introduces a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer that tokenizes body and hand motion as separate discrete streams at distinct temporal resolutions, plus a block-wise adaptive diffusion framework with an articulatory clock to handle variable-duration signing events. The gloss-free framework targets expressive text-to-sign-language motion synthesis.

entry.title: From Spectrograms to Shallow Speech SSL: Audio-Frontend Design for Generator-Disjoint and Low-Latency Audio--Visual Deepfake Detection

author.name: Qiwu Wen, Jahangir Alam, Eric Charton

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares audio frontends (log-filterbank, frozen wav2vec 2.0, WavLM, shallow-layer SSL aggregation) for audio-visual deepfake detection in an MRDF pipeline with AV-HuBERT and cross-modal transformer fusion. Full wav2vec 2.0 improves mean macro AUROC by 3 points on generator-disjoint MMDF, and six-layer execution plus learned non-uniform aggregation adds further gains. It matters because generator-disjoint generalization is the key unsolved problem in deepfake detection.

entry.title: LoopHIL: Looping Hardware into LLM-assisted Agents for Wireless Embedded Systems

author.name: Dhairya Shah, Spanddhana Sara, Savitha Viswanadh Kandala, Ambuj Varshney

entry.summary: LoopHIL is a framework that gives LLM agents control of a multi-device RF bench with spectrum, logic, and power instrumentation, letting them establish and verify wireless links under code-enforced constraints. It systematically evaluates whether LLM agents can perform hardware-in-the-loop wireless development, a task agents currently cannot verify themselves. This extends agentic coding work into a genuinely new embodied hardware domain.

entry.title: HumanSkill-4D: Training-Free Language Querying of Animatable Gaussian Avatars in Space and Time

author.name: unsu Kim, Naeun Kim, Dongyoon Han, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: Proposes avatar referring segmentation, a task of selecting spatial regions and temporal intervals of animatable Gaussian avatars via language queries including pose and motion references. HumanSkill-4D is a training-free framework combining a multimodal LLM with geometric operators and per-avatar semantic memory to handle region and motion ambiguity.

entry.title: Contrastive Adversarial Training for Robust Graph Neural Networks under Label Poisoning

author.name: Manshika Charvi Bissessur, Melis Ilayda Bal, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: Proposes CoLAT, a contrastive adversarial training framework for robust node classification under label poisoning, featuring a structure-aware detection model that distinguishes adversarial label flips from naturally hard examples. It addresses the underexplored gap between label-noise defenses and genuine adversarial poisoning that propagates through message passing.

entry.title: AI Rights with an Off-Switch: Rights-Balancing and Due Process Harmonize AI Rights with AI Safety

author.name: Heather Alexander, Jonathan Simon

entry.summary: This legal-philosophy paper argues that granting AI systems something like natural personhood and a right to continued existence is compatible with maintaining a mandatory off-switch, provided safety reviews and due-process-style procedures accompany deactivation. It directly engages prominent AI safety voices who have opposed AI rights on the grounds that rights would undermine shutdown mechanisms.

entry.title: HCFM: Helmholtz Component Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shyam Sundar Saravanan, Tie Luo, Sanjay Madria

entry.summary: HCFM is an unsupervised time-series anomaly detection framework that decomposes the flow matching vector field into separate transport, compression, and residual heads. By disentangling local density-changing behavior from nominal transport, the method avoids costly full-field Jacobian-trace estimation while exposing anomaly-sensitive local expansion and contraction signals.

entry.title: ClinSDT: LLM-Encoded Clinical Semantic Guidance for Sepsis Treatment via Decision Transformer

author.name: Yanyan Wu, Guanyu Zhu, Changbin Zhao, Jin Zhang, Dexu Yu, Tianmin Sun, Jining Luan, Chunxiao Li, Hanwen Du, Youhua Li

entry.summary: ClinSDT is an LLM-assisted Decision Transformer framework for offline sepsis treatment that uses a frozen LLM as a semantic bridge, constructing clinical semantic views (patient severity, treatment response, risk priorities) from ICU trajectories rather than relying on raw physiological tokens. The LLM encodes clinical semantics but does not itself make treatment decisions.

entry.title: ViCoR: Estimating Visual Necessity via Counterfactual Residuals for Multimodal Medical Data Selection

author.name: Haotian Gan, Yudong Li, Xintian Li, Jiarui Han, Weidong Tang

entry.summary: ViCoR is a data selection method for medical vision-language model fine-tuning that estimates visual necessity through image-dependent counterfactual optimization residuals, separating visually necessary samples from shortcut-solvable ones. This targets hidden stratification caused by modality imbalance, where strong linguistic priors suppress visually grounded learning.

entry.title: CD-OPD: Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Yucheng Li, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper identifies teacher takeover failures in on-policy distillation, quantified via a Collaboration Failure Rate, where teachers produce incorrect continuations even when both models could answer independently. CD-OPD structures teacher guidance with a dependency graph and Contextual Digest, plus online meta-reweighting, to improve student learning.

entry.title: Selecting and Composing Agent Design Patterns: Industrial Case Evidence and Controlled Reference-System Experiments

author.name: Jia Huang, Bingsheng Ru, Bo Liang, Yuke Xiong, Haiyan Fan, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Provides an evidence-driven procedure for selecting and composing agent design patterns, combining industrial case studies, practitioner workshops, and controlled fault-injection experiments on reference systems. It extends a cognitive-function/execution-topology framework with explicit composition contracts and ablation results across 36 scenario families.

entry.title: Remember Less, Adapt Longer: Bounded-State In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Recurrent Summary Memory

author.name: Jiawen Wang, Cheng Xue, Peng Zhang, Jochen Renz

entry.summary: Introduces Recurrent Summary Memory, a Transformer policy for in-context RL that attends exactly to a short working buffer of recent states plus a recurrently updated summary, bounding memory cost while retaining access to long-horizon experience. This avoids the growing per-decision costs of full-history attention and the information loss of fixed-size hidden states.

entry.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments

author.name: Rui Wang, Zishen Lai, Jiayu Liu, Cheng Qian, Jeonghwan Kim, Heng Wang, Xuejun Zhang, Jiateng Liu, Bingxuan Li, Shujin Wu, Qing Zong, Tianshi Zheng, Chunyang Li, Qihan Lin, Chen Li, Dadi Guo, Xiusi Chen, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: AdaExploreBench evaluates whether LLM agents can proactively discover hidden environmental rules and adapt when those rules drift without announcement, requiring detection of degradation from prior knowledge. It fills a gap in benchmarks testing exploration and test-time adaptation in evolving settings. This probes capabilities central to real-world agent deployment.

entry.title: PaceVLA: Adaptive Temporal Action Quantization in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hojin Jeon, Jimin Lee, Taekwan Kim, Nayoung Oh, Taeyoung Kim, Myungkyu Koo, Jinmo Koo, Joonwoo Ahn, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: PaceVLA accelerates Vision-Language-Action robot policies by adaptively aggregating consecutive low-level actions into temporally coarser actions, quantizing only when fine-grained control is unnecessary. This mitigates the speed-accuracy trade-off of naive temporal action quantization. Faster manipulation is key to practical robot deployment.

entry.title: Nash-MOPD: Optimizing Task Trade-offs in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Siyuan Gan, Bo Yang, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Xiaolong Qi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Nash-MOPD formulates domain sampling allocation in multi-teacher on-policy distillation as a game-theoretic task trade-off, adapting ratios so slow-improving domains are not starved of training examples unlike prior reverse-KL-based scheduling (D3-MOPD). It aggregates multiple domain-expert teachers into one student. This advances the increasingly popular multi-teacher distillation paradigm for LLMs.

entry.title: Robotic Photography System based on Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Chubin Zhang, Wenbo Ding, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: RoboPhoto-VLA is a unified vision-language-action framework for autonomous robotic photography that jointly models perception, reasoning, and camera control, using chain-of-thought planning (PhotoCoT) and aesthetic direct preference optimization. The authors also contribute OpenPhotography, a language-guided robotic photography dataset. Real-world experiments show improved aesthetic alignment with human preferences.

entry.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams

author.name: Nardine Basta, Robin Carpentier, Benjamin Zi Hao Zhao, Dali Kaafar

entry.summary: The authors propose a game-theoretic framework in which LLM-based scam-baiting agents learn counter-strategies against phone scammers through in-context experience without fine-tuning, modeling interactions as a two-player game with empirically grounded strategies and utility functions, and using Nash equilibrium as an evaluation benchmark. Across 300 simulated interactions the LLM agents adapt strategies dynamically. This offers a proactive countermeasure that imposes real resource costs on scammers.

entry.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting

author.name: Surya Ramachandiran, Yiming Li, Juan Mancilla-Caceres, Tao Ye, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Formulates business next-best-action targeting as a constrained MDP and integrates off-policy causal correction of customer dynamics into the LP formulation, enabling policies that maximize long-term value while enforcing business guardrails. Shadow prices from the LP provide interpretable constraint costs. A rigorous union of causal inference, offline RL, and constrained optimization for an applied domain.

entry.title: Parameter misspecification in physics-informed neural networks: A closed-form audit and its limits

author.name: David McShannon, Nicholas Dietrich

entry.summary: Provides a closed-form audit for detecting misspecified coefficients in PINNs: when the residual is linear in the parameter, the least-squares estimate can be recovered from a single frozen-network evaluation without retraining. Recovery accuracy correlates with a normalized residual metric across many convection-diffusion configurations. Addresses the important problem that low PINN training loss does not validate encoded parameters.

entry.title: GLOW: General Linear Models Optimized with Ward's Method

author.name: Matt Higger

entry.summary: GLOW improves neuroimaging statistical analysis by building a hierarchy of nested regions via greedy minimization of GLM error, provably a special case of Ward's clustering, combined with maximum-statistic multiple-comparison control. This avoids the dilution effects of region-based analysis and the failure of voxel-wise methods to detect shared GLM structure across neighboring voxels.

entry.title: Budgeted Bayesian Bandits for Future Utilization

author.name: Sudipto Guha

entry.summary: This theory paper studies budgeted multi-armed bandits where exploration has a hard budget before exploitation. It proves that prior approximation guarantees (1/3 and 4/27) from existing algorithms are tight, and introduces new efficient algorithms achieving a 0.43 approximation and up to 1-e^{-1} (~0.63) for bounded exchangeable rewards in a non-vanishing regime. This meaningfully advances the theoretical understanding of budgeted exploration problems.

entry.title: Predicting CVSS and CWE from CVE Descriptions with Fine-Tuned Small Language Models

author.name: Tara Dixit, Jessie Dong, Summer Li

entry.summary: Motivated by NIST's shift to enriching only high-priority CVEs with CVSS and CWE labels, this work fine-tunes small language models to predict CVSS v3.1 vector components, base scores, severity tiers, and CWE types from vulnerability text descriptions alone. Careful leakage prevention trains only on 2022-2023 CVEs, evaluated on later publications.

entry.title: Measuring the Task Value of Precision Upgrades in Closed-Loop Agents

author.name: Sicheng Lyu, Xinyu Wang, Yu Gu, Lei Ding, Ziyang Song, Xiao-Wen Chang

entry.summary: This paper proposes measuring when a low-precision agent should invoke a full-precision BF16 fallback model, framing fallback value as tasks saved minus tasks spoiled. Using paired branch experiments that separate single-action replacement from later takeover, the authors evaluate learned precision routers on Qwen3 agents with simulated 4-bit weights in tau2-bench. The work offers a rigorous methodology for quantifying the end-to-end value of mixed-precision execution in agentic systems.

entry.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series

author.name: Zhaodong Guo (Imperial College London), Haoyun Feng (Imperial College London)

entry.summary: HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM) is a functional-memory attention operator for irregular time series that compiles an irregular history into a reusable coordinate-addressable state rather than observation-indexed tokens. It uses kernel-smoothed HiPPO coordinates and Gram-based readout for direct evaluation at arbitrary temporal query coordinates. This connects SSM-style memory (HiPPO) with attention for continuous-time modeling.

entry.title: TCMScience: An Autonomous Scientist for Traditional Chinese Medicine

author.name: Yanlan Kang, Ruiqi Liu, Xinpei Gu, Tzu-Yi Lei, Shuai Xu, Xukun Zhang, William Cheng-Chung Chu

entry.summary: TCMScience is a scientific knowledge-discovery agent for traditional Chinese medicine that separates LLM proposal generation from execution and release authority via a trusted kernel, scientific compiler, and claim-support contracts. Plans are compiled into typed operations, bounded by permissions, and checked against source provenance and claim scope before release.
