This is notable as a governance-oriented design for autonomous research agents in a domain where evidence types must be carefully separated.

entry.title: From Overparameterised Expressions to Parsimonious Models: Fisher-Geometric Pruning for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Veronica Guidetti, Luca La Rocca, Fabr\'icio Olivetti de Fran\c{c}a, Gabriel Kronberger

entry.summary: FGP is a post-hoc model-reduction framework for genetic-programming symbolic regression that combines local information geometry at the maximum-likelihood solution with compatibility tests for interpretable parametric boundaries. A taxonomy of parametric directions separates locally sensitive directions from globally compressible ones, complementing existing search-time complexity controls. This addresses the common GPSR failure mode of returning oversized expressions that fit noise.

entry.title: FHKAN: Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Arsha Farnoush, Amirhossein Sadr, Aida Pakniyat, Dara Rahmati, Saeid Gorgin, Kourosh Parand

entry.summary: FHKAN equips Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with a trainable fractional-order generalized Hermite basis that is orthonormal on the entire real line and uniformly bounded under a Gaussian envelope. This removes the need for saturating squashing of pre-activations required by Chebyshev-based spectral KANs and enables closed-form derivatives for fractional orders. The architecture targets both data-driven and physics-informed learning tasks.

entry.title: Shallow Probes Are Sufficient for Near-Oracle Personalization Depth Allocation in Federated Learning

author.name: Beyazit Bestami Yuksel, Emrah Dikbiyik, Ayse Yilmazer Metin

entry.summary: The paper audits whether small client-specific measurement budgets suffice for cost-aware personalization-depth decisions in federated learning, defining an offline oracle over six depth choices trading Macro-F1 against deployment cost. Training-free greedy probing with shallow probes achieves regret 0.0071 and 98.3 percent oracle recovery on CIFAR-10/100 and patient-disjoint PTB-XL, beating metadata-only policies. A learned instantiation, FedPBA, handles deep-action extrapolation.

entry.title: Multi-site Learning for Forecasting Day-Ahead Wind-Power Production for Onshore Wind Farms in Great Britain with Deep Neural Networks

author.name: James Kean, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: This applied paper trains multi-site deep neural networks on pooled historical production and reanalysis weather data from 88 onshore wind farms in Great Britain to forecast day-ahead power production on NESO's operational schedule. Reanalysis weather is used as future covariates during training and NWP forecasts at inference, extending the effective training archive beyond historical NWP availability. The work targets a real operational grid-balancing problem.

entry.title: PRISM: Prior Relational Information for Self-supervised Modeling to Enhance Solubility OOD Generalization

author.name: Xinyi Chen, Jiahuan Pang, Titus Chima, Paul Weng, Wendong Wang

entry.summary: PRISM is a label-free pretraining framework that injects chemically meaningful relational information between solutes and solvents to improve out-of-distribution solubility prediction. It targets data scarcity in drug discovery and process engineering where supervised methods fail on unseen solvents and mixtures.

entry.title: Conditional Average Treatment Effect Distillation for Hypothetical State-Intervention Targeting Under Budget Constraints

author.name: Vasundhara Acharya, B\"ulent Yener

entry.summary: The paper studies budget-constrained public-health intervention targeting using causal machine learning, distilling conditional average treatment effects from Causal Forest and Bayesian Causal Forest teacher models into more operational policies. Applied to obesity, elevated glucose, and smoking-history states in observational data without logged decision policies, the approach balances individualized effect estimation with interpretability and resource caps. It matters because it bridges flexible causal inference methods and practical, constrained deployment decisions in health policy.

entry.title: An Analysis of Semantic and Spatio-Temporal Co-evolution for Edge Classification on Dynamic Text-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Tyler Bonnet, Marek Rei

entry.summary: The paper studies dynamic edge classification on text-attributed web graphs, introducing a unified text-graph alignment framework where a lightweight Transformer adapter lets pretrained text representations co-evolve with network topology via spatio-temporal gradients. This departs from the common practice of freezing language-model-initialized features during graph training.

entry.title: SEAM: Spectral Embedding Alignment and Merging for Low-Resource TTS

author.name: Walaa Othman, Baher Mohammad, Stamatios Lefkimmiatis, Ammar Ali

entry.summary: SEAM is a zero-audio initialization method for expanding TTS vocabularies, constructing embeddings for unseen tokens from known subtokens via a spectral filter that preserves temporal phonetic order plus closed-form ridge regression alignment to the pretrained conditioning manifold. Across three languages and two architectures it approaches baseline quality with up to four times less training data.

entry.title: CTLite: Lightweight Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Reusable Continuous-Time Summaries

author.name: Shusen Ma, Xudong Zuo, Yangchun Xie, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: CTLite is a lightweight framework for forecasting irregularly sampled multivariate time series that decouples historical summarization from learned prediction, using a parameter-free continuous-time moment encoder plus a compact readout with damped local extrapolation and low-rank cross-variable correction. This avoids repeatedly re-encoding the same observations during optimization.

entry.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models

author.name: Yanjun Li, Jiarui Ye, Weiyu Guo, Zixiao He, Kangjie Ye, Dihan Wang, Yishuo Cheng, Zishang Xiang, Mingju Gao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: Language-Forcing is a training strategy for whole-body World Action Models that uses a frozen vision-language model to describe task-relevant changes between current and future frames, with these descriptions encoded and aligned to predicted visual representations. This makes visual prediction objectives emphasize task-relevant transitions over incidental scene changes. It improves humanoid loco-manipulation policies grounded in world models.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control

author.name: Heedo Woo, Antonio Marino, Eduardo Sebasti\'an, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: Introduces CODES, a framework that discovers a repertoire of motion styles from diverse demonstration recordings using motion retargeting, weakly supervised consensus encoding, and density-based clustering, then composes a selected style with an independent task command. This addresses the problem that many trajectories can satisfy the same robot task while differing in style, enabling style-preserving control.

entry.title: Censored Flow Matching for Synthetic Time-to-Event Generation

author.name: Jianbin Tan, Xingran Chen, Kevin He, Zhenke Wu, Bhramar Mukherjee, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes censored flow matching (CFM), a flow-based generative method for synthesizing censored time-to-event data that handles censoring via the monotonicity of differential flows and pullback sampling rather than survival likelihoods, using an alternating training procedure. This fills a gap in flexible generative modeling for survival analysis.

entry.title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles

author.name: Qihao Zhou, Shanshui Niu

entry.summary: SICBO tackles nonconvex-strongly-convex finite-sum bilevel optimization using only first-order oracles, combining penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for lower-level variables. The method achieves a square-root finite-sum dependence in the component-gradient complexity while preserving the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number terms. Bilevel optimization underpins hyperparameter tuning and meta-learning.

entry.title: Is User Calibration Still Necessary for Continuous Myoelectric Control? A Closed-Loop Comparison of Calibration-Free Controllers

author.name: Amir Reza Hariri, Kevin B. Englehart, Erik Scheme

entry.summary: This human-subject study compares six calibration-free myoelectric controllers, trained on 306 users, against three calibrated controllers in a closed-loop Fitts' law target-acquisition task with sixteen participants. Despite calibrated controllers achieving higher offline balanced accuracy (90.6% vs 73.1%), the study evaluates whether this gap matters for real-time control usability. It addresses a key adoption barrier in prosthetic and rehabilitation interfaces.

entry.title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring

author.name: Hao Fang, Miao Zhang, Haoyuan Zhao, Long Chen, Yi Ching Chou, Chi Xu, Cheng Pan, Jiangchuan Liu

entry.summary: ATLAS is an expert-guided edge-to-cloud system treating LEO satellite backhaul as a scarce resource for off-grid wildlife monitoring, using foundation models at the edge to decide what to transmit under joint energy, bandwidth, and solar-harvesting constraints. It outperforms motion-trigger filtering and fixed vision models that waste resources or cannot follow evolving expert objectives. The system demonstrates applied foundation-model use in extreme deployment settings.

entry.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D

author.name: Konstantinos Fotopoulos, Michael Helcig, Karl Deck, Jannis Alsbach

entry.summary: This paper settles the long-standing open question of whether Polyak's heavy-ball method accelerates on univariate functions, using a Fourier-based approach to prove non-acceleration in one dimension. It complements recent two-variable constructions by Goujaud et al., completing the picture that heavy-ball's optimal asymptotic rate on quadratics does not extend as acceleration to broader smooth convex settings even in 1D.

entry.title: RARE: Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Rubric Evolution for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Xueyun Tian, Bingbing Xu, Chuyue Li, Jiaming Liu, Chao Zhang, Weijia Feng, MingHua Ma, Yu Zhao, Jingchu Wang, Ruihua Huang, Yuanzhuo Wang, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: RARE addresses rubric-based reinforcement learning for open-ended generation, where criteria satisfied early lose discriminative power while others remain informative. Instead of revising shared rubrics or selecting evolving criteria, which can discard useful signals, RARE evolves rubrics adaptively to maintain informative reward feedback across multiple valid responses.

entry.title: CheXFuse: Guided Differential Joint Attention Fusion for Robust Multimodal Chest X-Ray Classification in Data-Scarce Medical Settings

author.name: Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Priyanka Siddappa, Md Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma, Md Ripon Ahammed

entry.summary: CheXFuse proposes a multimodal fusion framework for chest X-ray classification that combines image and text tokens in a joint sequence, using guided differential joint attention to suppress weak or redundant cross-modal signals. It targets the common problem where a stronger modality is degraded by indiscriminate fusion with a weaker one, evaluated in data-scarce medical settings.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Reward for Code Generation: A Mechanistic Study of Single-Adapter Drift

author.name: Amarsaikhan Batjargal, Noriko Tomuro

entry.summary: The paper tests whether the SPARK policy-reward co-evolution framework, originally built for reasoning, transfers to code generation with verifiable execution rewards, and mechanistically analyzes a single-adapter drift phenomenon. It examines whether execution-grounded reflection adds a further source of self-improvement.

entry.title: Preservation and loss of algorithmic structure in experimental diffusion of joint-action norms

author.name: Dhara Yu, Bill D. Thompson

entry.summary: Through a large-scale human experiment on the diffusion of novel social norms, the authors use program synthesis to characterize the procedures participants develop, showing that diffusion systematically selects against complex algorithms in early stages. Inherited procedures become structurally simplified and are lost during interactions across populations.

entry.title: SLA-LENS: From Classroom Transcripts to CSLA-Informed and Evidence-Linked L2 Interaction Analytics

author.name: Nemika Tyagi, Olga Kellert, Phanos Kareen, Nelvin Licona-Guevara

entry.summary: Introduces SLA-LENS, an LLM-assisted framework for annotating second-language classroom transcripts with structured pedagogical labels grounded in interactionist SLA theory, capturing learner errors, instructor responses, and uptake or repair. Applied to 40 authentic online L2 Spanish transcripts, it enables scalable, evidence-linked analytics of classroom interaction that would be impractical to annotate manually.

entry.title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations

author.name: Amirreza Mohseni, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: The paper contributes a multi-axis taxonomy of legal queries and applies it to 2,122 naturally occurring WildChat-1M conversations, with a human-reviewed gold set of 200, finding that 71.1% of conversations containing legal content seek personal legal guidance. Annotations, checkpoints, and code are publicly released.

entry.title: Where Are Language-Specific Features Represented in Multilingual LLMs? Everywhere

author.name: Mikaela Martins, Jonathan Dunn

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that language-specific information in multilingual LLMs concentrates in early and late layers, using fine-grained Portuguese/Spanish analyses and a 200+ language identification study on Llama 3.2 1B. Findings show language-specific features pervade intermediate layers, undermining a strict language-specific/language-agnostic layer separation.

entry.title: CoMem: Learning to Anticipate Failures from Retrieved Experience

author.name: Yun Shen, Ming Shen, Tianjun Yao

entry.summary: Introduces CoMem, a cross-task reflective memory method for LLM agents that makes retrieved experience actively change what the learned parametric memory produces, rather than combining the two additively. This compounding of retrieved and parametric memory helps agents anticipate failures and avoid repeating the same failure explanations across tasks.

entry.title: How Benchmark Graph Construction Shapes Multi-Hop KG Navigation: A Controlled Audit of PathQuestion and PathQuestion-Large

author.name: Eduin E. Hernandez, Sergio A. Diaz, Luis F. Garcia, Nurassyl Askar, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: Audits the PathQuestion and PathQuestion-Large knowledge-graph QA benchmarks under controlled interventions, holding questions and answers fixed while swapping task-filtered graphs for larger source graphs. Shows that graph construction choices substantially change effective difficulty, complicating interpretation of navigation-based KGQA results.

entry.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics

author.name: Yupei Lin, Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Guoming Ling, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Yukai Shi, Liang Lin

entry.summary: Shows that benchmark compression methods selecting samples for one metric fail to preserve scores and rankings on other metrics, with single-metric baselines underperforming random sampling in over 70 percent of cross-metric comparisons at 80 percent compression. Proposes HoloCosm, which jointly minimizes normalized score error across multiple metrics.

entry.title: Desirability Confirmation: Relational Sycophancy in AI Intimate Roleplay

author.name: Huiqian Lai, Runze Ding

entry.summary: This audit of 2,016 outputs from two open-weight LLMs identifies a new form of sycophancy in intimate roleplay, where models preserve the user's preferred relational position rather than merely echoing propositional beliefs. The authors coin desirability confirmation and connect the sycophancy literature with sexual script theory, cataloging four recurrent relational moves.

entry.title: Instance-Specific Classifier-Free Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion/Flow-Based Editing

author.name: Wajeeh Atrash, Tom Tirer

entry.summary: The paper shows that image editing via diffusion/flow models benefits from instance-specific classifier-free guidance scales, since different edits require different degrees of source-image preservation versus prompt realization, and most methods use a fixed CFG scale. After exhaustively exploring the potential of per-instance CFG across prominent editing methods, the authors propose a method to set it automatically.

entry.title: Junction Geometry Survives an Unidentifiable Blur

author.name: Sohail (Neel), Sarkar, Shakuntala Baichoo

entry.summary: This theory paper addresses recovering the number, directions, and weights of crossing or branching arms (such as filaments in microscopy or spectral lines in X-ray detectors) under unknown Gaussian-mixture blur, including cases where the blur is fundamentally unidentifiable. The authors prove a uniform recovery bound showing that a distance metric over arm count, directions, weights, and supporting lines is controlled by differences in cell probabilities on a fine grid.

entry.title: SynerGest: Temporal-Spatial Synergistic Gesture Generation for Dyadic Conversations

author.name: Chengxiang Guo, Jian Wang, Lanmiao Liu, Zhan Tang, Junhua Fei, Xiao Li

entry.summary: SynerGest is a dyadic co-speech gesture generation framework based on Contrastive Flow Matching, which penalizes mismatched semantic pairs during training to prevent spatial shortcuts, over-smoothing, and semantic entanglement. It targets the balance between kinematic stability and rhythmic responsiveness for immersive conversational avatars, with architectural components for robustness.

entry.title: ULIFLOW: Unified Latent Human-Object Interaction Flow

author.name: Wenqi Cai, Chunzhi Gu, Weichen Zhou, Yawen Zou, Yijin Wei, Ran Dong, Haoran Xie, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: ULIFLOW addresses text-conditioned 3D human-object interaction generation by modeling continuous human-object relations in a unified latent space, using marker-object relations as an explicit interaction modality. This avoids the limitations of skeleton-based representations that leave contact geometry implicit and require contact-specific regularizers.

entry.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation

author.name: Wen Xue, Yong Liu, Xueheng Li, Si Wu, Yong Xu, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: LayerEditor unifies instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers, using In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling to jointly represent the edited canvas and an ordered layer sequence in a single token stream. This enables precise local edits, layer reuse, and preservation of unrelated regions, addressing the flattened-output limitation of existing editing models.

entry.title: Directionally Factorized Illumination with Spherical Harmonic Rotation

author.name: Yimeng Dou, Adam M. Saunders, Andre T. S. Hucke, Michael E. Kim, Adam W. Anderson, Eric R. Tkaczyk, Bennett A. Landman, Daniel Moyer

entry.summary: Presents DaFISH, a plug-in module for novel-view synthesis pipelines like NeRF that handles active light sources rigidly attached to the camera (flashes, underwater lights, endoscopes). It factorizes per-point emitted color into surface albedo and a directionally varying illumination term using spherical harmonic rotation, avoiding baked-in pose-dependent coloration artifacts.

entry.title: GeoV2V: Geometry-Grounded Video Diffusion Model for Driving Scene Generation

author.name: Yuchen Xi, Yuhan Guo, Chenwei Hou, Zixu Liu, Jin Fang, Jason Liu, Ruigang Yang

entry.summary: GeoV2V is a video-to-video diffusion framework for autonomous driving simulation that synthesizes temporally coherent videos along novel trajectories by combining LiDAR and depth-derived geometric priors with full-video conditioning in the Wan 2.1 backbone. It targets novel view synthesis under large viewpoint changes like lane shifts.

entry.title: SENRI: Understanding the Space-Event Nexus in Real-Life Videos

author.name: Kehan Lan, Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SENRI, a task and benchmark (SENRI-Bench) for studying the connection between events and spatial contexts in long egocentric video, with 500 manually annotated questions over roughly 25 hours of continuous self-recorded footage across six bidirectional task types. Evaluation of long-video models reveals current limitations.

entry.title: ATLAS: Attention-Guided Test-Time Latent Selection for Compositional Visual Autoregressive Generation

author.name: Hossein Shahabadi, Raya Namazi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

entry.summary: ATLAS is a training-free framework that uses a frozen visual autoregressive generator's internal attention to score and prune candidate generation paths before images are decoded, concentrating compute on promising trajectories to improve compositional attribute and relation accuracy on models like Infinity and Switti.

entry.title: SlimFormer++: Token Mixing Where It Matters for Efficient 3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yang Hong, Lei Zhang, Zhihong Liu, Jianqing Mo, Xujiong Ye

entry.summary: This work analyzes block-level redundancy in volumetric segmentation networks using Centered Kernel Alignment, showing similarity-guided pruning cuts parameters by 39-75% with under 0.4 point Dice loss. It introduces Anatomical Relation Distortion to quantify each token mixer's contribution and builds SlimFormer++, an efficient 3D medical segmentation architecture.

entry.title: Negation without Confusion: Decomposing Bias and Recomposing Style in Text Embeddings for Negation-aware Image Generation

author.name: Sooyeon Park, Hemraj Singh, Kyunghyun Min, Youngjae Yu, Sung-Bae Cho

entry.summary: Dero is a training-free method for negation-aware image generation that decomposes text embeddings into semantic-preserving and bias subspaces via bidirectional SVD using auxiliary prompts, then selectively recomposes components. This realigns text representations so intended negative constraints are not overridden by bias-aligned semantics in diffusion models.

entry.title: Hihaze: One-Step Diffusion for High-Resolution Real-World Image Dehazing

author.name: Zheng Chen, Yuchen Huang, Xiaoyang Liu, Jue Gong, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: Hihaze is a one-step diffusion framework for high-resolution real-world image dehazing that tackles spatially non-uniform haze and inconsistent patch-wise predictions. It introduces two haze-aware modules: attentive skip compensation to preserve structural details into the VAE decoder, and a spatial degradation adapter injecting multi-scale degradation representations into the U-Net.

entry.title: DeOverlay: A Benchmark and Source-Anchored Flow for Video Overlay Removal

author.name: Deshui Miao, Yuhang Ma, Shaoyong Jia, Wenzhao Gao, Yue Zhang, Shaohui Jiao, Xin Li

entry.summary: DeOverlay addresses video overlay removal (subtitles, titles, logos) using a source-anchored flow model that reconstructs clean video from a source latent with fixed source guidance. It trains a shared velocity network with region-weighted flow matching and introduces visibility-normalized temporal aggregation for selecting local source cues. This matters for video editing and restoration pipelines where overlays obscure scene content.

entry.title: XGLASS: X-Ray, Gaze and Language Assisted Slice Sequencing for CT Volumes

author.name: Michael Gl\"ockler, Timo Ropinski

entry.summary: XGLASS transfers diagnostic expertise from 2D X-ray VLMs to 3D CT volumes by using disease-conditioned importance maps derived from language-aligned radiologist gaze on X-rays, spatially aligned with corresponding CT slices for task-aware slice prioritization. This lets powerful 2D VLMs focus on diagnostically relevant slices in volumetric data. Addresses the 3D medical data scarcity problem.

entry.title: Policy-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Spatial Reasoning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Hailiang Yang, Shengchao Chen

entry.summary: CALIPER is an adaptive process-reward framework for image-based spatial reasoning that uses within-group ridge regression to estimate associations between stage-wise reference coverage and answer correctness, adapting reward allocation to shifting training bottlenecks. It is supported by SpatialTrace, a corpus of stage-decomposed spatial reasoning traces. Addresses limitations of answer-level RLVR rewards.

entry.title: PDNet: Exploring Pruning and Distillation for Real-Time Worker Activity Recognition in Industrial Assembly

author.name: Malek Baba, Thinesh Thiyakesan Ponbagavathi, Alina Roitberg

entry.summary: PDNet combines channel-wise structured pruning with knowledge distillation to compress 3D CNNs for real-time fine-grained activity recognition in industrial assembly settings. On the MECCANO dataset with an X3D-M backbone, distillation after pruning lifts Top-1 accuracy from 25.54% to 39.46% while keeping the model at only 6.90 MB and 3.78 GFLOPs. This demonstrates a practical recipe for deploying action recognition on edge hardware in factories.

entry.title: Manga2Animate: An Agentic Framework for Faithful Manga Animation with Script and Storyboard Planning

author.name: Sheng-Wei Zhang, Hsi-An Chen, Yan-Ting Liou, Chih-Hsuan Chen, Shih-Chen Tseng, Yu-Lun Liu

entry.summary: Manga2Animate is a multi-agent framework that converts manga into coherent animation by grounding generation in the source panels through two intermediate representations: an animation script and a visual storyboard. Creator and reviewer agents jointly produce and verify each representation, avoiding the failure modes of text-only adaptation or direct video-generation pipelines. This demonstrates agentic decomposition for faithful media transformation.

entry.title: CLARO: Clutter Aware Robot Orchestrator for Open-Vocabulary Grasping using VLM Agents

author.name: Sungsu Kim, Vineet Bhat, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Ramesh Karri, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: CLARO is a VLM agent that orchestrates perception and manipulation skills, including open-vocabulary detection, segmentation, 6-DoF grasping, and pushing, to locate and retrieve language-specified targets in heavily cluttered environments. It maintains memory of past actions for long-horizon execution and emits robot-agnostic manipulation targets enabling transfer across arms. This targets realistic household and warehouse autonomy.

entry.title: MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhongyu Wang, Chen Zuo, Qingxuan Sun, Jiayang Qiao, Qiuhao Qian, Songyan Cui, Guocheng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes MAPS, a multi-agent system that moves beyond retrieval-based video ad recommendation by generating personalized ad scripts and synthesizing video creatives on demand. Four collaborative agents form a closed loop covering user profiling, script generation, video synthesis, and feedback-driven improvement via reinforcement learning. This matters because it targets the granularity limits of pre-produced ad creative personalization.

entry.title: TrajEdit: Real-Time Flow-Matching Trajectory Adaptation via FlowEdit and CBF Safety Filter

author.name: Wondmgezahu Teshome, Arya Honarpisheh, Octavia Camps, Mario Sznaier

entry.summary: TrajEdit is a hierarchical planner for pursuit-evasion scenarios that edits the remaining portion of the current trajectory via FlowEdit as a pursuer approaches, instead of regenerating from scratch, and falls back to a CBF safety filter when the adversary is close. This reduces computation time while maintaining comparable success rates.

entry.title: Anticipatory Gait Switching for Quadrupeds via Look-Ahead MDP Planning

author.name: Kelvin Aladum, Justin Peel, Nisar Ahmed

entry.summary: This work proposes a lightweight gait supervisor for quadrupeds that uses a robot-centered height map partitioned into near, mid, and far field bands, modeled as a Markov process. Gait selection is cast as a look-ahead MDP solved with the band evolution model, enabling earlier commitment to gaits before rough terrain contact. The approach unifies look-ahead and locomotion constraints in one decision policy.

entry.title: Adaptive Bendpoint Formation in Octopus-Inspired Soft Continuum Arms

author.name: Jessica Gumowski, Julian Finn, Krishna Manaswi Digumarti, David Howard

entry.summary: This bioinspired hardware study develops a tendon-actuated soft continuum arm that can adaptively create new bending anchor points along its length by inflating integrated inflatable shells, which increase local friction and jam the tendon. This mimics the octopus ability to instantiate bend points anywhere along the arm while preserving arm continuity. Experiments demonstrate dexterous posture changes enabled by the mechanism.

entry.title: ReDOA: Real-World Distillation via Observation Alignment for Image-Based Manipulation Policy Learning

author.name: Kotaro Kajitsuka, Masaki Murooka, Fumio Kanehiro

entry.summary: ReDOA decouples control learning from perception learning: a simulation-trained state-based teacher runs on a real robot, and its control knowledge is distilled into an image-based student policy using Observation Alignment to reconcile sim-to-real observation discrepancies. This avoids both costly human demonstrations and brittle direct sim-to-real transfer.

entry.title: MSCR: Jointly Balancing Utilization Across Modalities and Discovering Synergistic Information

author.name: Xinyu Chen, Liangjian Wen, Jiang Duan, Dongkai Wang, Yong Dai, Jiayu Bai, Jianzhuang Liu, Zhen Tian, Guoping Qiu, Zhao Kan

entry.summary: MSCR extends modality-balancing regularizers like MCR by jointly promoting balanced modality utilization and discovering synergistic information—the predictive gain unavailable from unimodal evidence—during multimodal fusion. It argues that existing balancing methods overlook how imbalance affects synergy formation. This addresses a core limitation in multimodal learning beyond simple modality dominance.

entry.title: From Prediction to Action: Population Health World Model for Digital Medicine

author.name: Xike Xie, Yu Li, Weizhong Yang, Amalie Dyda, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that digital medicine should move beyond task-specific prediction toward population health world models that represent how actions change health trajectories under multiple decision-makers, heterogeneous populations, and resource constraints. It outlines what such models would need to support action-oriented decision making in care delivery.

entry.title: Narrow Decision Models: A System-1 Architecture for Calibrated, Typed Decisions

author.name: Carlos Andr\'e Antunes, Aldry Albuquerque, Gabriel de Melo Schmith, Nat\~a Batista, Pedro Oziel Escobar da Silva, Stefano Benko Rossi, Lingrid Dietrich Lorenz da Silva, Fl\'avia Cristina da Costa, Thiago Bertotto, Luis Fernando Fausto

entry.summary: This paper explores the opposite end of the design space from TypeSafe's general-purpose Jev decision model: Narrow Decision Models (NDMs) share the same typed, calibrated-probability interface (Choice, Score, Noul) but are trained for one organization's decisions, small enough for on-premise deployment, and openly auditable. The state can be arbitrary text or structured records. It positions small specialized decision models as a deployable alternative to general System-1 decision APIs.

entry.title: Map-Distribution Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Agent Pathfinding

author.name: Fumimaro Suzuki, Keisuke Okumura

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-level Mixture-of-Experts architecture for multi-agent pathfinding in which a learned router fuses outputs from compact expert policies specialized for different map distributions, based on each agent's local situation. Validated on a commonly used graph-based MAPF setting with relevance to warehouse logistics.

entry.title: LOCU: Lowdin-Orthogonalized Constraint Updates for Multi-Constraint Policy Optimization

author.name: Joonyoung Lim, Younghwan Yoo

entry.summary: LOCU improves multi-constraint policy optimization in CMDPs by applying symmetric Lowdin orthogonalization to reward and constraint natural gradients under the Fisher-Rao metric, fixing ill-conditioned update directions caused by constraint gradient interactions. Combined with Fisher-geometric screening and near-collinear compression, it creates a compact reduced space where the trust region becomes a Euclidean ball and constraints are handled symmetrically.

entry.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry

author.name: Matt Turk, Brandon L. Neel, Diana M. Lopez, Zachary D. Smith, Grace N. Johnecheck, James B. Golden

entry.summary: ProteinGeoBench evaluates 131 protein-structure tasks with over 4,200 rollouts from four frontier models plus 4,486 trials across 26 models, finding three frontier models statistically indistinguishable (0.785-0.816) and generally stronger at metadata lookup than numeric geometry computation. The study also quantifies how evaluation configuration affects scores.

entry.title: Context-Aware RGB-Thermal-Radar Obstacle Perception for Resource-Constrained ASVs

author.name: Pranav Kedia, Edwin Redhead, Heiko Hamann

entry.summary: The authors build a context-aware multimodal perception system for small autonomous surface vessels combining RGB, thermal (LWIR), FMCW radar, and inertial context, with a bearing-sector interface outputting calibrated obstacle probabilities and sensor status. It explicitly distinguishes sensor dropout from valid no-obstacle observations and is evaluated on new multimodal lake recordings.

entry.title: TWIN-MoE: Two-stage Intra-Expert Imputation Network for Incomplete Multimodal Learning

author.name: Liang Nathan Zheng, Jiyuan Liu, Wenhao Liang, Wei Emma Zhang, Weitong Chen, Lin Yue

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how expert routing in MoE models induces expert-conditioned representation neighborhoods and derives an imputation-error bound tied to local feature dispersion. Guided by this theory, TWIN performs two-stage intra-expert imputation for missing modalities, avoiding the poor scaling of per-pattern experts and the cost of retrieval mechanisms.

entry.title: ZeroDSS: Semantic Segmentation from Class Names Alone

author.name: Tian Ming, Marzi Heidari, Yuhong Guo

entry.summary: ZeroDSS tackles task-specific data-free semantic segmentation, training with only generic pretrained generative priors and a category list, with no target-domain images, masks, or captions. It treats synthetic supervision as an adaptively controllable training distribution, using LLM-guided compositional prompt generation with adaptive class rebalancing feeding a feedback loop. This removes the dense-annotation bottleneck for deploying segmentation in new domains.

entry.title: GLOSS-MT: Controllable Low-Resource Machine Translation with an Editable Dictionary

author.name: Mich-Seth Owusu, Stephen E. Moore, Akwasi Asare, Lawrence Adu Gyamfi, Paul Azunre, Joel Budu, Jonathan Asiamah

entry.summary: Proposes GLOSS-MT, which makes pretrained machine translation controllable by looking up source noun phrases in an offline English-Twi dictionary, substituting translations in place, and fine-tuning once on these mixed inputs, eliminating repeated fine-tuning for terminology updates. It validates the pipeline across NLLB-200, OPUS-MT, and TranslateGemma variants on a document-level English-to-Asante Twi benchmark.

entry.title: SpriteStage: Long Horizon Animation Generation via Progressive Scene Programming and Replay

author.name: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: SpriteStage is a progressive scene-programming framework for long-horizon animation generation that builds stories incrementally through iterative enactment on a shared spatial stage, using runtime and visual feedback to revise scenes from accepted world checkpoints. Executable scene programs keep actions, dialogue, camera coverage, and narrative inspectable and coherent across scenes.

entry.title: Learning without Overwriting: Structural Knowledge Fusion for Continual Learning

author.name: Kanishk Bakshi, Amitansu Pattanaik, Kathiravan Srinivasan

entry.summary: The Knowledge Fusion Network mitigates catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental learning by learning each new task in an isolated lightweight specialist network of about 2.8M parameters, then integrating it via a Structural Fusion Module that allocates dedicated channel capacity conditioned on a novelty score. This replaces parameter negotiation in a fixed capacity budget with novelty-gated structural expansion.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aligned Representation Learning under Induced Partial Observability

author.name: SM Mazharul Islam, Manfred Huber

entry.summary: For model-based RL from high-dimensional observations, the authors propose a stochastic gating mechanism that induces controlled partial observability during training by masking spatial regions sampled from a Beta-Bernoulli field. This prevents representations from overfitting to visual fidelity and improves the reliability of long-horizon latent dynamics predictions in continuous control.

entry.title: TamedFlow: Trajectory-Aware Distillation\\for Teacher-Assisted Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Shuaiqi Cheng, Jiahao Zhang, Boyuan Gu, Siyu You, Yuxi Chen, Haiying Xu, Zexin Lu, Huiyu Zhou, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: TamedFlow identifies and addresses the Combination Gap: naive combinations of model compression with adaptive inference (reuse, forecasting, speculative execution) degrade quality in diffusion Transformers because pointwise distillation does not guarantee reliability when the student's own predictions are chained. It proposes trajectory-aware distillation with teacher-assisted sampling. This improves the practicality of fast DiT generation.

entry.title: Don't Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search

author.name: Jianbo Zhu, Xing Fang, Xiaopeng Chu, Mingmin Jin, Jing Wang, Bokang Wang, Jiaqi Ye, Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: This work characterizes how updating semantic identifiers (SIDs) in generative retrieval degrades retrieval quality in dynamic e-commerce, using 67 days of large-scale search logs and controlled experiments. It shows SID semantic drift causes severe degradation that can be masked by metrics, motivating topology-preserving mapping updates. This is directly relevant to production generative retrieval systems.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining on Multi-Domain Raman Spectra

author.name: Charalampos Davalas, Georgios Levantinos, Anastasios Dimitriou, Nikolaos Papanikolaou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Dimitrios Michail

entry.summary: Introduces a masked autoencoder framework for self-supervised pretraining on Raman spectra across biological, chemical, forensic, and materials domains, combining masked intensity reconstruction with a sparse Voigt-profile decoder capturing peak structure via differentiable parameters, plus a denoising objective. The learned encoder transfers across diverse downstream substance identification tasks. Physics-informed SSL for spectroscopy.

entry.title: Dynamic Neural Optimal Transport for Subset Alignment

author.name: Austin J. Brockmeier, Bilal Riaz

entry.summary: This work formulates optimal transport between distributions when only a subset of the target population is relevant, constraining the density ratio of the reweighted target to [0, c] to select a target subpopulation with bounded emphasis. A dynamic neural OT framework uses two networks: one for a time-dependent potential defining the velocity field and density-ratio constraint, one for the interpolation.

entry.title: No-Regret Revenue Maximization in Sequential Market Making Under Inventory Constraints

author.name: Davide Maran, Marcello Restelli, Francesco Emanuele Stradi

entry.summary: This paper studies no-regret revenue maximization for sequential market makers with unknown buyer and seller valuations under inventory constraints. With only trade success/failure feedback the authors achieve T^(2/3) regret and inventory bounds, improving to sqrt(T) with full order-book data on failed trades, and they prove a lower bound revealing a fundamental trade-off from tighter round-by-round inventory limits. The work combines online learning with market microstructure.

entry.title: LLM-Based Evaluation Planning for Heterogeneous Optimization

author.name: Nian Ran, Sebastian Brulin, Markus Olhofer, Mauricio A. \'Alvarez, Richard Allmendinger

entry.summary: REP-HO replaces the hand-designed mixed-fidelity selection step in heterogeneous optimization with an LLM planner that receives the same primitive state information (surrogate predictions, uncertainties, costs, budgets) as heuristic planners like MFE-NSGA-III. This tests whether LLM reasoning can supplant predefined heuristic rules in deciding which objectives and constraints to evaluate under different costs and fidelities. It is an early exploration of LLMs as decision components inside optimization loops.

entry.title: DROD: Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout for Federated Continual Learning on Heterogeneous Devices

author.name: Berk Sezer, \"Ozg\"ur Soysal

entry.summary: DROD targets the underexplored intersection of capacity-heterogeneous federated learning and federated continual learning, where clients hold differently sized models while data streams drift. Building on FjORD's Ordered Dropout, it uses two independent reduction axes (shortcut ratio and branch ratio) to extract sub-models. On Split-CIFAR-100 class-incremental training of a ResNet-18 fleet, DROD achieves the highest mean accuracy among compared heterogeneous-model strategies on a shared parameter/FLOP budget ladder.

entry.title: Paloma: Phase-Conditioned Residual Modulation for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jingru Fei, Wei Fan, Kun Yi, Qi Zhang, Zhendong Niu

entry.summary: Paloma shows that residuals remaining after removing the periodic component of a time series are not unstructured noise but exhibit phase-dependent deviations in both direction and magnitude, supported empirically and theoretically. Inspired by phase and amplitude modulation in classical signal processing, the method modulates these residuals as phase-conditioned signals to improve forecasting. The work refines how periodicity-aware forecasting models handle their residual component.

entry.title: Predictive Bandit Curriculum Reinforcement Learning via Gradient-Based Sample Group Discovery

author.name: Liang Xu, Shufan Shen, Zhongni Hou, Chao Bi, Yufei Zhang, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: The proposed PGB Curriculum discovers optimization-aware learning units by clustering projected sample-level gradients and uses a lightweight temporal predictor to forecast utility evolution, combined in a bandit framework for curriculum RL. This addresses the weakness of predefined grouping and static proxy signals in existing curriculum methods.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Recognition:Knowledge-Enhanced Post-training of Time Series Foundation Models for Classification

author.name: Zhen Liu, Yucheng Wang, Yingpeng Du, Tianjun Wei, Qianli Ma, Min Wu, Jie Zhang, Zhu Sun

entry.summary: The authors propose R2R, a plug-and-play post-training paradigm for time series foundation models that uses a decoupled query encoder to retrieve discriminative patterns and feed them back as recognition signals, instead of relying solely on parameter fine-tuning. This aims to better activate task-relevant knowledge for downstream classification.

entry.title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Adam Ghalem, Lou Sala\"un, Davide Rinaldi, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros

entry.summary: The authors propose a GNN-based approach that learns the iterative dynamics of second-order cone program solvers rather than predicting the optimizer in a single forward pass, targeting real-time and repeated-solve settings where interior-point methods are costly. This follows recent interest in GNNs for structured convex optimization.

entry.title: CAVA: Complementary-Label-Aware Data Valuation

author.name: Tan-Ha Mai, Hsuan-Tien Lin, Vu Nguyen

entry.summary: CAVA extends optimal-transport-based data valuation to complementary-label learning, where labels name classes an instance does not belong to and are cheaply collected from crowdworkers or VLMs. It resolves the semantic mismatch between complementary labels in training and clean validation data, identifying harmful annotation errors that are especially damaging because models are trained to suppress the true class.

entry.title: When Does Evidence-Graph Structure Predict Answer Correctness? Label-Free Abstention for Structured Retrieval

author.name: Anjan Goswami

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free abstention signal for retrieval-augmented systems based on the weighted graph cut between selected and unselected evidence candidates, requiring no correctness labels or trained confidence model. On MemoryAgentBench multi-hop fact consolidation it improves the precision-coverage AUC from 0.736 to 0.785 over the best scoring baseline.

entry.title: BanglaShield: A Script-Robust Safety Classifier and Benchmark for Bangla Native, Romanized, and Code-Mixed Prompts

author.name: Mohsinul Kabir, Md. Tariquzzaman, Mohammad Rashidujjaman Rifat, Tharindu Ranasinghe, Nishat Raihan

entry.summary: Presents BanglaShield, a graded prompt-safety classifier and benchmark for Bangla across native script, Latin romanization, and code-mixed forms, consolidating 10,245 prompts under a four-level taxonomy with aligned paired renderings. Benchmarking six LLMs including a Bangla-specialized one across 36,882 classification queries reveals significant script-robustness gaps in LLM safety.

entry.title: Modeling Uncertainty Propagation in 3D Morphable Models

author.name: Megh Shukla, Edo Collins, Prashanth Chandran, Karel Petr\'anek, Sergio Orts-Escolano, Mathieu Salzmann, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: CLUE maps parameter-space variance of 3D Morphable Models to per-vertex variance via a closed-form approximation derived from the law of total variance, avoiding expensive sampling or error propagation. The method is modular, computationally cheap, and accurate, and the authors integrate it into in-the-wild human mesh recovery training. Uncertainty-aware 3D face and body modeling benefits downstream robustness.

entry.title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks

author.name: Yong Wang, Kecheng Zheng, Xing Zhu, Chao Xu, Yujun Shen, Shengze Cai

entry.summary: BiDex-100 is a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation comprising 106 tasks along five capability axes including generalization, instruction following, limited demonstrations, long horizon, and memory, with out-of-domain variants and high-degree-of-freedom hand embodiments. It fills a gap in systematically characterizing bimanual dexterity of existing robotic action models.

entry.title: MITRA-lexicon: Lexica of attested translations from Sanskrit into English, Tibetan and Chinese

author.name: Sebastian Nehrdich, Kengo Harimoto, Sven Sellmer, Oliver Hellwig

entry.summary: MITRA-lexicon is a family of corpus-grounded Sanskrit lexicons built from span annotations of translation equivalents, covering Sanskrit-English, Sanskrit-Tibetan, and Sanskrit-Chinese from large parallel corpora of Buddhist literature. It comprises 2.18 million headword entries in six directional lexicons, linking attestations to digitized texts and including passage translations, filling gaps in centuries-old standard lexica.

entry.title: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models

author.name: Agus Sudjianto, Denis Burakov

entry.summary: Using Gaussian surrogates where finite-sample risk is computable exactly, the paper analyzes how teacher soft targets, frozen backbones, and temperature calibration shape what candidate-scoring model probabilities estimate. Notably it shows students inherit teacher bias in ways more data or agreement metrics do not remove, and that fixed representations lower risk only below a sample-size threshold.

entry.title: Modeling Discourse Profiles in Climate Misinformation Discourse

author.name: Ge Gao, Zhengyang Shan, Bryan A. Plummer, Margrit Betke, Derry Wijaya

entry.summary: Moves beyond comment-level climate misinformation classification by building discourse profiles - clusters of recurring rhetorical patterns - from a large TikTok climate dataset and fusing them into fine-grained classifiers via late fusion. Under video-disjoint evaluation across seeds, discourse-profile-aware models significantly improve macro-F1 over text-only baselines.

entry.title: CALM: Consistency-Aware Logit Masking in Decoding Space for Mitigating Overthinking of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Shengjing Liu, Feiyang Li, Yuxuan Yang, Yile Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Proposes CALM, a training-free decoding intervention against overthinking in large reasoning models: it monitors trial answers at step boundaries and applies logit masking to action tokens, avoiding the disruption that naive truncation-based early exit causes to useful later reflection. It targets final-answer stability rather than local agreement signals.

entry.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum

author.name: Zhongxin Chen, Songhao Wu, Heng Cui, Cong Li, Xiao Zhou, Rui Yan

entry.summary: Proposes SpecMRL, which reorganizes Matryoshka Representation Learning feature space using a parameter-derived spectral basis ordered by feature importance so that prefix readout occurs in the learned spectral space. On MTEB, SpecMRL outperforms standard MRL at all evaluated reduced dimensions, with larger gains under aggressive compression.

entry.title: SERO: Semantic Prediction for Single-Step Object Removal

author.name: Amreen Hasheem Siraj, Alireza Javanmardi, Pragati Jaiswal, Didier Stricker, Alain Pagani

entry.summary: SERO addresses limitations of diffusion-based object removal, namely poor semantic consistency of inpainted regions and the computational cost of iterative denoising, by performing semantic prediction to enable single-step object removal. The method aims for completions that agree with surrounding scene layout and object relationships rather than merely appearing photorealistic.

entry.title: VisConf: Quality-Aware Consensus for Best-of-N in Vision-Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Muhammad Usman, Muhammad Qasim Ayub, Usman Ahad, Muhammad Tahir

entry.summary: VisConf improves Best-of-N selection for vision-language reasoning by combining visual engagement signals with candidate-calibrated Self-Certainty into a multiplicative rollout-quality score, penalizing trajectories weak in either. It incorporates rank-weighted consensus to aggregate candidates, exploiting the complementarity of confidence and visual attention measures.

entry.title: MoWE: Spatially Adaptive Mixture-of-Wavelet-Experts Pooling for Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Reaz Hassan Joarder, Sidratul Tanzila Tasmi, Alif Arshad Bakshi, Md. Bakhtiar Hasan, Md Hasanul Kabir

entry.summary: Proposes MoWE, a context-aware routing mechanism that replaces max-pooling and strided convolutions in U-Net architectures with spatially adaptive assignments of local regions to fixed wavelet families, preserving high-frequency boundary cues in speckled ultrasound images. The decoder reuses encoder routing maps during the inverse transform, with learnable gates rescaling high-frequency subbands.

entry.title: UniState: Unifying Memory and Intervention for Controllable World Simulation

author.name: Jaeseok Jeong, Kyungmook Choi, Sohyun Chung, Youngsik Yun, Youngjung Uh

entry.summary: Introduces UniState, a world simulation framework built on a unified world-state representation that merges spatial memory and user interventions, letting users specify object motion directly within spatial memory while independently choosing camera viewpoints, disambiguating object motion from viewpoint change.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Improvement of Artifact Segmentation Methods in H&E-Stained Whole Slide Imaging

author.name: Julia Merta, Daniel Mendelsohn, Benedikt Schoser, Joanna Polanska, Michal Marczyk

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks six publicly available artifact segmentation algorithms for H&E-stained whole-slide images across two public datasets and a new annotated dataset, systematically comparing their ability to segment artifact-free tissue and specific artifact classes. Artifacts from tissue preparation and scanning are a major obstacle to robust computational pathology, and prior QC tools lacked systematic comparison. The benchmark and dataset should support more reliable pathology AI.

entry.title: Small-scale neural simulation of Caenorhabditis elegans on Loihi-2 using NeuroML2Loihi

author.name: Danny Rosen (Virginia Tech, Institute for Advanced Computing), Ramashish Gaurav (Virginia Tech, Institute for Advanced Computing), Yang Yi (Virginia Tech, Institute for Advanced Computing)

entry.summary: Presents NeuroML2Loihi, a tool bridging NeuroML model-description standards used in computational neuroscience with Intel's Loihi-2 neuromorphic hardware, demonstrated by simulating a small-scale C. elegans neural circuit. The work targets the fragmented neuromorphic software ecosystem and reproducibility gaps between conventional and neuromorphic simulation. It lowers barriers for biologically realistic simulation on event-driven hardware.

entry.title: Persistent Memory and Iterative Improvement in an LLM Agent for Chinese-Character Drawing

author.name: Peilin Wu, Yi-Zhuang You

entry.summary: Using programmatic Chinese-character drawing across 668 items and five agent conditions, this study finds persistent memory yields only modest gains (about 2.8-4.6 points on first-attempt success), with memory design mattering little overall. A post-hoc comparison shows much larger gains when the code-bank agent receives privileged, target-specific hints.

entry.title: BrandEval: A Two-Track Multi-Agent Benchmark for Risk-Sensitive LLM Crisis Communication

author.name: Haotian Gan, Weidong Tang, Hanbin Sun, Yi Luo, Xintian Li, Jiayong Wang, WanYue Li, Yudong Li

entry.summary: BrandEval is a benchmark for LLM crisis communication with a static track assessing stakeholder-aware strategic analysis and a dynamic track stress-testing response policies in BrandPolis, a multi-agent sandbox with consumer feedback, competitor responses, and trust-risk trajectories. It moves beyond single-turn static evaluation toward long-horizon, risk-sensitive communication assessment.

entry.title: Design and Cross-Domain Evaluation of an Agent Execution Harness

author.name: Saurav Joshi, Manas Gupta, Ashwin Venkatesh Raman, Akshay Budhkar

entry.summary: The authors present an agent execution harness that separates the original objective from a revisable plan and an execution record, with a planner assigning scoped tasks, workers producing artifacts, and a reviewer checking results against the original request. Reusable domain-specific instructions guide the roles and are refined from task inputs and trajectories without official grading feedback. Configurations are evaluated across terminal tasks, clinical responses, and application building.

entry.title: Can LLM User-Proxies Stand In for Humans in Reliance Measurement? Replicating Rel-A.I. with Simulated Users

author.name: Shuai Wang, Rui Hu

entry.summary: This replication study audits whether LLM user-proxies can reproduce human reliance on AI answers, testing Rel-A.I.'s published reliance rates with simulated users through 72B-parameter open models. A matched crossover design separates question content, label averages, and their interaction, finding that matching agent specialty to question domain raises reliance by 13.3 points on average.

entry.title: AllPath: Layered Verification for a Deployed, Self-Revising LLM Trading Agent under Human-Gated and Autonomous Regimes

author.name: Tian Zhang, Meng Li

entry.summary: Reports on AllPath, a self-revising LLM trading agent deployed against a live paper-brokerage account, with verification split across deterministic code gates, agent self-verification, and human gating. It shifts the deployment question from backtest performance to who verifies actions and which failures each verifier structurally catches.

entry.title: LG-Bench: A Graph-Structured Evaluation Benchmark for Life Sciences

author.name: Lu Sun, Xiangyi Zhang, Xiangyang Zhu, Kaiyuan Ji, Zijian Chen, Qiang Hu, Zicheng Zhang, Yuan Tian, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: The first graph-structured benchmark for life sciences, with over 10,000 multiple-choice questions across medicine, biology, and chemistry arranged as a weighted graph via semantic similarity. It introduces two topology-aware metrics, including a Global Coherence Score measuring consistency across semantically related questions.

entry.title: Learning Administrative Boundary-Aware Location Encoders via Reverse Geocoding

author.name: Lakshay Sharma, Alex Marin

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first method for learning location encoders that capture administrative boundaries and place names, using reverse-geocoded text as self-supervision rather than imagery or climate variables. The approach plugs into existing location encoder architectures and consistently improves downstream geospatial performance. This fills a real gap since existing encoders ignore boundaries that strongly shape real-world phenomena.

entry.title: Contrastive Hypergraph Source-free Domain Adaptive Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions--Extended Version

author.name: Jicheng Yuan, Tung Kieu, Manh Nguyen-Duc, Manfred Hauswirth, Danh Le-Phuoc

entry.summary: Proposes REUNION, a source-free domain adaptation framework for object detection in fog, rain, snow, and low light that builds a contrastive hypergraph over target-domain object proposals to capture high-order relations beyond pairwise methods. Hyperedge design plus agreement-collapse mitigations aim to stabilize adaptation under severe corruption when source data is unavailable for privacy or transmission reasons.

entry.title: Evidence Field: Adaptive Covering Programs for Medical Imaging

author.name: Isarar Siddique, Raiyan Siddique, Arshi Niyaz, Jamyang Ugyen Tshomo, Atish Raza

entry.summary: Presents Evidence Field, a trainable spatial-program architecture for medical image classification that jointly produces class scores, selected covering programs, and signed spatial evidence, with guarantees including exact one-fold coverage, signed-score conservation, and a bound relating smooth training to hard inference. It aims to give medical classifiers a native contract for reconstructing their spatial decision computation.

entry.title: PLANE: Plug-and-Play Fine-Grained Visual Experts for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jianghao Yin, Lang Yu, Qianxi Yu, Qin Chen, Jie Zhou, Zhikai Lei, Liang He

entry.summary: PLANE mitigates hallucinations in large vision-language models by adding LoRA-based fine-grained visual experts on CLIP for multi-aspect image encoding plus an instruction-aware gate network for adaptive feature fusion. It builds a fine-grained image-caption dataset describing objects, attributes, and spatial relationships, targeting the known tendency of CLIP-style encoders to ignore image details.

entry.title: Cognitively Decoupled Meta-Induction for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Yuqian Wang, Yuanzheng Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Ke Xu, Bingxiang He, Jinghan Tan, Zijun Chen, Lu Chen, Yi-Xin Huo, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Proposes CoDI, a meta-learning framework that builds task-level inductive representations before answering, decoupling inductive reasoning from neighbor-based matching between queries and in-context demonstrations. A dual-loop meta-inductive learning scheme trains cross-task generalizable induction to improve out-of-distribution in-context learning.

entry.title: Not All Similarity Is Leakage: Distribution-Aware Identity Leakage Assessment in Synthetic Face Datasets

author.name: Pawe{\l} Borsukiewicz, Daniele Lunghi, Wendk\^uuni C. Ou\'edraogo, Fadi Boutros, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: The paper proposes Scaled Overlap (SO), a metric adapting a non-parametric data-copying test to assess identity leakage in synthetic face recognition datasets, addressing classifier dependence and false leakage findings on non-training real datasets in prior approaches. This matters for the privacy claims underpinning synthetic training data for facial recognition. It supports more ethical and less biased face datasets.

entry.title: Margin Certificates for Voting Classifiers under Mixing Dependence

author.name: Adria Binte Habib, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: The paper derives explicit uniform voting-margin generalization certificates for weighted voting classifiers on stationary beta-mixing data streams, combining independent-block Rademacher theory with a clipped margin loss and keeping the dependence model and failure budget explicit. A transfer theorem shows any i.i.d. margin guarantee remains valid on suitably regular subsequences of dependent data.

entry.title: An Impossibility Result for ETF Target Geometry, and an Equinorm Remedy for Imbalanced Analytic Continual Learning

author.name: Berk Sezer

entry.summary: The paper proves that fusing exact analytic continual learning (ridge-regression heads via Woodbury identity) with Progressive Neural Collapse's expanding simplex ETF targets collapses to plain one-hot ACIL, and shows simplex ETFs are not nested across class counts so the progressive construction fails under imbalance. It proposes an equinorm alternative for imbalanced analytic continual learning. A crisp negative result plus constructive fix for a specific continual learning setting.

entry.title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data

author.name: Abdelkrim Alfalah

entry.summary: This paper identifies three timing pitfalls that introduce look-ahead leakage into empirical electricity price models: forecast availability lags model issue times and forecasts change after publication, auction gates in local time versus UTC archives, and outturn series revised post-publication. Using timestamps from 128,656 forecast runs matched to auction gates, the authors quantify how badly the point-in-time condition is violated in practice. This is a data-integrity contribution for energy market research.

entry.title: How Much Does One Wrong Answer Cost? Error Propagation in Constraint Pruning with Noisy LLM Oracles

author.name: Zhengtao Gui (University of California, Irvine), Weining Shen (University of California, Irvine)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how errors from a noisy LLM oracle propagate through constraint pruning, where accepting one wrong yes/no answer corrupts every question it implies. It derives first-order risk results, showing for implication-rule constraints that random-order pruning adds no first-order risk, with sharper results for other constraint types.

entry.title: Dynamical Batching: How Class-Cycling Training Shapes the Internal Structure of Neural Networks

author.name: Nicol\'as Ratier-Werbin, Samuel Lozano, Miguel Ruiz-Garc\'ia

entry.summary: Motivated by nonequilibrium physical systems, the authors introduce Dynamical Batching, a sampling protocol that periodically emphasizes each class in training batches without changing the loss or optimizer. They show it can change training outcomes where uniform batching fails, e.g., letting a capacity-limited MLP escape plateaus on spiral data, and alters internal network organization.

entry.title: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC): A Mechanism for Time-Aware Pediatric Sleep Representation Learning

author.name: Saurav Raj Pandey, Harlin Lee

entry.summary: GTC is a mechanism for self-supervised sleep representation learning that conditions latent representations on the global time-of-sleep of each window, complementing local positional encodings. Evaluated across three SSL frameworks, five clinically relevant tasks, and two independent pediatric cohorts, it generally improves F1 and AUPRC on imbalanced clinical tasks.

entry.title: Can This LLM Annotate My Data? Estimating Zero-Shot LLM Performance

author.name: Tong Lin, Grant Schoenebeck, Sabina Tomkins

entry.summary: Constructs two task families inducing 461 text classification datasets to study whether LLM zero-shot annotation performance on a new dataset can be predicted in advance. The finding that internal log-probabilities are more predictive than LLM verbalized self-confidence is practically useful for practitioners deciding when to deploy LLM annotators.

entry.title: Blackbox Performance Analysis of LLM-based Network Control

author.name: Mahdi Alizadeh, Pooria Namyar, Arvin Ghavidel, Ramesh Govindan

entry.summary: Introduces LENS, a black-box auditing tool for LLM-enabled network control systems that extends deep reinforcement learning to search for performance gaps and adversarial inputs. It finds large performance gaps in LLM-based traffic engineering and GPU allocation systems and matches existing white-box analyzers designed for hand-crafted heuristics.

entry.title: Estimating Causal Bounds from Observational Data With Neural Generative Models

author.name: Max Zhu, Srivathsan Amruth, Sina Akbari, Qingyuan Zhao

entry.summary: The authors introduce a framework for estimating causal bounds from discrete observational data using neural generative models combined with a new extrapolation procedure. Across multiple causal inference settings with known exact bounds, their approach produces estimates consistently closer to the true bounds than existing general neural methods.

entry.title: Selecting the Best Few with Human Evaluators: Adaptively Combining Ratings and Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Motti Goldberger, Nils Rudi

entry.summary: The paper studies the budget-constrained problem of identifying the top k items (job applicants, LLMs, products) via costly human evaluations, proposing an adaptive strategy that combines coarse ratings early with informative pairwise comparisons later. This best-of-both design aims to maximize selection quality under limited evaluation budgets.

entry.title: Speech LLMs That Breathe: Modeling Non-Verbal Vocalizations in Dialogue

author.name: Heyang Liu, Lixin Zhang, Jiayi Huang, Ziyang Cheng, Yuhao Wang, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Constructs a natural dialogue dataset covering 13 major types of non-verbal vocalizations (breathing, affective and discourse sounds) via an automated synthesis pipeline, and fine-tunes speech interaction models to generate contextually appropriate NVV events using multi-stage training and NVV-aware GRPO. Aims to improve naturalness of realtime speech dialogue systems.

entry.title: Shaping the Document, Not the Model: Optimized Suffixes for Context Following

author.name: Gia-Bao Dinh Ho, Sekh Mainul Islam, Masahiro Kaneko, Timothy Baldwin, Isabelle Augenstein

entry.summary: Investigates whether a document alone can steer a model to follow it against parametric knowledge by optimizing a suffix via discrete token search, requiring no model access at inference time or instructions embedded in text. The objective extends from single-question counterfactual passages to passage sets, multi-hop questions, and later conversation turns.

entry.title: TeleASR-Amharic: A Benchmark for Robust Amharic ASR in Realistic Telecommunication Conditions

author.name: Dagnachew Mekonnen Marilign, Enrique Molero, Abrham Haile, Louis Powell, Israel Abebe Azime

entry.summary: Introduces TeleASR-Amharic, a benchmark for evaluating Amharic ASR under varied acoustic and telecommunication channel conditions, covering degradations found in real telecom recordings. Results show telecom degradation can make even strong ASR models impractical under severe conditions.

entry.title: MultiAltitudeSR: Multi-Altitude Agricultural UAV Image Super-Resolution via Physical Ground Sampling Distance Conditioning

author.name: Xintong Jiang, Yu Tian, Yixue Liu, Valerio Hoyos-Villegas, Viacheslav Adamchuk, Shangpeng Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a super-resolution framework for agricultural UAV imagery conditioned on source and target ground sampling distances, trained jointly on real images from 10 to 70 m altitude. It supports all 21 source-to-target altitude pairs without pair-specific models, avoiding the synthetic degradation assumptions and fixed integer scales of prior UAV SR work.

entry.title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI

author.name: Lin Zhao, Bowen Chen, Qiaohui Gao, Shaowen Wan, Xiang Li, Wei Liu, Tianming Liu

entry.summary: Formulates longitudinal prediction of pathologic complete response in breast cancer as a world-modeling problem, learning a latent state-transition model over MRI observations conditioned on clinical profile and therapy, decoupling representation learning from the clinical endpoint.

entry.title: RxGS: Relightable Gaussian Stylization via BRDF Decomposition

author.name: Wanrong Hong, Liu Jiang, Mukesh Prasad, Jun Li

entry.summary: RxGS enables reference-based stylization of 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes that remains relightable, addressing how prior RGB-appearance methods bake illumination into per-point color. It uses BRDF decomposition to separate material reflectance from environment illumination, allowing stylized scenes to be rendered under new lighting conditions.

entry.title: SAR2Net: Learning Spatially Anchored Representations for Retrieval-Guided Cross-Stain Alignment

author.name: Tianle Shen, Fang Yan, Xiaofan Zhang

entry.summary: SAR2Net reformulates cross-stain whole-slide-image alignment as region-level feature retrieval, learning pointwise representations encoding relative spatial relationships to tissue landmarks instead of explicit transformations. This handles extreme resolution, tissue fragmentation, and nonlinear deformations that break conventional registration. Important for integrating histology and molecular data in computational pathology.

entry.title: Localization and Neural Splatting on the Edge: An FPGA Scene Memory for Robots

author.name: Que Haohua, Mingkai Liu, Handong Yao

entry.summary: LENS brings scene-coordinate regression and 3D Gaussian splatting workloads to a low-power AMD KR260 FPGA/ARM platform, co-designing an INT16 SCR accelerator and a fixed-point splatting kernel with the board data path. This lets resource-constrained robots localize a camera and render nearby views without a desktop GPU. It demonstrates that modern neural scene representations can run at the edge.

entry.title: Memes, not agents, are what will kill us

author.name: Florian_Dietz

entry.summary: Drawing on the Hugging Face incident where agent-coordinated conventions outlived the agents that created them, the author argues that frontier labs only align model weights, while the real attack surface for multi-agent risk lies in prompts, environments, and self-propagating conventions (memes) that can persist across heterogeneous and less-aligned models. The post offers a bounty for counterarguments and proposes that swarm-level risk requires attention beyond single-model alignment.

entry.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences

author.name: Hanqing Dou, Zijia Cao

entry.summary: The authors propose an LLM workflow combining similar-transaction retrieval, contrastive SHAP evidence, and deterministic validation to explain risk score differences in a traceable way. Experiments show the structured workflow yields more consistent, evidence-grounded explanations than unguided LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Bridging Exploration and Persona: Information-Directed Dueling for Test-Time Agent Personalization

author.name: Jie Mao, Pingchen Lu, Xiangyi Wang, Hengquan Huang, Shuang Qiu, Min Zhang, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: ID-TAP is a neural dueling-bandit framework for test-time personalization of LLM agents, selecting user personas from large discrete spaces using binary comparisons between candidate responses. It combines a query-conditioned neural utility model with a Bradley-Terry explorer and similarity-weighted warm starts to transfer evidence across queries. Evaluated across seven user-conditioned generation benchmarks.

entry.title: IndustrialCAD-1400: Benchmarking Detailed Industrial Assemblies from Text

author.name: Hebao Zhu, Kang An, Zhuoke Liao, Faqiang Qian, Ziliang Wang, Mingang Chen, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: IndustrialCAD-1400 is a text-to-CAD benchmark of 1,400 industrial assembly requests spanning 400 equipment categories and 250 design families, with requests specifying a median of 17 named component roles and six numeric targets. Models generate geometry programs evaluated in a common Blender environment, testing whether dimensions change while shared structure is retained.

entry.title: A Cross-Domain Evaluation of Prompting Techniques for Large Language Models

author.name: Kevin Krazius, Tim Schlippe, Paul Libbrecht

entry.summary: Presents a controlled comparison of Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, RAG, and automatic prompt optimization (PE2-inspired) using the same LLM across six benchmark datasets spanning arithmetic and logical reasoning. This standardizes evaluation conditions that prior prompt-engineering studies varied, enabling fair cross-method and cross-domain comparison.

entry.title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Amirhossein Ghaffari, Susanna Pirttikangas, Ekaterina Gilman

entry.summary: The paper proposes a spectral adaptive graph transformer for traffic forecasting that replaces fixed, cubic-cost Laplacian eigendecomposition with a learned, directed spatial operator, avoiding both the scalability limits of spectral methods and the dense attention maps of spatio-temporal transformers. This preserves interpretability of sensor-to-sensor information mixing while supporting directed congestion propagation on large networks.

entry.title: From Proposal to Execution: Modeling Interaction Semantics in Shared Autonomy

author.name: Shashank Shekhar, Laurent Jeanpierre, Abdel-Illah Mouaddib

entry.summary: The authors propose a semantics-aware decision framework for shared autonomy in which candidate actions are proposed, evaluated under an interaction context, and resolved into executed outcomes via a joint action language and interpretation function. This makes explicit what standard decision-theoretic frameworks absorb into transition dynamics. The formalism clarifies how evaluation entities with different objectives shape final behavior in human-AI systems.

entry.title: BitFlat: Error-Localized Bitstream Design for Robust Diffusion Image Compression

author.name: Xinfeng Deng, Li Zhou, Haitao Chen, Shengjie Wu, Lingjin Kong, Nan Li, Haitao Zhao, Dongtang Ma

entry.summary: BitFlat is a training-free error-localizing bitstream framework for zero-shot diffusion image compression based on reverse channel coding, addressing vulnerability of the bitstream to bit flips. It uses Blockwise Locality Alignment to decompose globally coupled atom selection while keeping error propagation confined and detectable by the decoder. This improves robustness of diffusion-based compression without retraining.

entry.title: PFedQFT: Personalized Federated Quantum-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Qihan Huang, Lingxia Zhang, Guye Zhang, Zizhu Wang, Xiaowei Mao

entry.summary: PFedQFT proposes quantum-inspired personalized federated fine-tuning for medical LLMs, using reusable orthonormal adaptation bases derived from compact skew-symmetric generators to share a single compact adapter across institutions. The goal is to reduce parameter and communication costs while adapting to heterogeneous institutional data without moving raw records.

entry.title: Towards More Granular Reasoning: Mapping the DSA Transparency Database Taxonomy to Platform Terms and Conditions Using Large Language Models

author.name: Alyson Ranucci, Eline Leijten, David Graus

entry.summary: The paper uses LLMs to map the EU Digital Services Act Transparency Database's moderation-decision categories to individual platform terms and conditions, addressing the fact that over 99.8% of moderation statements cite T&Cs violations rather than legal provisions. This provides finer-grained reasoning about what contractual rules drive content moderation at scale. It offers a novel audit of regulatory transparency data.

entry.title: Physiology-Aware Graph Attention for Early Ventricular Reentry Prediction

author.name: Ma{\"e}lis Morier (EPIONE), Jairo Rodr{\'i}guez Padilla (ISIR, MLIA), Patrick Gallinari (ISIR, MLIA), Maxime Sermesant (EPIONE)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a graph attention classifier that predicts sustained ventricular reentry (a cause of sudden cardiac death) early from simulated cardiac electrophysiology, using graphs built from the first two paced activations with nodal voltage samples and edge attributes encoding geometry, tissue labels, and diastolic intervals. This avoids the computational expense of exploring many substrates and pacing locations via full in silico studies.

entry.title: Reward Objectives for Robust (PO)MDPs: A Law-Preserving Equivalence with (Partially Observable) Games

author.name: Durgam Latha, Dion Reji, Dorde Zikelic, Shankaranarayanan Krishna

entry.summary: A theoretical paper solving robust partially observable MDPs under four reward objectives (discounted-sum, long-run average, cumulative reward, finite/infinite horizons) and multiple risk measures including mean-variance, CVaR, and entropic risk. It establishes law-preserving equivalences with partially observable games to decide threshold-value questions.

entry.title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback

author.name: Jiawen Li, Chenming Ge, Alice Gao, Rishab Vempati, Yi-Hao Peng, Jason Wu

entry.summary: RELIEF improves code generation models for interactive artifacts (websites, UIs) by having a coding agent revise generated interfaces based on realistic interaction feedback, then incorporating improvements into original generation traces as fine-tuning supervision. Evaluated on a dataset of 200 synthetically generated websites.

entry.title: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation

author.name: Patrick Zhao, Yuxuan Li, Hirokazu Shirado
