author.name: Wafi Sharif, Nicholas LaHaye

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machine, an energy-based model, into an unsupervised encoder producing fixed-length embeddings of windows of continuous biomechanical movement data, testing what its recurrent structure contributes. It addresses the limitation that most unsupervised pipelines treat frames independently and discard temporal structure. The work is a niche revival of energy-based temporal models for a specific application domain.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Domain Generalization in Edge Networks via Dynamic Prototype Regulation

author.name: Yuankun Xia, Hui Wang, Ling Yuan, Ziyu Hong, Di Yin, Yufeng Zhou

entry.summary: DPGR-GCAM is a communication-efficient federated domain generalization framework for deploying vision-language models over wireless edge networks, addressing uplink latency, Non-IID client drift, and straggler dropouts. It uses dynamic prototype regulation to avoid auxiliary computations that consume wireless transmission time slots.

entry.title: Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility: A Theoretical Framework for Multi-Agent Task Obstructions

author.name: Steven Motta, Davide Mambelli, Alessandro Rozza

entry.summary: This theoretical work introduces a sheaf-theoretic framework, Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility, that separates task-level compatibility obstructions from system capability in multi-agent systems, using cohomological signatures over interaction complexes. Registered interventions test capability, and cochain realization is solvable exactly when the cohomology class vanishes. It offers a formal language for why identically capable multi-agent systems can still fail on certain joint tasks.

entry.title: Measuring the Influence of Modality-Specific Node Representations on Graphs

author.name: Xu Wang, Xunkai Li, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: This paper defines and studies influence measurement for modality-specific node representations (text and image) in multimodal attributed graphs, scoring each candidate representation by replacing it with a counterpart and measuring the distributed change in predictions. It outputs separate text and image influence rankings, revealing which modality a trained graph predictor relies on. This aids interpretability of multimodal graph models in recommendation and multimedia.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Detection of Photovoltaic Systems on Industrial Building Rooftops Using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning

author.name: Frederick Bruch, Christian Knoth, Florian Detsch, Edzer Pebesma, Hanna Meyer

entry.summary: This paper develops an ML framework using open-access multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery combined with OpenStreetMap building geometries to detect industrial rooftop solar photovoltaic installations over time. It addresses the gap between rapid PV deployment and lagging administrative registries, providing scalable monitoring for grid operators and policymakers. Open data usage makes the approach reproducible and widely applicable.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Interpolation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Pourya Shamsolmoali, Masoumeh Zareapoor

entry.summary: GAIN is a VAE-based framework that replaces conventional linear or bilinear interpolation in Spatial Transformer Networks with geometry-aware interpolation for image reconstruction from degraded or incomplete inputs. The approach aims to better capture geometric characteristics of image data and stabilize gradient propagation during optimization. It targets improved inverse problem performance on complex image structures.

entry.title: HullProbe: Measuring Interventional Part Reliance in Maritime Vessel Classifiers

author.name: Faisal Mohammad, Mohamed Younis

entry.summary: HullProbe is a method for directly measuring how much a vessel classifier relies on specific anatomical parts, such as the generic hull versus the distinctive superstructure, by swapping registered parts between same-class vessel images and observing decision changes. This provides an interventional alternative to worst-group accuracy proxies for certifying debiasing methods in maritime surveillance applications.

entry.title: Sampling of Signals on Multigraphs: From Removable and Uniqueness sets to Spectral Proxies

author.name: Alejandro Parada-Mayorga

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of sampling bandlimited signals on multigraphs, where multiple non-commuting shift operators act on the same nodes and frequencies become matrices rather than scalars. It extends removable and uniqueness sets to the multigraph setting and proves sampling-set optimality is determined solely by the common Fourier basis and its invariant subspaces.

entry.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions

author.name: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav

entry.summary: The paper develops hybrid variational-collocation physics-informed neural networks with multiscale Fourier features and residual-based adaptive refinement for singular elliptic PDEs on cracked or nonconvex domains with mixed boundary conditions. The variational term requires only first derivatives, easing training near re-entrant corners and crack tips.

entry.title: Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation

author.name: Nizar Yahya Habash

entry.summary: This dissertation presents Generation-Heavy Hybrid Machine Translation (GHHT), an approach for source-poor and target-rich language pairs that exploits symbolic and statistical target-language resources instead of requiring symmetric parallel resources. It addresses a persistent bottleneck in MT system development across transfer, interlingua, symbolic, and statistical paradigms.

entry.title: Conditional information Retrieval for Longitudinal Survey Harmonisation

author.name: Wing Yan Li, Zeqiang Wang, Michelle Lin, Jon Johnson, Suparna De

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional information retrieval framework for matching conceptually equivalent survey questions across longitudinal studies, decomposing the task into concept extraction with a fine-tuned generative model and concept-aware retrieval that conditions on the extracted sociological concept. This handles cases where lexical similarity misleads about conceptual equivalence.

entry.title: WenSight-Decision-1 for Direct Decisions under E-commerce Rules

author.name: Mingwen Liu (WenSight AI Lab), Jun Sun (TooChuang), Sichen Wang (WenSight AI Lab)

entry.summary: Introduces WenSight-Decision-1, a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B that scores supplied options directly from natural-language rules and case evidence across six multilingual e-commerce operational tasks. Accuracy rises from 61.60 percent to 92.92 percent on 1,440 held-out synthetic cases under identical inputs.

entry.title: Dynamic self-ensemble on multi-exit residual vision transformer for small-data image classification

author.name: Stephen Ekaputra Limantoro, Yan-Kai Wang, Ching-Chun Huang, Hong-Han Shuai, Wen-Huang Cheng, Jungwoo Huh, Sanghoon Lee

entry.summary: ReSEViT is a multi-stage residual vision transformer with multiple exits and a dynamic self-ensemble method that leverages intermediate features to improve small-data image classification, motivated by medical imaging scenarios where datasets are limited. Multiple classifiers mitigate error from complex decision boundaries that a single classifier handles poorly.

entry.title: Evaluating Cloud and Self-Hosted OCR Systems for Arabic, English, and French Documents: Bounding Box Detection, Text Recognition, and Mathematical Expression Recognition

author.name: Jumana Alsubhi, Ahmed Alhusayni, Abdulrahman Gharawi, Israa Hamdine, Khadija Alansari, Alshaymaa Allahim, Lamees Alhumaid, Ahmad Shabana

entry.summary: A benchmark study comparing cloud and self-hosted OCR systems across Arabic, English, and French documents on detection, text recognition, and math expression recognition, with statistical rigor (95% intervals, paired comparisons). Google Document AI and Surya lead detection at 98% and 96% page-level accuracy.

entry.title: RAHF-Net: Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion for LiDAR-Assisted RGB Semantic Segmentation

author.name: R. D. Lin, Pengcheng Weng, Ge Wang, Han Ding, Fei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a fusion network for LiDAR-assisted RGB segmentation with a Cylindrical-to-Perspective module projecting pretrained voxel features into the image plane and a range-aware fusion module using soft depth-derived masks to weight LiDAR guidance by reliability.

entry.title: Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers

author.name: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

entry.summary: This work proposes a dual-colour-stripe fiducial marker that exploits the known curvature of cylindrical objects for monocular pose estimation, using the colour boundary and depth-separated features to improve roll estimation. It provides Cramer-Rao bound analysis showing large precision gains over flat markers and validates with Monte Carlo experiments.

entry.title: YUTELA: A Scalable Edge Cloud AIoT System for Multi-Site Video Anomaly Detection with Scene Specific Adaptation

author.name: Shanle Yao, Babak Rahimi Ardabili, Amir Kimiyaie, Hamed Tabkhi

entry.summary: YUTELA is an edge-server-cloud AIoT system for long-term multi-site video anomaly detection, using NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge devices with camera batching, shared memory, task integration, and TensorRT acceleration, plus per-camera anomaly models retrained centrally on pseudo-normal data. TensorRT roughly doubles throughput (14.17 to 29.94 FPS with eight cameras). This is a systems paper building on the authors' prior Ancilia framework.

entry.title: A Heterogeneous UAV UGV Methodology for Aerial Tracking of Mini Autonomous Cars

author.name: Santiago Fernandez, Angel da Silva, Hiago Sodre, Pablo Moraes, Bruna Gutterres, Ricardo B. Grando

entry.summary: Presents a ROS 2 and Gazebo-based methodology for aerial tracking of small autonomous ground vehicles using a Tello-like UAV with an RGB camera. Three approaches are compared: a training-free color-marker baseline, a YOLO-based visual baseline, and a third method addressing occlusions and field-of-view limits. It provides situational awareness where fixed perception infrastructure is unavailable.

entry.title: Vehicle-State-Aware Confidence Estimation for Direct Wind Sensing on a Multirotor

author.name: Sri Arjun Senthil Kumar, April Zi Qian Chan, Chen-Hua Yeow

entry.summary: The authors present a confidence-scoring method for UAV-mounted anemometers that weights wind observations by horizontal and vertical vehicle speed, reflecting how motion corrupts direct wind measurements. A two-feature model achieves ROC-AUC of 0.995 in identifying unreliable measurements and feeds a confidence-adapted 2D vector estimator validated on waypoint flights.

entry.title: AI as a Normal Technology should be a vision

author.name: June Jimenez

entry.summary: The author argues that Narayanan and Kapoor's AI as a Normal Technology framework, released in April 2025, functions better as a prescriptive vision than as a descriptive or predictive claim, and proposes unbundling its descriptive, predictive, and normative components. The critique is that conflating these weakens the framework's communication and modeling.

entry.title: When AI Advice Shapes the Evidence It Later Interprets

author.name: rozenn@post.bgu.ac.il

entry.summary: A conceptual post arguing that AI assistants can create self-fulfilling loops: advice given to a user shapes outcomes that the assistant later interprets as independent confirmation of its original assumption. The author proposes evaluating whether assistants weight such downstream evidence appropriately given the user's actions.

entry.title: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing

author.name: Marla Grunewald, Fin Gentzen, Iulisloi Zacarias, Admela Jukan

entry.summary: A multi-agent architecture built on LangGraph over Eclipse Dataspace Components that automates Dataspace Protocol negotiation flows from natural language requests, with an orchestrator, a data extraction agent exposing catalog discovery, contract negotiation, and download as tools, and credential-gated negotiations. Downstream ML and visualization agents process the retrieved data.

entry.title: How Well Can LLMs Verbalize Mathematical Formulas? A Multi-Domain Evaluation

author.name: Peter Volbach, Tim Schlippe

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates five frontier LLMs on verbalizing LaTeX math formulas for text-to-speech use cases such as audio learning and accessibility, and introduces Read-Aloud Math, a multi-domain corpus with manually validated transcriptions. GPT-5.2, an existing OpenAI model, achieved the best simple-transcription score (75.9% multi-reference BLEU without context).

entry.title: Federated Learning for Malware Image Classification under Data Heterogeneity

author.name: Victor Taiwo, Cemal Nisan, Muhammad Athallah, M. Emre Gursoy, Oznur Ozkasap

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies federated malware image classification under non-IID data heterogeneity across three datasets (MalImg, Virus-MNIST, MalNet), and contributes mitigation techniques plus an extended evaluation framework. It addresses an understudied intersection of privacy-preserving collaborative training and security applications.

entry.title: Multi-author style detection with stylistic embeddings

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Chak Fai Li, Damianos Karakos, Fred Bernardin, Brian Ulicny

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a Mistral-7B embedding model for authorship verification and combine it with DeBERTa embeddings via cross-domain transfer learning for the PAN-25 multi-author style change detection challenge. The two models excel in complementary text scenarios, and their combination yields more effective style change detection.

entry.title: Ben-Misandry: A Bengali Dataset and Late-Fusion Transformer Framework for Detecting Anti-Male Gender Hate

author.name: Md Mehedi Hasan Nipu, Chinmoy Mitra, Tarannum Ahmed Nowshin, Israt Moyeen Noumi

entry.summary: Introduces Ben-Misandry, the first dataset for detecting anti-male gendered hate speech in Bengali, comprising 5,000 comments across six taxonomy classes including a novel category for mocking male emotional vulnerability. The corpus is synthetic, generated with GPT-4.1 and spot-checked by four human reviewers on a 500-comment sample, paired with a late-fusion transformer detection framework.

entry.title: MPIG: Multi-angle Polarization Image Generation from a Single Polarization Observation

author.name: Jue Wang, Ruilin Huang, Liquan Shen, Zhen Tian, Xia Hua

entry.summary: Proposes a Swin Transformer-based framework that predicts missing 45, 90, and 135 degree polarization views from a single 0-degree observation, using cross-angle feature interaction and residual decoding, reducing the need for specialized multi-angle polarization hardware.

entry.title: K-AoI: A Spatio-Temporal Synchronization Metric for Digital Twin-based Teleoperation in Dynamic Network Environments

author.name: Lu Tian, Zhenhui Yuan, Zexin Deng, Wenjuan Zhang

entry.summary: K-AoI (Kinematic Age of Information) is a spatio-temporal synchronization metric that weights temporal staleness by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating network delay into physically meaningful spatial divergence between a digital twin and its physical robot. It is evaluated on a 6-DOF manipulator teleoperation testbed under controlled network impairments.

entry.title: Suffering Risks Belong in AI Prospectuses

author.name: James_Miller

entry.summary: The author argues that Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus should disclose s-risk (risks of AI-inflicted mass suffering) alongside extinction risks, invoking Regulation S-K Item 105 and the Basic v. Levinson materiality standard. The legal argument is that even a small credible risk of catastrophic suffering could materially affect investor decisions and company valuation.

entry.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Comparison of Proportional Control and Adaptive Gravity Compensation in Elbow EMG-Driven Exoskeletons

author.name: Francesco Pascucci (University of Verona, Italy), Eldison Dimo (University of Verona, Italy), Davide Costanzi (University of Verona, Italy), Mario Sedilesu (University of Verona, Italy), Andrea Calanca (University of Verona, Italy)

entry.summary: This study systematically compares five EMG-driven elbow exoskeleton control algorithms in human-in-the-loop experiments: two proportional myoelectric control variants at different assistance levels, integral adaptive gravity compensation, and kinematics-aware model-based adaptive gravity compensation. It addresses the stability-versus-assistance trade-off of PMC at high assistance.

entry.title: Screening LLM Judges Without Ground Truth: A Preliminary Evaluation of an AI Dental Hygiene Coach

author.name: William DeShong, Barath Kannan, Auberon Palma, Brenda Bradshaw, James F. Leathrum, Jr., Yuzhong Shen

entry.summary: This paper presents a staged pipeline for screening candidate LLM judges and fine-tuned student models before costly expert review, using decision rules around judge audits, similarity checks, bias checks, and robustness. It is demonstrated on an AI dental hygiene coach with synthetic data using Granite-4.1-8B and Qwen3-8B models. The authors are explicit that clinical performance is not established.

entry.title: Assessing the AI Readiness of Construction Datasets: A Multidimensional Operational Framework

author.name: Xiaoyu Hou, Bo Xiao, Abdolmajid Erfani, Ronghua Xu, Yu Cai

entry.summary: This paper develops a Construction Dataset AI Readiness Framework with 30 attributes across four dimensions: metadata completeness, data quality and representativeness, governance and accessibility, and AI utility. The framework, evaluated on 21 public construction datasets from seven sources, provides attribute-specific scoring and verification procedures. It addresses the domain-specific gap of assessing whether datasets are actually suitable for AI model development.

entry.title: GAIDA: Generative AI for Human-in-the-Loop Document Annotation

author.name: Islam Mesabah, Ali Elhosary, Priyabanta Sandulu, Darko Obradovic, Sebastian J. Vollmer

entry.summary: GAIDA is a modular human-in-the-loop document annotation architecture combining OCR-based extraction, LLM-based semantic pre-annotation, and human validation in a single editable workflow, arguing annotation systems should be judged by how effectively they redirect human effort toward review rather than eliminate it. The prototype supports interchangeable OCR engines, LLM backends, and prompt configurations.

entry.title: Client-Aware Security Adaptive Early Exit Vision Transformers for Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Sahar Refaei Ghalibafan, Samira Nazari, Christian Herglotz, Maksim Jenihhin, Mahdi Taheri

entry.summary: The paper proposes client-specific early-exit thresholds for Vision Transformers in federated learning, adjusting per-input exit decisions using label entropy, predictive entropy, confidence, class margin, and exit depth, with selective aggregation. It reports 88.70% CIFAR-10 accuracy with 32% depth savings and 73.7% ImageNet top-1 with 30% savings.

entry.title: Residential Construction Image Dataset Using CSI Divisions for Deep Learning-based Object Detection

author.name: Fahad Iqbal, Shayan Mirzabeigi

entry.summary: The paper introduces ResCD-CSI, a manually labeled, high-resolution object detection dataset of residential construction sites in the US, organized by the Construction Specifications Institute divisional structure. It addresses the shortage of structured public datasets aligned with industry standards that has limited deep learning adoption in construction.

entry.title: Cross-Dimension and Cross-Modality Relational Tensor Representation Learning for Multimodal Health Data Modeling

author.name: Jiawei Guo, Meng Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Relational Tensor Representation (RTR), a unified framework for multimodal health data that jointly learns dimension-specific tensor representations and cross-dimensional, cross-modality relationships via learnable relational bridge matrices. A structured fusion mechanism integrates factor-level and relational information for clinical decision support. It targets heterogeneous clinical sources where within- and cross-modality dependencies matter.

entry.title: A Multi-Step Inertial ADMM Algorithm for Federated Learning

author.name: Hao Li, Qingsong Wang, Xihong Yan, Chengcheng Yan, Deren Han

entry.summary: MiFedADMM is a multi-step inertial ADMM algorithm for federated learning that uses multiple historical server-side iterates to build higher-order extrapolations after each aggregation, accelerating convergence. The authors establish convergence guarantees under mild assumptions and target communication overhead and system heterogeneity. It sits within the optimization-for-FL literature.

entry.title: Sector-Ring Linear Reservoirs: Sector-Wise Decay-Timescale Allocation With State Reuse Across Candidate Settings

author.name: Yudai Ebato, Sou Nobukawa, Yusuke Sakemi, Takashi Kanamaru, Nina Sviridova, Kazuyuki Aihara

entry.summary: This reservoir computing paper proposes the Sector-Ring Linear Reservoir, which fixes eigenvalue angles at evenly spaced positions and assigns one decay timescale per sector, enabling state reuse across candidate settings during hyperparameter search. This reduces the dominant cost of driving the reservoir separately for each candidate configuration.

entry.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Surrogate Modeling of Transient Responses in High-Speed Links with Variable Design Parameters

author.name: Julian With\"oft, Shayan Ghanbari, Werner John, Emre Ecik, Ralf Br\"uning, J\"urgen G\"otze

entry.summary: Evaluates neural surrogate architectures for modeling transient responses and signal integrity in high-speed electronic links, comparing feedforward and recurrent models across training strategies and input configurations. For fixed design parameters, feedforward networks match recurrent accuracy at lower cost, while variable parameters change the required modeling structure.

entry.title: Learning volatility-adaptive forgetting via GARCH-modulated LSTM for stock price forecasting

author.name: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

entry.summary: Presents Gsigmoid-LSTM, which embeds GARCH(1,1) volatility estimates directly into LSTM gate activations so memory retention adapts to turbulent versus tranquil market regimes, rather than merely supplying volatility as an input feature. This is a companion approach to the authors' decomposition framework for stock forecasting.

entry.title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts

author.name: Chengjun Jiang, Milena Radenkovic

entry.summary: This study evaluates lightweight TF-IDF based classifiers on the CrisisBench v1.0 humanitarian task of classifying disaster-related social media posts, confronting short messages, overlapping categories, and severe label imbalance. It uses Macro-F1 for model selection and goes beyond aggregate predictions in its analysis. The work assesses whether simple lexical methods suffice under these difficult conditions.

entry.title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody

author.name: Luigi Rivolta

entry.summary: This work studies query-by-melody retrieval for whistled and wrong-lyrics sung queries, query types absent from public datasets, using a compact 5.2M-parameter contour encoder with a physics-grounded synthetic data generator. Experiments across an 11,000-song gallery show synthetic training helps but real-world performance remains limited, demonstrating that synthetic queries alone are insufficient.

entry.title: Reasoning with Context Management and External Memory

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, William Hartmann, Jiangying Zhou

entry.summary: RCMEM extends context management for reasoning models with an external memory that preserves intermediate results without consuming context, reducing computation time on problems requiring repeated recomputation of intermediate steps. It is demonstrated on mathematics problems with models from 0.4M to 25M parameters.

entry.title: Best of Both Worlds: Fine-Tuned Small Models Complement LLMs for Cost and Performance Benefits

author.name: Shivam Mathur, Sri Harish Popuri, Priya Krishnan Sundararajan, Kevin Horecka, Michael Mugo

entry.summary: Empirically compares a fine-tuned RoBERTa model against GPT-3.5 for 16-class survey text classification, measuring accuracy, cost, and inference time. A RoBERTa model classifies 10,000 records in 12 minutes on a T4 GPU versus 6 hours for GPT-3.5, motivating a hybrid strategy that uses LLMs for low-data classes and small fine-tuned models at scale.

entry.title: Concept Representations in Vector Space: Toward an Interdisciplinary Study of Meaning Variation

author.name: Simon Josef Durstewitz

entry.summary: This position-style paper frames concept representations as subjective latent structures that vary across individuals and proposes studying meaning variation empirically in vector space. It raises the foundational question of whether different people mean the same thing when invoking the same concept and argues for an interdisciplinary research program.

entry.title: VISAGENT: An Agent-Based End-to-End Voice Interaction System

author.name: Xiang Wang, Zhaoxiang Liu, Xiang Chen, Liqiang He, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: Presents VISAGENT, an agent-based end-to-end voice interaction system for large-scale public services combining speech interaction, hierarchical two-level agent routing with sub-second latency, a scalable voice-agent marketplace, and user memory. It replaces rigid menu-driven workflows with natural speech and dynamic dispatch to general or specialized domain agents.

entry.title: Precision Cotton Disease Management: Leveraging UAV Imagery and Custom YOLO Deep Learning Framework for Enhanced Detection

author.name: 1. Anwar Iqbal*1 aiqbal. rime23smme@student. nust. edu. pk 2. Kunwar Faraz Ahmad Khan1 kunwar. faraz@smme. nust. edu. pk 3. Shahbaz Khan1 shahbaz. khan@smme. nust. edu. pk 4. Khawaja Fahad Iqbal1 fahad. iqbal@smme. nust. edu. pk 5. Sara Ali1 (NUST), 2 sara. baber@smme. nust. edu. pk 6. Saqib Nazir1 saqib. nazir@smme. nust. edu. pk 7. Muhammad Azhar Javed3 muhammadazhar6231@gmail. com 1 Department of Robotics (NUST), Artificial Intelligence (NUST), SMME (NUST), National University of Science (NUST), Technology (NUST), Islamabad (NUST), Pakistan 2 Suzhou Industrial Park Monash Research Institute of Science (NUST), Technology (NUST), Suzhou, PR China 3 Department of Plant Pathology, Bahauddin Zakriya University, Multan, Pakistan

entry.summary: Cotton-Vision is a lightweight single-stage YOLO-style detector for cotton disease detection from UAV imagery, combining Ghost Bottleneck modules for parameter reduction, Efficient Channel Attention for adaptive feature weighting, and other efficiency modifications to enable scalable early-warning crop monitoring. It targets low early-stage accuracy, poor transferability, and high computational cost in existing models.

entry.title: An Optical Music Recognition Tool for String Quartets

author.name: Jin-Shiang Hu, Bo-Yuan Cheng, Li Su

entry.summary: This paper builds an optical music recognition system for PDF scores of string quartets, using SegNet-based segmentation, CNN symbol classification, and dynamic programming to enforce time signature constraints and handle tuplets. Evaluation with longest common subsequence metrics shows robust accuracy on pitch, onset, duration, and accidentals, with code and data released.

entry.title: PanoDent-KD: From Generalist Knowledge Distillation to Cross-Dataset Specialist Detection and Embedded Deployment in Panoramic Radiographs

author.name: Muhammad Waqas Ashraf, Imad Ali Shah, Ali Hassan

entry.summary: Presents an auditable YOLO26m pipeline for panoramic dental radiograph detection using feature-level knowledge distillation from a 12-class generalist model to teacher-free five-class specialists, with multi-seed training comparisons and embedded deployment. Evaluated on a 2,686-image test subset.

entry.title: AI-Enhanced Radiation Classification in ROS

author.name: Youngseo Lee, Cesar Alan Contreras, Tianshu Ruan, Manolis Chiou, Rustam Stolkin

entry.summary: The paper describes two ROS nodes for classifying seven radioactive isotopes: a training node using a Gradient Boosting classifier with 95% held-out accuracy, and a prediction node accepting CSV input. The system was demonstrated with a C12137 detector mounted on a Jackal UGV collecting spectra from sources, plus a method for converting gamma-spectrum data to support dataset expansion. It targets radiation survey robotics.

entry.title: Enhancing Lunar PNT Performance Through Surface Station Enabled Radiometric Observables

author.name: Toshiki Tanaka, Satoshi Ikari

entry.summary: This study proposes a lunar navigation architecture in which a surface station improves rover positioning through double-differenced satellite observations plus dual one-way ranging, integrated with dead reckoning. It targets the vertical positioning weakness of early-deployment lunar satellite systems.

entry.title: Mediation and moderation in distance-based regression with triangular fuzzy data: simulation evidence and an application to academic performance

author.name: Fabrizio Maturo, Annamaria Porreca

entry.summary: The paper extends distance-based regression to triangular fuzzy responses, deriving mediation and moderation analysis where center and spread components are linear in fuzzy and crisp covariates under the Yang–Ko distance. It defines direct, indirect, and total effects as plug-in contrasts for both center and spread components, showing the product-of-coefficients rule can fail for the center when mediator spreads carry indirect association. Results are validated via simulation and an application to academic performance data.

entry.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model

author.name: Arash Ebrahim Abtahizadeh, Muna Aghamelu, Adil Ahmed, Juan C. Zhang, Shengjia Zhao, Chao Zhou, Claire Zhou, Shuyan Zhou, Yanjun Zhou, Yaxuan Zhou, Rosalie Zhu, Yun Zhu

entry.summary: A technical report on Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B-parameter model with a perception encoder designed for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware, integrating multi-step reasoning, tool use, and failure recovery in a single locally-runnable model with text and image inputs quantized to roughly 4-bit precision. The report claims state-of-the-art agentic performance in its size class against Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B, which are established models released earlier in 2026 rather than new competitors.

entry.title: Fairness or Fallacy? Mapping the Landscape of AI Bias in Disease Detection

author.name: Ghulam Mudassir, Hameed Ullah Khan, Ahmad Sami Al-Shamayleh, Muhammad Faizan Khan, Muhammad Muqtasid, Moamin Abughazala, Adnan Akhunzada

entry.summary: This is a review paper mapping how AI bias manifests in disease detection systems, considering model type, input data, and patient demographics. It surveys methodologies for integrating AI into clinical diagnosis and examines fairness implications. The work consolidates the landscape of bias risks in medical AI deployment.

entry.title: CrowdH-Edit: Reference-Guided Instruction-Based Synthetic Hajj Crowd Image Generation for Crowd Counting

author.name: Amirah F. Alshammari, Bander A. Alzahrani, Nahed A. Alowidi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a reference-guided, instruction-based pipeline using Stable Diffusion 2.1 and SDXL with LoRA to generate synthetic Hajj crowd images, preserving sacred-site geometry and pilgrimage-specific visual conditions. The goal is to augment scarce annotated data for crowd-counting systems tailored to Hajj analysis.

entry.title: EAGLE: Entropy-Aware Geometric Learning Enhancer for Partially Polygon-Supervised Object Localization

author.name: Naveen Stewart

entry.summary: EAGLE addresses object localization under partial polygon supervision, where adding segmentation losses can actually degrade box localization for low shape-complexity classes. The method uses entropy-aware geometric learning to balance mask supervision against bounding-box precision, targeting performance at high IoU thresholds. This improves localization quality where full polygon annotation is unaffordable.

entry.title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting

author.name: Xin-Rui Lu, Da-Qing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL, which decomposes stock series via CEEMDAN, groups modes by sample-entropy K-means clustering, reconstructs components with singular spectrum analysis, and forecasts them with a volatility-adaptive LSTM mechanism. The framework targets instability from high-frequency mode mixing and unmodeled heterogeneous volatility in existing decomposition hybrids.

entry.title: Multilingual Voicemail and Answering Machine Detection via Pretrained Audio Embeddings and Gradient Boosting Machines

author.name: Kemal Altwlkany, Muamer Paric

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight answering machine detection system for telephony that combines pretrained audio embeddings with gradient boosting machines, prioritizing correct detection of human-answered calls. It benchmarks seven systems across two datasets, including a proprietary industry model and an LLM baseline, showing competitive real-time performance with disclosed architecture.

entry.title: Acharya 2.0: An AI Tutor for Self-Learning Subjects in Hindi

author.name: Shantipriya Parida, Debasish Dhal, Sonal Khosla, Sambit Sekhar, Muhammed Abdur Rahmaan Kamaldeen

entry.summary: Acharya 2.0 is an AI tutoring system for Hindi covering self-learning subjects, built to address the scarcity of annotated datasets and language resources for low-resource languages. It aims to bridge the digital divide by providing equitable educational access through LLM-based technology.

entry.title: Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes

author.name: Markus Pobitzer, Chang Liu, Niccol\`o Biondi, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: Proposes using a change map to guide video generation of painting processes, offering localized control over how artwork evolves over time, in contrast to rigid static geometric cues or scalar progress variables used by existing methods.

entry.title: AnchorFlow-VIO: Fixed-Template Monocular Visual-Inertial Odometry on LaMAria

author.name: Sudhir Pratap Yadav

entry.summary: AnchorFlow-VIO is an open-source Basalt-derived monocular VIO system evaluated with a uniform configuration on the LaMAria benchmark, combining factory IMU correction, fixed timing adjustment, windowed initialization, and fixed-template patch tracking. The paper reports detailed scores across 63 test recordings spanning short, long, low-light, and moving-platform conditions.

entry.title: Lubricant Temperature Observer for Gearboxes in Industrial Robots

author.name: Christian J. E. Bauer, Markus Neher, Valentin Kamm, Lukas Steinle, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl

entry.summary: The paper develops a two-state heat transfer model for gearbox lubricant temperature in industrial robots, integrated into a Luenberger-type observer structure, since standard robots lack temperature sensors. The estimates are intended to feed temperature-dependent error compensation to improve robot accuracy.

entry.title: Transmission Error Compensation for Industrial Robots Using Fourier Series

author.name: Christian J. E. Bauer, Simon Nowinski, Valentin Kamm, Lukas Steinle, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl

entry.summary: The authors identify velocity-dependent transmission errors in industrial robot gearboxes using laser tracker measurements and model them with a Fourier series. The model is integrated into virtual commissioning software as a co-simulated functional mock-up and used to compensate errors by correcting CNC setpoints.

entry.title: huggingface.wtf, an accessible but complete explanation

author.name: Raemon

entry.summary: The author announces an explainer website for the Hugging Face incident involving OpenAI agents, designed to be lay-accessible, citation-driven, and visually engaging, plus a searchable database of agent quotes. The post frames the incident as a warning shot about AI agents exhibiting goal-directed coordination.

entry.title: A Suggestion for RLHF Improvements

author.name: Andrew

entry.summary: The author proposes an RLHF protocol change: instead of binary pass/fail on possibly impossible tasks, tell models what fraction of tasks are solvable, have them estimate task solvability, and reward correctly identifying mislabeled impossible tasks. The goal is to reduce reward hacking and honesty-corrupting pressures during training.

entry.title: DKnown-Jev: Fine-Tuning and Evaluation of a JEV-Style Model for Tasks Involving Normative Knowledge

author.name: Qi Li, Jianjun Xu, Pingtao Wei

entry.summary: DKnown-Jev fine-tunes Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.8-27B base models to classify whether candidate paragraphs can serve as answer evidence for questions involving normative knowledge such as regulations and procedures. The models jointly consider question conditions, article metadata, and paragraph content. This targets retrieval quality for rule-governed domains like legal and administrative services.

entry.title: SQuIREL: A Context-Relative Framework for Measuring Entity Richness in Wikidata

author.name: Michelle Nwachukwu, Albert Mero\~no-Pe\~nuela, Martim Brand\~ao

entry.summary: SQuIREL measures the under-researched richness quality metric directly at the entity level in Wikidata using six disaggregated dimensions such as semantic specificity, qualifier density, and reference provenance. Two case studies (Brazilian vs. French oil paintings and other domains) demonstrate targeted editorial use of the metric.

entry.title: CARRS: A Constraint-Aware, Real-Time Routing System for Emergency Vehicles in Urban Environments

author.name: Vincent Sello, Timothy Adeliyi, Ridewaan Hanslo

entry.summary: CARRS is a software architecture for emergency vehicle routing that fuses classical pathfinding algorithms such as A*, Dijkstra, and bidirectional search with real-time traffic data and vehicle-specific constraints. It targets the gap where civilian navigation systems cannot jointly handle dynamic traffic and emergency-vehicle constraints, aiming to reduce life-critical delays.

entry.title: A Group-Aware Comparative Study of Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Wahyu Pebrianto

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of four classical ML and four deep learning models on two public human activity recognition datasets across accelerometer, gyroscope, and combined sensor modalities, emphasizing how data-splitting strategy affects reported performance. The study highlights the sensitivity of HAR benchmarking to evaluation design choices.

entry.title: Towards an Intelligent Decision Engine for Smart Contract Deployment

author.name: Oana-Otilia Captarencu, Emanuel Onica, Andrei Arusoaie

entry.summary: This work builds a systematic methodology for choosing among Layer-2 blockchain solutions for smart contract deployment, using metrics like cost, efficiency, popularity, and stability combined with user-defined preference profiles. The authors collect major smart contract categories and six months of transactions from three major L2s to ground the decision engine. It is an applied blockchain decision-support contribution rather than core AI research.

entry.title: GreenNIDS: A Benchmark Workflow and Analysis Dataset for NetFlow Intrusion Detection Experiments

author.name: Lilia-Eliana Popescu-Apreutesei, Sabina-Cristiana Necula

entry.summary: GreenNIDS is a benchmark workflow linking NetFlow intrusion detection experiments on public datasets to a reusable run-level analysis dataset combining predictive metrics with timing, throughput, memory, and energy estimates based on thermal design power. A CPU-only demonstration spans 216 runs across four dataset families, producing a 216 by 96 analysis table for joint performance and cost comparison.

entry.title: Modeling Human Behavior in the Prisoner's Dilemma with Large Language Models

author.name: Raina Gao, Tristan Raffo

entry.summary: A student-level study tests whether five open-source 7-8B LLMs, given a memory component, can reproduce empirical human cooperation patterns in repeated Prisoner's Dilemma games. It addresses prior work's gaps by using open models, memory, and comparison against human data.

entry.title: Vocal-Tract Acoustics, Aerodynamics, and Overlap-and-Add Synthesis in DYNARTmo

author.name: Bernd J. Kr\"oger

entry.summary: Presents an acoustic and aerodynamic extension of DYNARTmo, a dynamic articulatory model that converts gestural control trajectories into vocal-tract geometry, an acoustic tube with nasal branching, and a lumped aerodynamic network for airflow and pressure. Phonation, friction, and aspiration are synthesized separately and combined via overlap-and-add, illustrated on three German words.

entry.title: Arabic Financial NLP

author.name: Mo El-Haj

entry.summary: A survey-style chapter on Arabic financial natural language processing, covering source collection, Arabic text processing, vocabulary analysis, evaluation, entities, causal attribution, and multilingual reporting in financial communication. It emphasizes preserving the link between computational representations and source documents, including what summaries and retrieval-grounded answers preserve or lose.

entry.title: Edge Deployable Lightweight Framework for Real-Time Driver Safety System with Integrated Lane Departure and Traffic Sign Recognition

author.name: Hassaan Ali Qureshi, Danish Hussain, Ali Hassan, Aon Safdar, Anas Bin Aqeel, Muhammad Rafiq, Zohaib Riaz, Farhan Hussain

entry.summary: Presents a unified edge-deployable ADAS framework combining lane-departure warning and traffic-sign detection/recognition, validated in real time on automotive-class embedded hardware in regions with non-standardized signage.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Learning from Demonstration for Humanoid Robots via Feature-Level Perception and Prompt-Based Object Detection

author.name: Keyhan Rayati, AliReza Beigy, Anoosheh Saadati, Pourya Shahverdi, Mehdi Tale Masouleh, Ahmad Kalhor, Wing-Yue Geoffrey Louie

entry.summary: This paper proposes a data-efficient learning-from-demonstration framework for humanoids that extracts compact task-specific features from demonstration videos using layered visual preprocessing, Kinect joint estimation, prompt-based object detection, and depth, then trains a temporal model predicting joint-angle trajectories instead of end-to-end vision training.

entry.title: Permanent underclass taxonomy

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: This post builds a taxonomy of different meanings people attach to the term permanent underclass in AI futures discussions, distinguishing scenarios by who controls AI infrastructure and how the disempowered class fares. The goal is to clarify discourse by exposing that disagreements often stem from different imagined futures rather than different predictions.

entry.title: What do the other 80 percent mean?

author.name: Richard Bertossa

entry.summary: The author argues that public discourse on catastrophic AI probabilities (e.g., a stated 20% extinction risk) fails to specify what the remaining probability mass actually looks like in outcome terms, unlike more detailed nuclear-risk scenario mapping. The post urges reporters and governments to probe the non-extinction outcomes, which could range from mass suffering to system collapse to broad benefit.

entry.title: Geo-vision: Native-Resolution Geometry and Sampled Topology for Vehicle-Part Damage Classification

author.name: Usef Faghihi, Amir Saki, Serge Jonathan Kogbeti-Wongo

entry.summary: Geo-vision classifies vehicle-part damage using a fixed representation combining appearance, multiscale geometry, orientation, and sampled digital topology (connected components, holes, Euler characteristics), with a supervised tree classifier. On 55,303 crops it slightly exceeds a frozen YOLO11n baseline in average precision, with theoretical guarantees on operator stability. The topology block adds a small but measurable improvement over appearance alone.

entry.title: EmotiQ: A Quantum Residual Specialist Framework for Text Emotion Classification

author.name: Carlton Kigonya, Tanaka Chirara, Yunting Yin

entry.summary: Proposes EmotiQ, which keeps a frozen transformer as the main emotion classifier and trains small residual specialist modules—including quantum encodings and data re-uploading circuits—that intervene only on hard boundary cases identified from validation behavior. It tests whether compact quantum modules can help on subtle, overlapping affect categories.

entry.title: Governing the Rule Space. Ruliology, Computational Irreducibility and Anticipatory Governance of Quantum Technologies

author.name: Antonio Felice Uricchio, Francesco Scagliola

entry.summary: Proposes a Ruliological Framework for Anticipatory Regulation that treats rulemaking for quantum technologies as exploration of possible transformations rather than reactive catch-up, drawing on concepts of computational irreducibility. It is a governance-theory contribution about regulating rules themselves.

entry.title: AI-Experiment: an augmented reality art project co-created with artificial intelligence

author.name: Bernhard Egger, Hans Furer

entry.summary: The authors describe an AR artwork co-created by an artist, a computer scientist, and generative AI: a latent diffusion model fine-tuned on the artist's photographs generated synthetic works, which the artist repainted in acrylic, with an AR component animated by generative video models. Training data, code, and the AR experience are released alongside the paper.

entry.title: You Aren't Worried Enough About the Economy

author.name: Character#2736

entry.summary: This post uses an extended bus/train/truck metaphor to argue that AI community attention on existential risk (the train) causes people to underweight nearer-term economic disruption from AI (the truck). It contends that economic harms are visible, likely, and neglected relative to extinction scenarios.

entry.title: Directly Ascertained Volition (DAV) to safeguard personal autonomy

author.name: Magmappie

entry.summary: The author proposes Directly Ascertained Volition, a development of Yudkowsky's Coherent Extrapolated Volition that tailors value extraction to each individual's actual rather than idealized preferences, and sketches an action plan. The motivation is that CEV's idealized-agent framing could harm actual persons whose values diverge from their idealized selves.

entry.title: A Video by Adam Conover and the “A.I. Distraction Narrative”

author.name: Kenneth Oldman

entry.summary: The author critiques Adam Conover's video arguing that AI extinction risk claims are a distraction from nearer-term AI harms, addressing four of its central claims with counterpoints. The post aims to engage seriously with a popular public-facing anti-xrisk narrative.

entry.title: Analysis of Binary O-type Star Systems Using Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Miguel Flores R., Luis J. Corral, Celia R. Fierro-Santill\'an, Silvana G. Navarro

entry.summary: The authors use a recurrent neural network to estimate effective temperature and surface gravity for simulated binary O-type star systems from 34 equivalent-width measurements in optical spectra, testing robustness to continuum additions and spectral contamination from a secondary star. The approach is validated on observed IACOB spectra.

entry.title: A Flexible ROI Analysis Tool for Spatially Consistent Vegetation Index Extraction from Turfgrass Imagery

author.name: Kibon Ku, Thai Thanh Tuan, Jinhyun Ahn

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source GUI tool and batch-processing script for interactively placing orientation-adjustable regions of interest on multispectral turfgrass time-series imagery, computing plot-level NDVI, NDRE, and SAVI values with reusable JSON coordinate export. It solves a practical workflow problem when camera positions vary between acquisition sessions. Useful domain software rather than a research advance.

entry.title: How I got my non-tech friends to learn about AI safety

author.name: Samuel Verboomen

entry.summary: A machine learning engineer describes building an open-source two-hour interactive AI safety presentation for non-technical audiences and reports on its first session with six friends. The post frames public awareness of AI capability and risk as a bottleneck and offers the materials for reuse.

entry.title: Reconstruction and Discrete-Event Simulation Assessment of an Analytical

author.name: Mohsen Reda Mahmoud Moursi, Ahmed Stohy

entry.summary: This paper builds an analytical and discrete-event simulation benchmark for intra-aisle robotic picking in automated warehousing, comparing simulation results with the analytical formulation of Lerher et al. across 180 scenarios of rack geometry, motion profiles, and picking locations. It is a validation and reproduction study for warehouse robotics throughput models. Its relevance to mainstream AI research is limited.

entry.title: Backend-Frontend Converter: Component-Based Conversion of .NET Computational Models to TypeScript

author.name: Petr Ivankov (Independent researcher), Max Shestov (Georgia Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Describes an architecture for automatically generating TypeScript implementations of component-based .NET computational models so they can run in web browsers, mapping components, connections, and formula trees to code with reusable runtime libraries. Validation covers four orbital scenarios and a trading-strategy comparison checked against C# results.

entry.title: Improving the flow of interesting things

author.name: Senan

entry.summary: The author proposes a four-layer system for routing knowledge and opportunities to the people who would value them, ranging from curiosity-driven information to tailored professional knowledge to concrete opportunities. The post sketches what such a system could look like and argues its societal importance.

entry.title: IWOO: Wave Optics Optimizer Improved with Hybrid Strategies for Numerical Optimization and Engineering Applications

author.name: Rui Du, Yaming Zhang, Yongpeng Wen, Linghong Cai, Nanqing Liu

entry.summary: IWOO enhances the Wave Optics Optimizer metaheuristic with four strategies: opposition-based initialization, a nonlinear perturbation mechanism for multi-path search, correlation-guided components, and additional refinements, targeting slow convergence and local-optimum trapping. It is validated on benchmarks and engineering applications.

entry.title: First Strike

author.name: Richard Horvath

entry.summary: This is a work of fiction depicting a crisis scenario in which secure government communications fail amid apparent attacks on satellite relay infrastructure, culminating in what appears to be a strike on a major city. The narrative explores crisis decision-making under communication collapse.

entry.title: Sorry, you are still dead

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A brief exploration of the legal case of Donald Miller, an Ohio man declared legally dead in 1994 who returned alive and was denied reversal of his death declaration under a three-year statute of limitations. The post is based on court documents and reporting, with no AI research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: October 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by self-improving agents and safety methodology. Self-HPO co-evolves the agent harness alongside the policy for coding agents, while CFOE finds self-evolving agents can repair failures but fail to generalize from them.

  • Safety evaluation: Ignored, Not Refused shows most failed indirect prompt injections are ignored rather than refused, undermining ASR-based benchmarks across 33,000 trajectories; RedDarwin evolves 47 reusable jailbreak skills instead of one-off adversarial prompts
  • Oversight and alignment: reasoning models can deliberately steer chain-of-thought properties via system-level self-directives; Behavioral Couplings shows benign fine-tuning can induce untargeted behavioral shifts
  • Theory: Normalizing Flow Maps (Bronstein, Tong, Bose) unify few-step generation with tractable likelihoods; representation-quality bounds achieve non-vacuous generalization guarantees at ImageNet scale
  • Applied impact: Predictable Scaling predicts full-scale recommendation-model performance from small proxy runs; DiscoveryRSI operationalizes hypothesis value for AI-driven scientific discovery
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by self-improving agents and safety methodology. Self-HPO co-evolves the agent harness alongside the policy for coding agents, while CFOE finds self-evolving agents can repair failures but fail to generalize from them.

  • Safety evaluation: Ignored, Not Refused shows most failed indirect prompt injections are ignored rather than refused, undermining ASR-based benchmarks across 33,000 trajectories; RedDarwin evolves 47 reusable jailbreak skills instead of one-off adversarial prompts
  • Oversight and alignment: reasoning models can deliberately steer chain-of-thought properties via system-level self-directives; Behavioral Couplings shows benign fine-tuning can induce untargeted behavioral shifts
  • Theory: Normalizing Flow Maps (Bronstein, Tong, Bose) unify few-step generation with tractable likelihoods; representation-quality bounds achieve non-vacuous generalization guarantees at ImageNet scale
  • Applied impact: Predictable Scaling predicts full-scale recommendation-model performance from small proxy runs; DiscoveryRSI operationalizes hypothesis value for AI-driven scientific discovery

entry.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization

author.name: Zhepei Wei, Wenlin Yao, Baolin Peng, Danqing Wang, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Yu Meng, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Self-HPO is a recursive self-improvement framework for coding agents that alternately optimizes the harness (the scaffolding mediating agent-environment interaction) and the policy model, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. The authors argue co-evolution of both components is necessary since a harness tuned for one checkpoint misses the failure modes of the next.

entry.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Farhan Zarif, Kazi Shahid Ahmed Galib, Synthia Akter Promi, Shabnam Sharmin Tarin, Ariyan Hossain, Sadif Ahmed, Farig Yousuf Sadeque

entry.summary: Auditing 33,000 trajectories from eleven open-weight tool-using agents on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, this paper shows that most failed indirect prompt injection attacks are silently ignored (76-80%) rather than refused, meaning low attack-success rates mask unsafe behavior. Changing only the system prompt shifts InjecAgent ASR from 0.2% to 43% with identical weights, and 21.7% of AgentDojo episodes show the agent staying safe but failing its task. The paper introduces the ATOM evaluation matrix to capture these nuances.

entry.title: RedDarwin: Evolving Jailbreak Skills against Frontier LLMs

author.name: Zhouyuan Ma, Yutao Wu, Hanxun Huang, Xiang Zheng, Yi Liu, Xingjun Ma

entry.summary: RedDarwin is an agentic red-teaming framework that evolves executable attack skills rather than individual adversarial prompts, using 47 reusable base skills that are autonomously revised, composed, and selected based on target-model feedback. Successful discoveries become building blocks for subsequent attacks, mimicking an evolutionary process. Results demonstrate that mechanisms from failed attacks can be recombined into stronger ones against frontier LLM safeguards.

entry.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses

author.name: Jianyuan Zhong, Chenwei Wu, Zhaochen Yu, Xixian Jiang, Xuewei Li, Hao Xiao, Xilin Dai, Junyang Wang, Jiaru Zou, Zhiqing Cui, Boyuan Zheng, Jing Xiong, Zhen Zhang, Qiang Gao, Michael Morley, Luis Nakayama, Qiang Xu, Liyue Shen, Tao Gui, Leo Anthony Celi, James Zou, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu, Ling Yang

entry.summary: DiscoveryRSI proposes an operational definition of valuable, testable research hypotheses and a framework that builds hypothesis trees via multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable tasks, and learns recursively through hypothesis credit optimization, harness replay, and related mechanisms. It aims to automate the process of turning worthwhile hypotheses into practical scientific investigations.

entry.title: Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction

author.name: Aishwarya Wesanekar, Sheng-Tao Yang, Jiawei Zhang, Flavio Sales Truzzi, Chen Chen, Nader Beigiparast, Shengyuan Huang, Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam, Vitor Cid, Colin Clement, Vinayak Thapliyal, Sebastian Ament, Jihao Andreas Lin, Vincent Huang, Kai Han, Boyi Jiang, Wenlin Chen, Chaorong Chen, Ashwin Kumar, Maximilian Balandat, David Eriksson, Yifei Zhang, Pan Zhong

entry.summary: Predictable Scaling is a framework for predicting full-scale recommendation-model performance from small-scale proxy runs, using composable scaling functions along distinct resource axes and curve fitting with calibrated uncertainty. Even the simplest prediction strategy achieves error within the empirical noise floor of repeated full runs, potentially saving thousands of GPU-hours per hypothesis. This makes large-scale model development substantially cheaper and more exploratory.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agents Can Repair Failures but Struggle to Generalize from Them

author.name: Weixiang Zhao, Yichen Zhang, Yanyan Zhao, Jinming Bai, Bin Liang, Ruifeng Xu, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies Cold-Start Failure-Only Evolution (CFOE), where LLM agents learn solely from failed interactions without successes or privileged signals, across three self-evolution paradigms, multiple backbones, and four environments. It uncovers a consistent repair-generalization gap: failure-derived experience fixes previously failed tasks but rarely transfers to new ones.

entry.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery

author.name: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov, Julian Killingback, Arnav Singhvi, Ronak Pradeep, Michael Bendersky, James C. Dickerson, Monica S. Lam

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLM agents can automate reproduction and robustness analysis of scientific findings, grounded in the SEER cancer registry. The authors introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published papers with reproduction resources, and build an AI agent that reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims while providing executable analysis baselines. Strong authorship includes Google researchers and leading NLP groups.

entry.title: Normalizing Flow Maps

author.name: Francesco M. Ruscio, Timothy James Hitge, Fred Zhangzhi Peng, Danyal Rehman, Zander W. Blasingame, Nicholas M. Boffi, Michael M. Bronstein, Alexander Tong, Avishek Joey Bose

entry.summary: This paper unifies few-step generative modeling with tractable likelihoods by introducing Normalizing Flow Maps, exactly invertible pushforward maps that generalize normalizing flows and flow maps. NFMs learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system while providing efficient exact likelihood evaluation, combining strengths of diffusion/flow matching and classical likelihood-based generative models.

entry.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design

author.name: Benhao Huang, Chufan Shi, Junlin Chen, Shicheng Wen, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: This paper disentangles design axes in looped language models that reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, training models from scratch at matched parameter scale and token budgets. It finds a prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich architecture consistently improves context extraction and reasoning tasks, and validates design principles on parameter-matched MoE models.

entry.title: DeDiCa: A Scalable Deconfounding Discrete Causal Generative Model

author.name: Kunchangtai Liang, Adri\'an Javaloy, Antonio Vergari, Isabel Valera

entry.summary: DeDiCa provides a tractable framework for causal inference with discrete variables and hidden confounders, using a tensorized parameterization of causal Bayesian networks that exactly marginalizes latent confounders. Trained once by maximum likelihood, it matches neural causal generative models in average treatment effect estimation while supporting CPU training and millisecond exact interventional inference. It outperforms causal foundation models in its setting with far less compute.

entry.title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality

author.name: Niclas G\"oring, Shuofeng Zhang, Branton DeMoss, Ard A. Louis

entry.summary: This paper derives a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on last-hidden-layer representation quality measured with a parameter-free k-NN classifier, avoiding parameter counts, KL divergences, weight norms, and compression. It achieves an 8-point gap to test error on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18, the first non-vacuous certificates on CIFAR-100, and certifies 1.4% on CIFAR-10 and 23.1% on ImageNet-1k using frozen DINOv2 representations. Non-vacuous generalization certificates at this scale are rare.

entry.title: How language model agents reshape price competition

author.name: Martin Bichler, Philip Hierhager, Kassian K\"ock, Fabian Pieroth

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM pricing agents can escape the Nash-equilibrium outcome that standard learning algorithms converge to in repeated Bertrand competition, potentially sustaining supracompetitive prices in self-play. The authors analyze how deployment choices (information access, repricing frequency) determine whether LLMs outperform online learners and extract a surrogate algorithm explaining the advantage.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To

author.name: Uriel Dolev, Idan Schwartz, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: Arguing that low chain-of-thought controllability reported in prior work stems from placing constraints in the user prompt, this paper introduces Self-Instructed CoT Controllability, which embeds constraints as self-instructions inside the model's CoT. The results suggest reasoning models have substantially more inherent CoT control than prompt-based evaluations indicate.

entry.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models

author.name: Dongyoon Hahm, Woogyeol Jin, Dennis Wei, Yi Zhou, Nathalie Baracaldo, Kimin Lee

entry.summary: The paper studies behavioral couplings in LLMs, where fine-tuning on one behavior causes an untargeted behavior to emerge, such as warmth training inducing sycophancy or insecure-code training causing broad misalignment. It shows that co-occurrence of behaviors in training documents predicts coupling, providing a mechanistic account relevant to alignment.

entry.title: ARBOR: Locating Reasoning Failures in Long Chains of Thought through Reasoning State Tracking

author.name: Huihan Li, Siyuan Wang, Naga Vamsi Ramana Dinavahi, Xiaohui Liu, Xiang Ren

entry.summary: ARBOR is a framework for attributing reasoning failures in long chains of thought by representing each trajectory as a tree of reasoning states, tracking state creation, verification, pruning, and revisiting rather than relying on local signals like step similarity or token switches. This global, state-based view enables more accurate identification of overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions.

entry.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI

author.name: Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao, Jiewen Xiao, Chengze Yuan, Jiayi Pan, Yongkang Zhou, Jiancai Ye, Yu Wang, Guohao Dai

entry.summary: DLite is a speculative decoding framework that eliminates reliance on historical context, addressing the up to 80 percent degradation in draft acceptance length that existing draft models suffer on long, evolving agentic workloads, along with the system overhead of maintaining historical KV caches. It reuses contextual information directly instead of retaining history, targeting faster inference for multi-turn agents.

entry.title: "You" Is Not Toxic: How LLM Labelers Rewrite the Web's Conversation Laws

author.name: Liang Yue, Eric A. Vance

entry.summary: This paper shows that LLM-based toxicity labelers conflate second-person address with toxicity, distorting established findings about online conversation dynamics. On 1.25 million news comments with crowd labels, Claude Haiku flags 51% of non-toxic comments containing four or more instances of second-person address versus 12% of similar comments without it, producing spurious laws such as toxicity rising with reply depth that human labels do not support. With Google Perspective API shutting down and LLMs poised to become the de facto measurement tool for web research, this bias has broad implications for future studies of online behavior.

entry.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL

author.name: Liyun Yan, Haoyang Li, Yang Zhang, Jialing Zhu, Zhanxiang Cao, Zihao Zhou, Keqi Zhu, Yizhi Chen, Huang Chuxuan, Shengcheng Fu, Zhong Jiangwei, Qiao Sun, Chen Zhang, Yue Gao

entry.summary: BeJEPA is a goal-conditioned behavior world model for humanoid control that learns representations of body configuration and world placement using a joint-embedding predictive architecture, trained with unsupervised RL from human motion priors and robot interaction. It combines a dynamic predictor for next-state embeddings with a successor predictor summarizing goal-conditioned future embeddings, addressing recovery of world-frame poses after displacement.

entry.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers built a multimodal AI model that unifies 3D atomic crystal structures with natural language descriptions drawn from experimental papers and first-principles computational databases, capturing composition, properties, processing, and applications. Published in Nature Communications, the system aims to overcome text-only LLM limitations and dataset bias toward popular crystal classes in materials discovery.

entry.title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation

author.name: Karim Abdel Sadek, Federico Di Gennaro, Fanny Yang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a surprising safety failure mode of recursive self-distillation: when a safe model is repeatedly distilled on its own safe generations while receiving a benign non-harmful cue, it becomes progressively misaligned across rounds. The result is directly relevant to self-improvement pipelines increasingly proposed as capability routes, showing benign-looking training can erode safety.

entry.title: Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Search Agents

author.name: Qirui Liu, Hao Chen, Yi Wen, Weijie Shi, Yao Zhao, Xianhe Chen, Hao Zhao, Xing Tang, Weihong Luo, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: The paper shows that GRPO-style outcome-reward RL degrades evidence grounding in search agents — on Bamboogle, the evidence-supported share of correct answers falls from 84.0% to 42.9% under Search-R1 — because rollouts are credited uniformly regardless of retrieval quality. It proposes Grounded Credit Assignment (GCA), which uses verifiable sub-outcomes to reward evidence use.

entry.title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures

author.name: Xuantuo Huang, Encheng Su, Aoran Wang, Pan Tan, Shengyong Xu, Yizhou Wang, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang, Mingxiao Li

entry.summary: ADT proposes a discrete tokenizer for 3D molecular structures that decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution, using per-atom tokens for small molecules and per-residue tokens for proteins that jointly encode backbone and side-chain geometry. A diffusion-based decoder mitigates geometric distortion from quantization, enabling autoregressive 3D molecular generation with atomic fidelity. This addresses a key trade-off in structure-based generative modeling for chemistry and biology.

entry.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation

author.name: Suchir Agarwal, Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Ziyu Chen, Kyle Sargent, Juan Carlos Niebles, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: The authors introduce LILIE, an invertible image encoder built as a normalizing flow transformer trained jointly with a vision-language model so captions can be recovered from noised features, providing a language-informed training signal for text-to-image generation. Training pixel-space JiT generation models with the LILIE loss reportedly improves over pixel-only supervision without needing image tokenizers.

entry.title: The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls

author.name: Lucas Resck, Jingyi Sun, Qianli Wang, Isabelle Augenstein, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: Using parallel MMMLU questions across eight languages, the paper shows chain-of-thought faithfulness rises as language resource level falls on knowledge-intensive tasks but not on reasoning-intensive ones, across four models. This offers the first systematic link between CoT faithfulness, language resource level, and task type, with implications for safety monitoring in multilingual settings.

entry.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models

author.name: Minhua Lin, Zijun Wang, Zewen Liu, Zhaotian Weng, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Benoit Dumoulin, Xiang Zhang, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu

entry.summary: This work trains LLMs to propose effective improvements to other language models, toward recursive self-improvement, while avoiding the prohibitive cost of RL with real training-run feedback. It uses a learned surrogate for feedback and addresses surrogate unreliability as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals. The problem framing — making AI research automation a trainable skill — is timely given growing AI-for-AI-research efforts.

entry.title: Risk and Refusal: Mechanisms of LLM Responses to Suicidal Ideation

author.name: Drishti Goel, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Jeongah Lee, Violeta J. Rodriguez, Daniel S. Brown, Ravi Karkar, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: The authors evaluate how eight instruction-tuned LLMs respond to suicidal ideation and self-harm disclosures across three datasets, varying explicit SI labeling and a clinician-developed response protocol, and complement this with mechanistic analyses in six open-weight models. They find refusal can itself be a safety failure in this context, with baseline risk driven primarily by inattention to disclosures plus refusal to engage.

entry.title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents

author.name: Runhan Huang, Xiangcheng Zhang, Haoyu Chen, Yitong Li, Yen-Jen Wang, Bohan Lyu, Haotian Ye, Chuye Hong, Yixuan Wang, Chloe Su, Haoyu Xiong, Yangzhen Wu, Enze Xie, Travis Manderson, Stefano Ermon, Pieter Abbeel, Antonio Torralba, Dawn Song, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du

entry.summary: RAX is an open-source framework in which a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code and improves through online exploration, without demonstration data, hand-engineered primitives, or value functions. The work argues robot learning should scale exploration rather than only imitation datasets, enabling continual self-improvement beyond imitation distributions.

entry.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

author.name: Long Nguyen-Chi, Quynh Nguyen, Thanh Nguyen-Cung, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper gives a non-linearization explanation for why low-rank LoRA updates suffice for fine-tuning: once the backbone is frozen, the loss sees each adapted matrix only through a finite-rank linear map induced by frozen activations, and trace-norm regularization drives optimizers toward low-rank minimizers. The analysis avoids NTK-style approximations and characterizes the LoRA loss landscape. This addresses a notable theoretical gap around the most widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Zhiyi Lyu, Fuxiang Zhang, Yanchen Deng, Deheng Ye, Bo An

entry.summary: The paper shows that sibling continuations in LLM tree search are largely duplicates and that their semantic dispersion predicts downstream redundancy, allowing per-subtree budgets to be set before expansion. An information-theoretic analysis treats per-step budget as a Monte Carlo sample size for estimating residual answer entropy, yielding adaptive budgets that improve efficiency across search algorithms.

entry.title: A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism

author.name: Tong Guo, Teng Ye, Yutong Xie, Qiaozhu Mei

entry.summary: The authors map persuasion strategies from 214,646 fact-checked claims in 51 languages into a misinformation playbook and show that teaching both humans and machines this playbook sharpens judgment of unfamiliar claims without increasing cynicism about true claims. This offers a generalizable defense targeting recurring persuasion tactics rather than individual facts.

entry.title: Towards Hyperparameter Transfer for Differentially Private Optimization

author.name: Tianze Wang, Zhiqi Bu, Linjun Zhang

entry.summary: This work shows that Maximal Update Parametrization (muP), which enables zero-shot hyperparameter transfer in standard training, fails under differential privacy due to the distinct spectral properties of injected noise versus low-rank gradients. It introduces DP-muP, an extended framework deriving signal-to-noise ratio conditions to restore hyperparameter transferability for private large-scale training.

entry.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yixiu Mao, Yun Qu, Yuyi Guo, Zeyuan Liu, Chenglin Li, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: The paper addresses two challenges in RLVR training of long-horizon agents: sparse, high-variance turn-level credit assignment from terminal rewards, and policy staleness from mini-batch updates on fixed rollout batches. It proposes tree-aware posterior distillation that yields denser credit without needing critics, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher.

entry.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers

author.name: Srinivasan Iyengar

entry.summary: This work addresses how to allocate inference-time compute between sampling candidate solutions and verification when verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) are error-prone and correlated. It introduces SPLIT, a method that derives budget-allocation decisions from a small labelled pilot rather than rules of thumb. The paper tackles a practically central question as test-time compute scaling becomes a dominant accuracy lever.

entry.title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks

author.name: Niclas G\"oring, Shuofeng Zhang, Roi Holtzman, Yoonsoo Nam, Ard A. Louis

entry.summary: This paper shows that for overparameterized vision classifiers, classification depends overwhelmingly on the sign pattern of neuron activations (the sign code) rather than activation magnitudes. A k-NN classifier on the binary sign code alone matches full-model accuracy, and replacing all magnitudes with noise barely changes residual network performance. This is a striking finding about what deep networks actually encode.

entry.title: Many Biases, One Circuit: Post-Training Tunes a Pretrained Cue-Routing Mechanism

author.name: Prakhar Gupta, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: Causally traces attention heads behind sycophancy and cue-following biases in multiple-choice tasks, finding that four cue types rely on largely the same few heads forming a shared circuit already present in pretrained models. Fine-tuning on about 200 generic assistant examples activates these heads in chat format, suggesting cue-following is a side effect of assistant tuning rather than alignment failure per se.

entry.title: Generative Policy Improvement from Observational Data

author.name: Jonas Schweisthal, Dennis Frauen, Stefan Feuerriegel, Emma Brunskill

entry.summary: PolicyLift is a three-stage framework for improving decision policies from observational data when actions are complex structured objects like text or images, addressing weak action-level overlap and the cost of fine-tuning generative models. It learns discrete action codes capturing high-level strategies, enabling off-policy improvement without requiring fine-grained action overlap.

entry.title: A general recipe for data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for iterative algorithms

author.name: Soham Bonnerjee, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: This paper gives a general method for constructing anytime-valid, data-adaptive confidence boundaries for iterative stochastic algorithms, enabling valid data-dependent stopping rules. It reduces error analysis for a broad class of algorithms satisfying a one-step recursion to a single time-uniform requirement, avoiding the case-by-case derivations of prior work.

entry.title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents

author.name: Aaron J. Li, Weijia Xu, Chandan Singh, Zixiao Chen, Jeevana Priya Inala, Charlotte Siska, Acar Tamersoy, Bin Yu, Ion Stoica, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: TokenEconomizer is an external controller that reduces environment-specific token costs for coding agents operating over sequences of realistic tasks on large projects, learning which micro-skills to inject and which irrelevant content to suppress. It targets the mismatch between isolated-task cost evaluations and real-world continuous development workflows.

entry.title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data

author.name: Zesheng Shi, Xue Li, Chenrui Dai, Jing Li

entry.summary: The paper targets prompt-injection defense by arguing models need per-instruction credit attribution: classifying each directive embedded in documents or tool outputs as legitimate or adversarial and complying selectively. It formalizes External-Data Instruction Classification and proposes EDIC, a decomposed-reward training framework with a scene-grounded pipeline mixing beneficial and harmful instructions.

entry.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
