author.name: Yuhan Sun, Jiaxin Zhao, Yongdong Luo, Yibo Hu, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Weixun Wang, Weihang Pan, Zhongan Bi

entry.summary: MultiAgent-OPD jointly trains a hierarchical Leader-Searcher-Answerer multi-agent system end to end by combining on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning. A frozen Teacher, trained on answer correctness, scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision, solving the problem that final-answer feedback is too indirect for subagents. This addresses a core training bottleneck for multi-agent LLM systems.

entry.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding

author.name: Chiatzen Wang, Bill Xu, Haochen Gu, Hongyang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a length-inflation phenomenon in lossy (relaxed) speculative decoding: relaxed verification lengthens completions, mainly by extending reasoning traces, largely canceling out apparent gains in accepted tokens per round. Evaluating twelve target-drafter pairs, it shows that acceptance rate is a misleading speed proxy once the output distribution changes.

entry.title: SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kai Tang, Xing Zheng, Haobo Wang, Guangcheng Zhu, Shenzhi Yang, Zhengqing Zang, Yingfan Ma, Bowen Song, Weiqiang Wang

entry.summary: SimOPD proposes transferring teacher knowledge in on-policy distillation through response similarities rather than token probabilities or hidden-state matching. Using paired memory banks of student-generated responses, the teacher produces similarity distributions that the student matches in its own representation space, enabling cross-architecture transfer. This sidesteps the feature-space alignment problems of hidden-state matching.

entry.title: OmniXRef: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Multi-Reference Video Editing

author.name: Xiaoyan Cong, Tianyu Wang, Hyeonho Jeong, Zhifei Zhang, Yuqian Zhou, Yijun Li, Shaoteng Liu, Zhe Lin, Srinath Sridhar, Soo Ye Kim

entry.summary: OmniXRef enables video editing controlled by arbitrary combinations of text, image, and video references via a reference-bank interface and a novel R2-RoPE for generalizing to variable reference counts. A single-stream diffusion transformer jointly processes the source video and multimodal context from an MLLM in an interleaved format.

entry.title: PONDER: Learning to Generate in the Right Order

author.name: Julius Erbach, Dominik Narnhofer, Bernt Schiele, Jan Eric Lenssen, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: PONDER learns a policy that decides in which order a masked generative image model should fill in content and which already-filled positions to remask for regeneration, a mechanism called rethinking. By conditioning on partially generated samples and generator features, it improves on random or confidence-based generation ordering strategies.

entry.title: Video Diffusion Avatars: Taming Video Diffusion Models into Controllable 3D Avatars

author.name: Simon Giebenhain, Tobias Kirschstein, Liam Schoneveld, Davide Davoli, Zhe Chen, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: Introduces Video Diffusion Avatars, which fine-tunes video diffusion models to create photorealistic, multi-view consistent avatars from a single image with control over camera, facial expression, and upper-body pose. It replaces 3D morphable models with a learned expression space and identifies viewpoint bias in learned expression codes via a DISTRACT benchmark, proposing a mitigation.

entry.title: GRASP: Global-Local Representation Alignment and Spatial-Physical Grounding for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zeyuan Ren, Guanxun Zhao, Qi Li, Hao Wang, Wenlong Liao, Keyi Luo, Xijing Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Jingye Cui, Qibin Gu, Zhichen Wang, Yucheng Hu, Liqiao Xia, Nan Bu, Zhengde Ma, Rankun Li, Xue Yang, Wende Xie

entry.summary: GRASP addresses a mismatch in VLA models trained with joint-space losses by injecting physics-based priors during training for bimanual manipulation. It supervises differentiably computed tool center point poses and inter-arm relative poses through forward kinematics within a flow-matching loss, and aligns representations with hand-object interaction regions.

entry.title: LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing

author.name: Yuyan Zhou, Zeyuan Yang, Yuxuan Song, Zhicheng Cai, Hongli Yu, Weiying Ma, Hao Zhou, James Kwok

entry.summary: The paper theoretically compares masked and uniform diffusion language models, showing MDMs are easier to optimize but less computationally expressive while UDMs allow iterative revision but are harder to train. LED introduces a lookahead editing mechanism that brings iterative-revision expressivity to MDMs while retaining their simple transition schedule.

entry.title: Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference

author.name: Ivan Fomin, Ivan Koryabkin, Boris Sheludko

entry.summary: This work shows that relying on compilers like PyTorch Inductor to realize better operator orders for memory-efficient inference is unreliable, with predicted peak memory missed in a large fraction of tested CPU and GPU configurations and even altered numerical results on GPU. The authors instead profile generated programs, model memory exactly from statements, permute them, and prove realization of the modeled peak under stated conditions. This delivers certified, free-memory savings for real-time inference on small devices.

entry.title: Blitz: Accelerating the Diffusion Modules of AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2

author.name: Vinay Saji Mathew, Soundar Kumara, Gretta Kellogg, William K. M. Lai

entry.summary: Blitz is a few-step distillation framework that uses a geometric noise schedule and multistep consistency training to reduce the 200 denoising steps of diffusion-based structure prediction in AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 down to eight, with physical steering and candidate selection to reduce geometric defects. The evaluation is notable for comparing distilled models against teachers and other few-step methods under a common protocol. This could substantially cut the compute cost of protein structure prediction.

entry.title: Cross-Centaur: Modeling Individual Decision-Making Across Psychological Tasks with Language Models

author.name: Hikaru Asano, Hidezo Suganuma, Ryutaro Mori, Yukino Baba

entry.summary: The paper introduces Cross-Psych-101, a dataset of 591 participants with 261,551 valid decisions across 12 Bandit, Tradeoff, Structure, and Social tasks that links the same participants across tasks, enabling training of Cross-Centaur to predict an individual's actions on a target task from source-task behavior. It extends behavioral LLM modeling beyond population-level regularities to individual-level cross-task generalization.

entry.title: Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle

author.name: Manthan Gadhia, Alexander Hoyle, Karolina Sta\'nczak

entry.summary: Using the fully open OLMo 3 model family, this paper traces occupational gender bias across post-training stages by prompting each checkpoint with persona-based narrative generation in gender-given and gender-assumed settings. Findings complicate the assumption that post-training reduces bias: when gender is stated, post-training increases certain semantic gender disparities. The fully open pipeline enables unusually direct causal analysis of where bias enters.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Task-Redirection Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models via Closed-Loop Optimization

author.name: Chunjin Ye, Guanying Chen, Jianjie Huang, Jianhao Chen, Quanlin Chen, Hanjie Zhao, Haozhe Liang, Tieyun Qian, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: This paper shows that fixed-target supervision is a poor objective for visual attacks on VLA models because perturbations alter earlier actions and hence the physical states reached later, so matching fixed targets fails to sustain attacker-specified task progress. It introduces closed-loop optimization that re-derives supervision along the evolving attacked trajectory.

entry.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards

author.name: Ruida Wang, Gerald Friedland, Tong Zhang, Chris Kong

entry.summary: Lean4AgenticRL is claimed to be the first framework grounding multi-level process rewards in a unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL targeting software engineering and terminal-use tasks. It builds problem-specific workflow systems and provides toolcall-level, workflow-stage, and outcome rewards, addressing the low signal of pure outcome rewards in current large-scale agentic RL.

entry.title: The Ephemeral Cost of Switching Optimizers Across LLM Training Stages

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Davis Wertheimer, Ashutosh Sharma, Rameswar Panda, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: The authors systematically study optimizer mismatch between AdamW and Muon by pretraining 1.2B Llama-3 models from scratch while varying the proportion of updates with each optimizer, including continued pretraining and SFT interpolation. Surprisingly, they find little evidence of a meaningful mismatch penalty, with performance largely explained by independent optimizer effects and improving with more Muon updates.

entry.title: Large Diffusion Models Need More Than EMA

author.name: Chuyu Hu, Huanran Chen, Shitong Shao, Yinpeng Dong

entry.summary: This paper questions whether exponential moving average (EMA) is uniquely suited to training large diffusion models, developing theory showing that averaging constant-step trajectories has inherent optimization limitations while learning-rate decay and Schedule-Free optimization offer vanishing stationarity guarantees. Empirically, combining LR decay with EMA improves the standard baseline across most tested settings.

entry.title: Nearly Linear Private Learning of Littlestone Classes

author.name: Shay Moran, Chao Yan

entry.summary: For binary classification classes of Littlestone dimension d, the authors prove a nearly linear O(d log d) upper bound on private sample complexity, dramatically improving prior bounds of d^5, d^6, and doubly exponential order. The algorithmic core is a structural exponential mechanism using data-dependent candidate sets.

entry.title: Minimax-optimal Scaling Laws in Ridge Regression via Transfer Learning

author.name: Yalda Shabanzadeh, Diyuan Wu, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes transfer learning in high-dimensional ridge regression, deriving a deterministic equivalent for the risk of a two-step pretrain-then-finetune procedure under model and covariance shift. Specializing to shared regression functions and power-law spectra, it identifies minimax-optimal scaling laws. The results provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for questions about when pretraining genuinely improves downstream scaling.

entry.title: Tool Recommendation for Multi-Step Agents: Finding Every Tool a Task Needs

author.name: Sam Partee, River Stevens, Thierry Damiba, Valerie Fanelle

entry.summary: This paper presents Tool Recommendation, a deployed gateway system that gives language-model agents access to roughly 8,200 tools through a fixed three-tool interface, with calls executed under end-user credentials and checked against per-service consent. It addresses the problem that tool definitions exceed any model context window and that multi-step tasks fail when any needed tool is missing. Evaluation covers a public retrieval benchmark (ToolRet) and real billed session costs.

entry.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators

author.name: Vignesh Gopakumar, Zhuoyuan Wang, Ander Gray, Valentin Duruisseaux, Josh Williams, William Michael Edward Ellis, Nuno Nobre, Matthew Field, James Panayis, Alexander I. Blair, Andrew Davis, Stanislas Pamela, Robert Akers, Marc Peter Deisenroth, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: The authors introduce L-SplineFNO, which couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured engineering meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalized scatter preserves compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction, avoiding geometry-dependent solves.

entry.title: Anytime Contracts for AI Services

author.name: Boris Velasevic, Eden Saig, Eric Mazumdar

entry.summary: Extends contract theory to AI services consumed via subscriptions and pay-as-you-go APIs, where users can terminate at any time based on observed performance, a flexibility that breaks standard moral-hazard contracts designed for fixed-duration interactions. The authors propose anytime contract payment rules robust to strategic abuse by either providers (silent model routing) or users.

entry.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas

author.name: Haoming Li, Defu Cao, Xu Hu, Yingtao Luo, Yiyang Wang, Xianghe Xu, Jiashu He, Wanting Jiang, Yifan Zhang, Yunhan Zhao, Siyang Wu, Chen Yang, Haixin Wang, Zheyuan Deng, Taoran Li, Jingwen Zhang, Zhejian Peng, Shushu Liang, Yue Zhao, Bingzhe Li, Feng Chen, Yifan Wang, Jintao Huang, Yijun Wang, Yuexing Hao, Xiaomin Li

entry.summary: Introduces PersonaCUABench, which holds 74 computer-use tasks fixed across 11 domains while varying who asks, with 44 personas rewriting instructions and interacting with the agent through dialogue only. Across nine backbones and 3,330 runs, mean task completion falls 36 percent versus original requests, revealing failures in clarification and approval-seeking behavior.

entry.title: Information-Geometric Blind Spots of Conformal Test Martingales

author.name: Johan Hallberg Szabadv\'ary

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a fundamental limitation of conformal test martingales used for sequential exchangeability testing: distribution shifts that preserve the push-forward of the p-value under the conformity function are invisible to the test. The author introduces the A-equivalence class and the A-cryptic I-projection, providing a Pythagorean decomposition into detectable and cryptic shift components.

entry.title: Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs

author.name: Yang Ni

entry.summary: A review of modern causal discovery methods that exploit distributional properties beyond conditional independence, covering distributional asymmetries, conditional-moment restrictions, and environment/individual variation for DAGs and cyclic graphs. It organizes the field by separating identification sources from statistical estimators and their computational implementations, including settings with latent confounding and feedback.

entry.title: ProPerAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance

author.name: Shenglai Zeng, Xiao Yang, Tiffany Ma, Xinyuan Zhang, Nanshu Wang, Deren Lei, Kai Sun, Xilun Chen, Tammy Stark, Xianhui Zhu, Yuetai Li, Rulin Shao, Tianxin Wei, Rakesh Wanga, Anuj Kumar, Jiliang Tang, Wen-tau Yih, Xin Luna Dong

entry.summary: Introduces ProPerMem, a benchmark for memory-driven proactive assistance pairing egocentric video with year-long, distractor-rich user memories (~618K tokens average), human-verified trigger windows, and joint scoring of intervention content and timing. All evaluated baselines perform poorly (at most 15%), including frontier-style approaches, indicating the problem is far from solved.

entry.title: Watermarkability: Measuring and Improving Language-Model Compatibility with Logit-Based Watermarks

author.name: Zewei Deng, Mohamed Seif, Liyan Xie

entry.summary: The paper introduces watermarkability, a metric quantifying how compatible a model is with logit-based watermarks: the expected minimum KL divergence needed to push probability mass onto a watermark token set at a target level. Because a model's native probability mass on the watermark set varies, the same bias can yield very different adherence and perplexity costs, and the paper proposes ways to improve compatibility.

entry.title: Disentangling Language Effects on Tool Admission and Post-Retrieval Safety

author.name: Aditya Nawal, Manit Baser, Mohan Gurusamy

entry.summary: Independently varying request, retrieved-page, and response languages across ten models and seven languages, the paper identifies SLIP (Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing): non-English harmful requests raise mean tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, a pattern persisting in autonomous retrieval setups. Answering in the page language further increases harmfulness on matched tool calls.

entry.title: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection

author.name: Yujing Wang, Yulan He, Wenya Wang, Hanqi Yan

entry.summary: This paper introduces VERITAS, a method for detecting when chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning is unfaithful by verbalizing a model's internal computation rather than relying only on outputs or static activations. Using layer-wise Jacobian projection, it produces token-level traces showing how reasoning anchors emerge and move across layers, and a classifier trained on these structured features can identify how and where reasoning diverges from the stated rationale. The work matters because faithfulness of CoT is foundational to interpretability and safety, and this approach offers a dynamic, process-level view of when reasoning goes wrong during generation.

entry.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs

author.name: Xin Qiu, Junlong Tong, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: The paper builds the first training-and-evaluation suite (337K train, 44K eval samples) covering Perceive, Solve, and Reason capabilities for time series understanding in LLMs, and studies how and in what order time series should enter the model. Key findings: a dedicated encoder lets a 4B model surpass GPT-4o on every perception attribute, while textualizing the series costs 8-10 points in reasoning. It provides a systematic foundation for multimodal time series reasoning.

entry.title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data

author.name: Zihao Zhao, Avi Schwarzschild, Casey Meehan, Katherine Lee, Zhili Feng, Dylan Sam

entry.summary: This paper presents a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for the capability-privacy tradeoff when training language models on sensitive data, using synthetic medical records with canaries to probe leakage. It finds direct finetuning maximizes capability but leaks most, DP-SGD reduces leakage at high capability cost, and privacy-aware synthetic data generation offers a favorable middle ground.

entry.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces

author.name: Arun Josephraj Arokiaraj, Chenyi Huang, Sahan Bulathwela, Zekun Wu, Bin Wu

entry.summary: Annotrace is a tooling workbench for step-level annotation of LLM agent traces, ingesting six trace formats (including OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith, and Langfuse) and converting runs into ordered, nested step hierarchies. It supports a joint human-AI annotation workflow in which a frontier model proposes an initial codebook from sample traces and answers the same questions as the human annotator. This addresses a real gap, since existing observability platforms record traces but lack structured labeling.

entry.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models

author.name: Weiyang Jin, Jiwen Yu, Sihan Xu, Yuwei Niu, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: The authors introduce MIST, an evaluation framework that disentangles whether a video world model actually executed an instructed change from whether it retained memory of that change over time. Prior benchmarks collapse these into a single score, so low performance is easily misread as forgetting when the model may simply have failed to perform the edit at all. Applying MIST reveals that the bottleneck in current video world models is execution of the instructed change rather than memory retention.

entry.title: VISTA: A Multimodal Egocentric Benchmark for Goal-Oriented Perception and Assistance to Blind and Low-Vision Users

author.name: No\'e Mosca, Mohamed Rayan Barhdadi, Muhammad Hamza, Joshua Yeh, Suryodaya Bikram Shahi, Zhiyan Li, Selim-Antoine Lali, Weiyue Li, Hasan Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Gang Luo, Yue Zhang, Minghan Li, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces VISTA, a new multimodal egocentric benchmark designed to evaluate whether vision-based AI assistants can provide practical, goal-oriented help to blind and low-vision users. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on scene understanding and question answering with visual and textual inputs, VISTA incorporates signals common to egocentric wearables such as gaze, inertial measurements, and spatial trajectories, and evaluates goal-conditioned guidance across everyday tasks.

entry.title: From GAN-Based Models to GPT-5: A Taxonomy-Guided Study of Human Performance in Detecting Deepfake Face Images

author.name: Zhiqing Guo, Lixin Jia, Luning Sun, Xiaowei Chen, Guofeng Yu, Liejun Wang, Gaobo Yang, David Stillwell, Thorsten Holz, Shujun Li

entry.summary: This human-subjects study examines how well people detect deepfake face images as generative models evolved from GANs to diffusion models and multimodal LLMs. The authors propose the Deepfake Face Artifact Taxonomy (DFAT), build general-purpose and model-specific training materials from it, and run an online experiment with 524 participants. Findings on whether model-specific training beats general-purpose training have direct implications for media literacy and misinformation defense.

entry.title: Momentum: Persistent Dynamics for Video World Models

author.name: Nedko Savov, Stefan Maria Ailuro, Danda Pani Paudel, Yilun Du, Xi Wang, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: Proposes representing evolving scenes for video world models via synchronized eight-camera reference rigs connected in a graph, propagating generation between views so off-screen dynamic content (vehicles, pedestrians) remains persistent and physically consistent when it re-enters view. This addresses a key limitation of observation-history or point-cloud approaches used in world models.

entry.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models

author.name: Yuze He, Bin Tan, Zelin Gao, Yujun Shen, Yong-Jin Liu, Nan Xue, Yinghao Xu

entry.summary: Proposes PPMem, a video world model that maintains a persistent 3D memory using compact plane primitives, combining a planar prediction head and Depth Token Fusion module with a video diffusion transformer. Autoregressive chunks produce RGB video and planar geometry that merge into a persistent memory conditioning future generation, supporting large-scale exploration of generated environments.

entry.title: LAW: Unifying Language, Action, and World Modeling for Agentic Physical Intelligence

author.name: Jiajun Cao, Kai Tang, Bohua Zhang, Zezhong Qian, Ying Li, Xiaozhu Ju, Xiaobao Wei, Jiaming Liu, Yang Ding, Sixiang Chen, Yiding Sun, Siyuan Qian, Tinghao Wang, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Yi Zhang, Shilong Zou, Yong Dai, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: LAW is a closed-loop framework unifying a vision-language model and a world-action model for long-horizon manipulation, where the VLM plans remaining subtasks, estimates values of proposed actions, and assesses execution status asynchronously. The WAM uses a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts design integrating modality-specific and shared computation, closing the loop through semantic subtask progress.

entry.title: Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search-Free Planning in Latent Space

author.name: Guanchen Du, Jinhao Du, Yanpeng Sun, Shan Zhang, Na Zhao, Zechao Li

entry.summary: HIJP replaces costly test-time search in latent world models with a goal-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations. It jointly ensures goal representations encode action-relevant information and that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent dynamics, enabling search-free visual planning.

entry.title: Self-Building Labs

author.name: Jiaru Bai, Yuchi Zhao, Han Hao, Miroslav Bogdanovic, Yang Cao, Varinia Bernales, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: Introduces the self-building laboratory concept, in which an AI agent designs, configures, and operates a laboratory setup starting only from a high-level scientific goal, generating the lab layout, digital twin, robot skills, and workflows itself. This removes the bottleneck where self-driving labs can only run experiments they were manually engineered for. It points toward AI systems that flexibly scale scientific discovery infrastructure.

entry.title: Knowingly Wrong

author.name: Ariana Villegas

entry.summary: Research from LASR Labs Summer 2026 showing that fine-tuning a model on statements it knows to be false induces broad misalignment even when the data is benign, with misalignment reaching up to 60 percent on Betley and AISI alignment questions. The authors find a correlation between the belief-statement conflict and misalignment severity, that a single contradicted fact suffices, and that no screening method tested predicted which data would cause misalignment. This extends emergent misalignment findings toward mechanistically grounded safety screening.

entry.title: The Alignment Problem: Computer Science Meets Analytic Philosophy

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy

entry.summary: Vanessa Kosoy articulates her view of the technical AI alignment problem, synthesizing theoretical computer science and machine learning theory traditions with analytic philosophy and MIRI/LessWrong-derived perspectives. She introduces the notion of minimal viable safety, arguing that safe but useless solutions (e.g., homomorphically encrypted AI) or task-narrow solutions fail to address the real danger from actors who ignore safety guidelines.

entry.title: Local proxies for memory-efficient training

author.name: Wu S. Zihan, Brian A. Yuan, Guillaume Bellec

entry.summary: This paper trains a local proxy network per transformer block to predict the global network output via distillation, allowing gradients to propagate independently through proxies while approximating backpropagation gradients, thus avoiding storing all activations. The approach is exact for deep linear networks, and gradient error is bounded in non-linear residual models.

entry.title: RECREG: Recovery-based Shielding for Regular Safety Properties in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Alexander W. Goodall, Francesco Belardinelli

entry.summary: RecReg is a safe RL framework enforcing non-Markovian regular safety properties via recovery-based shielding, providing rigorous safety and convergence guarantees in the tabular setting with support for varying levels of a priori knowledge. It includes extensive experiments with the MASA-Safe-RL library and outlines an extension to deep RL. This formalizes safety enforcement beyond Markovian constraints, which is important for real-world RL deployment.

entry.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

author.name: Rida Assalouh, Tom Jacobs, Rebekka Burkholz, Yani Ioannou, Umut \c{S}im\c{s}ekli

entry.summary: BMuon modifies the Muon optimizer's spectral-norm geometry so that hidden channels across transformer blocks compete for a shared sparsity budget, enabling structured pruning after training without the sharp degradation that plain Muon-trained models suffer. The method is framed as normalized steepest descent under norms interpolating between Muon's geometry and structured sparse geometries. This connects optimizer design directly to model compressibility, an important practical concern.

entry.title: Is a Linear Probe Evidence of a Linear Representation?

author.name: Nadir Kutluozen, Christian Intern\`o, David Klindt

entry.summary: This paper argues that the standard linear-probe test for the linear representation hypothesis is too permissive: asymptotically any sufficiently rich feature map, even a random one, admits a linear readout. High probe accuracy is consistent with both a true linear world model and a kernel-machine geometry, and the distinction matters because orthogonal curved structure affects out-of-distribution behavior.

entry.title: Conformal Policy Selection: When to Deploy AI Decisions for Targeted Intervention

author.name: Junyu Cao, Ruijiang Gao, Maytal Saar-Tsechansky, Mingzhang Yin

entry.summary: Recasts targeted deployment of AI policies as a multiple-testing problem: for each unit, test whether the outcome under the AI policy would exceed a threshold, controlling false discovery rate via weighted conformal p-values and off-policy data. This gives per-unit rather than population-level guarantees, addressing adverse treatment effects for individuals in medicine, finance, and public services.

entry.title: NestedVLA: Learning to Consolidate and Generate Skills for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Guodong Du, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: NestedVLA proposes a post-hoc skill consolidation paradigm for vision-language-action models: instead of merging parameters, a nested hypernetwork conditioned on the target task generates task-adaptive action-expert parameters that compose with a frozen base VLA. This addresses interference in joint multi-task training and conflicts in model merging across heterogeneous robotic platforms.

entry.title: ECG-SDI: Single-lead Electrocardiogram Enables Continuous Sleep Depth Index Profiling and Scalable Digital Biomarkers for Sleep Health

author.name: Donglin Xie, Qingshuo Zhao, Songchi Zhou, Haoyu Wang, Jingyu Wang, Yuxi Zhou, Thomas Penzel, Shenda Hong

entry.summary: ECG-SDI is a two-stage deep learning framework that produces continuous sleep-depth profiles from a single-lead ECG, trained and validated on 12,392 overnight polysomnographic recordings with external validation in the Cleveland Family Study. It achieves stage correlations of 0.828-0.848 and REM AUROCs of 0.954-0.977, and derives digital biomarkers including disturbed sleep signatures.

entry.title: Causal Latent Workspaces for Looped Transformers

author.name: Ilia Zaznov

entry.summary: This architecture work augments looped (weight-reused) transformers with a causal latent workspace: each position writes gated vectors into prefix-specific latent slots and retrieves content-addressed summaries before successive applications of the shared block. It achieves the best mean held-out perplexity in most configurations across three byte-level corpora, three seeds, and two parameter budgets.

entry.title: Same Person, Different Advice: Auditing LLM Financial Advice with Repeated Risk-Tolerance Responses

author.name: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose, Aishwarya Bose, Sandip Nandi

entry.summary: Auditing seven LLMs from five providers on 800 real household profiles, the paper shows recommended stock allocations swing 10-16 percentage points on average when only the stated risk-tolerance answer changes, and 24-35 points when the answer changes, versus 0.6-4.2 for identical re-prompts, grounded in real data showing people's risk answers are themselves unstable over time. It quantifies how brittle and noise-sensitive one-turn financial advice from LLMs is.

entry.title: What LLMs Do in the Shadows: Reading Context Reliance from the Unembedding Dark Space

author.name: Alexandra Kuleshova, Andrey Volodichev, Daria Kotova, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: The authors show that context reliance in LLMs can be estimated by projecting hidden states onto the so-called dark space — directions that compose weakly with the unembedding matrix — avoiding costly methods like attention map materialization or auxiliary probes. This provides a cheap signal for detecting faithfulness hallucinations in high-stakes deployments. It also advances interpretability understanding of how context is processed internally.

entry.title: Recognizing Study Lineage Is Not Enough: Over-Crediting Same-Trial Evidence in LLM-Based Medical Verification

author.name: Mukand Krishna, Anoushka Harit, Chenghao Xiao, Zhongtian Sun

entry.summary: The authors show that LLM-based medical verification systems can correctly recognize that two publications share the same clinical trial lineage yet still over-credit duplicate evidence when aggregating, using 14 source-audited clinical families and five model conditions. The evaluation includes the existing GPT-5.5 model, which identifies independent updates reliably in direct recognition tasks but still double-counts same-trial reports in separate aggregation calls.

entry.title: Not Every Mention Is a Claim: Rethinking Object Hallucination Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hsin-Ling Hsu, Neeraja Kirtane, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: This work identifies a flaw in object hallucination evaluation: benchmarks and detectors treat every object mention in a caption as a claim the object is present, but mentions can be non-assertive, such as a bench described for people to sit on. Treating such mentions as hallucinations inflates measured error rates. The authors introduce NAME-Bench with 25,497 object mentions to separate non-assertive mentions from genuine hallucinations.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report

author.name: Pei Fu, Yike Liu, Yue Sun, Hanmo Wang, Xiuwen Xi, Ruoceng Zhang, Shaojie Zhang, Chao Jiang, Hang Li, Bingrui Liu, Zhenbo Luo, Heng Qu, Changjian Xu, Ming Xu, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal LLM, built on Qwen3.5, designed for fine-grained region understanding by predicting masks directly from its own visual representations. A lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features, visual latents, and language-model mask-token states so mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an extra segmentation encoder. The model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents, enabling grounded reasoning with visual latents.

entry.title: Look Before You Act: Bridging Active Perception and Vision-Language-Action Models via Observation-Aligned Data Adaptation

author.name: Jiawei Geng, Zhenyang Liu, Yuzheng Wu, Yongchong Gu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: The paper identifies first-frame distribution sensitivity in VLA policies: prepending camera repositioning to pi_0.5 in LIBERO drops success from 46.3% to 11.5%. ActiveAlign adapts VLA training to the states where active perception terminates, using closed-loop offline alignment so that active camera motion and manipulation policies compose reliably.

entry.title: Learning Robot Metareasoning: Adaptive Computation Budgets for Real-Time Control

author.name: Lorenzo Magnino, Antonio Marino, Michael Amir, Daigo Shishika, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: The paper recasts the deliberation-versus-reactivity trade-off in concurrent planning-and-execution as a learned metareasoning problem, dynamically choosing how long to commit to open-loop action chunks based on state. Because optimal computation time is highly state-dependent, offline static tuning either blinds systems during critical maneuvers or prevents finding globally effective solutions.

entry.title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents

author.name: Liqin Ye, Rongzhi Zhang, Xin Liu, Zheng Li, Yuan He, Qingyu Yin, Priyanka Nigam, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: AlphaBet is an agentic RL framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report calibrated probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates, scoring each dated forecast with proper scoring rules against eventual outcomes. It decomposes forecasting regret into evidence-acquisition and probability-calibration gaps, bringing evidence search inside the training loop.

entry.title: "Deep lifts": Neural networks can generalize even with the dumbest optimizer

author.name: Sunil Madhow, Yu-Xiang Wang

entry.summary: The authors study generalization of a parameter vector drawn uniformly at random from those interpolating a dataset in a wide ReLU architecture, showing that when the data is explainable by a smaller network, random interpolation achieves a generalization rate of roughly wdWD/n rather than being governed by the full VC dimension. The result stems from an inductive bias whereby small-network witnesses induce structure over the larger class.

entry.title: Process Reward Modeling with Reliability- and Conservatism-Aware Bayesian Belief

author.name: Zhongjian Qiao, Zhixiang Zhou, Jiafei Lyu, Peisong Wang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Siyang Gao, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper identifies two sources of PRM unreliability in test-time scaling — PRM uncertainty from imperfect training and policy uncertainty from distribution mismatch causing systematic reward overestimation — and proposes BayesianPRM, which treats process rewards as random variables and maintains a belief distribution to be reliability- and conservatism-aware.

entry.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents

author.name: BHVSP Subrahmanyam, Neeraj Choudhary

entry.summary: This paper studies per-decision memory sufficiency for LLM agents, selecting minimal subsets of memory records that preserve full-memory behavior even when evidence is redundant or jointly necessary. It introduces JointCoreBench with exact sufficient-set oracles across nine interaction families and JointCore, a group-deletion baseline that achieves 100% minimum-cost sufficient-set recovery on 6,912 conditions. The work highlights a blind spot in relevance-based retrieval for agent memory.

entry.title: Information Estimation with Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Alberto Foresti, Giulio Franzese, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: InfoSEDD introduces a discrete diffusion-based approach for estimating information-theoretic measures such as mutual information directly on discrete data, avoiding lossy continuous embeddings and the engineering burden of continuous neural estimators. It bridges information estimation and generative modeling, addressing high-dimensionality issues that plague existing methods. This is valuable for analyzing categorical real-world data across sciences.

entry.title: When Plans Change, Remember: Replanning-Guided Visual Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Victoria Smelova, Daniil Kazachkov, Georgiy Kazantsev, Iuliia Tsvetkova, Egor Cherepanov, Nikita Kachaev, Artem Latyshev, Aleksandr I. Panov, Alexey K. Kovalev

entry.summary: RePlanMem-VLA turns a VLA policy's own plan revisions into an online memory-write signal: large disagreement between temporally aligned predictions from consecutive action chunks indicates a task-relevant event worth storing as a keyframe. The authors compare 35 disagreement measures and enable long-horizon multi-stage tasks without retaining the full observation history.

entry.title: Optimal approximation of smooth functions by ReLU neural networks

author.name: Thomas Nagler

entry.summary: The paper closes the gap between existing ReLU network approximation constructions and the information-theoretic limit for Hoelder-smooth functions: networks with width O(N), depth O(L), and bounded parameters attain uniform error of order (N^2 L^2 log N)^(-s/D) for all s>0 and D>=1, with no width-depth tradeoff required. The construction uses new encoding/decoding via higher-order finite-difference bounds on local Taylor coefficients.

entry.title: Unit-level aggregation breaks coverage in causal foundation models

author.name: Gabe Schulman, Lucius E. J. Bynum, Yoav Wald

entry.summary: Shows that credible intervals from causal foundation models (CFMs), which look competitive at the unit level for treatment-effect estimation, become badly miscalibrated when averaged over groups: on ACIC 2016, temperature-calibrated 95 percent intervals from CausalPFN cover the true full-sample average only 20 percent of the time. This challenges the reliability of CFMs for group-level decision-making.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models Towards Counterfactual Invariance

author.name: Basar Demir, Emily Shen, Ksheeraj Sai Vepuri, Sourabh Kulkarni, Harihar Subramanyam, Ankit Jain, Nan Jiang, Chirag Nagpal

entry.summary: Shows that standard alignment recipes like RLHF increase disparities in response quality across demographic prompt variations even while improving overall performance, and proposes methods to enforce counterfactual invariance to causally irrelevant sensitive attributes without sacrificing utility. The work formalizes the tension between semantic coherence and insensitivity to group variables.

entry.title: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context

author.name: Manh Nguyen, Sunil Gupta, Hung Le

entry.summary: The authors develop a token-budget theory formalizing the trade-off in reasoning systems where reading (e.g., peers' debate messages or one's own drafts) and generating share a fixed context window. Accuracy is modeled as a function of remaining reasoning budget after reading, using a Condorcet jury model with correlated errors, with analyses for multi-agent debate and self-refinement.

entry.title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling

author.name: Yicheng Chen, Xiaoyun Yu, Hyejeong Song, Xintian Wang, Zihui Li, Zixi Xia, Junmin Chen, Peichen Zhong

entry.summary: The work introduces a machine-learning interatomic potential design that analytically separates long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges into a global electrostatics calculation plus strictly local derivatives, preserving distributed parallel computation. This enables accurate atomistic simulation of materials under electric fields at length scales beyond conventional first-principles methods.

entry.title: Mesoscopic learning dynamics of extensive-width neural networks

author.name: Shu Zhou, Jean Barbier, Sebastian Goldt

entry.summary: The paper develops a mesoscopic description of SGD learning in two-layer networks of extensive width trained on rich target functions, characterizing the distribution of overlaps between learned and target features rather than tracking a diverging number of individual overlaps. This yields a tractable order-parameter description in a regime where standard asymptotic tools fail.

entry.title: Prune the Leaky Neurons: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in Fine-Tuned LLMs via Joint-Embedding-Guided Pruning

author.name: Mohamed Shaaban, Mohamed Elmahallawy

entry.summary: JEPA-Prune is a post-hoc neuron pruning defense that removes privacy-leaking neurons from fine-tuned LLMs, guided by a reference model trained only on PII-free and masked views of the same records to distinguish identity-specific neurons from useful ones. It aims to balance private data removal with utility preservation, unlike sanitization or differential privacy.

entry.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference

author.name: Zhenxu Tian, Kebin Liu, Zhengwu Yang, Yi Su, Qingqing Dang, Yanlin Sha, Kaipeng Deng, Dianhai Yu, Yanjun Ma, Juntao Li, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Prism Attention addresses long-context inference KV-cache costs by refining layer-shared sparse attention indices: instead of static reuse at anchor layers, it uses a proposal-refinement mechanism that adapts shared indices to layer-specific attention evolution. Industry-authored (Baidu-affiliated by author list), it targets the gap between token-level sparse attention savings and index recomputation overhead.

entry.title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal

author.name: Ailiang Lin, Zhuoyun Li, Yusong Wang, Keyu Mao, Kotaro Funakoshi, Manabu Okumura

entry.summary: This is the first systematic study of multilingual training-free text embeddings from frozen LLMs, revealing that semantically equivalent sentences remain misaligned across languages due to language-conditioned embedding geometry. The proposed Paired-Residual Subspace Removal (PRSR) is a training-free inference-time intervention that removes language-specific variation to produce more language-invariant embeddings.

entry.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift

author.name: Aniruddha Chattopadhyay, Kanishka Halder, Partha Sarathi Roy

entry.summary: This paper identifies interface drift — post-deployment changes to tool descriptions, schemas, and tool lists — as a key reliability failure mode for function-calling agents. The proposed SchemaShield-Lite is a training-free repair layer combining schema validation, candidate-set retry, and one-shot constrained repair. On Qwen3.5-9B it substantially improves accuracy, lifting BFCL-200 from 0.580 to 0.805.

entry.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report

author.name: MOSI. AI

entry.summary: MOSS-Image is an open-weight text-to-image system combining a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer pretrained from scratch with bilingual long-form text rendering and precise layout control, plus an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement module that translates user requests into content and layout specifications. It targets the gap with closed-source systems on dense text and intricate layouts. The system demonstrates that open models can approach closed systems on information-dense generation.

entry.title: When Evidence Vanishes: Distilling Visual-Evidence Dependency in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qizhen Lan, Yiling Ma, Ruiqi Chen, Mengchen Fan, Xi Xiao, Lin Zhao, Liang He, Baocheng Geng, Pulin Che, Tianyang Wang, Xiaoqian Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces ECDD, a distillation method for medical VLMs that ensures answer support drops when the required visual evidence is removed, by pairing each image with an evidence-matched control and distilling the teacher's margin drop across the pair. This targets the failure mode where compact medical models answer correctly via question priors rather than the image.

entry.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Soumik Mukhopadhyay, Long Mai, Abhinav Shrivastava, Aniruddha Mahapatra

entry.summary: Revisits parameterization choices in pixel-space diffusion transformers and introduces MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between clean image (x0) and velocity (u) prediction across principal data directions during training. The work shows the preferred parameterization varies systematically with data representation, improving vanilla pixel diffusion.

entry.title: Generative AI Produces and Transmits Beauty Bias

author.name: AJ Alvero, Deepak Varuvel Dennison, Alexandra Crespin, Heeyon Kim, Alejandra Regla-Vargas, Avani Akerkar, Jasmine McNealy, Ren\'e Kizilcec

entry.summary: Audits 27 text-to-image generators released between 2022 and 2026 with neutral prompts, analyzing 51,300 generated faces against 160,196 real photographs with automated measures and 550 human raters. Nearly all generators produce faces judged significantly more attractive than real photographed faces, revealing how generative AI may amplify and transmit appearance bias tied to gender and race.

entry.title: SenseSwarm: Swarm Exploration via Neural Structure Estimation with Shared World-Anticipation for Rapid Mapping

author.name: Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Mingkai Liu, Hoiian Au, Qian Zhang, Jiayue Xie, Yule Cai, Bokui Chen, Xueqian Wang, Fei Qiao

entry.summary: SenseSwarm enables a decentralized robot swarm to anticipate the structure of unexplored building space ahead of physical coverage by running a lightweight 709K-parameter learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and feeding predictions into a stigmergic guidance field. The paper demonstrates that fine-tuning on multi-robot observations is essential, as single-robot predictors collapse on multi-front views. It includes a substantial benchmark of twelve real building floors up to 24,000 square meters and 1,620 simulations across nine coordination methods.

entry.title: ORD-WM: Learning Object-Centric Rigid Dynamics for 3D World Modeling in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yueyang Weng, Xiaopeng Zhang, Yuxi Ou, Yongjin Mu, Chengzhi Zhao, Yanjie Li

entry.summary: ORD-WM is a 3D world model that imposes explicit object-level rigid motion for manipulation, using a vector-neuron variational autoencoder supervised by signed distance fields to encode object point clouds into geometry-aware latents. An action-conditioned dynamics model then reduces shape drift and motion inconsistency in multi-step rollouts compared to image-based or dense 3D world models.

entry.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents

author.name: Hongcheng Gao, Alex Zhou, Jay Zhu, Zelin Zheng, Shijia Ge, Xiping Li, Di Wu, Yazhe Wang, Jianshu Zeng, Xuan Shangguan, Yongli Wang, Yexing Wan, Lingyu He, Zhiqi Jia, Sihang Wu, Xiao He

entry.summary: HexaShell gives a VLM-based coding agent control of a two-armed robot through a command-line interface with three calibrated RGB cameras, requiring the agent to read failure logs and write reusable tools from robot observations, including triangulation for object localization. The deliberately thin harness probes how far general coding agents go at physical manipulation and where they fail.

entry.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts

author.name: Antonia Bronars, Younghyo Park, Kushal Kedia, Pulkit Agrawal

entry.summary: Trains blind assembly policies that rely only on a short history of joint positions, velocities, and past actions, with no vision, force, torque, or tactile sensing, to perform millimeter-scale contact-rich assembly with unknown fixture and part poses. The paper asks whether the robot's own joint sensors suffice for precise insertion tasks. This challenges the assumption that dedicated tactile or force sensing is required for fine manipulation.

entry.title: The Alignment Problem: Computer Science Meets Analytic Philosophy

author.name: Vanessa Kosoy

entry.summary: Vanessa Kosoy lays out her view of the technical alignment problem, defining the task via the Prezent-Realizable and Minimal Viable Safety framings and arguing why narrow safe-AI solutions are insufficient given incentives and uncontrolled actors. The perspective merges theoretical CS, analytic philosophy, and MIRT/LessWrong traditions. It provides a structured conceptual foundation for alignment research priorities.

entry.title: Residual Stochastic Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Stephen Marcou, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Sonia Laguna, Moritz Vandenhirtz, Julia E. Vogt, Mateja Jamnik

entry.summary: Res-SCBM addresses concept incompleteness in concept-based models by adding a residual pathway that recovers task performance, while controlling the leakage and intervention-weakening problems such pathways introduce. The stochastic formulation aims to keep test-time concept interventions meaningful despite the unconstrained residual. This advances interpretable models that remain accurate in realistic, incomplete-concept settings.

entry.title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback

author.name: Kaixuan Ji, Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Cheng Qian, Heng Wang, Weizhi Zhang, Jielin Qiu, Liangwei Yang, Quanquan Gu, Silvio Savarese, Shelby Heinecke, Huan Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies fact-level memory gating for language-model agents, proposing a retrieval-based labeling strategy where facts are labeled by whether they are later retrieved into responses. Memory gating is formulated as contextual apple tasting with delayed one-sided feedback, solved by Warm-Start UCB combining offline learning with online per-user adaptation, with high-probability regret guarantees. It addresses a real limitation of user-agnostic memory policies in long-term agent personalization.

entry.title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Oscar Kemme, Janek Haberer, Ali Hojjat, Olaf Landsiedel

entry.summary: HydraLLM is an elastic MQA-based architecture in which the number of active attention heads determines effective widths across the network, forming nested subnetworks from a single parameter set. A static-to-elastic conversion pipeline with importance-driven weight reordering converts pre-trained checkpoints into elastic models deployable across data-center and edge hardware.

entry.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Shaoang Li, Yanhang Shi, Yufei Li, Mingfu Liang, Frank Shyu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon, Xi Liu, Jian Li

entry.summary: ReDiST is a distillation framework that constructs reasoning traces conditioned on the target student model: it revises the student's own answer-correct drafts against evidence and repairs failed drafts using the verified answer, then screens candidates with a frozen student-matched reader. This improves learning beyond answer-only supervision by tailoring trace accessibility to the learner.

entry.title: On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs

author.name: Jaewon Sok, Jewon Yeom, Seonghyeon Park, Jeongjae Park, Hwiyeong Lee, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: The authors show that many closed-book factual errors in LLMs are first-token recall failures: the model commits to a wrong first token, but given the correct one it often completes and recognizes the right answer. Their First-Token Cueing probe prefills the response with the gold first token, with model uncertainty peaking at the first answer token where it already predicts correctness, validated across 16 open models. This reframes some 'missing knowledge' errors as retrieval failures.

entry.title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis

author.name: Giovanni Vaccarino, Emanuele La Malfa, Dehai Min, Hanrong Zhang, Pier Luca Lanzi, Lu Cheng, Michael J. Wooldridge, Philip S. Yu, Sara Bernardini

entry.summary: DRAGO is a repair framework for LLM-generated formal specifications that replaces ungrounded LLM critique with deterministic, formalism-based diagnosis; the paper shows purely LLM-based diagnosis often misses semantic errors and causes regressions in 11.8 percent of initially correct specifications. The approach targets specifications that run but encode incorrect constraints, domains, or goals.

entry.title: AWAM: Active Trajectory-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiawei Geng, Zhenyang Liu, Yuzheng Wu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: AWAM introduces a virtual active-perception paradigm in which the robot predicts task-relevant camera motion and queries a geometry-conditioned world model to imagine observations along a planned trajectory before acting. The imagined views yield a reusable spatial prior that improves manipulation robustness under clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints.

entry.title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Gunmay Jhingran

entry.summary: The paper challenges the binary trust assumption in absorbing discrete diffusion, where corrupted context is copied as ground truth and errors propagate into generated spans. It proposes combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels with region-dependent rates, plus an inference-time sampler that re-injects noise into suspicious context with annealed intensity. Only an 8,000-step finetune of a pretrained model is needed, making the approach practical.

entry.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Parv Kapoor, Teresa Fortes, Claudia Mamede, Rui Abreu, Jonathan Aldrich, Eunsuk Kang

entry.summary: This safety paper introduces bounded continuation analysis (BCA), which models autoregressive generation as a stochastic process over token prefixes and computes the finite-horizon probability that generation reaches harmful continuations. It demonstrates that a sampled refusal can coexist with substantial probability mass on harmful generation paths, showing attack success rate alone understates safety risks.

entry.title: GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yushu Wang, Renkai Yang, Jingcao Xu, Zili Geng, Haihong Tang, Yaohui Jin, Hao He

entry.summary: GR-OPD decouples feedback computation from credit assignment in on-policy distillation by aggregating token-level teacher feedback into calibrated sequence-level credit, with a theoretical proof that broadcasting summed feedback yields an unbiased gradient estimate of the sequence-level reverse-KL objective. It also discounts later feedback that becomes less reliable under drift.

entry.title: Contracting with an Agent under Model Mismatch

author.name: Elif Y{\i}lmaz, Jakub T{\l}uczek, Victor Villin, Christos Dimitrakakis

entry.summary: This paper studies principal-agent problems in a Markov decision process setting where the agent acts under a misspecified model of the environment, leading to systematically suboptimal behavior. The principal, who knows the true transition model, repeatedly designs contracts to align the agent's incentives. This extends contract theory into RL, with implications for AI alignment and mechanism design under model error.

entry.title: Out of Support, Not Out of Reach: In-Context Learning with Unsupported Instructions and Composed Tasks

author.name: Xuhan Tong, Yuchen Zeng, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper builds a theoretical framework for in-context learning when instructions or target tasks fall outside the pretraining distribution. It separates two forms of distribution shift, showing that demonstrations can identify pretraining-supported tasks and reduce template sensitivity, while also characterizing when ICL can generalize to unsupported instructions under a fixed model. This matters because it extends ICL theory beyond the idealized case where the latent task is already represented in pretraining.

entry.title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems

author.name: Nithin Chalapathi, Theo Sternlieb, Ethan Han, Sonya M. Hanson, Pilar Cossio, Aditi S. Krishnapriyan, Ritwik Gupta

entry.summary: The authors study learning a common representation across cryo-EM inverse problems, pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction, which are typically solved independently despite sharing protein structure and image formation. They apply self-distillation with spatially localized differences to capture biologically meaningful conformational variability.

entry.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models

author.name: Jingkai Guo, Ziyi Zhao, Chaitali Chakrabarti, Deliang Fan

entry.summary: Proposes Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which performs LLM unlearning by updating a single selected transformer layer with a confidence-weighted forgetting-plus-retain regularization rather than fine-tuning the whole model. A reduced-compute variant called Brief is also introduced, targeting the known trade-off where suppressing target information damages retained knowledge.

entry.title: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD

author.name: Yibo Zhou, Yirong Xiang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the difficulty of cleanly evaluating relational out-of-distribution errors in vision-language models, where many existing tests can be solved via shortcuts without checking image-caption pairing. It proposes counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same images and captions while changing only the pairing, causing component shortcuts to cancel exactly.

entry.title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding

author.name: Amit Ranjan Trivedi, Sruthikesh Surineni, Kyong Ho Lee, Mohit Mittal, Steven Li, Rex Hill

entry.summary: The paper studies sparse collaborative decoding, where a small draft model generates most tokens and a large target model is invoked only for short corrective segments, with the key question being when to call the target. The authors show local uncertainty features are nearly useless failure predictors (AUC 0.50-0.53) while aggregate trajectory-shape features reach AUC 0.86 with a lightweight logistic predictor.

entry.title: Learning User Representations to Improve Simulation Fidelity

author.name: Shuhaib Mehri, Philippe Laban, Michel Galley, Dilek T\"ur, Jennifer Neville, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Identifies user representations as a bottleneck in user simulators used for training and evaluating AI assistants, proposing a conversation reconstruction task to evaluate and optimize these representations. The authors include well-known Meta and Microsoft researchers (Laban, Galley, Tur, Gao, Neville).

entry.title: ReLaDrift: Recurrent Language Generation via Drifting for Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yuki Otsuka, Daisuke Oba, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: ReLaDrift extends one-step Drifting Models — which generate samples in a single function evaluation — to support iterative refinement by reusing a shared model to draft from noise and refine in a continuous latent space. Training applies the drifting loss only at the final round with stopped gradients through preceding rounds, enabling a compute-versus-quality trade-off at test time. This bridges fast parallel generation and test-time scaling.

entry.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence) makes LLM agents pre-commit to evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified, with a separate program recording check results and refusing conclusions the evidence does not support. It targets record-verification tasks, such as triaging vulnerability reports, where agents otherwise accept conclusions after failed checks or settle for weaker ones.

entry.title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval

author.name: Haoming Li, Dingyi Kang, Xu Hu, Jinxin Yang, Zhu Xu, Chenru Wang, Yi Ge, Miao Yin, Guanpeng Li, Feng Chen, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: SAFE-Mem is a fine-grained governance framework for LLM agent persistent memory that annotates atomic claims with authority metadata so untrusted external statements cannot be treated as authorized preferences, policies, or permissions. Its governance-aware retrieval improves security while preserving legitimate memory use, unlike content filtering or coarse provenance tracking.

entry.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning

author.name: Yizhe Zhang, Xujia Wang, Songqi Tang, Xujie Tang, Leo Jiahao Jiang, Jiacheng Wang, Bowen Qu, JinBo Li, Qin Wang, Ji Qi, Lei Hou, Bin Xu, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: Event-STVG redefines spatio-temporal video grounding around event-level reasoning rather than instance-specific target localization, unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding. The authors contribute a large-scale benchmark with 4,016 annotated event occurrences designed to stress multimodal LLMs. This connects a classic vision-language task to modern long-form video understanding.

entry.title: EgoP$^{2}$C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video

author.name: Chaoyu Li, Arka Sadhu, Yuliang Li, Hyo Jin Kim, Yuning Chai, Pooyan Fazli

entry.summary: EgoP2C internalizes an agentic plan-perceive-compose process into a single vision-language model for spatial reasoning over egocentric video, rather than relying on external vision and geometry tools. Using Dual-LoRA teacher experts and subsequent fine-tuning, it addresses the failure mode where agentic systems inherit errors from imperfect external tool outputs.

entry.title: Query-adaptive Recurrent Tokenization

author.name: Bavesh Balaji, Pranav Gopinath, Pouya Sadeghi, Sirisha Rambhatla

entry.summary: The paper presents QART, a backbone-agnostic tokenization module that makes visual representations query-steerable and token-budget adaptive in vision-language models. Instead of allocating a fixed visual token budget to every image regardless of the query, QART progressively allocates tokens until query-relevant visual features are represented with sufficient fidelity, starting from frozen encoder features.

entry.title: Agentic Image Generation in the Wild

author.name: Yifan Li, Bowen Qin, Kun Zhou, Haochen Zhao, Zikang Liu, Zheng Li, Minsheng Hao, Yuhao Cheng, Haosheng Zou, Jeff Chen, Wayne Xin Zhao

entry.summary: This work defines Image Generation in the Wild, where agentic generators must retrieve web references to create images of entities that appeared only days ago, with limited visual evidence and easily confused search results. The authors build an automated pipeline that synthesizes hard but natural prompts from recent headlines and construct Savanna, a 500-prompt benchmark. The benchmark exposes real limitations of agentic image generation systems on recent, ambiguous entities.

entry.title: ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Ge Ya Luo, Daniel Severo, Brian Karrer, Christopher Pal, Adriana Romero-Soriano, Michal Drozdzal

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for 3D-consistent novel view synthesis that jointly generates a target view and its depth map, conditioning the diffusion pipeline on the source image, source depth, and target camera rays. A per-pixel depth consistency constraint verifies and enforces 3D alignment even under drastic viewpoint changes.

entry.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Tengda Guo (Tsinghua University), Jiawang Hu (StepFun), Yifei Tao (Nanyang Technological University), Yin Wang (StepFun), Haotian Hu (Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology Co., Ltd), Fanyi Wang (Honor), Liujuan Tang (StepFun)

entry.summary: Proposes ECHOES for long-horizon GUI agents, using a Compression-Think-Action format to recursively maintain a compressed textual history state while reasoning, avoiding the cost of retaining screenshots. A teacher with privileged multi-image inputs provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student rollouts, guided by a Perception-Memory Fidelity gap metric.

entry.title: RTISSLAM-3D: Full 6-DoF SLAM With an In-Air 3D Imaging Sonar

author.name: Jan Steckel, Vincent Katter, Wouter Jansen

entry.summary: This paper introduces RTISSLAM-3D, the first SLAM system to achieve full 6-DoF trajectory estimation using an in-air 3D imaging sonar on a wheeled robot, inspired by echolocating bats. Prior sonar SLAM systems were limited to planar 2D trajectories, discarding elevation information that matters on rough terrain. The system combines a CFAR detector on the sphere, 3D acoustic odometry with beam modeling, IMU and wheel encoders, and polar submap-based place recognition.

entry.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Lingyi Hong, Weiren Cai, Jiayu Chen, Xinyu Zhou, Bailin He, Yunfei Guo, Qiao Sun, Boyu Ma, Jianfei Yang, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: SimpleVLN asks whether native multimodal LLMs can handle vision-and-language navigation before adding task-specific architectures, and proposes an architecture-preserving framework with single-turn decision inputs and fixed-budget global-local memory for navigation history. The work systematically studies navigation formulation, data construction, and optimization to make vanilla MLLMs competitive at VLN.

entry.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Dominic Maggio, Lorenzo Shaikewitz, Aryan Naveen, Kris Hauser, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Building on FOUND-IT, the paper integrates real-time open-set 3D scene graphs generated from a single uncalibrated camera into a full mobile manipulation autonomy pipeline from MIT's Carlone group. It identifies the systems-level advancements needed to make foundation-model spatial memory usable and evaluates the effectiveness and limitations of this 3D memory in deployment.

entry.title: EmbodiedMidtrain: Bridging the Gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models via Mid-training

author.name: Yiyang Du, Zhanqiu Guo, Haochen Zhang, Annabella Macaluso, Xin Ye, Liu Ren, Yonatan Bisk, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes a mid-training stage that adapts off-the-shelf VLMs to the embodied domain before VLA fine-tuning, using a learnable proximity estimator to select VLA-aligned data from large VLM corpora. The authors first characterize the distribution gap between VLM and VLA data. This targets a known weakness: most VLAs inherit visual and linguistic capabilities from VLMs poorly matched to embodied tasks.

entry.title: Deconfusing Corrigibility

author.name: berns

entry.summary: This Alignment Forum post argues that existing definitions of corrigibility are flawed, being either over-epistemicized (framing corrigibility as goal uncertainty, which leads to fully updated deference problems) or evaluatively thickened (making corrigibility depend on the AI adopting human norms as goals). The author, working with Abram Demski, proposes a new formulation consistent with the original 2015 desiderata that admits formal safety guarantees.

entry.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction

author.name: Eliezer Shlomi, Eliron Rahimi, Avi Mendelson, Chaim Baskin

entry.summary: SPOT adapts lossless speculative decoding to diffusion language models by learning to predict the commit order of positions, the missing piece since DLMs must choose both what to generate and where. The key observation is that a model's previous-pass predictions already give the right token at 92-100 percent of positions, and a small 0.62M-parameter predictor is enough to learn the order.

entry.title: Flash RNN-T: Memory-Efficient Joint Network and Transducer Loss Computation

author.name: Mahmoud Ashraf

entry.summary: Flash RNN-T provides a memory-efficient joint network and transducer loss implementation using specialized kernels with optional tiled recomputation, forming the measured throughput-memory frontier for streaming speech recognition training. On H100, it achieves 24-39% higher throughput with 26-56% less memory than the fastest baseline, with tiling reducing memory up to ninefold. This is a direct systems-level speedup for a widely used ASR architecture.

entry.title: JAXtari: High-Throughput and Easy-to-Modify Arcade Learning Environment

author.name: Quentin Delfosse, Raban Emunds, Paul Seitz, Sebastian Wette, Jannis Bl\"uml, Daniel Kirn, Dominik Mandok, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: JAXtari is an open-source, GPU-parallelized reimplementation of the Arcade Learning Environment (Atari 2600) in JAX, addressing the CPU emulation bottleneck in modern RL pipelines. It natively supports object extraction and environment modification, enabling studies of whether agents learn causal models or brittle visual heuristics. PPO agents can reportedly train at substantially higher throughput than with the original ALE.

entry.title: Where's the Indirect Evidence? Investigating Grammatical Generalization with Influence Functions

author.name: William Dai, Zhenghao Herbert Zhou, Maya Viswanathan, Robert Frank

entry.summary: Uses influence functions to identify, bottom-up, which training sentences drive grammatical generalization across 15 BLiMP phenomena, filtering out direct evidence with hand-built rules and ranking the 60,000 most influential remaining sentences as indirect evidence. This goes beyond prior work that merely inferred indirect evidence exists or tested specific hypotheses about its nature.

entry.title: Beyond Success Rate: Interventional Evaluation of Memory in Vision-Language-Action Systems

author.name: Keyuan Luo, Yi Xie, Wanyun Ling, Yuanzhe Li, Ziyue Li, Zhuoqi Zeng

entry.summary: The authors propose IMEP, an interventional memory evaluation protocol for VLA systems, asking whether robot memory actually causally contributes to task success via target-fact substitutions, fact-preserving replacements, and minimal perturbations at the retrieval interface. This goes beyond success-rate ablations, which confound information and computation changes.

entry.title: ConvexLLM: Scaling Convex-Hull Speech Interfaces to General-Purpose Audio Intelligence

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Shujie Liu, Yuxuan Hu, Yuxiang Wang, Yingda Shen, Jinyu Li, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: ConvexLLM is a general-purpose speech and audio language model whose C-Gate interface represents audio as continuous convex combinations of frozen text embeddings, grounding acoustic features in the decoder's existing text embedding space. This better preserves pretrained text capabilities compared to MLP or Q-Former interfaces. It reports the highest known eleven-task VoiceBench aggregate of 75.36.

entry.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Kentaro Ozeki, Risako Ando, Takanobu Morishita, Hirohiko Abe, Koji Mineshima, Mitsuhiro Okada

entry.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena to evaluate whether large reasoning models align with everyday reasoning patterns that depart from textbook formal logic. They find reasoning models often show degraded performance when everyday reasoning deviates from formal patterns, and compare against non-reasoning models under controlled prompting.

entry.title: Too Emotional to Be Fake? Intra-Utterance Emotion Shifts Expose Failure Modes in Speech Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Jingyi Chen, Surya Koppisetti

entry.summary: The paper introduces EmoShift, a benchmark with 7,240 bona fide and 9,720 synthetic utterances from four expressive TTS systems, comparing emotion-stable and emotion-changing speech to probe speech deepfake detectors. It finds intra-utterance emotion shifts make synthetic speech appear more genuine (raising spoof miss rates by up to 25.3 percentage points) and emotion-changing real speech raises false alarms by up to 24.4 points.

entry.title: JAVIS: Joint Audio-Visual Interaction and Streaming for Real-Time Conversational Agents

author.name: Junseok Ahn, Jaehyun Park, Jeongsoo Choi, Joon Son Chung, Ji-Hoon Kim

entry.summary: JAVIS is an end-to-end streaming framework for real-time audio-visual conversational agents in which voice and face generation derive from a single shared representation produced by a Joint Refined Head atop a shared LLM. Dedicated streaming branches for speech and face generation avoid intermediate bottlenecks, enabling real-time multimodal generation. This extends conversational systems beyond text and speech to include visual feedback.

entry.title: Three LiDARs, Twenty-Five Datasets: Cross-Source Generalization in Tree-Species Recognition

author.name: Jae Joong Lee, Bedrich Benes

entry.summary: The authors build a multi-resolution, multi-view ConvNeXtV2 model that improves the FOR-species20K LiDAR tree-species classification hidden-test accuracy from 79.5% to 85.0%, ranking first at submission. They then critically examine what the score measures, showing the species-balanced hidden test masks long-tailed behavior and that the official random split leaks source identity — a logistic probe recovers source from out-of-fold model probabilities. This exposes dataset-leakage issues in the benchmark.

entry.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

author.name: Lieqi Liu, Rui gao, Jia-Chen Gu, Wenbo Hu, Zhaobin Mo, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar, Wei Wang, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: STRIDE is an object-centric benchmark for evaluating VLM spatiotemporal reasoning in long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios, spanning six task families including spatial perception, temporal memory, and temporal extrapolation. It addresses the gap where existing benchmarks test edge cases with basic perception questions or simple temporal scenarios.

entry.title: Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations

author.name: Huanqian Wang, Boshi Tang, Botong Xiao, Jie Zhang, Yang Yue, Danhua Tao, Shiji Song, Gao Huang

entry.summary: This work improves task progress estimation for RL reward shaping by rejecting the assumption that all actions in a demonstration contribute to success, which fails in high-precision manipulation where subtle errors cause failure. It injects a global prior about task evaluation criteria, likely leveraging foundation models, to distinguish meaningful progress from human mistakes in imperfect demonstrations.

entry.title: Where Latents Belong and How They Flow: Joint Identification of Structural Roles

author.name: Xintong Li, Kun Zhang, Yujia Zheng

entry.summary: This work formalizes the structural role of latent factors in dynamical systems — where they are expressed, whether they inherit influence from the past, and whether they transmit influence forward — and addresses the correspondence problem of aligning these structures to the same latent coordinate. Under suitable conditions, all three roles can be jointly identified, with an estimation method proposed.

entry.title: A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On-Policy Bidirectional Distillation

author.name: Haoyu Chen, Jun Bai, Yang Liu, Jianfei Zhang, Wenge Rong

entry.summary: MoEvolve exploits the MoE architecture itself as a self-teacher by increasing the per-token expert activation budget to expose latent expert capacity, using bidirectional on-policy distillation to make newly co-activated experts work together. This avoids requiring an external stronger teacher for dense token-level feedback during RLVR training.

entry.title: RTSM: Adapting Recursive Models to Multivariate Time-Series Classification

author.name: Georg Tenzing, Anna Tegon, Luca Benini, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson

entry.summary: RTSM adapts weight-tied recursive refinement to multivariate time-series classification, combining a learned convolutional tokenizer, single-state refinement, and pooled classification readout. It achieves the highest observed mean accuracy (72.81%) across the 30 UEA datasets among compared models. This demonstrates that parameter-efficient recursive architectures can be competitive in the time-series domain.

entry.title: Bridging Compressed Communication and Local Steps via Spectral Method in Federated Learning

author.name: Dmitriy Bystrov, George Chirkov, Daniil Medyakov, Dmitry Bylinkin, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: This paper introduces a spectral federated learning method based on the Muon optimizer that supports both communication compression and local updates, the two foundational efficiency techniques of FL that prior Muon-based FL approaches lacked. It tackles data heterogeneity and communication overhead simultaneously. The work connects a hot centralized optimizer trend to practical distributed training constraints.

entry.title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading

author.name: Ingo Marquardt, Anthilia Alchanat, Priyanka Jain
